entries.zh: 縱韓不能聽我，韓必德王也，必不為鴈行以來，是秦韓不和也，兵雖至，楚不大病也。
entries.en: Even if Han does not heed us, they will be grateful to Your Majesty and will not march in formation alongside Qin. This means Qin and Han will not act in concert. Even if their troops come, Chu will suffer no serious harm.
entries.literal: Even if Han cannot listen to us, Han will certainly feel grateful to the wang and will not come in wild goose formation. This means Qin and Han are not harmonious. Though troops arrive, Chu will not be greatly harmed.

entries.zh: 為能聽我絕和於秦，秦必大怒，以厚怨韓。
entries.en: If Han does heed us and breaks off peace with Qin, then Qin will be furious and bear deep resentment toward Han.
entries.literal: If they can listen to us and cut peace with Qin, Qin will certainly be greatly angry and harbor thick resentment toward Han.

entries.zh: 韓之南交楚，必輕秦；
entries.en: If Han allies with Chu in the south, they will inevitably slight Qin;
entries.literal: Han south ally Chu, must slight Qin;

entries.zh: 輕秦，其應秦必不敬：是因秦、韓之兵而免楚國之患也。」
entries.en: if they slight Qin, their response to Qin will surely be disrespectful, and thus we may use the rift between Qin and Han to free Chu from danger."
entries.literal: Slight Qin, their respond Qin must not respectful: this through Qin, Han troops avoid Chu state calamity.'

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「善。」
entries.en: The King of Chu said, "Excellent."
entries.literal: The King of Chu said, "Good."

entries.zh: 乃警四境之內，興師言救韓。
entries.en: They then mobilized troops throughout the kingdom and raised an army, proclaiming that they would rescue Han.
entries.literal: Thus, they alerted within the four borders and raised troops, saying they would save Han.

entries.zh: 命戰車滿道路，發信臣，多其車，重其幣。
entries.en: They ordered war chariots to fill the roads and dispatched trusted envoys with grand retinues and lavish gifts.
entries.literal: They ordered chariots to fill the roads and sent trusted ministers with many chariots and heavy gifts.

entries.zh: 謂韓王曰：「不穀國雖小，已悉發之矣。
entries.en: The envoys told the King of Han, "Though our humble kingdom is small, we have already mobilized every soldier.
entries.literal: They told the King of Han, "Though our unworthy state is small, we have already mobilized everything.

entries.zh: 願大國遂肆志於秦，不穀將以楚殉韓。」
entries.en: We hope Your Majesty's great state will press forward against Qin without restraint. Our humble king will commit Chu to Han's cause."
entries.literal: Wish great state freely vent will on Qin, unworthy will with Chu follow Han.'

entries.zh: 韓王聞之大說，乃止公仲之行。
entries.en: When the King of Han heard this, he was greatly pleased and called off Gong Zhong's mission.
entries.literal: The King of Han heard this and was greatly pleased, and so he stopped Gong Zhong's mission.

entries.zh: 公仲曰：「不可。
entries.en: Gong Zhong said, "No, Your Majesty must not do this.
entries.literal: Gong Zhong said, "This must not be done.

entries.zh: 夫以實伐我者秦也，以虛名救我者楚也。
entries.en: It is Qin that attacks us with real force; it is Chu that rescues us with empty promises.
entries.literal: The one attacking us with reality is Qin. The one saving us with empty name is Chu.

entries.zh: 王恃楚之虛名，而輕絕彊秦之敵，王必為天下大笑。
entries.en: If Your Majesty relies on Chu's empty promises and carelessly breaks with mighty Qin, you will surely become the laughingstock of the realm.
entries.literal: The wang relying on Chu's empty name, lightly cutting alliance with strong Qin - the wang will certainly become the world's great laughingstock.

entries.zh: 且楚韓非兄弟之國也，又非素約而謀伐秦也。
entries.en: Moreover, Chu and Han are not brother states, nor have they been longstanding allies plotting against Qin.
entries.literal: Moreover, Chu and Han are not brother states, and moreover they are not long-time allies who planned to attack Qin.

entries.zh: 已有伐形，因發兵言救韓，此必陳軫之謀也。
entries.en: They already show every sign of military aggression, yet they send troops claiming to rescue Han. This must be a stratagem devised by Chen Zhen.
entries.literal: They already have the outward marks of war, yet they send troops claiming to rescue Han. This must be Chen Zhen's stratagem.

entries.zh: 且王已使人報於秦矣，今不行，是欺秦也。
entries.en: Besides, Your Majesty has already sent word to Qin. To reverse course now would be to deceive them.
entries.literal: Moreover, the wang has already sent people to report to Qin. Now not going would be deceiving Qin.

entries.zh: 夫輕欺彊秦而信楚之謀臣，恐王必悔之。」
entries.en: If you recklessly deceive mighty Qin while trusting a Chu strategist, I fear Your Majesty will come to regret this deeply."
entries.literal: Lightly deceive strong Qin trust Chu strategist minister, fear wang must regret it.'

entries.zh: 韓王不聽，遂絕於秦。
entries.en: The King of Han would not listen, and so he broke off relations with Qin.
entries.literal: The King of Han would not listen and thus broke off relations with Qin.

entries.zh: 秦因大怒，益甲伐韓，大戰，楚救不至韓。
entries.en: Qin was enraged, reinforced its armies, and attacked Han. A great battle ensued, but Chu's promised relief forces never arrived.
entries.literal: Qin thus became greatly angry, increased its armor and attacked Han. There was a great battle, but Chu's rescue did not arrive at Han.

entries.zh: 十九年，大破我岸門。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year, they inflicted a devastating defeat on us at Anmen.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, they greatly broke our An Men.

entries.zh: 太子倉質於秦以和。
entries.en: The crown prince Cang was sent as a hostage to Qin to sue for peace.
entries.literal: Crown prince Cang became a hostage in Qin for peace.

entries.zh: 楚圍雍氏，韓求救於秦。
entries.en: Chu besieged Yongshi, and Han appealed to Qin for help.
entries.literal: Chu besieged Yong Shi, and Han sought rescue from Qin.

entries.zh: 秦未為發，使公孫昧入韓。
entries.en: Qin had not yet dispatched troops, but sent Gongsun Mei to Han.
entries.literal: Qin had not yet sent troops and sent Gongsun Mei to enter Han.

entries.zh: 公仲曰：「子以秦為且救韓乎？」
entries.en: Gong Zhong asked, "Do you suppose Qin is really about to rescue Han?"
entries.literal: Gong Zhong asked, "Do you think Qin will actually come to rescue Han?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「秦王之言曰『請道南鄭、藍田，出兵於楚以待公』，殆不合矣。」
entries.en: Gongsun Mei replied, "The King of Qin says he will march through Nanzheng and Lantian, deploy troops against Chu, and await your forces there—but I doubt this will come to pass."
entries.literal: He replied, "The King of Qin said, 'Please open the route through Nanzheng and Lantian; I will send troops against Chu to await you'—but that will probably not come to pass."

entries.zh: 公仲曰：「子以為果乎？」
entries.en: Gong Zhong asked, "Do you truly believe that?"
entries.literal: Gong Zhong said: 'You think truly?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「秦王必祖張儀之故智。
entries.en: Gongsun Mei replied, "The King of Qin will surely follow the old stratagem of Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: He replied, "The King of Qin will surely follow Zhang Yi's old stratagem.

entries.zh: 楚威王攻梁也，張儀謂秦王曰：『與楚攻魏，魏折而入於楚，韓固其與國也，是秦孤也。
entries.en: When King Wei of Chu attacked Liang, Zhang Yi told the King of Qin, 'If Qin joins Chu in attacking Wei, Wei will break and submit to Chu; Han is already Wei's ally, so Qin will be left isolated.
entries.literal: When King Wei of Chu attacked Liang, Zhang Yi told the King of Qin: if Qin joined Chu in attacking Wei, Wei would break and submit to Chu; Han was already Wei's allied state, so Qin would be isolated.

entries.zh: 不如出兵以到之，魏楚大戰，秦取西河之外以歸。』
entries.en: It would be better to deploy troops as a show of force. While Wei and Chu exhaust themselves in battle, Qin can seize the lands beyond the West River and return home.'
entries.literal: It would be better to send troops as a show of force. While Wei and Chu fought a great battle, Qin could seize the lands beyond the West River and return.

entries.zh: 今其狀陽言與韓，其實陰善楚。
entries.en: Now Qin outwardly professes alliance with Han, but in truth secretly favors Chu.
entries.literal: Now their appearance openly says alliance with Han, but actually secretly favors Chu.

entries.zh: 公待秦而到，必輕與楚戰。
entries.en: If you wait for Qin's forces to arrive, you will surely rush into battle with Chu without caution.
entries.literal: The duke waits for Qin to arrive and will certainly lightly battle with Chu.

entries.zh: 楚陰得秦之不用也，必易與公相支也。
entries.en: Chu will secretly know that Qin has no intention of intervening, and will find it easy to hold out against you.
entries.literal: Chu secretly gets that Qin will not be used and will certainly easily support the duke.

entries.zh: 公戰而勝楚，遂與公乘楚，施三川而歸。
entries.en: If you fight and defeat Chu, Qin will then join you in pursuing the victory over Chu, seize the Three Rivers region, and go home.
entries.literal: The duke battles and wins against Chu, thus rides with the duke on Chu, bestows San Chuan and returns.

entries.zh: 公戰不勝楚，楚塞三川守之，公不能救也。
entries.en: If you fight but fail to defeat Chu, then Chu will block the Three Rivers region and hold it, and you will be unable to recover it.
entries.literal: If you fight but do not defeat Chu, Chu will block the Three Passes and hold them, and you cannot recover them.

entries.zh: 竊為公患之。
entries.en: I am deeply worried about you on this account.
entries.literal: I secretly worry for the duke about it.

entries.zh: 司馬庚三反於郢，甘茂與昭魚遇於商於，其言收璽，實類有約也。」
entries.en: Sima Geng has traveled to Ying three times; Gan Mao has met Zhao Yu at Shangyu. Though they speak of recovering seals, it appears they have already reached a secret agreement."
entries.literal: Sima Geng three times return Ying, Gan Mao with Zhao Yu meet Shang Yu, their words take seal, actually similar have agreement.'

entries.zh: 公仲恐，曰：「然則柰何？」
entries.en: Gong Zhong grew alarmed and asked, "Then what should we do?"
entries.literal: Gong Zhong grew alarmed and said, "Then what should we do?"

entries.zh: 曰：「公必先韓而後秦，先身而後張儀。
entries.en: Gongsun Mei said, "You must put Han first and Qin second, your own interests before those of Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: Gongsun Mei said, "You must put Han before Qin, and your own interests before Zhang Yi's.

entries.zh: 公不如亟以國合於齊楚，齊楚必委國於公。
entries.en: You had better make haste to align the state with Qi and Chu. Qi and Chu will surely entrust matters of state to you.
entries.literal: The duke should quickly unite the state with Qi and Chu. Qi and Chu will certainly entrust the state to the duke.

entries.zh: 公之所惡者張儀也，其實猶不無秦也。」
entries.en: What you truly oppose is Zhang Yi, not Qin itself. Even so, you need not cut ties with Qin entirely."
entries.literal: Duke what hate Zhang Yi, actually still not without Qin.'

entries.zh: 於是楚解雍氏圍。
entries.en: Thereupon Chu lifted the siege of Yongshi.
entries.literal: Thus, Chu lifted the siege of Yong Shi.

entries.zh: 韓厥，晉景公之三年，晉司寇屠岸賈將作亂，誅靈公之賊趙盾。
entries.en: In the third year of Duke Jing of Jin, the Minister of Justice Tu'an Jia plotted to carry out a purge, intending to punish Zhao Dun for the assassination of Duke Ling.
entries.literal: Han Jue, in Jin Jing Gong's third year, the Jin Si Kou Tu An Jia was about to rebel and execute Ling Gong's traitor Zhao Dun.

entries.zh: 趙盾已死矣，欲誅其子趙朔。
entries.en: Zhao Dun was already dead, so Tu'an Jia sought to execute his son, Zhao Shuo.
entries.literal: Zhao Dun was already dead, and they desired to execute his son Zhao Shuo.

entries.zh: 韓厥止賈，賈不聽。
entries.en: Han Jue tried to dissuade him, but Tu'an Jia would not listen.
entries.literal: Han Jue tried to stop Jia, but Jia would not listen.

entries.zh: 厥告趙朔令亡。
entries.en: Han Jue warned Zhao Shuo and urged him to flee.
entries.literal: Jue told Zhao Shuo to flee.

entries.zh: 朔曰：「子必能不絕趙祀，死不恨矣。」
entries.en: Zhao Shuo said, "If you can ensure that the Zhao sacrifices are not extinguished, I will die without regret."
entries.literal: Shuo said, "If you, sir, can ensure the Zhao sacrifices are not cut off, I shall die without regret."

entries.zh: 韓厥許之。
entries.en: Han Jue gave him his word.
entries.literal: Han Jue promised him.

entries.zh: 及賈誅趙氏，厥稱疾不出。
entries.en: When Tu'an Jia massacred the Zhao clan, Han Jue feigned illness and stayed away.
entries.literal: When Jia executed the Zhao clan, Jue claimed illness and did not go out.

entries.zh: 程嬰、公孫杵臼之藏趙孤趙武也，厥知之。
entries.en: When Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu hid the orphan Zhao Wu, Han Jue knew of it.
entries.literal: Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chu Jiu hid the Zhao orphan Zhao Wu, and Jue knew it.

entries.zh: 襄王四年，與秦武王會臨晉。
entries.en: In the fourth year of King Xiang, he met with King Wu of Qin at Linjin.
entries.literal: In Xiang Wang's fourth year, they met with Qin Wu Wang at Lin Jin.

entries.zh: 其秋，秦使甘茂攻我宜陽。
entries.en: That autumn, Qin sent Gan Mao to attack our city of Yiyang.
entries.literal: That autumn, Qin sent Gan Mao to attack our Yi Yang.

entries.zh: 五年，秦拔我宜陽，斬首六萬。
entries.en: In the fifth year, Qin captured our Yiyang and took sixty thousand heads.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Qin captured our Yi Yang and beheaded sixty thousand.

entries.zh: 秦武王卒。
entries.en: King Wu of Qin died.
entries.literal: Qin Wu Wang died.

entries.zh: 六年，秦復與我武遂。
entries.en: In the sixth year, Qin returned Wusui to us.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, Qin again gave us Wu Sui.

entries.zh: 九年，秦復取我武遂。
entries.en: In the ninth year, Qin took Wusui from us once again.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, Qin again took our Wu Sui.

entries.zh: 十年，太子嬰朝秦而歸。
entries.en: In the tenth year, the crown prince Ying attended an audience at the Qin court and returned.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, crown prince Ying went for audience in Qin and returned.

entries.zh: 十一年，秦伐我，取穰。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, Qin attacked us and captured Rang.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, Qin attacked us and took Rang.

entries.zh: 與秦伐楚，敗楚將唐眛。
entries.en: They joined Qin in attacking Chu and defeated the Chu general Tang Mei.
entries.literal: They attacked Chu with Qin and defeated Chu general Tang Mei.

entries.zh: 十二年，太子嬰死。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, the crown prince Ying died.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, crown prince Ying died.

entries.zh: 公子咎、公子蟣蝨爭為太子。
entries.en: Prince Jiu and Prince Ji Shi contended for the position of crown prince.
entries.literal: Prince Jiu and Prince Jishi contended to become crown prince.

entries.zh: 時蟣蝨質於楚。
entries.en: At that time, Jishi was held as a hostage in Chu.
entries.literal: At the time, Jiu Jie was a hostage in Chu.

entries.zh: 蘇代謂韓咎曰：「蟣蝨亡在楚，楚王欲內之甚。
entries.en: Su Dai said to Han Jiu, "Ji Shi has fled and is in Chu, and the King of Chu is very eager to install him.
entries.literal: Su Dai said to Han Jiu, "Ji Shi has fled and is in Chu, and the King of Chu is very eager to bring him in.

entries.zh: 今楚兵十餘萬在方城之外，公何不令楚王筑萬室之都雍氏之旁，韓必起兵以救之，公必將矣。
entries.en: Now Chu has over a hundred thousand troops beyond Fangcheng. Why not have the King of Chu build a great city beside Yongshi? Han will surely raise an army to counter it, and you, my lord, will certainly be given command of the forces.
entries.literal: Now Chu has over one hundred thousand troops outside Fang Cheng. Why doesn't the duke order the Chu wang to build a city of ten thousand rooms beside Yong Shi? Han will certainly raise troops to save it, and the duke will certainly be the general.

entries.zh: 公因以韓楚之兵奉蟣蝨而內之，其聽公必矣，必以楚韓封公也。」
entries.en: Then you can use the combined forces of Han and Chu to escort Ji Shi and install him as heir. He will certainly heed your counsel, and Chu and Han will surely grant you a fief in return."
entries.literal: Duke thus with Han Chu troops support Jiu Jie take him in, he listen duke must, must with Chu Han enfeoff duke.'

entries.zh: 韓咎從其計。
entries.en: Han Jiu followed this plan.
entries.literal: Han Jiu followed his plan.

entries.zh: 韓之先與周同姓，姓姬氏。
entries.en: The ancestors of the Han shared the same surname as the Zhou royal house—they were of the Ji clan.
entries.literal: The Han ancestors shared the same surname as the Zhou royal house, the Ji clan.

entries.zh: 其後苗裔事晉，得封於韓原，曰韓武子。
entries.en: Their later descendants served the state of Jin and received a fief at Hanyuan. The first lord of that line was known as Han Wuzi.
entries.literal: Later descendants served Jin, obtained enfeoffment at Han Yuan, and were called Han wuzi.

entries.zh: 武子後三世有韓厥，從封姓為韓氏。
entries.en: Three generations after Wuzi, there arose Han Jue, who took the surname Han from his fief.
entries.literal: Three generations after wuzi there was Han Jue, who from his enfeoffment took the surname Han clan.

entries.zh: 十九年，宣王卒，子湣王地立。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year, King Xuan died. His son, King Min, whose personal name was Di, succeeded him.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, King Xuan died. His son King Min Di succeeded him.

entries.zh: 湣王元年，秦使張儀與諸侯執政會於齧桑。
entries.en: In the first year of King Min, Qin sent Zhang Yi to meet the chief ministers of the feudal lords at Niesang.
entries.literal: In King Min's first year, Qin sent Zhang Yi to meet with the governing ministers of the feudal lords at Niesang.

entries.zh: 三年，封田嬰於薛。
entries.en: In the third year, Tian Ying received Xue as his fief.
entries.literal: In the third year, Tian Ying was enfeoffed at Xue.

entries.zh: 四年，迎婦於秦。
entries.en: In the fourth year, he brought in a bride from Qin.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he welcomed a bride from Qin.

entries.zh: 七年，與宋攻魏，敗之觀澤。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Qi joined Song in attacking Wei and defeated it at Guanze.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he joined Song in attacking Wei and defeated it at Guanze.

entries.zh: 十二年，攻魏。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of King Min's reign, Qi attacked Wei.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, they attacked Wei.

entries.zh: 楚圍雍氏，秦敗屈丐。
entries.en: At the same time, Chu besieged the city of Yongshi, and Qin defeated the Chu general Qu Gai.
entries.literal: Chu besieged Yongshi. Qin defeated Qu Gai.

entries.zh: 蘇代謂田軫曰：「臣願有謁於公，其為事甚完，使楚利公，成為福，不成亦為福。
entries.en: Su Dai addressed Tian Zhen: "I have a proposal for you, my lord. The plan is airtight: whether it succeeds or fails, it will work to your advantage in relation to Chu.
entries.literal: Su Dai said to Tian Zhen: 'Your servant wishes to present something to you. The plan is very thorough: if Chu benefits you, success is fortunate, and failure is also fortunate.

entries.zh: 今者臣立於門，客有言曰魏王謂韓馮、張儀曰：『煮棗將拔，齊兵又進，子來救寡人則可矣；
entries.en: Today, as I stood at the gate, a visitor reported that the King of Wei told Han Feng and Zhang Yi: 'Zaozao is about to fall, and the army of Qi presses forward. Come to my rescue, and all will be well.
entries.literal: Today as I stood at the gate, a guest said that the King of Wei told Han Feng and Zhang Yi: 'Zaozao is about to fall, and Qi's army advances further. If you come to rescue me, it will be sufficient.

entries.zh: 不救寡人，寡人弗能拔。』
entries.en: If you do not rescue me, I shall not be able to hold out.'
entries.literal: If you do not rescue me, I will not be able to hold out.'

entries.zh: 此特轉辭也。
entries.en: But this is merely a diplomatic ploy.
entries.literal: This is merely a diversionary statement.

entries.zh: 秦、韓之兵毋東，旬餘，則魏氏轉韓從秦，秦逐張儀，交臂而事齊楚，此公之事成也。」
entries.en: If the troops of Qin and Han do not march east, then within ten days Wei will detach Han from Qin's cause, Qin will dismiss Zhang Yi, and they will all clasp hands to serve Qi and Chu. Then your designs will be realized."
entries.literal: If the troops of Qin and Han do not move east, then within ten days Wei will shift Han to follow Qin, Qin will send Zhang Yi away, and they will join together to serve Qi and Chu — then your affairs will be accomplished.'

entries.zh: 田軫曰：「柰何使無東？」
entries.en: Tian Zhen asked: "But how can we prevent them from marching east?"
entries.literal: Tian Zhen asked: 'How can we prevent them from marching east?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「韓馮之救魏之辭，必不謂韓王曰『馮以為魏』，必曰『馮將以秦韓之兵東卻齊宋，馮因摶三國之兵，乘屈丐之獘，南割於楚，故地必盡得之矣』。
entries.en: Su Dai replied: "When Han Feng makes his case for rescuing Wei, he will never tell the King of Han, 'I am doing this for Wei.' Instead, he will say: 'I shall lead the combined forces of Qin and Han eastward to repel Qi and Song. Then I shall unite the armies of three states, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, and carve territory from Chu in the south. All the old lands shall surely be recovered.'
entries.literal: He replied: 'When Han Feng argues for rescuing Wei, he will certainly not tell the King of Han "Feng does this for Wei's sake." He will surely say: "Feng will use the troops of Qin and Han to drive Qi and Song eastward, then unite the three states' armies, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, and carve territory from Chu to the south — all the former lands will be recovered.'

entries.zh: 張儀救魏之辭，必不謂秦王曰『儀以為魏』，必曰『儀且以秦韓之兵東距齊宋，儀將摶三國之兵，乘屈丐之獘，南割於楚，名存亡國，實伐三川而歸，此王業也』。
entries.en: Likewise, when Zhang Yi argues for rescuing Wei, he will never tell the King of Qin, 'I am doing this for Wei.' He will say: 'I shall lead the forces of Qin and Han eastward to block Qi and Song, then unite the three states' armies, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, and seize territory from Chu. In name, we save a perishing state; in reality, we conquer Sanchuan and return in triumph. This is the enterprise of a true king.'
entries.literal: Zhang Yi's argument for rescuing Wei will certainly not tell the King of Qin 'Yi does this for Wei.' He will surely say: 'Yi will lead the troops of Qin and Han east to repel Qi and Song, then unite the three states' armies, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, carve territory from Chu in the south — in name saving a perishing state, in reality attacking Sanchuan and returning. This is a royal enterprise.'

entries.zh: 公令楚王與韓氏地，使秦制和，謂秦王曰『請與韓地，而王以施三川，韓氏之兵不用而得地於楚』。
entries.en: If you persuade the King of Chu to cede land to Han and let Qin broker the peace, saying to the King of Qin: 'Grant land to Han, and Your Majesty may extend your influence over Sanchuan. Han's armies need not march, and yet they gain territory from Chu.'
entries.literal: If you have the King of Chu give land to Han and let Qin mediate the peace, saying to the King of Qin: 'Please give land to Han, and the King can bestow his favor upon Sanchuan. Han's troops need not be used and they will gain territory from Chu.'

entries.zh: 韓馮之東兵之辭且謂秦何？
entries.en: And what will Han Feng say to Qin when he argues for sending troops east?
entries.literal: What will Han Feng say to Qin in his argument for marching the troops east?

entries.zh: 曰『秦兵不用而得三川，伐楚韓以窘魏，魏氏不敢東，是孤齊也』。
entries.en: He will say: 'Qin gains Sanchuan without deploying a single soldier, while attacking Chu and Han corners Wei. Wei will not dare move east — and Qi will be isolated.'
entries.literal: He will say: 'Qin gains Sanchuan without using its troops, attacks Chu and Han to corner Wei, Wei dares not move east — this isolates Qi.'

entries.zh: 張儀之東兵之辭且謂何？
entries.en: And what will Zhang Yi say in his argument for sending troops east?
entries.literal: What will Zhang Yi say in his argument for marching troops east?

entries.zh: 曰『秦韓欲地而兵有案，聲威發於魏，魏氏之欲不失齊楚者有資矣』。
entries.en: He will say: 'Qin and Han desire territory while keeping their armies in reserve. Their military prestige is directed at Wei, and Wei's desire to maintain ties with Qi and Chu will have the leverage it needs.'
entries.literal: He will say: 'Qin and Han desire territory while their troops stand ready. The prestige and power are directed at Wei; Wei's desire not to lose Qi and Chu will have resources to rely on.'

entries.zh: 魏氏轉秦韓爭事齊楚，楚王欲而無與地，公令秦韓之兵不用而得地，有一大德也。
entries.en: Wei will then redirect Qin and Han into competing to serve Qi and Chu. The King of Chu desires this outcome but has offered no territory. If you enable Qin and Han to acquire territory without deploying their armies, that will be an immense favor.
entries.literal: Wei will then shift Qin and Han into competing to serve Qi and Chu. The King of Chu wishes this but has given no territory. You enable Qin and Han to gain territory without using their troops — this is one great favor.

entries.zh: 秦韓之王劫於韓馮、張儀而東兵以徇服魏，公常執左券以責於秦韓，此其善於公而惡張子多資矣。」
entries.en: If the kings of Qin and Han are pressured by Han Feng and Zhang Yi to march east and coerce Wei, you will always hold the tally against Qin and Han. This arrangement greatly favors you while undermining Zhang Yi."
entries.literal: If the kings of Qin and Han are pressured by Han Feng and Zhang Yi to march east and coerce Wei into submission, you will always hold the left half of the tally to make demands upon Qin and Han. This benefits you greatly while working against Zhang Yi.'

entries.zh: 陳完者，陳厲公他之子也。
entries.en: Chen Wan was the son of Duke Li of Chen, whose personal name was Ta.
entries.literal: Chen Wan was the son of Chen Li Gong Ta.

entries.zh: 完生，周太史過陳，陳厲公使卜完，卦得觀之否：「是為觀國之光，利用賓于王。
entries.en: When Wan was born, the Grand Astrologer of Zhou happened to pass through the state of Chen. Duke Li had him cast a divination for the child. The hexagram obtained was Guan changing to Pi, and the reading declared: 'This signifies one who shall observe the glory of a state, and it is auspicious for him to serve as a guest of a king.
entries.literal: When Wan was born, the Grand Astrologer of Zhou passed through Chen. Duke Li of Chen had him divine for Wan. The hexagram obtained was Guan changing to Pi: 'This means observing the glory of the state, advantageous to be a guest of the king.

entries.zh: 此其代陳有國乎？
entries.en: Could it be that his line will one day supplant Chen and possess a state of its own?
entries.literal: Will this one replace Chen and possess a state?

entries.zh: 不在此而在異國乎？
entries.en: Yet perhaps not in this state, but in a foreign land?
entries.literal: Not in this state but in a different state?

entries.zh: 非此其身也，在其子孫。
entries.en: It will not come to pass in his own lifetime, but through his descendants.
entries.literal: Not in this person himself, but in his descendants.

entries.zh: 若在異國，必姜姓。
entries.en: If it is to be in a foreign state, then it must be one ruled by the Jiang clan.
entries.literal: If in a different state, it must be a state of the Jiang surname.

entries.zh: 姜姓，四嶽之後。
entries.en: The Jiang are descendants of the Four Peaks.
entries.literal: The Jiang surname are descendants of the Four Peaks.

entries.zh: 物莫能兩大，陳衰，此其昌乎？」
entries.en: Nothing in this world can sustain two great powers at once — when Chen declines, his line shall surely flourish."
entries.literal: No thing can have two greats; when Chen declines, this one shall flourish.'

entries.zh: 陳勝雖已死，其所置遣侯王將相竟亡秦，由涉首事也。
entries.en: Though Chen Sheng himself was already dead, the lords, kings, generals, and ministers he had appointed and dispatched ultimately destroyed Qin. It was She who lit the first flame.
entries.literal: Though Chen Sheng was already dead, the marquises, kings, generals, and chancellors he established and dispatched ultimately destroyed Qin. It was She who first raised the standard.

entries.zh: 高祖時為陳涉置守冢三十家碭，至今血食。
entries.en: In the time of Emperor Gaozu, thirty households were established at Dang to tend Chen She's tomb. To this day, sacrifices are offered there.
entries.literal: During the time of Emperor Gaozu, thirty households were established at Dang to guard Chen She's tomb. Sacrifices are offered there to this day.

entries.zh: 陳勝者，陽城人也，字涉。
entries.en: Chen Sheng was a native of Yangcheng, styled She.
entries.literal: Chen Sheng was a man from Yangcheng. His courtesy name was She.

entries.zh: 吳廣者，陽夏人也，字叔。
entries.en: Wu Guang was a native of Yangxia, styled Shu.
entries.literal: Wu Guang was a man from Yangxia. His courtesy name was Shu.

entries.zh: 陳涉少時，嘗與人傭耕，輟耕之壟上，悵恨久之，曰：「茍富貴，無相忘。」
entries.en: In his youth, Chen She once worked as a hired laborer plowing fields alongside others. He stopped his plowing and climbed to the top of a ridge, where he stood brooding for a long while before saying, 'If any of us should ever become wealthy and noble, let us not forget one another.'
entries.literal: Chen She young time, once with people hired plow, paused plow on ridge, melancholy resent long time, said: 'If rich noble, no mutually forget.'

entries.zh: 庸者笑而應曰：「若為庸耕，何富貴也？」
entries.en: The other laborers laughed and replied, 'You are nothing but a hired hand plowing fields — how could you ever become wealthy and noble?'
entries.literal: Hired ones laugh respond said: 'You as hired plow, what rich noble?'

entries.zh: 陳涉太息曰：「嗟乎，燕雀安知鴻鵠之志哉！」
entries.en: Chen She heaved a deep sigh and said, 'Alas! How can sparrows and swallows know the ambitions of swans and wild geese?'
entries.literal: Chen She sighed deeply and said: 'Alas! How can sparrows and swallows know the ambitions of swans and wild geese!'

entries.zh: 楚元王劉交者，高祖之同母少弟也，字游。
entries.en: Liu Jiao, King Yuan of Chu, was the youngest brother of Emperor Gaozu by the same mother, and bore the courtesy name You.
entries.literal: King Yuan of Chu, Liu Jiao, was Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother, styled You.

entries.zh: 高祖六年，已禽楚王韓信於陳，乃以弟交為楚王，都彭城。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Gaozu's reign, having captured Han Xin, the King of Chu, at Chen, the emperor appointed his brother Jiao as King of Chu, with his capital at Pengcheng.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's sixth year, after capturing the Chu king Han Xin at Chen, he made his brother Jiao King of Chu, with his capital at Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 即位二十三年卒，子夷王郢立。
entries.en: After twenty-three years on the throne, he died, and his son Ying succeeded him as King Yi.
entries.literal: He reigned for twenty-three years and died. His son, King Yi Ying, succeeded him.

entries.zh: 夷王四年卒，子王戊立。
entries.en: King Yi reigned for four years before his death, and his son Wu succeeded him.
entries.literal: King Yi reigned for four years and died. His son, King Wu, succeeded him.

entries.zh: 高祖兄弟四人，長兄伯，伯蚤卒。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu had four brothers in all. The eldest, Bo, died young.
entries.literal: Gaozu had four brothers: the eldest was Bo, who died young.

entries.zh: 始高祖微時，嘗辟事，時時與賓客過巨嫂食。
entries.en: In the early days, when Gaozu was still a man of humble station, he would shirk his duties and often bring guests to dine at his eldest brother's wife's home.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was still of humble status, he once avoided official duties and frequently went with guests to eat at his elder brother's wife's house.

entries.zh: 嫂厭叔，叔與客來，嫂詳為羹盡，櫟釜，賓客以故去。
entries.en: His sister-in-law grew tired of her brother-in-law. Whenever he arrived with guests, she would pretend the stew had run out and scrape the pot loudly, so the guests would take their leave.
entries.literal: The sister-in-law disliked her husband's younger brother. When he came with guests, she pretended the stew was gone and scraped the pot, so the guests left.

entries.zh: 已而視釜中尚有羹，高祖由此怨其嫂。
entries.en: But when they looked in the pot afterward, there was still plenty of stew. From that day on, Gaozu bore a grudge against his sister-in-law.
entries.literal: Later, when they checked the pot, there was still stew left. From this, Gaozu resented his sister-in-law.

entries.zh: 及高祖為帝，封昆弟，而伯子獨不得封。
entries.en: When Gaozu became emperor and enfeoffed his brothers, Bo's son alone received no fief.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became emperor, he enfeoffed his brothers, but Bo's son alone did not receive an enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 太上皇以為言，高祖曰：「某非忘封之也，為其母不長者耳。」
entries.en: The Retired Emperor raised the matter, and Gaozu replied, "It is not that I forgot to grant him a fief—it is because his mother was no woman of virtue."
entries.literal: The Supreme Emperor spoke of this, and Gaozu said, "It is not that I forgot to enfeoff him; it is because his mother was not virtuous."

entries.zh: 於是乃封其子信為羹頡侯。
entries.en: He then enfeoffed Bo's son Xin as the Marquis of Gengjie.
entries.literal: Therefore, he enfeoffed Bo's son Xin as Marquis of Gengjie.

entries.zh: 而王次兄仲於代。
entries.en: His second brother, Zhong, was made King of Dai.
entries.literal: He then established his second brother Zhong as king in Dai.

entries.zh: 漢已平吳楚，孝景帝欲以德侯子續吳，以元王子禮續楚。
entries.en: After Han had pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wished to restore the line of Wu through the son of the Marquis of De, and the line of Chu through King Yuan's son Liu Li.
entries.literal: After Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wanted to continue Wu with the son of Marquis De, and continue Chu with King Yuan's son Liu Li.

entries.zh: 竇太后曰：「吳王，老人也，宜為宗室順善。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Dou said, "The King of Wu was an elder of the realm. He should have been a model of obedience and virtue among the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Empress Dou said: "The King of Wu was an old man, he should have been compliant and virtuous within the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 今乃首率七國，紛亂天下，柰何續其後！」
entries.en: Instead, he took the lead in rallying seven states to throw the realm into chaos—how can we perpetuate his line!"
entries.literal: Now he was the first to lead the seven states in throwing the realm into chaos—how can we continue his descendants!"

entries.zh: 不許吳，許立楚後。
entries.en: The request for Wu was denied, but permission was granted to continue the line of Chu.
entries.literal: Wu was not allowed, but Chu was permitted to establish descendants.

entries.zh: 是時禮為漢宗正。
entries.en: At that time, Li was serving as the Director of the Imperial Clan for the Han court.
entries.literal: At this time Li served as Han's Director of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 乃拜禮為楚王，奉元王宗廟，是為楚文王。
entries.en: Li was then appointed King of Chu to carry on the ancestral sacrifices of King Yuan, and he became known as King Wen of Chu.
entries.literal: Li was appointed King of Chu to maintain King Yuan's ancestral temples, and became King Wen of Chu.

entries.zh: 趙王劉遂者，其父高祖中子，名友，謚曰「幽」。
entries.en: Liu Sui, King of Zhao—his father was the middle son of Emperor Gaozu, named You, who was given the posthumous title of You, 'the Secluded.'
entries.literal: King Zhao Liu Sui—his father was Gaozu's middle son, whose personal name was You and whose posthumous title was You, "the Secluded."

entries.zh: 幽王以憂死，故為「幽」。
entries.en: King You died of grief, and so received the posthumous name 'the Secluded.'
entries.literal: King You died of sorrow, hence "You."

entries.zh: 高后王呂祿於趙，一歲而高后崩。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Gao installed Lü Lu as King of Zhao, but within a year she passed away.
entries.literal: Empress Gao established Lü Lu as king in Zhao, and after one year Empress Gao passed away.

entries.zh: 大臣誅諸呂呂祿等，乃立幽王子遂為趙王。
entries.en: The great ministers put to death the Lu clansmen, including Lu Lu, and then established Sui, son of King You, as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: The ministers executed the various Lü clansmen including Lü Lu, and established King You's son Sui as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 王戊立二十年，冬，坐為薄太后服私姦，削東海郡。
entries.en: In the twentieth year of King Wu's reign, during winter, he was found guilty of committing adultery during the mourning period for Empress Dowager Bo, and the commandery of Donghai was stripped from him.
entries.literal: King Wu reigned for twenty years. In winter, he was convicted of committing adultery while mourning Empress Bo, and Donghai commandery was stripped from him.

entries.zh: 春，戊與吳王合謀反，其相張尚、太傅趙夷吾諫，不聽。
entries.en: In spring, King Wu of Chu joined the King of Wu in a conspiracy to rebel. His chancellor Zhang Shang and Grand Tutor Zhao Yiwu remonstrated with him, but he refused to listen.
entries.literal: In spring, King Wu joined the King of Wu in conspiring to rebel. His chancellor Zhang Shang and tutor Zhao Yiwu advised against it, but he would not listen.

entries.zh: 戊則殺尚、夷吾，起兵與吳西攻梁，破棘壁。
entries.en: Wu had Shang and Yiwu executed, raised his troops, and marched west with the forces of Wu against Liang, breaching the fortifications at Jibi.
entries.literal: King Wu then executed Shang and Yiwu, raised troops, and marched west with the King of Wu against Liang, breaking through Jibi.

entries.zh: 至昌邑南，與漢將周亞夫戰。
entries.en: They advanced as far south as Changyi, where they engaged the Han general Zhou Yafu in battle.
entries.literal: They reached south of Changyi and fought with the Han general Zhou Yafu.

entries.zh: 漢絕吳楚糧道，士卒饑，吳王走，楚王戊自殺，軍遂降漢。
entries.en: The Han forces cut off the supply lines of Wu and Chu. The soldiers starved. The King of Wu fled, and King Wu of Chu took his own life. The army then surrendered to Han.
entries.literal: Han cut off Wu and Chu's supply lines. The soldiers grew hungry. The King of Wu fled. King Wu of Chu committed suicide. The army surrendered to Han.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：國之將興，必有禎祥，君子用而小人退。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: When a state is about to rise, auspicious signs are sure to appear—the worthy are given office and the petty retreat.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: When a state is about to flourish, there will certainly be auspicious omens, the worthy are employed and the petty withdraw.

entries.zh: 國之將亡，賢人隱，亂臣貴。
entries.en: When a state is about to fall, the wise withdraw into seclusion and the treacherous are elevated.
entries.literal: When a state is about to perish, the worthy hide themselves and traitors are honored.

entries.zh: 使楚王戊毋刑申公，遵其言，趙任防與先生，豈有篡殺之謀，為天下僇哉？
entries.en: Had King Wu of Chu not punished Master Shen but heeded his counsel, and had Zhao entrusted its affairs to Master Fangyu, how could there have been conspiracies of usurpation and bloodshed, bringing shame upon the realm?
entries.literal: If King Wu of Chu had not punished Master Shen and had followed his counsel, and if Zhao had employed Master Fangyu, how could there have been plots of usurpation and murder, bringing disgrace upon the realm?

entries.zh: 賢人乎，賢人乎！
entries.en: O, the worthy! O, the worthy!
entries.literal: Ah, the worthy! Ah, the worthy!

entries.zh: 非質有其內，惡能用之哉？
entries.en: Without possessing true substance within oneself, how can one make use of the worthy?
entries.literal: If one does not possess the substance within, how can one employ it?

entries.zh: 甚矣，「安危在出令，存亡在所任」，誠哉是言也！
entries.en: How profoundly true is the saying: 'Whether a state knows security or peril depends on the decrees it issues; whether it survives or perishes depends on whom it appoints'—these words ring true indeed!
entries.literal: How true it is that 'security and danger lie in issuing commands, survival and extinction lie in whom one employs'—truly this saying is correct!

entries.zh: 遂既王趙二十六年，孝景帝時坐晁錯以適削趙王常山之郡。
entries.en: After Sui had been King of Zhao for twenty-six years, in Emperor Jing's time, because of Chao Cuo's plan to reduce the feudal domains, the commandery of Changshan was stripped from his domain.
entries.literal: Sui had been king of Zhao for twenty-six years when, in Emperor Jing's time, on account of Chao Cuo's policy of reducing the feudal domains, the Changshan commandery was stripped from the Zhao king.

entries.zh: 吳楚反，趙王遂與合謀起兵。
entries.en: When Wu and Chu rose in rebellion, King Sui of Zhao joined the conspiracy and raised his own troops.
entries.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, King Zhao Sui conspired with them and raised troops.

entries.zh: 其相建德、內史王悍諫，不聽。
entries.en: His chancellor Jiande and Interior Minister Wang Han remonstrated with him, but he would not listen.
entries.literal: His chancellor Jiande and interior minister Wang Han advised against it, but he wouldn't listen.

entries.zh: 遂燒殺建德、王悍，發兵屯其西界，欲待吳與俱西。
entries.en: Sui had Jiande and Wang Han burned alive, deployed troops to garrison his western border, and planned to wait for the forces of Wu before advancing west together.
entries.literal: Sui burned and killed Jiande and Wang Han, sent troops to garrison his western border, and wished to wait for Wu to advance west together.

entries.zh: 北使匈奴，與連和攻漢。
entries.en: He dispatched envoys northward to the Xiongnu, seeking an alliance to jointly attack Han.
entries.literal: He sent envoys north to the Xiongnu, allied with them, and planned to attack Han.

entries.zh: 漢使曲周侯酈寄擊之。
entries.en: Han dispatched Li Ji, the Marquis of Quzhou, to attack him.
entries.literal: Han sent Marquis Quzhou Li Ji to attack him.

entries.zh: 趙王遂還，城守邯鄲，相距七月。
entries.en: King Sui of Zhao withdrew and fortified Handan. The two sides held each other at bay for seven months.
entries.literal: King Zhao Sui returned and defended Handan. They confronted each other for seven months.

entries.zh: 吳楚敗於梁，不能西。
entries.en: Wu and Chu were defeated at Liang and could advance no further west.
entries.literal: Wu and Chu were defeated at Liang and could not advance west.

entries.zh: 匈奴聞之，亦止，不肯入漢邊。
entries.en: When the Xiongnu learned of this, they too held back and refused to cross into Han territory.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu heard about this and also stopped, refusing to enter Han territory.

entries.zh: 欒布自破齊還，乃并兵引水灌趙城。
entries.en: Luan Bu, returning from his victory over Qi, combined his forces and diverted the river to flood the Zhao capital.
entries.literal: Luan Bu returned from defeating Qi and combined forces to divert water and flood Zhao city.

entries.zh: 趙城壞，趙王自殺，邯鄲遂降。
entries.en: The walls of Zhao collapsed. The King of Zhao took his own life, and Handan surrendered.
entries.literal: Zhao city was breached. King Zhao committed suicide. Handan surrendered.

entries.zh: 趙幽王絕後。
entries.en: The line of King You of Zhao was thus extinguished.
entries.literal: The line of King Zhao You was extinguished.

entries.zh: 漢四年，漢王之敗成皋，北渡河，得張耳、韓信軍，軍修武，深溝高壘，使劉賈將二萬人，騎數百，渡白馬津入楚地，燒其積聚，以破其業，無以給項王軍食。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Han, after the King of Han suffered defeat at Chenggao and crossed the Yellow River northward, he joined forces with the armies of Zhang Er and Han Xin. He encamped at Xiuwu behind deep trenches and high ramparts, then dispatched Liu Jia with twenty thousand infantry and several hundred cavalry to cross at Baima Ford into Chu territory. There they burned the enemy's grain stores, devastating their supply lines so that Xiang Yu's army could no longer be fed.
entries.literal: In Han year 4, when the Han King was defeated at Chenggao and crossed north over the river, obtaining the armies of Zhang Er and Han Xin, he stationed at Xiuwu with deep moats and high ramparts, commanding Liu Jia to lead 20,000 men and several hundred cavalry across the Baima Ford into Chu territory, burning their grain stores to disrupt their war effort and prevent them from supplying Xiang Yu's army with food.

entries.zh: 已而楚兵擊劉賈，賈輒壁不肯與戰，而與彭越相保。
entries.en: Before long, Chu forces struck at Liu Jia, but he fortified his position and refused to engage, instead joining with Peng Yue to hold firm.
entries.literal: Soon after, Chu troops attacked Liu Jia, but Jia entrenched himself and refused to fight, instead holding out with Peng Yue.

entries.zh: 荊王劉賈者，諸劉，不知其何屬初起時。
entries.en: Liu Jia, the King of Jing, was a member of the Liu clan, though no one knows which branch he belonged to at the time of the initial uprising.
entries.literal: King Jing Liu Jia was one of the various Liu clansmen; no one knows which branch he belonged to during the initial uprising.

entries.zh: 漢王元年，還定三秦，劉賈為將軍，定塞地，從東擊項籍。
entries.en: In the first year of the King of Han, after the Three Qin territories had been subdued, Liu Jia served as a general, pacifying the frontier regions before marching east to attack Xiang Ji.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Han King, after pacifying the Three Qins, Liu Jia served as general, secured the border regions, and followed east to attack Xiang Yu.

entries.zh: 漢五年，漢王追項籍至固陵，使劉賈南渡淮圍壽春。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Han, the King of Han pursued Xiang Ji to Guling and ordered Liu Jia to cross the Huai River southward to lay siege to Shouchun.
entries.literal: In Han year 5, the Han King pursued Xiang Yu to Guling, commanding Liu Jia to cross south over the Huai and besiege Shouchun.

entries.zh: 還至，使人閒招楚大司馬周殷。
entries.en: Upon his return, he sent agents to covertly win over Zhou Yin, the Grand Marshal of Chu.
entries.literal: On the return, he sent agents to secretly recruit Chu's Grand Marshal Zhou Yin.

entries.zh: 周殷反楚，佐劉賈舉九江，迎武王黥布兵，皆會垓下，共擊項籍。
entries.en: Zhou Yin turned against Chu and helped Liu Jia seize the Jiujiang region. They then welcomed the forces of King Wu, Ying Bu, and all their armies converged at Gaixia to strike against Xiang Ji.
entries.literal: Zhou Yin defected from Chu and assisted Liu Jia in capturing Jiujiang, welcoming King Wu Ying Bu's troops, all gathering at Gaixia to jointly attack Xiang Yu.

entries.zh: 漢王因使劉賈將九江兵，與太尉盧綰西南擊臨江王共尉。
entries.en: The King of Han then directed Liu Jia to lead the Jiujiang troops and, together with Grand Commandant Lu Wan, march southwest to attack Gong Wei, the King of Linjiang.
entries.literal: The Han King then commanded Liu Jia to lead the Jiujiang troops southwest with Grand Commandant Lu Wan to attack King Linjiang Gong Wei.

entries.zh: 共尉已死，以臨江為南郡。
entries.en: After Gong Wei's death, the territory of Linjiang was converted into the Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: Gong Wei had already died, so Linjiang was made into Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 漢六年春，會諸侯於陳，廢楚王信，囚之，分其地為二國。
entries.en: In the spring of the sixth year of Han, the emperor assembled the feudal lords at Chen, deposed Han Xin, the King of Chu, had him imprisoned, and divided his territory into two kingdoms.
entries.literal: In spring of Han year 6, he assembled the feudal lords at Chen, deposed King Chu Xin, imprisoned him, and divided his territory into two kingdoms.

entries.zh: 當是時也，高祖子幼，昆弟少，又不賢，欲王同姓以鎮天下，乃詔曰：「將軍劉賈有功，及擇子弟可以為王者。」
entries.en: At that time, Emperor Gaozu's sons were still young, and his brothers were few and lacked distinction. Wishing to install kings who shared his surname to anchor the realm, he issued an edict: 'General Liu Jia has rendered great service. Let worthy members of the clan be selected and made kings.'
entries.literal: At this time, Gaozu's sons were young, his brothers few, and moreover not worthy; he wished to enfeoff kings of the same surname to stabilize the realm. He issued an edict saying: 'General Liu Jia has merit; let clansmen who can be made kings be selected.'

entries.zh: 群臣皆曰：「立劉賈為荊王，王淮東五十二城；
entries.en: All the ministers said: 'Let Liu Jia be established as King of Jing, to rule over fifty-two cities east of the Huai;
entries.literal: All the ministers said: 'Establish Liu Jia as King of Jing, to rule over fifty-two cities east of the Huai;

entries.zh: 高祖弟交為楚王，王淮西三十六城。」
entries.en: and let Jiao, the emperor's younger brother, be made King of Chu, ruling over thirty-six cities west of the Huai.'
entries.literal: Gaozu's younger brother Jiao as King of Chu, ruling over 36 cities west of the Huai.'

entries.zh: 因立子肥為齊王。
entries.en: He also established his son Fei as the King of Qi.
entries.literal: He then established his son Fei as King of Qi.

entries.zh: 始王昆弟劉氏也。
entries.en: This marked the beginning of enfeoffing members of the Liu clan as kings.
entries.literal: This began the enfeoffment of brothers from the Liu clan.

entries.zh: 高祖十一年秋，淮南王黥布反，東擊荊。
entries.en: In the autumn of the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Ying Bu, the King of Huainan, rose in rebellion and marched east to attack the kingdom of Jing.
entries.literal: In autumn of Gaozu year 11, King Huainan Ying Bu rebelled and marched east to attack Jing.

entries.zh: 荊王賈與戰，不勝，走富陵，為布軍所殺。
entries.en: King Jia of Jing fought against him but could not prevail. He fled to Fuling, where he was slain by Ying Bu's forces.
entries.literal: King Jing Jia fought him but was defeated, fled to Fuling, and was killed by Bu's army.

entries.zh: 高祖自擊破布。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu personally led the campaign that crushed Ying Bu.
entries.literal: Gaozu personally attacked and defeated Bu.

entries.zh: 十二年，立沛侯劉濞為吳王，王故荊地。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, he installed Liu Pi, the Marquis of Pei, as the King of Wu, to rule over the former Jing territory.
entries.literal: In year 12, he established Marquis Pei Liu Pi as King of Wu, ruling over the former Jing territory.

entries.zh: 燕王劉澤者，諸劉遠屬也。
entries.en: Liu Ze, the King of Yan, was a distant kinsman of the Liu clan.
entries.literal: King Yan Liu Ze was a distant relation of the various Liu clansmen.

entries.zh: 高帝三年，澤為郎中。
entries.en: In the third year of Emperor Gao's reign, Liu Ze served as a palace gentleman.
entries.literal: In Gaozu year 3, Ze served as a palace attendant.

entries.zh: 高帝十一年，澤以將軍擊陳豨，得王黃，為營陵侯。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, Liu Ze campaigned as a general against Chen Xi. He captured Wang Huang and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yingling.
entries.literal: In Gaozu year 11, Ze as a general attacked Chen Xi, captured Wang Huang, and was made Marquis of Yingling.

entries.zh: 高后時，齊人田生游乏資，以畫干營陵侯澤。
entries.en: During the reign of Empress Dowager Gao, a man from Qi named Tian Sheng, who had exhausted his travel funds, approached the Marquis of Yingling with his stratagems.
entries.literal: During Empress Gao's time, a man from Qi named Tian Sheng, traveling without funds, sought patronage from Marquis Yingling Ze by offering stratagems.

entries.zh: 澤大說之，用金二百斤為田生壽。
entries.en: Liu Ze was greatly delighted with him and presented Tian Sheng with two hundred jin of gold as a gift.
entries.literal: Ze was greatly pleased with him and gave two hundred jin of gold to Tian Sheng as a gift.

entries.zh: 田生已得金，即歸齊。
entries.en: Once Tian Sheng had the gold in hand, he promptly returned to Qi.
entries.literal: After Tian Sheng received the gold, he immediately returned to Qi.

entries.zh: 二年，澤使人謂田生曰：「弗與矣。」
entries.en: In the second year, Liu Ze sent a messenger to tell Tian Sheng: 'I will not help you anymore.'
entries.literal: Two years later, Ze sent someone to tell Tian Sheng: 'I will not give [any more help].'

entries.zh: 田生如長安，不見澤，而假大宅，令其子求事呂后所幸大謁者張子卿。
entries.en: Tian Sheng traveled to Chang'an but did not call upon Liu Ze. Instead, he rented a grand residence and had his son seek a position under Zhang Ziqing, the Grand Usher who enjoyed the special favor of Empress Lü.
entries.literal: Tian Sheng went to Chang'an but did not see Ze. Instead, he rented a large residence and had his son seek service with Zhang Ziqing, the Grand Usher favored by Empress Lü.

entries.zh: 居數月，田生子請張卿臨，親修具。
entries.en: After several months, Tian Sheng's son invited Zhang Qing to visit, personally preparing an elaborate feast for the occasion.
entries.literal: After several months, Tian Sheng's son invited Zhang Qing to visit, preparing elaborate arrangements personally.

entries.zh: 張卿許往。
entries.en: Zhang Qing accepted the invitation.
entries.literal: Zhang Qing agreed to go.

entries.zh: 田生盛帷帳共具，譬如列侯。
entries.en: Tian Sheng laid out sumptuous curtains and furnishings rivaling those of a marquis's household.
entries.literal: Tian Sheng prepared lavish curtains and furnishings, comparable to those of marquises.

entries.zh: 張卿驚。
entries.en: Zhang Qing was taken aback.
entries.literal: Zhang Qing was astonished.

entries.zh: 酒酣，乃屏人說張卿曰：「臣觀諸侯王邸弟百餘，皆高祖一切功臣。
entries.en: When the wine was flowing freely, Tian Sheng dismissed the attendants and spoke to Zhang Qing in confidence: 'I have observed that more than a hundred youths lodged at the feudal kings' mansions in the capital are all descendants of Emperor Gaozu's meritorious officials.
entries.literal: When the wine flowed freely, Tian Sheng dismissed the attendants and spoke confidentially to Zhang Qing: 'I have observed that more than a hundred youths lodged at the feudal kings' mansions in the capital are all descendants of Emperor Gaozu's meritorious officials.

entries.zh: 今呂氏雅故本推轂高帝就天下，功至大，又親戚太后之重。
entries.en: Now the Lü clan, as old allies, originally helped propel Emperor Gao to conquer the realm. Their merit is immense, and they hold the additional weight of being close kinsmen of the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Now the Lü clan, as old allies, originally helped Gaozu from the outset to win the realm; their merit is extremely great, and moreover they bear the weight of kinship with the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 太后春秋長，諸呂弱，太后欲立呂產為［呂］王，王代。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager is advanced in years, and the Lü are still weak. She wishes to establish Lü Chan as the King of Lü, to rule over Dai.
entries.literal: The empress dowager is advanced in years, the various Lü are weak, the empress dowager wishes to establish Lü Chan as king of Lü, ruling Dai.

entries.zh: 太后又重發之，恐大臣不聽。
entries.en: Yet the Empress Dowager hesitates to raise the matter again, fearing the ministers will refuse.
entries.literal: The empress dowager finds it hard to bring the matter up again, fearing the ministers will not heed it.

entries.zh: 今卿最幸，大臣所敬，何不風大臣以聞太后，太后必喜。
entries.en: You are the most favored at court and respected by the ministers. Why not hint to them to bring this matter before the Empress Dowager? She will certainly be delighted.
entries.literal: Now you are most favored, respected by the ministers—why not sound out the ministers to inform the empress dowager? The empress dowager will certainly be pleased.

entries.zh: 諸呂已王，萬戶侯亦卿之有。
entries.en: Once the Lü clan members are made kings, a marquisate of ten thousand households will be yours as well.
entries.literal: Once the various Lü are kings, a marquisate of ten thousand households will also be yours.

entries.zh: 太后心欲之，而卿為內臣，不急發，恐禍及身矣。」
entries.en: The Empress Dowager desires this in her heart. As an inner minister, if you do not act swiftly, I fear disaster will fall upon you.'
entries.literal: The empress dowager desires this in her heart, and you as an inner minister, if you do not act quickly, disaster may befall you.'

entries.zh: 張卿大然之，乃風大臣語太后。
entries.en: Zhang Qing wholeheartedly agreed and began dropping hints to the ministers, who then spoke to the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Zhang Qing greatly approved and began sounding out the ministers to speak to the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 太后朝，因問大臣。
entries.en: At the next court audience, the Empress Dowager raised the matter with the ministers.
entries.literal: At court, the empress dowager questioned the ministers.

entries.zh: 大臣請立呂產為呂王。
entries.en: The ministers petitioned to establish Lü Chan as the King of Lü.
entries.literal: The ministers requested establishing Lü Chan as King of Lü.

entries.zh: 太后賜張卿千斤金，張卿以其半與田生。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager rewarded Zhang Qing with a thousand jin of gold, and Zhang Qing gave half of it to Tian Sheng.
entries.literal: The empress dowager granted Zhang Qing a thousand jin of gold, and Zhang Qing gave half of it to Tian Sheng.

entries.zh: 田生弗受，因說之曰：「呂產王也，諸大臣未大服。
entries.en: Tian Sheng declined the gift and counseled him: 'Although Lü Chan has been made king, the great ministers are not yet fully won over.
entries.literal: Tian Sheng did not accept it, and instead advised him: 'Lü Chan is now king, but the various ministers are not yet greatly convinced.

entries.zh: 今營陵侯澤，諸劉，為大將軍，獨此尚觖望。
entries.en: At present, the Marquis of Yingling, Liu Ze of the Liu clan, serves as Grand General, and he alone still harbors resentment.
entries.literal: Now Marquis Yingling Ze, of the Liu clan, serves as Grand General, and he alone still harbors resentment.

entries.zh: 今卿言太后，列十餘縣王之，彼得王，喜去，諸呂王益固矣。」
entries.en: If you now speak to the Empress Dowager and have her enfeoff him as king over ten or more counties, he will be delighted and depart the capital, making the Lü kingships all the more secure.'
entries.literal: If you speak to the empress dowager now and have her enfeoff him as king of more than ten counties, he will obtain kingship, leave happily, and the various Lü kingships will be even more secure.'

entries.zh: 張卿入言，太后然之。
entries.en: Zhang Qing entered the palace and presented the proposal. The Empress Dowager approved.
entries.literal: Zhang Qing went in and spoke, and the empress dowager agreed to it.

entries.zh: 乃以營陵侯劉澤為瑯邪王。
entries.en: Accordingly, Liu Ze, the Marquis of Yingling, was made the King of Langya.
entries.literal: Thus, Marquis Yingling Liu Ze was made King of Langye.

entries.zh: 瑯邪王乃與田生之國。
entries.en: The King of Langya then set out for his kingdom, taking Tian Sheng with him.
entries.literal: The King of Langye then went to his kingdom with Tian Sheng.

entries.zh: 田生勸澤急行，毋留。
entries.en: Tian Sheng urged Liu Ze to travel with all haste and make no stops along the way.
entries.literal: Tian Sheng urged Ze to proceed quickly without delay.

entries.zh: 出關，太后果使人追止之，已出，即還。
entries.en: Once they had passed through the frontier passes, the Empress Dowager did indeed send men in pursuit to stop them, but they had already left, and the pursuers returned empty-handed.
entries.literal: They passed through the passes, and the empress dowager indeed sent people to pursue and stop them, but they had already left, so they returned.

entries.zh: 及太后崩，瑯邪王澤乃曰：「帝少，諸呂用事，劉氏孤弱。」
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager died, the King of Langya, Liu Ze, declared: 'The emperor is young. The Lü clan holds power, and the house of Liu is isolated and vulnerable.'
entries.literal: When the empress dowager passed away, King Langye Ze said: 'The emperor is young, the various Lü hold power, the Liu clan is isolated and weak.'

entries.zh: 乃引兵與齊王合謀西，欲誅諸呂。
entries.en: He raised his troops and conspired with the King of Qi to march west, intending to destroy the Lü clan.
entries.literal: He then led troops west in conspiracy with the King of Qi, wishing to execute the various Lü.

entries.zh: 至梁，聞漢遣灌將軍屯滎陽，澤還兵備西界，遂跳驅至長安。
entries.en: When they reached Liang, word came that the Han court had dispatched General Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang. Liu Ze sent his troops back to guard the western frontier and rode hard for Chang'an.
entries.literal: When they reached Liang, hearing that Han had sent General Guan to garrison Xingyang, Ze returned his troops to defend the western border, then galloped swiftly to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 代王亦從代至。
entries.en: The King of Dai had also arrived from his domain.
entries.literal: The King of Dai also arrived from Dai.

entries.zh: 諸將相與瑯邪王共立代王為天子。
entries.en: The generals and ministers, together with the King of Langya, jointly enthroned the King of Dai as the new Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: The generals, together with the King of Langye, jointly established the King of Dai as Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 天子乃徙澤為燕王，乃復以瑯邪予齊，復故地。
entries.en: The new emperor then transferred Liu Ze to become the King of Yan and restored Langya to the kingdom of Qi, returning it to its former territory.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven then moved Ze to become King of Yan, and returned Langye to Qi, restoring the old territory.

entries.zh: 至孫定國，與父康王姬姦，生子男一人。
entries.en: By the time of his grandson Dingguo, the king committed adultery with his father King Kang's concubine and fathered one son.
entries.literal: Down to his grandson Dingguo, who committed adultery with his father King Kang's concubine and fathered one son.

entries.zh: 奪弟妻為姬。
entries.en: He also seized his younger brother's wife and took her as a concubine.
entries.literal: He seized his younger brother's wife as a concubine.

entries.zh: 與子女三人姦。
entries.en: He also committed incest with three of his own daughters.
entries.literal: He committed adultery with three daughters.

entries.zh: 定國有所欲誅殺臣肥如令郢人，郢人等告定國，定國使謁者以他法劾捕格殺郢人以滅口。
entries.en: Dingguo wished to have an official killed—Yingren, the magistrate of Feiru. When Yingren and others reported Dingguo's crimes, Dingguo had the court usher bring trumped-up charges against them, arresting and killing Yingren to silence him.
entries.literal: Dingguo wished to have a minister killed—the magistrate of Feiru, a man from Ying. When the man from Ying and others reported Dingguo, Dingguo had the usher indict and arrest them on other charges, killing the man from Ying to silence them.

entries.zh: 至元朔元年，郢人昆弟復上書具言定國陰事，以此發覺。
entries.en: In the first year of the Yuanshuo era, the brothers of the man from Ying submitted another memorial laying out all of Dingguo's secret crimes, and the matter was at last brought to light.
entries.literal: In Yuanshuo year 1, the man from Ying's brothers submitted another memorial fully detailing Dingguo's secret affairs, and thus it was discovered.

entries.zh: 詔下公卿，皆議曰：「定國禽獸行，亂人倫，逆天，當誅。」
entries.en: The case was referred to the high ministers, who all concluded: 'Dingguo's conduct is that of a beast. He has violated the bonds of human morality and defied the will of Heaven. He deserves execution.'
entries.literal: The edict was issued to the ministers, and all discussed saying: 'Dingguo's conduct is that of beasts, disrupting human relationships, opposing heaven—he should be executed.'

entries.zh: 上許之。
entries.en: The emperor gave his assent.
entries.literal: The emperor approved it.

entries.zh: 定國自殺，國除為郡。
entries.en: Dingguo took his own life, and the kingdom was abolished and converted into a commandery.
entries.literal: Dingguo committed suicide, and the state was abolished to become a commandery.

entries.zh: 漢聞齊發兵而西，相國呂產乃遣大將軍灌嬰東擊之。
entries.en: When word reached the Han court that Qi had raised an army and was marching west, the Chancellor Lü Chan dispatched the Grand General Guan Ying eastward to intercept them.
entries.literal: Han heard that Qi had raised troops and gone west, so Chancellor Lü Chan sent Grand General Guan Ying east to attack them.

entries.zh: 灌嬰至滎陽，乃謀曰：「諸呂將兵居關中，欲危劉氏而自立。
entries.en: When Guan Ying reached Xingyang, he deliberated: 'The Lü clan has massed troops within the passes, intent on overthrowing the Liu house and seizing the throne for themselves.
entries.literal: Guan Ying reached Xingyang and plotted saying: 'The various Lü command troops and reside in Guanzhong, wishing to endanger the Liu clan and establish themselves.

entries.zh: 我今破齊還報，是益呂氏資也。」
entries.en: If I crush Qi and return victorious, I will only be adding to the Lü clan's strength.'
entries.literal: If I now defeat Qi and return to report, this will increase the Lü clan's resources.'

entries.zh: 乃留兵屯滎陽，使使喻齊王及諸侯，與連和，以待呂氏之變而共誅之。
entries.en: He therefore kept his army at Xingyang and sent envoys to the King of Qi and the other feudal lords, forming an alliance to wait for the Lü clan to make their move and then strike them down together.
entries.literal: He stationed troops at Xingyang and sent envoys to explain to the King of Qi and the various feudal lords, allying with them to await the Lü clan's rebellion and jointly execute them.

entries.zh: 齊王聞之，乃西取其故濟南郡，亦屯兵於齊西界以待約。
entries.en: When the King of Qi learned of this, he seized his former territory of Jinan Commandery to the west and stationed troops along Qi's western frontier to await the agreed-upon signal.
entries.literal: The King of Qi heard this and took back his former Jinan commandery to the west, also stationing troops on Qi's western border to await the agreement.

entries.zh: 灌嬰在滎陽，聞魏勃本教齊王反，既誅呂氏，罷齊兵，使使召責問魏勃。
entries.en: Guan Ying, still at Xingyang, learned that it was Wei Bo who had originally urged the King of Qi to rebel. Now that the Lü clan had been destroyed and Qi's army disbanded, he summoned Wei Bo to answer for his actions.
entries.literal: Guan Ying was at Xingyang. Hearing that Wei Bo had originally instructed the King of Qi to rebel, and now that the Lü clan had been executed and Qi troops disbanded, he sent envoys to summon and question Wei Bo.

entries.zh: 勃曰：「失火之家，豈暇先言大人而後救火乎！」
entries.en: Wei Bo replied, "When a house is on fire, can one afford to inform the elders before putting out the flames?"
entries.literal: Bo said, "In a house where fire has broken out, how can one have time to inform the elders before putting out the fire!"

entries.zh: 因退立，股戰而栗，恐不能言者，終無他語。
entries.en: Then he stepped back, his legs shaking with fear, as though he could not utter another word, and indeed he said nothing more.
entries.literal: He stepped back and stood there, his legs trembling and shivering as if he could not speak, and in the end said nothing else.

entries.zh: 灌將軍熟視笑曰：「人謂魏勃勇，妄庸人耳，何能為乎！」
entries.en: General Guan studied him closely and laughed. 'People call Wei Bo brave, but he is nothing but a cowardly fool. What could he possibly accomplish?'
entries.literal: General Guan stared at him intently and laughed: 'People say Wei Bo is brave, but he's just a cowardly mediocrity—what can he accomplish!'

entries.zh: 乃罷魏勃。
entries.en: And so he let Wei Bo go.
entries.literal: Thus, he dismissed Wei Bo.

entries.zh: 魏勃父以善鼓琴見秦皇帝。
entries.en: Wei Bo's father had once been granted an audience with the First Emperor of Qin on account of his skill at playing the zither.
entries.literal: Wei Bo's father was skilled at playing the zither and was received by the Qin emperor.

entries.zh: 及魏勃少時，欲求見齊相曹參，家貧無以自通，乃常獨早夜埽齊相舍人門外。
entries.en: In his youth, Wei Bo wished to gain an audience with Cao Shen, the chancellor of Qi, but his family was too poor for him to arrange an introduction. So each day, from dawn to dusk, he swept the ground outside the door of the chancellor's steward.
entries.literal: When Wei Bo was young, he wished to seek an audience with Qi Chancellor Cao Shen. Being poor with no means to gain access, he often alone swept the doorway of the chancellor's retainers from early morning to night.

entries.zh: 相舍人怪之，以為物，而伺之，得勃。
entries.en: The steward found this peculiar and, suspecting it was the work of some spirit, kept watch and discovered it was Wei Bo.
entries.literal: The chancellor's retainers found it strange, thinking it some sort of spirit, and spied on it, discovering Bo.

entries.zh: 勃曰：「願見相君，無因，故為子埽，欲以求見。」
entries.en: Wei Bo said, 'I wish to see the chancellor, but I have no way to gain an introduction. That is why I have been sweeping your doorstep—in hopes of earning an audience.'
entries.literal: Bo said: 'I wish to see the chancellor. Having no connections, I sweep for you in order to seek an audience.'

entries.zh: 於是舍人見勃曹參，因以為舍人。
entries.en: The steward then brought Wei Bo before Cao Shen, who took him on as a retainer.
entries.literal: Thus, the retainers introduced Bo to Cao Shen, who made him a retainer.

entries.zh: 一為參御，言事，參以為賢，言之齊悼惠王。
entries.en: On one occasion, while serving as Cao Shen's charioteer, Wei Bo discussed affairs of state, and Cao Shen, impressed by his ability, recommended him to King Daohui of Qi.
entries.literal: Once while serving Cao Shen and discussing affairs, Shen considered him worthy and spoke of him to King Daohui of Qi.

entries.zh: 悼惠王召見，則拜為內史。
entries.en: King Daohui summoned him for an audience and promptly appointed him interior minister.
entries.literal: King Daohui summoned and saw him, then appointed him interior minister.

entries.zh: 始，悼惠王得自置二千石。
entries.en: Originally, King Daohui had been granted the privilege of appointing his own officials ranked at two thousand shi.
entries.literal: At first, King Daohui was permitted to appoint officials of 2000 shi stipend himself.

entries.zh: 及悼惠王卒而哀王立，勃用事，重於齊相。
entries.en: After King Daohui died and King Ai succeeded him, Wei Bo took charge of affairs and wielded more influence than the chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: When King Daohui died and King Ai ascended, Bo took charge of affairs and was more important than the Qi chancellor.

entries.zh: 齊孝王十一年，吳王濞、楚王戊反，興兵西，告諸侯曰「將誅漢賊臣晁錯以安宗廟」。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of King Xiao of Qi, King Pi of Wu and King Wu of Chu rose in rebellion, marching their armies westward and declaring to the feudal lords: 'We shall execute the traitorous Han minister Chao Cuo to safeguard the ancestral temples.'
entries.literal: In King Xiao of Qi's eleventh year, King Pi of Wu and King Wu of Chu rebelled, raised troops west, and informed the feudal lords saying 'We will execute Han's traitorous minister Chao Cuo to pacify the ancestral temples.'

entries.zh: 膠西、膠東、菑川、濟南皆擅發兵應吳楚。
entries.en: The kingdoms of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Zichuan, and Jinan all raised troops on their own authority to join Wu and Chu.
entries.literal: Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Zichuan, and Jinan all arbitrarily raised troops to respond to Wu and Chu.

entries.zh: 欲與齊，齊孝王狐疑，城守不聽，三國兵共圍齊。
entries.en: They wished Qi to join them, but King Xiao of Qi hesitated, fortified his cities, and refused. The armies of the three kingdoms then laid siege to Qi.
entries.literal: They wished to join with Qi, but King Xiao of Qi was doubtful, defended his cities and would not listen. The troops of the three states jointly besieged Qi.

entries.zh: 齊王使路中大夫告於天子。
entries.en: The King of Qi sent Palace Grandee Lu to carry word to the Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: The King of Qi sent Palace Grandee Lu to report to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 天子復令路中大夫還告齊王：「善堅守，吾兵今破吳楚矣。」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven instructed Palace Grandee Lu to return to Qi with this message: 'Hold fast in your defense. My armies have now defeated Wu and Chu.'
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven commanded Palace Grandee Lu to return and inform the King of Qi: 'Hold firm in your defense. My troops have now defeated Wu and Chu.'

entries.zh: 路中大夫至，三國兵圍臨菑數重，無從入。
entries.en: When Palace Grandee Lu arrived, the armies of the three kingdoms had encircled Linzi in layer upon layer, and there was no way to enter the city.
entries.literal: Palace Grandee Lu arrived, but the three states' troops surrounded Linzi in multiple layers, and there was no way to enter.

entries.zh: 三國將劫與路中大夫盟，曰：「若反言漢已破矣，齊趣下三國，不且見屠。」
entries.en: The generals of the three kingdoms seized Palace Grandee Lu and forced him to swear an oath, saying, "When you return, say that Han has already been defeated and that Qi should quickly surrender to the three kingdoms. If you do not, you will be killed."
entries.literal: The generals of the three states seized Palace Grandee Lu and forced him to swear an oath, saying, "When you return, say that Han has already been defeated and that Qi should quickly surrender to the three states. If you do not, you will be killed."

entries.zh: 路中大夫既許之，至城下，望見齊王，曰：「漢已發兵百萬，使太尉周亞夫擊破吳楚，方引兵救齊，齊必堅守無下！」
entries.en: Palace Grandee Lu agreed to their terms, but when he reached the city walls and caught sight of the King of Qi, he cried out: 'Han has raised a million troops and sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu to crush Wu and Chu. The imperial army is on its way to relieve Qi. You must hold fast and never surrender!'
entries.literal: Palace Grandee Lu agreed to their terms, but when he reached the city walls and caught sight of the King of Qi, he said: 'Han has already raised a million troops and sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu to defeat Wu and Chu. They are now leading troops to rescue Qi. Qi must hold firm and not surrender!'

entries.zh: 三國將誅路中大夫。
entries.en: The generals of the three kingdoms put Palace Grandee Lu to death.
entries.literal: The generals of the three states executed Palace Grandee Lu.

entries.zh: 主父偃方幸於天子，用事，因言：「齊臨菑十萬戶，市租千金，人眾殷富，巨於長安，此非天子親弟愛子不得王此。
entries.en: Zhu Fu Yan, who at that time enjoyed the Son of Heaven's favor and wielded great influence, remarked: 'Linzi in Qi has a hundred thousand households. Its market revenues amount to a thousand jin. Its population is vast and its wealth surpasses that of Chang'an itself. No one but the Son of Heaven's own brother or beloved son should be allowed to rule such a place.
entries.literal: Zhu Fu Yan was currently favored by the Son of Heaven and held power. He thus spoke: 'Qi's Linzi has a hundred thousand households, market rents of a thousand jin, the people are numerous and wealthy, greater than Chang'an. This is not a place for anyone but the Son of Heaven's own younger brother or beloved son to rule.

entries.zh: 今齊王於親屬益疏。」
entries.en: Yet the present King of Qi grows ever more remote in kinship from the throne.'
entries.literal: Now the King of Qi is increasingly distant in kinship.'

entries.zh: 乃從容言：「呂太后時齊欲反，吳楚時孝王幾為亂。
entries.en: He then added casually, 'During the time of Empress Dowager Lü, Qi tried to revolt. During the rebellion of Wu and Chu, King Xiao very nearly joined the insurgents.
entries.literal: He then leisurely spoke: 'During Empress Lü's time Qi wished to rebel. During the Wu and Chu time King Xiao nearly caused chaos.

entries.zh: 今聞齊王與其姊亂。」
entries.en: And now I hear the King of Qi is carrying on an incestuous affair with his own sister.'
entries.literal: Now I hear the King of Qi is committing incest with his sister.'

entries.zh: 於是天子乃拜主父偃為齊相，且正其事。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven thereupon appointed Zhu Fu Yan as chancellor of Qi to investigate the matter and bring it to justice.
entries.literal: Thus, the Son of Heaven appointed Zhu Fu Yan as Qi chancellor, and moreover to investigate this matter.

entries.zh: 主父偃既至齊，乃急治王後宮宦者為王通於姊翁主所者，令其辭證皆引王。
entries.en: Upon arriving in Qi, Zhu Fu Yan swiftly interrogated the eunuchs of the inner palace who had facilitated the King's liaisons with his sister, the Princess, compelling all their testimony and evidence to implicate the King.
entries.literal: Zhu Fu Yan having arrived in Qi, urgently interrogated the eunuchs in the king's rear palace who arranged the king's liaisons with his sister Princess Ji, commanding their testimonies and evidence to all implicate the king.

entries.zh: 王年少，懼大罪為吏所執誅，乃飲藥自殺。
entries.en: The King was young and terrified that the gravity of his crime would lead to his arrest and execution. He drank poison and took his own life.
entries.literal: The king was young and feared the great crime would lead to his arrest and execution by the officials, so he took poison and committed suicide.

entries.zh: 絕無後。
entries.en: His line was extinguished, leaving no heir.
entries.literal: The line was extinguished without descendants.

entries.zh: 是時趙王懼主父偃一出廢齊，恐其漸疏骨肉，乃上書言偃受金及輕重之短。
entries.en: At this time, the King of Zhao, alarmed that Zhu Fu Yan had engineered the downfall of Qi and might gradually turn the throne against the rest of the imperial family, submitted a memorial accusing Yan of accepting bribes and abusing his authority.
entries.literal: At this time the King of Zhao feared that Zhu Fu Yan, having once deposed Qi, would gradually alienate the royal kin. He submitted a memorial speaking of Yan's receiving gold and his faults of weighing lightly and heavily.

entries.zh: 天子亦既囚偃。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven had Zhu Fu Yan imprisoned.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven also imprisoned Yan.

entries.zh: 公孫弘言：「齊王以憂死毋後，國入漢，非誅偃無以塞天下之望。」
entries.en: Gongsun Hong declared, 'The King of Qi died in anguish, leaving no heir, and his kingdom has reverted to the Han. Unless Zhu Fu Yan is put to death, the expectations of the realm will not be satisfied.'
entries.literal: Gongsun Hong spoke: 'The King of Qi died of sorrow without descendants, the state reverted to Han. Not executing Yan will not satisfy the realm's expectations.'

entries.zh: 遂誅偃。
entries.en: And so Zhu Fu Yan was executed.
entries.literal: Thus, Yan was executed.

entries.zh: 齊悼惠王後尚有二國，城陽及菑川。
entries.en: Among the descendants of King Daohui of Qi, two kingdoms still survived: Chengyang and Zichuan.
entries.literal: King Daohui of Qi's descendants still had two states: Chengyang and Zichuan.

entries.zh: 菑川地比齊。
entries.en: Zichuan's territory lay adjacent to Qi.
entries.literal: Zichuan territory bordered Qi.

entries.zh: 天子憐齊，為悼惠王冢園在郡，割臨菑東環悼惠王冢園邑盡以予菑川，以奉悼惠王祭祀。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven took pity on Qi. Since King Daohui's tomb and park lay within the commandery, he carved out all the settlements east of Linzi that encircled the tomb and granted them to Zichuan, so that the sacrifices to King Daohui might continue.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven pitied Qi and, because King Daohui's tomb and garden were in the commandery, carved out the settlements east of Linzi encircling King Daohui's tomb and garden and gave them all to Zichuan to maintain King Daohui's sacrifices.

entries.zh: 頃王二十（八）［六］年卒，子義立，是為敬王。
entries.en: King Qing reigned for twenty-six years and died. His son Yi succeeded him and became King Jing.
entries.literal: King Qing reigned for twenty-six years and died. His son Yi ascended the throne, becoming King Jing.

entries.zh: 敬王九年卒，子武立，是為惠王。
entries.en: King Jing reigned for nine years and died. His son Wu succeeded him and became King Hui.
entries.literal: King Jing reigned for nine years and died. His son Wu ascended the throne, becoming King Hui.

entries.zh: 惠王十一年卒，子順立，是為荒王。
entries.en: King Hui reigned for eleven years and died. His son Shun succeeded him and became King Huang.
entries.literal: King Hui reigned for eleven years and died. His son Shun ascended the throne, becoming King Huang.

entries.zh: 荒王四十六年卒，子恢立，是為戴王。
entries.en: King Huang reigned for forty-six years and died. His son Hui succeeded him and became King Dai.
entries.literal: King Huang reigned for forty-six years and died. His son Hui ascended the throne, becoming King Dai.

entries.zh: 戴王八年卒，子景立，至建始三年，十五歲，卒。
entries.en: King Dai reigned for eight years and died. His son Jing succeeded him and died in the third year of the Jianshi era, at the age of fifteen.
entries.literal: King Dai reigned for eight years and died. His son Jing ascended the throne. In the third year of Jianshi, at fifteen years of age, he died.

entries.zh: 孝文帝二年，以齊之濟北郡立興居為濟北王，與城陽王俱立。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Wen's reign, Qi's Jibei Commandery was used to establish Xingju as King of Jibei, at the same time as the King of Chengyang was installed.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wen's second year, he used Qi's Jibei commandery to establish Xingju as King of Jibei, standing together with the King of Chengyang.

entries.zh: 立二年，反。
entries.en: After two years on the throne, he rebelled.
entries.literal: He reigned for two years and rebelled.

entries.zh: 始大臣誅呂氏時，朱虛侯功尤大，許盡以趙地王朱虛侯，盡以梁地王東牟侯。
entries.en: When the ministers first destroyed the Lü clan, the Marquis of Zhuxu's contribution had been the greatest. He was promised all of Zhao as his kingdom, while the Marquis of Dongmou was promised all of Liang.
entries.literal: At first when the ministers executed the Lü clan, Marquis Zhuxu's merit was especially great. It was promised to enfeoff Marquis Zhuxu with all Zhao territory, and to enfeoff Marquis Dongmu with all Liang territory.

entries.zh: 及孝文帝立，聞朱虛、東牟之初欲立齊王，故絀其功。
entries.en: But when Emperor Wen came to the throne, he learned that Zhuxu and Dongmou had initially wanted to make the King of Qi emperor, and so he downgraded their achievements.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended, he heard that Zhuxu and Dongmu had initially wished to establish the King of Qi, so he diminished their merit.

entries.zh: 及二年，王諸子，乃割齊二郡以王章、興居。
entries.en: In the second year, when the emperor enfeoffed the princes, he carved out only two commanderies from Qi to grant kingdoms to Zhang and Xingju.
entries.literal: By the second year when he enfeoffed the various sons, he carved out two Qi commanderies to enfeoff Zhang and Xingju.

entries.zh: 章、興居自以失職奪功。
entries.en: Zhang and Xingju felt they had been cheated of the positions and rewards they deserved.
entries.literal: Zhang and Xingju considered themselves to have lost their positions and had their merit stolen.

entries.zh: 章死，而興居聞匈奴大入漢，漢多發兵，使丞相灌嬰擊之，文帝親幸太原，以為天子自擊胡，遂發兵反於濟北。
entries.en: Zhang died, but Xingju heard that the Xiongnu had launched a massive invasion and that Han had mobilized a great army, dispatching Chancellor Guan Ying to repel them while Emperor Wen himself traveled to Taiyuan. Judging that the Son of Heaven was personally occupied with the Hu campaign, Xingju raised his troops and revolted in Jibei.
entries.literal: Zhang died, but Xingju heard that the Xiongnu had greatly invaded Han, and Han had raised many troops, sending Chancellor Guan Ying to attack them. Emperor Wen personally went to Taiyuan, considering that the Son of Heaven himself was attacking the Hu, so Xingju raised troops and rebelled in Jibei.

entries.zh: 天子聞之，罷丞相及行兵，皆歸長安。
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven learned of this, he recalled the chancellor and the expeditionary forces, all of whom returned to Chang'an.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven heard of this and dismissed the chancellor and the expeditionary troops, all returning to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 使棘蒲侯柴將軍擊破虜濟北王，王自殺，地入于漢，為郡。
