entries.en: He dispatched General Chai, the Marquis of Jipu, who defeated and captured the King of Jibei. The King took his own life, and his territory reverted to the Han as a commandery.
entries.literal: He sent General Chai, the Marquis of Jipu, who defeated and captured the King of Jibei. The king committed suicide, and the territory reverted to Han as a commandery.

entries.zh: 齊悼惠王劉肥者，高祖長庶男也。
entries.en: Liu Fei, King Daohui of Qi, was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu, born to a concubine.
entries.literal: King Daohui of Qi, Liu Fei, was Gaozu's eldest son by a concubine.

entries.zh: 其母外婦也，曰曹氏。
entries.en: His mother was a woman of the Cao clan who had been Emperor Gaozu's mistress.
entries.literal: His mother was an outside mistress (wai fu), of the Cao clan.

entries.zh: 高祖六年，立肥為齊王，食七十城，諸民能齊言者皆予齊王。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Gaozu's reign, Fei was made King of Qi, with seventy cities under his domain, and all the people who spoke the Qi dialect were placed under his rule.
entries.literal: In Gaozu year 6, he established Fei as King of Qi, ruling over seventy cities, and all people who could speak the Qi dialect were given to the King of Qi.

entries.zh: 高祖為布衣時，何數以吏事護高祖。
entries.en: Back when Gaozu was still a commoner, Xiao He often used his official position to shield him from trouble.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was a commoner, He frequently used his official duties to protect Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖為亭長，常左右之。
entries.en: After Gaozu became a village headman, Xiao He was always at his side to help.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became pavilion chief, He constantly assisted him.

entries.zh: 高祖以吏繇咸陽，吏皆送奉錢三，何獨以五。
entries.en: When Gaozu was conscripted for labor service in Xianyang, every other official gave him three cash as a parting gift, but Xiao He alone gave five.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was drafted as an official to Xianyang, all the officials presented three coins for the farewell feast, but He alone presented five.

entries.zh: 及高祖起為沛公，何常為丞督事。
entries.en: When Gaozu rose in rebellion and became the Lord of Pei, Xiao He served as his deputy and managed all administrative affairs.
entries.literal: When Gaozu rose up to become Lord of Pei, He constantly served as deputy and oversaw affairs.

entries.zh: 沛公至咸陽，諸將皆爭走金帛財物之府分之，何獨先入收秦丞相御史律令圖書藏之。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei entered Xianyang, all the other generals raced to the treasuries to divide the gold, silk, and valuables among themselves. Xiao He alone went first to secure the Qin chancellor's and imperial censor's collections of laws, decrees, maps, and registers.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Pei reached Xianyang, all the generals rushed to the treasuries of gold, silk, and valuables to divide them up, but He alone first entered and collected the Qin chancellor's and imperial secretary's statutes, orders, maps, and books to store them away.

entries.zh: 沛公為漢王，以何為丞相。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei was named King of Han, he appointed Xiao He as his chancellor.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Pei became Han King, he made He chancellor.

entries.zh: 項王與諸侯屠燒咸陽而去。
entries.en: Xiang Yu and the other lords sacked and burned Xianyang before departing.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu and the feudal lords massacred and burned Xianyang and left.

entries.zh: 漢王所以具知天下阸塞，戶口多少，彊弱之處，民所疾苦者，以何具得秦圖書也。
entries.en: Because Xiao He had secured the complete Qin archives, the King of Han came to know precisely where every strategic pass lay and how many households and people lived in each region. He also knew which areas were strong or weak, and what grievances the people bore.
entries.literal: The reason the Han King fully knew the strategic passes of the realm, the number of households and population, the strong and weak places, and what the people suffered from was because He had obtained all the Qin maps and books.

entries.zh: 何進言韓信，漢王以信為大將軍。
entries.en: Xiao He recommended Han Xin, and the King of Han appointed him as supreme general.
entries.literal: He recommended Han Xin, and the Han King made Xin grand general.

entries.zh: 語在淮陰侯事中。
entries.en: The details of this are recorded in the account of the Marquis of Huaiyin.
entries.literal: The words are in the affairs of Marquis Huaiyin.

entries.zh: 漢五年，既殺項羽，定天下，論功行封。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Han, after Xiang Yu had been slain and the realm pacified, the court debated each man's merits and awarded fiefs accordingly.
entries.literal: In Han year 5, after killing Xiang Yu and pacifying the realm, they discussed merits and bestowed enfeoffments.

entries.zh: 群臣爭功，歲餘功不決。
entries.en: The ministers quarreled over who deserved the most credit, and for more than a year no verdict was reached.
entries.literal: The ministers disputed over merits, and for more than a year the merits were not decided.

entries.zh: 高祖以蕭何功最盛，封為酂侯，所食邑多。
entries.en: Gaozu judged Xiao He's contributions the greatest and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zan, granting him the largest fief of all.
entries.literal: Gaozu considered Xiao He's merit the greatest, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Cuo, with many fief households.

entries.zh: 功臣皆曰：「臣等身被堅執銳，多者百餘戰，少者數十合，攻城略地，大小镑有差。
entries.en: The other ministers with war records protested, 'We have donned armor and taken up arms, fighting over a hundred battles at most and several dozen at least, storming cities and seizing territory, each with his own record of distinction.
entries.literal: All the meritorious ministers said: 'We have worn armor and wielded sharp weapons, the many fought over a hundred battles, the few fought several dozen engagements, attacking cities and seizing territory, with distinctions between large and small contributions.

entries.zh: 今蕭何未嘗有汗馬之勞，徒持文墨議論，不戰，顧反居臣等上，何也？」
entries.en: Yet Xiao He has never once broken a sweat on horseback. All he did was wield a writing brush and talk. He never fought, and yet he is ranked above every one of us. How can this be?'
entries.literal: Now Xiao He has never had the labor of sweating horses, merely holding brush and ink to discuss affairs, not fighting, yet instead he ranks above us all—why is this?'

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「諸君知獵乎？」
entries.en: The Emperor said, 'Do you gentlemen know anything about hunting?'
entries.literal: Gaozu said: 'Do you gentlemen know hunting?'

entries.zh: 曰：「知之。」
entries.en: They replied, 'We do.'
entries.literal: They said, 'We know it.'

entries.zh: 「知獵狗乎？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, 'Do you know about hunting dogs?'
entries.literal: The emperor said, 'Do you know hunting dogs?'

entries.zh: 曰：「知之。」
entries.en: They replied, 'We do.'
entries.literal: They said, 'We know it.'

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「夫獵，追殺獸兔者狗也，而發蹤指示獸處者人也。
entries.en: The Emperor said, 'In a hunt, the ones who chase down and kill the game are the dogs, but the one who picks up the trail and directs the dogs to the quarry is the hunter.
entries.literal: Gaozu said: 'In hunting, those who pursue and kill beasts and rabbits are dogs, while those who discern tracks and point out where the beasts are are humans.

entries.zh: 今諸君徒能得走獸耳，功狗也。
entries.en: Now, you gentlemen can only run down the game. Your merit is that of the dogs.
entries.literal: Now you gentlemen can only catch fleeing beasts—your merit is that of dogs.

entries.zh: 至如蕭何，發蹤指示，功人也。
entries.en: But Xiao He picked up the trail and pointed the way. His merit is that of the hunter.
entries.literal: As for Xiao He, he discerns tracks and points them out—his merit is that of a human.

entries.zh: 且諸君獨以身隨我，多者兩三人。
entries.en: Furthermore, each of you followed me with at most two or three of your kin.
entries.literal: Moreover, you gentlemen followed me with only your own persons, at most two or three people.

entries.zh: 今蕭何舉宗數十人皆隨我，功不可忘也。」
entries.en: Xiao He brought his entire clan of several dozen people to follow me. That kind of merit must not be forgotten.'
entries.literal: Now Xiao He raised his entire clan of several dozen people to all follow me—his merit cannot be forgotten.'

entries.zh: 群臣皆莫敢言。
entries.en: None of the ministers dared say another word.
entries.literal: All the ministers dared not speak further.

entries.zh: 列侯畢已受封，及奏位次，皆曰：「平陽侯曹參身被七十創，攻城略地，功最多，宜第一。」
entries.en: After all the marquises had received their fiefs, the question of precedence arose. They all declared, 'The Marquis of Pingyang, Cao Shen, bore seventy wounds on his body, storming cities and seizing territory. His merit is the greatest; he should rank first.'
entries.literal: The marquises had all received their enfeoffments, and when they memorialized about positions in order, all said: 'Marquis Pingyang Cao Shen suffered seventy wounds on his body, attacking cities and seizing territory—his merit is the greatest, he should be first.'

entries.zh: 上已橈功臣，多封蕭何，至位次未有以復難之，然心欲何第一。
entries.en: The emperor had already overruled the ministers once by granting the largest fief to Xiao He. On the matter of precedence, he had no ready argument to counter them, yet in his heart he wanted Xiao He to be first.
entries.literal: The emperor had already thwarted the meritorious ministers by greatly enfeoffing Xiao He, but regarding positions in order, there was nothing to challenge it again, yet in his heart he wished He to be first.

entries.zh: 關內侯鄂君進曰：「群臣議皆誤。
entries.en: E Jun, who held the rank of Marquis within the Passes, stepped forward and said, 'The ministers are all wrong.
entries.literal: Marquis within the Pass E Jun advanced and said: 'The ministers' discussion is all mistaken.

entries.zh: 夫曹參雖有野戰略地之功，此特一時之事。
entries.en: Cao Shen may have the merit of campaigning in the field and seizing territory, but these are achievements of the moment.
entries.literal: Although Cao Shen has merit in attacking cities and seizing territory in the field, this is merely the matter of a single time.

entries.zh: 夫上與楚相距五歲，常失軍亡眾，逃身遁者數矣。
entries.en: The emperor confronted Chu for five years, repeatedly losing his army and his men, and fled for his life on more than one occasion.
entries.literal: The emperor confronted Chu for five years, frequently losing troops and men, escaping and fleeing several times.

entries.zh: 然蕭何常從關中遣軍補其處，非上所詔令召，而數萬眾會上之乏絕者數矣。
entries.en: Yet Xiao He kept dispatching troops from within the passes to fill the gaps, without any edict or summons from the emperor, and on several occasions sent tens of thousands of reinforcements to relieve the emperor's desperate shortages.
entries.literal: Yet Xiao He constantly sent troops from Guanzhong to fill the gaps, not by the emperor's edict or summons, and tens of thousands gathered to supply the emperor's shortages several times.

entries.zh: 夫漢與楚相守滎陽數年，軍無見糧，蕭何轉漕關中，給食不乏。
entries.en: When Han and Chu were locked in a standoff at Xingyang for years and the army had no grain in sight, it was Xiao He who shipped provisions from within the passes, ensuring the troops never went hungry.
entries.literal: Han and Chu confronted each other at Xingyang for several years, the army had no visible grain, but Xiao He transported grain from Guanzhong, supplying food without shortage.

entries.zh: 陛下雖數亡山東，蕭何常全關中以待陛下，此萬世之功也。
entries.en: Though Your Majesty lost the lands east of the mountains time and again, Xiao He always kept the heartland within the passes intact, waiting for Your Majesty's return. This is a merit that will endure for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: Though Your Majesty frequently lost Shandong, Xiao He constantly preserved Guanzhong to await Your Majesty—this is merit for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 今雖亡曹參等百數，何缺於漢？
entries.en: Even if we had lost a hundred men like Cao Shen, what real harm would it have done to Han?
entries.literal: Now even if we lacked a hundred Cao Shens and the like, what would Han lack?

entries.zh: 漢得之不必待以全。
entries.en: The survival of Han did not depend on having every last one of them.
entries.literal: Han obtaining it does not necessarily depend on them for completeness.

entries.zh: 柰何欲以一旦之功而加萬世之功哉！
entries.en: How can you place the merit of a single day above merit for ten thousand generations!
entries.literal: How can one wish to place the merit of a single day above the merit of ten thousand generations!

entries.zh: 蕭何第一，曹參次之。」
entries.en: Xiao He should rank first, and Cao Shen second.'
entries.literal: Xiao He first, Cao Shen second.'

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「善。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, 'Well spoken.'
entries.literal: Gaozu said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 於是乃令蕭何，賜帶劍履上殿，入朝不趨。
entries.en: He thereupon ordered Xiao He and granted him the privilege of wearing his sword and shoes into the audience hall and of walking at his own pace when entering court.
entries.literal: Thus, he commanded Xiao He, granting him the right to wear sword and shoes on the hall, and not to hasten when entering court.

entries.zh: 漢十一年，陳豨反，高祖自將，至邯鄲。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Han, Chen Xi rose in rebellion. Gaozu personally led the campaign and marched to Handan.
entries.literal: In Han year 11, Chen Xi rebelled. Gaozu personally led troops and arrived at Handan.

entries.zh: 未罷，淮陰侯謀反關中，呂后用蕭何計，誅淮陰侯，語在淮陰事中。
entries.en: Before the campaign was over, the Marquis of Huaiyin plotted rebellion within the passes. Empress Lu used a stratagem devised by Xiao He to have the marquis executed. The details are recorded in the account of the Marquis of Huaiyin.
entries.literal: Before the campaign had ended, the Marquis of Huaiyin plotted rebellion within the passes. Empress Lü used Xiao He's plan to execute the Marquis of Huaiyin. The account is in the affairs of Huaiyin.

entries.zh: 上已聞淮陰侯誅，使使拜丞相何為相國，益封五千戶，令卒五百人一都尉為相國衛。
entries.en: When the emperor learned of the Marquis of Huaiyin's execution, he sent a messenger to promote Chancellor He to the title of Prime Minister, increased his fief by five thousand households, and assigned five hundred soldiers under a commandant as the Prime Minister's personal guard.
entries.literal: The emperor had already heard of Marquis Huaiyin's execution and sent an envoy to appoint Chancellor He as Prime Minister, increasing his enfeoffment by five thousand households, and commanding five hundred soldiers and one Commandant to guard the Prime Minister.

entries.zh: 諸君皆賀，召平獨弔。
entries.en: Everyone offered congratulations, but Shao Ping alone came to offer condolences.
entries.literal: All the ministers congratulated him, but Zhao Ping alone offered condolences.

entries.zh: 召平者，故秦東陵侯。
entries.en: Shao Ping had been the Marquis of Dongling under the Qin dynasty.
entries.literal: Zhao Ping was formerly the Qin Marquis of Dongling.

entries.zh: 秦破，為布衣，貧，種瓜於長安城東，瓜美，故世俗謂之「東陵瓜」，從召平以為名也。
entries.en: After Qin fell, he became a poor commoner and grew melons east of Chang'an. The melons were so fine that people called them 'Dongling melons' after his former title.
entries.literal: After Qin was destroyed, he became a commoner, poor, and grew melons east of Chang'an city. The melons were delicious, so the world called them 'Dongling melons,' taking the name from Zhao Ping.

entries.zh: 召平謂相國曰：「禍自此始矣。
entries.en: Shao Ping said to the Prime Minister, 'This is where your troubles begin.
entries.literal: Zhao Ping told the Prime Minister: 'Disaster begins from this.

entries.zh: 上暴露於外而君守於中，非被矢石之事而益君封置衛者，以今者淮陰侯新反於中，疑君心矣。
entries.en: The emperor is enduring hardship in the field while you guard the capital. You have faced no arrows or stones, yet he increases your fief and stations guards around you. The Marquis of Huaiyin just rebelled from within the capital—the emperor now suspects your loyalty.
entries.literal: The emperor is exposed abroad while you guard within. Though not suffering arrow and stone affairs, yet increasing your enfeoffment and placing guards for you—because recently Marquis Huaiyin rebelled within, he doubts your heart.

entries.zh: 夫置衛衛君，非以寵君也。
entries.en: The guards posted around you are not a mark of favor; they are there to watch you.
entries.literal: Placing guards to guard you is not to favor you.

entries.zh: 願君讓封勿受，悉以家私財佐軍，則上心說。」
entries.en: I urge you to decline the new fief and instead donate your entire personal fortune to support the army. Only then will the emperor's mind be set at ease.'
entries.literal: I wish you to decline the enfeoffment and not accept it, using all your private family wealth to assist the army, then the emperor's heart will be pleased.'

entries.zh: 相國從其計，高帝乃大喜。
entries.en: The Prime Minister followed this advice, and Gaozu was overjoyed.
entries.literal: The Prime Minister followed his plan, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 上罷布軍歸，民道遮行上書，言相國賤彊買民田宅數千萬。
entries.en: When the emperor returned from defeating Ying Bu, people along the road blocked his procession to present petitions, accusing the Prime Minister of using his power to buy up their fields and houses at low prices, spending tens of millions in all.
entries.literal: The emperor disbanded the Bu army and returned. People along the road intercepted him to submit memorials, saying the Prime Minister forcibly bought people's fields and houses cheaply for tens of millions.

entries.zh: 上至，相國謁。
entries.en: When the emperor reached the capital, the Prime Minister came to present himself at court.
entries.literal: When the emperor arrived, the Prime Minister made his audience.

entries.zh: 上笑曰：「夫相國乃利民！」
entries.en: The emperor laughed and said, 'So the Prime Minister has been profiting from the people!'
entries.literal: The emperor laughed: 'The Prime Minister is benefiting the people!'

entries.zh: 民所上書皆以與相國，曰：「君自謝民。」
entries.en: He handed all the people's petitions to the Prime Minister and said, 'You can apologize to them yourself.'
entries.literal: He gave all the people's submitted memorials to the Prime Minister, saying: 'You personally apologize to the people.'

entries.zh: 相國因為民請曰：「長安地狹，上林中多空地，棄，願令民得入田，毋收槁為禽獸食。」
entries.en: The Prime Minister then petitioned on behalf of the people, saying, 'The farmland around Chang'an is scarce. There is much vacant land lying unused in the Shanglin Park. I ask that the people be allowed to enter and cultivate it, leaving the stubble in the fields as fodder for the wild animals rather than collecting it.'
entries.literal: The Prime Minister thus petitioned for the people: 'Chang'an land is narrow. In Shanglin Park there is much empty land, abandoned. I wish to allow people to enter and farm it, not collecting the stubble for birds and beasts to eat.'

entries.zh: 上大怒曰：「相國多受賈人財物，乃為請吾苑！」
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage, saying, 'The Prime Minister has taken bribes from the merchants, and now he dares petition for my royal park!'
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angered: 'The Prime Minister has received much wealth from merchants, and thus petitions for my park!'

entries.zh: 乃下相國廷尉，械繫之。
entries.en: He had the Prime Minister handed over to the Commandant of Justice, who clapped him in fetters and chains.
entries.literal: He sent the Prime Minister to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, shackling and binding him.

entries.zh: 數日，王衛尉侍，前問曰：「相國何大罪，陛下系之暴也？」
entries.en: Several days later, the Commandant of the Palace Guard, Wang, was in attendance and ventured to ask, 'What terrible crime has the Prime Minister committed that Your Majesty treats him so harshly?'
entries.literal: Several days later, Wang Weiwei attended and asked before him: 'What great crime has the Prime Minister committed that Your Majesty shackles him so violently?'

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾聞李斯相秦皇帝，有善歸主，有惡自與。
entries.en: The emperor replied, 'I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor under the First Emperor of Qin, he credited every good deed to his ruler and took every failing upon himself.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor under the First Emperor of Qin, he attributed good deeds to his ruler and took failings upon himself.

entries.zh: 今相國多受賈豎金而為民請吾苑，以自媚於民，故系治之。」
entries.en: Now the Prime Minister has accepted gold from petty merchants and then petitioned for my park on behalf of the people, all to ingratiate himself with them. That is why I have had him arrested and put under investigation.'
entries.literal: Now the Prime Minister has received much gold from merchants and petitions for my park on behalf of the people, to curry favor with the people, thus I shackle and investigate him.'

entries.zh: 王衛尉曰：「夫職事茍有便於民而請之，真宰相事，陛下柰何乃疑相國受賈人錢乎！
entries.en: The Commandant Wang said, 'If a minister discovers something that would benefit the people and petitions for it, that is precisely what a prime minister ought to do. How can Your Majesty suspect the Prime Minister of taking merchants' bribes?
entries.literal: Wang Weiwei said: 'If in one's duties one petitions for what benefits the people, that is truly a prime minister's affair. How can Your Majesty doubt that the Prime Minister received merchants' money!

entries.zh: 且陛下距楚數歲，陳豨、黥布反，陛下自將而往，當是時，相國守關中，搖足則關以西非陛下有也。
entries.en: Moreover, Your Majesty fought Chu for years, and when Chen Xi and Ying Bu rose in rebellion, Your Majesty personally led the armies against them. During all that time, the Prime Minister guarded the lands within the passes. Had he so much as stamped his foot, everything west of the passes would have ceased to be yours.
entries.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty confronted Chu for several years. Chen Xi and Ying Bu rebelled. Your Majesty personally led troops there. At that time, the Prime Minister guarded Guanzhong—if he stamped his foot, west of the pass would not be yours.

entries.zh: 相國不以此時為利，今乃利賈人之金乎？
entries.en: The Prime Minister did not seize his advantage then. Would he now stoop to profit from the gold of petty merchants?
entries.literal: The Prime Minister did not take advantage at that time—now would he take advantage of merchants' gold?

entries.zh: 且秦以不聞其過亡天下，李斯之分過，又何足法哉。
entries.en: Besides, Qin lost the empire precisely because it refused to hear criticism. Li Si's practice of deflecting blame was hardly worth emulating.
entries.literal: Moreover, Qin perished because they did not hear their faults. Li Si's sharing of faults—what is there to emulate?

entries.zh: 陛下何疑宰相之淺也。」
entries.en: Why does Your Majesty suspect the Prime Minister on such slight grounds?'
entries.literal: Why does Your Majesty harbor such petty suspicions of the prime minister?'

entries.zh: 高帝不懌。
entries.en: Gaozu was not pleased to hear this.
entries.literal: Gaozu was displeased.

entries.zh: 是日，使使持節赦出相國。
entries.en: Yet that very day, he sent an envoy bearing the imperial tally to pardon and release the Prime Minister.
entries.literal: That day, he sent an envoy holding the tally to pardon and release the Prime Minister.

entries.zh: 相國年老，素恭謹，入，徒跣謝。
entries.en: The Prime Minister, old and ever deferential by nature, came before the emperor barefoot to offer his apology.
entries.literal: The Prime Minister was old and usually respectful. He entered barefoot to apologize.

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「相國休矣！
entries.en: Gaozu said, 'Enough, Prime Minister!
entries.literal: Gaozu said: 'Prime Minister, that's enough!

entries.zh: 相國為民請苑，吾不許，我不過為桀紂主，而相國為賢相。
entries.en: You petitioned for the park on behalf of the people, and I refused. That only makes me a tyrant like Jie or Zhou, while you are a worthy minister.
entries.literal: The Prime Minister petitions for the park on behalf of the people. I do not permit it. I am merely a Jie or Zhou ruler, while the Prime Minister is a worthy chancellor.

entries.zh: 吾故系相國，欲令百姓聞吾過也。」
entries.en: I had you arrested deliberately, so that the people would hear of my faults.'
entries.literal: I therefore shackled the Prime Minister to make the people hear of my faults.'

entries.zh: 漢王引兵東定三秦，何以丞相留收巴蜀，填撫諭告，使給軍食。
entries.en: When the King of Han led his troops east to subdue the Three Qin kingdoms, Xiao He stayed behind as chancellor to secure Ba and Shu, pacifying the people with proclamations and keeping the army supplied with provisions.
entries.literal: When the Han King led troops east to pacify the Three Qins, He as chancellor remained to collect Bashu, fill and pacify by proclamation and instruction, and supply the army with food.

entries.zh: 漢二年，漢王與諸侯擊楚，何守關中，侍太子，治櫟陽。
entries.en: In the second year of Han, the King of Han joined the other lords in attacking Chu. Xiao He remained to guard the lands within the passes, attend the crown prince, and govern from Yueyang.
entries.literal: In Han year 2, the Han King together with the feudal lords attacked Chu. He guarded Guanzhong, attended to the crown prince, and governed from Liyang.

entries.zh: 為法令約束，立宗廟社稷宮室縣邑，輒奏上，可，許以從事；
entries.en: He drafted laws and regulations, established ancestral temples, altars to the gods of soil and grain, palaces, and administrative districts. Whenever he submitted a memorial that was approved, he was permitted to proceed.
entries.literal: He established statutes and regulations, erected ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, palaces, chambers, districts, and counties. Whenever he memorialized upward, if approved, he was permitted to proceed;

entries.zh: 即不及奏上，輒以便宜施行，上來以聞。
entries.en: When there was no time to wait for approval, he acted as he saw fit and reported the matter upon the emperor's return.
entries.literal: if there was no time to memorialize upward, he would proceed according to what was expedient, and report upward when the emperor came.

entries.zh: 關中事計戶口轉漕給軍，漢王數失軍遁去，何常興關中卒，輒補缺。
entries.en: He managed the affairs within the passes by tallying households and organizing grain shipments to supply the army. Each time the King of Han lost his forces and had to flee, Xiao He raised fresh troops from within the passes and promptly filled the gaps.
entries.literal: Guanzhong affairs were calculated by households and population, transporting grain to supply the army. The Han King frequently lost troops and fled, but He constantly raised Guanzhong soldiers and promptly filled the gaps.

entries.zh: 上以此專屬任何關中事。
entries.en: For this reason, the emperor entrusted Xiao He with sole authority over all affairs within the passes.
entries.literal: The emperor therefore specially entrusted all Guanzhong affairs to He.

entries.zh: 漢三年，漢王與項羽相距京索之閒，上數使使勞苦丞相。
entries.en: In the third year of Han, while the King of Han faced Xiang Yu between Jing and Suo, the emperor repeatedly sent messengers to offer his regards to the chancellor.
entries.literal: In Han year 3, the Han King confronted Xiang Yu between Jing and Suo, and the emperor frequently sent envoys to console the chancellor.

entries.zh: 鮑生謂丞相曰：「王暴衣露蓋，數使使勞苦君者，有疑君心也。
entries.en: A man named Bao Sheng told the chancellor, 'The king endures hardship in the open field yet keeps sending messengers to inquire after you. This means he harbors suspicions about your loyalty.
entries.literal: Bao Sheng told the chancellor: 'The king exposes himself to wind and dew, frequently sending envoys to console you—this shows doubt in his heart toward you.

entries.zh: 為君計，莫若遣君子孫昆弟能勝兵者悉詣軍所，上必益信君。」
entries.en: For your own sake, you should send every one of your sons, grandsons, and brothers who can bear arms to join the army at the front. The emperor will certainly trust you all the more for it.'
entries.literal: For your sake, nothing would be better than sending all your sons, grandsons, younger brothers who can bear arms to the army camp—the emperor will certainly trust you even more.'

entries.zh: 於是何從其計，漢王大說。
entries.en: Xiao He followed this advice, and the King of Han was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: Thus, He followed this plan, and the Han King was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 漢十二年秋，黥布反，上自將擊之，數使使問相國何為。
entries.en: In the autumn of the twelfth year of Han, Ying Bu rose in rebellion. The emperor personally led the campaign against him, and kept sending messengers back to ask what the Prime Minister was doing.
entries.literal: In Han year 12 autumn, Ying Bu rebelled. The emperor personally led troops to attack him, frequently sending envoys to ask what the Prime Minister was doing.

entries.zh: 相國為上在軍，乃拊循勉力百姓，悉以所有佐軍，如陳豨時。
entries.en: Since the emperor was away at war, the Prime Minister comforted and rallied the people and poured all available resources into supporting the army, just as he had done during the campaign against Chen Xi.
entries.literal: The Prime Minister, because the emperor was in the army, stroked and encouraged the people, using all he had to assist the army, like during Chen Xi's time.

entries.zh: 客有說相國曰：「君滅族不久矣。
entries.en: A retainer warned the Prime Minister, 'It will not be long before your entire clan is wiped out.
entries.literal: A guest advised the Prime Minister: 'Your clan will be extinguished soon.

entries.zh: 夫君位為相國，功第一，可復加哉？
entries.en: You hold the office of Prime Minister and rank first in merit. What more could possibly be added?
entries.literal: Your position is Prime Minister, merit first—can it be increased further?

entries.zh: 然君初入關中，得百姓心，十餘年矣，皆附君，常復孳孳得民和。
entries.en: Ever since you first entered the lands within the passes, you have held the hearts of the people. For more than ten years they have all rallied to you, and you have worked tirelessly to win their goodwill.
entries.literal: Yet when you first entered Guanzhong, you won the people's hearts. For more than ten years, all have attached themselves to you, and you constantly diligently obtain the people's harmony.

entries.zh: 上所為數問君者，畏君傾動關中。
entries.en: The reason the emperor keeps asking about you is that he fears you might stir up the lands within the passes.
entries.literal: The reason the emperor frequently asks about you is that he fears you will overturn Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 今君胡不多買田地，賤貰貸以自汙？
entries.en: Why not buy up large tracts of land on the cheap, even taking loans at low interest, and so tarnish your own reputation?
entries.literal: Now why don't you buy more fields and land, borrow cheaply to defile yourself?

entries.zh: 上心乃安。」
entries.en: Then the emperor's mind will be put at ease.'
entries.literal: Then the emperor's heart will be at peace.'

entries.zh: 於是相國從其計，上乃大說。
entries.en: The Prime Minister took this advice, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: Thus, the Prime Minister followed his plan, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 何素不與曹參相能，及何病，孝惠自臨視相國病，因問曰：「君即百歲後，誰可代君者？」
entries.en: Xiao He and Cao Shen had never been on good terms. When Xiao He fell gravely ill, Emperor Hui came personally to visit him at his sickbed and asked, 'When you are gone, who could take your place?'
entries.literal: He normally did not get along with Cao Shen. When He fell ill, Emperor Hui personally visited to see the Prime Minister's illness, and asked: 'If you pass away after a hundred years, who can replace you?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「知臣莫如主。」
entries.en: Xiao He replied, 'No one knows his ministers better than their lord.'
entries.literal: He replied: 'No one knows a minister better than his ruler.'

entries.zh: 孝惠曰：「曹參何如？」
entries.en: Emperor Hui asked, 'What do you think of Cao Shen?'
entries.literal: Emperor Hui said: 'What about Cao Shen?'

entries.zh: 何頓首曰：「帝得之矣！
entries.en: Xiao He bowed his head to the ground and said, 'Your Majesty has found the right man!
entries.literal: He bowed his head to the ground and said, 'Your Majesty has found the right man!

entries.zh: 臣死不恨矣！」
entries.en: I can die without regret.'
entries.literal: I will die without regret!'

entries.zh: 孝惠二年，相國何卒，謚為文終侯。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Prime Minister Xiao He passed away. He was given the posthumous title of Marquis Wenzhong.
entries.literal: In Emperor Hui's second year, Prime Minister He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Wenzhong.

entries.zh: 蕭相國何者，沛豐人也。
entries.en: Chancellor Xiao He was a native of Feng in the district of Pei.
entries.literal: Prime Minister Xiao He was a man from Feng in Pei.

entries.zh: 以文無害為沛主吏掾。
entries.en: His skill with documents and administrative competence earned him the position of chief clerk in Pei.
entries.literal: Through his mastery of documents and faultless administration, he became the chief clerk of Pei.

entries.zh: 高祖為沛公而初起也，參以中涓從。
entries.en: When Gaozu first rose as the Lord of Pei, Cao Shen joined him as a personal attendant.
entries.literal: When Gaozu rose as Duke of Pei, Cao Shen followed as an attendant.

entries.zh: 將擊胡陵、方與，攻秦監公軍，大破之。
entries.en: Leading the attack on Huling and Fangyu, he engaged the army of the Qin Inspector and routed it.
entries.literal: He led attacks on Huling and Fangyu, assaulting the Qin Inspector's army and greatly defeating it.

entries.zh: 東下薛，擊泗水守軍薛郭西。
entries.en: Marching east, he took Xue and struck the Sishui commandery garrison west of the outer walls of Xue.
entries.literal: He advanced east to Xue, attacking the garrison of the Si River warden west of Xue's outer walls.

entries.zh: 復攻胡陵，取之。
entries.en: A second assault captured Huling.
entries.literal: He attacked Huling again and captured it.

entries.zh: 徙守方與。
entries.en: He was then reassigned to defend Fangyu.
entries.literal: He was transferred to defend Fangyu.

entries.zh: 方與反為魏，擊之。
entries.en: When Fangyu defected to Wei, he attacked it.
entries.literal: Fangyu defected to Wei, so he attacked it.

entries.zh: 豐反為魏，攻之。
entries.en: When Feng defected to Wei, he attacked it as well.
entries.literal: Feng defected to Wei, so he attacked it.

entries.zh: 賜爵七大夫。
entries.en: He was awarded the rank of Seventh-Order Grandee.
entries.literal: He was granted the rank of Seventh Rank Noble.

entries.zh: 擊秦司馬夷軍碭東，破之，取碭、狐父、祁善置。
entries.en: Against the army of the Qin Marshal Yi east of Dang, he won a victory and captured Dang, Hufu, and Qishan.
entries.literal: He attacked the Qin Marshal Yi's army east of Dang, defeated it, and captured Dang, Hufu, and Qishanzhi.

entries.zh: 又攻下邑以西，至虞，擊章邯車騎。
entries.en: Advancing west from Xiayi to Yu, he engaged Zhang Han's chariot and cavalry forces.
entries.literal: He further attacked west from Xiayi to Yu, attacking Zhang Han's chariots and cavalry.

entries.zh: 攻爰戚及亢父，先登。
entries.en: At Yuanqi and Kangfu he stormed the walls and was the first man over them.
entries.literal: He attacked Yuanqi and Kangfu, being first to scale the walls.

entries.zh: 遷為五大夫。
entries.en: He was promoted to the rank of Fifth-Order Grandee.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Fifth Rank Noble.

entries.zh: 北救阿，擊章邯軍，陷陳，追至濮陽。
entries.en: Marching north to relieve E, he attacked Zhang Han's army, broke through its battle lines, and pursued the enemy as far as Puyang.
entries.literal: He went north to rescue E, attacked Zhang Han's army, broke through their formations, and pursued to Puyang.

entries.zh: 攻定陶，取臨濟。
entries.en: At Dingtao he attacked and took Linji.
entries.literal: He attacked Dingtao and captured Linji.

entries.zh: 南救雍丘。
entries.en: He went south to relieve the siege of Yongqiu.
entries.literal: He went south to rescue Yongqiu.

entries.zh: 擊李由軍，破之，殺李由，虜秦候一人。
entries.en: In the battle against the army of Li You, he defeated the enemy, slew Li You, and captured a Qin marquis.
entries.literal: He attacked Li You's army, defeated it, killed Li You, and captured one Qin noble.

entries.zh: 秦將章邯破殺項梁也，沛公與項羽引而東。
entries.en: After the Qin general Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, the Lord of Pei and Xiang Yu withdrew their forces eastward.
entries.literal: When Qin general Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, the Duke of Pei and Xiang Yu led their armies east.

entries.zh: 楚懷王以沛公為碭郡長，將碭郡兵。
entries.en: King Huai of Chu appointed the Lord of Pei as the governor of Dang commandery and placed the commandery's troops under his command.
entries.literal: King Huai of Chu appointed the Duke of Pei as governor of Dang commandery to lead Dang commandery troops.

entries.zh: 於是乃封參為執帛，號曰建成君。
entries.en: Thereupon Cao Shen was given the title of Holder of Silk and styled Lord of Jiancheng.
entries.literal: Thus, he enfeoffed Cao Shen as Holder of Silk, with the title Lord Jiancheng.

entries.zh: 遷為戚公，屬碭郡。
entries.en: He was promoted to the rank of Lord of Qi, under the jurisdiction of Dang commandery.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Lord of Qi, belonging to Dang commandery.

entries.zh: 項羽至，以沛公為漢王。
entries.en: When Xiang Yu arrived, he installed the Lord of Pei as King of Han.
entries.literal: When Xiang Yu arrived, he made the Duke of Pei King of Han.

entries.zh: 漢王封參為建成侯。
entries.en: The King of Han granted Cao Shen the title Marquis of Jiancheng.
entries.literal: The King of Han enfeoffed Cao Shen as Marquis of Jiancheng.

entries.zh: 從至漢中，遷為將軍。
entries.en: He accompanied the king to Hanzhong and was promoted to general.
entries.literal: He followed to Hanzhong, promoted to general.

entries.zh: 從還定三秦，初攻下辯、故道、雍、斄。
entries.en: In the campaign to return and pacify the Three Qin kingdoms, he first took Xiabian, Gudao, Yong, and Tai.
entries.literal: He followed returning to pacify the Three Qins, initially attacking and capturing Bian, Gudao, Yong, and Lai.

entries.zh: 擊章平軍於好畤南，破之，圍好畤，取壤鄉。
entries.en: At Haozhi, he defeated Zhang Ping's army south of the city, then besieged Haozhi and seized Rangxiang.
entries.literal: He attacked Zhang Ping's army south of Haozhi, defeated it, besieged Haozhi, and captured Rangxiang.

entries.zh: 擊三秦軍壤東及高櫟，破之。
entries.en: Against the Three Qin forces east of Rang and at Gaoli, he won another victory.
entries.literal: He attacked the Three Qins army east of Rang and at Gaoque, defeating it.

entries.zh: 復圍章平，章平出好畤走。
entries.en: Zhang Ping was besieged once more and fled from Haozhi.
entries.literal: He besieged Zhang Ping again, Zhang Ping fled from Haozhi.

entries.zh: 因擊趙賁、內史保軍，破之。
entries.en: Turning next against Zhao Ben and the Grand Administrator Bao, he defeated both armies.
entries.literal: He then attacked Zhao Ben and Grand Administrator Bao's army, defeating it.

entries.zh: 東取咸陽，更名曰新城。
entries.en: Xianyang was taken to the east and renamed Xincheng.
entries.literal: He captured Xianyang to the east, renaming it New City.

entries.zh: 參將兵守景陵二十日，三秦使章平等攻參，參出擊，大破之。
entries.en: Cao Shen garrisoned Jingling for twenty days. When the Three Qin kingdoms dispatched Zhang Ping and others to attack him, he sallied forth and routed them.
entries.literal: Cao Shen led troops guarding Jingling for twenty days, the Three Qins sent Zhang Ping and others to attack Cao Shen, Cao Shen sallied to attack, greatly defeating them.

entries.zh: 賜食邑於寧秦。
entries.en: He was granted a food fief at Ningqin.
entries.literal: He was granted fief income in Ningqin.

entries.zh: 參以將軍引兵圍章邯於廢丘。
entries.en: As general, Cao Shen led his troops to besiege Zhang Han at Feiqiu.
entries.literal: Cao Shen as general led troops besieging Zhang Han at Fei Qiu.

entries.zh: 以中尉從漢王出臨晉關。
entries.en: Serving as Commandant, he accompanied the King of Han through Linjin Pass.
entries.literal: As Commandant he followed the King of Han out of Linjin Pass.

entries.zh: 至河內，下修武，渡圍津，東擊龍且、項他定陶，破之。
entries.en: After reaching Henei, he took Xiuwu, crossed at Weijin, and struck eastward against Long Ju and Xiang Ta at Dingtao, defeating them.
entries.literal: Arriving in Henei, he captured Xiuwu, crossed at Weijin, attacked Long Ju and Xiang Ta at Dingtao to the east, defeating them.

entries.zh: 東取碭、蕭、彭城。
entries.en: From there he marched east to capture Dang, Xiao, and Pengcheng.
entries.literal: He captured Dang, Xiao, and Pengcheng to the east.

entries.zh: 擊項籍軍，漢軍大敗走。
entries.en: In battle with Xiang Yu's army, the Han forces suffered a crushing defeat and fled.
entries.literal: He attacked Xiang Yu's army, the Han army suffered great defeat and fled.

entries.zh: 參以中尉圍取雍丘。
entries.en: As Commandant, Cao Shen besieged and took Yongqiu.
entries.literal: Cao Shen as Commandant besieged and captured Yongqiu.

entries.zh: 王武反於［外］黃，程處反於燕，往擊，盡破之。
entries.en: When Wang Wu revolted at Waihuang and Cheng Chu revolted at Yan, he marched against them and defeated them all.
entries.literal: Wang Wu rebelled at Waihuang, Cheng Chu rebelled at Yan, he went to attack them, completely defeating both.

entries.zh: 柱天侯反於衍氏，又進破取衍氏。
entries.en: The Marquis of Zhutian revolted at Yanshi, and Cao Shen advanced to take the city.
entries.literal: Marquis Zhutian rebelled at Yanshi, he advanced and defeated and captured Yanshi.

entries.zh: 擊羽嬰於昆陽，追至葉。
entries.en: At Kunyang he attacked Yu Ying and pursued him as far as Ye.
entries.literal: He attacked Yu Ying at Kunyang, pursuing to Ye.

entries.zh: 還攻武彊，因至滎陽。
entries.en: Turning back, he attacked Wuqiang and then made his way to Xingyang.
entries.literal: He returned attacking Wujiang, thus reaching Xingyang.

entries.zh: 參自漢中為將軍中尉，從擊諸侯，及項羽敗，還至滎陽，凡二歲。
entries.en: From the time Cao Shen left Hanzhong as General-Commandant, following the campaigns against the feudal lords until Xiang Yu's defeat and the return to Xingyang, two full years had passed.
entries.literal: Cao Shen from Hanzhong served as General Commandant, following to attack the feudal lords, and when Xiang Yu was defeated, returned to Xingyang, altogether two years.

entries.zh: 項籍已死，天下定，漢王為皇帝，韓信徙為楚王，齊為郡。
entries.en: After Xiang Yu's death and the pacification of the realm, the King of Han became emperor. Han Xin was transferred to the kingship of Chu, and Qi was made a commandery.
entries.literal: After Xiang Ji died and the realm was pacified, the King of Han became emperor, Han Xin was moved to King of Chu, Qi became a commandery.

entries.zh: 參歸漢相印。
entries.en: Cao Shen returned the Han chancellor's seal.
entries.literal: Cao Shen returned the Han chancellorship seal.

entries.zh: 高帝以長子肥為齊王，而以參為齊相國。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu made his eldest son Fei the King of Qi and appointed Cao Shen as the Chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: Gaozu made his eldest son Fei King of Qi, and appointed Cao Shen as Qi's prime minister.

entries.zh: 以高祖六年賜爵列侯，與諸侯剖符，世世勿絕。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Gaozu's reign, he was granted the rank of full marquis, receiving a tallied covenant with the feudal lords that his line would never be extinguished.
entries.literal: In Gaozu year 6 he was granted marquis rank, sharing the tally with feudal lords, never to be extinguished generation after generation.

entries.zh: 食邑平陽萬六百三十戶，號曰平陽侯，除前所食邑。
entries.en: His fief was set at Pingyang with ten thousand six hundred and thirty households, and he was styled Marquis of Pingyang, superseding all previous fiefs.
entries.literal: His fief income was Pingyang with 10,630 households, titled Marquis of Pingyang, removing his previous fief income.

entries.zh: 其後從攻東郡尉軍，破之成武南。
entries.en: Afterward, he joined in attacking the army of the Dongjun commandant and defeated it south of Chengwu.
entries.literal: Afterwards he followed in attacking the Dongjun warden's army, defeating it south of Chengwu.

entries.zh: 擊王離軍成陽南，復攻之杠裏，大破之。
entries.en: Against Wang Li's army south of Chengyang, he pressed the attack again at Gangli and crushed it.
entries.literal: He attacked Wang Li's army south of Chengyang, then attacked it again at Gangli, greatly defeating it.

entries.zh: 追北，西至開封，擊趙賁軍，破之，圍趙賁開封城中。
entries.en: Pursuing the fleeing enemy westward to Kaifeng, he defeated Zhao Ben's army and besieged Zhao Ben within the city walls.
entries.literal: He pursued the routed enemy west to Kaifeng, attacked Zhao Ben's army, defeated it, and besieged Zhao Ben in Kaifeng city.

entries.zh: 西擊將楊熊軍於曲遇，破之，虜秦司馬及御史各一人。
entries.en: Striking west against General Yang Xiong's army at Quyu, he defeated it and captured a Qin marshal and an imperial censor.
entries.literal: He attacked General Yang Xiong's army at Quyü to the west, defeated it, and captured one Qin marshal and one imperial secretary each.

entries.zh: 遷為執珪。
entries.en: He was promoted to the rank of Holder of Jade.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Holder of Jade.

entries.zh: 從攻陽武，下軒轅、緱氏，絕河津，還擊趙賁軍尸北，破之。
entries.en: Joining the attack on Yangwu, he took Xuanyuan and Goushi, severed the river crossings, then wheeled back to defeat Zhao Ben's army north of Shi.
entries.literal: He followed in attacking Yangwu, captured Xuanyuan and Goushi, cut off the river crossings, returned to attack Zhao Ben's army north of Shi, and defeated it.

entries.zh: 從南攻犨，與南陽守齮戰陽城郭東，陷陳，取宛，虜齮，盡定南陽郡。
entries.en: Marching south against Chou, he fought the Nanyang governor Yi east of Yangcheng's walls, broke through the enemy lines, captured Wan, took Yi prisoner, and brought the entire Nanyang commandery under control.
entries.literal: He followed south attacking Yan, fought with the Nanyang warden Yi east of Yangcheng's outer walls, broke through formations, captured Wan, captured Yi, and completely pacified Nanyang commandery.

entries.zh: 從西攻武關、峣關，取之。
entries.en: Pressing westward, he attacked and captured Wuguan and Yaoguan.
entries.literal: He followed west attacking Wuguan and Yaoguan, capturing them.

entries.zh: 前攻秦軍藍田南，又夜擊其北，秦軍大破，遂至咸陽，滅秦。
entries.en: Cao Shen advanced against the Qin army south of Lantian, then struck its northern flank by night. The Qin army was shattered, and the Han forces pressed on to Xianyang, bringing the Qin dynasty to its end.
entries.literal: He advanced attacking the Qin army south of Lantian, then at night attacked its north, the Qin army was greatly defeated, thus reaching Xianyang and destroying Qin.

entries.zh: 高祖（三）［二］年，拜為假左丞相，入屯兵關中。
entries.en: In the second year of Gaozu's reign, he was appointed Acting Left Chancellor and entered Guanzhong to garrison the region.
entries.literal: In Gaozu year 2, he was appointed Acting Left Chancellor, entering to station troops in Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 月餘，魏王豹反，以假左丞相別與韓信東攻魏將軍孫遬軍東張，大破之。
entries.en: A little over a month later, King Bao of Wei rebelled. As Acting Left Chancellor, Cao Shen joined Han Xin on a separate campaign eastward, attacking the Wei general Sun Su's army at Dongzhang and routing it.
entries.literal: After more than a month, King Wei Bao rebelled, so as Acting Left Chancellor he separately went east with Han Xin to attack Wei general Sun Ju's army at Dongzhang, greatly defeating it.

entries.zh: 因攻安邑，得魏將王襄。
entries.en: Anyi was then attacked, and the Wei general Wang Xiang was captured.
entries.literal: He then attacked Anyi, capturing Wei general Wang Xiang.

entries.zh: 擊魏王於曲陽，追至武垣，生得魏王豹。
entries.en: At Quyang he struck the King of Wei, pursued him to Wuyuan, and took King Bao of Wei alive.
entries.literal: He attacked the King of Wei at Quyang, pursuing to Wuyuan, capturing the King of Wei Bao alive.

entries.zh: 取平陽，得魏王母妻子，盡定魏地，凡五十二城。
entries.en: Pingyang fell next; he seized the King of Wei's mother, wife, and children, bringing all of Wei's territory under control—fifty-two cities in all.
entries.literal: He captured Pingyang, obtaining the King of Wei's mother, wife, and children, completely pacifying Wei territory, altogether fifty-two cities.

entries.zh: 賜食邑平陽。
entries.en: A food fief at Pingyang was granted to him.
entries.literal: He was granted fief income in Pingyang.

entries.zh: 因從韓信擊趙相國夏說軍於鄔東，大破之，斬夏說。
entries.en: He next joined Han Xin in attacking the Zhao Chancellor Xia Yue's army east of Wu, inflicting a devastating defeat and beheading Xia Yue.
entries.literal: He then followed Han Xin attacking Chancellor of Zhao Xia Yue's army east of Wu, greatly defeating it, beheading Xia Yue.

entries.zh: 韓信與故常山王張耳引兵下井陘，擊成安君，而令參還圍趙別將戚將軍於鄔城中。
entries.en: Han Xin and the former King of Changshan, Zhang Er, led their forces down through the Jingxing Pass to attack the Lord of Cheng'an, while ordering Cao Shen to turn back and besiege the Zhao commander General Qi inside the walls of Wu.
entries.literal: Han Xin and former King Changshan Zhang Er led troops down Jingxing, attacking Lord Cheng'an, while ordering Cao Shen to return and besiege Zhao's separate general Lord Qi in Wu city.

entries.zh: 戚將軍出走，追斬之。
entries.en: General Qi broke out and fled, but Cao Shen pursued and killed him.
entries.literal: Lord Qi fled, he pursued and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 乃引兵詣敖倉漢王之所。
entries.en: From there he led his forces to the Ao Granary, where the King of Han was stationed.
entries.literal: He then led troops to Aocang where the King of Han was located.

entries.zh: 韓信已破趙，為相國，東擊齊。
entries.en: Han Xin, having already conquered Zhao and been made Chancellor, now turned east to attack Qi.
entries.literal: Han Xin had already defeated Zhao, became Chancellor, attacking Qi to the east.

entries.zh: 參以右丞相屬韓信，攻破齊歷下軍，遂取臨菑。
entries.en: As Right Chancellor serving under Han Xin, Cao Shen smashed the Qi army at Lixia and went on to capture the capital Linzi.
entries.literal: Cao Shen as Right Chancellor under Han Xin attacked and broke the Qi army at Lixia, thus capturing Linzi.

entries.zh: 還定濟北郡，攻著、漯陰、平原、鬲、盧。
entries.en: Returning to pacify Jibei commandery, he attacked Zhu, Taoyin, Pingyuan, Ge, and Lu.
entries.literal: He returned to pacify Jibei commandery, attacking Zhu, Taoyin, Pingyuan, Ge, and Lu.

entries.zh: 已而從韓信擊龍且軍於上假密，大破之，斬龍且，虜其將軍周蘭。
entries.en: Soon afterward he joined Han Xin in attacking Long Ju's army at Shangjia. They dealt it a crushing blow, beheading Long Ju and capturing his general Zhou Lan.
entries.literal: Soon after he followed Han Xin attacking Long Ju's army at Shang Jiami, greatly defeating it, beheading Long Ju, capturing his general Zhou Lan.

entries.zh: 定齊，凡得七十餘縣。
entries.en: With Qi fully pacified, they had secured more than seventy counties in all.
entries.literal: He pacified Qi, altogether obtaining over seventy counties.

entries.zh: 得故齊王田廣相田光，其守相許章，及故齊膠東將軍田既。
entries.en: He captured Tian Guang, the chancellor of the former King of Qi Tian Guang; Xu Zhang, the defending chancellor; and Tian Ji, the former Jiaodong general of Qi.
entries.literal: He obtained the former King of Qi Tian Guang's chancellor Tian Guang, his defending chancellor Xu Zhang, and the former Jiaodong general of Qi Tian Ji.

entries.zh: 韓信為齊王，引兵詣陳，與漢王共破項羽，而參留平齊未服者。
entries.en: When Han Xin, now King of Qi, led his forces to Chen to join the King of Han in destroying Xiang Yu, Cao Shen stayed behind to subdue the parts of Qi that had not yet submitted.
entries.literal: Han Xin became King of Qi, led troops to Chen, together with the King of Han defeated Xiang Yu, while Cao Shen remained to pacify those in Qi who had not submitted.

entries.zh: 以齊相國擊陳豨將張春軍，破之。
entries.en: As Chancellor of Qi, he attacked the army of Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun and defeated it.
entries.literal: As Qi prime minister he attacked Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun's army, defeating it.

entries.zh: 黥布反，參以齊相國從悼惠王將兵車騎十二萬人，與高祖會擊黥布軍，大破之。
entries.en: When Ying Bu revolted, Cao Shen, as Chancellor of Qi, accompanied King Daohui with a force of one hundred and twenty thousand infantry, chariots, and cavalry to join Emperor Gaozu in striking Ying Bu's army. They inflicted a crushing defeat.
entries.literal: Ying Bu rebelled, Cao Shen as Qi prime minister followed King Daohui leading troops and chariots of 120,000 men, meeting with Gaozu to attack Ying Bu's army, greatly defeating it.

entries.zh: 南至蘄，還定竹邑、相、蕭、留。
entries.en: Pressing south as far as Qi, he then turned back to pacify Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao, and Liu.
entries.literal: He went south to Qi, returning to pacify Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao, and Liu.

entries.zh: 參子窋為中大夫。
entries.en: Cao Shen's son Zhu served as a Palace Grandee.
entries.literal: Cao Shen's son Zhu served as Palace Grandee.

entries.zh: 惠帝怪相國不治事，以為「豈少朕與」？
entries.en: Emperor Hui found it strange that the chancellor took no interest in governance, and wondered, "Could it be that he thinks little of me?"
entries.literal: Emperor Hui was surprised the prime minister did not handle affairs, thinking, "Could it be that he thinks little of me?"

entries.zh: 乃謂窋曰：「若歸，試私從容問而父曰：『高帝新棄群臣，帝富於春秋，君為相，日飲，無所請事，何以憂天下乎？』
entries.en: So the emperor told Zhu, "When you go home, find a quiet moment and ask your father casually: 'Emperor Gaozu has only recently departed from his ministers. The emperor is young, and you, the chancellor, do nothing but drink all day. You never bring a single matter before the throne. How can you claim to be worrying about the realm?'
entries.literal: He then told Zhu, "When you return, try privately and at your leisure to ask your father, 'Gaozu has newly abandoned his ministers; the emperor is still young; you serve as chancellor, yet you drink all day and bring no business before the throne—how can you claim to be worrying about the realm?'

entries.zh: 然無言吾告若也。」
entries.en: But do not let on that I put you up to it."
entries.literal: However, do not say I told you."

entries.zh: 窋既洗沐歸，窋侍，自從其所諫參。
entries.en: On his next rest day, Zhu went home. While attending his father, he followed the emperor's instructions and raised the matter with Cao Shen.
entries.literal: Zhu, having bathed and returned, while attending his father, privately followed the emperor's instructions and remonstrated with Cao Shen.

entries.zh: 參怒，而笞窋二百，曰：「趣入侍，天下事非若所當言也。」
entries.en: Cao Shen flew into a rage and had Zhu caned two hundred strokes, saying, "Get back to the palace and attend the emperor. The affairs of the realm are no concern of yours."
entries.literal: Cao Shen was angry and caned Zhu two hundred strokes, saying, "Hurry back to attend the emperor—the affairs of the realm are not for you to speak of."

entries.zh: 至朝時，惠帝讓參曰：「與窋胡治乎？
entries.en: At the next audience, Emperor Hui reproached Cao Shen: "Why did you punish Zhu?
entries.literal: At court, Emperor Hui reproached Cao Shen, saying, "Why did you punish Zhu?

entries.zh: 乃者我使諫君也。」
entries.en: It was I who told him to speak with you."
entries.literal: It was I who sent him to remonstrate with you.'

entries.zh: 參免冠謝曰：「陛下自察聖武孰與高帝？」
entries.en: Cao Shen doffed his cap and apologized, then asked, "Would Your Majesty say that in sagely martial virtue you are the equal of Emperor Gaozu?"
entries.literal: Cao Shen removed his cap and apologized: 'Your majesty yourself examine—whose sagely martial qualities compare with Gaozu's?'

entries.zh: 上曰：「朕乃安敢望先帝乎！」
entries.en: The emperor replied, "How would I dare compare myself to the former emperor!"
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'How would I dare aspire to the former emperor!'

entries.zh: 曰：「陛下觀臣能孰與蕭何賢？」
entries.en: Cao Shen continued, "And does Your Majesty consider me the equal of Xiao He in ability?"
entries.literal: Cao Shen said, "Your Majesty, whose ability do you consider the equal of Xiao He's?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「君似不及也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "You do not seem to be his equal."
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'You seem not to match him.'

entries.zh: 參曰：「陛下言之是也。
entries.en: Cao Shen said, "Your Majesty speaks truly.
entries.literal: Cao Shen said: 'Your majesty's words are correct.

entries.zh: 且高帝與蕭何定天下，法令既明，今陛下垂拱，參等守職，遵而勿失，不亦可乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu and Xiao He pacified the realm, and the laws and ordinances they laid down are clear. Now if Your Majesty sits with folded hands, and men like myself faithfully guard our posts, following those precedents without deviation—is that not sufficient?"
entries.literal: Moreover, Gaozu and Xiao He pacified the realm, laws and ordinances already clear, now your majesty hangs sleeves and does nothing, we and others guard our positions, follow without losing them—is this not acceptable?'

entries.zh: 惠帝曰：「善。
entries.en: Emperor Hui said, "Very well.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui said: 'Good.

entries.zh: 君休矣！」
entries.en: You may retire."
entries.literal: You are excused!'

entries.zh: 孝惠帝元年，除諸侯相國法，更以參為齊丞相。
entries.en: In the first year of Emperor Hui's reign, the law governing the appointment of feudal chancellors was abolished, and Cao Shen's title was changed to Chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: In Emperor Hui year 1, the law for feudal lords' prime ministers was abolished, changing Cao Shen to Qi chancellor.

entries.zh: 參之相齊，齊七十城。
entries.en: When Cao Shen served as Chancellor of Qi, the kingdom comprised seventy cities.
entries.literal: When Cao Shen served as chancellor of Qi, Qi had seventy cities.

entries.zh: 天下初定，悼惠王富於春秋，參盡召長老諸生，問所以安集百姓，如齊故［俗］諸儒以百數，言人人殊，參未知所定。
entries.en: The realm had only just been settled, and King Daohui was still young. Cao Shen summoned all the elders and scholars to ask how best to bring peace and stability to the people. The Confucian scholars of Qi numbered in the hundreds, and each one had a different answer, so Cao Shen could not decide on a course of action.
entries.literal: The realm had just been pacified, King Daohui was young, Cao Shen summoned all the elders and scholars, asking how to pacify and gather the people, scholars of Qi custom numbered in the hundreds, each speaking differently, Cao Shen did not know what to decide.

entries.zh: 聞膠西有蓋公，善治黃老言，使人厚幣請之。
entries.en: He then heard that in Jiaoxi there lived a certain Master Gai, well versed in the teachings of Huang-Lao, and sent emissaries bearing generous gifts to invite him.
entries.literal: He heard there was Master Gai in Jiaoxi who was skilled in Huang-Lao teachings, sent people with generous gifts to invite him.

entries.zh: 既見蓋公，蓋公為言治道貴清靜而民自定，推此類具言之。
entries.en: When they met, Master Gai explained that the essence of good governance lies in prizing stillness and non-interference, so that the people settle of their own accord. He elaborated on this principle at length.
entries.literal: When he met Master Gai, Master Gai spoke of the way of governance valuing tranquility and the people naturally settling, elaborating on this category comprehensively.

entries.zh: 參於是避正堂，舍蓋公焉。
entries.en: Cao Shen thereupon vacated his own principal hall and lodged Master Gai in it.
entries.literal: Thus, Cao Shen vacated the main hall and housed Master Gai there.

entries.zh: 其治要用黃老術，故相齊九年，齊國安集，大稱賢相。
entries.en: The core of his administration rested on Huang-Lao methods. He served as Chancellor of Qi for nine years, during which the kingdom was peaceful and orderly, and he was universally acclaimed as a worthy chancellor.
entries.literal: His governance essentials used Huang-Lao methods, thus serving as chancellor of Qi for nine years, Qi was pacified and stable, greatly acclaimed as a worthy chancellor.

entries.zh: 惠帝二年，蕭何卒。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Xiao He died.
entries.literal: In Emperor Hui year 2, Xiao He died.

entries.zh: 參聞之，告舍人趣治行，「吾將入相」。
entries.en: When Cao Shen heard the news, he told his retainers to pack at once, saying, "I am about to be summoned to serve as chancellor."
entries.literal: Cao Shen heard of it, told his retainers to quickly prepare for travel, 'I will enter as prime minister.'

entries.zh: 居無何，使者果召參。
entries.en: Before long, imperial envoys arrived to summon him, just as he had predicted.
entries.literal: Before long, envoys indeed summoned Cao Shen.

entries.zh: 參去，屬其後相曰：「以齊獄市為寄，慎勿擾也。」
entries.en: Before departing, Cao Shen instructed his successor as chancellor: "Treat the prisons and markets of Qi as a sacred trust, and take care not to meddle with them."
entries.literal: Cao Shen departed, instructing his successor chancellor: 'Consider Qi's prisons and markets as entrusted, do not disturb them.'

entries.zh: 後相曰：「治無大於此者乎？」
entries.en: The new chancellor asked, "Is there truly nothing more important in governing than this?"
entries.literal: The successor chancellor said: 'Is there nothing more important than this in governance?'

entries.zh: 參曰：「不然。
entries.en: Cao Shen replied, "No, that is not so.
entries.literal: Cao Shen said: 'Not so.

entries.zh: 夫獄市者，所以并容也，今君擾之，姦人安所容也？
entries.en: The prisons and markets are places that accommodate all sorts of people. If you interfere with them, where will the troublemakers go?
entries.literal: Prisons and markets are for accommodating all sorts—now if you disturb them, where will wicked people find accommodation?

entries.zh: 吾是以先之。」
entries.en: That is why I place this matter above all else."
entries.literal: This is why I put it first.'

entries.zh: 平陽侯曹參者，沛人也。
entries.en: Cao Shen, the Marquis of Pingyang, was a native of Pei.
entries.literal: Marquis Pingyang Cao Shen was a native of Pei.

entries.zh: 秦時為沛獄掾，而蕭何為主吏，居縣為豪吏矣。
entries.en: Under the Qin, he served as the assistant jailer in Pei, while Xiao He was the chief clerk. Both were among the most prominent officials in the county.
entries.literal: During Qin times he served as assistant jailer in Pei, while Xiao He was the chief clerk—they were both outstanding officials in the county.

entries.zh: 項王竟不肯遣韓王，乃以為侯，又殺之彭城。
entries.en: In the end, the King of Xiang refused to release the King of Han, demoted him to a mere marquis, and then had him killed at Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Xiang Wang ultimately refused to send the King of Han, made him a marquis instead, then killed him at Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 良亡，間行歸漢王，漢王亦已還定三秦矣。
entries.en: Liang escaped and traveled by hidden paths back to the King of Han, who by that time had already returned from Bashu and subdued the Three Qins.
entries.literal: Liang fled, secretly traveled back to the King of Han, the King of Han had also returned and pacified the Three Qins.

entries.zh: 復以良為成信侯，從東擊楚。
entries.en: He once again enfeoffed Liang as Marquis of Chengxin, and Liang followed him eastward to attack Chu.
entries.literal: Again appointed Liang as Marquis of Chengxin, following east to attack Chu.

entries.zh: 至彭城，漢敗而還。
entries.en: At Pengcheng the Han forces suffered a devastating defeat and retreated.
entries.literal: Arrived at Pengcheng, Han was defeated and returned.

entries.zh: 至下邑，漢王下馬踞鞍而問曰：「吾欲捐關以東等棄之，誰可與共功者？」
entries.en: When they reached Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and sat upon his saddle, asking, 'I would give up everything east of the passes. Who can share the achievement with me?'
entries.literal: When they reached Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and sat on his saddle, asking: 'I wish to abandon everything east of the passes—who can share merit with me?'

entries.zh: 良進曰：「九江王黥布，楚梟將，與項王有郄；
entries.en: Liang stepped forward and said, 'Ying Bu, King of Jiujiang, is a fearsome Chu commander who bears a grudge against the King of Xiang.
entries.literal: Liang advanced and said: 'King Jiu Jiang Ying Bu is a fierce Chu general, has a grudge with Xiang Wang;

entries.zh: 彭越與齊王田榮反梁地：此兩人可急使。
entries.en: Peng Yue has raised a revolt in the Liang region alongside Tian Rong of Qi. These two can be called upon immediately.
entries.literal: Peng Yue is rebelling in Liang territory with King Qi Tian Rong: these two can be urgently employed.

entries.zh: 而漢王之將獨韓信可屬大事，當一面。
entries.en: Among your own generals, Han Xin alone can be trusted with great undertakings and entrusted to hold an independent front.
entries.literal: Among the King of Han's generals, only Han Xin can be entrusted with great matters, to hold one front.

entries.zh: 即欲捐之，捐之此三人，則楚可破也。」
entries.en: If you are willing to cede those lands, cede them to these three men, and Chu can be defeated.'
entries.literal: If you wish to abandon it, abandon it to these three men, then Chu can be broken.'

entries.zh: 漢王乃遣隨何說九江王布，而使人連彭越。
entries.en: The King of Han then dispatched Sui He to win over Ying Bu, King of Jiujiang, and sent envoys to make contact with Peng Yue.
entries.literal: The King of Han then sent Sui He to persuade King Jiu Jiang Bu, and sent people to contact Peng Yue.

entries.zh: 及魏王豹反，使韓信將兵擊之，因舉燕、代、齊、趙。
entries.en: When King Bao of Wei rebelled, the King of Han sent Han Xin to lead an army against him, and Han Xin went on to conquer Yan, Dai, Qi, and Zhao.
entries.literal: When King Wei Bao rebelled, he had Han Xin lead troops to attack him, thus raising Yan, Dai, Qi, and Zhao.

entries.zh: 然卒破楚者，此三人力也。
entries.en: In the end, it was these three men whose strength brought about the defeat of Chu.
entries.literal: Yet those who ultimately broke Chu were these three men's strength.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：學者多言無鬼神，然言有物。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Most scholars deny the existence of ghosts and spirits, yet they acknowledge the existence of strange phenomena.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: Scholars mostly say there are no ghosts and spirits, yet they speak of having things.

entries.zh: 至如留侯所見老父予書，亦可怪矣。
entries.en: As for the old man whom the Marquis of Liu encountered, who bestowed a book upon him — that too is a strange affair indeed.
entries.literal: As for the Marquis of Liu seeing the old man give the book, it can also be considered strange.

entries.zh: 高祖離困者數矣，而留侯常有功力焉，豈可謂非天乎？
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu escaped from peril time and again, and each time the Marquis of Liu proved instrumental in his deliverance — can this be called anything but the work of Heaven?
entries.literal: Gaozu encountered difficulties several times, yet the Marquis of Liu constantly had meritorious strength—how can this not be called Heaven?

entries.zh: 上曰：「夫運籌筴帷帳之中，決勝千里外，吾不如子房。」
entries.en: The Emperor himself declared: 'When it comes to devising strategies within the command tent and securing victory a thousand li away, I am no match for Zifang.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Planning strategies within the tent, deciding victories a thousand li away—I am not equal to Zifang.'

entries.zh: 余以為其人計魁梧奇偉，至見其圖，狀貌如婦人好女。
entries.en: I had always imagined such a man to be a towering, imposing figure, but when I saw his portrait, his features were as delicate as those of a beautiful woman.
entries.literal: I had supposed this man to be stalwart and extraordinary, until seeing his portrait; his appearance was like that of a woman or a beautiful girl.

entries.zh: 蓋孔子曰：「以貌取人，失之子羽。」
entries.en: As Confucius once said: 'If you judge a man by his appearance, you would have misjudged Ziyu.'
entries.literal: As Confucius said: 'To take people by appearance loses Zi Yu.'

entries.zh: 留侯亦云。
entries.en: The same could well be said of the Marquis of Liu.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu was also thus.

entries.zh: 留侯從上擊代，出奇計馬邑下，及立蕭何相國，所與上從容言天下事甚眾，非天下所以存亡，故不著。
entries.en: The Marquis of Liu accompanied the emperor on the campaign against Dai, devised a brilliant stratagem at Mayi, and played a role in appointing Xiao He as Chancellor of State. He discussed a great many affairs of the realm with the emperor at leisure, but since they did not bear on questions of the empire's survival, they are not recorded here.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu followed the emperor attacking Dai, put forth extraordinary plans at Maiyi, and when establishing Xiao He as prime minister, the affairs of the realm he discussed leisurely with the emperor were very many, but they were not the realm's matters of survival and extinction, thus not recorded.

entries.zh: 留侯乃稱曰：「家世相韓，及韓滅，不愛萬金之資，為韓報讐彊秦，天下振動。
entries.en: The Marquis of Liu once declared, "My family served for generations as chancellors of Han. When Han was destroyed, I did not begrudge a fortune of ten thousand pieces of gold to avenge the state against mighty Qin, and the whole empire trembled at my deed.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu then said: 'My family for generations served as chancellors of Han, and when Han was extinguished, I did not spare ten thousand jin of wealth, to avenge Han I strongly opposed Qin, shaking the realm.

entries.zh: 今以三寸舌為帝者師，封萬戶，位列侯，此布衣之極，於良足矣。
entries.en: Now, with nothing more than a three-inch tongue, I have become the teacher of an emperor, received a fief of ten thousand households, and attained the rank of marquis. For a man who began as a commoner, this is the summit of achievement. It is more than enough for me.
entries.literal: Now with three cun tongue I serve as the emperor's teacher, enfeoffed with ten thousand households, position as marquis—this is the extreme for a commoner, sufficient for Liang.

entries.zh: 願棄人間事，欲從赤松子游耳。」
entries.en: I wish to leave behind the affairs of this world and wander with Master Red Pine."
entries.literal: I wish to abandon worldly affairs, desire to follow Master Chisong in roaming.'

entries.zh: 乃學辟穀，道引輕身。
entries.en: He then took up the practice of abstaining from grain and performed Daoist exercises to lighten his body.
entries.literal: Thus, he studied avoiding grain, guiding and pulling to lighten the body.

entries.zh: 會高帝崩，呂后德留侯，乃彊食之，曰：「人生一世間，如白駒過隙，何至自苦如此乎！」
entries.en: When Emperor Gao died, Empress Lu, grateful for all the Marquis of Liu had done, pressed him to eat again, saying, "A man's life in this world is as brief as a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall. Why torment yourself so?"
entries.literal: When Gaozu passed away, Empress Lü was grateful to the Marquis of Liu and pressed him to eat, saying: 'A person's life in the world is like a white colt flashing past a crack—why torment yourself so?'

entries.zh: 留侯不得已，彊聽而食。
entries.en: The Marquis of Liu had no choice but to comply, and reluctantly began eating again.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu had no choice, strongly listened and ate.

entries.zh: 子房始所見下邳圯上老父與太公書者，後十三年從高帝過濟北，果見穀城山下黃石，取而葆祠之。
entries.en: The old man whom Zifang had met on the bridge at Xiapi, the one who gave him the book of Taigong — thirteen years later, while accompanying Emperor Gao through Jibei, Zhang Liang came upon a yellow stone at the foot of Mount Gucheng, just as the old man had foretold. He took it and enshrined it with reverence.
entries.literal: Zifang at first saw the old man on the Xiapi bridge who gave him the Taigong book—thirteen years later following Gaozu passing Jibei, indeed saw the yellow stone under Gucheng Mountain, took it and treasured and sacrificed to it.

entries.zh: 留侯死，并葬黃石（冢）。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Liu died, the yellow stone was buried with him in his tomb.
entries.literal: When the Marquis of Liu died, he was buried together with the yellow stone tomb.

entries.zh: 每上冢伏臘，祠黃石。
entries.en: At each seasonal sacrifice, when the family visited the tomb, they offered rites to the yellow stone as well.
entries.literal: Every time ascending the tomb at winter sacrifices, he sacrificed to the yellow stone.

entries.zh: 漢十一年，黥布反，上病，欲使太子將，往擊之。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Han, Ying Bu revolted. The emperor was ill and wished to send the crown prince to lead the army against him.
entries.literal: Han year 11, Ying Bu rebelled, the emperor was ill, wished to have the crown prince lead troops, go attack him.

entries.zh: 四人相謂曰：「凡來者，將以存太子。
entries.en: The Four Elders said to one another, "We came here for the sole purpose of safeguarding the crown prince.
entries.literal: The four men said to one another: 'We came in general to preserve the crown prince.

entries.zh: 太子將兵，事危矣。」
entries.en: If the crown prince is sent to command the army, his position will be in grave danger."
entries.literal: If the crown prince leads troops, the matter is dangerous.'

entries.zh: 乃說建成侯曰：「太子將兵，有功則位不益太子；
entries.en: They went to the Marquis of Jiancheng and counseled him, "If the crown prince leads the army and wins, his rank cannot rise any higher than it already is.
entries.literal: Thus, they advised the Marquis of Jiancheng: 'If the crown prince leads troops and has merit, his position will not benefit the crown prince;

entries.zh: 無功還，則從此受禍矣。
entries.en: But if he returns without distinction, disaster will surely follow.
entries.literal: if no merit and returns, then from this he will receive disaster.

entries.zh: 且太子所與俱諸將，皆嘗與上定天下梟將也，今使太子將之，此無異使羊將狼也，皆不肯為盡力，其無功必矣。
entries.en: Moreover, every general assigned to serve under the crown prince once helped the emperor conquer the empire — battle-hardened veterans all. Setting the crown prince over them is no different from sending a lamb to lead a pack of wolves. None will fight with full effort, and failure is certain.
entries.literal: Moreover, the various generals accompanying the crown prince have all once been fierce generals who pacified the realm with the emperor, now to have the crown prince command them—this is no different from making a sheep lead wolves, they will all be unwilling to exert full effort, it will certainly be no merit.

entries.zh: 臣聞『母愛者子抱』，今戚夫人日夜待御，趙王如意常抱居前，上曰『終不使不肖子居愛子之上』，明乎其代太子位必矣。
entries.en: We have heard the saying, 'The child of the favored mother is held in the arms.' Lady Qi attends the emperor day and night, and Ruyi, the King of Zhao, is always at his father's side. The emperor has declared, 'I will never let an unworthy son stand above the son I love.' It is plain that the crown prince will be replaced.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard 'a mother who loves her child embraces him'; now Lady Qi serves day and night, Ruyi, King of Zhao, is constantly held in front; the emperor says 'I will never let an unworthy son be placed above a beloved son'; clearly his replacing the crown prince's position is certain.

entries.zh: 君何不急請呂后承間為上泣言：『黥布，天下猛將也，善用兵，今諸將皆陛下故等夷，乃令太子將此屬，無異使羊將狼，莫肯為用，且使布聞之，則鼓行而西耳。
entries.en: You should urge Empress Lu to find the right moment and plead with the emperor through tears, saying that Ying Bu is one of the most fearsome generals alive and a master of warfare. The generals you would assign to the crown prince are all men who once fought as your equals. To put the crown prince in command of them is no different from setting a lamb over wolves — not one will obey. And if Ying Bu hears of it, he will march on us without hesitation.
entries.literal: Why don't you urgently request Empress Lü to seize the opportunity and weepingly tell the emperor: 'Ying Bu is a fierce general of the realm, skilled in using troops, now the various generals are all your majesty's former equals, to command the crown prince to lead these people is no different from making a sheep lead wolves, none will be willing to be employed, moreover if Bu hears of it, he will drum and advance west.

entries.zh: 上雖病，彊載輜車，臥而護之，諸將不敢不盡力。
entries.en: Though Your Majesty is ill, you must force yourself into a supply wagon and oversee the campaign even from a reclining position. With you present, none of the generals will dare hold anything back.
entries.literal: Although your majesty is ill, force yourself to ride in the baggage cart, lie down and supervise them, the various generals will dare not not exert full effort.

entries.zh: 上雖苦，為妻子自彊。』」
entries.en: It will be hard on you, but for the sake of your wife and children, you must bear it."
entries.literal: Although your majesty suffers, for the sake of wife and children force yourself.'

entries.zh: 於是呂澤立夜見呂后，呂后承間為上泣涕而言，如四人意。
entries.en: Lu Ze went to see Empress Lu that very night. The empress found the right moment, and through her tears she spoke to the emperor exactly as the Four Elders had directed.
entries.literal: Thus, Lü Ze that night saw Empress Lü, Empress Lü seized the opportunity and weeping told the emperor, as the four people's intention.

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾惟豎子固不足遣，而公自行耳。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I have always known the boy is not up to the task. I shall lead the campaign myself."
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'I only considered the brat certainly insufficient to send, so I must go myself.'

entries.zh: 於是上自將兵而東，群臣居守，皆送至灞上。
entries.en: The emperor then took personal command of the army and marched east. The ministers who remained behind to guard the capital escorted him as far as Bashang.
entries.literal: Thus, the emperor personally led troops east, the ministers remained to guard, all escorted to Bashang.

entries.zh: 留侯病，自彊起，至曲郵，見上曰：「臣宜從，病甚。
entries.en: The Marquis of Liu was ill, but he forced himself out of bed and traveled to Quyu to see the emperor. He said, "I ought to accompany you, but my illness is too severe.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu was ill, forced himself to rise, arrived at Quyü, saw the emperor and said: 'Your servant should follow, but illness is severe.

entries.zh: 楚人剽疾，願上無與楚人爭鋒。」
entries.en: The men of Chu are fierce and quick to attack. I beg Your Majesty not to meet them head-on."
entries.literal: Chu people are fierce and swift, I wish your majesty not to contend with Chu people at the spearpoint.'

entries.zh: 因說上曰：「令太子為將軍，監關中兵。」
entries.en: He also advised, "Appoint the crown prince as general to command the garrison troops within the passes."
entries.literal: Thus, he advised the emperor: 'Have the crown prince serve as general, oversee Guanzhong troops.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「子房雖病，彊臥而傅太子。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Zifang, even though you are ill, I ask you to stay at your rest and serve as tutor to the crown prince."
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Zifang although ill, force yourself to lie down and instruct the crown prince.'

entries.zh: 是時叔孫通為太傅，留侯行少傅事。
entries.en: At that time Shusun Tong held the office of Grand Tutor, while the Marquis of Liu served as Junior Tutor.
entries.literal: At this time Shu Sun Tong served as Grand Tutor, the Marquis of Liu performed Junior Tutor duties.

entries.zh: 漢十二年，上從擊破布軍歸，疾益甚，愈欲易太子。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Han, the emperor returned from his victory over Ying Bu's forces. His illness had grown worse, and his desire to replace the crown prince became more pressing than ever.
entries.literal: Han year 12, the emperor returned from attacking and defeating Bu's army, illness grew worse, even more wished to change the crown prince.

entries.zh: 留侯諫，不聽，因疾不視事。
entries.en: The Marquis of Liu remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen. Pleading illness, the marquis withdrew from public affairs.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu remonstrated, not listened to, thus due to illness did not handle affairs.

entries.zh: 叔孫太傅稱說引古今，以死爭太子。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Shusun Tong invoked precedents from antiquity and the present, staking his very life on the defense of the crown prince.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Shu Sun cited and explained ancient and modern to contend for the crown prince to the death.

entries.zh: 上詳許之，猶欲易之。
entries.en: The emperor feigned agreement, yet in his heart still intended to make the change.
entries.literal: The emperor pretended to permit it, yet still wished to change him.

entries.zh: 及燕，置酒，太子侍。
entries.en: At a banquet one evening, wine was served, and the crown prince attended upon his father.
entries.literal: When feasting, set up wine, the crown prince attended.

entries.zh: 四人從太子，年皆八十有餘，鬚眉皓白，衣冠甚偉。
entries.en: Four men accompanied the crown prince, all past eighty years of age, with snow-white beards and brows, clad in robes and caps of striking dignity.
entries.literal: The four people followed the crown prince, ages all over eighty, beards and eyebrows white, clothing and caps extremely magnificent.

entries.zh: 上怪之，問曰：「彼何為者？」
entries.en: The emperor was startled and asked, "Who are these men?"
entries.literal: The emperor was astonished, asked: 'Who are those?'

entries.zh: 四人前對，各言名姓，曰東園公，角里先生，綺里季，夏黃公。
entries.en: The four men stepped forward, and each gave his name: Master Dongyuan, Master Jiaoli, Master Qili, and Master Xiahuang.
entries.literal: The four men advanced and replied, each stating his name: Master Dongyuan, Master Jiaoli, Master Qili, and Master Xiahuang.

entries.zh: 上乃大驚，曰：「吾求公數歲，公辟逃我，今公何自從吾兒游乎？」
entries.en: The emperor was greatly astonished and exclaimed, "I have sought you for years, and you always fled from me. Why have you now chosen to follow my son?"
entries.literal: The emperor then greatly astonished, said: 'I have sought you gentlemen for several years, you gentlemen avoided and fled me, now why do you gentlemen follow my son in leisure?'

entries.zh: 四人皆曰：「陛下輕士善罵，臣等義不受辱，故恐而亡匿。
entries.en: The four men all replied, "Your Majesty despises scholars and is given to cursing them. We could not in good conscience endure such insult, so we withdrew in fear and went into hiding.
entries.literal: The four people all said: 'Your majesty lightly esteems scholars and is good at cursing, we servants righteously would not accept insult, thus feared and fled into hiding.

entries.zh: 竊聞太子為人仁孝，恭敬愛士，天下莫不延頸欲為太子死者，故臣等來耳。」
entries.en: But we have heard that the crown prince is humane and filial, respectful and fond of scholars. All under heaven crane their necks, eager to lay down their lives for him. That is why we have come."
