entries.literal: We secretly heard the crown prince is humane and filial, respectful and loves scholars, the realm none do not crane necks desiring to die for the crown prince, thus we servants came.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「煩公幸卒調護太子。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I am grateful. I ask you to continue looking after the crown prince."
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'I trouble you gentlemen to happily finally protect and care for the crown prince.'

entries.zh: 四人為壽已畢，趨去。
entries.en: When the four men had finished offering their toasts, they withdrew.
entries.literal: The four people having made toasts finished, hurried away.

entries.zh: 上目送之，召戚夫人指示四人者曰：「我欲易之，彼四人輔之，羽翼已成，難動矣。
entries.en: The emperor watched them go, then summoned Lady Qi and pointed after the four men, saying, "I wanted to replace the heir, but those four now stand behind him. His wings are fully formed — he can no longer be displaced.
entries.literal: The emperor watched them depart, summoned Lady Qi, and pointing at the four men said: 'I wished to replace him, but those four now assist him; his wings are already formed—he can no longer be displaced.

entries.zh: 呂后真而主矣。」
entries.en: Empress Lu is truly his protector now."
entries.literal: Empress Lü is truly the master.'

entries.zh: 戚夫人泣，上曰：「為我楚舞，吾為若楚歌。」
entries.en: Lady Qi wept. The emperor said, "Dance the dance of Chu for me, and I will sing a song of Chu for you."
entries.literal: Lady Qi wept, the emperor said: 'Dance the Chu dance for me, I will sing the Chu song for you.'

entries.zh: 歌曰：「鴻鴈高飛，一舉千里。
entries.en: He sang, "The wild swan soars on high, a thousand leagues in a single flight.
entries.literal: He sang: 'The wild swan soars on high, a thousand leagues in a single flight.

entries.zh: 羽翮已就，橫絕四海。
entries.en: Its wings are fully fledged; it sweeps across the four seas.
entries.literal: Feathers and wings already formed, spanning across the four seas.

entries.zh: 橫絕四海，當可奈何！
entries.en: It sweeps across the four seas — what can be done?
entries.literal: Spanning across the four seas, what can be done about it!

entries.zh: 雖有矰繳，尚安所施！」
entries.en: Though you have arrows tethered with silk, where would you aim them now?"
entries.literal: Even if there are arrows and strings, where can they still be applied!'

entries.zh: 歌數闋，戚夫人噓唏流涕，上起去，罷酒。
entries.en: After singing several verses, Lady Qi broke into sobs. The emperor rose and departed, and the banquet came to an end.
entries.literal: He sang several stanzas, Lady Qi sobbed and wept, the emperor rose and left, the banquet ended.

entries.zh: 竟不易太子者，留侯本招此四人之力也。
entries.en: In the end, the crown prince was never replaced, and this was entirely owing to the Marquis of Liu's stratagem of summoning the Four Elders.
entries.literal: In the end he did not change the crown prince—the Marquis of Liu originally summoned these four people's strength.

entries.zh: 留侯張良者，其先韓人也。
entries.en: Zhang Liang, the Marquis of Liu, was descended from a family of the state of Han.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu Zhang Liang was originally from the state of Han.

entries.zh: 大父開地，相韓昭侯、宣惠王、襄哀王。
entries.en: His grandfather Kaidi served as chancellor to Marquis Zhao, King Xuanhui, and King Xiang'ai of Han.
entries.literal: His grandfather Kai Di served as chancellor to Han kings Zhao Hou, Xuan Hui Wang, and Xiang Ai Wang.

entries.zh: 父平，相釐王、悼惠王。
entries.en: His father Ping served as chancellor to King Xi and King Daohui.
entries.literal: His father Ping served as chancellor to Xi Wang and Dao Hui Wang.

entries.zh: 悼惠王二十三年，平卒。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year of King Daohui's reign, Ping died.
entries.literal: In Dao Hui Wang year 23, Ping died.

entries.zh: 卒二十歲，秦滅韓。
entries.en: Twenty years after his death, the state of Qin conquered Han.
entries.literal: Twenty years after his death, Qin destroyed Han.

entries.zh: 良年少，未宦事韓。
entries.en: Liang was still young and had not yet entered government service for Han.
entries.literal: Liang was young and had not yet taken office to serve Han.

entries.zh: 韓破，良家僮三百人，弟死不葬，悉以家財求客刺秦王，為韓報仇，以大父、父五世相韓故。
entries.en: When Han fell, Liang's household still numbered three hundred servants. Though his younger brother died, he did not pause even to arrange a burial, instead spending the entire family fortune to recruit an assassin to strike down the King of Qin—all to avenge Han, for his grandfather and father had served the state as chancellors for five generations.
entries.literal: When Han was destroyed, Liang had three hundred household slaves, his younger brother died unburied, he used all his family wealth to hire assassins to stab the Qin king, to avenge Han, because his grandfather and father had served as chancellors of Han for five generations.

entries.zh: 絳侯、灌嬰等咸讒陳平曰：「平雖美丈夫，如冠玉耳，其中未必有也。
entries.en: The Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying, and others all spoke against Chen Ping: "Ping may be a handsome fellow, but he is like jade on a cap—all show on the outside, with nothing of substance within.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying and others all slandered Chen Ping, saying: "Ping, though a handsome man, is like a jade crown—beautiful outside but may have nothing inside.

entries.zh: 臣聞平居家時，盜其嫂；
entries.en: We have heard that while he lived at home, he had an affair with his sister-in-law;
entries.literal: We have heard that when Ping lived at home, he stole his sister-in-law;

entries.zh: 事魏不容，亡歸楚；
entries.en: that he served Wei but was cast out, and fled to Chu;
entries.literal: Served Wei but was not tolerated, fled and joined Chu;

entries.zh: 歸楚不中，又亡歸漢。
entries.en: that he did not fit in at Chu either, and fled again to Han.
entries.literal: Did not fit in Chu, fled again and joined Han.

entries.zh: 今日大王尊官之，令護軍。
entries.en: Now the Great King has honored him with high office and set him over the army.
entries.literal: Now the Great King honors him with high office and has him oversee the army.

entries.zh: 臣聞平受諸將金，金多者得善處，金少者得惡處。
entries.en: We hear that Ping accepts gold from the generals—those who give generously receive favorable assignments, while those who give little are sent to the worst posts.
entries.literal: We have heard Ping accepts gold from the generals—those who give much gold get good positions, those who give little get bad positions.

entries.zh: 平，反覆亂臣也，願王察之。」
entries.en: Ping is a faithless, disloyal minister. We beg Your Majesty to look into the matter."
entries.literal: Ping is a treacherous minister of repeated betrayals. We hope the king will investigate him."

entries.zh: 漢王疑之，召讓魏無知。
entries.en: The King of Han grew suspicious and summoned Wei Wuzhi to reprimand him.
entries.literal: The Han King doubted him and summoned to rebuke Wei Wuzhi.

entries.zh: 無知曰：「臣所言者，能也；
entries.en: Wei Wuzhi replied, "What I recommended him for was his ability;
entries.literal: Wei Wuzhi said: "What I spoke of was his ability;

entries.zh: 陛下所問者，行也。
entries.en: what Your Majesty is asking about is his personal conduct.
entries.literal: What Your Majesty is asking about is his conduct.

entries.zh: 今有尾生、孝己之行而無益處於勝負之數，陛下何暇用之乎？
entries.en: Even if a man possessed the virtue of Weisheng or Xiaoji, yet contributed nothing to the reckoning of victory and defeat, would Your Majesty have the leisure to employ him?
entries.literal: Now if one has the conduct of Weisheng or Xiao Ji but is of no benefit to the calculations of victory and defeat, why would Your Majesty have leisure to employ such a person?

entries.zh: 楚漢相距，臣進奇謀之士，顧其計誠足以利國家不耳。
entries.en: With Chu and Han locked in a standoff, your servant recommends men of extraordinary stratagem. The only question is whether their plans can truly benefit the state.
entries.literal: Chu and Han are at standoff. Your servant advances extraordinary strategists—only considering whether their plans can truly benefit the state.

entries.zh: 且盜嫂受金又何足疑乎？」
entries.en: Besides, even if he did seduce a sister-in-law or accept some gold—what does that matter?"
entries.literal: Moreover, committing adultery with a sister-in-law and accepting gold—what is there to doubt?"

entries.zh: 漢王召讓平曰：「先生事魏不中，遂事楚而去，今又從吾游，信者固多心乎？」
entries.en: The King of Han summoned Ping and rebuked him: "Sir, you served Wei without gaining their trust, then served Chu and left there too. Now you follow me—should a man of such shifting loyalties not arouse suspicion?"
entries.literal: The Han King summoned Ping and rebuked him, saying: "Sir, you served Wei without success, then served Chu and left; now you follow me—should a trustworthy man have so many hearts?"

entries.zh: 平曰：「臣事魏王，魏王不能用臣說，故去事項王。
entries.en: Ping replied, "Your servant served the King of Wei, but he would not heed my counsel, so I left and went to serve the King of Xiang.
entries.literal: Ping said: "Your servant served the King of Wei. The King of Wei could not use my advice, so I left to serve Xiang Yu.

entries.zh: 項王不能信人，其所任愛，非諸項即妻之昆弟，雖有奇士不能用，平乃去楚。
entries.en: The King of Xiang cannot trust others. Those he favors and appoints are either members of the Xiang clan or his wife's kinsmen—even men of extraordinary talent find no place with him. So I left Chu.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu could not trust people. Those he appointed and favored were either various Xiang clan members or his wife's brothers—even if there were extraordinary men, he could not use them, so Ping left Chu.

entries.zh: 聞漢王之能用人，故歸大王。
entries.en: I heard that the King of Han knows how to employ men of talent, so I came to serve Your Majesty.
entries.literal: I heard the Han King was good at employing people, so I came to Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 臣躶身來，不受金無以為資。
entries.en: I arrived with nothing but the clothes on my back. Without accepting some gold, I would have had no means to sustain myself.
entries.literal: Your servant came naked, without receiving gold I have no means to provide for myself.

entries.zh: 誠臣計畫有可采者，（顧）［願］大王用之；
entries.en: If my plans have any merit worth adopting, I beg the Great King to employ them;
entries.literal: If my servant's plans have merit that can be adopted, I hope the Great King will use them;

entries.zh: 使無可用者，金具在，請封輸官，得請骸骨。」
entries.en: if they are of no use, the gold is all still here—seal it and return it to the treasury, and grant me leave to retire."
entries.literal: If none are usable, the gold is still there—please seal it and return it to the treasury, and allow me to retire."

entries.zh: 漢王乃謝，厚賜，拜為護軍中尉，盡護諸將。
entries.en: The King of Han thereupon apologized, bestowed generous gifts upon him, and formally appointed him Commandant Protector of the Army, placing all the generals under his supervision.
entries.literal: The Han King then apologized, gave generous gifts, appointed him Protector of the Army Commandant, and put him in charge of overseeing all the generals.

entries.zh: 諸將乃不敢復言。
entries.en: After that, none of the generals dared raise the matter again.
entries.literal: The generals then dared not speak again.

entries.zh: 平行聞高帝崩，平恐呂太后及呂媭讒怒，乃馳傳先去。
entries.en: While on the road, Ping received word that Emperor Gaozu had died. Fearing that Empress Dowager Lu and Lu Xu would slander him in their anger, he raced ahead by relay.
entries.literal: Now the emperor wants to behead him, we should follow the command."

entries.zh: 逢使者詔平與灌嬰屯於滎陽。
entries.en: On the way he encountered a messenger bearing an edict ordering Ping and Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang.
entries.literal: On the way he met a messenger with an edict ordering Ping and Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang.

entries.zh: 平受詔，立復馳至宮，哭甚哀，因奏事喪前。
entries.en: Ping received the edict but immediately galloped to the palace, where he wept with great sorrow and made his report before the funeral bier.
entries.literal: Ping received the command, immediately galloped back to the palace, wept extremely sorrowfully, and because of the funeral matters made his report.

entries.zh: 呂太后哀之，曰：「君勞，出休矣。」
entries.en: Empress Dowager Lu was moved by his grief and said, "You have labored hard. Go and rest."
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Lu was moved by his grief and said: "You have labored; go out and rest."

entries.zh: 平畏讒之就，因固請得宿衛中。
entries.en: Ping feared the slanders that might befall him if he left, so he insisted on being allowed to remain in the palace as a guard.
entries.literal: Ping feared that slander would take hold, so he firmly requested to remain on night-guard duty in the palace.

entries.zh: 太后乃以為郎中令，曰：「傅教孝惠。」
entries.en: The Empress Dowager thereupon appointed him Palace Counselor, saying, "Serve as tutor and guide to Emperor Xiaohui."
entries.literal: Now ill, who will strategize for the army?"

entries.zh: 是後呂媭讒乃不得行。
entries.en: From then on, Lu Xu's slanders could gain no purchase.
entries.literal: Thereafter Lu Xu's slanders could not take effect.

entries.zh: 樊噲至，則赦復爵邑。
entries.en: When Fan Kuai arrived at the capital, he was pardoned and had his title and fief restored.
entries.literal: When Fan Kuai arrived, he was pardoned and had his rank and fief restored.

entries.zh: 陳丞相平者，陽武戶牖鄉人也。
entries.en: Chancellor Chen Ping was a native of Huyou Township in the district of Yangwu.
entries.literal: Prime Minister Chen Ping was a native of Huyou village in Yangwu.

entries.zh: 少時家貧，好讀書，有田三十畝，獨與兄伯居。
entries.en: In his youth, his family was poor, yet he loved to read. He owned just thirty mu of farmland and lived alone with his elder brother Bo.
entries.literal: In his youth his family was poor, but he loved reading books. He had thirty mu of fields and lived only with his elder brother Bo.

entries.zh: 伯常耕田，縱平使游學。
entries.en: Bo worked the fields without cease, letting Ping roam freely in pursuit of learning.
entries.literal: Bo constantly tilled the fields, allowing Ping to travel and study.

entries.zh: 平為人長［大］美色。
entries.en: Ping was tall, imposing, and strikingly handsome.
entries.literal: Ping was tall and handsome in appearance.

entries.zh: 人或謂陳平曰：「貧何食而肥若是？」
entries.en: Someone once asked Chen Ping, "You are so poor—what do you eat to look so well-fed?"
entries.literal: Someone said to Chen Ping: 'Though poor, how do you eat to become so plump?'

entries.zh: 其嫂嫉平之不視家生產，曰：「亦食糠覈耳。
entries.en: His sister-in-law, who resented Ping for never tending to the family livelihood, snapped, "He eats nothing but chaff and husks.
entries.literal: His sister-in-law resented that Ping did not oversee the family production and said: 'He also eats only bran and husks.

entries.zh: 有叔如此，不如無有。」
entries.en: Better to have no brother-in-law at all than one like him."
entries.literal: Having an uncle like this, it would be better to have none.'

entries.zh: 伯聞之，逐其婦而棄之。
entries.en: When Bo heard this, he drove his wife out and divorced her.
entries.literal: Bo heard this and drove away his wife, divorcing her.

entries.zh: 高祖之為沛公初起，勃以中涓從攻胡陵，下方與。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Gaozu first rose in revolt as the Duke of Pei, Bo joined him as an attendant and took part in the attack on Huling, capturing Fangyu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu as Duke Pei first rose up, Bo as attendant followed in attacking Hu Ling, captured Fangyu.

entries.zh: 方與反，與戰，卻適。
entries.en: When Fangyu revolted, Bo fought the rebels and drove them back.
entries.literal: Fangyu rebelled, fought with them, drove them back.

entries.zh: 攻豐。
entries.en: Bo attacked Feng.
entries.literal: Attacked Feng.

entries.zh: 擊秦軍碭東。
entries.en: He struck the Qin army east of Dang.
entries.literal: Struck Qin army east of Dang.

entries.zh: 還軍留及蕭。
entries.en: The army then withdrew to Liu and Xiao.
entries.literal: Returned army to Liu and Xiao.

entries.zh: 復攻碭，破之。
entries.en: Bo attacked Dang again and took it.
entries.literal: Again attacked Dang, broke it.

entries.zh: 下下邑，先登。
entries.en: At Xiayi, he captured the city and was the first to scale its walls.
entries.literal: Captured Xiayi, first to ascend the walls.

entries.zh: 賜爵五大夫。
entries.en: For this he was granted the rank of Grandee of the Fifth Order.
entries.literal: Granted rank of Grandee of the Fifth Degree.

entries.zh: 攻蒙、虞，取之。
entries.en: Bo attacked Meng and Yu and took both.
entries.literal: Attacked Meng and Yu, took them.

entries.zh: 擊章邯車騎，殿。
entries.en: He engaged Zhang Han's chariots and cavalry, serving as the rearguard.
entries.literal: Struck Zhang Han's chariots and cavalry, brought up the rear.

entries.zh: 定魏地。
entries.en: This campaign pacified the territory of Wei.
entries.literal: Pacified Wei territory.

entries.zh: 攻爰戚、東緡，以往至栗，取之。
entries.en: From there he attacked Yuanqi and Dongmin, then advanced to Li and captured it.
entries.literal: Attacked Yuanqi and Dongmin, proceeding to Li, took it.

entries.zh: 攻齧桑，先登。
entries.en: At Niesang, he attacked and was the first to scale the walls.
entries.literal: Attacked Nie Sang, first to ascend.

entries.zh: 擊秦軍阿下，破之。
entries.en: Below E, he struck the Qin army and defeated it.
entries.literal: Struck Qin army below E, broke it.

entries.zh: 追至濮陽，下甄城。
entries.en: Pursuing the enemy to Puyang, he captured the city of Zhen.
entries.literal: Pursued to Puyang, captured Zhen city.

entries.zh: 攻都關、定陶，襲取宛朐，得單父令。
entries.en: Bo attacked Duguan and Dingtao, raided and seized Wanqu, and captured the magistrate of Shanfu.
entries.literal: Attacked Duchuan and Dingtao, raided and took Wanju, captured Shanfu magistrate.

entries.zh: 夜襲取臨濟，攻張，以前至卷，破之。
entries.en: In a night raid he took Linji, attacked Zhang, then advanced to Juan and broke through its defenses.
entries.literal: Night raided and took Linji, attacked Zhang, advancing first to Juan, broke it.

entries.zh: 擊李由軍雍丘下。
entries.en: Bo engaged the army of Li You beneath the walls of Yongqiu.
entries.literal: Struck Li You's army below Yongqiu.

entries.zh: 攻開封，先至城下為多。
entries.en: At Kaifeng, he led the largest contingent to reach the city walls first.
entries.literal: Attacked Kaifeng, first to reach the city walls with the most.

entries.zh: 後章邯破殺項梁，沛公與項羽引兵東如碭。
entries.en: Later, Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, and the Duke of Pei and Xiang Yu led their troops east to Dang.
entries.literal: Later Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, Duke Pei and Xiang Yu led troops east to Dang.

entries.zh: 自初起沛還至碭，一歲二月。
entries.en: From the initial rising at Pei to the return to Dang, one year and two months had passed.
entries.literal: From first rising in Pei returning to Dang, one year two months.

entries.zh: 楚懷王封沛公號安武侯，為碭郡長。
entries.en: King Huai of Chu bestowed upon the Duke of Pei the title of Marquis of Anwu and appointed him magistrate of Dang Commandery.
entries.literal: King Huai of Chu enfeoffed Duke Pei with the title Peaceful Martial Marquis, made him magistrate of Dang commandery.

entries.zh: 沛公拜勃為虎賁令，以令從沛公定魏地。
entries.en: The Duke of Pei appointed Bo as Commander of the Tiger Guard, and in that capacity Bo followed the Duke to pacify the lands of Wei.
entries.literal: Duke Pei appointed Bo as Commander of the Tiger Braves, as commander followed Duke Pei to pacify Wei territory.

entries.zh: 攻東郡尉於城武，破之。
entries.en: Bo attacked the Governor of the Eastern Commandery at Chengwu and defeated him.
entries.literal: Attacked the East Commandery Governor at Chengwu, broke him.

entries.zh: 擊王離軍，破之。
entries.en: He struck Wang Li's army and routed it.
entries.literal: Struck Wang Li's army, broke it.

entries.zh: 攻長社，先登。
entries.en: At Changshe, he attacked and was the first to scale the walls.
entries.literal: Attacked Changshe, first to ascend.

entries.zh: 攻潁陽、緱氏，絕河津。
entries.en: He attacked Yingyang and Goushi, cutting off the river crossing.
entries.literal: Attacked Yingyang and Goushi, cut off the river crossing.

entries.zh: 擊趙賁軍尸北。
entries.en: North of Shi, he struck Zhao Ben's army.
entries.literal: Struck Zhao Ben's army north of Shi.

entries.zh: 南攻南陽守齮，破武關、峣關。
entries.en: Marching south, he attacked the Governor of Nanyang, Yi, and breached the passes of Wuguan and Yaoguan.
entries.literal: South attacked Nanyang Governor Yi, broke Wuguan and Yaoguan.

entries.zh: 破秦軍於藍田，至咸陽，滅秦。
entries.en: At Lantian, he defeated the Qin army, reached Xianyang, and brought the Qin dynasty to its end.
entries.literal: Broke Qin army at Lantian, reached Xianyang, extinguished Qin.

entries.zh: 項羽至，以沛公為漢王。
entries.en: When Xiang Yu arrived, he made the Duke of Pei the King of Han.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu arrived, made Duke Pei King of Han.

entries.zh: 漢王賜勃爵為威武侯。
entries.en: The King of Han conferred upon Bo the rank of Marquis of Weiwu.
entries.literal: The King of Han granted Bo rank as Martial Marquis.

entries.zh: 從入漢中，拜為將軍。
entries.en: Bo followed him into Hanzhong and was appointed general.
entries.literal: Followed in entering Hanzhong, appointed as general.

entries.zh: 還定三秦，至秦，賜食邑懷德。
entries.en: Returning to pacify the Three Qins, he reached the Qin heartland and was granted the fief of Huaide.
entries.literal: Returned to pacify the Three Qins, reached Qin, granted fief in Huaide.

entries.zh: 攻槐裏、好畤，最。
entries.en: He attacked Huaili and Haozhi and earned the highest distinction.
entries.literal: Attacked Huaili and Haozhi, first in merit.

entries.zh: 擊趙賁、內史保於咸陽，最。
entries.en: At Xianyang, he struck Zhao Ben and the Chamberlain Bao, again earning the highest distinction.
entries.literal: Struck Zhao Ben and Chamberlain Bao at Xianyang, first in merit.

entries.zh: 北攻漆。
entries.en: Marching north, he attacked Qi.
entries.literal: North attacked Qi.

entries.zh: 擊章平、姚卬軍。
entries.en: There he struck the armies of Zhang Ping and Yao Ang.
entries.literal: Struck Zhang Ping and Yao Ang's army.

entries.zh: 西定汧。
entries.en: To the west, he pacified Qian.
entries.literal: West pacified Qian.

entries.zh: 還下郿、頻陽。
entries.en: Returning, he captured Mei and Pinyang.
entries.literal: Returned and captured Mei and Fenyang.

entries.zh: 圍章邯廢丘。
entries.en: He laid siege to Zhang Han at Feiqiu.
entries.literal: Besieged Zhang Han at Fei Qiu.

entries.zh: 破西丞。
entries.en: The Western Chamberlain was defeated.
entries.literal: Broke the Western Chamberlain.

entries.zh: 擊盜巴軍，破之。
entries.en: He attacked Ba's bandit army and defeated it.
entries.literal: Struck the bandit Ba army, broke it.

entries.zh: 攻上邽。
entries.en: From there he attacked Shanggui.
entries.literal: Attacked Shangui.

entries.zh: 東守峣關。
entries.en: He guarded Yaoguan Pass to the east.
entries.literal: East guarded Yaoguan.

entries.zh: 轉擊項籍。
entries.en: Then he turned to strike against Xiang Yu.
entries.literal: Turned to strike Xiang Ji.

entries.zh: 攻曲逆，最。
entries.en: He attacked Quni and earned the highest distinction.
entries.literal: Attacked Qu Ni, first in merit.

entries.zh: 還守敖倉，追項籍。
entries.en: He returned to guard the Ao Granary, then pursued Xiang Yu.
entries.literal: Returned to guard Aocang, pursued Xiang Ji.

entries.zh: 籍已死，因東定楚地泗（川）［水］、東海郡，凡得二十二縣。
entries.en: After Xiang Yu was already dead, Bo went east to pacify the former Chu territories of Sishui and Donghai Commandery, securing twenty-two counties in all.
entries.literal: Ji was already dead; thus he went east to pacify Chu territory Sishui and Donghai commandery, securing twenty-two counties in all.

entries.zh: 還守雒陽、櫟陽，賜與潁（陽）［陰］侯共食鐘離。
entries.en: He returned to garrison Luoyang and Yueyang, and was granted a share of Zhongli's revenues together with the Marquis of Yingyin.
entries.literal: Returned to guard Luoyang and Yueyang, granted to share eating Zhongli with Marquis Yingyin.

entries.zh: 以將軍從高帝反者燕王臧荼，破之易下。
entries.en: As a general, he followed Emperor Gaozu against the rebel King of Yan, Zang Tu, and defeated him at Yi.
entries.literal: As general followed Gaozu against the rebel King Yan Zang Tu, broke him at Yi Xia.

entries.zh: 所將卒當馳道為多。
entries.en: Among the contingents assigned to the imperial road, the troops under his command were the most numerous.
entries.literal: The troops he led facing the imperial roadway were the most numerous.

entries.zh: 賜爵列侯，剖符世世勿絕。
entries.en: He was granted the rank of full marquis, with the tally split as a pledge that his line would never be extinguished.
entries.literal: Granted rank of noble, shared the tally never to be extinguished generation after generation.

entries.zh: 食絳八千一百八十戶，號絳侯。
entries.en: He received a fief of eight thousand one hundred and eighty households at Jiang and was titled the Marquis of Jiang.
entries.literal: Ate Jiang with eight thousand one hundred eighty households, titled Marquis of Jiang.

entries.zh: 竇太后曰：「皇后兄王信可侯也。」
entries.en: Empress Dowager Dou said: "The empress's elder brother, Wang Xin, should be made a marquis."
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Dou said: 'The queen's elder brother Wang Xin can be made marquis.'

entries.zh: 景帝讓曰：「始南皮、章武侯先帝不侯，及臣即位乃侯之。
entries.en: Emperor Jing demurred: "The late emperor did not enfeoff the Marquises of Nanpi and Zhangwu; it was only after I came to the throne that they were made marquises.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing declined saying: 'Originally Nanpi and Zhangwu marquises the late emperor did not make marquises, when I ascended the throne then made them marquises.

entries.zh: 信未得封也。」
entries.en: Xin has not yet received an enfeoffment."
entries.literal: Xin has not yet received enfeoffment.'

entries.zh: 竇太后曰：「人主各以時行耳。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Dou said: "Every sovereign acts as the times require.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Dou said: 'Rulers each act according to their time.

entries.zh: 自竇長君在時，竟不得侯，死後乃［封］其子彭祖顧得侯。
entries.en: While Dou Changjun was still alive, he never managed to become a marquis. It was only after his death that his son Pengzu finally received the title.
entries.literal: From when Dou Changjun was alive, ultimately could not become marquis, after death then [enfeoffed] his son Pengzu and he became marquis.

entries.zh: 吾甚恨之。
entries.en: I have always deeply regretted this.
entries.literal: I greatly resent it.

entries.zh: 帝趣侯信也！」
entries.en: Make haste and enfeoff Wang Xin!"
entries.literal: Your majesty quickly make Xin marquis!'

entries.zh: 景帝曰：「請得與丞相議之。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing replied: "Allow me to discuss the matter with the chancellor."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: 'Please allow me to discuss with the chancellor.'

entries.zh: 丞相議之，亞夫曰：「高皇帝約『非劉氏不得王，非有功不得侯。
entries.en: When the matter was put to the chancellor, Yafu replied: "Emperor Gaozu's covenant states: 'None who is not of the Liu clan may be made king; none without merit may be made marquis.
entries.literal: When the emperor consulted the chancellor, Yafu said: "Emperor Gaozu's covenant states: 'None who is not of the Liu clan may be made king; none without merit may be made marquis.

entries.zh: 不如約，天下共擊之』。
entries.en: Any who violate this covenant shall be attacked by the whole realm.'
entries.literal: If not follow the covenant, the realm together will attack them'.

entries.zh: 今信雖皇后兄，無功，侯之，非約也。」
entries.en: Now, although Wang Xin is the empress's brother, he has no merit. To make him a marquis would violate the covenant."
entries.literal: Now Xin though queen's elder brother, without merit, make him marquis, not follow the covenant."

entries.zh: 景帝默然而止。
entries.en: Emperor Jing fell silent and let the matter drop.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing was silent and stopped.

entries.zh: 以將軍從高帝擊反韓王信於代，降下霍人。
entries.en: As a general, he followed Emperor Gaozu to strike the rebel King of Han, Xin, in Dai, and accepted the surrender of the people of Huo.
entries.literal: As general followed Gaozu to strike the rebel King Han Xin in Dai, surrendered and captured Huo people.

entries.zh: 以前至武泉，擊胡騎，破之武泉北。
entries.en: Advancing ahead to Wuquan, he engaged the Xiongnu cavalry and defeated them north of the city.
entries.literal: Advancing first to Wuquan, struck Xiongnu cavalry, broke them north of Wuquan.

entries.zh: 轉攻韓信軍銅鞮，破之。
entries.en: Then he turned to attack Han Xin's army at Tongdi and defeated it.
entries.literal: Turned to attack Han Xin's army at Tongdi, broke it.

entries.zh: 還，降太原六城。
entries.en: On his return, he accepted the surrender of six cities in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Returned, surrendered six cities in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 擊韓信胡騎晉陽下，破之，下晉陽。
entries.en: Below Jinyang, he struck Han Xin's Xiongnu cavalry and defeated them, then captured the city.
entries.literal: Struck Han Xin's Xiongnu cavalry below Jinyang, broke it, captured Jinyang.

entries.zh: 後擊韓信軍於硰石，破之，追北八十里。
entries.en: Later he struck Han Xin's army at Langshi, defeated it, and pursued the fleeing enemy for eighty li.
entries.literal: Later struck Han Xin's army at Langshi, broke it, pursued the defeated for eighty li.

entries.zh: 還攻樓煩三城，因擊胡騎平城下，所將卒當馳道為多。
entries.en: Returning to Loufan, he attacked three cities, then engaged the Xiongnu cavalry below Pingcheng, commanding the largest contingent assigned to the imperial road.
entries.literal: Returned to attack three cities in Loufan, thus struck Xiongnu cavalry below Pingcheng, the troops he led facing the imperial roadway were the most numerous.

entries.zh: 勃遷為太尉。
entries.en: Bo was promoted to the office of Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Bo was promoted to Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 燕王盧綰反，勃以相國代樊噲將，擊下薊，得綰大將抵、丞相偃、守陘、太尉弱、御史大夫施，屠渾都。
entries.en: When the King of Yan, Lu Wan, rebelled, Bo, as Chancellor of State, replaced Fan Kuai in command. He attacked and captured Ji, seizing Lu Wan's Grand General Di, Chancellor Yan, Commander Xing, Grand Commandant Ruo, and Censor-in-Chief Shi, and slaughtered Hundu.
entries.literal: King Yan Lu Wan rebelled, Bo as prime minister replaced Fan Kuai as general, struck and captured Ji, obtained Wan's great general Di, chancellor Yan, guard Xing, grand commandant Ruo, censor-in-chief Shi, slaughtered Hundu.

entries.zh: 破綰軍上蘭，復擊破綰軍沮陽。
entries.en: At Shanglan, he defeated Lu Wan's army, then struck and defeated it again at Juyang.
entries.literal: Broke Wan's army at Shanglan, again struck and broke Wan's army at Juyang.

entries.zh: 追至長城，定上谷十二縣，右北平十六縣，遼西、遼東二十九縣，漁陽二十二縣。
entries.en: He pursued the enemy as far as the Great Wall, pacifying twelve counties of Shanggu, sixteen of Youbeiping, twenty-nine of Liaoxi and Liaodong, and twenty-two of Yuyang.
entries.literal: Pursued to the Great Wall, pacified Shanggu twelve counties, Youbeiping sixteen counties, Liaoxi and Liaodong twenty-nine counties, Yuyang twenty-two counties.

entries.zh: 最從高帝得相國一人，丞相二人，將軍、二千石各三人；
entries.en: In all, while following Emperor Gaozu, he captured one chancellor of state, two chancellors, and three each of generals and officials ranked at two thousand shi.
entries.literal: In all, following Gaozu, he captured one chancellor of state, two chancellors, and three each of generals and officials of two thousand shi;

entries.zh: 別破軍二，下城三，定郡五，縣七十九，得丞相、大將各一人。
entries.en: On independent campaigns, he defeated two armies, captured three cities, pacified five commanderies and seventy-nine counties, and seized one chancellor and one grand general.
entries.literal: Separately broke armies two, captured cities three, pacified commanderies five, counties seventy-nine, captured chancellor and great general each one.

entries.zh: 勃為人木彊敦厚，高帝以為可屬大事。
entries.en: Bo was by nature plain-spoken, steadfast, and honest, and Emperor Gaozu believed he could be entrusted with great affairs.
entries.literal: Bo as a person was stolid, strong, and honest, Gaozu considered him reliable for important matters.

entries.zh: 勃不好文學，每召諸生說士，東鄉坐而責之：「趣為我語。」
entries.en: Bo had no taste for letters. Whenever he summoned scholars and rhetoricians, he would sit facing east and press them: "Just speak up—tell me plainly."
entries.literal: Bo did not care for letters. Whenever he summoned scholars and persuaders, he would sit facing east and press them: "Speak to me at once."

entries.zh: 其椎少文如此。
entries.en: Such was his blunt and unrefined nature.
entries.literal: His simple lack of polish was like this.

entries.zh: 勃既定燕而歸，高祖已崩矣，以列侯事孝惠帝。
entries.en: By the time Bo pacified Yan and returned, Emperor Gaozu had already passed away. He served Emperor Hui as a marquis.
entries.literal: Bo having pacified Yan and returned, Gaozu had already passed away, served Emperor Xiaohui as a noble.

entries.zh: 孝惠帝六年，置太尉官，以勃為太尉。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign, the office of Grand Commandant was established, and Bo was appointed to it.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaohui year 6, established the office of Grand Commandant, appointed Bo as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 十歲，高后崩。
entries.en: Ten years later, Empress Dowager Gao passed away.
entries.literal: Ten years, Empress Gao passed away.

entries.zh: 呂祿以趙王為漢上將軍，呂產以呂王為漢相國，秉漢權，欲危劉氏。
entries.en: Lu Lu, as King of Zhao, became Supreme General of Han, and Lu Chan, as King of Lu, became Chancellor of State, seizing the reins of Han power and plotting to overthrow the house of Liu.
entries.literal: Lu Lu as King of Zhao became Han Supreme General, Lu Chan as King Lu became Han Chancellor, wielded Han power, wished to endanger the Liu clan.

entries.zh: 勃為太尉，不得入軍門。
entries.en: Bo, though Grand Commandant, was barred from entering the army gates.
entries.literal: Bo as Grand Commandant, could not enter the army gates.

entries.zh: 陳平為丞相，不得任事。
entries.en: Chen Ping, though Chancellor, was shut out from the conduct of affairs.
entries.literal: Chen Ping as Chancellor, could not manage affairs.

entries.zh: 於是勃與平謀，卒誅諸呂而立孝文皇帝。
entries.en: Thereupon Bo and Chen Ping conspired together and at last destroyed the entire Lu clan, establishing Emperor Wen on the throne.
entries.literal: Thus, Bo and Ping plotted, ultimately executed the various Lu and established Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 其語在呂后、孝文事中。
entries.en: The full account appears in the records of Empress Lu and Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: The conversation is in the Empress Lu and Xiaowen affairs.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：絳侯周勃始為布衣時，鄙樸人也，才能不過凡庸。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: When the Marquis of Jiang, Zhou Bo, was still a commoner, he was an unpolished rustic of no more than ordinary ability.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: Marquis Jiang Zhou Bo when beginning as commoner, was a vulgar rustic, ability no more than ordinary.

entries.zh: 及從高祖定天下，在將相位，諸呂欲作亂，勃匡國家難，復之乎正。
entries.en: Yet when he followed Emperor Gaozu to pacify the realm and rose to the rank of general and chancellor, and when the Lu clan plotted to seize power, it was Bo who saved the state in its hour of peril and restored it to the rightful course.
entries.literal: When followed Gaozu to settle the realm, in general and chancellor position, the various Lü wished to make rebellion, Bo rectified the state's difficulties, returned it to correctness.

entries.zh: 雖伊尹、周公，何以加哉！
entries.en: Even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou could scarcely have done more!
entries.literal: Even Yi Yin and Zhou Gong, what could surpass this!

entries.zh: 亞夫之用兵，持威重，執堅刃，穰苴曷有加焉！
entries.en: As for Yafu's command of armies, maintaining stern authority and wielding iron discipline, even Rangju could not have surpassed him!
entries.literal: Yafu's use of troops, held authority and weight, grasped firm blade, Rang Ju what could surpass this!

entries.zh: 足己而不學，守節不遜，終以窮困。
entries.en: Yet he was self-satisfied and unwilling to learn, unyielding in his principles to the point of obstinacy, and in the end came to ruin.
entries.literal: Satisfied with himself and unwilling to learn, he held to his principles without deference, and in the end met with ruin.

entries.zh: 悲夫！
entries.en: How tragic!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 擊陳豨，屠馬邑。
entries.en: He attacked the rebel Chen Xi and sacked Mayi.
entries.literal: Struck Chen Xi, slaughtered Maiyi.

entries.zh: 所將卒斬豨將軍乘馬絺。
entries.en: The troops under his command beheaded Chen Xi's general Chengma Chi.
entries.literal: The troops he led beheaded Xi's general Riding Horse Chi.

entries.zh: 擊韓信、陳豨、趙利軍於樓煩，破之。
entries.en: At Loufan, he engaged the combined forces of Han Xin, Chen Xi, and Zhao Li and defeated them.
entries.literal: Struck Han Xin, Chen Xi, Zhao Li's army at Loufan, broke it.

entries.zh: 得豨將宋最、鴈門守圂。
entries.en: He captured Chen Xi's general Song Zui and the Governor of Yanmen, Chou.
entries.literal: Captured Xi's generals Song Zui, Yanmen governor Chou.

entries.zh: 因轉攻得雲中守遬、丞相箕肆、將勳。
entries.en: He then turned his forces elsewhere and captured the Governor of Yunzhong, Su, along with the chancellor Ji Si and the general Xun.
entries.literal: Thus, turned to attack and captured Yunzhong governor Su, chancellor jisi, general Xun.

entries.zh: 定鴈門郡十七縣，雲中郡十二縣。
entries.en: He pacified seventeen counties of Yanmen Commandery and twelve counties of Yunzhong Commandery.
entries.literal: Pacified Yanmen commandery seventeen counties, Yunzhong commandery twelve counties.

entries.zh: 因復擊豨靈丘，破之，斬豨，得豨丞相程縱、將軍陳武、都尉高肆。
entries.en: At Lingqiu, he struck Chen Xi again, defeated him, and beheaded him, capturing his chancellor Cheng Zong, general Chen Wu, and commandant Gao Si.
entries.literal: Thus, again struck Xi at Lingqiu, broke it, beheaded Xi, captured Xi's chancellor Cheng Zong, general Chen Wu, and commandant Gao Si.

entries.zh: 定代郡九縣。
entries.en: He pacified nine counties of Dai Commandery.
entries.literal: Pacified Dai commandery nine counties.

entries.zh: 太尉既會兵滎陽，吳方攻梁，梁急，請救。
entries.en: After the Grand Commandant had assembled his forces at Xingyang, Wu was pressing its attack on Liang. Liang was in dire straits and begged for relief.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant having assembled troops at Xingyang, Wu was attacking Liang, Liang was urgent, requested rescue.

entries.zh: 太尉引兵東北走昌邑，深壁而守。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant marched his troops northeast to Changyi, where he dug in deep and held his position.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant led troops northeast to Changyi, entrenched deeply and defended.

entries.zh: 梁日使使請太尉，太尉守便宜，不肯往。
entries.en: Liang sent envoys day after day imploring the Grand Commandant, but he held firm to his strategic advantage and refused to move.
entries.literal: Liang daily sent envoys to request the Grand Commandant, the Grand Commandant held to what was advantageous, would not go.

entries.zh: 梁上書言景帝，景帝使使詔救梁。
entries.en: Liang appealed directly to Emperor Jing in a memorial, and the emperor dispatched envoys with a decree ordering the Grand Commandant to rescue Liang.
entries.literal: Liang submitted a memorial to Emperor Jing, Emperor Jing sent envoys to decree rescue Liang.

entries.zh: 太尉不奉詔，堅壁不出，而使輕騎兵弓高侯等絕吳楚兵後食道。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant declined to obey the decree. He held his entrenchments and refused to sally forth, but sent the Marquis of Gonggao with light cavalry to sever the supply lines behind the Wu and Chu forces.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant did not obey the decree, firmly entrenched without going out, but sent light cavalry general Gonggao Hou and others to cut off Wu and Chu troops' rear grain routes.

entries.zh: 吳兵乏糧，饑，數欲挑戰，終不出。
entries.en: The Wu troops ran short of provisions and grew hungry. They repeatedly tried to provoke a battle, but the Grand Commandant would not come out.
entries.literal: Wu troops lacked grain, hungry, several times wished to challenge, ultimately did not come out.

entries.zh: 夜，軍中驚，內相攻擊擾亂，至於太尉帳下。
entries.en: One night, panic swept through the camp. Soldiers attacked one another in the confusion, and the tumult reached the very entrance of the Grand Commandant's tent.
entries.literal: At night, the army was alarmed, internally attacked each other in confusion, reaching the Grand Commandant's tent.

entries.zh: 太尉終臥不起。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant remained lying down and did not rise.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant lay still without rising.

entries.zh: 頃之，復定。
entries.en: Before long, order was restored.
entries.literal: After a moment, again settled.

entries.zh: 後吳奔壁東南陬，太尉使備西北。
entries.en: Later, when the Wu forces charged toward the southeast corner of the ramparts, the Grand Commandant ordered his troops to reinforce the northwest instead.
entries.literal: Later Wu fled toward the southeast corner of the wall, the Grand Commandant had them prepare northwest.

entries.zh: 已而其精兵果奔西北，不得入。
entries.en: Sure enough, the enemy's elite forces soon rushed the northwest, but they could not break through.
entries.literal: Soon their elite troops indeed fled northwest, could not enter.

entries.zh: 吳兵既餓，乃引而去。
entries.en: The Wu troops, now starving, finally withdrew.
entries.literal: Wu troops having starved, then led away.

entries.zh: 太尉出精兵追擊，大破之。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant unleashed his elite troops in pursuit and inflicted a devastating defeat.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant sent out elite troops to pursue and strike, greatly broke them.

entries.zh: 吳王濞棄其軍，而與壯士數千人亡走，保於江南丹徒。
entries.en: The King of Wu, Bi, abandoned his army and fled with several thousand of his strongest men, taking refuge at Dantu south of the Yangtze.
entries.literal: Wu King Bi abandoned his army, and with several thousand strong men fled and ran, defended in Jiangnan Dantu.

entries.zh: 漢兵因乘勝，遂盡虜之，降其兵，購吳王千金。
entries.en: The Han forces pressed their advantage and captured every last one, accepting the surrender of the remaining troops and placing a bounty of a thousand jin of gold on the King of Wu.
entries.literal: Han troops thus took advantage of victory, completely captured them, surrendered their troops, offered thousand jin bounty for Wu King.

entries.zh: 月餘，越人斬吳王頭以告。
entries.en: Over a month later, the Yue people beheaded the King of Wu and sent his head as proof.
entries.literal: More than a month, Yue people beheaded Wu King to report.

entries.zh: 凡相攻守三月，而吳楚破平。
entries.en: In all, the campaign of attack and defense lasted three months before Wu and Chu were utterly defeated and pacified.
entries.literal: Altogether attacked and defended three months, Wu and Chu were broken and pacified.

entries.zh: 於是諸將乃以太尉計謀為是。
entries.en: The generals then acknowledged that the Grand Commandant's strategy had been right all along.
entries.literal: Thus, the generals considered the Grand Commandant's strategy correct.

entries.zh: 由此梁孝王與太尉有卻。
entries.en: From this time on, King Xiao of Liang bore a lasting grudge against the Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: From this Liang Xiaowang had resentment toward the Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 孝景三年，吳楚反。
entries.en: In the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, Wu and Chu rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing year 3, Wu and Chu rebelled.

entries.zh: 亞夫以中尉為太尉，東擊吳楚。
entries.en: Yafu was promoted from Commandant of the Capital Guard to Grand Commandant and sent east to campaign against Wu and Chu.
entries.literal: Yafu as Commandant of the Guards became Grand Commandant, east attacked Wu and Chu.

entries.zh: 因自請上曰：「楚兵剽輕，難與爭鋒。
entries.en: He personally petitioned the emperor: "The troops of Chu are swift and aggressive; it would be unwise to confront them head-on.
entries.literal: Thus, personally requested the emperor saying: 'Chu troops are fierce and swift, difficult to contend with directly.

entries.zh: 願以梁委之，絕其糧道，乃可制。」
entries.en: I ask that we let Liang absorb their attack while we cut off their supply lines; only then can we bring them under control."
entries.literal: I wish to let Liang bear their assault while we cut off their grain routes; only then can we bring them under control."

entries.zh: 上許之。
entries.en: The emperor approved the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor permitted it.

entries.zh: 孝文且崩時，誡太子曰：「即有緩急，周亞夫真可任將兵。」
entries.en: When Emperor Wen lay on his deathbed, he admonished the Crown Prince: "If ever there is an emergency, Zhou Yafu is the man you can truly entrust to command the army."
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was about to pass away, admonished the crown prince saying: 'If there is emergency, Zhou Yafu truly can be entrusted to lead troops.'

entries.zh: 文帝崩，拜亞夫為車騎將軍。
entries.en: After Emperor Wen passed away, Yafu was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen passed away, appointed Yafu as Chariot and Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 歸，復置太尉官。
entries.en: Upon his return, the office of Grand Commandant was reestablished.
entries.literal: Returned, again established the Grand Commandant office.

entries.zh: 五歲，遷為丞相，景帝甚重之。
entries.en: Five years later, he was promoted to chancellor, and Emperor Jing esteemed him greatly.
entries.literal: Five years, promoted to chancellor, Emperor Jing greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 景帝廢栗太子，丞相固爭之，不得。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing deposed Crown Prince Li, the chancellor argued strenuously against it but could not prevail.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing deposed Crown Prince Li, the chancellor firmly contended against it, could not prevail.

entries.zh: 景帝由此疏之。
entries.en: From that point on, Emperor Jing grew distant toward him.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing from this distanced him.

entries.zh: 而梁孝王每朝，常與太后言條侯之短。
entries.en: Moreover, each time King Xiao of Liang attended court, he would speak to the Empress Dowager of the Marquis of Tiao's failings.
entries.literal: Moreover, Liang Xiaowang each court audience, often spoke of Marquis Tiao's faults to the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 其後匈奴王［唯］徐盧等五人降，景帝欲侯之以勸後。
entries.en: Some time later, the Xiongnu king Xu Lu and four others surrendered. Emperor Jing wished to enfeoff them as marquises to encourage future defections.
entries.literal: Afterwards Xiongnu kings [Wei] Xu Lu and others five people surrendered, Emperor Jing wished to make them marquises to encourage later surrenders.

entries.zh: 丞相亞夫曰：「彼背其主降陛下，陛下侯之，則何以責人臣不守節者乎？」
entries.en: Chancellor Yafu objected: "These men betrayed their own lord to surrender to Your Majesty. If Your Majesty rewards them with marquisates, by what standard can you censure ministers who fail to keep faith?"
entries.literal: Chancellor Yafu said: 'They betrayed their lord and surrendered to your majesty, your majesty makes them marquises, then how to blame ministers who do not maintain loyalty?'

entries.zh: 景帝曰：「丞相議不可用。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing declared: "The chancellor's advice is unacceptable."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: 'The chancellor's counsel cannot be used.'

entries.zh: 乃悉封［唯］徐盧等為列侯。
entries.en: He proceeded to enfeoff Xu Lu and the others as marquises, every one of them.
entries.literal: Thus, all enfeoffed [Wei] Xu Lu and others as nobles.

entries.zh: 亞夫因謝病。
entries.en: Yafu thereupon pleaded illness and withdrew.
entries.literal: Yafu thus pleaded illness.

entries.zh: 景帝中三年，以病免相。
entries.en: In the middle third year of Emperor Jing's reign, he was dismissed from the chancellorship on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing middle year 3, because of illness dismissed from chancellor.

entries.zh: 頃之，景帝居禁中，召條侯，賜食。
entries.en: Not long afterward, Emperor Jing, from within the inner palace, summoned the Marquis of Tiao and offered him a meal.
entries.literal: Shortly after, Emperor Jing resided in the inner palace, summoned Marquis Tiao, granted food.

entries.zh: 獨置大胾，無切肉，又不置櫡。
entries.en: Before him was placed a single large joint of meat, but there was no knife to cut it with, nor were there any chopsticks.
entries.literal: Alone placed a large joint of meat, no knife for cutting, also did not place chopsticks.

entries.zh: 條侯心不平，顧謂尚席取櫡。
entries.en: The Marquis of Tiao was displeased. He turned and asked the steward to fetch chopsticks.
entries.literal: Marquis Tiao's heart was not at peace, turned and told the food attendant to get chopsticks.

entries.zh: 景帝視而笑曰：「此不足君所乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Jing watched and said with a smile: "Is this not enough for you?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing watched and laughed saying: 'This is not enough for sir?'

entries.zh: 條侯免冠謝。
entries.en: The Marquis of Tiao removed his cap and apologized.
entries.literal: Marquis Tiao removed his cap and apologized.

entries.zh: 上起，條侯因趨出。
entries.en: When the emperor rose, the Marquis of Tiao hastily withdrew.
entries.literal: The emperor rose, Marquis Tiao thus hurried out.

entries.zh: 景帝以目送之，曰：「此怏怏者非少主臣也！」
entries.en: Emperor Jing watched him go and remarked: "This sullen man is not one to serve a young ruler!"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing followed with his eyes, said: 'This discontented one is not a minister for a young lord!'

entries.zh: 居無何，條侯子為父買工官尚方甲楯五百被可以葬者。
entries.en: Not long after, the Marquis of Tiao's son purchased five hundred suits of armor and shields from the Imperial Workshop for use as burial goods for his father.
entries.literal: After not long, Marquis Tiao's son for father bought from the artisan office Shangfang five hundred suits of armor and shields that could be used for burial.

entries.zh: 取庸苦之，不予錢。
entries.en: He hired laborers to transport them but worked them harshly and refused to pay.
entries.literal: Took laborers to work them hard, did not give money.

entries.zh: 庸知其盜買縣官器，怒而上變告子，事連汙條侯。
entries.en: The laborers, aware that government equipment had been illicitly purchased, were enraged and reported the crime, accusing the son. The case implicated the Marquis of Tiao himself.
entries.literal: The laborers knew they were illicitly buying government equipment, angered and reported the irregularity, accusing the son, the matter implicated and defiled Marquis Tiao.

entries.zh: 書既聞上，上下吏。
entries.en: When the report reached the emperor, he ordered officials to investigate.
entries.literal: The memorial having reached the emperor, sent down officials.

entries.zh: 吏簿責條侯，條侯不對。
entries.en: The officials interrogated the Marquis of Tiao based on the charges, but the marquis refused to answer.
entries.literal: The officials interrogated Marquis Tiao according to the records, Marquis Tiao did not answer.

entries.zh: 景帝罵之曰：「吾不用也。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing rebuked him, saying: "I have no need of you."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing cursed saying: 'I will not employ you.'

entries.zh: 召詣廷尉。
entries.en: He was summoned before the Commandant of Justice.
entries.literal: Summoned to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.

entries.zh: 廷尉責曰：「君侯欲反邪？」
entries.en: The Commandant of Justice interrogated him: "Does the marquis intend to rebel?"
entries.literal: The Chamberlain for Law Enforcement interrogated saying: 'Marquis wishes to rebel?'

entries.zh: 亞夫曰：「臣所買器，乃葬器也，何謂反邪？」
entries.en: Yafu replied: "What I purchased were burial goods. How can you call that rebellion?"
entries.literal: Yafu said: "What I purchased were burial goods. How can you call that rebellion?"

entries.zh: 吏曰：「君侯縱不反地上，即欲反地下耳。」
entries.en: The officials retorted: "Even if the marquis does not intend to rebel above ground, he surely means to rebel underground."
entries.literal: The officials said: 'Even if marquis does not rebel on the earth, he wishes to rebel under the earth.'

entries.zh: 吏侵之益急。
entries.en: The officials pressed their accusations more and more harshly.
entries.literal: The officials pressed him increasingly urgently.

entries.zh: 初，吏捕條侯，條侯欲自殺，夫人止之，以故不得死，遂入廷尉。
entries.en: When the officials first came to arrest the Marquis of Tiao, he had wished to take his own life, but his wife stopped him. Unable to die, he was brought before the Commandant of Justice.
entries.literal: Initially when officials arrested Marquis Tiao, Marquis Tiao wished to commit suicide, his wife stopped him, because of this could not die, thus entered the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.

entries.zh: 因不食五日，嘔血而死。
entries.en: He refused to eat for five days, vomited blood, and died.
entries.literal: Thus, did not eat for five days, vomited blood and died.

entries.zh: 國除。
entries.en: His marquisate was abolished.
entries.literal: State abolished.

entries.zh: 絕一歲，景帝乃更封絳侯勃他子堅為平曲侯，續絳侯後。
entries.en: After a lapse of one year, Emperor Jing enfeoffed another of the Marquis of Jiang's sons, Jian, as the Marquis of Pingqu to carry on the line.
entries.literal: Cut off for one year, Emperor Jing then re-enfeoffed Marquis Jiang Bo's other son Jian as Marquis of Pingqu, continued the Marquis of Jiang's line.

entries.zh: 十九年卒，謚為共侯。
entries.en: He died after nineteen years and was given the posthumous title of Marquis Gong.
entries.literal: Nineteen years died, posthumous title Marquis Gong.

entries.zh: 子建德代侯，十三年，為太子太傅。
entries.en: His son Jiande succeeded to the marquisate. After thirteen years, he was appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Son Jiande succeeded to the marquisate, thirteen years, served as crown prince tutor.

entries.zh: 坐酎金不善，元鼎五年，有罪，國除。
entries.en: He was found guilty of presenting substandard tribute gold in the fifth year of the Yuanding era, and his marquisate was abolished.
entries.literal: Because of unsatisfactory tribute wine, Yuanding year 5, had crime, state abolished.

entries.zh: 條侯果餓死。
entries.en: The Marquis of Tiao did indeed die of starvation.
entries.literal: Marquis Tiao indeed starved to death.

entries.zh: 死後，景帝乃封王信為蓋侯。
entries.en: After his death, Emperor Jing enfeoffed Wang Xin as the Marquis of Gai.
entries.literal: After death, Emperor Jing then enfeoffed Wang Xin as Marquis of Gai.

entries.zh: 絳侯周勃者，沛人也。
entries.en: The Marquis of Jiang, Zhou Bo, was a man of Pei.
entries.literal: Marquis Jiang Zhou Bo was a native of Pei.

entries.zh: 其先卷人，徙沛。
entries.en: His forebears originally came from Juan before relocating to Pei.
entries.literal: His ancestors were from Juan, migrated to Pei.

entries.zh: 勃以織薄曲為生，常為人吹簫給喪事，材官引彊。
entries.en: Bo earned his living weaving reed mats, often played the flute at funerals, and served as a crossbowman in the local militia.
entries.literal: Bo made his living weaving reed mats, often played flute for people's funerals, served as a skilled crossbowman in the reserves.

entries.zh: 梁孝王武者，孝文皇帝子也，而與孝景帝同母。
entries.en: King Xiao of Liang, whose given name was Wu, was a son of Emperor Wen, born of the same mother as Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Liang, Liu Wu, was a son of Emperor Xiaowen, and shared the same mother as Emperor Xiaojing.

entries.zh: 母，竇太后也。
entries.en: Their mother was Empress Dowager Dou.
entries.literal: Their mother was Empress Dowager Dou.

entries.zh: 孝文帝凡四男：長子曰太子，是為孝景帝；
entries.en: Emperor Wen had four sons in all. The eldest was appointed Crown Prince and would later become Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen had four sons altogether: the eldest son was the Crown Prince, who became Emperor Xiaojing;

entries.zh: 次子武；
entries.en: The second was Wu.
entries.literal: the second son was Wu;

entries.zh: 次子參；
entries.en: The third was Can.
entries.literal: the third son was Can;

entries.zh: 次子勝。
entries.en: And the fourth was Sheng.
entries.literal: the fourth son was Sheng.

entries.zh: 孝文帝即位二年，以武為代王，以參為太原王，以勝為梁王。
entries.en: In the second year after Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Sheng as King of Liang.
entries.literal: In the second year after Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Sheng as King of Liang.

entries.zh: 二歲，徙代王為淮陽王。
entries.en: Two years later, he transferred the King of Dai to serve as King of Huaiyang.
entries.literal: Two years later, he transferred the King of Dai to be King of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 以代盡與太原王，號曰代王。
entries.en: The territory of Dai was given entirely to the King of Taiyuan, who then assumed the title King of Dai.
entries.literal: He gave all of Dai to the King of Taiyuan, who was then titled King of Dai.

entries.zh: 參立十七年，孝文後二年卒，謚為孝王。
entries.en: Can reigned for seventeen years and died in the second year of Emperor Wen's Later Reign. He was posthumously titled King Xiao.
entries.literal: Can reigned seventeen years, died in the second year of Xiaowen's Later Reign, and received the posthumous title King Xiao.

entries.zh: 子登嗣立，是為代共王。
entries.en: His son Deng succeeded him and became King Gong of Dai.
entries.literal: His son Deng succeeded him, becoming King Gong of Dai.

entries.zh: 立二十九年，元光二年卒。
entries.en: He reigned for twenty-nine years and died in the second year of the Yuanguang era.
entries.literal: He reigned twenty-nine years, died in Yuanguang year 2.

entries.zh: 子義立，是為代王。
entries.en: His son Yi succeeded him and became King of Dai.
entries.literal: His son Yi succeeded him, becoming King of Dai.

entries.zh: 十九年，漢廣關，以常山為限，而徙代王王清河。
entries.en: Nineteen years later, the Han court extended the frontier passes, setting Mount Changshan as the boundary, and transferred the King of Dai to rule over Qinghe.
entries.literal: Nineteen years later, Han expanded the passes, using Changshan as the boundary, and transferred the King of Dai to rule Qinghe.

entries.zh: 清河王徙以元鼎三年也。
entries.en: This transfer to Qinghe took place in the third year of the Yuanding era.
entries.literal: The King of Qinghe's transfer was in Yuanding year 3.

entries.zh: 其春，吳楚齊趙七國反。
entries.en: That spring, the seven kingdoms — Wu, Chu, Qi, Zhao, and the rest — rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: That spring, Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao—the seven kingdoms—rebelled.

entries.zh: 吳楚先擊梁棘壁，殺數萬人。
entries.en: Wu and Chu first struck at the fortress of Jibi in Liang, killing tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Wu and Chu first attacked Liang's Ji Wall, killing tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 梁孝王城守睢陽，而使韓安國、張羽等為大將軍，以距吳楚。
entries.en: King Xiao of Liang held fast within the walls of Suiyang, dispatching Han Anguo, Zhang Yu, and others as grand generals to resist Wu and Chu.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Liang defended the city of Suiyang, and sent Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as grand generals to resist Wu and Chu.

entries.zh: 吳楚以梁為限，不敢過而西，與太尉亞夫等相距三月。
entries.en: Wu and Chu were checked by Liang and dared not press westward, remaining locked in a standoff with Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu and his forces for three months.
entries.literal: Wu and Chu used Liang as their limit, dared not cross west, and confronted Grand Commandant Yafu and others for three months.

entries.zh: 吳楚破，而梁所破殺虜略與漢中分。
entries.en: When Wu and Chu were finally crushed, the enemy forces that Liang had routed, slain, and captured rivaled the tally of the imperial armies.
entries.literal: Wu and Chu were defeated, and Liang's captured, killed, and plundered was shared equally with Han.

entries.zh: 明年，漢立太子。
entries.en: The following year, the Han court formally established a crown prince.
entries.literal: The next year, Han established the crown prince.

entries.zh: 其後梁最親，有功，又為大國，居天下膏腴地。
entries.en: After these events, Liang stood closest to the throne in kinship, had earned great merit, and ranked among the largest kingdoms, its lands encompassing the most fertile territory in the empire.
entries.literal: Afterwards Liang was closest, had merit, was also a great kingdom, occupying the fertile lands of the realm.

entries.zh: 地北界泰山，西至高陽，四十餘城，皆多大縣。
entries.en: Its territory stretched north to Mount Tai and west to Gaoyang, comprising more than forty cities, all of them large and populous counties.
entries.literal: Its territory bordered Mount Tai in the north, reached Gaoyang in the west, over forty cities, all with many large counties.

entries.zh: 二十九年十月，梁孝王入朝。
entries.en: In the tenth month of his twenty-ninth year, King Xiao of Liang traveled to court.
entries.literal: In year twenty-nine, tenth month, Prince Xiao of Liang entered court.

entries.zh: 景帝使使持節乘輿駟馬，迎梁王於關下。
entries.en: Emperor Jing dispatched envoys bearing the imperial tally, with a chariot drawn by four horses, to welcome the King of Liang at the pass.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing sent envoys holding the tally with imperial chariot and four horses, to welcome the King of Liang at the pass.

entries.zh: 既朝，上疏因留，以太后親故。
entries.en: After attending court, he submitted a memorial requesting permission to remain in the capital, citing his close bond with the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Having attended court, he submitted a memorial requesting to remain, because of the empress dowager's close relation.

entries.zh: 王入則侍景帝同輦，出則同車游獵，射禽獸上林中。
entries.en: At court the king rode in the same carriage as Emperor Jing; abroad they hunted together, shooting birds and beasts in the Shanglin Park.
entries.literal: When the king entered he served Emperor Jing in the same chariot, when going out they rode in the same carriage hunting, shooting birds and beasts in Shanglin Park.

entries.zh: 梁之侍中、郎、謁者著籍引出入天子殿門，與漢宦官無異。
entries.en: Liang's palace attendants, gentlemen, and ushers were registered and allowed to pass freely through the gates of the Son of Heaven's palace, no differently from the Han court officials themselves.
entries.literal: Liang's attendants-in-ordinary, gentlemen, and ushers were registered and led in and out of the Son of Heaven's palace gates, no different from Han eunuchs.

entries.zh: 初，武為淮陽王十年，而梁王勝卒，謚為梁懷王。
entries.en: Earlier, Wu had served as King of Huaiyang for ten years when the King of Liang, Sheng, died and was posthumously titled King Huai of Liang.
entries.literal: Initially, Wu served as King of Huaiyang for ten years, while the King of Liang Sheng died, posthumous title King Huai of Liang.

entries.zh: 懷王最少子，愛幸異於他子。
entries.en: King Huai had been the youngest son and was loved and favored far more than his brothers.
entries.literal: King Huai was the youngest son, loved and favored differently from the other sons.

entries.zh: 其明年，徙淮陽王武為梁王。
entries.en: The following year, the King of Huaiyang, Wu, was transferred to become King of Liang.
entries.literal: The next year, he transferred the King of Huaiyang Wu to be King of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁王之初王梁，孝文帝之十二年也。
entries.en: The King of Liang first received his fief in the twelfth year of Emperor Wen's reign.
entries.literal: The King of Liang's first enfeoffment in Liang was in Emperor Xiaowen's twelfth year.

entries.zh: 梁王自初王通歷已十一年矣。
entries.en: By this time, the King of Liang had already held a royal title for eleven years since his first enfeoffment.
entries.literal: The King of Liang, from his initial enfeoffment to now, had experienced eleven years.

entries.zh: 三十五年冬，復朝。
entries.en: In the winter of his thirty-fifth year, he again traveled to court.
entries.literal: In year thirty-five, winter, he attended court again.

entries.zh: 上疏欲留，上弗許。
entries.en: He petitioned to remain in the capital, but the emperor refused.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial desiring to remain, the emperor did not permit.

entries.zh: 歸國，意忽忽不樂。
entries.en: He returned to his kingdom in a state of restless melancholy.
entries.literal: Returned to his fief, his thoughts were melancholy and unhappy.

entries.zh: 北獵良山，有獻牛，足出背上，孝王惡之。
entries.en: While hunting in the north at Mount Liang, someone presented him with a monstrous ox whose legs protruded from its back. King Xiao took this as an evil omen.
entries.literal: He hunted north at Liangshan, someone presented a cow whose feet came out its back, Prince Xiao considered it ominous.

entries.zh: 六月中，病熱，六日卒，謚曰孝王。
entries.en: In the middle of the sixth month, he fell ill with a fever and died after six days. He was posthumously titled King Xiao.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, he fell ill with fever, died after six days, posthumous title Prince Xiao.

entries.zh: 孝王，竇太后少子也，愛之，賞賜不可勝道。
entries.en: King Xiao was the youngest son of Empress Dowager Dou, who loved him dearly and showered him with gifts and rewards beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao was Empress Dowager Dou's youngest son, she loved him, rewards and grants beyond counting.

entries.zh: 於是孝王筑東苑，方三百餘里。
entries.en: King Xiao built the Eastern Park, which stretched more than three hundred li on each side.
entries.literal: Thus, Prince Xiao built the Eastern Park, covering over three hundred li square.

entries.zh: 廣睢陽城七十里。
entries.en: He expanded the walls of Suiyang by seventy li.
entries.literal: He expanded Suiyang city seventy li.

entries.zh: 大治宮室，為複道，自宮連屬於平臺三十餘里。
entries.en: He built grand palaces and constructed covered walkways that ran from the palace to the Terrace, extending more than thirty li without interruption.
entries.literal: He greatly constructed palaces, built covered walkways connecting from the palace to the Platform for over thirty li.

entries.zh: 得賜天子旌旗，出從千乘萬騎。
entries.en: He was granted the imperial banners of the Son of Heaven, and when he went abroad, a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen followed in his train.
entries.literal: He received the emperor's banners and flags as grants, went out followed by a thousand chariots and ten thousand cavalry.

entries.zh: 東西馳獵，擬於天子。
entries.en: He hunted east and west in a splendor rivaling that of the Son of Heaven himself.
entries.literal: He galloped hunting east and west, comparable to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 出言蹕，入言警。
entries.en: When he went abroad, heralds cried 'Clear the way!' and when he returned, they called 'Be alert!'
entries.literal: When going out he used 'clear the way,' when entering he used 'be alert.'

entries.zh: 招延四方豪桀，自山以東游說之士。
entries.en: He recruited heroes and men of talent from every quarter, as well as itinerant persuaders from east of the mountains.
entries.literal: He recruited and welcomed heroes and outstanding men from the four directions, wandering persuaders from east of the mountains.

entries.zh: 莫不畢至，齊人羊勝、公孫詭、鄒陽之屬。
entries.en: All of them flocked to his court — men of Qi such as Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and Zou Yang.
entries.literal: None failed to arrive completely—men from Qi like Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, Zou Yang and such.

entries.zh: 公孫詭多奇邪計，初見王，賜千金，官至中尉，梁號之曰公孫將軍，梁多作兵器弩弓矛數十萬，而府庫金錢且百巨萬，珠玉寶器多於京師。
entries.en: Gongsun Gui was a man of many cunning and unorthodox schemes. At his first audience with the king, he was granted a thousand catties of gold, and his rank rose to Commandant of the Capital. In Liang, he was known as General Gongsun. The kingdom manufactured hundreds of thousands of weapons — crossbows, bows, and spears — while its treasury held nearly a hundred million in gold and cash, and its pearls, jade, and precious objects exceeded those of the imperial capital.
entries.literal: Gongsun Gui had many strange and crooked schemes, first meeting the king, granted a thousand jin, office reaching Commandant of the Guards, Liang titled him General Gongsun, Liang made many weapons—crossbows, bows, spears—several tens of thousands, while the treasury had gold and cash nearly a hundred million, pearls, jade, and precious objects more than the capital.

entries.zh: 梁孝王長子買為梁王，是為共王；
entries.en: King Xiao's eldest son, Mai, became King of Liang — he was King Gong.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao's eldest son Mai became King of Liang, this was King Gong;

entries.zh: 子明為濟川王；
entries.en: His son Ming became King of Jichuan.
entries.literal: son Ming became King of Jichuan;

entries.zh: 子彭離為濟東王；
entries.en: His son Pengli became King of Jidong.
entries.literal: son Pengli became King of Jidong;

entries.zh: 子定為山陽王；
entries.en: His son Ding became King of Shanyang.
entries.literal: son Ding became King of Shanyang;

entries.zh: 子不識為濟陰王。
entries.en: And his son Bushi became King of Jiyin.
entries.literal: son Bushi became King of Jiyin.

entries.zh: 孝王慈孝，每聞太后病，口不能食，居不安寢，常欲留長安侍太后。
entries.en: King Xiao was devoted and filial. Whenever he heard that the Empress Dowager was ill, he could not eat and could not sleep, always wishing to remain in Chang'an to attend her in person.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao was filial and kind, whenever he heard the empress dowager was ill, could not eat, lived and slept restlessly, constantly wished to remain in Chang'an serving the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 太后亦愛之。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager loved him dearly in return.
entries.literal: The empress dowager also loved him.

entries.zh: 及聞梁王薨，竇太后哭極哀，不食，曰：「帝果殺吾子！」
entries.en: When she learned that the King of Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou wept inconsolably, refused to eat, and cried, "The emperor has truly killed my son!"
entries.literal: When she heard the King of Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou cried extremely mournfully, did not eat, said: 'The emperor indeed killed my son!'

entries.zh: 景帝哀懼，不知所為。
entries.en: Emperor Jing was stricken with grief and fear, at a loss for what to do.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing was sorrowful and fearful, did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 與長公主計之，乃分梁為五國，盡立孝王男五人為王，女五人皆食湯沐邑。
entries.en: He consulted with the Grand Princess, and together they divided Liang into five kingdoms, enfeoffing all five of King Xiao's sons as kings. His five daughters were each granted revenue from a bathing fief.
entries.literal: Consulted with the eldest princess, then divided Liang into five kingdoms, all enfeoffing Prince Xiao's five sons as kings, five daughters all received bath and grooming fiefs.

entries.zh: 於是奏之太后，太后乃說，為帝加壹湌 。
entries.en: When this plan was reported to the Empress Dowager, she was pleased and took an extra meal for the emperor's sake.
entries.literal: Thus, memorialized to the empress dowager, the empress dowager then was pleased, added one extra meal for the emperor.

entries.zh: 梁平王襄十四年，母曰陳太后。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of King Ping of Liang, Xiang — his mother was known as Empress Dowager Chen.
entries.literal: Liang King Ping Xiang's fourteenth year, his mother was called Empress Dowager Chen.

entries.zh: 共王母曰李太后。
entries.en: King Gong's mother was known as Empress Dowager Li.
entries.literal: King Gong's mother was called Empress Dowager Li.

entries.zh: 李太后，親平王之大母也。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Li was in fact King Ping's grandmother.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Li was King Ping's paternal grandmother.

entries.zh: 而平王之后姓任，曰任王后。
entries.en: King Ping's queen bore the surname Ren and was known as Queen Ren.
entries.literal: And King Ping's queen was surnamed Ren, called Queen Ren.

entries.zh: 任王后甚有寵於平王襄。
entries.en: Queen Ren was greatly favored by King Ping.
entries.literal: Queen Ren was greatly favored by King Ping Xiang.

entries.zh: 初，孝王在時，有罍樽，直千金。
entries.en: In earlier times, when King Xiao was still alive, the house possessed a ceremonial wine vessel worth a thousand catties of gold.
entries.literal: Initially, when Prince Xiao was alive, there was a lei zun vessel, worth a thousand jin.

entries.zh: 孝王誡後世，善保罍樽，無得以與人。
entries.en: King Xiao had left strict instructions to his descendants to guard this vessel well and never give it away.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao admonished later generations to carefully preserve the lei zun, not to give it to anyone.

entries.zh: 任王后聞而欲得罍樽。
entries.en: Queen Ren heard of it and coveted the vessel.
entries.literal: Queen Ren heard and desired to obtain the lei zun.

entries.zh: 平王大母李太后曰：「先王有命，無得以罍樽與人。
entries.en: King Ping's grandmother, Empress Dowager Li, declared, "The former king left explicit orders that the vessel must not be given to anyone.
entries.literal: King Ping's paternal grandmother Empress Dowager Li said: 'The former king had commands, not to give the lei zun to anyone.

entries.zh: 他物雖百巨萬，猶自恣也。」
entries.en: As for other treasures, even those worth a hundred million, you may dispose of them as you please."
entries.literal: Other things though a hundred million, still at your own discretion.'

entries.zh: 任王后絕欲得之。
entries.en: But Queen Ren was determined to have it.
entries.literal: Queen Ren absolutely desired to obtain it.

entries.zh: 平王襄直使人開府取罍樽，賜任王后。
entries.en: King Ping simply ordered his men to open the treasury, remove the vessel, and present it to Queen Ren.
entries.literal: King Ping Xiang directly sent men to open the treasury and take the lei zun, granting it to Queen Ren.

entries.zh: 李太后大怒，漢使者來，欲自言，平王襄及任王后遮止，閉門，李太后與爭門，措指，遂不得見漢使者。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Li was furious. When the Han envoys arrived, she wished to speak with them herself, but King Ping and Queen Ren barred her way and shut the gates. The Empress Dowager struggled at the doors and had her finger caught and crushed in them, and in the end was prevented from seeing the Han envoys.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Li greatly angered, Han envoys came, wished to speak herself, King Ping Xiang and Queen Ren blocked and stopped her, closed the gate, Empress Dowager Li contended at the gate, her finger was pinched, thus could not see the Han envoys.

entries.zh: 李太后亦私與食官長及郎中尹霸等士通亂，而王與任王后以此使人風止李太后，李太后內有淫行，亦已。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Li had also been carrying on illicit affairs with the Chief of the Food Office and the Gentleman-in-Attendance Yin Ba, among others. The king and Queen Ren used this knowledge to send people to silence her, and since the Empress Dowager was compromised by her own misconduct, the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Li also privately had illicit relations with the food official chief and Gentleman-in-Attendance Yin Ba and other scholars, while the king and Queen Ren used this to send people to warn and stop Empress Dowager Li, Empress Dowager Li internally had lewd conduct, and that was all.

entries.zh: 後病薨。
entries.en: Later she fell ill and died.
entries.literal: Later she fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 病時，任后未嘗請病；
entries.en: During her illness, Queen Ren never once inquired after her health.
entries.literal: When ill, Queen Ren never inquired about the illness;

entries.zh: 薨，又不持喪。
entries.en: When she died, the queen did not observe the mourning rites.
entries.literal: When she died, moreover did not observe mourning.

entries.zh: 其夏四月，上立膠東王為太子。
entries.en: That summer, in the fourth month, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince.
entries.literal: That summer, fourth month, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince.

entries.zh: 梁王怨袁盎及議臣，乃與羊勝、公孫詭之屬陰使人刺殺袁盎及他議臣十餘人。
entries.en: The King of Liang harbored a deep grudge against Yuan Ang and the other ministers who had spoken against him. Together with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and their associates, he secretly dispatched assassins who murdered Yuan Ang and more than ten of the other ministers who had advised against the succession.
entries.literal: The King of Liang resented Yuan Ang and the discussing ministers, so secretly sent men with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others to assassinate Yuan Ang and more than ten other discussing ministers.

entries.zh: 逐其賊，未得也。
entries.en: The authorities pursued the assassins but failed to apprehend them.
entries.literal: They pursued the assassins, did not catch them.

entries.zh: 於是天子意梁王，逐賊，果梁使之。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven suspected the King of Liang, and when the assassins were tracked down, it was indeed confirmed that Liang had sent them.
entries.literal: Thus, the Son of Heaven suspected the King of Liang, pursuing the assassins—indeed it was Liang who sent them.

entries.zh: 乃遣使冠蓋相望於道，覆按梁，捕公孫詭、羊勝。
entries.en: He dispatched envoys in such numbers that their carriages stretched in an unbroken line along the road, to investigate Liang and arrest Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
entries.literal: Thus, he sent envoys with coronets and canopies meeting each other on the road, to investigate Liang, arresting Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.

entries.zh: 公孫詭、羊勝匿王後宮。
entries.en: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng hid within the king's inner palace.
entries.literal: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng hid in the king's rear palace.

entries.zh: 使者責二千石急，梁相軒丘豹及內史韓安國進諫王，王乃令勝、詭皆自殺，出之。
entries.en: The imperial envoys pressed Liang's senior officials relentlessly. The Chancellor of Liang, Xuanqiu Bao, and the Chamberlain Han Anguo went before the king to remonstrate. At last the king ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to take their own lives, and their bodies were handed over.
entries.literal: The envoys pressed the two thousand shi officials urgently, Liang chancellor Xuanqiu Bao and Chamberlain Han Anguo advanced to remonstrate with the king, the king then ordered Sheng and Gui both to commit suicide, and handed them out.

entries.zh: 上由此怨望於梁王。
entries.en: From this point on, the emperor bore a lasting resentment toward the King of Liang.
entries.literal: The emperor from this resented and distrusted the King of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁王恐，乃使韓安國因長公主謝罪太后，然后得釋。
entries.en: The King of Liang, now fearful, sent Han Anguo to intercede through the Grand Princess and beg the Empress Dowager's forgiveness. Only then was the matter set aside.
entries.literal: The King of Liang feared, so sent Han Anguo through the eldest princess to apologize to the empress dowager, then was released.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：梁孝王雖以親愛之故，王膏腴之地，然會漢家隆盛，百姓殷富，故能植其財貨，廣宮室，車服擬於天子。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: King Xiao of Liang was granted fertile lands because of the close affection he enjoyed. Yet he was able to amass such wealth, expand his palaces, and adopt carriages and robes rivaling those of the Son of Heaven only because his reign coincided with the flourishing of the Han dynasty. At that time, the common people were prosperous and well-off.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: Though Prince Xiao of Liang because of close affection was enfeoffed with fertile lands, yet meeting when the Han house was flourishing, people wealthy, thus could accumulate his wealth, expand palaces, carriages and robes comparable to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 然亦僭矣。
entries.en: Even so, this was presumptuous indeed.
entries.literal: Yet it was also presumptuous.

entries.zh: 梁王十四年，入朝。
entries.en: In his fourteenth year, the King of Liang traveled to the capital for a court audience.
entries.literal: In the King of Liang's fourteenth year, he entered court.

entries.zh: 十七年，十八年，比年入朝，留，其明年，乃之國。
entries.en: In his seventeenth and eighteenth years, he attended court in consecutive years and stayed on, returning to his kingdom only the following year.
entries.literal: In years seventeen and eighteen, he entered court consecutively, remained, and only the next year returned to his fief.

entries.zh: 二十一年，入朝。
entries.en: In his twenty-first year, he again attended court.
entries.literal: In year twenty-one, he entered court.

entries.zh: 二十二年，孝文帝崩。
entries.en: In his twenty-second year, Emperor Wen passed away.
entries.literal: In year twenty-two, Emperor Xiaowen passed away.

entries.zh: 二十四年，入朝。
entries.en: In his twenty-fourth year, he attended court.
entries.literal: In year twenty-four, he entered court.

entries.zh: 二十五年，復入朝。
entries.en: In his twenty-fifth year, he attended court once more.
entries.literal: In year twenty-five, he entered court again.

entries.zh: 是時上未置太子也。
entries.en: At that time, the emperor had not yet designated a crown prince.
entries.literal: At this time the emperor had not yet established a crown prince.

entries.zh: 上與梁王燕飲，嘗從容言曰：「千秋萬歲後傳於王。」
entries.en: During a private banquet with the King of Liang, the emperor once remarked casually, "When I am gone, I shall pass the throne to you."
entries.literal: The emperor and the King of Liang were feasting together, and the emperor once said casually, "After a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, I shall pass the throne to you."

entries.zh: 王辭謝。
entries.en: The king politely declined.
entries.literal: The king declined politely.

entries.zh: 雖知非至言，然心內喜。
entries.en: Though he knew the words were not meant in earnest, he was secretly delighted.
entries.literal: Though he knew these were not serious words, in his heart he was inwardly pleased.

entries.zh: 太后亦然。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager felt the same.
entries.literal: The empress dowager was the same.

entries.zh: 十一月，上廢栗太子，竇太后心欲以孝王為後嗣。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, the emperor deposed Crown Prince Li. Empress Dowager Dou secretly wished to make King Xiao the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor deposed Crown Prince Li, Empress Dowager Dou's heart wished to make Prince Xiao the successor.

entries.zh: 大臣及袁盎等有所關說於景帝，竇太后義格，亦遂不復言以梁王為嗣事由此。
entries.en: The great ministers and Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Jing. Empress Dowager Dou, moved by considerations of propriety, relented and from that point on never again raised the matter of making the King of Liang the heir.
entries.literal: The ministers and Yuan Ang and others remonstrated with Emperor Jing. Empress Dowager Dou, restrained by considerations of propriety, relented and from that point no longer spoke of making the King of Liang the successor.

entries.zh: 以事秘，世莫知。
