entries.en: Because the affair was kept secret, the world at large knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: Because the matter was secret, the world did not know.

entries.zh: 乃辭歸國。
entries.en: The king then took his leave and returned to his kingdom.
entries.literal: So he took leave and returned home.

entries.zh: 上怒稍解，因上書請朝。
entries.en: When the emperor's anger had subsided somewhat, the king submitted a memorial requesting permission to attend court.
entries.literal: The emperor's anger slightly eased, thus he submitted a memorial requesting to attend court.

entries.zh: 既至關，茅蘭說王，使乘布車，從兩騎入，匿於長公主園。
entries.en: When they reached the pass, Mao Lan advised the king to ride in a plain cloth-covered cart, enter with only two horsemen as escort, and conceal himself in the Grand Princess's garden.
entries.literal: Having reached the pass, Mao Lan advised the king to ride a cloth carriage, enter following two riders, hide in the eldest princess's garden.

entries.zh: 漢使使迎王，王已入關，車騎盡居外，不知王處。
entries.en: The Han court sent envoys to welcome the king, but he had already slipped through the pass. His chariots and cavalry were all left outside, and no one knew where the king had gone.
entries.literal: Han sent envoys to welcome the king, the king had already entered the pass, chariots and cavalry all stayed outside, did not know the king's location.

entries.zh: 太后泣曰：「帝殺吾子！」
entries.en: The Empress Dowager wept and cried, "The emperor has killed my son!"
entries.literal: The empress dowager wept saying: 'The emperor has killed my son!'

entries.zh: 景帝憂恐。
entries.en: Emperor Jing was deeply alarmed.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing was worried and fearful.

entries.zh: 於是梁王伏斧質於闕下，謝罪，然後太后、景帝大喜，相泣，復如故。
entries.en: The King of Liang then appeared before the palace gate, prostrating himself beside the executioner's axe and block to beg forgiveness for his crimes. The Empress Dowager and Emperor Jing were overjoyed, wept together, and all was restored as before.
entries.literal: Thus, the King of Liang prostrated himself with axe and block at the palace gate, apologized for his crimes, then the empress dowager and Emperor Jing greatly rejoiced, wept together, restored as before.

entries.zh: 悉召王從官入關。
entries.en: All the king's attendants and retinue were then summoned through the pass.
entries.literal: He then summoned all of the king's attendants and retinue into the pass.

entries.zh: 然景帝益疏王，不同車輦矣。
entries.en: Yet from that time on, Emperor Jing grew increasingly distant from the king and no longer shared a carriage with him.
entries.literal: Yet Emperor Jing increasingly distanced the king, no longer rode in the same chariot.

entries.zh: 孝王未死時，財以巨萬計，不可勝數。
entries.en: Before King Xiao died, his wealth was reckoned in the tens of millions, too vast to count.
entries.literal: Before Prince Xiao died, his wealth was counted in millions, beyond numbering.

entries.zh: 及死，藏府餘黃金尚四十餘萬斤，他財物稱是。
entries.en: At his death, the treasury still held more than four hundred thousand catties of gold, and his other possessions were proportionate.
entries.literal: When he died, the treasury still had over 400,000 jin of yellow gold remaining, other valuables matched this.

entries.zh: 濟川王明者，梁孝王子，以桓邑侯孝景中六年為濟川王。
entries.en: King Ming of Jichuan was a son of King Xiao. Formerly the Marquis of Huanyi, he was made King of Jichuan in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: King Ming of Jichuan was Prince Xiao's son, as Marquis of Huanyi in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Jichuan.

entries.zh: 七歲，坐射殺其中尉，漢有司請誅，天子弗忍誅，廢明為庶人。
entries.en: After seven years, he was convicted of shooting and killing his Commandant of the Capital. The Han officials petitioned for his execution, but the Son of Heaven could not bring himself to carry it out and instead deposed Ming to the status of a commoner.
entries.literal: Seven years, because he shot and killed his commandery lieutenant, Han officials requested execution, the Son of Heaven could not bear to execute, deposed Ming as commoner.

entries.zh: 遷房陵，地入于漢為郡。
entries.en: He was exiled to Fangling, and his territory was absorbed into the Han empire as a commandery.
entries.literal: Relocated to Fangling, the land entered Han as a commandery.

entries.zh: 濟東王彭離者，梁孝王子，以孝景中六年為濟東王。
entries.en: King Pengli of Jidong was a son of King Xiao who was made King of Jidong in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: King Pengli of Jidong was Prince Xiao's son, in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Jidong.

entries.zh: 二十九年，彭離驕悍，無人君禮，昏暮私與其奴、亡命少年數十人行剽殺人，取財物以為好。
entries.en: Over twenty-nine years, Pengli grew arrogant and savage, heedless of the deportment expected of a ruler. Under cover of darkness, he would steal out with his slaves and bands of fugitive youths, dozens strong, to rob and murder travelers, taking their goods for his amusement.
entries.literal: Twenty-nine years, Pengli was arrogant and fierce, without ruler's ritual, at dusk privately went with his slaves and fugitive youths several dozen people to plunder and kill people, taking wealth as pleasure.

entries.zh: 所殺發覺者百餘人，國皆知之，莫敢夜行。
entries.en: More than a hundred murders were eventually discovered. Everyone in the kingdom knew of his crimes, and no one dared travel after dark.
entries.literal: Those killed and discovered were over a hundred people, the kingdom all knew it, none dared travel at night.

entries.zh: 所殺者子上書言。
entries.en: The son of one of his victims submitted a memorial denouncing him.
entries.literal: The son of one who was killed submitted a memorial to report.

entries.zh: 漢有司請誅，上不忍，廢以為庶人，遷上庸，地入于漢，為大河郡。
entries.en: The Han officials again petitioned for execution, but the emperor could not bring himself to agree. Pengli was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Shangyong. His territory was absorbed into the Han empire as the Commandery of Dahe.
entries.literal: Han officials requested execution, the emperor could not bear it, deposed as commoner, relocated to Shangyong, land entered Han, became Dahe commandery.

entries.zh: 山陽哀王定者，梁孝王子，以孝景中六年為山陽王。
entries.en: King Ai of Shanyang, whose name was Ding, was a son of King Xiao. He was made King of Shanyang in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: King Ai Ding of Shanyang was Prince Xiao's son, in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Shanyang.

entries.zh: 九年卒，無子，國除，地入于漢，為山陽郡。
entries.en: He died after nine years on the throne, leaving no heir. The kingdom was abolished, and its territory was absorbed into the Han empire as the Commandery of Shanyang.
entries.literal: Nine years died, no son, kingdom abolished, land entered Han, became Shanyang commandery.

entries.zh: 濟陰哀王不識者，梁孝王子，以孝景中六年為濟陰王。
entries.en: King Ai of Jiyin, whose name was Bushi, was a son of King Xiao. He was made King of Jiyin in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: King Ai Bushi of Jiyin was Prince Xiao's son, in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Jiyin.

entries.zh: 一歲卒，無子，國除，地入于漢，為濟陰郡。
entries.en: He died after only one year, leaving no heir. The kingdom was abolished, and its territory was absorbed into the Han empire as the Commandery of Jiyin.
entries.literal: One year died, no son, kingdom abolished, land entered Han, became Jiyin commandery.

entries.zh: 褚先生曰：臣為郎時，聞之於宮殿中老郎吏好事者稱道之也。
entries.en: Master Chu says: When I served as a Gentleman at court, I heard this tale from old officials in the palace halls who were fond of recounting such stories.
entries.literal: Master Chu says: When your servant was a gentleman, heard it from old gentleman officials in the palace halls who liked history relating it.

entries.zh: 竊以為令梁孝王怨望，欲為不善者，事從中生。
entries.en: I believe that the resentment that drove King Xiao of Liang to contemplate wrongdoing arose from within the court itself.
entries.literal: I privately consider that causing Prince Xiao of Liang to resent and wish to do evil, the matter arose from within.

entries.zh: 今太后，女主也，以愛少子故，欲令梁王為太子。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager, a woman wielding power, wished out of love for her youngest son to make the King of Liang the crown prince.
entries.literal: Now the empress dowager is a female ruler, because she loved the youngest son, wished to make the King of Liang crown prince.

entries.zh: 大臣不時正言其不可狀，阿意治小，私說意以受賞賜，非忠臣也。
entries.en: The great ministers failed to speak up forthrightly against this impropriety at the proper time. Instead, they flattered and dealt in trivialities, whispering agreeable words in hopes of rewards — the behavior not of loyal ministers.
entries.literal: Ministers did not timely correctly speak of the impropriety, flattered and handled trifles, privately spoke pleasing words to receive rewards and grants, not loyal ministers.

entries.zh: 齊如魏其侯竇嬰之正言也，何以有後禍？
entries.en: Had they all spoken as forthrightly as the Marquis of Weiqi, Dou Ying, what later calamity could have arisen?
entries.literal: How like Marquis Weiqi Dou Ying's correct speech—what future calamity would there be?

entries.zh: 景帝與王燕見，侍太后飲，景帝曰：「千秋萬歲之後傳王。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing and the king attended a banquet together, serving the Empress Dowager wine. Emperor Jing said, "When I am gone, I shall pass the throne to you."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing and the king attended a banquet, serving the Empress Dowager wine. Emperor Jing said, "After a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, I shall pass the throne to you."

entries.zh: 太后喜說。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was overjoyed.
entries.literal: The empress dowager was pleased and happy.

entries.zh: 竇嬰在前，據地言曰：「漢法之約，傳子適孫，今帝何以得傳弟，擅亂高帝約乎！」
entries.en: But Dou Ying stepped forward, struck the ground, and declared, "The covenant of Han law mandates succession from father to son and grandson. How can the emperor pass the throne to his brother and recklessly violate the compact established by Emperor Gaozu!"
entries.literal: Dou Ying was in front, struck the ground and said: 'The Han law's covenant is to pass to son and grandson, now how can the emperor pass to younger brother, arbitrarily disrupt Gaozu's covenant!'

entries.zh: 於是景帝默然無聲。
entries.en: Emperor Jing fell silent.
entries.literal: Thus, Emperor Jing was silent without sound.

entries.zh: 太后意不說。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was displeased.
entries.literal: The empress dowager's intent was displeased.

entries.zh: 故成王與小弱弟立樹下，取一桐葉以與之，曰：「吾用封汝。」
entries.en: In ancient times, King Cheng of Zhou stood with his young brother beneath a tree, plucked a paulownia leaf, and said, "With this I shall enfeoff you."
entries.literal: Thus, King Cheng stood with his young weak brother under a tree, took one paulownia leaf and gave it to him, saying: 'I will use this to enfeoff you.'

entries.zh: 周公聞之，進見曰：「天王封弟，甚善。」
entries.en: When the Duke of Zhou heard of this, he came forward and said, "The Son of Heaven has enfeoffed his younger brother — this is most excellent."
entries.literal: When the Duke of Zhou heard of it, he came forward and said, "The Son of Heaven has enfeoffed his younger brother — this is excellent."

entries.zh: 成王曰：「吾直與戲耳。」
entries.en: King Cheng replied, "I was only playing."
entries.literal: King Cheng said: 'I was just playing with him.'

entries.zh: 周公曰：「人主無過舉，不當有戲言，言之必行之。」
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou said, "A ruler must make no careless gesture and speak no idle word. What the ruler says, he must carry out."
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou said: 'A ruler has no erroneous actions, should not have joking words—words spoken must be carried out.'

entries.zh: 於是乃封小弟以應縣。
entries.en: And so the young brother was indeed enfeoffed with the district of Ying.
entries.literal: Thus, he enfeoffed the young brother with Ying county.

entries.zh: 是後成王沒齒不敢有戲言，言必行之。
entries.en: From that day forward, King Cheng never dared to speak in jest for the rest of his life; every word he uttered, he carried out.
entries.literal: After this King Cheng to the end of his life dared not have joking words, words spoken must be carried out.

entries.zh: 《孝經》曰：「非法不言，非道不行。」
entries.en: The Classic of Filial Piety says, "Speak nothing that is contrary to propriety; do nothing that is contrary to the Way."
entries.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Do not speak what is not according to law, do not act what is not according to the Way.'

entries.zh: 此聖人之法言也。
entries.en: These are the guiding words of the sages.
entries.literal: This is the legal words of the sages.

entries.zh: 今主上不宜出好言於梁王。
entries.en: The sovereign should never have spoken such encouraging words to the King of Liang.
entries.literal: Now the sovereign should not speak favorable words to the King of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁王上有太后之重，驕蹇日久，數聞景帝好言，千秋萬世之後傳王，而實不行。
entries.en: The King of Liang, backed by the Empress Dowager's formidable influence, had long grown arrogant and willful. He had repeatedly heard Emperor Jing's promise that the throne would pass to him after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, yet this promise was never fulfilled.
entries.literal: The King of Liang above has the empress dowager's weight, arrogant and willful for a long time, repeatedly heard Emperor Jing's favorable words that after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years he would pass to the king, yet in reality not carried out.

entries.zh: 又諸侯王朝見天子，漢法凡當四見耳。
entries.en: Furthermore, when feudal kings attend court before the Son of Heaven, Han law prescribes only four audiences in all.
entries.literal: Moreover, feudal lords' kings attending court to see the Son of Heaven, Han law generally should be four audiences.

entries.zh: 始到，入小見；
entries.en: Upon first arriving, there is an informal audience.
entries.literal: First arrival, enter for small audience;

entries.zh: 到正月朔旦，奉皮薦璧玉賀正月，法見；
entries.en: On New Year's Day, the king presents leather, recommends jade discs, and offers congratulations at a formal audience.
entries.literal: Arrive at New Year's first dawn, present leather and recommend jade discs to congratulate New Year, formal audience;

entries.zh: 後三日，為王置酒，賜金錢財物；
entries.en: Three days later, a banquet is held in the king's honor, and he is presented with gifts of gold, money, and valuables.
entries.literal: Three days later, set wine for the king, grant gold money and valuables;

entries.zh: 後二日，復入小見，辭去。
entries.en: Two days after that, there is a final informal audience, after which the king takes his leave and departs.
entries.literal: Two days later, again enter for small audience, take leave and depart.

entries.zh: 凡留長安不過二十日。
entries.en: In total, the stay in Chang'an should not exceed twenty days.
entries.literal: Altogether remaining in Chang'an not over twenty days.

entries.zh: 小見者，燕見於禁門內，飲於省中，非士人所得入也。
entries.en: The informal audience is a private meeting within the palace gates, with drinking in the inner chambers — a privilege not extended to ordinary scholars.
entries.literal: Small audience means banquet meeting within the forbidden gates, drinking in the administration quarters, not where scholars can enter.

entries.zh: 今梁王西朝，因留，且半歲。
entries.en: Yet the King of Liang came west to court and stayed on for nearly half a year.
entries.literal: Now the King of Liang comes west to court, thus stays, nearly half a year.

entries.zh: 入與人主同輦，出與同車。
entries.en: At court, he rode in the same carriage as the emperor, and abroad he shared the emperor's chariot.
entries.literal: When entering court he rode in the same carriage as the ruler; when going abroad he rode in the same chariot.

entries.zh: 示風以大言而實不與，令出怨言，謀畔逆，乃隨而憂之，不亦遠乎！
entries.en: To make grand promises in word while refusing to deliver in deed, thereby provoking resentment and scheming, and then to follow up with anxiety over the consequences — is this not the height of shortsightedness!
entries.literal: To hold out great promises in word yet in deed not deliver, thereby provoking resentment and plotting rebellion and treason, and then afterward to fret over it — is this not utterly perverse!

entries.zh: 非大賢人，不知退讓。
entries.en: Only a person of the highest virtue knows when to yield and step back.
entries.literal: If not a great worthy person, does not know yielding and retreating.

entries.zh: 今漢之儀法，朝見賀正月者，常一王與四侯俱朝見，十餘歲一至。
entries.en: Under Han ritual protocol, those attending the New Year court audience are normally one king and four marquises at a time, and each comes only once every ten or more years.
entries.literal: Now Han's ritual law, those attending court and congratulating New Year, normally one king with four marquises together attend court, once every ten or more years.

entries.zh: 今梁王常比年入朝見，久留。
entries.en: Yet the King of Liang attended court year after year and stayed for prolonged periods.
entries.literal: Now the King of Liang constantly attends court consecutively, stays long.

entries.zh: 鄙語曰「驕子不孝」，非惡言也。
entries.en: The common saying goes, "A spoiled son is an unfilial son" — and this is no idle proverb.
entries.literal: The vulgar saying goes 'spoiled son is unfilial', not evil words.

entries.zh: 故諸侯王當為置良師傅，相忠言之士，如汲黯、韓長孺等，敢直言極諫，安得有患害！
entries.en: This is why feudal kings should be given worthy tutors and chancellors, men of loyal counsel such as Ji An and Han Changru, who dare to speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve. If this were done, how could any calamity arise!
entries.literal: Therefore, feudal kings should be given good tutors and chancellors, loyal speaking officials, like Ji An, Han Changru and such, who dare to speak directly and remonstrate extremely—how can there be calamity and harm!

entries.zh: 蓋聞梁王西入朝，謁竇太后，燕見，與景帝俱侍坐於太后前，語言私說。
entries.en: I have heard that the King of Liang traveled west to court, paid his respects to Empress Dowager Dou, and was granted a private audience. He sat together with Emperor Jing before the Empress Dowager, and they spoke freely among themselves.
entries.literal: I heard that the King of Liang entered west to court, greeted Empress Dowager Dou, banquet meeting, together with Emperor Jing served and sat before the empress dowager, private language pleased.

entries.zh: 太后謂帝曰：「吾聞殷道親親，周道尊尊，其義一也。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager said to the emperor, "I have heard that the way of the Yin dynasty was to cherish kinship, while the way of the Zhou was to honor authority, and in principle these amount to the same thing.
entries.literal: The empress dowager told the emperor: 'I heard Yin way loves relatives, Zhou way honors superiors, their meanings are one.

entries.zh: 安車大駕，用梁孝王為寄。」
entries.en: When the great carriage and imperial procession pass to another, let King Xiao of Liang be the one entrusted with them."
entries.literal: Peaceful carriage great procession, use Prince Xiao of Liang as the heir.'

entries.zh: 景帝跪席舉身曰：「諾。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing straightened on his mat, bowed, and said, "Yes."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing knelt on the mat and raised his body saying: 'Yes.'

entries.zh: 罷酒出，帝召袁盎諸大臣通經術者曰：「太后言如是，何謂也？」
entries.en: After the banquet ended, they withdrew. The emperor then summoned Yuan Ang and other ministers learned in the classics and asked, "The Empress Dowager speaks thus. What does she mean?"
entries.literal: Finished the wine and went out, the emperor summoned Yuan Ang and various ministers versed in classics saying: 'The empress dowager speaks like this, what does it mean?'

entries.zh: 皆對曰：「太后意欲立梁王為帝太子。」
entries.en: They all replied, "The Empress Dowager intends to establish the King of Liang as the imperial heir."
entries.literal: All replied: 'The empress dowager intends to establish the King of Liang as imperial crown prince.'

entries.zh: 帝問其狀，袁盎等曰：「殷道親親者，立弟。
entries.en: The emperor asked them to explain. Yuan Ang and the others said, "The way of the Yin dynasty was to cherish kinship, and so the younger brother was made heir.
entries.literal: The emperor asked the circumstances, Yuan Ang and others said: 'Yin way loves relatives establishes younger brother.

entries.zh: 周道尊尊者，立子。
entries.en: The way of the Zhou was to honor seniority, and so the son was made heir.
entries.literal: Zhou way honors superiors establishes son.

entries.zh: 殷道質，質者法天，親其所親，故立弟。
entries.en: The way of Yin valued substance. Substance follows Heaven, which draws close those who are nearest, and so the younger brother was made heir.
entries.literal: Yin way substantial, substantial follows Heaven, loves those close to it, thus establishes younger brother.

entries.zh: 周道文，文者法地，尊者敬也，敬其本始，故立長子。
entries.en: The way of Zhou valued refinement. Refinement follows Earth, which honors authority — and to honor authority is to respect one's origins, so the eldest son was made heir.
entries.literal: Zhou way cultured, cultured follows Earth, honor means respect, respects its origin, thus establishes eldest son.

entries.zh: 周道，太子死，立適孫。
entries.en: Under the Zhou system, if the crown prince dies, the legitimate grandson succeeds.
entries.literal: Zhou way, crown prince dies, establishes proper grandson.

entries.zh: 殷道。
entries.en: Under the Yin system —
entries.literal: Yin way.

entries.zh: 太子死，立其弟。」
entries.en: if the crown prince dies, his younger brother succeeds."
entries.literal: Crown prince dies, establishes his younger brother.'

entries.zh: 帝曰：「於公何如？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "What is your view, gentlemen?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'To you gentlemen what is it?'

entries.zh: 皆對曰：「方今漢家法周，周道不得立弟，當立子。
entries.en: They all replied, "The Han house now follows the Zhou system. Under the way of Zhou, a younger brother cannot be made heir; the son must succeed.
entries.literal: All replied: 'Now the Han house follows Zhou, Zhou way cannot establish younger brother, should establish son.

entries.zh: 故春秋所以非宋宣公。
entries.en: This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals censures Duke Xuan of Song.
entries.literal: Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals criticizes Duke Xuan of Song.

entries.zh: 宋宣公死，不立子而與弟。
entries.en: When Duke Xuan of Song died, he did not establish his son but passed the throne to his younger brother.
entries.literal: Duke Xuan of Song died, did not establish son but gave to younger brother.

entries.zh: 弟受國死，復反之與兄之子。
entries.en: When the younger brother received the state and later died, he returned it to his elder brother's son.
entries.literal: Younger brother received the state died, again returned it to elder brother's son.

entries.zh: 弟之子爭之，以為我當代父後，即刺殺兄子。
entries.en: But the younger brother's son disputed this, reasoning that he should succeed his own father, and so he assassinated the elder brother's son.
entries.literal: Younger brother's son contended for it, considering I should succeed father's place, thus stabbed and killed elder brother's son.

entries.zh: 以故國亂，禍不絕。
entries.en: As a result, the state was thrown into chaos and calamities followed without end.
entries.literal: Therefore, the state was chaotic, calamities did not cease.

entries.zh: 故春秋曰『君子大居正，宋之禍宣公為之』。
entries.en: Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals declares, 'The gentleman holds fast to what is correct; the calamity that befell Song was brought about by Duke Xuan.'
entries.literal: Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals says 'The gentleman greatly occupies correctness, Song's calamity Duke Xuan made it.'

entries.zh: 臣請見太后白之。」
entries.en: We request permission to see the Empress Dowager and explain this to her."
entries.literal: Your servants request to see the empress dowager and inform her.'

entries.zh: 袁盎等入見太后：「太后言欲立梁王，梁王即終，欲誰立？」
entries.en: Yuan Ang and the others entered and asked the Empress Dowager, "If Your Majesty establishes the King of Liang, and the King of Liang later dies, whom would you choose after him?"
entries.literal: Yuan Ang and the others went in to see the Empress Dowager and asked, "Your Majesty wishes to establish the King of Liang as heir. But if the King of Liang should die, whom would you then wish to establish?"

entries.zh: 太后曰：「吾復立帝子。」
entries.en: The Empress Dowager said, "Then I would establish the emperor's son."
entries.literal: The empress dowager said: 'I will again establish the emperor's son.'

entries.zh: 袁盎等以宋宣公不立正，生禍，禍亂後五世不絕，小不忍害大義狀報太后。
entries.en: Yuan Ang and the others presented the case of Duke Xuan of Song, who had failed to follow the proper line of succession and thereby brought about a calamity that plagued his state for five generations. They explained to the Empress Dowager how a small indulgence could undermine the greater good.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang and others with Duke Xuan of Song not establishing properly, produced calamity, calamity and chaos after five generations not ceased, little intolerance harming great righteousness, reported to the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 太后乃解說，即使梁王歸就國。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was persuaded and abandoned the idea, immediately directing the King of Liang to return to his kingdom.
entries.literal: The empress dowager then dispelled her idea, immediately had the King of Liang return to his fief.

entries.zh: 而梁王聞其義出於袁盎諸大臣所，怨望，使人來殺袁盎。
entries.en: When the King of Liang learned that the arguments against him had come from Yuan Ang and the other ministers, he was consumed with resentment and sent men to assassinate Yuan Ang.
entries.literal: And the King of Liang heard that the righteousness came from Yuan Ang and the various ministers, resented, sent men to come kill Yuan Ang.

entries.zh: 袁盎顧之曰：「我所謂袁將軍者也，公得毋誤乎？」
entries.en: Yuan Ang turned to face the assassin and said, "I am the one known as General Yuan. Are you sure you have the right man?"
entries.literal: Yuan Ang looked at him saying: 'The one called General Yuan is me, sir has not mistaken?'

entries.zh: 刺者曰：「是矣！」
entries.en: The assassin replied, "You are the one!"
entries.literal: The assassin said: 'Correct!'

entries.zh: 刺之，置其劍，劍著身。
entries.en: He stabbed him and left the sword behind, still lodged in the body.
entries.literal: Stabbed him, left his sword, the sword stuck in the body.

entries.zh: 視其劍，新治。
entries.en: When they examined the sword, they found it was newly forged.
entries.literal: Looked at his sword, newly forged.

entries.zh: 問長安中削厲工，工曰：「梁郎某子來治此劍。」
entries.en: They inquired among the sword-smiths of Chang'an, and one of them said, "A young attendant from Liang came to have this sword made."
entries.literal: Asked Chang'an's sword sharpening workers, the worker said: 'A Liang attendant some son came to forge this sword.'

entries.zh: 以此知而發覺之，發使者捕逐之。
entries.en: This led to the discovery of the plot, and envoys were dispatched to apprehend and pursue the culprits.
entries.literal: With this knew and discovered it, sent envoys to capture and pursue them.

entries.zh: 獨梁王所欲殺大臣十餘人，文吏窮本之，謀反端頗見。
entries.en: In all, the King of Liang had targeted more than ten ministers for assassination. When the legal officials traced the matter to its source, clear signs of a conspiracy to rebel emerged.
entries.literal: Only the King of Liang desired to kill ministers more than ten, the civil officials investigated to the root, rebellion signs much appeared.

entries.zh: 太后不食，日夜泣不止。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager refused to eat and wept day and night without ceasing.
entries.literal: The empress dowager did not eat, day and night wept without stopping.

entries.zh: 景帝甚憂之，問公卿大臣，大臣以為遣經術吏往治之，乃可解。
entries.en: Emperor Jing was deeply troubled and consulted his ministers. They advised that officials well-versed in the classics be sent to handle the matter, as this was the only way to resolve the crisis.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing greatly worried about it, asked the dukes and ministers, ministers considered sending classic versed officials to handle it, then could resolve.

entries.zh: 於是遣田叔、呂季主往治之。
entries.en: Accordingly, Tian Shu and Lu Jizhu were dispatched to handle the matter.
entries.literal: Thus, sent Tian Shu, Lu Jizhu to handle it.

entries.zh: 此二人皆通經術，知大禮。
entries.en: Both men were thoroughly versed in the classics and understood the demands of high propriety.
entries.literal: These two both versed in classics, knew great ritual.

entries.zh: 來還，至霸昌廄，取火悉燒梁之反辭，但空手來對景帝。
entries.en: On their return journey, when they reached the Bachang post station, they set fire to all the incriminating documents from Liang and came before Emperor Jing with empty hands.
entries.literal: Coming back, arrived at Bachang stable, took fire and completely burned Liang's rebellion documents, but came with empty hands to answer Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 景帝曰：「何如？」
entries.en: Emperor Jing asked, "What did you find?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: 'What is it like?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「言梁王不知也。
entries.en: They replied, "The King of Liang knew nothing of the plot.
entries.literal: They replied, "We report that the King of Liang knew nothing of it.

entries.zh: 造為之者，獨其幸臣羊勝、公孫詭之屬為之耳。
entries.en: The conspirators were solely his favored ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and their associates.
entries.literal: Those who fabricated it were only his favored ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and such did it.

entries.zh: 謹以伏誅死，梁王無恙也。」
entries.en: They have already submitted to the law and been put to death. The King of Liang is well and bears no guilt."
entries.literal: They have already submitted to execution and been put to death. The King of Liang is unharmed."

entries.zh: 景帝喜說，曰：「急趨謁太后。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing was delighted and said, "Go at once and report this to the Empress Dowager."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing pleased and happy, said: 'Quickly go announce to the empress dowager.'

entries.zh: 太后聞之，立起坐湌，氣平復。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager heard the news, she rose at once, took a meal, and her spirits were restored.
entries.literal: The empress dowager heard it, immediately rose and sat drinking, her energy calmed and recovered.

entries.zh: 故曰，不通經術知古今之大禮，不可以為三公及左右近臣。
entries.en: Therefore, it is said: those who are not versed in the classics and do not understand the great principles of propriety, both ancient and modern, are unfit to serve as one of the Three Excellencies or as a minister close to the throne.
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said, if not versed in classics and knowing ancient and modern great ritual, cannot serve as three dukes and left and right close ministers.

entries.zh: 少見之人，如從管中闚天也。
entries.en: Those of narrow vision are like men trying to see the sky through a tube.
entries.literal: People of little knowledge are like peeking at heaven from a tube.

entries.zh: 梁共王三年，景帝崩。
entries.en: In the third year of King Gong of Liang, Emperor Jing passed away.
entries.literal: In Liang King Gong's third year, Emperor Jing passed away.

entries.zh: 共王立七年卒，子襄立，是為平王。
entries.en: King Gong reigned for seven years before dying. His son Xiang succeeded him and became King Ping.
entries.literal: King Gong reigned seven years and died, his son Xiang succeeded him, becoming King Ping.

entries.zh: 孝景皇帝子凡十三人為王，而母五人，同母者為宗親。
entries.en: Emperor Jing had thirteen sons who were enfeoffed as kings, each born to one of five mothers. Those who shared the same mother were reckoned as one maternal lineage.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaojing had thirteen sons who became kings, born to five different mothers. Those from the same mother were considered clan relatives.

entries.zh: 栗姬子曰榮、德、閼于。
entries.en: Consort Li bore three sons: Rong, De, and Eyu.
entries.literal: Consort Li's sons were Rong, De, and A Yu.

entries.zh: 程姬子曰餘、非、端。
entries.en: Consort Cheng bore three sons: Yu, Fei, and Duan.
entries.literal: Consort Cheng's sons were Yu, Fei, and Duan.

entries.zh: 賈夫人子曰彭祖、勝。
entries.en: Lady Jia bore two sons: Pengzu and Sheng.
entries.literal: Lady Jia's sons were Pengzu and Sheng.

entries.zh: 唐姬子曰發。
entries.en: Consort Tang bore one son: Fa.
entries.literal: Consort Tang's son was Fa.

entries.zh: 王夫人兒姁子曰越、寄、乘、舜。
entries.en: Lady Wang, also known as Erxu, bore four sons: Yue, Ji, Cheng, and Shun.
entries.literal: Lady Wang, Erxu, bore sons Yue, Ji, Cheng, and Shun.

entries.zh: 河閒獻王德，以孝景帝前二年用皇子為河閒王。
entries.en: King Xian of Hejian, whose name was De, was enfeoffed as King of Hejian as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: King Xian of Hejian, De, was made King of Hejian as imperial son in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

entries.zh: 好儒學，被服造次必於儒者。
entries.en: He was devoted to Confucian learning, and in both his dress and his conduct, even in moments of haste, he invariably adhered to the ways of the Confucian scholars.
entries.literal: He loved Confucian learning. Even in his clothing and hasty actions, he always followed Confucian scholars.

entries.zh: 山東諸儒多從之游。
entries.en: Many Confucian scholars from east of the mountains came to study under him.
entries.literal: Many Confucian scholars from Shandong traveled to study with him.

entries.zh: 臨江哀王閼于，以孝景帝前二年用皇子為臨江王。
entries.en: King Ai of Linjiang, whose name was Eyu, was enfeoffed as King of Linjiang as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: King Ai of Linjiang, Eyu, was made King of Linjiang as imperial son in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

entries.zh: 三年卒，無後，國除為郡。
entries.en: He died after three years without an heir, and his kingdom was abolished and converted into a commandery.
entries.literal: He died after three years without heirs. The kingdom was abolished as a commandery.

entries.zh: 江都易王非，以孝景前二年用皇子為汝南王。
entries.en: King Yi of Jiangdu, whose name was Fei, was enfeoffed as King of Runan as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: King Yi of Jiangdu, Fei, was made King of Runan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's second year before his reign.

entries.zh: 吳楚反時，非年十五，有材力，上書願擊吳。
entries.en: When the kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in rebellion, Fei was only fifteen, yet he possessed both talent and strength, and he submitted a memorial requesting permission to march against Wu.
entries.literal: During the Wu and Chu rebellion, Fei was fifteen and possessed talent and strength. He submitted a memorial volunteering to attack Wu.

entries.zh: 景帝賜非將軍印，擊吳。
entries.en: Emperor Jing bestowed upon Fei a general's seal and dispatched him to fight against Wu.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing granted Fei a general's seal and sent him to attack Wu.

entries.zh: 吳已破，二歲，徙為江都王，治吳故國，以軍功賜天子旌旗。
entries.en: After Wu was crushed, two years passed before Fei was transferred to become King of Jiangdu, governing the former territory of Wu. In recognition of his military valor, he was awarded the imperial banners.
entries.literal: After Wu was defeated, two years later he was moved to become King of Jiangdu, ruling the former Wu territory. For his military achievements, he was granted the emperor's banners.

entries.zh: 元光五年，匈奴大入漢為賊，非上書願擊匈奴，上不許。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Yuanguang era, the Xiongnu launched a major incursion into Han territory, raiding and plundering. Fei submitted a memorial requesting permission to strike against them, but the emperor refused.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanguang, the Xiongnu invaded Han territory on a large scale. Fei petitioned to attack the Xiongnu, but the emperor would not allow it.

entries.zh: 非好氣力，治宮觀，招四方豪桀，驕奢甚。
entries.en: Fei delighted in feats of strength, built lavish palaces and towers, and gathered bold and daring men from every quarter. His arrogance and extravagance knew no bounds.
entries.literal: Fei was fond of physical strength and built palaces and towers. He attracted bold heroes from all directions and lived in great extravagance.

entries.zh: 趙王彭祖，以孝景前二年用皇子為廣川王。
entries.en: King Pengzu of Zhao was first enfeoffed as King of Guangchuan as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: King Pengzu of Zhao was made King of Guangchuan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's second year before his reign.

entries.zh: 趙王遂反破後，彭祖王廣川。
entries.en: After King Sui of Zhao's rebellion was crushed, Pengzu ruled as King of Guangchuan.
entries.literal: After King Sui of Zhao's rebellion was crushed, Pengzu became King of Guangchuan.

entries.zh: 四年，徙為趙王。
entries.en: Four years later, he was transferred to become King of Zhao.
entries.literal: After four years, he was moved to become King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 十五年，孝景帝崩。
entries.en: Fifteen years into his reign, Emperor Jing passed away.
entries.literal: After fifteen years, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.

entries.zh: 彭祖為人巧佞卑諂，足恭而心刻深。
entries.en: Pengzu was by nature artful, fawning, and obsequious, deferential in outward manner but ruthless and calculating at heart.
entries.literal: Pengzu was crafty and flattering by nature, outwardly respectful but inwardly deeply treacherous.

entries.zh: 好法律，持詭辯以中人。
entries.en: He had a passion for legal matters and wielded sophistry to entrap others.
entries.literal: He loved legal affairs and used clever arguments to trap people.

entries.zh: 彭祖多內寵姬及子孫。
entries.en: Pengzu kept a great number of favored consorts in his inner palace, and sired many children and grandchildren.
entries.literal: Pengzu had many favored consorts in his palace and many children and grandchildren.

entries.zh: 相、二千石欲奉漢法以治，則害於王家。
entries.en: Any chancellor or official of two-thousand-shi rank who attempted to govern by Han law inevitably ran afoul of the royal household's interests.
entries.literal: If prime ministers and officials of two thousand shi wished to follow Han law to govern, it would harm the king's family.

entries.zh: 是以每相、二千石至，彭祖衣皁布衣，自行迎，除二千石舍，多設疑事以作動之，得二千石失言，中忌諱，輒書之。
entries.en: For this reason, whenever a new chancellor or official of two-thousand-shi rank arrived, Pengzu would don coarse black cloth and personally go out to welcome him. He would prepare the official's quarters and contrive all manner of provocations to unsettle him. If the official let slip an indiscreet word or violated some taboo, Pengzu recorded it at once.
entries.literal: Therefore, whenever prime ministers and officials of two thousand shi arrived, Pengzu would wear mourning clothes and personally go to welcome them. He would clear out the officials' residences and set up many suspicious matters to provoke them. If he caught them making slips of the tongue or taboo violations, he would record them.

entries.zh: 二千石欲治者，則以此迫劫；
entries.en: Should an official of two-thousand-shi rank attempt to govern, Pengzu would use these records to coerce and threaten him;
entries.literal: When officials of two thousand shi wished to govern, he would use this to coerce and threaten them.

entries.zh: 不聽，乃上書告，及汙以姦利事。
entries.en: and if the official still refused to comply, Pengzu would submit a memorial of accusation to the throne, smearing him with charges of corruption and profiteering.
entries.literal: If they did not listen, he would submit memorials accusing them and slander them with charges of corruption and personal gain.

entries.zh: 彭祖立五十餘年，相、二千石無能滿二歲，輒以罪去，大者死，小者刑，以故二千石莫敢治。
entries.en: Over the course of Pengzu's reign of more than fifty years, not a single chancellor or official of two-thousand-shi rank lasted a full two years before being removed on charges. Those convicted of greater offenses died; those of lesser ones were punished. As a result, no official dared to govern.
entries.literal: Pengzu reigned for more than fifty years. No prime minister or official of two thousand shi could complete two years in office before being dismissed for crimes—major ones died, minor ones were punished. Therefore, no officials of two thousand shi dared to govern.

entries.zh: 而趙王擅權，使使即縣為賈人榷會，入多於國經租稅。
entries.en: The King of Zhao thus monopolized all authority, dispatching agents to the counties to operate trading monopolies on his behalf, which brought in revenue exceeding the kingdom's regular rents and taxes.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao monopolized power, sending envoys to counties to act as merchants and collect monopolies, bringing in more than the kingdom's regular taxes.

entries.zh: 以是趙王家多金錢，然所賜姬諸子，亦盡之矣。
entries.en: As a result, the house of Zhao amassed a great fortune in gold and coin, yet what Pengzu lavished upon his consorts and sons consumed it all.
entries.literal: Because of this the Zhao royal family had abundant gold and money, though what he bestowed on his consorts and sons also exhausted it all.

entries.zh: 彭祖取笔江都易王寵姬王建所盜與姦淖姬者為姬，甚愛之。
entries.en: Pengzu took as his own consort the very Lady Nao whom King Jian of Jiangdu had abducted from the late King Yi's inner palace and bedded unlawfully. Pengzu doted on her greatly.
entries.literal: Pengzu took the favored consort of King Yi of Jiangdu that King Jian had stolen and committed adultery with—Nao Ji—as his own consort, and loved her deeply.

entries.zh: 魯共王餘，以孝景前二年用皇子為淮陽王。
entries.en: King Gong of Lu, whose name was Yu, was first enfeoffed as King of Huaiyang as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: King Gong of Lu, Yu, was made King of Huaiyang as imperial son in the second year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

entries.zh: 二年，吳楚反破後，以孝景前三年徙為魯王。
entries.en: Two years later, after the rebellion of Wu and Chu had been crushed, he was transferred to become King of Lu in the third year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: In the second year, after the Wu and Chu rebellion was crushed, he was moved to become King of Lu in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign.

entries.zh: 好治宮室苑囿狗馬。
entries.en: He delighted in building palaces and gardens, and in keeping dogs and horses.
entries.literal: He enjoyed constructing palaces, gardens, and parks, as well as dogs and horses.

entries.zh: 季年好音，不喜辭辯。
entries.en: In his later years he grew fond of music but had no taste for literary disputation.
entries.literal: In his later years he loved music but disliked literary debate.

entries.zh: 為人吃。
entries.en: He had a stammer.
entries.literal: In disposition he stammered.

entries.zh: 臨江閔王榮，以孝景前四年為皇太子，四歲廢，用故太子為臨江王。
entries.en: King Min of Linjiang, whose name was Rong, was made Crown Prince in the fourth year of Emperor Jing's early reign. After four years he was deposed, and the former Crown Prince was then enfeoffed as King of Linjiang.
entries.literal: King Min of Linjiang, Rong, was made crown prince in the fourth year of Emperor Xiaojing's early reign. He was deposed after four years and the former crown prince was made King of Linjiang.

entries.zh: 膠西于王端，以孝景前三年吳楚七國反破後，端用皇子為膠西王。
entries.en: King Yu of Jiaoxi, whose name was Duan, was enfeoffed as King of Jiaoxi as an imperial prince in the third year of Emperor Jing's early reign, after the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms of Wu and Chu had been put down.
entries.literal: King Yu of Jiaoxi, Duan, was made King of Jiaoxi as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's third year before his reign, after the Wu and Chu Seven Kingdoms rebellion was crushed.

entries.zh: 端為人賊戾，又陰痿，一近婦人，病之數月。
entries.en: Duan was cruel and violent by temperament, and he also suffered from a hidden affliction of impotence. Whenever he lay with a woman, he would fall ill for months afterward.
entries.literal: Duan was cruel and tyrannical by nature, and moreover suffered from impotence. Whenever he approached a woman, he would fall ill for several months.

entries.zh: 而有愛幸少年為郎。
entries.en: Instead, he kept a favored young man as a gentleman-in-attendance at court.
entries.literal: He had a beloved young man who served as a gentleman-in-attendance.

entries.zh: 為郎者頃之與後宮亂，端禽滅之，及殺其子母。
entries.en: Before long, this attendant carried on illicit affairs with the women of the inner palace. Duan seized and put him to death, and killed his mother and children as well.
entries.literal: This attendant soon committed adultery with the women of the rear palace. Duan captured and executed him, along with his mother and children.

entries.zh: 數犯上法，漢公卿數請誅端，天子為兄弟之故不忍，而端所為滋甚。
entries.en: He transgressed the imperial statutes time and again. The ministers and nobles of the Han court repeatedly petitioned for his execution, but the Son of Heaven, for the bond of brotherhood, could not bring himself to act. Meanwhile, Duan's outrages only grew worse.
entries.literal: He repeatedly violated the laws of the court. Han's nobles and ministers repeatedly requested his execution, but the emperor spared him for the sake of brotherhood. Yet Duan's offenses grew worse.

entries.zh: 有司再請削其國，去太半。
entries.en: The responsible officials twice petitioned to have his kingdom reduced, and more than half its territory was stripped away.
entries.literal: The officials twice requested that his kingdom be reduced, removing more than half.

entries.zh: 端心慍，遂為無訾省。
entries.en: Duan seethed with resentment, and from that point on he spent nothing at all, living in the most extreme frugality.
entries.literal: Duan was resentful and became extremely frugal.

entries.zh: 府庫壞漏盡，腐財物以巨萬計，終不得收徙。
entries.en: His storehouses and treasuries fell into ruin, their roofs leaking, until goods worth tens of millions had rotted away, yet he still refused to collect or relocate them.
entries.literal: His storehouses and treasuries all rotted and leaked, with spoiled goods worth millions. In the end he could not collect or move them.

entries.zh: 令吏毋得收租賦。
entries.en: He forbade his officials from collecting rents or taxes.
entries.literal: He ordered his officials not to collect rents and taxes.

entries.zh: 端皆去衛，封其宮門，從一門出游。
entries.en: Duan dismissed all his guards and sealed every gate of the palace, leaving only a single gate through which he would come and go.
entries.literal: Duan dismissed all his guards and sealed his palace gates, going out to travel through only one gate.

entries.zh: 數變名姓，為布衣，之他郡國。
entries.en: He would frequently change his name, disguise himself as a commoner, and travel incognito to other commanderies and kingdoms.
entries.literal: He frequently changed his name and surname, dressed as a commoner, and traveled to other commanderies and kingdoms.

entries.zh: 中山靖王勝，以孝景前三年用皇子為中山王。
entries.en: King Jing of Zhongshan, whose name was Sheng, was enfeoffed as King of Zhongshan as an imperial prince in the third year of Emperor Jing's early reign.
entries.literal: King Jing of Zhongshan, Sheng, was made King of Zhongshan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's third year before his reign.

entries.zh: 十四年，孝景帝崩。
entries.en: Fourteen years into his reign, Emperor Jing passed away.
entries.literal: After fourteen years, Emperor Xiaojing passed away.

entries.zh: 勝為人樂酒好內，有子枝屬百二十餘人。
entries.en: Sheng was a man who delighted in wine and women, and he fathered more than a hundred and twenty sons and descendants across his branches.
entries.literal: Sheng loved wine and women by nature, with over one hundred twenty children and descendants.

entries.zh: 常與兄趙王相非，曰：「兄為王，專代吏治事。
entries.en: He often quarreled with his elder brother, the King of Zhao, saying: "My brother, though a king, concerns himself solely with taking over the work of officials.
entries.literal: He often quarreled with his elder brother, the King of Zhao, saying, "My brother, though a king, monopolizes the work of officials in governing.

entries.zh: 王者當日聽音樂聲色。」
entries.en: A king ought to spend his days enjoying music and the pleasures of the senses."
entries.literal: As king, one should daily listen to music and enjoy beauty.'

entries.zh: 趙王亦非之，曰：「中山王徒日淫，不佐天子拊循百姓，何以稱為藩臣！」
entries.en: The King of Zhao countered: "The King of Zhongshan does nothing but wallow in excess day after day. He does not assist the Son of Heaven in nurturing and guiding the people. How can he claim to be a worthy vassal?"
entries.literal: The King of Zhao also quarreled with him, saying: 'The King of Zhongshan merely indulges in debauchery daily, does not assist the Son of Heaven in comforting and guiding the people. How can he be called a vassal minister!'

entries.zh: 長沙定王發，發之母唐姬，故程姬侍者。
entries.en: King Ding of Changsha, whose name was Fa, was the son of Consort Tang, who had formerly served as a lady-in-waiting to Consort Cheng.
entries.literal: King Ding of Changsha, Fa, Fa's mother Consort Tang, formerly Consort Cheng's attendant.

entries.zh: 景帝召程姬，程姬有所辟，不願進，而飾侍者唐兒使夜進。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing summoned Consort Cheng, she was indisposed and unwilling to attend. Instead, she adorned her attendant, known as Tang Er, and sent the girl in her place under cover of night.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing summoned Consort Cheng. Consort Cheng made some excuse and did not wish to come forward. Instead she dressed up her attendant Tang Er and sent her in at night.

entries.zh: 上醉不知，以為程姬而幸之，遂有身。
entries.en: The emperor, drunk and unsuspecting, took her for Consort Cheng and lay with her. She conceived.
entries.literal: The emperor was drunk and did not realize, thinking it was Consort Cheng and favored her, so she became pregnant.

entries.zh: 已乃覺非程姬也。
entries.en: Only afterward did the emperor realize that the woman had not been Consort Cheng.
entries.literal: Only then did he realize it was not Consort Cheng.

entries.zh: 及生子，因命曰發。
entries.en: When she gave birth to a son, he was given the name Fa.
entries.literal: When she gave birth to a son, he named him Fa.

entries.zh: 以孝景前二年用皇子為長沙王。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Jing's early reign, Fa was enfeoffed as King of Changsha as an imperial prince.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xiaojing's second year before his reign, Fa was made King of Changsha as imperial son.

entries.zh: 以其母微，無寵，故王卑溼貧國。
entries.en: Because his mother was of humble origin and enjoyed no imperial favor, he was consigned to rule over a poor and swampy kingdom.
entries.literal: Because his mother was of lowly status and had no favor, he was made king of a poor and damp kingdom.

entries.zh: 右一國本王唐姬之子也。
entries.en: The founding king of the above kingdom was a son of Consort Tang.
entries.literal: This one kingdom was originally ruled by a son of Consort Tang.

entries.zh: 廣川惠王越，以孝景中二年用皇子為廣川王。
entries.en: King Hui of Guangchuan, whose name was Yue, was enfeoffed as King of Guangchuan as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
entries.literal: King Hui of Guangchuan, Yue, was made King of Guangchuan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle second year.

entries.zh: 膠東康王寄，以孝景中二年用皇子為膠東王。
entries.en: King Kang of Jiaodong, whose name was Ji, was enfeoffed as King of Jiaodong as an imperial prince in the second year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
entries.literal: King Kang of Jiaodong, Ji, was made King of Jiaodong as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle second year.

entries.zh: 二十八年卒。
entries.en: He died after twenty-eight years on the throne.
entries.literal: He died after twenty-eight years.

entries.zh: 淮南王謀反時，寄微聞其事，私作樓車鏃矢戰守備，候淮南之起。
entries.en: When the King of Huainan was plotting rebellion, Ji caught wind of the scheme and secretly had siege towers, arrowheads, and other military defenses constructed, standing ready for the moment Huainan would rise.
entries.literal: During the Huainan king's rebellion, Ji had heard rumors of the matter. He privately built tower chariots, arrowheads, and defensive preparations, waiting for Huainan's uprising.

entries.zh: 及吏治淮南之事，辭出之。
entries.en: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, the confessions that emerged implicated him.
entries.literal: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, the evidence implicated him.

entries.zh: 寄於上最親，意傷之，發病而死，不敢置後，於是上（問）［聞］。
entries.en: Ji had been the emperor's most beloved brother, and the affair weighed heavily upon him. He fell ill with grief and died, not having dared to designate an heir. Only then did the emperor learn what had happened.
entries.literal: Ji was most beloved by the emperor, who was grieved by this. Ji fell ill and died, not daring to appoint an heir. Thus, the emperor heard of it.

entries.zh: 寄有長子者名賢，母無寵；
entries.en: Ji's eldest son was named Xian, but his mother had never enjoyed imperial favor;
entries.literal: Ji had an eldest son named Xian whose mother had no favor.

entries.zh: 少子名慶，母愛幸，寄常欲立之，為不次，因有過，遂無言。
entries.en: his younger son was named Qing, whose mother was beloved and favored. Ji had always wished to name Qing as his heir, but since doing so would violate the order of succession, and because of the taint of his own offenses, he said nothing.
entries.literal: His younger son was named Qing, whose mother was beloved and favored. Ji had often wished to establish Qing as heir, but since it would violate proper order, and because he himself had offenses, he said nothing.

entries.zh: 上憐之，乃以賢為膠東王奉康王嗣，而封慶於故衡山地，為六安王。
entries.en: The emperor, moved by pity, made Xian King of Jiaodong to carry on King Kang's line, and enfeoffed Qing in the former territory of Hengshan as King of Liu'an.
entries.literal: The emperor pitied him and made Xian King of Jiaodong to continue King Kang's line, while enfeoffing Qing in the former Hengshan territory as King of Liu'an.

entries.zh: 清河哀王乘，以孝景中三年用皇子為清河王。
entries.en: King Ai of Qinghe, whose name was Cheng, was enfeoffed as King of Qinghe as an imperial prince in the third year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
entries.literal: King Ai of Qinghe, Cheng, was made King of Qinghe as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle third year.

entries.zh: 十二年卒，無後，國除，地入于漢，為清河郡。
entries.en: He died after twelve years without an heir. His kingdom was abolished, its territory absorbed into the Han domain and reorganized as the Commandery of Qinghe.
entries.literal: He died after twelve years with no heirs. The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Qinghe Commandery.

entries.zh: 常山憲王舜，以孝景中五年用皇子為常山王。
entries.en: King Xian of Changshan, whose name was Shun, was enfeoffed as King of Changshan as an imperial prince in the fifth year of Emperor Jing's middle reign.
entries.literal: King Xian of Changshan, Shun, was made King of Changshan as imperial son in Emperor Xiaojing's middle fifth year.

entries.zh: 舜最親，景帝少子，驕怠多淫，數犯禁，上常寬釋之。
entries.en: Shun was the most cherished of the brothers, being Emperor Jing's youngest son. He was arrogant, indolent, and given to excess, and he frequently ran afoul of the law. Yet the emperor always pardoned him.
entries.literal: Shun was most beloved. As Emperor Jing's youngest son, he was arrogant and indolent, frequently committing excesses. The emperor often pardoned him leniently.

entries.zh: 立三十二年卒，太子勃代立為王。
entries.en: After thirty-two years on the throne he died, and his heir apparent, Bo, succeeded him as king.
entries.literal: He reigned for thirty-two years and died. Crown Prince Bo succeeded as king.

entries.zh: 四年，坐侵廟壖垣為宮，上徵榮。
entries.en: In his fourth year as king, he was charged with encroaching upon the temple precinct walls to expand his palace. The emperor summoned Rong to the capital.
entries.literal: In his fourth year, he was convicted of encroaching on the temple grounds to build a palace. The emperor summoned Rong to court.

entries.zh: 榮行，祖於江陵北門。
entries.en: As Rong departed, he performed the farewell sacrifice at the north gate of Jiangling.
entries.literal: As Rong departed, he performed farewell rites at Jiangling's north gate.

entries.zh: 既已上車，軸折車廢。
entries.en: He had already mounted his carriage when the axle snapped and the carriage collapsed.
entries.literal: He had already boarded his carriage when the axle broke and the carriage was ruined.

entries.zh: 江陵父老流涕竊言曰：「吾王不反矣！」
entries.en: The elders of Jiangling wept and whispered to one another, "Our king will never return!"
entries.literal: The elders of Jiangling wept and whispered among themselves: 'Our king will never return!'

entries.zh: 榮至，詣中尉府簿。
entries.en: When Rong arrived in the capital, he presented himself at the office of the Commandant of Justice to be registered.
entries.literal: When Rong arrived, he reported to the Commandant of Justice's office.

entries.zh: 中尉郅都責訊王，王恐，自殺。
entries.en: The Commandant Zhi Du interrogated the king with harsh rebukes; terrified, Rong took his own life.
entries.literal: Commandant Zhi Du interrogated the king, who became terrified and committed suicide.

entries.zh: 葬藍田。
entries.en: He was buried at Lantian.
entries.literal: He was buried at Lantian.

entries.zh: 燕數萬銜土置冢上，百姓憐之。
entries.en: Tens of thousands of swallows carried earth in their beaks and placed it upon his tomb, and the common people mourned him.
entries.literal: Tens of thousands of swallows carried earth in their beaks and placed it on his tomb mound. The common people pitied him.

entries.zh: 榮最長，死無後，國除，地入于漢，為南郡。
entries.en: Rong had been the eldest son, but he died without an heir. His kingdom was abolished, and its territory was absorbed into the Han domain as Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: Rong was the eldest but died without heirs. The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 立四十二年卒，子哀王昌立。
entries.en: After forty-two years on the throne he died, and his son, King Ai, whose name was Chang, succeeded him.
entries.literal: He reigned for forty-two years and died. His son, King Ai Chang, succeeded him.

entries.zh: 一年卒，子昆侈代為中山王。
entries.en: He died after just one year, and his son Kunchi succeeded him as King of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: He died after one year. His son Kun Chi succeeded as King of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：高祖時諸侯皆賦，得自除內史以下，漢獨為置丞相，黃金印。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: In the time of Emperor Gaozu, the feudal lords all collected their own taxes and were permitted to appoint their own officials from the rank of Interior Minister downward. Only the chancellors were appointed by the Han court, and they bore golden seals.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: In Gaozu's time the feudal lords all collected their own taxes and were able to appoint their own officials from the rank of interior minister downward. Only the Han court appointed chancellors for them, with golden seals.

entries.zh: 諸侯自除御史、廷尉正、博士，擬於天子。
entries.en: The feudal lords appointed their own censors, chief justices, and erudites, rivaling the Son of Heaven in their establishments.
entries.literal: The feudal lords appointed their own censors, directors of convicts at the Court of Justice, and erudites, rivaling the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 自吳楚反後，五宗王世，漢為置二千石，去「丞相」曰「相」，銀印。
entries.en: After the rebellion of Wu and Chu, through the successive generations of the five royal lineages, the Han court appointed officials of two-thousand-shi rank in every kingdom, replaced the title of "chancellor" with the lesser designation of "administrator," and issued silver seals in place of gold.
entries.literal: After the Wu and Chu rebellion, the five clans of kings generation after generation, Han appointed officials of two thousand shi for them, removed 'chancellor' and called it 'prime minister', silver seal.

entries.zh: 諸侯獨得食租稅，奪之權。
entries.en: The feudal lords were left with nothing but the right to collect their rents and taxes; all real power had been stripped away.
entries.literal: The feudal lords only received rent taxes, their power was taken away.

entries.zh: 其後諸侯貧者或乘牛車也。
entries.en: In the years that followed, some of the more impoverished feudal lords were even reduced to riding in ox-drawn carts.
entries.literal: Afterward the impoverished feudal lords sometimes rode ox-carts.

entries.zh: 立二十六年卒，子建立為王。
entries.en: After twenty-six years on the throne he died, and his son Jian was established as king in his stead.
entries.literal: He reigned for twenty-six years and died. His son Jian succeeded him.

entries.zh: 七年自殺。
entries.en: Seven years later, Jian took his own life.
entries.literal: He committed suicide after seven years.

entries.zh: 淮南、衡山謀反時，建頗聞其謀。
entries.en: When the kings of Huainan and Hengshan were plotting rebellion, Jian had caught wind of their conspiracy.
entries.literal: During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellion, Jian had heard rumors of their plot.

entries.zh: 自以為國近淮南，恐一日發，為所并，即陰作兵器，而時佩其父所賜將軍印，載天子旗以出。
entries.en: Believing his kingdom lay dangerously close to Huainan, he feared that should the revolt erupt, he might be swallowed up. He therefore had weapons forged in secret, and whenever he ventured out he wore the general's seal his father had received and displayed the imperial banners.
entries.literal: Since his kingdom bordered Huainan, he feared that if rebellion broke out he would be annexed. So he secretly manufactured weapons while always wearing his father's general's seal and going out with the emperor's banners.

entries.zh: 易王死未葬，建有所說易王寵美人淖姬，夜使人迎與姦服舍中。
entries.en: Before King Yi had even been laid to rest, Jian became enamored of the late king's favored consort, Lady Nao. Under cover of night he sent men to bring her to his quarters, where he took her as his own.
entries.literal: Before King Yi was even buried, Jian took a fancy to King Yi's favored beauty Nao Ji and sent men at night to bring her to his chambers for illicit relations.

entries.zh: 及淮南事發，治黨與頗及江都王建。
entries.en: When the Huainan conspiracy was uncovered, the investigation of its accomplices extended to implicate King Jian of Jiangdu.
entries.literal: When the Huainan affair broke out, the investigation of accomplices implicated King Jian of Jiangdu.

entries.zh: 建恐，因使人多持金錢，事絕其獄。
entries.en: Jian grew alarmed and dispatched agents laden with gold and coin to bribe officials and quash the proceedings against him.
entries.literal: Jian became frightened and sent men with large amounts of gold and money to bribe officials and suppress the case.

entries.zh: 而又信巫祝，使人禱祠妄言。
entries.en: He also relied on shamans and diviners, sending them to offer prayers and utter slanderous prophecies.
entries.literal: He also trusted shamans and prayer-officiants, sending them to perform sacrifices and spread false claims.

entries.zh: 建又盡與其姊弟姦。
entries.en: Jian further committed incest with all of his elder sisters and younger brothers.
entries.literal: Jian also committed incest with all his elder sisters and younger brothers.

entries.zh: 事既聞，漢公卿請捕治建。
entries.en: When these affairs came to light, the ministers and nobles of the Han court petitioned for Jian's arrest and prosecution.
entries.literal: When this became known, Han nobles requested Jian's arrest and trial.

entries.zh: 天子不忍，使大臣即訊王。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven could not bear to act so harshly and instead sent senior ministers to interrogate the king in person.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven spared him and sent ministers to interrogate the king.

entries.zh: 王服所犯，遂自殺。
entries.en: The king confessed to his offenses and then took his own life.
entries.literal: The king admitted his crimes and committed suicide.

entries.zh: 國除，地入于漢，為廣陵郡。
entries.en: His kingdom was abolished, its territory absorbed into the Han domain and reorganized as the Commandery of Guangling.
entries.literal: The kingdom was abolished and its territory incorporated into Han as Guangling Commandery.

entries.zh: 初，憲王舜有所不愛姬生長男棁。
entries.en: Originally, King Xian Shun had a consort whom he did not favor, and she bore him his eldest son, Tiao.
entries.literal: At first, King Xian Shun had an unfavored consort who bore his eldest son Tiao.

entries.zh: 棁以母無寵故，亦不得幸於王。
entries.en: Because his mother enjoyed no favor, Tiao likewise received none from the king.
entries.literal: Because his mother had no favor, Tiao also did not receive favor from the king.

entries.zh: 王後修生太子勃。
entries.en: The queen, whose name was Xiu, later bore the crown prince, Bo.
entries.literal: Later the queen bore Crown Prince Bo.

entries.zh: 王內多，所幸姬生子平、子商，王后希得幸。
entries.en: The king kept many women in his inner palace, and his favored consorts bore him sons named Ping and Shang. The queen herself rarely enjoyed his attentions.
entries.literal: The king had many consorts. His favored consorts bore sons Ping and Shang. The queen rarely received favor.

entries.zh: 及憲王病甚，諸幸姬常侍病，故王后亦以妒媢不常侍病，輒歸舍。
entries.en: When King Xian fell gravely ill, his favored consorts took turns attending at his bedside. The queen, out of jealous resentment, declined to attend regularly and would withdraw to her own chambers.
entries.literal: When King Xian fell gravely ill, his favored consorts constantly attended to his illness. The queen, out of jealousy, did not constantly attend but would return to her chambers.

entries.zh: 醫進藥，太子勃不自嘗藥，又不宿留侍病。
entries.en: When the physician prepared medicine, Crown Prince Bo did not taste it first to test it, as filial duty required, nor did he keep vigil at his father's bedside through the night.
entries.literal: When the physician administered medicine, Crown Prince Bo did not personally taste the medicine, nor did he stay overnight attending to the illness.

entries.zh: 及王薨，王后、太子乃至。
entries.en: Only when the king breathed his last did the queen and the crown prince finally appear.
entries.literal: Only when the king passed away did the queen and crown prince arrive.

entries.zh: 憲王雅不以長子棁為人數，及薨，又不分與財物。
entries.en: King Xian had never treated his eldest son Tiao as a person of consequence, and upon his death he left Tiao no share of the estate.
entries.literal: King Xian had never considered his eldest son Tiao as part of the family. When he died, he did not divide any property with him.

entries.zh: 郎或說太子、王后，令諸子與長子棁共分財物，太子、王后不聽。
entries.en: Certain gentlemen-attendants urged the crown prince and queen to let the other sons share the estate with the eldest, Tiao, but neither would hear of it.
entries.literal: Some gentlemen advised the crown prince and queen to have the various sons share property with the eldest son Tiao. The crown prince and queen did not listen.

entries.zh: 太子代立，又不收恤棁。
entries.en: Even after the crown prince succeeded to the throne, he still refused to look after Tiao or offer him any support.
entries.literal: After succeeding the throne, he still neglected Tiao.

entries.zh: 棁怨王后、太子。
entries.en: Tiao nursed a deep grudge against the queen and the crown prince.
entries.literal: Tiao resented the queen and crown prince.

entries.zh: 漢使者視憲王喪，棁自言憲王病時，王后、太子不侍，及薨，六日出舍，太子勃私姦，飲酒，博戲，擊筑，與女子載馳，環城過市，入牢視囚。
entries.en: When Han envoys arrived to oversee King Xian's funeral, Tiao came forward and personally testified that during the king's illness, neither the queen nor the crown prince had attended him. After the king's death, they had left their mourning quarters within six days. He further reported that Crown Prince Bo had conducted illicit affairs, drunk wine, gambled, and played the bamboo zither. He had raced in carriages with women through the streets, ridden around the city walls and through the markets, and entered the prison to inspect the inmates.
entries.literal: Han envoys inspecting King Xian's funeral, Tiao personally stated that during King Xian's illness, the queen and crown prince did not attend. When he died, they left the residence after six days. Crown Prince Bo privately committed adultery, drank wine, gambled, played zither, raced chariots with women, circled the city through the markets, and entered prisons to inspect prisoners.

entries.zh: 天子遣大行騫驗王后及問王勃，請逮勃所與姦諸證左，王又匿之。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven dispatched the Grand Herald, Qian, to investigate the queen and interrogate King Bo. He requested the arrest of all accomplices and witnesses to Bo's illicit activities, but the king concealed them.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Grand Herald Qian to investigate the queen and interrogate King Bo, requesting to arrest Bo's accomplices in adultery and witnesses. The king hid them.

entries.zh: 吏求捕勃大急，使人致擊笞掠，擅出漢所疑囚者。
entries.en: When the officials pressed urgently to apprehend Bo, he had his men resort to beatings and floggings, and he took it upon himself to release prisoners whom the Han court had placed under suspicion.
entries.literal: When officials urgently sought to apprehend Bo, he had men inflict beatings and floggings, and arbitrarily released prisoners whom the Han court held under suspicion.

entries.zh: 有司請誅憲王後修及王勃。
entries.en: The responsible officials petitioned to have Queen Xiu and King Bo put to death.
entries.literal: The officials requested execution of King Xian's queen Xiu and King Bo.

entries.zh: 上以修素無行，使棁陷之罪，勃無良師傅，不忍誅。
entries.en: The emperor, reflecting that Xiu had always been of poor conduct, making it easy for Tiao to entrap her, and that Bo had never had the benefit of a worthy tutor, could not bring himself to have them executed.
entries.literal: The emperor, considering that Xiu had always been immoral, allowing Tiao to frame her with crimes, and Bo had no good teachers, could not bear to execute them.

entries.zh: 有司請廢王後修，徙王勃以家屬處房陵，上許之。
entries.en: The officials petitioned instead to depose Queen Xiu and exile King Bo along with his family to Fangling. The emperor consented.
entries.literal: The officials requested deposing Queen Xiu and exiling King Bo with his family to Fangling. The emperor approved.

entries.zh: 勃王數月，遷于房陵，國絕。
entries.en: Bo had reigned as king for only a few months before he was removed to Fangling, and the kingdom came to an end.
entries.literal: Bo had been king for several months when he was moved to Fangling. The kingdom was extinguished.

entries.zh: 月餘，天子為最親，乃詔有司曰：「常山憲王蚤夭，后妾不和，適孽誣爭，陷于不義以滅國，朕甚閔焉。
entries.en: A little more than a month later, mindful that Changshan had been ruled by his closest kin, the Son of Heaven issued an edict to his ministers: "King Xian of Changshan died before his time. His queen and consorts were at odds, and legitimate and illegitimate sons slandered one another and quarreled until they fell into disgrace and the kingdom was extinguished. We are deeply grieved by this.
entries.literal: More than a month later, considering that he was most beloved, the emperor instructed the officials: 'King Xian of Changshan died young. His queen and consorts were not harmonious. Legitimate and illegitimate sons slandered and contended, falling into unrighteousness and extinguishing the kingdom. I greatly pity this.

entries.zh: 其封憲王子平三萬戶，為真定王；
entries.en: Enfeoff King Xian's son Ping as King of Zhending, with thirty thousand households;
entries.literal: Let King Xian's son Ping be enfeoffed with thirty thousand households as King of Zhending;

entries.zh: 封子商三萬戶，為泗水王。」
entries.en: and enfeoff his son Shang as King of Sishui, also with thirty thousand households."
entries.literal: and let his son Shang be enfeoffed with thirty thousand households as King of Sishui."

entries.zh: 六安王慶，以元狩二年用膠東康王子為六安王。
entries.en: King Qing of Liu'an, a son of King Kang of Jiaodong, was enfeoffed as King of Liu'an in the second year of the Yuanshou era.
entries.literal: King Qing of Liu'an was made King of Liu'an as son of King Kang of Jiaodong in the second year of Yuanshou.

entries.zh: 真定王平，元鼎四年用常山憲王子為真定王。
entries.en: King Ping of Zhending, a son of King Xian of Changshan, was enfeoffed as King of Zhending in the fourth year of the Yuanding era.
entries.literal: King Ping of Zhending was made King of Zhending as son of King Xian of Changshan in the fourth year of Yuanding.

entries.zh: 「維六年四月乙巳，皇帝使御史大夫湯廟立子閎為齊王。
entries.en: "In the sixth year, fourth month, on the yisi day, the Emperor sent the Grandee Secretary Tang to the ancestral temple to invest his son Hong as King of Qi.
entries.literal: 'In the fourth month of year 6, day yi-si, the Emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Tang to establish son Hong as King of Qi in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 曰：於戲，小子閎，受茲青社！
entries.en: He proclaimed: Alas, my young son Hong, receive this Altar of the Blue Earth!
entries.literal: Saying: Ah, young son Hong, receive this blue altar!

entries.zh: 朕承祖考，維稽古建爾國家，封于東土，世為漢藩輔。
entries.en: I, inheriting the legacy of my ancestors, have looked to the precedents of antiquity to establish your state. You are enfeoffed in the eastern lands and shall serve as a bulwark and support for the Han dynasty through all generations.
entries.literal: I succeed the ancestors, examining antiquity establish your state, enfeoff in the eastern lands, generation after generation as Han's border auxiliary.

entries.zh: 於戲念哉！
entries.en: Alas, keep this in mind!
entries.literal: Ah, remember this!

entries.zh: 抱朕之詔，惟命不于常。
entries.en: Cherish this edict of mine and remember that the mandate of Heaven is not constant.
entries.literal: Cherish my command, the mandate is not constant.

entries.zh: 人之好德，克明顯光。
entries.en: Those who love virtue can shine with a bright and brilliant light.
entries.literal: People who love virtue can clearly shine brightly.

entries.zh: 義之不圖，俾君子怠。
entries.en: When righteousness is not pursued, even the worthy become complacent.
entries.literal: Righteousness not planned for, causes the worthy to be indolent.

entries.zh: 悉爾心，允執其中，天祿永終。
entries.en: Devote your whole heart, faithfully hold to the Mean, and Heaven's blessings will endure forever.
entries.literal: Devote your whole heart, faithfully hold to the center; Heaven's blessings will endure to the end.

entries.zh: 厥有愆不臧，乃凶于而國，害于爾躬。
entries.en: Should there be transgressions or wrongdoing, disaster will befall your state and harm will come to your person.
entries.literal: If there are faults not good, then disaster to your state, harm to your person.

entries.zh: 於戲，保國艾民，可不敬與！
entries.en: Alas, to protect the state and cherish the people—can you afford not to be reverent!
entries.literal: Ah, protect the state and cherish the people, can you not be respectful!

entries.zh: 王其戒之。」
entries.en: Let the King take heed of this."
entries.literal: King, take heed of this.'

entries.zh: 「維六年四月乙巳，皇帝使御史大夫湯廟立子旦為燕王。
entries.en: "In the sixth year, fourth month, on the yisi day, the Emperor sent the Grandee Secretary Tang to the ancestral temple to invest his son Dan as King of Yan.
entries.literal: 'In the fourth month of year 6, day yi-si, the Emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Tang to establish son Dan as King of Yan in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 曰：於戲，小子旦，受茲玄社！
entries.en: He proclaimed: Alas, my young son Dan, receive this Altar of the Black Earth!
entries.literal: Saying: Ah, young son Dan, receive this black altar!

entries.zh: 朕承祖考，維稽古，建爾國家，封于北土，世為漢藩輔。
entries.en: I, inheriting the legacy of my ancestors and looking to the precedents of antiquity, have established your state. You are enfeoffed in the northern lands and shall serve as a bulwark and support for the Han dynasty through all generations.
entries.literal: I succeed the ancestors, examining antiquity establish your state, enfeoff in the northern lands, generation after generation as Han's border auxiliary.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Ah!

entries.zh: 葷粥氏虐老獸心，侵犯寇盜，加以姦巧邊萌。
entries.en: The Xiongnu are cruel to the aged and beast-hearted, invading and plundering as bandits and thieves, and moreover they deal treacherously with the border settlements.
entries.literal: The Hun You clan cruel aged beast heart, invading as bandits and thieves, moreover treacherous at the border settlements.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Ah!

entries.zh: 朕命將率徂征厥罪，萬夫長，千夫長，三十有二君皆來，降期奔師。
entries.en: I commanded my generals to march forth and punish their crimes; leaders of ten thousand, leaders of a thousand, and thirty-two chieftains all came forth, surrendering at the appointed time and rallying to our forces.
entries.literal: I commanded generals to go punish their crimes; ten-thousand-man leaders, thousand-man leaders, and thirty-two lords all came, surrendering at the appointed time and fleeing to our forces.

entries.zh: 葷粥徙域，北州以綏。
entries.en: The Xiongnu withdrew from their lands, and the northern provinces were thereby pacified.
entries.literal: Hun You moved their territory, northern provinces thus pacified.

entries.zh: 悉爾心，毋作怨，毋卹德，毋乃廢備。
entries.en: Devote your whole heart to this charge: do not stir up resentment, do not turn from virtue, and do not abandon your defenses.
entries.literal: Devote your whole heart; do not stir up resentment, do not turn from virtue, and do not neglect your preparations.

entries.zh: 非教士不得從徵。
entries.en: Those who have not been trained in proper conduct may not be taken on military campaigns.
entries.literal: Non-educated men may not follow the expedition.

entries.zh: 於戲，保國艾民，可不敬與！
entries.en: Alas, to protect the state and cherish the people—can you afford not to be reverent!
entries.literal: Ah, protect the state and cherish the people, can you not be respectful!

entries.zh: 王其戒之。」
entries.en: Let the King take heed of this."
entries.literal: King, take heed of this.'

entries.zh: 「維六年四月乙巳，皇帝使御史大夫湯廟立子胥為廣陵王。
entries.en: "In the sixth year, fourth month, on the yisi day, the Emperor sent the Grandee Secretary Tang to the ancestral temple to invest his son Xu as King of Guangling.
entries.literal: 'In the fourth month of year 6, day yi-si, the Emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Tang to establish son Xu as King of Guangling in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 曰：於戲，小子胥，受茲赤社！
entries.en: He proclaimed: Alas, my young son Xu, receive this Altar of the Red Earth!
entries.literal: Saying: Ah, young son Xu, receive this red altar!

entries.zh: 朕承祖考，維稽古建爾國家，封于南土，世為漢藩輔。
entries.en: I, inheriting the legacy of my ancestors and looking to the precedents of antiquity, have established your state. You are enfeoffed in the southern lands and shall serve as a bulwark and support for the Han dynasty through all generations.
entries.literal: I succeed the ancestors, examining antiquity establish your state, enfeoff in the southern lands, generation after generation as Han's border auxiliary.

entries.zh: 古人有言曰：『大江之南，五湖之閒，其人輕心。
entries.en: The ancients had a saying: 'South of the Great River, among the Five Lakes, the people are fickle of heart.
entries.literal: Ancient people have said: 'South of the great river, between the five lakes, their people are light-hearted.

entries.zh: 楊州保疆，三代要服，不及以政。』
entries.en: The region of Yang Province guards its borders; through the Three Dynasties it was a tributary territory that the central administration did not fully reach.'
entries.literal: Yang province guards the borders, three dynasties' important territory, not reached by administration.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Ah!

entries.zh: 悉爾心，戰戰兢兢，乃惠乃順，毋侗好軼，毋邇宵人，維法維則。
entries.en: Devote your whole heart to this charge, trembling with caution; be benevolent and compliant. Do not be reckless or fond of excess, do not draw near to petty men, and cleave to the laws and rules.
entries.literal: Use all your heart, be cautious and fearful, be benevolent and compliant, do not be ignorant and fond of excess, do not approach villains, follow law and rules.

entries.zh: 《書》云：『臣不作威，不作福，靡有後羞。』
entries.en: The Book of Documents says: 'Let the minister not arrogate authority, nor bestow favors on his own—then there shall be no later shame.'
entries.literal: The Book says: 'Ministers do not create awe, do not create blessings, there will be no later shame.'

entries.zh: 於戲，保國艾民，可不敬與！
entries.en: Alas, to protect the state and cherish the people—can you afford not to be reverent!
entries.literal: Ah, protect the state and cherish the people, can you not be respectful!

entries.zh: 王其戒之。」
entries.en: Let the King take heed of this."
entries.literal: King, take heed of this.'

entries.zh: 太史公曰：古人有言曰「愛之欲其富，親之欲其貴」。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: The ancients had a saying: "Those you love, you wish to be wealthy; those you are close to, you wish to be honored."
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: Ancient people have said 'Love them wish them rich, be close wish them noble'.

entries.zh: 故王者壃土建國，封立子弟，所以褒親親，序骨肉，尊先祖，貴支體，廣同姓於天下也。
entries.en: For this reason kings demarcate territories and establish states, investing their sons and younger brothers. In this way they honor their closest kin, order the bonds of flesh and blood, venerate their ancestors, exalt the collateral branches, and spread their surname throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Therefore, kings pile earth and establish states, enfeoff and establish sons and younger brothers, thus to praise close relatives, order flesh and blood, honor ancestors, value branches and limbs, spread same surname throughout the world.
