entries.zh: 是以形勢彊而王室安。
entries.en: In this way, the strategic position grows strong, and the royal house remains secure.
entries.literal: Therefore, the situation is strong and the royal house secure.

entries.zh: 自古至今，所由來久矣。
entries.en: From antiquity down to the present, this has been the established practice for a very long time.
entries.literal: From ancient times to now, what has come from this is long established.

entries.zh: 非有異也，故弗論箸也。
entries.en: Since there is nothing unusual about it, I have not discussed or recorded it at length.
entries.literal: No difference, therefore not discussed and recorded.

entries.zh: 燕齊之事，無足采者。
entries.en: As for the affairs of the kingdoms of Yan and Qi, there is nothing of particular note worth recording.
entries.literal: Yan and Qi matters have nothing worth collecting.

entries.zh: 然封立三王，天子恭讓，群臣守義，文辭爛然，甚可觀也，是以附之世家。
entries.en: However, in the investiture of the three kings, the Son of Heaven displayed exemplary modesty, the ministers upheld their principles, and the documents produced are brilliant in their literary quality and well worth reading. For this reason I have appended them to the Hereditary Houses.
entries.literal: However, establishing the three kings, the Son of Heaven is respectfully modest, ministers uphold righteousness, the literary style is brilliant, very worthy of observation, therefore attached to the hereditary houses.

entries.zh: 蓋聞孝武帝之時，同日而俱拜三子為王：封一子於齊，一子於廣陵，一子於燕。
entries.en: I have heard that in the time of Emperor Xiaowu, on a single day all three of his sons were invested as kings: one was enfeoffed in Qi, one in Guangling, and one in Yan.
entries.literal: I have heard that in Xiaowu Emperor's time, on the same day all three sons were appointed as kings: enfeoffed one son in Qi, one son in Guangling, one son in Yan.

entries.zh: 各因子才力智能，及土地之剛柔，人民之輕重，為作策以申戒之。
entries.en: For each son, according to his talents, abilities, and intelligence, and according to the character of the land—whether harsh or gentle—and the temperament of the people—whether headstrong or docile—the Emperor composed charters to earnestly admonish them.
entries.literal: Each according to the son's talent strength intelligence, and the land's hardness softness, people's lightness heaviness, made charters to earnestly warn them.

entries.zh: 謂王：「世為漢藩輔，保國治民，可不敬與！
entries.en: He told each king: "You shall serve through all generations as a bulwark and support of the Han—to protect the state and govern the people, can you afford not to be reverent!
entries.literal: Telling the kings: 'Generation after generation as Han's border auxiliaries, protect the state govern the people, can you not be respectful!

entries.zh: 王其戒之。」
entries.en: Let the King take heed of this."
entries.literal: Kings, take heed of this.'

entries.zh: 夫賢主所作，固非淺聞者所能知，非博聞彊記君子者所不能究竟其意。
entries.en: What a wise sovereign composes is certainly beyond the understanding of those of shallow learning; only a gentleman of broad erudition and powerful memory can fathom its full meaning.
entries.literal: What a wise ruler makes is certainly not something shallow learners can know; it is not something that gentlemen of broad learning and strong memory cannot thoroughly fathom in its intent.

entries.zh: 至其次序分絕，文字之上下，簡之參差長短，皆有意，人莫之能知。
entries.en: Even the ordering, divisions, and breaks, the arrangement of the text, and the varying lengths of the bamboo slips—all carry meaning that ordinary people cannot discern.
entries.literal: Even the sequence divisions and breaks, the up and down of writing, the uneven lengths of slips, all have meaning, people cannot know it.

entries.zh: 謹論次其真草詔書，編于左方。
entries.en: I have respectfully arranged the authentic draft edicts in proper order, compiled on the left.
entries.literal: Respectfully arranged their true draft edicts, compiled on the left side.

entries.zh: 令覽者自通其意而解說之。
entries.en: I leave it to the reader to work out the meaning and interpret it for himself.
entries.literal: Cause viewers to connect their meaning and explain it themselves.

entries.zh: 褚先生曰：臣幸得以文學為侍郎，好覽觀太史公之列傳。
entries.en: Master Chu says: I was fortunate enough to serve as a Palace Attendant through my literary abilities, and I took pleasure in reading the Grand Historian's Biographies.
entries.literal: Master Chu says: Subject fortunately became a literary attendant, likes to view and observe the Grand Historian's biographies.

entries.zh: 傳中稱三王世家文辭可觀，求其世家終不能得。
entries.en: In the Biographies it is stated that the Hereditary House of the Three Kings is noteworthy for the quality of its prose, yet when I searched for this hereditary house chapter, I could never find it.
entries.literal: The biographies mention the Three Kings hereditary house literary style worthy of observation, sought its hereditary house ultimately could not obtain.

entries.zh: 竊從長老好故事者取其封策書，編列其事而傳之，令後世得觀賢主之指意。
entries.en: I privately obtained the enfeoffment charters from elderly scholars who were fond of historical precedents, arranged the events in order, and transmitted them, so that later generations might observe the intentions of a wise sovereign.
entries.literal: Secretly from elders who love precedents took their enfeoffment charter writings, arranged and transmitted their matters, causing later generations to observe the wise ruler's intentions.

entries.zh: 王夫人者，趙人也，與衛夫人并幸武帝，而生子閎。
entries.en: Lady Wang was a native of Zhao. She and Lady Wei were both favored by Emperor Wu, and she bore him a son named Hong.
entries.literal: Lady Wang was a woman of Zhao, together with Lady Wei both favored by Wudi, and bore son Hong.

entries.zh: 閎且立為王時，其母病，武帝自臨問之。
entries.en: When Hong was about to be invested as king, his mother fell ill, and Emperor Wu personally went to visit her.
entries.literal: When Hong was about to be established as king, his mother was ill, Wudi personally visited and asked her.

entries.zh: 曰：「子當為王，欲安所置之？」
entries.en: He asked: "Your son is to be made a king—where would you like him to be placed?"
entries.literal: Saying: 'Son should become king, where do you wish to place him?'

entries.zh: 王夫人曰：「陛下在，妾又何等可言者。」
entries.en: Lady Wang replied: "While Your Majesty is alive, what should I possibly have to say?"
entries.literal: Lady Wang said: 'Your Majesty is alive, what else can subject wife say.'

entries.zh: 帝曰：「雖然，意所欲，欲於何所王之？」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Even so, what is your wish? In what place would you like him to be made king?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Although this, what is your intention, in what place do you wish to make him king?'

entries.zh: 王夫人曰：「願置之雒陽。」
entries.en: Lady Wang said: "I would wish to have him placed in Luoyang."
entries.literal: Lady Wang said: 'Wish to place him in Luoyang.'

entries.zh: 武帝曰：「雒陽有武庫敖倉，天下衝阸，漢國之大都也。
entries.en: Emperor Wu said: "Luoyang has the imperial armory and the Ao granary; it is the crossroads of the realm and the great capital of the Han.
entries.literal: Wudi said: 'Luoyang has the armory and Ao granary, world's thoroughfare, Han's great capital.

entries.zh: 先帝以來，無子王於雒陽者。
entries.en: Since the time of the former emperors, no prince has ever been made king at Luoyang.
entries.literal: From previous emperors, no son has been made king in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 去雒陽，餘盡可。」
entries.en: Apart from Luoyang, all other places are acceptable."
entries.literal: Except Luoyang, the rest are all acceptable.'

entries.zh: 王夫人不應。
entries.en: Lady Wang made no reply.
entries.literal: Lady Wang did not respond.

entries.zh: 武帝曰：「關東之國無大於齊者。
entries.en: Emperor Wu said: "Among the states east of the passes, none is greater than Qi.
entries.literal: Wudi said: 'Among the Guandong states none is greater than Qi.

entries.zh: 齊東負海而城郭大，古時獨臨菑中十萬戶，天下膏腴地莫盛於齊者矣。」
entries.en: Qi has the sea at its eastern back and great city walls; in ancient times, the capital Linzi alone contained a hundred thousand households. Of all the fertile lands in the realm, none surpasses Qi."
entries.literal: Qi east faces the sea with great city walls, in ancient times Linzi alone had 100,000 households, the world's fertile lands none more prosperous than Qi.'

entries.zh: 王夫人以手擊頭，謝曰：「幸甚。」
entries.en: Lady Wang struck her forehead with her hand in gratitude and said: "How fortunate!"
entries.literal: Lady Wang struck her head with her hand, thanked saying: 'Very fortunate.'

entries.zh: 王夫人死而帝痛之，使使者拜之曰：「皇帝謹使使太中大夫明奉璧一，賜夫人為齊王太后。」
entries.en: When Lady Wang died, the Emperor grieved for her deeply and sent an envoy to make a posthumous proclamation: "The Emperor respectfully dispatches the Grand Palace Attendant Ming to present one jade bi disk and bestows upon the Lady the title of Queen Dowager of the King of Qi."
entries.literal: Lady Wang died and the emperor grieved for her, sent envoys to confer saying: 'The Emperor respectfully sends Grand Palace Attendant Ming to present one jade disk, granting Lady to be Queen Mother of King of Qi.'

entries.zh: 子閎王齊，年少，無有子，立，不幸早死，國絕，為郡。
entries.en: Her son Hong reigned as King of Qi, but he was young and had no sons. After his investiture he unfortunately died young, the kingdom was extinguished, and its territory was converted into a commandery.
entries.literal: Son Hong ruled Qi, young, had no sons, established, unfortunately died early, kingdom extinguished, became a commandery.

entries.zh: 天下稱齊不宜王云。
entries.en: People throughout the realm said that Qi was not a suitable place for a king.
entries.literal: The world says Qi is not suitable for kings.

entries.zh: 會孝武帝崩，孝昭帝初立，先朝廣陵王胥，厚賞賜金錢財幣，直三千餘萬，益地百里，邑萬戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu passed away and Emperor Xiaozhao first ascended the throne, he summoned the King of Guangling, Xu, to court and lavished upon him rewards of gold, money, and other valuables worth over thirty million, adding a hundred li to his territory and ten thousand households to his domain.
entries.literal: When Xiaowu Emperor passed away, Xiao Zhao Emperor first established, first summoned King Xu of Guangling, thickly rewarded gold money wealth currency, worth over 30 million, increased land 100 li, townships 10,000 households.

entries.zh: 傳曰「青采出於藍，而質青於藍」者，教使然也。
entries.en: The tradition that says "blue dye comes from the indigo plant, yet is bluer than indigo itself" speaks to the transformative power of proper instruction.
entries.literal: The tradition says 'Blue comes from indigo but is bluer than indigo', teaching makes it so.

entries.zh: 遠哉賢主，昭然獨見：誡齊王以慎內；
entries.en: How far-sighted was the wise sovereign, seeing clearly what no one else perceived! He admonished the King of Qi to be prudent in internal affairs;
entries.literal: Far indeed the wise ruler, clearly seeing alone: warned King of Qi to be careful within;

entries.zh: 誡燕王以無作怨，無修德；
entries.en: he admonished the King of Yan not to stir up resentment and not to cultivate virtue;
entries.literal: warned the King of Yan not to create resentment, not to cultivate virtue;

entries.zh: 誡廣陵王以慎外，無作威與福。
entries.en: and he admonished the King of Guangling to be prudent in external affairs and not to arrogate authority or bestow favors.
entries.literal: warned King of Guangling to be careful without, not to create awe and blessings.

entries.zh: 齊地多變詐，不習於禮義，故戒之曰「恭朕之詔，唯命不可為常。
entries.en: The land of Qi is prone to scheming and deception, its people unaccustomed to ritual propriety and righteousness. Therefore, the admonishment states: "Revere this edict of mine. Remember that the mandate is never constant.
entries.literal: Qi land has much deceit and deception, not accustomed to rites and righteousness, therefore warned saying 'Cherish my edict, the mandate cannot be constant.

entries.zh: 人之好德，能明顯光。
entries.en: Those who love virtue can shine with a bright and brilliant light.
entries.literal: People who love virtue can clearly shine brightly.

entries.zh: 不圖於義，使君子怠慢。
entries.en: When righteousness is not pursued, even the worthy become negligent.
entries.literal: Not planning for righteousness causes the worthy to be indolent.

entries.zh: 悉若心，信執其中，天祿長終。
entries.en: Devote your whole heart, faithfully hold to the Mean, and Heaven's blessings will endure to the end.
entries.literal: Devote your whole heart, faithfully hold to the center; Heaven's blessings will endure to the end.

entries.zh: 有過不善，乃凶于而國，而害于若身」。
entries.en: Should there be transgressions or wrongdoing, disaster will befall your state and harm will come to your person."
entries.literal: If there are faults not good, then disaster to your state, harm to your person.'

entries.zh: 齊王之國，左右維持以禮義，不幸中年早夭。
entries.en: The King of Qi governed his state with those around him upholding ritual propriety and righteousness, but unfortunately he died young in his prime.
entries.literal: The King of Qi's rule, left and right maintained with rites and righteousness, unfortunately died young in middle age.

entries.zh: 然全身無過，如其策意。
entries.en: Nevertheless, he preserved himself without fault, just as the charter had intended.
entries.literal: However, kept body without faults, as the charter intended.

entries.zh: 夫廣陵在吳越之地，其民精而輕，故誡之曰「江湖之閒，其人輕心。
entries.en: Guangling lies in the lands of Wu and Yue, whose people are clever but fickle. Therefore, the admonishment states: "Among the rivers and lakes, the people are inconstant of heart.
entries.literal: Now Guangling is in Wu and Yue lands, their people are clever and light, therefore warned saying 'Between the rivers and lakes, their people are light-hearted.

entries.zh: 楊州葆疆，三代之時，迫要使從中國俗服，不大及以政教，以意御之而已。
entries.en: Yang Province guarded its borders; in the time of the Three Dynasties it was compelled to adopt the customs and attire of the Central States, but the central government did not fully extend its administration and instruction there, governing it in principle only.
entries.literal: Yang province guards borders, in Three Dynasties time, compelled to make follow Central States customs and clothing, not greatly reaching with governance and teaching, only control with intention.

entries.zh: 無侗好佚，無邇宵人，維法是則。
entries.en: Do not be reckless or fond of idleness, do not draw near to petty men, and always take the law as your guide.
entries.literal: Do not be ignorant fond of leisure, do not approach villains, follow law as rule.

entries.zh: 無長好佚樂馳騁弋獵淫康，而近小人。
entries.en: Do not develop a lasting fondness for idle pleasures, racing, hunting, and indulgence, or draw close to petty men.
entries.literal: Do not long love leisure pleasure racing hunting indulgence, and approach small men.

entries.zh: 常念法度，則無羞辱矣」。
entries.en: Always keep the laws and standards in mind, and you will be free of shame and disgrace."
entries.literal: Always think of law and standards, then there will be no shame and humiliation.'

entries.zh: 三江、五湖有魚鹽之利，銅山之富，天下所仰。
entries.en: The Three Rivers and Five Lakes yield the profits of fish and salt, and the copper mountains produce great wealth—resources upon which the entire realm depends.
entries.literal: The three rivers and five lakes have fish and salt profits, copper mountain wealth, what the world looks up to.

entries.zh: 故誡之曰「臣不作福」者，勿使行財幣，厚賞賜，以立聲譽，為四方所歸也。
entries.en: Therefore, the admonishment "let the minister not bestow favors" means that he should not distribute wealth and gifts freely or lavish rewards in order to build a reputation and become a rallying point for people from all quarters.
entries.literal: Therefore, warned saying 'ministers do not create blessings' means do not let them circulate wealth and currency, give thick rewards, to establish reputation, become what four directions return to.

entries.zh: 又曰「臣不作威」者，勿使因輕以倍義也。
entries.en: The further admonishment "let the minister not arrogate authority" means that he should not exploit the people's fickleness to forsake righteousness.
entries.literal: Also saying 'ministers do not create awe' means do not let them because of lightness betray righteousness.

entries.zh: 會昭帝崩，宣帝初立，緣恩行義，以本始元年中，裂漢地，盡以封廣陵王胥四子：一子為朝陽侯；
entries.en: When Emperor Zhao passed away and Emperor Xuan first ascended the throne, extending favor and practicing righteousness, in the middle of the first year of the Benshi era he carved out Han territory and enfeoffed all four sons of the King of Guangling, Xu: one son was made Marquis of Chaoyang;
entries.literal: When Zhao Emperor passed away, Xuan Emperor first established, following benevolence practicing righteousness, in Benshi first year middle, split Han territory, all to enfeoff King Xu of Guangling's four sons: one son as Chaoyang Marquis;

entries.zh: 一子為平曲侯；
entries.en: one son was made Marquis of Pingqu;
entries.literal: one son as Pingqu Marquis;

entries.zh: 一子為南利侯；
entries.en: one son was made Marquis of Nanli;
entries.literal: one son as Nanli Marquis;

entries.zh: 最愛少子弘，立以為高密王。
entries.en: and his most beloved youngest son, Hong, was established as King of Gaomi.
entries.literal: most loved youngest son Hong, established as King of Gaomi.

entries.zh: 會武帝年老長，而太子不幸薨，未有所立，而旦使來上書，請身入宿衛於長安。
entries.en: In time, Emperor Wu grew old, and the Crown Prince unfortunately died. No successor had yet been established when Dan sent a memorial requesting permission to come to Chang'an in person to serve in the palace guard.
entries.literal: When Wudi grew old, and the crown prince unfortunately died, not yet established successor, yet Dan sent to submit memorial, requesting personally enter guard duty in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 孝武見其書，擊地，怒曰：「生子當置之齊魯禮義之鄉，乃置之燕趙，果有爭心，不讓之端見矣。」
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu read the memorial, he struck the ground in rage and said: "When a son is born, he should be placed in the land of Qi and Lu, where ritual propriety and righteousness prevail. Instead, I placed him in Yan and Zhao, and sure enough he has developed a contentious spirit—the first signs of insubordination are already showing."
entries.literal: Xiaowu seeing his memorial, struck ground, angry saying: 'Giving birth to son should place in Qi Lu rites and righteousness lands, yet placed in Yan Zhao, indeed has contending heart, unyielding beginning appears.'

entries.zh: 於是使使即斬其使者於闕下。
entries.en: He then had Dan's envoy beheaded at the foot of the palace gate.
entries.literal: Thus, sent envoys immediately behead his envoy at the palace gate.

entries.zh: 會武帝崩，昭帝初立，旦果作怨而望大臣。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died and Emperor Zhao first ascended the throne, Dan did indeed nurture resentment and harbored expectations of the great ministers.
entries.literal: When Wudi passed away, Zhao Emperor first established, Dan indeed created resentment and hoped from ministers.

entries.zh: 自以長子當立，與齊王子劉澤等謀為叛逆，出言曰：「我安得弟在者！
entries.en: Considering himself the eldest surviving son and therefore the rightful heir, he plotted rebellion with the son of a former King of Qi, Liu Ze, and others. He declared: "How can it be that I have a younger brother who still lives!
entries.literal: Considering himself eldest son should establish, with Qi king's son Liu Ze and others plotted rebellion, spoke saying: 'How can I have younger brother alive!

entries.zh: 今立者乃大將軍子也。」
entries.en: The one now on the throne is merely the son of the Grand General."
entries.literal: Now established is the Grand General's son.'

entries.zh: 欲發兵。
entries.en: He intended to raise troops.
entries.literal: Wished to raise troops.

entries.zh: 事發覺，當誅。
entries.en: The plot was discovered, and by rights he should have been executed.
entries.literal: Matter discovered, should be executed.

entries.zh: 昭帝緣恩寬忍，抑案不揚。
entries.en: Emperor Zhao, out of familial kindness and forbearance, suppressed the case and did not publicize it.
entries.literal: Zhao Emperor following benevolence tolerant, suppressed case not publicized.

entries.zh: 公卿使大臣請，遣宗正與太中大夫公戶滿意、御史二人，偕往使燕，風喻之。
entries.en: The ministers at court petitioned for action, and the Director of the Imperial Clan was dispatched along with the Grand Palace Attendant Gong Hu Manyi and two Imperial Censors, who together traveled as envoys to Yan to admonish Dan indirectly.
entries.literal: Dukes and ministers had ministers request, sent Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan and Grand Palace Attendant Gong Hu Man Yi, two censors, together go as envoys to Yan, indirectly admonish him.

entries.zh: 到燕，各異日，更見責王。
entries.en: When they arrived in Yan, they visited the King on different days, each in turn reproaching him.
entries.literal: Arrived in Yan, each different day, alternately saw and reproached the king.

entries.zh: 宗正者，主宗室諸劉屬籍，先見王，為列陳道昭帝實武帝子狀。
entries.en: The Director of the Imperial Clan, who oversees the genealogical registers of all the Liu members of the imperial family, was the first to see the King. He methodically laid out the evidence that Emperor Zhao was in truth the son of Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, manages imperial clan various Liu genealogy, first saw king, listed and explained Zhao Emperor truly Wudi's son situation.

entries.zh: 侍御史乃復見王，責之以正法，問：「王欲發兵罪名明白，當坐之。
entries.en: The Attendant Censor then visited the King in turn, confronting him with the law. He declared: "The King's intention to raise troops is a clearly established crime, and by law he should be condemned for it.
entries.literal: Attendant Censor then again saw king, reproached with proper law, asked: 'King wishes to raise troops crime name clear, should condemn him.

entries.zh: 漢家有正法，王犯纖介小罪過，即行法直斷耳，安能寬王。」
entries.en: The House of Han has its established law: if the King commits even the slightest offense, the law is carried out and judgment delivered—how could leniency be shown to the King?"
entries.literal: Han house has proper law, king commits tiny small offense, immediately carries out law straight judgment, how can pardon king.'

entries.zh: 驚動以文法。
entries.en: He shook and intimidated the King with the statutes and laws.
entries.literal: Shocked and moved with statutes and laws.

entries.zh: 王意益下，心恐。
entries.en: The King's defiance crumbled further, and fear seized his heart.
entries.literal: King's intent increasingly lowered, heart feared.

entries.zh: 公戶滿意習於經術，最後見王，稱引古今通義，國家大禮，文章爾雅。
entries.en: Gong Hu Manyi, well versed in the classics, was the last to see the King. He cited the universal principles of antiquity and the present, spoke of the great rites of the state, and his words were elegant and refined.
entries.literal: Gong Hu Man Yi versed in classics, last saw king, cited ancient and modern universal principles, state great rites, writings elegant and proper.

entries.zh: 謂王曰：「古者天子必內有異姓大夫，所以正骨肉也；
entries.en: He addressed the King: "In ancient times, the Son of Heaven always had ministers of different surnames within the court to keep his own flesh and blood in check;
entries.literal: Told king: 'Anciently Son of Heaven must have different surname officials within, thus to correct flesh and blood;

entries.zh: 外有同姓大夫，所以正異族也。
entries.en: and he had ministers of the same surname without to keep other clans in order.
entries.literal: without have same surname officials, thus to correct different clans.

entries.zh: 周公輔成王，誅其兩弟，故治。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou, in assisting King Cheng, put his own two brothers to death, and thereby brought order to the realm.
entries.literal: Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, executed his two younger brothers, thus orderly.

entries.zh: 武帝在時，尚能寬王。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu was alive, he could still afford to show the King leniency.
entries.literal: Wudi in his time, still could pardon king.

entries.zh: 今昭帝始立，年幼，富於春秋，未臨政，委任大臣。
entries.en: Now Emperor Zhao has only just ascended the throne; he is young in years, still in his youth, has not yet taken personal charge of the government, and has entrusted affairs to the ministers.
entries.literal: Now Zhao Emperor first established, year young, rich in springtime, not yet administering government, entrusts ministers.

entries.zh: 古者誅罰不阿親戚，故天下治。
entries.en: In ancient times, executions and punishments were carried out without favoritism toward kinsmen, and thus the realm was well governed.
entries.literal: Anciently executions and punishments did not favor relatives, thus world orderly.

entries.zh: 方今大臣輔政，奉法直行，無敢所阿，恐不能寬王。
entries.en: At present the great ministers assist in governing and apply the law without deviation; none dares to show partiality. I fear they will not be able to show the King leniency.
entries.literal: Now ministers assist government, follow law straight action, none dare favor, fear cannot pardon king.

entries.zh: 王可自謹，無自令身死國滅，為天下笑。」
entries.en: The King should exercise the utmost caution, lest he bring about his own death and the destruction of his kingdom, making himself a laughingstock for all the realm."
entries.literal: King can be careful himself, not cause body die kingdom extinguish, become world's laughter.'

entries.zh: 於是燕王旦乃恐懼服罪，叩頭謝過。
entries.en: At this, the King of Yan, Dan, was seized with fear and admitted his guilt, kowtowing and begging forgiveness for his offense.
entries.literal: Thus, King Dan of Yan then feared and submitted to crime, kowtowed apologized for offense.

entries.zh: 大臣欲和合骨肉，難傷之以法。
entries.en: The great ministers wished to preserve harmony among the imperial kinsmen and found it difficult to apply the full force of the law against him.
entries.literal: Ministers wished to harmonize flesh and blood, difficult to harm with law.

entries.zh: 燕土墝埆，北迫匈奴，其人民勇而少慮，故誡之曰「葷粥氏無有孝行而禽獸心，以竊盜侵犯邊民。
entries.en: The land of Yan is rocky and barren, pressed close to the Xiongnu on the north, and its people are brave but reckless. Therefore, the admonishment states: "The Xiongnu have no sense of filial duty and are beastly in nature, plundering and invading the border settlements.
entries.literal: Yan land is uneven and barren, north presses Xiongnu, their people brave but little thought, therefore warned saying 'Xiongnu clan has no filial conduct but beast heart, with theft invades border people.

entries.zh: 朕詔將軍往征其罪，萬夫長，千夫長，三十有二君皆來，降旗奔師。
entries.en: I commanded my generals to march forth and punish their crimes; leaders of ten thousand, leaders of a thousand, and thirty-two chieftains all came forward, lowering their banners and surrendering to our forces.
entries.literal: I commanded generals to go punish their crimes, ten thousand man leaders, thousand man leaders, thirty-two lords all came, surrendered banners fled army.

entries.zh: 葷粥徙域遠處，北州以安矣」。
entries.en: The Xiongnu withdrew to their distant territories, and the northern provinces were thereby pacified."
entries.literal: Xiongnu moved territory far away, northern provinces thus pacified.'

entries.zh: 「悉若心，無作怨」者，勿使從俗以怨望也。
entries.en: "Devote your whole heart, do not stir up resentment" means that he should not follow local customs in harboring grudges and resentful ambitions.
entries.literal: 'Use all your heart, do not create resentment' means do not let them follow customs to resent and hope.

entries.zh: 「無俷德」者，勿使（上）［王］背德也。
entries.en: "Do not turn from virtue" means that the King should not turn his back on virtuous conduct.
entries.literal: 'Do not go against virtue' means do not let the king turn back on virtue.

entries.zh: 「無廢備」者，無乏武備，常備匈奴也。
entries.en: "Do not abandon your defenses" means do not let the martial preparations lapse, but maintain constant readiness against the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: 'Do not neglect preparations' means do not lack martial preparations, constantly prepare for Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 「非教士不得從徵」者，言非習禮義不得在於側也。
entries.en: "Those who have not been trained may not be taken on campaigns" means that those who have not been instructed in ritual propriety and righteousness may not serve at his side.
entries.literal: 'Non-educated men may not follow expedition' means non-accustomed to rites and righteousness may not be at the side.

entries.zh: 宣帝初立，推恩宣德，以本始元年中盡復封燕王旦兩子：一子為安定侯；
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan first ascended the throne, he extended favor and proclaimed his virtue. In the middle of the first year of the Benshi era, he restored the enfeoffments of both of the late King Dan of Yan's sons: one was made Marquis of Anding;
entries.literal: Xuan Emperor first established, extended benevolence proclaimed virtue, in Benshi first year middle all restored enfeoffment of King Dan of Yan's two sons: one son as An Ding Marquis;

entries.zh: 立燕故太子建為廣陽王，以奉燕王祭祀。
entries.en: and the former Crown Prince of Yan, Jian, was established as King of Guangyang, to continue the sacrifices to the kings of Yan.
entries.literal: established Yan's former crown prince Jian as King of Guangyang, to carry out Yan king's sacrifices.

entries.zh: 「大司馬臣去病昧死再拜上疏皇帝陛下：陛下過聽，使臣去病待罪行閒。
entries.en: "Your servant, the Grand Marshal Qubing, at the risk of death bows twice and submits this memorial to His Imperial Majesty: Your Majesty has shown me far too much favor, allowing your servant Qubing to hold an undeserved position among the ranks of honor.
entries.literal: 'Grand Marshal subject Qubing, risking death, bows twice and submits memorial to Emperor Your Majesty: Your Majesty has favored me excessively, allowing subject Qubing to await punishment in the ranks of the honored.

entries.zh: 宜專邊塞之思慮，暴骸中野無以報，乃敢惟他議以干用事者，誠見陛下憂勞天下，哀憐百姓以自忘，虧膳貶樂，損郎員。
entries.en: By rights, I ought to devote all my thoughts to the frontier, and even if I left my bones bleaching in the wilderness I could never repay Your Majesty's grace. Yet I dare raise another matter and trouble those who conduct affairs of state, for I have truly witnessed Your Majesty toiling on behalf of the realm, pitying the common people until you forget your own well-being, cutting your meals, forgoing your pleasures, and reducing the number of court attendants.
entries.literal: I should focus my thoughts solely on border defenses, yet even exposing my bones in the wilderness cannot repay, yet I dare contemplate other matters to interfere with those handling affairs, sincerely seeing Your Majesty toil for the world, pity the people to the point of forgetting yourself, reducing meals and diminishing pleasures, cutting the number of attendants.

entries.zh: 皇子賴天，能勝衣趨拜，至今無號位師傅官。
entries.en: The imperial princes, blessed by Heaven, have grown old enough to dress in formal robes and perform court obeisances, yet to this day they have received no royal titles, no official positions, and no appointed tutors.
entries.literal: The imperial sons rely on heaven, able to dress and make formal bows, yet to this day have no titles, positions, tutors, or officials.

entries.zh: 陛下恭讓不恤，群臣私望，不敢越職而言。
entries.en: Your Majesty, out of modesty, has not attended to this matter. The ministers all harbor private hopes regarding it, yet none dares overstep his office to speak.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is respectfully modest and does not worry, the ministers privately hope, but dare not speak beyond their duties.

entries.zh: 臣竊不勝犬馬心，昧死願陛下詔有司，因盛夏吉時定皇子位。
entries.en: Your servant, unable to restrain his humble devotion, at the risk of death begs Your Majesty to command the proper officials to take advantage of this auspicious midsummer season to establish the imperial princes in their rightful positions.
entries.literal: Your servant secretly cannot contain his dog-and-horse heart, risking death wishes Your Majesty to command the officials, taking advantage of the auspicious summer season to establish the imperial sons' positions.

entries.zh: 唯陛下幸察。
entries.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to consider this petition.
entries.literal: Only may Your Majesty be so gracious as to examine this.

entries.zh: 臣去病昧死再拜以聞皇帝陛下。」
entries.en: Your servant Qubing, at the risk of death, bows twice to bring this to His Imperial Majesty's attention."
entries.literal: Subject Qubing risks death, bows twice, to inform Emperor Your Majesty.'

entries.zh: 三月乙亥，御史臣光守尚書令奏未央宮。
entries.en: On the yihai day of the third month, the Imperial Censor Guang, serving as Prefect of the Imperial Secretariat, presented the memorial at Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: Third month, day yi-hai, Censor subject Guang acting as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat memorialized at Weiyang Palace.

entries.zh: 制曰：「下御史。」
entries.en: The imperial edict read: "Forward this to the Imperial Censor."
entries.literal: Imperial command: 'Send to the Censor.'

entries.zh: 伯夷、叔齊，孤竹君之二子也。
entries.en: Bo Yi and Shu Qi were sons of the ruler of Guzhu.
entries.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi were the two sons of the lord of Guzhu.

entries.zh: 父欲立叔齊，及父卒，叔齊讓伯夷。
entries.en: Their father wished to establish Shu Qi. When their father died, Shu Qi yielded to Bo Yi.
entries.literal: Father wished to establish Shu Qi, when father died, Shu Qi yielded to Bo Yi.

entries.zh: 伯夷曰：「父命也。」
entries.en: Bo Yi said, "It is our father's command."
entries.literal: Bo Yi said: 'It is our father's command.'

entries.zh: 遂逃去。
entries.en: Thus, he fled away.
entries.literal: Thus, fled away.

entries.zh: 叔齊亦不肯立而逃之。
entries.en: Shu Qi likewise refused to take the throne and fled.
entries.literal: Shu Qi also refused to take the throne and fled.

entries.zh: 國人立其中子。
entries.en: The people of the state then installed the middle son.
entries.literal: The people of the state established their middle son.

entries.zh: 於是伯夷、叔齊聞西伯昌善養老，盍往歸焉。
entries.en: Thereupon Bo Yi and Shu Qi heard that the Earl of the West, Chang, was good at supporting the elderly, and thought they would go and attach themselves to him.
entries.literal: Thereupon Bo Yi and Shu Qi heard that the Earl of the West, Chang, was good at supporting the elderly, and thought, why not go and attach themselves to him?

entries.zh: 及至，西伯卒，武王載木主，號為文王，東伐紂。
entries.en: When they arrived, the Earl of the West had died. King Wu carried the wooden spirit tablet, styled him King Wen, and marched east to attack King Zhou.
entries.literal: When they arrived, the Earl of the West had died; King Wu carried the wooden spirit tablet, styled him King Wen, and marched east to attack King Zhou.

entries.zh: 伯夷、叔齊叩馬而諫曰：「父死不葬，爰及干戈，可謂孝乎？
entries.en: Bo Yi and Shu Qi grasped the horse's bridle and remonstrated, saying: 'Father has died and not been buried, yet you resort to weapons—can this be called filial?
entries.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi grasped the horse and remonstrated saying: 'Father died not buried, moreover to weapons, can this be called filial?

entries.zh: 以臣弒君，可謂仁乎？」
entries.en: For a minister to kill his lord—can this be called benevolent?'
entries.literal: With minister killing lord, can this be called benevolent?'

entries.zh: 左右欲兵之。
entries.en: Those at his side wished to kill them with weapons.
entries.literal: Those at his side wished to use weapons on them.

entries.zh: 太公曰：「此義人也。」
entries.en: The Grand Duke said, "These men are righteous."
entries.literal: The Grand Duke said: 'These are righteous men.'

entries.zh: 扶而去之。
entries.en: He supported them and sent them away.
entries.literal: Supported and sent them away.

entries.zh: 武王已平殷亂，天下宗周，而伯夷、叔齊恥之，義不食周粟，隱於首陽山，采薇而食之。
entries.en: After King Wu had pacified the disorder of Yin and the world acknowledged Zhou as paramount, Bo Yi and Shu Qi were ashamed of it. For righteousness' sake they would not eat Zhou grain. They hid on Mount Shouyang, gathered ferns, and ate them.
entries.literal: King Wu having pacified the Yin disorder, the world took Zhou as its lord, yet Bo Yi and Shu Qi were ashamed of this; for righteousness they would not eat Zhou grain; they hid on Mount Shouyang, gathered ferns, and ate them.

entries.zh: 及餓且死，作歌。
entries.en: When they were hungry and about to die, they composed a song.
entries.literal: When hungry and about to die, composed a song.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：「登彼西山兮，采其薇矣。
entries.en: Its words said, "We climb that western mountain, gathering its ferns.
entries.literal: The lyrics say: 'Ascending that western mountain, gathering its ferns.

entries.zh: 以暴易暴兮，不知其非矣。
entries.en: To replace violence with violence, not knowing that it is wrong.
entries.literal: Replacing violence with violence—we do not know its wrongness.

entries.zh: 神農、虞、夏忽焉沒兮，我安適歸矣？
entries.en: Shennong, Yu, and Xia have suddenly perished—where shall I return?
entries.literal: Shennong, Yu, Xia suddenly gone, where shall I return?

entries.zh: 于嗟徂兮，命之衰矣！」
entries.en: Alas, I am going—fate's decline!'
entries.literal: Alas going, fate's decline!'

entries.zh: 遂餓死於首陽山。
entries.en: So they starved to death on Mount Shouyang.
entries.literal: Thus, they starved to death on Mount Shouyang.

entries.zh: 或曰：「天道無親，常與善人。」
entries.en: Some say: 'Heaven's way has no partiality—it constantly sides with good people.'
entries.literal: Some say: 'Heaven's way has no partiality, constantly with good people.'

entries.zh: 若伯夷、叔齊，可謂善人者非邪？
entries.en: Could Bo Yi and Shu Qi not be called good men?
entries.literal: As for Bo Yi and Shu Qi—were they not good men?

entries.zh: 積仁絜行如此而餓死！
entries.en: They accumulated benevolence and pure conduct like this, yet starved to death!
entries.literal: Accumulated benevolence and pure conduct like this yet starved to death!

entries.zh: 且七十子之徒，仲尼獨薦顏淵為好學。
entries.en: Moreover, among the seventy disciples, Confucius singled out Yan Yuan alone as one who loved learning.
entries.literal: Moreover, among the seventy disciples, Confucius alone praised Yan Yuan as fond of learning.

entries.zh: 然回也屢空，糟糠不厭，而卒蚤夭。
entries.en: Yet Yan Hui often went hungry, did not reject coarse food, and ultimately died young.
entries.literal: Yet Yan Hui often was empty, did not reject coarse food, yet died young.

entries.zh: 天之報施善人，其何如哉？
entries.en: Heaven's rewards and punishments for good people—what are they like?
entries.literal: Heaven's reward and punishment for good people, what is it like?

entries.zh: 盜蹠日殺不辜，肝人之肉，暴戾恣睢，聚黨數千人橫行天下，竟以壽終。
entries.en: Robber Zhi daily killed the innocent and ate human flesh. Violent and arrogant, he gathered a band of several thousand men and rampaged across the realm, yet in the end died of old age.
entries.literal: Robber Zhi daily killed the innocent and ate human flesh; violent and arrogant, he gathered a band of several thousand men and rampaged across the realm, yet in the end died of old age.

entries.zh: 是遵何德哉？
entries.en: What virtue did this follow?
entries.literal: This followed what virtue?

entries.zh: 此其尤大彰明較著者也。
entries.en: This is the clearest and most conspicuous example.
entries.literal: This is the most glaringly clear and evident example.

entries.zh: 若至近世，操行不軌，專犯忌諱，而終身逸樂，富厚累世不絕。
entries.en: If we come to recent times, there are those whose conduct is unseemly and who deliberately violate taboos, yet enjoy ease and pleasure all their lives, with wealth and eminence continuing for generations without end.
entries.literal: If we come to recent times, those whose conduct is unseemly and who deliberately violate taboos yet enjoy ease and pleasure all their lives, with wealth and eminence continuing for generations without end—

entries.zh: 或擇地而蹈之，時然後出言，行不由徑，非公正不發憤，而遇禍災者，不可勝數也。
entries.en: Others choose proper ground before stepping, speak only when the moment is right, refuse to take crooked paths, and grow indignant only over injustice, yet those among them who suffer disaster are innumerable.
entries.literal: Others tread only on proper ground, speak only when the time is right, walk by no crooked path, and vent indignation only when faced with injustice—yet those who meet with disaster are beyond counting.

entries.zh: 余甚惑焉，儻所謂天道，是邪非邪？
entries.en: I am greatly confused about this. Perhaps what is called heaven's way—is it so or not?
entries.literal: I am greatly confused about this, perhaps what is called heaven's way, is it so or not?

entries.zh: 「君子疾沒世而名不稱焉。」
entries.en: "The gentleman hates to leave the world with his name unpraised."
entries.literal: 'The gentleman hates to leave the world with his name unpraised.'

entries.zh: 賈子曰：「貪夫徇財，烈士徇名，夸者死權，眾庶馮生。」
entries.en: Master Jia said, "The greedy man dies for wealth, the ardent knight dies for fame, the boaster dies for power, the common multitude cling to life."
entries.literal: Master Jia said: 'The greedy man dies for wealth, the ardent knight dies for fame, the boaster dies for power, the common multitude cling to life.'

entries.zh: 「同明相照，同類相求。」
entries.en: "Like brightness illuminates one another; like kind seeks one another."
entries.literal: 'Like brightness illuminates one another; like kind seeks one another.'

entries.zh: 雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物睹。
entries.en: Clouds gather around the dragon and wind follows the tiger; when a sage appears, all things turn toward him.
entries.literal: Clouds follow the dragon, wind follows the tiger; when a sage arises, the myriad things look to him.

entries.zh: 伯夷、叔齊雖賢，得夫子而名益彰。
entries.en: Bo Yi and Shu Qi were worthy men, but once they had the Master, their names became all the more illustrious.
entries.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi, though worthy, came to have the Master, and their names became the more illustrious.

entries.zh: 顏淵雖篤學，附驥尾而行益顯。
entries.en: Yan Yuan studied with utmost devotion; by attaching himself to a great steed's tail, his conduct became all the more prominent.
entries.literal: Yan Yuan, though he studied with utmost devotion, by attaching to a steed's tail his conduct became the more prominent.

entries.zh: 巖穴之士，趣舍有時若此，類名堙滅而不稱，悲夫！
entries.en: Recluses of cliff and cave, advancing and withdrawing as the times require—like these, entire classes of names are buried in oblivion and go unmentioned. Alas!
entries.literal: Recluses of cliff and cave, advancing and withdrawing as the times require—like these, whole classes of names are buried in oblivion and go unmentioned. Alas!

entries.zh: 閭巷之人，欲砥行立名者，非附青雲之士，惡能施于後世哉？
entries.en: People of the lanes and alleys who wish to hone their conduct and establish a name: unless they attach themselves to men who have risen to the blue clouds, how can they make themselves known to later generations?
entries.literal: Men of lanes and alleys who wish to polish their conduct and establish their names—if they do not attach themselves to men who have risen to the blue clouds, how can they leave their mark on posterity?

entries.zh: 夫學者載籍極博，猶考信於六藝。
entries.en: The writings preserved by scholars are exceedingly vast, yet they still verify their trustworthiness against the Six Classics.
entries.literal: Scholars' recorded writings are exceedingly vast, yet they still verify trustworthiness against the Six Classics.

entries.zh: 詩書雖缺，然虞夏之文可知也。
entries.en: Though the Poetry and Documents are incomplete, the writings of Yu and Xia can still be known.
entries.literal: Though the Poetry and Documents are incomplete, yet the writings of Yu and Xia can still be known.

entries.zh: 堯將遜位，讓於虞舜，舜禹之閒，岳牧咸薦，乃試之於位，典職數十年，功用既興，然後授政。
entries.en: When Yao was about to abdicate the throne and yield it to Yu Shun—and in the interval between Shun and Yu—the mountain lords and pastors all recommended him. They tested him in office; he held his duties for several decades, and when his merits and achievements had flourished, they transferred the administration to him.
entries.literal: Yao was about to abdicate the throne and yield it to Yu Shun; between Shun and Yu, the mountain lords and pastors all recommended him; then they tested him in office, he held his duties for several decades, and when his merits and achievements had flourished, they transferred the administration to him.

entries.zh: 示天下重器，王者大統，傳天下若斯之難也。
entries.en: Thus, they showed the world the great vessel of state and the king's supreme succession—transmitting the realm is so difficult.
entries.literal: Thus, showing the world the great vessel of state and the king's supreme succession—transmitting the realm is so difficult.

entries.zh: 而說者曰堯讓天下於許由，許由不受，恥之逃隱。
entries.en: Yet storytellers say that Yao yielded the realm to Xu You, that Xu You did not accept, and that, ashamed, he fled into seclusion.
entries.literal: Yet storytellers say Yao yielded the realm to Xu You; Xu You did not accept, took it as shame, and fled into seclusion.

entries.zh: 及夏之時，有卞隨、務光者。
entries.en: By the time of Xia, there were men such as Bian Sui and Wu Guang.
entries.literal: And in Xia's time, there were Bian Sui and Wu Guang.

entries.zh: 此何以稱焉？
entries.en: How is this to be regarded?
entries.literal: How is this to be regarded?

entries.zh: 太史公曰：余登箕山，其上蓋有許由冢云。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: I climbed Mount Ji, where there is said to be the tomb of Xu You.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: I ascended Mount Ji, and on it there is said to be the tomb of Xu You.

entries.zh: 孔子序列古之仁聖賢人，如吳太伯、伯夷之倫詳矣。
entries.en: Confucius arranged and set forth the ancient benevolent sages and worthy men, including figures such as Wu Taibo and Bo Yi, in detail.
entries.literal: Confucius set forth the ancient benevolent sages and worthy men, such as Wu Taibo and Bo Yi, in detail.

entries.zh: 余以所聞由、光義至高，其文辭不少概見，何哉？
entries.en: The righteousness of men such as Xu You and Wu Guang, of which I have heard, is very lofty indeed; yet one cannot find even the slightest trace of them in the writings of the past—why is this?
entries.literal: As for the righteousness of Xu You and Wu Guang, of which I have heard, it is extremely lofty; yet their accounts are not visible even in the slightest overview—why is this?

entries.zh: 管仲夷吾者，潁上人也。
entries.en: Guan Zhong, whose courtesy name was Yiwu, was a man of Yingshang.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong, whose courtesy name was Yiwu, was a man of Ying Shang.

entries.zh: 少時常與鮑叔牙游，鮑叔知其賢。
entries.en: In his youth, he often spent time with Bao Shuya, who recognized his worth.
entries.literal: In his youth he often associated with Bao Shuya, and Bao Shu recognized his worth.

entries.zh: 管仲貧困，常欺鮑叔，鮑叔終善遇之，不以為言。
entries.en: Guan Zhong was impoverished and often deceived Bao Shu, but Bao Shu in the end treated him well and did not take it amiss.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong was impoverished, often deceived Bao Shu, Bao Shu in the end treated him well, did not take it amiss.

entries.zh: 已而鮑叔事齊公子小白，管仲事公子糾。
entries.en: Later, Bao Shu served Prince Xiaobai of Qi, while Guan Zhong served Prince Jiu.
entries.literal: Soon after, Bao Shu served Prince Xiaobai of Qi, while Guan Zhong served Prince Jiu.

entries.zh: 及小白立為桓公，公子糾死，管仲囚焉。
entries.en: When Prince Xiaobai was installed as Duke Huan, Prince Jiu died and Guan Zhong was imprisoned.
entries.literal: When Xiaobai was installed as Duke Huan, Prince Jiu died and Guan Zhong was imprisoned.

entries.zh: 鮑叔遂進管仲。
entries.en: Bao Shu then recommended Guan Zhong to him.
entries.literal: Bao Shu thereupon presented Guan Zhong.

entries.zh: 管仲既用，任政於齊，齊桓公以霸，九合諸侯，一匡天下，管仲之謀也。
entries.en: Once Guan Zhong was employed, he took charge of government in Qi. Duke Huan of Qi achieved hegemony, nine times assembled the feudal lords, and once brought the realm into order—all through Guan Zhong's strategy.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong having been employed took charge of government in Qi; Duke Huan of Qi achieved hegemony, nine times assembled the feudal lords, once brought the realm into order—it was Guan Zhong's strategy.

entries.zh: 管仲曰：「吾始困時，嘗與鮑叔賈，分財利多自與，鮑叔不以我為貪，知我貧也。
entries.en: Guan Zhong said, "When I first was in straits, I once traded with Bao Shu; in dividing the profits I took much for myself. Bao Shu did not consider me greedy—he knew I was poor.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong said, "When I first was in straits, I once traded with Bao Shu; in dividing profits I took much for myself. Bao Shu did not consider me greedy—he knew I was poor.

entries.zh: 吾嘗為鮑叔謀事而更窮困，鮑叔不以我為愚，知時有利不利也。
entries.en: I once planned affairs for Bao Shu and became even more impoverished, but Bao Shu did not consider me foolish—he knew there are times of advantage and disadvantage.
entries.literal: I once planned affairs for Bao Shu and became even more impoverished, Bao Shu did not consider me foolish, knew there are times of advantage and disadvantage.

entries.zh: 吾嘗三仕三見逐於君，鮑叔不以我為不肖，知我不遭時也。
entries.en: I once served three times and was dismissed three times by lords, but Bao Shu did not consider me unworthy—he knew I did not meet the times.
entries.literal: I once served three times and three times was dismissed by lords, Bao Shu did not consider me unworthy, knew I did not meet the times.

entries.zh: 吾嘗三戰三走，鮑叔不以我怯，知我有老母也。
entries.en: I once fought three times and fled three times, but Bao Shu did not consider me cowardly—he knew I had an aged mother.
entries.literal: I once fought three times and fled three times, Bao Shu did not consider me cowardly, knew I had an aged mother.

entries.zh: 公子糾敗，召忽死之，吾幽囚受辱，鮑叔不以我為無恥，知我不羞小睗而恥功名不顯于天下也。
entries.en: When Prince Jiu was defeated, Zhao Hu died for him. I was imprisoned and humiliated, but Bao Shu did not consider me shameless—he knew I was not ashamed of petty disgrace but ashamed that my merit and fame would not shine forth under Heaven.
entries.literal: Prince Jiu was defeated and Zhao Hu died for him. I was imprisoned and humiliated. Bao Shu did not consider me shameless—he knew I was not ashamed of petty disgrace but ashamed that merit and fame would not shine forth under Heaven.

entries.zh: 生我者父母，知我者鮑子也。」
entries.en: Those who gave me life are my parents; the one who truly knows me is Bao Shu."
entries.literal: Those who gave me life are my parents; the one who knows me is Master Bao."

entries.zh: 鮑叔既進管仲，以身下之。
entries.en: Bao Shu, having recommended Guan Zhong, humbled himself below him.
entries.literal: Bao Shu having recommended Guan Zhong, humbled himself below him.

entries.zh: 子孫世祿於齊，有封邑者十餘世，常為名大夫。
entries.en: His descendants received hereditary stipends in Qi. Those with fiefs numbered over ten generations and always were famous grand officers.
entries.literal: His descendants received hereditary stipends in Qi, those with fiefs numbered over ten generations, always were famous grand officers.

entries.zh: 天下不多管仲之賢而多鮑叔能知人也。
entries.en: The world does not praise Guan Zhong's worthiness so much as it praises Bao Shu's ability to recognize people.
entries.literal: The world does not praise Guan Zhong's worthiness so much as praises Bao Shu's ability to recognize people.

entries.zh: 管仲既任政相齊，以區區之齊在海濱，通貨積財，富國彊兵，與俗同好惡。
entries.en: Guan Zhong having taken charge of government as prime minister of Qi, with tiny Qi by the seacoast, circulated wealth and accumulated riches, enriched the state and strengthened the army, and shared likes and dislikes with the customs.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong having taken charge of government as prime minister of Qi, with tiny Qi by the seacoast, circulated wealth accumulated riches, enriched the state strengthened the army, shared likes and dislikes with the customs.

entries.zh: 故其稱曰：「倉廩實而知禮節，衣食足而知榮辱，上服度則六親固。
entries.en: Therefore, he said, "When granaries are full, the people know ritual and propriety; when clothing and food are sufficient, they know honor and shame; when superiors observe measure, the six kin are secure.
entries.literal: Therefore, his saying runs: "When granaries are full, the people know ritual and propriety; when clothing and food are sufficient, they know honor and shame; when superiors observe measure, the six kin are secure.

entries.zh: 四維不張，國乃滅亡。
entries.en: When the four cardinal bonds are left slack, the state perishes.
entries.literal: If the four cardinal bonds are not upheld, the state will perish.

entries.zh: 下令如流水之原，令順民心。」
entries.en: Issue orders like the source of flowing water, so that the orders follow the people's hearts."
entries.literal: Issue orders like the source of flowing water, so that orders follow the people's hearts."

entries.zh: 故論卑而易行。
entries.en: Therefore, his policies were modest and easy to put into practice.
entries.literal: Therefore, his policies were modest and easy to carry out.

entries.zh: 俗之所欲，因而予之；
entries.en: What the customs desire, therefore grant it;
entries.literal: What the customs desire, therefore grant it;

entries.zh: 俗之所否，因而去之。
entries.en: What the customs reject, therefore remove it.
entries.literal: what the customs reject, therefore remove it.

entries.zh: 其為政也，善因禍而為福，轉敗而為功。
entries.en: In his governance, he was good at turning calamity into fortune and converting defeat into success.
entries.literal: In his governance, he was good at turning calamity into fortune, converting defeat into success.

entries.zh: 貴輕重，慎權衡。
entries.en: He valued balancing light and heavy and was careful with weights and measures.
entries.literal: Valued balancing light and heavy, was careful with weights and measures.

entries.zh: 桓公實怒少姬，南襲蔡，管仲因而伐楚，責包茅不入貢於周室。
entries.en: Duke Huan was actually angry at the young consort and marched south against Cai; Guan Zhong then attacked Chu and charged that they had not sent the bundled-thatch tribute to the Zhou court.
entries.literal: Duke Huan was actually angry at the young consort and attacked Cai to the south; Guan Zhong therefore attacked Chu and charged that they had not sent the bundled thatch tribute to the Zhou court.

entries.zh: 桓公實北征山戎，而管仲因而令燕修召公之政。
entries.en: Duke Huan's northern expedition was in fact against the Mountain Rong, but Guan Zhong used it to have Yan restore Duke Shao's government.
entries.literal: Duke Huan actually campaigned north against the Mountain Rong, yet Guan Zhong thereby had Yan restore the government of Duke Shao.

entries.zh: 於柯之會，桓公欲背曹沫之約，管仲因而信之，諸侯由是歸齊。
entries.en: At the Ke meeting, Duke Huan wished to renege on Cao Mo's agreement, but Guan Zhong therefore kept faith with it, and the feudal lords therefore turned to Qi.
entries.literal: At the Ke meeting, Duke Huan wished to renege on Cao Mo's agreement, Guan Zhong therefore kept faith with it, the feudal lords therefore turned to Qi.

entries.zh: 故曰：「知與之為取，政之寶也。」
entries.en: Therefore, it is said, "To know that by giving one takes—that is the treasure of governance."
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said, "To know that giving is taking is the treasure of governance."

entries.zh: 管仲富擬於公室，有三歸、反坫，齊人不以為侈。
entries.en: Guan Zhong's wealth equaled the ducal house. He had three wives' quarters and return stands, yet the people of Qi did not consider it extravagant.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong's wealth equaled the ducal house, had three wives' quarters and return stands, the people of Qi did not consider it extravagant.

entries.zh: 管仲卒，齊國遵其政，常彊於諸侯。
entries.en: Guan Zhong died, and the state of Qi followed his governance, constantly remaining strong among the feudal lords.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong died, Qi state followed his governance, constantly strong among the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 後百餘年而有晏子焉。
entries.en: More than a century later, Yan Zi appeared.
entries.literal: Over a hundred years later there was Yan Zi.

entries.zh: 管仲世所謂賢臣，然孔子小之。
entries.en: The world calls Guan Zhong a worthy minister, yet Confucius treated him as small.
entries.literal: Guan Zhong the world calls a worthy minister, yet Confucius belittled him.

entries.zh: 豈以為周道衰微，桓公既賢，而不勉之至王，乃稱霸哉？
entries.en: Was this because, with the Zhou way in decline and Duke Huan already worthy, Guan Zhong did not urge him toward true kingship, but only helped him become hegemon?
entries.literal: Was it because the Zhou Way had declined, and though Duke Huan was worthy, Guan Zhong did not urge him on to kingship but only to hegemony?

entries.zh: 語曰「將順其美，匡救其惡，故上下能相親也」。
entries.en: As the saying goes, "Promote and follow their excellence, correct and rescue their faults—thus superiors and inferiors can be close."
entries.literal: The saying goes, "Promote and follow their excellence, correct and rescue their faults—thus superiors and inferiors can be close."

entries.zh: 豈管仲之謂乎？
entries.en: Is this not speaking of Guan Zhong?
entries.literal: Is this not speaking of Guan Zhong?

entries.zh: 太史公曰：吾讀管氏牧民、山高、乘馬、輕重、九府，及晏子春秋，詳哉其言之也。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: I read the Guan clan's Shepherding the People, Mountain Height, Cavalry, Light and Heavy, Nine Treasuries, and Yan Zi's Spring and Autumn—detailed indeed are their words.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: I read the Guan clan's Shepherding the People, Mountain Height, Cavalry, Light and Heavy, Nine Treasuries, and Yan Zi's Spring and Autumn, detailed indeed are their words.

entries.zh: 既見其著書，欲觀其行事，故次其傳。
entries.en: Having seen their written books, I wished to observe their conduct, therefore I arranged their biographies.
entries.literal: Having seen their written books, wished to observe their conduct, therefore arranged their biographies.

entries.zh: 至其書，世多有之，是以不論，論其軼事。
entries.en: As for their books, the world has many of them, therefore I do not discuss them—I discuss their scattered affairs.
entries.literal: As for their books, the world has many of them, therefore do not discuss, discuss their scattered affairs.

entries.zh: 晏平仲嬰者，萊之夷維人也。
entries.en: Yan Ying, whose style was Ping Zhong, was a man of Yiwei in Lai.
entries.literal: Yan Ying, styled Ping Zhong, was a man of Yiwei in Lai.

entries.zh: 事齊靈公、莊公、景公，以節儉力行重於齊。
entries.en: He served Dukes Ling, Zhuang, and Jing of Qi, and with frugality and diligent conduct was honored in Qi.
entries.literal: Served Duke Ling, Duke Zhuang, Duke Jing of Qi, with frugality and diligent conduct was honored in Qi.

entries.zh: 既相齊，食不重肉，妾不衣帛。
entries.en: Having become prime minister of Qi, he did not eat meat twice a day, and his concubines did not wear silk.
entries.literal: Having become prime minister of Qi, did not eat meat twice, concubines did not wear silk.

entries.zh: 其在朝，君語及之，即危言；
entries.en: At court, if the ruler's words touched on the matter, Yan Zi spoke forthrightly;
entries.literal: When at court, if the ruler's words touched on the matter, he would speak forthrightly;

entries.zh: 語不及之，即危行。
entries.en: If the ruler's words did not touch on it, he would act forthrightly.
entries.literal: if the ruler's words did not touch on it, he would act forthrightly.

entries.zh: 國有道，即順命；
entries.en: If the state possessed the Way, he obeyed commands;
entries.literal: if the state possessed the Way, he obeyed commands;

entries.zh: 無道，即衡命。
entries.en: If the state lacked the Way, he would weigh his compliance with commands.
entries.literal: if the state lacked the Way, he would weigh his compliance with commands.

entries.zh: 以此三世顯名於諸侯。
entries.en: With this he made a famous name among the feudal lords for three generations.
entries.literal: With this made famous name among the feudal lords for three generations.

entries.zh: 越石父賢，在縲紲中。
entries.en: Yue Shifu was a worthy man but was in fetters.
entries.literal: Yue Shifu was worthy but was in fetters.

entries.zh: 晏子出，遭之涂，解左驂贖之，載歸。
entries.en: Yan Zi went out and encountered him on the road. He unyoked the left trace horse to redeem him and carried him home.
entries.literal: Yan Zi went out, encountered him on the road, unyoked the left trace horse to redeem him, carried him home.

entries.zh: 弗謝，入閨。
entries.en: He did not thank him and entered the inner chambers.
entries.literal: Did not thank him, entered the inner chambers.

entries.zh: 久之，越石父請絕。
entries.en: After some time, Yue Shifu asked to sever their relationship.
entries.literal: After a long time, Yue Shifu asked to break off relations.

entries.zh: 晏子懼然，攝衣冠謝曰：「嬰雖不仁，免子於緦何子求絕之速也？」
entries.en: Yan Zi, startled, straightened his robes and cap and apologized, saying, "Though I, Ying, am not benevolent, I freed you from bonds—why do you seek to break off relations so quickly?"
entries.literal: Yan Zi, startled, straightened his robes and cap and apologized, saying, "Ying, though lacking in benevolence, freed you from bonds—why do you seek to break off relations so quickly?"

entries.zh: 石父曰：「不然。
entries.en: Shifu said, "Not so.
entries.literal: Shifu said, "Not so.

entries.zh: 吾聞君子詘於不知己而信於知己者。
entries.en: I have heard that a gentleman bends before those who do not know him, but stands firm before those who do.
entries.literal: I have heard that gentlemen bend to those who do not know them but extend faith to those who know them.

entries.zh: 方吾在縲紲中，彼不知我也。
entries.en: When I was bound in fetters, those men did not know me.
entries.literal: When I was in fetters and handcuffs, they did not know me.

entries.zh: 夫子既已感寤而贖我，是知己；
entries.en: Master having already been moved and redeemed me—this is knowing me;
entries.literal: Master having already been moved and redeemed me, this is knowing me;

entries.zh: 知己而無禮，固不如在縲紲之中。」
entries.en: To know me yet treat me without ritual is surely not as good as being in fetters."
entries.literal: to know me yet treat me without ritual is surely not as good as being in fetters."

entries.zh: 晏子於是延入為上客。
entries.en: Yan Zi then invited him in as an honored guest.
entries.literal: Yan Zi then invited him in as honored guest.

entries.zh: 晏子為齊相，出，其御之妻從門閒而闚其夫。
entries.en: When Yan Zi was prime minister of Qi and going out, his charioteer's wife peeked at her husband from the gate.
entries.literal: When Yan Zi was prime minister of Qi, going out, his charioteer's wife peeked at her husband from the gate.

entries.zh: 其夫為相御，擁大蓋，策駟馬，意氣揚揚甚自得也。
entries.en: Her husband drove the prime minister's chariot, held the large canopy, whipped the four horses, and rode with spirit and energy soaring—he was very self-satisfied.
entries.literal: Her husband drove the prime minister's chariot, held the large canopy, whipped the four horses, spirit and energy soaring very self-satisfied.

entries.zh: 既而歸，其妻請去。
entries.en: After he returned home, his wife asked to leave him.
entries.literal: Having returned home, his wife requested to leave.

entries.zh: 夫問其故。
entries.en: The husband asked the reason.
entries.literal: The husband asked the reason.

entries.zh: 妻曰：「晏子長不滿六尺，身相齊國，名顯諸侯。
entries.en: His wife said, "Yan Zi is less than six feet tall, yet personally serves as prime minister of Qi, and his name is illustrious among the feudal lords.
entries.literal: The wife said, "Yan Zi is less than six feet tall, yet personally serves as prime minister of Qi; his name is illustrious among the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 今者妾觀其出，志念深矣，常有以自下者。
entries.en: Now when I observed his going out, his thoughts and reflections were deep—he constantly had ways to humble himself.
entries.literal: Now when I observed his going out, his thoughts and reflections were deep, constantly had ways to humble himself.

entries.zh: 今子長八尺，乃為人仆御，然子之意自以為足，妾是以求去也。」
entries.en: You are eight feet tall, yet you serve as another man's charioteer, and you consider yourself fully satisfied—that is why I ask to leave you."
entries.literal: Now you are eight feet tall, yet serve as another man's charioteer, and you consider yourself fully satisfied—therefore I ask to leave you."

entries.zh: 其後夫自抑損。
entries.en: Afterward, the husband humbled himself.
entries.literal: Afterwards the husband humbled himself.

entries.zh: 晏子怪而問之，御以實對。
entries.en: Yan Zi was surprised and asked him, and the charioteer told the truth.
entries.literal: Yan Zi was surprised and asked him, the charioteer told the truth.

entries.zh: 晏子薦以為大夫。
entries.en: Yan Zi recommended him as a grand officer.
entries.literal: Yan Zi recommended him as grand officer.

entries.zh: 方晏子伏莊公尸哭之，成禮然後去，豈所謂「見義不為無勇」者邪？
entries.en: When Yan Zi prostrated himself over Duke Zhuang's corpse, wept for him, completed the rites, and only then departed, was this not what is meant by "seeing what is right and failing to act shows lack of courage"?
entries.literal: When Yan Zi prostrated himself on Duke Zhuang's corpse and wept for him, completed the rites, and then departed—is this not what is meant by "seeing righteousness and not acting is lack of courage"?

entries.zh: 至其諫說，犯君之顏，此所謂「進思盡忠，退思補過」者哉！
entries.en: As for his remonstrations, speaking to the point of offending the ruler's countenance—is this not what is called "in advancing, think how to exhaust loyalty; in withdrawing, think how to remedy faults"?
entries.literal: As for his remonstrations, speaking so as to offend the ruler's countenance—this is what is called "in advancing, think how to exhaust loyalty; in withdrawing, think how to remedy faults"!

entries.zh: 假令晏子而在，余雖為之執鞭，所忻慕焉。
entries.en: If Yan Zi were alive today, I would gladly hold the whip for him—that is how much I admire him.
entries.literal: If Yan Zi were alive today, even to hold the whip for him I would be glad and admire him.

entries.zh: 伊尹為庖，百里奚為虜，皆所由干其上也。
entries.en: Yi Yin became a cook, Baili Xi became a captive—all the paths by which they petitioned their superiors.
entries.literal: Yi Yin became cook, Baili Xi became captive, all the paths by which they petitioned their superiors.

entries.zh: 故此二子者，皆聖人也，猶不能無役身而涉世如此其汙也，則非能仕之所設也。
entries.en: Therefore, although these two men were both sages, they still could not avoid debasing themselves and entering the world through such sordid means. This was not something they did because they loved office.
entries.literal: Therefore, these two men, both sages, yet could not avoid debasing their persons and entering the world in such filth; then this is not what those able to serve establish.

entries.zh: 老子者，楚苦縣厲鄉曲仁里人也，姓李氏，名耳，字耼，周守藏室之史也。
entries.en: Laozi was a man of Quren Village in Li Township, Ku County, Chu. His surname was Li, personal name Er, courtesy name Dan. He was the Zhou court's keeper of the archives.
entries.literal: Laozi was a man of Qu Ren Village, Li Township, Ku County, Chu, surname Li, name Er, courtesy name Dan, Zhou's keeper of the archives.

entries.zh: 司馬穰苴者，田完之苗裔也。
entries.en: Sima Rangju was a descendant of Tian Wan.
entries.literal: Sima Rangju was Tian Wan's descendant.

entries.zh: 齊景公時，晉伐阿、甄，而燕侵河上，齊師敗績。
entries.en: During the reign of Lord Jing of Qi, Jin attacked A and Zhen, while Yan invaded the lands along the river, and the Qi army suffered a defeat.
entries.literal: In the time of Lord Jing of Qi, Jin attacked A and Zhen, while Yan invaded the lands along the river, and the Qi army suffered a defeat.

entries.zh: 景公患之。
entries.en: Lord Jing was worried about it.
entries.literal: Jing Gong worried about it.

entries.zh: 晏嬰乃薦田穰苴曰：「穰苴雖田氏庶孽，然其人文能附眾，武能威敵，願君試之。」
entries.en: Yan Ying then recommended Tian Rangju, saying, "Though Rangju is only a minor collateral of the Tian clan, in civil affairs he can win the allegiance of the troops, and in martial affairs he can overawe the enemy. I hope Your Lordship will try him."
entries.literal: Yan Ying then recommended Tian Rangju, saying: "Though Rangju is a minor collateral of the Tian clan, in civil affairs he can win the allegiance of the troops, and in martial affairs he can overawe the enemy. I hope Your Lordship will try him."

entries.zh: 景公召穰苴，與語兵事，大說之，以為將軍，將兵捍燕晉之師。
entries.en: Lord Jing summoned Rangju and spoke with him about military affairs. He was greatly pleased, made him general, and had him lead troops to defend against the Yan and Jin armies.
entries.literal: Jing Gong summoned Rangju, spoke with him about military affairs, greatly pleased, made him general, led troops to defend against Yan and Jin armies.

entries.zh: 穰苴曰：「臣素卑賤，君擢之閭伍之中，加之大夫之上，士卒未附，百姓不信，人微權輕，願得君之寵臣，國之所尊，以監軍，乃可。」
entries.en: Rangju said, "I have long been lowly. Your Lordship raised me from among the common ranks and placed me above grand officers. The soldiers are not yet attached to me, the people do not yet trust me; my person is lowly and my authority light. I wish to obtain Your Lordship's favored minister, one whom the state honors, to supervise the army—only then will it do."
entries.literal: Rangju said: "I have long been lowly. Your Lordship raised me from among the common ranks and placed me above grand officers. The soldiers are not yet attached, the people do not yet trust me; my person is lowly and my authority light. I wish to obtain Your Lordship's favored minister, one whom the state honors, to supervise the army—only then will it do."

entries.zh: 於是景公許之，使莊賈往。
entries.en: Thus, Lord Jing permitted it and sent Zhuang Jia to go.
entries.literal: Thus, Jing Gong permitted it, sent Zhuang Jia to go.

entries.zh: 穰苴既辭，與莊賈約曰：「旦日日中會於軍門。」
entries.en: Rangju, having taken leave, made an agreement with Zhuang Jia, saying: 'Tomorrow at noon, meet at the army gate.'
entries.literal: Rangju having taken leave, made agreement with Zhuang Jia saying: 'Tomorrow noon meet at army gate.'

entries.zh: 穰苴先馳至軍，立表下漏待賈。
entries.en: Rangju first galloped to the army camp, erected a pole, set up a water clock, and awaited Jia.
entries.literal: Rangju first galloped to army, erected pole set water clock awaited Jia.

entries.zh: 賈素驕貴，以為將己之軍而己為監，不甚急；
entries.en: Jia was by nature arrogant and of high rank. He thought that the general would command the army while he himself was only the army supervisor, and so he was not in much of a hurry;
entries.literal: Jia was by nature arrogant and of high rank; he thought that the general would command the army while he himself was only the army supervisor, and was not very urgent;

entries.zh: 親戚左右送之，留飲。
entries.en: His relatives and attendants sent him off, and he stayed drinking.
entries.literal: relatives and attendants sent him, stayed drinking.

entries.zh: 日中而賈不至。
entries.en: At noon Jia had not arrived.
entries.literal: At noon Jia not arrived.

entries.zh: 穰苴則仆表決漏，入，行軍勒兵，申明約束。
entries.en: Rangju then overturned the pole and drained the water clock, entered the camp, marched through the army and mustered the troops, and proclaimed the regulations.
entries.literal: Rangju then overturned the pole and drained the water clock, entered, marched through the army and mustered the troops, and proclaimed the regulations.

entries.zh: 約束既定，夕時，莊賈乃至。
entries.en: The regulations having been established, at evening time Zhuang Jia then arrived.
entries.literal: Regulations established, evening time, Zhuang Jia then arrived.

entries.zh: 穰苴曰：「何後期為？」
entries.en: Rangju said, "Why did you arrive after the appointed time?"
entries.literal: Rangju said: "Why did you arrive after the appointed time?"

entries.zh: 賈謝曰：「不佞大夫親戚送之，故留。」
entries.en: Jia apologized, saying, "This unworthy officer's relatives saw me off, and so I stayed."
entries.literal: Jia apologized, saying: "This unworthy officer's relatives saw me off, and so I stayed."

entries.zh: 穰苴曰：「將受命之日則忘其家，臨軍約束則忘其親，援枹鼓之急則忘其身。
entries.en: Rangju said, "On the day a general receives his command, he forgets his household; when he faces army regulations, he forgets his kin; when the drumsticks are urgently needed, he forgets his own body.
entries.literal: Rangju said: "On the day a general receives his command, he forgets his household; when he faces army regulations, he forgets his kin; when the drumsticks are urgently needed, he forgets his own body.

entries.zh: 今敵國深侵，邦內騷動，士卒暴露於境，君寢不安席，食不甘味，百姓之命皆懸於君，何謂相送乎！」
entries.en: Now the enemy states are deeply invading, the state within is disturbed, the soldiers are exposed on the borders, the lord sleeps uneasily on his mat and eats without tasting sweetness, and the people's lives all hang on you—what do you mean by an escort!"
entries.literal: Now the enemy states deeply invade, the state within is disturbed, the soldiers are exposed on the borders, the lord sleeps uneasily on his mat and eats without tasting sweetness, and the people's lives all hang on you—what do you mean by an escort!"

entries.zh: 召軍正問曰：「軍法期而後至者雲何？」
entries.en: He summoned the army judge and asked, "According to military law, what is done to one who arrives after the appointed time?"
entries.literal: He summoned the army judge and asked, saying: "According to military law, what is done to one who arrives after the appointed time?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「當斬。」
entries.en: The army judge answered, "He should be beheaded."
entries.literal: The army judge answered: "He should be beheaded."

entries.zh: 莊賈懼，使人馳報景公，請救。
entries.en: Zhuang Jia was afraid and sent men galloping to report to Lord Jing, requesting rescue.
entries.literal: Zhuang Jia feared, sent men galloped to report Jing Gong, requested rescue.

entries.zh: 既往，未及反，於是遂斬莊賈以徇三軍。
entries.en: The messenger had already gone but not yet returned; thereupon Rangju beheaded Zhuang Jia to display the punishment before the three armies.
entries.literal: The messenger had already gone but not yet returned; thereupon he beheaded Zhuang Jia to display the punishment before the three armies.

entries.zh: 三軍之士皆振慄。
entries.en: All the soldiers in the three armies shuddered in fear.
entries.literal: The soldiers of the three armies all trembled in awe.

entries.zh: 久之，景公遣使者持節赦賈，馳入軍中。
entries.en: After some time, Lord Jing sent an envoy carrying his credentials of authority to pardon Jia; the envoy galloped straight into the army camp.
entries.literal: After a long time, Lord Jing sent an envoy holding credentials of authority to pardon Jia, and the envoy galloped into the army camp.

entries.zh: 穰苴曰：「將在軍，君令有所不受。」
entries.en: Rangju said, "When the general is in the army, he is not bound to accept all the lord's commands."
entries.literal: Rangju said: "When the general is in the army, he is not bound to accept all of the lord's commands."

entries.zh: 問軍正曰：「馳三軍法何？」
entries.en: He asked the army judge, "What does military law say about galloping through the army camp?"
entries.literal: He asked the army judge: "What does military law say about galloping through the army camp?"

entries.zh: 正曰：「當斬。」
entries.en: The army judge said, "He should be beheaded."
entries.literal: The army judge said: "He should be beheaded."

entries.zh: 使者大懼。
entries.en: The envoy was greatly afraid.
entries.literal: Envoy greatly feared.

entries.zh: 穰苴曰：「君之使不可殺之。」
entries.en: Rangju said, "The lord's envoy cannot be killed."
entries.literal: Rangju said: "The lord's envoy cannot be killed."

entries.zh: 乃斬其仆，車之左駙，馬之左驂，以徇三軍。
entries.en: Rangju then had the envoy's driver beheaded, the chariot's left upright cut off, and the team's left outside horse killed, displaying the punishment before the three armies.
entries.literal: Thereupon he beheaded the envoy's driver, cut off the chariot's left upright, and killed the team's left outside horse, displaying the punishment before the three armies.

entries.zh: 遣使者還報，然後行。
entries.en: He sent the envoy back to report, then proceeded.
entries.literal: Sent envoy back to report, then proceeded.

entries.zh: 士卒次舍井灶飲食問疾醫藥，身自拊循之。
entries.en: He personally oversaw the soldiers' encampments, wells, stoves, food, drink, and inquired about illnesses and medicine. He personally stroked and comforted them.
entries.literal: As for the soldiers' encampments, wells, stoves, food and drink, and inquiries about illness and medicine, he personally stroked and comforted them.

entries.zh: 悉取將軍之資糧享士卒，身與士卒平分糧食。
entries.en: He took all the general's provisions to feast the soldiers, and personally shared the rations equally with the soldiers.
entries.literal: He took all the general's provisions to feast the soldiers, and personally shared the rations equally with the soldiers.

entries.zh: 最比其羸弱者，三日而後勒兵。
entries.en: He waited until even the weakest men had recovered, and only after three days did he assemble and drill the troops.
entries.literal: He waited until the weakest had recovered; only after three days did he muster and drill the troops.

entries.zh: 病者皆求行，爭奮出為之赴戰。
entries.en: Even the sick asked to march; they vied to exert themselves and go out to fight for him.
entries.literal: The sick all asked to march; they vied to exert themselves and go out to fight for him.

entries.zh: 晉師聞之，為罷去。
entries.en: The Jin army heard of it and withdrew.
entries.literal: Jin army heard it, withdrew and left.

entries.zh: 燕師聞之，度水而解。
entries.en: When the Yan army heard of this, it crossed back over the river and dispersed.
entries.literal: The Yan army heard of it, crossed the river, and disbanded.

entries.zh: 於是追擊之，遂取所亡封內故境而引兵歸。
entries.en: Thus, he pursued them, then took back the lost territories within the former borders and led the troops back.
entries.literal: Thus, pursued them, then took the lost sealed territories former borders and led troops back.

entries.zh: 未至國，釋兵旅，解約束，誓盟而後入邑。
entries.en: Not yet having reached the state, he released the troops, dissolved the regulations, swore covenants, and then entered the towns.
entries.literal: Not yet reached state, released troops, dissolved regulations, swore covenant then entered towns.

entries.zh: 景公與諸大夫郊迎，勞師成禮，然後反歸寢。
entries.en: Lord Jing with the various grand officers welcomed them in the suburbs, rewarded the army and completed the rites, then returned to the palace.
entries.literal: Jing Gong with various grand officers welcomed in suburbs, rewarded army completed rites, then returned to palace.

entries.zh: 既見穰苴，尊為大司馬。
entries.en: After Lord Jing had seen Rangju, he honored him as Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: After he had seen Rangju, he honored him as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 田氏日以益尊於齊。
entries.en: The Tian clan day by day became increasingly honored in Qi.
entries.literal: Tian clan day by day increasingly honored in Qi.

entries.zh: 已而大夫鮑氏、高、國之屬害之，譖於景公。
entries.en: Before long, the grand officers of the Bao, Gao, and Guo families and their faction grew jealous of him and slandered him to Lord Jing.
entries.literal: Before long the grand officers of the Bao family, Gao, Guo, and their faction harmed him and slandered him to Lord Jing.

entries.zh: 景公退穰苴，苴發疾而死。
entries.en: Lord Jing dismissed Rangju, and Rangju fell ill and died.
entries.literal: Jing Gong dismissed Rangju, Rangju fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 田乞、田豹之徒由此怨高、國等。
entries.en: Tian Qi, Tian Bao and their followers thus resented Gao, Guo and the others.
entries.literal: Tian Qi, Tian Bao and followers thus resented Gao, Guo and others.

entries.zh: 其後及田常殺簡公，盡滅高子、國子之族。
entries.en: Later, when Tian Chang killed Lord Jian, he exterminated the lineages of Gaozi and Guozi completely.
entries.literal: Later, when it came to Tian Chang killing Lord Jian, he completely exterminated the lineages of the Gao and Guo families.

entries.zh: 至常曾孫和，因自立為齊威王，用兵行威，大放穰苴之法，而諸侯朝齊。
entries.en: By the time of Tian Chang's great-grandson He, he thereupon established himself as King Wei of Qi. He employed troops and exercised authority, greatly promulgated Rangju's methods, and the feudal lords came to court Qi.
entries.literal: By the time of Tian Chang's great-grandson He, he thereupon established himself as King Wei of Qi; he employed troops and exercised authority, greatly promulgated Rangju's methods, and the feudal lords came to court Qi.

entries.zh: 魏文侯既卒，起事其子武侯。
entries.en: After Marquis Wen of Wei died, Wu Qi served his son Marquis Wu.
entries.literal: After Marquis Wen of Wei died, Qi served his son Marquis Wu.

entries.zh: 武侯浮西河而下，中流，顧而謂吳起曰：「美哉乎山河之固，此魏國之寶也！」
entries.en: Marquis Wu floated down the Yellow River, and in midstream he turned to Wu Qi and said: “How beautiful are these mountain and river defenses! This is Wei's treasure!”
entries.literal: Marquis Wu floated down the Yellow River, and in midstream turned to say to Wu Qi: 'How beautiful are the mountain and river fortifications—this is Wei's treasure!'

entries.zh: 起對曰：「在德不在險。
entries.en: Wu Qi replied: “It depends on virtue, not on natural defenses.
entries.literal: Qi replied: 'It depends on virtue, not on natural defenses.

entries.zh: 昔三苗氏左洞庭，右彭蠡，德義不修，禹滅之。
entries.en: In ancient times the Three Miao tribes had Dongting Lake on the left and Pengli Lake on the right. They did not cultivate virtue and righteousness, so Yu destroyed them.
entries.literal: In ancient times the Three Miao tribes had Dongting on the left and Pengli on the right. They did not cultivate virtue and righteousness, so Yu destroyed them.

entries.zh: 夏桀之居，左河濟，右泰華，伊闕在其南，羊腸在其北，修政不仁，湯放之。
entries.en: Xia Jie resided with the Yellow River on the left and Mount Tai on the right, Yique Pass to the south and Yangchang to the north. He practiced unbenevolent government, so Tang exiled him.
entries.literal: Xia Jie resided with the Yellow River on the left and Mount Tai on the right, Yique to the south and Yangchang to the north. He practiced unbenevolent government, so Tang exiled him.

entries.zh: 殷紂之國，左孟門，右太行，常山在其北，大河經其南，修政不德，武王殺之。
