entries.en: King Zhou of Yin had Mengmen Pass on the left and the Taihang Mountains on the right, Changshan to the north and the great river flowing south. He practiced unvirtuous government, so King Wu killed him.
entries.literal: King Zhou of Yin had Mengmen on the left and the Taihang Mountains on the right, Changshan to the north and the great river flowing south. He practiced unvirtuous government, so King Wu killed him.

entries.zh: 由此觀之，在德不在險。
entries.en: From this we can see that it depends on virtue, not on natural defenses.
entries.literal: From this we can see it depends on virtue, not on natural defenses.

entries.zh: 若君不修德，舟中之人盡為敵國也。」
entries.en: If my lord does not cultivate virtue, everyone aboard this boat will become your enemy.”
entries.literal: If my lord does not cultivate virtue, everyone aboard this boat will become your enemies.'

entries.zh: 武侯曰：「善。」
entries.en: Marquis Wu said: “Excellent.”
entries.literal: Marquis Wu said: 'Excellent.'

entries.zh: 孫子武者，齊人也。
entries.en: Sun Wu, known as Sun Tzu, was a man of Qi.
entries.literal: Sun Wu, called Sun Tzu, was a native of Qi.

entries.zh: 以兵法見於吳王闔廬。
entries.en: He presented his military strategies to King Helü of Wu.
entries.literal: He presented himself to King Helü of Wu with his military strategies.

entries.zh: 闔廬曰：「子之十三篇，吾盡觀之矣，可以小試勒兵乎？」
entries.en: King Helü said, “I have read all thirteen of your chapters. May we try drilling the troops on a small scale?”
entries.literal: King Helü said: 'I have read all thirteen of your chapters. May we try drilling the troops on a small scale?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「可。」
entries.en: He replied: “Yes.”
entries.literal: He replied: 'Acceptable.'

entries.zh: 闔廬曰：「可試以婦人乎？」
entries.en: King Helü said, “May we try it with the palace women?”
entries.literal: King Helü said: 'May we try it with the palace women?'

entries.en: He said: “Yes.”
entries.literal: He said: 'Acceptable.'

entries.zh: 於是許之，出宮中美女，得百八十人。
entries.en: So he was permitted to do so. One hundred eighty palace ladies were selected.
entries.literal: So he was permitted to do so. Palace ladies were selected, one hundred and eighty of them.

entries.zh: 孫子分為二隊，以王之寵姬二人各為隊長，皆令持戟。
entries.en: Sun Tzu divided the women into two teams, appointing the king's two favorite consorts as captains of each team, and ordered all of them to carry halberds.
entries.literal: Sun Tzu divided them into two teams, with the king's two favored consorts as team leaders for each, and commanded all of them to hold halberds.

entries.zh: 令之曰：「汝知而心與左右手背乎？」
entries.en: He asked them, “Do you know where your heart, your left hand, your right hand, and your back are?”
entries.literal: He asked them: 'Do you know where your heart, your left hand, your right hand, and your back are?'

entries.zh: 婦人曰：「知之。」
entries.en: The women said: “Yes.”
entries.literal: The women said: 'We know them.'

entries.zh: 孫子曰：「前，則視心；
entries.en: Sun Tzu said, “When I say forward, look toward the chest;
entries.literal: Sun Tzu said: 'When I say forward, look toward the chest;

entries.zh: 左，視左手；
entries.en: when I say left, look to the left hand;
entries.literal: when I say left, look at the left hand;

entries.zh: 右，視右手；
entries.en: when I say right, look to the right hand;
entries.literal: when I say right, look at the right hand;

entries.zh: 後，即視背。」
entries.en: when I say back, look behind you.”
entries.literal: when I say back, look at the back.'

entries.zh: 婦人曰：「諾。」
entries.en: The women replied: “Yes.”
entries.literal: The women said: 'Yes.'

entries.zh: 約束既布，乃設鈇鉞，即三令五申之。
entries.en: Once the regulations were promulgated, he set up the executioner's axe and halberd, and repeated the commands three times while explaining them five times.
entries.literal: Once the rules were laid out, he set up the axe and halberd, and repeated the commands three times and explained them five times.

entries.zh: 於是鼓之右，婦人大笑。
entries.en: Then he beat the drum for turning right, and the women burst out laughing.
entries.literal: Then he drummed to the right, and the women burst out laughing.

entries.zh: 孫子曰：「約束不明，申令不熟，將之罪也。」
entries.en: Sun Tzu said: “If the regulations are unclear and the commands unfamiliar, it is the general's fault.”
entries.literal: Sun Tzu said: 'The rules are unclear, the commands are not familiar—the general's fault.'

entries.zh: 復三令五申而鼓之左，婦人復大笑。
entries.en: He repeated the commands three times and explained them five times again, then beat the drum for turning left, and the women burst out laughing once more.
entries.literal: He repeated the commands three times and explained them five times, then drummed to the left, and the women again burst out laughing.

entries.zh: 孫子曰：「約束不明，申令不熟，將之罪也；
entries.en: Sun Tzu said: “If the regulations are unclear and the commands unfamiliar, it is the general's fault;
entries.literal: Sun Tzu said: 'The rules are unclear, the commands are not familiar—the general's fault;

entries.zh: 既已明而不如法者，吏士之罪也。」
entries.en: once they are clear but not followed, it is the officers' and soldiers' fault.”
entries.literal: once they are clear but not followed, it is the officers' and soldiers' fault.'

entries.zh: 乃欲斬左右隊長。
entries.en: He was about to execute the two team leaders.
entries.literal: He was about to execute the team leaders on left and right.

entries.zh: 吳王從臺上觀，見且斬愛姬，大駭。
entries.en: King Helü watched from the terrace above. When he saw that his beloved consorts were about to be executed, he was badly alarmed.
entries.literal: King Helü watched from the terrace above, and seeing that his beloved consorts were about to be executed, he was greatly alarmed.

entries.zh: 趣使使下令曰：「寡人已知將軍能用兵矣。
entries.en: He hurriedly sent a messenger down with orders, saying: “I already know the general can use troops.
entries.literal: He hurriedly sent a messenger down with orders: 'I already know the general can use troops.

entries.zh: 寡人非此二姬，食不甘味，願勿斬也。」
entries.en: Without these two consorts, my food has no flavor. Please do not execute them.”
entries.literal: Without these two consorts, my food has no flavor. Please do not execute them.'

entries.zh: 孫子曰：「臣既已受命為將，將在軍，君命有所不受。」
entries.en: Sun Tzu said: “I have already received the command to serve as general. When in the army, there are some of the sovereign's orders that a general does not accept.”
entries.literal: Sun Tzu said: 'I have already received the command to be general; when in the army, the general does not accept the sovereign's orders.'

entries.zh: 遂斬隊長二人以徇。
entries.en: He proceeded to execute the two team leaders as an example to the army.
entries.literal: He executed the two team leaders as an example.

entries.zh: 用其次為隊長，於是復鼓之。
entries.en: He appointed their deputies as team leaders, then beat the drum again.
entries.literal: He appointed their seconds as team leaders, then drummed again.

entries.zh: 婦人左右前後跪起皆中規矩繩墨，無敢出聲。
entries.en: The women moved left and right, forward and back, kneeling and standing—all conformed perfectly to the rules and regulations. None dared make a sound.
entries.literal: The women moved left right forward back, kneeling and standing—all conformed to the rules and regulations, none dared make a sound.

entries.zh: 於是孫子使使報王曰：「兵既整齊，王可試下觀之，唯王所欲用之，雖赴水火猶可也。」
entries.en: Then Sun Tzu sent a messenger to report to the king, saying: “The troops are now well-ordered. Your Majesty can come down to observe them. Whatever you wish to use them for—even charging into water or fire—they will do it.”
entries.literal: Then Sun Tzu sent a messenger to report to the king: 'The troops are now well-ordered. Your Majesty can come down to observe them. Whatever you wish to use them for, even if it means charging into water or fire, they will do it.'

entries.zh: 吳王曰：「將軍罷休就舍，寡人不願下觀。」
entries.en: King Helü said, “General, please retire to your quarters. I do not wish to come down and observe.”
entries.literal: King Helü said: 'General, please retire to your quarters. I do not wish to come down and observe.'

entries.zh: 孫子曰：「王徒好其言，不能用其實。」
entries.en: Sun Tzu said, “The king only enjoys the theory but cannot put it into practice.”
entries.literal: Sun Tzu said: 'The king only enjoys the words but cannot put the method into practice.'

entries.zh: 於是闔廬知孫子能用兵，卒以為將。
entries.en: Thus, Helü knew that Sun Tzu could command troops, and at last he appointed him general.
entries.literal: Thus, Helü knew Sun Tzu could use troops and finally appointed him as general.

entries.zh: 西破彊楚，入郢，北威齊晉，顯名諸侯，孫子與有力焉。
entries.en: He broke the powerful state of Chu in the west and entered Ying. In the north he awed Qi and Jin, making his name illustrious among the feudal lords—Sun Tzu played a role in this.
entries.literal: He broke the strong state of Chu in the west, entered Ying, awed Qi and Jin in the north, made his name illustrious among the feudal lords—Sun Tzu had a role in this.

entries.zh: 其後五年，而吳王聞齊景公死而大臣爭寵，新君弱，乃興師北伐齊。
entries.en: Five years later, the Wu king heard that Duke Jing of Qi had died and ministers were contending for favor, with the new ruler weak. He raised troops and attacked Qi to the north.
entries.literal: Its after five years, Wu king heard Qi Jing Gong died ministers contended favor, new jun weak, raised troops north attacked Qi.

entries.zh: 伍子胥諫曰：「句踐食不重味，弔死問疾，且欲有所用之也。
entries.en: Wu Zixu remonstrated: 'Goujian eats no second dish, mourns the dead and visits the sick. He means to put all this to use.
entries.literal: Wu Zixu remonstrated: "Gou Jian eats not double flavors, mourns dead asks ill, moreover wishes use them.

entries.zh: 此人不死，必為吳患。
entries.en: If this man is not killed, he will surely become a calamity for Wu.
entries.literal: This person not die, must become Wu calamity.

entries.zh: 今吳之有越，猶人之有腹心疾也。
entries.en: For Wu to have Yue beside it is like a man carrying a disease in his heart and belly.
entries.literal: Now for Wu to have Yue is like a person having a disease of the heart and viscera.

entries.zh: 而王不先越而乃務齊，不亦謬乎！」
entries.en: Yet Your Majesty does not deal with Yue first, and instead devotes himself to Qi. Is this not a mistake?'
entries.literal: King not first Yue but strives Qi, not also mistaken?"

entries.zh: 吳王不聽，伐齊，大敗齊師於艾陵，遂威鄒魯之君以歸。
entries.en: The Wu king did not listen and attacked Qi. He greatly defeated the Qi troops at Ailing, then awed the rulers of Zou and Lu and returned.
entries.literal: Wu king not listened, attacked Qi, greatly defeated Qi troops at Ai Ling, then awed Zou Lu jun returned.

entries.zh: 益疏子胥之謀。
entries.en: He became increasingly estranged from Zixu's counsel.
entries.literal: He became increasingly estranged from Zixu's counsel.

entries.zh: 伍子胥者，楚人也，名員。
entries.en: Wu Zixu was a man from Chu, named Yuan.
entries.literal: Wu Zixu was a Chu man, named Yuan.

entries.zh: 員父曰伍奢。
entries.en: Yuan's father was named Wu She.
entries.literal: Yuan's father was named Wu She.

entries.zh: 員兄曰伍尚。
entries.en: Yuan's elder brother was named Wu Shang.
entries.literal: Yuan's elder brother was named Wu Shang.

entries.zh: 其先曰伍舉，以直諫事楚莊王，有顯，故其後世有名於楚。
entries.en: His ancestor was named Wu Ju, who served King Zhuang of Chu with upright remonstration and gained prominence. His descendants therefore became famous in Chu.
entries.literal: His ancestor was named Wu Ju, who served King Zhuang of Chu with upright remonstration, gained prominence, therefore his descendants were famous in Chu.

entries.zh: 孝公既用衛鞅，鞅欲變法，恐天下議己。
entries.en: Duke Xiao employed Wei Yang, who wished to change the laws. But Yang feared that the world would criticize him.
entries.literal: Duke Xiao employed Wei Yang, who wished to reform the laws. But Yang feared that the world would criticize him.

entries.zh: 衛鞅曰：「疑行無名，疑事無功。
entries.en: Wei Yang replied, "Doubtful actions bring no reputation; doubtful affairs achieve no merit.
entries.literal: Wei Yang said: 'Doubtful actions have no reputation, doubtful affairs have no merit.

entries.zh: 且夫有高人之行者，固見非於世；
entries.en: Moreover, those who practice superior conduct are inevitably criticized by their age;
entries.literal: Moreover, those who practice superior conduct are surely criticized by the age;

entries.zh: 有獨知之慮者，必見敖於民。
entries.en: Those with uniquely wise plans are inevitably scorned by the people.
entries.literal: those with unique wisdom are inevitably scorned by the people.

entries.zh: 愚者闇於成事，知者見於未萌。
entries.en: Fools are blind to accomplished facts; the wise see things at their inception.
entries.literal: Fools are blind to accomplished facts; wise men see things at their inception.

entries.zh: 民不可與慮始而可與樂成。
entries.en: The people cannot be consulted about beginnings, but can enjoy successes.
entries.literal: The people cannot be consulted about beginnings, but they can enjoy successes.

entries.zh: 論至德者不和於俗，成大功者不謀於眾。
entries.en: Those who discuss supreme virtue do not harmonize with custom; those who accomplish great deeds do not consult the multitude.
entries.literal: Those who discuss supreme virtue do not harmonize with custom; those who accomplish great merit do not consult the multitude.

entries.zh: 是以聖人茍可以彊國，不法其故；
entries.en: Therefore, if sages can strengthen the state, they do not follow old laws;
entries.literal: Therefore, sages if they can strengthen the state, do not follow old laws;

entries.zh: 茍可以利民，不循其禮。」
entries.en: if they can benefit the people, they do not follow old rituals."
entries.literal: If they can benefit the people, do not follow old rituals.'

entries.zh: 孝公曰：「善。」
entries.en: Duke Xiao replied, "Excellent."
entries.literal: Duke Xiao said: "Good."

entries.zh: 甘龍曰：「不然。
entries.en: Gan Long objected, "Not so.
entries.literal: Gan Long said: "Not so.

entries.zh: 聖人不易民而教，知者不變法而治。
entries.en: Sages do not change the people and then teach them; the wise do not alter laws and then govern.
entries.literal: Sages do not change the people and teach, wise men do not alter laws and govern.

entries.zh: 因民而教，不勞而成功；
entries.en: Teaching in accordance with the people's nature succeeds without toil;
entries.literal: Teaching in accordance with the people succeeds without toil;

entries.zh: 緣法而治者，吏習而民安之。」
entries.en: those who govern by following established laws—officials are familiar with them and the people find peace in them.'
entries.literal: Following laws and governing, officials are familiar and people at peace with them."

entries.zh: 衛鞅曰：「龍之所言，世俗之言也。
entries.en: Wei Yang said: 'What Long says is the talk of common customs.
entries.literal: Wei Yang said: "What Long says is the talk of common customs.

entries.zh: 常人安於故俗，學者溺於所聞。
entries.en: Ordinary people are content with old customs; scholars drown in what they have heard.
entries.literal: Ordinary people are at peace with old customs, scholars drown in what they have heard.

entries.zh: 以此兩者居官守法可也，非所與論於法之外也。
entries.en: These two types are suitable for occupying office and maintaining laws, but not for discussing matters beyond the laws.
entries.literal: With these two occupying office and keeping laws is acceptable, but not for discussing beyond the laws.

entries.zh: 三代不同禮而王，五伯不同法而霸。
entries.en: The Three Dynasties differed in ritual yet became kings; the Five Hegemons differed in law yet became hegemons.
entries.literal: The Three Dynasties differed in ritual yet became kings, the Five Hegemons differed in law yet became hegemons.

entries.zh: 智者作法，愚者制焉；
entries.en: The wise create laws; fools are bound by them;
entries.literal: Wise men create laws, fools are restricted by them;

entries.zh: 賢者更禮，不肖者拘焉。」
entries.en: the worthy change rituals; the worthless are constrained by them.'
entries.literal: Worthy men change rituals, worthless men are bound by them."

entries.zh: 杜摯曰：「利不百，不變法；
entries.en: Du Zhi said: 'If the benefit is not a hundredfold, do not change the law;
entries.literal: Du Zhi said: "Benefit not a hundredfold, do not change law;

entries.zh: 功不十，不易器。
entries.en: if the merit is not tenfold, do not change the institutions.
entries.literal: Merit not tenfold, do not change implements.

entries.zh: 法古無過，循禮無邪。」
entries.en: Following antiquity has no fault; following ritual has no error.'
entries.literal: Following antiquity has no fault, following ritual has no error."

entries.zh: 衛鞅曰：「治世不一道，便國不法古。
entries.en: Wei Yang said: 'Governing the age is not by one way alone; benefiting the state does not mean following antiquity.
entries.literal: Wei Yang said: "Governing the age is not one way, benefiting the state does not follow antiquity.

entries.zh: 故湯武不循古而王，夏殷不易禮而亡。
entries.en: Therefore, Tang and Wu did not follow antiquity yet became kings; Xia and Yin did not change their rituals yet perished.
entries.literal: Therefore, Tang and Wu did not follow antiquity and became kings, Xia and Yin did not change ritual and perished.

entries.zh: 反古者不可非，而循禮者不足多。」
entries.en: Those who oppose antiquity cannot be condemned, while those who merely follow ritual are not worth praising.'
entries.literal: Those who oppose antiquity cannot be criticized, those who follow ritual are not worth praising."

entries.zh: 孝公曰：「善。」
entries.en: Duke Xiao said: 'Excellent.'
entries.literal: Duke Xiao said: "Good."

entries.zh: 以衛鞅為左庶長，卒定變法之令。
entries.en: He appointed Wei Yang as Left Chamberlain and finally established the edict for changing the laws.
entries.literal: Employed Wei Yang as Left Senior Chamberlain, finally established the change law edict.

entries.zh: 商君相秦十年，宗室貴戚多怨望者。
entries.en: Lord Shang served as Qin chancellor for ten years. Many in the royal clan and nobles were resentful.
entries.literal: Lord Shang served as Qin chancellor ten years, royal clan nobles many resentful.

entries.zh: 趙良見商君。
entries.en: Zhao Liang met with Lord Shang.
entries.literal: Zhao Liang saw Lord Shang.

entries.zh: 商君曰：「鞅之得見也，從孟蘭皋，今鞅請得交，可乎？」
entries.en: Lord Shang said: 'Yang obtained this audience through Meng Lan Gao. Now Yang wishes to form a friendship with you. Is that acceptable?'
entries.literal: Lord Shang said: "Yang obtained audience through Meng Lan Gao, now Yang wishes to form friendship with you, acceptable?"

entries.zh: 趙良曰：「僕弗敢願也。
entries.en: Zhao Liang said, 'This servant would not dare wish for such a thing.
entries.literal: Zhao Liang said, “Your servant would not dare wish for this.

entries.zh: 孔丘有言曰：『推賢而戴者進，聚不肖而王者退。』
entries.en: Kong Qiu said, "When worthy men are advanced and honored, the ruler moves forward; when unworthy men are gathered around him, the ruler falls back."
entries.literal: Kong Qiu has said: 'When worthy people are promoted and honored, the ruler advances; when the unworthy are gathered together, the ruler retreats.

entries.zh: 仆不肖，故不敢受命。
entries.en: This servant is unworthy, therefore I dare not accept the command.
entries.literal: Servant unworthy, therefore dare not accept command.

entries.zh: 仆聞之曰：『非其位而居之曰貪位，非其名而有之曰貪名。』
entries.en: This servant has heard: 'To occupy a position that is not yours is called greedy for position; to possess a name that is not yours is called greedy for name.'
entries.literal: Servant heard: Not in position yet occupy it called greedy for position, not have name yet possess it called greedy for name.

entries.zh: 仆聽君之義，則恐仆貪位貪名也。
entries.en: If this servant listens to Your Lordship's righteousness, I fear it would make this servant appear greedy for position and greedy for name.
entries.literal: Servant hears Your Lordship righteousness, then fears servant greedy for position greedy for name.

entries.zh: 故不敢聞命。」
entries.en: Therefore, I dare not hear the command.'
entries.literal: Therefore, dare not hear command."

entries.zh: 商君曰：「子不說吾治秦與？」
entries.en: Lord Shang said: 'Are you not pleased with how I govern Qin?'
entries.literal: Lord Shang said: "You not pleased with my governing Qin?"

entries.zh: 趙良曰：「反聽之謂聰，內視之謂明，自勝之謂彊。
entries.en: Zhao Liang said: 'To listen to opposition is called intelligence; to examine oneself internally is called clarity; to conquer oneself is called strength.
entries.literal: Zhao Liang said: "Listen to opposition called intelligent, examine internally called clear, conquer self called strong.

entries.zh: 虞舜有言曰：『自卑也尚矣。』
entries.en: Yu Shun said, "To lower oneself remains the highest course."
entries.literal: Yu Shun has said: 'To humble oneself is still the highest course.

entries.zh: 君不若道虞舜之道，無為問仆矣。」
entries.en: Your Lordship would do better to follow Yu Shun's way. There is no need to ask this servant.'
entries.literal: Your Lordship not as good as follow Yu Shun way, no need ask servant."

entries.zh: 商君曰：「始秦戎翟之教，父子無別，同室而居。
entries.en: Lord Shang said: 'Initially Qin had the teachings of the Rong and Di barbarians. Fathers and sons had no distinctions and dwelt in the same rooms.
entries.literal: Lord Shang said: "Initially Qin Rong Di teachings, fathers and sons no distinction, same room dwelling.

entries.zh: 今我更制其教，而為其男女之別，大筑冀闕，營如魯衛矣。
entries.en: Now I have reformed those customs, established separation between men and women, built the palace watchtowers on a grand scale, and made Qin's settlements resemble those of Lu and Wei.
entries.literal: Now I have changed their customs, established distinctions between men and women, greatly built the Ji Que palace, and made Qin's settlements like those of Lu and Wei.

entries.zh: 子觀我治秦也，孰與五羖大夫賢？」
entries.en: Look at how I have governed Qin: compared with the Five Ram Skin Grand Master, who is worthier?'
entries.literal: You observe my governing of Qin: compared with the Five Ram Skin Grand Master, who is worthier?"

entries.zh: 趙良曰：「千羊之皮，不如一狐之掖；
entries.en: Zhao Liang said: 'A thousand sheep skins are not as good as one fox collar;
entries.literal: Zhao Liang said: "Thousand sheep skins, not as one fox collar;

entries.zh: 千人之諾諾，不如一士之諤諤。
entries.en: a thousand people saying 'yes, yes' are not as good as one scholar who is frank and direct.
entries.literal: Thousand people yes-yes, not as one scholar frank-frank.

entries.zh: 武王諤諤以昌，殷紂墨墨以亡。
entries.en: King Wu prospered through frankness, while Yin Zhou perished through flattery.
entries.literal: Wu Wang frank-frank to prosper, Yin Zhou flattering to perish.

entries.zh: 君若不非武王乎，則仆請終日正言而無誅，可乎？」
entries.en: If Your Lordship does not criticize King Wu, then this servant requests to speak correct words all day without punishment. Would that be acceptable?'
entries.literal: Your Lordship if not criticize Wu Wang, then servant please all day correct words without punishment, acceptable?"

entries.zh: 商君曰：「語有之矣，貌言華也，至言實也，苦言藥也，甘言疾也。
entries.en: Lord Shang said: 'There is a saying: flattering words are flowers, honest words are fruit, bitter words are medicine, and sweet words are sickness.
entries.literal: Lord Shang said: "There is a saying: flattering words are flowers, utmost words are fruit, bitter words are medicine, and sweet words are sickness.

entries.zh: 夫子果肯終日正言，鞅之藥也。
entries.en: If Sir is truly willing to speak correct words all day, it will be medicine for Yang.
entries.literal: Sir indeed willing all day correct words, Yang medicine.

entries.zh: 鞅將事子，子又何辭焉！」
entries.en: Yang will serve Sir. Why would Sir decline?'
entries.literal: Yang will serve Sir, Sir why decline!"

entries.zh: 趙良曰：「夫五羖大夫，荊之鄙人也。
entries.en: Zhao Liang said: 'The Five Ram Skin Grand Master was a rustic from Jing.
entries.literal: Zhao Liang said: "Five Ram Skin Grand Master, Jing barbarian.

entries.zh: 聞秦繆公之賢而願望見，行而無資，自粥於秦客，被褐食牛。
entries.en: He heard of Duke Mu of Qin's worthiness and wished to see him. Traveling without resources, he sold himself to a Qin merchant, wore coarse clothing, and tended cattle.
entries.literal: Heard Qin Mu Gong worthy wished see, traveled without resources, sold self to Qin guest, wore coarse ate cattle.

entries.zh: 期年，繆公知之，舉之牛口之下，而加之百姓之上，秦國莫敢望焉。
entries.en: After one year, Duke Mu discovered him, raised him from tending cattle, and placed him above the common people. No one in Qin dared to rival him.
entries.literal: One year, Mu Gong knew him, raised from cattle mouth below, placed above hundred families, Qin state none dared rival.

entries.zh: 相秦六七年，而東伐鄭，三置晉國之君，一救荊國之禍。
entries.en: He served as Qin's chancellor for six or seven years, attacked Zheng to the east, established Jin's rulers three times, and once saved Jing from calamity.
entries.literal: Served as Qin chancellor six seven years, east attacked Zheng, three times established Jin state rulers, once saved Jing state calamity.

entries.zh: 發教封內，而巴人致貢；
entries.en: He issued teachings within his borders, and the Ba people sent tribute;
entries.literal: Issued teachings within borders, Ba people sent tribute;

entries.zh: 施德諸侯，而八戎來服。
entries.en: He extended his virtue to the feudal lords, and the eight Rong tribes came to submit.
entries.literal: Extended virtue to feudal lords, eight Rong came submit.

entries.zh: 由余聞之，款關請見。
entries.en: You Yu heard of this and knocked at the border to request an audience.
entries.literal: You Yu heard of it, knocked border requested see.

entries.zh: 五羖大夫之相秦也，勞不坐乘，暑不張蓋，行於國中，不從車乘，不操干戈，功名藏於府庫，德行施於後世。
entries.en: When the Five Ram Skin Grand Master served as chancellor of Qin, he did not ride in carriages when laboring, did not spread a canopy in the heat, and traveled through the state without attendant carriages or weapons. His merit and fame were stored in the treasuries, and his virtue and conduct extended to later generations.
entries.literal: When the Five Ram Skin Grand Master served as chancellor of Qin, he did not ride in carriages when laboring, did not spread a canopy in the heat, and traveled through the state without attendant carriages or weapons; his merit and fame were stored in the treasuries, and his virtue and conduct extended to later generations.

entries.zh: 五羖大夫死，秦國男女流涕，童子不歌謠，舂者不相杵。
entries.en: When the Five Ram Skin Grand Master died, the men and women of Qin wept, children did not sing songs, and those pounding grain did not strike their pestles.
entries.literal: Five Ram Skin Grand Master died, Qin state males females flowed tears, children not sing songs, pestle not pound.

entries.zh: 此五羖大夫之德也。
entries.en: This was the virtue of the Five Ram Skin Grand Master.
entries.literal: This Five Ram Skin Grand Master virtue.

entries.zh: 今君之見秦王也，因嬖人景監以為主，非所以為名也。
entries.en: Now Your Lordship obtained an audience with the King of Qin through the patronage of the favored minister Jing Jian. That is not the way to establish a name.
entries.literal: Now Your Lordship gained audience with the King of Qin through the favored minister Jing Jian as sponsor; this is not the way to establish a reputation.

entries.zh: 相秦不以百姓為事，而大筑冀闕，非所以為功也。
entries.en: Serving as chancellor of Qin without taking the common people as your concern, but greatly building the Ji Que palace—this is not the way to achieve merit.
entries.literal: Chancellor Qin not take hundred families as affairs, greatly build Ji Que, not way to make merit.

entries.zh: 刑黥太子之師傅，殘傷民以駿刑，是積怨畜禍也。
entries.en: To punish and tattoo the crown prince's tutors, and to injure the people with severe penalties, is to pile up resentment and store away disaster.
entries.literal: Punishing and tattooing the crown prince's tutors, injuring the people with harsh punishments: this is accumulating resentment and storing up calamity.

entries.zh: 教之化民也深於命，民之效上也捷於令。
entries.en: Teaching transforms the people more deeply than commands; the people serve their superiors more swiftly than orders.
entries.literal: Teach transform people deeper than commands, people serve superiors swifter than orders.

entries.zh: 今君又左建外易，非所以為教也。
entries.en: Now Your Lordship has again set up perverse outward changes. That is not the way to teach the people.
entries.literal: Now Your Lordship has again established deviant external changes; this is not the way to teach.

entries.zh: 君又南面而稱寡人，日繩秦之貴公子。
entries.en: Your Lordship faces south and calls yourself 'the solitary one,' daily bringing Qin's noble sons under restraint.
entries.literal: Your Lordship again faces south and calls yourself 'the solitary one,' daily bringing Qin's noble sons under restraint.

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：『相鼠有體，人而無禮，人而無禮，何不遄死。』
entries.en: The Poetry says: 'Even rats have bodies; if a person lacks ritual propriety, if a person lacks ritual propriety, why not die quickly?'
entries.literal: Poetry says: Rat has body, person without ritual, person without ritual, why not quickly die.

entries.zh: 以詩觀之，非所以為壽也。
entries.en: Viewing it through the Poetry, this is not the way for longevity.
entries.literal: Observe with poetry, not way for longevity.

entries.zh: 公子虔杜門不出已八年矣，君又殺祝懽而黥公孫賈。
entries.en: Gongzi Qian has shut his door and not gone out for eight years already; Your Lordship has again killed Zhu Huan and tattooed Gongsun Jia.
entries.literal: Gongzi Qian closed door not go out already eight years, Your Lordship again kill Zhu Huan tattoo Gongsun Jia.

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：『得人者興，失人者崩。』
entries.en: The Poetry says: 'Those who gain the people's support will flourish; those who lose the people's support will collapse.'
entries.literal: Poetry says: Obtain people prosper, lose people collapse.

entries.zh: 此數事者，非所以得人也。
entries.en: These several matters are not the ways to gain the people's support.
entries.literal: These several matters are not the ways to obtain people.

entries.zh: 君之出也，後車十數，從車載甲，多力而駢脅者為驂乘，持矛而操闟戟者旁車而趨。
entries.en: When Your Lordship goes out, there are more than ten following carriages; retinue carriages carry armor, powerful men serve as chariot guards, and men holding spears and halberds hurry beside the carriages.
entries.literal: When Your Lordship goes out, there are more than ten following carriages, retinue carriages carry armor, powerful men with broad ribs serve as chariot guards, and men holding spears and halberds hurry beside the carriages.

entries.zh: 此一物不具，君固不出。
entries.en: If even one of these things is not prepared, Your Lordship certainly will not go out.
entries.literal: This one thing not prepared, Your Lordship certainly not go out.

entries.zh: 《書》曰：『恃德者昌，恃力者亡。』
entries.en: The Documents say: 'Those who rely on virtue will flourish; those who rely on force will perish.'
entries.literal: Documents say: Rely on virtue prosper, rely on force perish.

entries.zh: 君之危若朝露，尚將欲延年益壽乎？
entries.en: Your Lordship's position is as precarious as morning dew—do you still wish to prolong your years and increase your lifespan?
entries.literal: Your Lordship danger like morning dew, still wish prolong years increase life?

entries.zh: 則何不歸十五都，灌園於鄙，勸秦王顯巖穴之士，養老存孤，敬父兄，序有功，尊有德，可以少安。
entries.en: Why then not return the fifteen cities and tend gardens in the countryside? You could urge the King of Qin to bring forward scholars living in seclusion, care for the aged and the orphaned, respect fathers and elder brothers, rank those with merit, and honor those with virtue. This might bring you a little security.
entries.literal: Then why not return the fifteen cities and tend gardens in the countryside? Urge the Qin king to promote scholars living in mountain caves, care for the elderly and orphans, respect fathers and elder brothers, reward the meritorious, and honor the virtuous. This would bring some measure of security.

entries.zh: 君尚將貪商於之富，寵秦國之教，畜百姓之怨，秦王一旦捐賓客而不立朝，秦國之所以收君者，豈其微哉？
entries.en: Yet Your Lordship still covets the wealth of Shangyu, favors Qin's teachings, and stores up the resentment of the common people. If the King of Qin one day casts aside his guests and no longer appears at court, will the means by which Qin seizes Your Lordship be slight?
entries.literal: Your Lordship still covets the wealth of Shang, favors Qin's teachings, and accumulates the resentment of the common people. If the Qin king one day abandons his guests and no longer appears at court, the means by which Qin will seize Your Lordship will hardly be slight.

entries.zh: 亡可翹足而待。」
entries.en: Your ruin can be waited for while standing on tiptoe.'
entries.literal: Your destruction can be awaited with one foot raised."

entries.zh: 商君弗從。
entries.en: Lord Shang did not follow this advice.
entries.literal: Lord Shang did not follow this advice.

entries.zh: 商君者，衛之諸庶孽公子也，名鞅，姓公孫氏，其祖本姬姓也。
entries.en: Lord Shang was the illegitimate son of a minor noble from Wei. His name was Yang, his surname Gongsun, and his ancestors originally bore the Ji surname.
entries.literal: Lord Shang was an illegitimate son of a minor branch of the Wei nobility. His name was Yang, his surname Gongsun, and his ancestors originally bore the Ji surname.

entries.zh: 鞅少好刑名之學，事魏相公叔座為中庶子。
entries.en: From youth, Yang was devoted to the study of law and governance. He served as a junior aide to Gongshu Zuo, chancellor of Wei.
entries.literal: From a young age, Yang was fascinated by the study of law and political philosophy. He served as a junior aide to Gongshu Zuo, the chancellor of Wei.

entries.zh: 公叔座知其賢，未及進。
entries.en: Gongshu Zuo recognized Yang's talent but had not yet promoted him.
entries.literal: Gongshu Zuo recognized Yang's exceptional abilities but had not yet promoted him.

entries.zh: 會座病，魏惠王親往問病，曰：「公叔病有如不可諱，將柰社稷何？」
entries.en: Just then Gongshu fell ill. King Hui of Wei went in person to inquire after his health and asked, "If the chancellor should pass away, what will become of the state?"
entries.literal: Just then Zuo fell ill, King Hui of Wei personally went to inquire after his illness, said: 'If chancellor should die, what shall we do for the state?'

entries.zh: 公叔曰：「座之中庶子公孫鞅，年雖少，有奇才，願王舉國而聽之。」
entries.en: Gongshu replied, "My junior aide, Gongsun Yang, is young but possesses extraordinary talent. I urge Your Majesty to entrust the entire state to his care."
entries.literal: Gongshu said: 'My junior aide Gongsun Yang, though young, has extraordinary talent, I wish Your Majesty would entrust the entire state to him.'

entries.zh: 王嘿然。
entries.en: The king fell silent.
entries.literal: The king fell silent.

entries.zh: 王且去，座屏人言曰：「王即不聽用鞅，必殺之，無令出境。」
entries.en: As the king was about to depart, Gongshu dismissed his attendants and said in private, "If Your Majesty will not employ Yang, then you must kill him. Do not allow him to leave our borders."
entries.literal: The king was about to leave when Zuo dismissed his attendants and said: 'If Your Majesty does not employ Yang, you must kill him, do not let him leave the borders.'

entries.zh: 王許諾而去。
entries.en: The king agreed and departed.
entries.literal: The king agreed and left.

entries.zh: 公叔座召鞅謝曰：「今者王問可以為相者，我言若，王色不許我。
entries.en: Gongshu Zuo summoned Yang and apologized, saying, "Just now when the king asked who could serve as chancellor, I recommended you. But his expression showed he did not approve.
entries.literal: Gongshu Zuo summoned Yang and apologized: 'Just now when the king asked who could be chancellor, I recommended you, but the king's expression did not approve.

entries.zh: 我方先君後臣，因謂王即弗用鞅，當殺之。
entries.en: I place loyalty to the ruler above friendship with ministers, so I told the king that if he would not employ you, he should execute you.
entries.literal: I put loyalty to the ruler above ministerial friendship, so I told the king that if he would not employ you, he should have you killed.

entries.zh: 王許我。
entries.en: The king agreed with me.
entries.literal: The king agreed.

entries.zh: 汝可疾去矣，且見禽。」
entries.en: You should leave at once—you will soon be arrested."
entries.literal: You should leave quickly, you will soon be captured.'

entries.zh: 鞅曰：「彼王不能用君之言任臣，又安能用君之言殺臣乎？」
entries.en: Yang replied, "If the king cannot follow your advice to employ me, how can he follow your advice to kill me?"
entries.literal: Yang said: 'If that king cannot follow your advice to appoint me, how can he follow your advice to kill me?'

entries.zh: 卒不去。
entries.en: In the end, he did not leave.
entries.literal: In the end, Yang did not leave.

entries.zh: 惠王既去，而謂左右曰：「公叔病甚，悲乎，欲令寡人以國聽公孫鞅也，豈不悖哉！」
entries.en: After King Hui left, he remarked to his attendants, "Gongshu is gravely ill—how unfortunate! He wants me to entrust the entire state to Gongsun Yang. Is this not madness?"
entries.literal: King Hui having departed, he told his attendants: 'Gongshu is gravely ill, how lamentable, he wants me to entrust the state to Gongsun Yang, is this not absurd!'

entries.zh: 張儀者，魏人也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi was a native of Wei.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi was a man of Wei.

entries.zh: 始嘗與蘇秦俱事鬼谷先生，學術，蘇秦自以不及張儀。
entries.en: In his youth, he studied the arts of persuasion alongside Su Qin under Master Guigu of Ghost Valley. Su Qin always considered himself inferior to Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: In his youth, he studied the arts of persuasion alongside Su Qin under Master Guigu. Su Qin always considered himself inferior to Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 蘇秦之舍人乃辭去。
entries.en: Su Qin's attendants then departed.
entries.literal: Su Qin's attendants then took their leave.

entries.zh: 張儀曰：「賴子得顯，方且報德，何故去也？」
entries.en: Zhang Yi said, "Thanks to you, I have achieved prominence. I was just about to repay your kindness—why are you leaving?"
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said, 'Thanks to you I have become prominent. I was just about to repay your kindness—why are you leaving?'

entries.zh: 舍人曰：「臣非知君，知君乃蘇君。
entries.en: The attendant said, "I do not know you; I know only Su Qin.
entries.literal: The attendant said, 'I don't know you— I know Su Qin.

entries.zh: 蘇君憂秦伐趙敗從約，以為非君莫能得秦柄，故感怒君，使臣陰奉給君資，盡蘇君之計謀。
entries.en: Su Qin worried that Qin would attack Zhao and break the alliances. He believed that no one but you could control Qin's power, so he provoked you with anger and had me secretly support and provide for you, carrying out all of Su Qin's plans.
entries.literal: Su Qin worried that Qin would attack Zhao and break the alliances. He believed no one but you could control Qin's power, so he provoked you with anger and had me secretly support and provide for you, carrying out all of Su Qin's plans.

entries.zh: 今君已用，請歸報。」
entries.en: Now that you are employed, let me return and report."
entries.literal: Now that you are employed, let me return and report.'

entries.zh: 張儀曰：「嗟乎，此在吾術中而不悟，吾不及蘇君明矣！
entries.en: Zhang Yi said, "Alas, this was within my calculations, but I did not realize it. I am not as perceptive as Su Qin!
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said, 'Alas, this was within my calculations but I didn't realize it. I am not as perceptive as Su Qin!

entries.zh: 吾又新用，安能謀趙乎？
entries.en: I have just been appointed—how could I possibly plot against Zhao?
entries.literal: I have just been appointed—how can I plot against Zhao?

entries.zh: 為吾謝蘇君，蘇君之時，儀何敢言。
entries.en: Please apologize to Lord Su on my behalf. While Lord Su lives, how could I dare speak of such plans?
entries.literal: Please convey my apologies to Su Qin. As long as Su Qin lives, how would I dare speak of such matters?

entries.zh: 且蘇君在，儀寧渠能乎！」
entries.en: As long as Su Qin lives, how could I possibly rival him!"
entries.literal: As long as Su Qin lives, how could I possibly rival him!'

entries.zh: 張儀既相秦，為文檄告楚相曰：「始吾從若飲，我不盜而璧，若笞我。
entries.en: Once Zhang Yi became prime minister of Qin, he sent a formal declaration to the prime minister of Chu: "When I drank with you, I did not steal your jade disc, yet you had me beaten.
entries.literal: Once Zhang Yi became prime minister of Qin, he sent a formal declaration to the prime minister of Chu: 'When I drank with you, I didn't steal your jade disc, yet you had me beaten.

entries.zh: 若善守汝國，我顧且盜而城！」
entries.en: If you guard your state well, I might just steal your cities instead!"
entries.literal: If you guard your state well, I might just steal your cities instead!'

entries.zh: 苴蜀相攻擊，各來告急於秦。
entries.en: Ju and Shu attacked one another, and each came urgently to Qin requesting aid.
entries.literal: The rulers of Shu and Ba attacked each other and both sent urgent appeals to Qin for assistance.

entries.zh: 秦惠王欲發兵以伐蜀，以為道險狹難至，而韓又來侵秦，秦惠王欲先伐韓，後伐蜀，恐不利，欲先伐蜀，恐韓襲秦之敝。
entries.en: King Hui of Qin wanted to send troops against Shu, but considered the roads too dangerous and narrow to reach it easily. At the same time, Han had come to invade Qin. King Hui wanted to attack Han first and Shu afterward, but feared this would not be advantageous; he wanted to attack Shu first, but feared Han would strike Qin while it was exhausted.
entries.literal: King Hui of Qin wanted to send troops to attack Shu, but the roads were dangerous and narrow, making them difficult to traverse. Meanwhile, Han was invading Qin. King Hui wanted to attack Han first, then Shu, but feared it would be disadvantageous. He wanted to attack Shu first, but worried that Han would attack Qin while it was weakened.

entries.zh: 猶豫未能決。
entries.en: He wavered and could not make up his mind.
entries.literal: He hesitated and couldn't decide.

entries.zh: 司馬錯與張儀爭論於惠王之前，司馬錯欲伐蜀，張儀曰：「不如伐韓。」
entries.en: Sima Cuo and Zhang Yi debated before King Hui. Sima Cuo wanted to attack Shu; Zhang Yi said, "Better to attack Han."
entries.literal: Sima Cuo and Zhang Yi debated before King Hui. Sima Cuo wanted to attack Shu; Zhang Yi said, 'Better to attack Han.'

entries.zh: 王曰：「請聞其說。」
entries.en: The king said, "Let me hear your reasoning."
entries.literal: The king said, 'Let me hear your reasoning.'

entries.zh: 蘇秦已而告其舍人曰：「張儀，天下賢士，吾殆弗如也。
entries.en: Later, Su Qin told his attendants, "Zhang Yi is the most talented man in the world. I am no match for him.
entries.literal: Later, Su Qin told his attendants: 'Zhang Yi is the most talented man in the world. I am no match for him.

entries.zh: 今吾幸先用，而能用秦柄者，獨張儀可耳。
entries.en: Fortunately, I was employed first. The only one who can wield Qin's power is Zhang Yi alone.
entries.literal: Fortunately, I was employed first. The only one who can wield Qin's power is Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 然貧，無因以進。
entries.en: But Zhang Yi was poor and had no route by which to advance.
entries.literal: But he is poor and has no means to advance himself.

entries.zh: 吾恐其樂小利而不遂，故召辱之，以激其意。
entries.en: I feared that he might be satisfied with petty gains and fail to accomplish anything great, so I summoned him here and humiliated him in order to rouse his ambition.
entries.literal: I feared he might be content with small gains and not achieve great things, so I summoned and humiliated him to stir his ambition.

entries.zh: 子為我陰奉之。」
entries.en: Secretly support him for me."
entries.literal: Secretly support him for me.'

entries.zh: 乃言趙王，發金幣車馬，使人微隨張儀，與同宿舍，稍稍近就之，奉以車馬金錢，所欲用，為取給，而弗告。
entries.en: He spoke to the King of Zhao, who provided gold, coins, chariots, and horses. Su Qin sent people to secretly follow Zhang Yi, share his lodging with him, gradually draw close to him, and provide him with chariots, horses, gold, and money—whatever he needed was supplied, without revealing who was behind it.
entries.literal: He spoke to the King of Zhao, who provided gold, coins, chariots, and horses. Su Qin sent people to secretly follow Zhang Yi, share his lodging, gradually get close to him, and provide him with chariots, horses, gold, and money—whatever he needed, without telling him who was behind it.

entries.zh: 張儀遂得以見秦惠王。
entries.en: In this way, Zhang Yi gained an audience with King Hui of Qin.
entries.literal: Thus, Zhang Yi was able to gain an audience with King Hui of Qin.

entries.zh: 惠王以為客卿，與謀伐諸侯。
entries.en: King Hui made him a guest minister and discussed plans with him for attacking the other feudal lords.
entries.literal: King Hui appointed him as a guest minister and consulted with him on attacking the other feudal lords.

entries.zh: 張儀已學游說諸侯。
entries.en: After Zhang Yi had completed his studies, he traveled among the feudal lords as a persuader.
entries.literal: Once Zhang Yi had mastered the arts of diplomatic persuasion, he traveled among the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 嘗從楚相飲，已而楚相亡璧，門下意張儀，曰：「儀貧無行，必此盜相君之璧。」
entries.en: Once he drank with the prime minister of Chu. Later, the prime minister discovered that his precious jade disc was missing. His attendants suspected Zhang Yi, saying, "Zhang Yi is poor and of questionable character—he must have stolen the prime minister's jade disc."
entries.literal: He once drank with the Prime Minister of Chu. Later, the prime minister discovered his precious jade disc was missing. His attendants suspected Zhang Yi, saying, 'Zhang Yi is poor and of questionable character—he must have stolen the prime minister's jade disc.'

entries.zh: 共執張儀，掠笞數百，不服，醳之。
entries.en: They seized Zhang Yi and flogged him several hundred times. When he still refused to confess, they released him.
entries.literal: They seized Zhang Yi and flogged him several hundred times, but he refused to confess, so they branded him instead.

entries.zh: 其妻曰：「嘻！
entries.en: His wife said, "Alas!
entries.literal: His wife said, 'Alas!

entries.zh: 子毋讀書游說，安得此辱乎？」
entries.en: If you had not studied books and traveled as a persuader, how would you have come to this humiliation?"
entries.literal: If you hadn't studied and traveled as a persuader, how would you have come to this humiliation?'

entries.zh: 張儀謂其妻曰：「視吾舌尚在不？」
entries.en: Zhang Yi asked his wife, "Is my tongue still there?"
entries.literal: Zhang Yi asked his wife, 'Is my tongue still there?'

entries.zh: 其妻笑曰：「舌在也。」
entries.en: His wife laughed and said, "It's still there."
entries.literal: His wife laughed and said, 'It's still there.'

entries.zh: 儀曰：「足矣。」
entries.en: Zhang Yi replied, "That's enough."
entries.literal: Zhang Yi replied, 'That's enough.'

entries.zh: 蘇秦已說趙王而得相約從親，然恐秦之攻諸侯，敗約後負，念莫可使用於秦者，乃使人微感張儀曰：「子始與蘇秦善，今秦已當路，子何不往游，以求通子之願？」
entries.en: After Su Qin had persuaded the King of Zhao and secured alliances with neighboring states for united action, he worried that Qin might attack the other lords and break the alliances. Thinking of who might be useful in Qin, he secretly sent someone to sound out Zhang Yi: "You were once close to Su Qin. Now Qin holds power—why not go there to seek your fortune?"
entries.literal: After Su Qin had persuaded the King of Zhao and secured alliances with neighboring states, he worried that Qin might attack the other lords and break the alliances. Thinking of who might be useful in Qin, he secretly sent someone to tempt Zhang Yi: 'You were once close to Su Qin. Now Qin holds power—why not go there to seek your fortune?'

entries.zh: 張儀於是之趙，上謁求見蘇秦。
entries.en: Zhang Yi accordingly went to Zhao and requested an audience with Su Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then traveled to Zhao and sought an audience with Su Qin.

entries.zh: 蘇秦乃誡門下人不為通，又使不得去者數日。
entries.en: Su Qin instructed his attendants not to announce Zhang Yi, and made him wait for several days without allowing him to leave.
entries.literal: Su Qin ordered his attendants not to announce him, and kept him waiting for several days without letting him leave.

entries.zh: 已而見之，坐之堂下，賜仆妾之食。
entries.en: At last, when Su Qin received him, he seated Zhang Yi below the hall and gave him the fare of servants and concubines.
entries.literal: Finally, when he received him, he seated Zhang Yi below the main platform and served him food meant for servants and concubines.

entries.zh: 因而數讓之曰：「以子之材能，乃自令困辱至此。
entries.en: Then he repeatedly rebuked him, saying, "With your talents and abilities, you have brought yourself to this state of destitution and humiliation.
entries.literal: Then he repeatedly rebuked him: 'With your talents and abilities, you've brought yourself to this state of destitution and humiliation.

entries.zh: 吾寧不能言而富貴子，子不足收也。」
entries.en: I could easily speak on your behalf and make you wealthy and honored, but you are not worth saving."
entries.literal: I could speak on your behalf and make you wealthy and honored, but you're not worth saving.'

entries.zh: 謝去之。
entries.en: He sent him away.
entries.literal: He sent him away.

entries.zh: 張儀之來也，自以為故人，求益，反見辱，怒，念諸侯莫可事，獨秦能苦趙，乃遂入秦。
entries.en: Zhang Yi had come expecting to be treated as an old friend and receive assistance. Instead, he was humiliated. Angry, he realized that no other lord would employ him—only Qin could challenge Zhao. So he entered Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi had come expecting to be treated as an old friend and receive assistance. Instead he was humiliated. Angry, he realized no other lord would take him in—only Qin could challenge Zhao. So he went to Qin.

entries.zh: 儀曰：「親魏善楚，下兵三川，塞什谷之口，當屯留之道，魏絕南陽，楚臨南鄭，秦攻新城、宜陽，以臨二周之郊，誅周王之罪，侵楚、魏之地。
entries.en: Zhang Yi said, "Ally with Wei and befriend Chu. Send troops down to Sanchuan, block the Shigu pass, and occupy the Tunliu road. Cut off Nanyang from Wei, and have Chu threaten Nandun. Qin should attack Xincheng and Yiyang to approach the suburbs of the two Zhous. Punish the Zhou king's crimes, and invade Chu and Wei territory.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said: 'Ally with Wei and befriend Chu. Send troops down to Sanchuan, block the Shigu pass, occupy the Tunliu road. Cut off Nanyang from Wei, have Chu threaten Nandun. Qin attacks Xincheng and Yiyang to approach the suburbs of the two Zhous. Punish the Zhou king's crimes, invade Chu and Wei territory.

entries.zh: 周自知不能救，九鼎寶器必出。
entries.en: Zhou, knowing it cannot save itself, will be forced to surrender the Nine Tripods and its precious vessels.
entries.literal: Zhou will realize it cannot save itself and will inevitably surrender the Nine Tripods and precious vessels.

entries.zh: 據九鼎，案圖籍，挾天子以令於天下，天下莫敢不聽，此王業也。
entries.en: Seize the Nine Tripods, control the maps and registers, and hold the Son of Heaven hostage to command the world; none would dare disobey. This is the work of a true king.
entries.literal: Seize the Nine Tripods, control the maps and registers, hold the Son of Heaven hostage to command the world—none would dare disobey. This is the work of a true king.

entries.zh: 今夫蜀，西僻之國而戎翟之倫也，敝兵勞眾不足以成名，得其地不足以為利。
entries.en: As for Shu, it is a remote state in the west, of the same kind as the Rong and Di. To wear out the army and exhaust the people there would not win fame, and taking its territory would bring no real profit.
entries.literal: Now Shu is a remote western land inhabited by barbarians. Wasting troops and exhausting the people there would not bring fame; gaining its territory would bring no benefit.

entries.zh: 臣聞爭名者於朝，爭利者於市。
entries.en: I have heard that men contend for reputation at court, and contend for profit in the marketplace.
entries.literal: I have heard that those who compete for fame do so at court; those who compete for profit do so in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 今三川、周室，天下之朝市也，而王不爭焉，顧爭於戎翟，去王業遠矣。」
entries.en: Now Sanchuan and Zhou are the court and marketplace of the world. Yet Your Majesty does not compete there, instead competing with barbarians; that is far from true kingship."
entries.literal: Now Sanchuan and Zhou are the court and marketplace of the world. Yet Your Majesty does not compete there, instead competing with barbarians—that is far from true kingship.'

entries.zh: 秦惠王十年，使公子華與張儀圍蒲陽，降之。
entries.en: In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he dispatched Prince Hua and Zhang Yi to encircle Puyang, which yielded to them.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he sent Prince Hua and Zhang Yi to besiege Puyang, which surrendered.

entries.zh: 儀因言秦復與魏，而使公子繇質於魏。
entries.en: Zhang Yi then urged that Qin renew relations with Wei and send Prince You as hostage to Wei.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then proposed that Qin reconcile with Wei and send Prince You as hostage to Wei.

entries.zh: 儀因說魏王曰：「秦王之遇魏甚厚，魏不可以無禮。」
entries.en: Zhang Yi then addressed the King of Wei: "The King of Qin deals with Wei most generously. Wei cannot afford to be ungracious."
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then persuaded the King of Wei: 'The King of Qin treats Wei very generously. Wei cannot be discourteous.'

entries.zh: 魏因入上郡、少梁，謝秦惠王。
entries.en: Wei accordingly offered up Shangdun and Shaoliang as thanks to King Hui of Qin.
entries.literal: Wei therefore ceded Shangdun and Shaoliang to thank King Hui of Qin.

entries.zh: 惠王乃以張儀為相，更名少梁曰夏陽。
entries.en: King Hui therefore installed Zhang Yi as prime minister and rechristened Shaoliang as Xiayang.
entries.literal: King Hui then appointed Zhang Yi as prime minister and renamed Shaoliang to Xiayang.

entries.zh: 儀相秦四歲，立惠王為王。
entries.en: Zhang Yi served as Qin's prime minister for four years and helped establish King Hui as king.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi served as Qin prime minister four years, established King Hui as king.

entries.zh: 居一歲，為秦將，取陜。
entries.en: A year later, he commanded Qin's armies and captured Xie.
entries.literal: After one year, he served as Qin's general and took Xie.

entries.zh: 筑上郡塞。
entries.en: He constructed defensive barriers in Shangdun.
entries.literal: He built fortifications at Shangdun.

entries.zh: 其後二年，使與齊、楚之相會齧桑。
entries.en: Two years afterward, he met with the prime ministers of Qi and Chu at Yaosang.
entries.literal: Two years later, he met with the prime ministers of Qi and Chu at Yaosang.

entries.zh: 東還而免相，相魏以為秦，欲令魏先事秦而諸侯效之。
entries.en: Upon returning east, he was relieved of his premiership. He became prime minister of Wei in Qin's service, intending for Wei to submit to Qin first so that other lords would follow suit.
entries.literal: On his return east, he was dismissed as prime minister. He became prime minister of Wei to serve Qin, hoping Wei would submit to Qin first so other lords would follow.

entries.zh: 魏王不肯聽儀。
entries.en: The King of Wei would not heed Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: The King of Wei refused to listen to Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 秦王怒，伐取魏之曲沃、平周，復陰厚張儀益甚。
entries.en: The King of Qin grew furious and seized Wei's Quwo and Pingzhou. He covertly redoubled his patronage of Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: The King of Qin was angry and attacked Wei's Quwo and Pingzhou. He secretly increased his support for Zhang Yi even more.

entries.zh: 張儀慚，無以歸報。
entries.en: Zhang Yi burned with shame, having no accomplishments to report.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi was ashamed and had nothing to show for his efforts.

entries.zh: 留魏四歲而魏襄王卒，哀王立。
entries.en: He tarried in Wei for four years until King Xiang of Wei passed away, and King Ai took the throne.
entries.literal: He remained in Wei four years until King Xiang of Wei died and King Ai ascended.

entries.zh: 張儀復說哀王，哀王不聽。
entries.en: Zhang Yi once more urged King Ai, but he paid no heed.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi again persuaded King Ai, but he wouldn't listen.

entries.zh: 於是張儀陰令秦伐魏。
entries.en: Thus, Zhang Yi covertly commanded Qin to assault Wei.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi secretly ordered Qin to attack Wei.

entries.zh: 魏與秦戰，敗。
entries.en: Wei battled Qin and suffered defeat.
entries.literal: Wei fought Qin and was defeated.

entries.zh: 明年，齊又來敗魏於觀津。
entries.en: The following year, Qi once more vanquished Wei at Guanjin.
entries.literal: The next year, Qi again defeated Wei at Guanjin.

entries.zh: 秦復欲攻魏，先敗韓申差軍，斬首八萬，諸侯震恐。
entries.en: Qin sought to strike Wei once more. First they routed Han's Shen Chai army, taking eighty thousand heads. The feudal lords trembled in fear.
entries.literal: Qin wanted to attack Wei again. First they defeated Han's Shen Chai army, beheading eighty thousand. The feudal lords were terrified.

entries.zh: 而張儀復說魏王曰：「魏地方不至千里，卒不過三十萬。
entries.en: Zhang Yi once more addressed the King of Wei: "Wei's domain measures barely a thousand li square, its soldiers numbering no more than three hundred thousand.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi again persuaded the King of Wei: 'Wei's territory is not even a thousand li square, with troops not exceeding three hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 地四平，諸侯四通輻湊，無名山大川之限。
entries.en: The terrain lies flat in all directions, with highways from the feudal lords meeting like spokes at a wheel's hub, lacking famed mountains or mighty rivers for defense.
entries.literal: The land is flat all around, with roads from the feudal lords converging like spokes to a hub, without famous mountains or great rivers as barriers.

entries.zh: 從鄭至梁二百餘里，車馳人走，不待力而至。
entries.en: From Zheng to Liang spans barely two hundred li—chariots gallop and men sprint, reaching their destination without strain.
entries.literal: From Zheng to Liang is only two hundred li—chariots race and men run, arriving without effort.

entries.zh: 梁南與楚境，西與韓境，北與趙境，東與齊境，卒戍四方，守亭鄣者不下十萬。
entries.en: Liang abuts Chu southward, Han westward, Zhao northward, Qi eastward. Soldiers garrison the frontiers on all sides, with no less than ten thousand men defending the watchtowers and ramparts.
entries.literal: Liang borders Chu to the south, Han to the west, Zhao to the north, Qi to the east. Garrisons man the borders in all directions, with no fewer than ten thousand troops guarding the watchtowers and barriers.

entries.zh: 梁之地勢，固戰場也。
entries.en: Given Liang's strategic location, it is inherently a battleground.
entries.literal: Given Liang's geographical position, it is naturally a battlefield.

entries.zh: 梁南與楚而不與齊，則齊攻其東；
entries.en: Should Liang unite with Chu but not Qi, Qi will assault from the east;
entries.literal: If Liang allies with Chu but not Qi, Qi will attack from the east;

entries.zh: 東與齊而不與趙，則趙攻其北；
entries.en: Should it ally with Qi but not Zhao, Zhao will strike from the north;
entries.literal: If allied with Qi but not Zhao, Zhao will attack from the north;

entries.zh: 不合於韓，則韓攻其西；
entries.en: If not allied with Han, Han will invade from the west;
entries.literal: If not united with Han, Han will attack from the west;

entries.zh: 不親於楚，則楚攻其南：此所謂四分五裂之道也。
entries.en: If Wei is not close to Chu, Chu will attack from the south. This is what they call the path to being split apart.
entries.literal: If Wei is not close to Chu, Chu will attack from the south. This is what is called the path to being split apart.

entries.zh: 為大王計，莫如事秦。
entries.en: In planning for Your Majesty, nothing surpasses serving Qin.
entries.literal: For Your Majesty's sake, nothing is better than serving Qin.

entries.zh: 事秦則楚、韓必不敢動；
entries.en: By serving Qin, Chu, and Han will assuredly not dare stir;
entries.literal: Serving Qin means Chu and Han will certainly not dare move;

entries.zh: 無楚、韓之患，則大王高枕而臥，國必無憂矣。
entries.en: Free from the threats of Chu and Han, Your Majesty can rest easy, and the state will know no anxiety.
entries.literal: No Chu Han calamity, then great wang high pillow lie, state certainly no worry.

entries.zh: 哀王於是乃倍從約而因儀請成於秦。
entries.en: King Ai therefore betrayed the alliance and through Zhang Yi petitioned Qin for peace.
entries.literal: King Ai then abandoned the alliance and through Zhang Yi sought peace with Qin.

entries.zh: 張儀歸，復相秦。
entries.en: Zhang Yi returned home and resumed his premiership in Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi returned and again became prime minister of Qin.

entries.zh: 三歲而魏復背秦為從。
entries.en: Three years passed and Wei once more turned its back on Qin to form alliances.
entries.literal: Three years later, Wei again abandoned Qin for alliances.

entries.zh: 秦攻魏，取曲沃。
entries.en: Qin assaulted Wei and captured Quwo.
entries.literal: Qin attacked Wei and took Quwo.

entries.zh: 明年，魏復事秦。
entries.en: The following year, Wei once more submitted to Qin.
entries.literal: The next year, Wei again served Qin.

entries.zh: 秦欲伐齊，齊楚從親，於是張儀往相楚。
entries.en: Qin desired to campaign against Qi. Since Qi and Chu were confederated, Zhang Yi proceeded to Chu to serve as its premier.
entries.literal: Qin wanted to attack Qi. Qi and Chu were allied, so Zhang Yi went to become prime minister of Chu.

entries.zh: 楚懷王聞張儀來，虛上舍而自館之。
entries.en: King Huai of Chu learned of Zhang Yi's arrival and emptied the finest chambers to accommodate him himself.
entries.literal: King Huai of Chu heard Zhang Yi was coming and prepared the finest guest quarters to house him personally.

entries.zh: 曰：「此僻陋之國，子何以教之？」
entries.en: He said, "This is an out-of-the-way rustic land—what wisdom do you bring to enlighten it?"
entries.literal: He said, 'This is a remote and backward country—what teachings do you bring?'

entries.zh: 儀說楚王曰：「大王誠能聽臣，閉關絕約於齊，臣請獻商於之地六百里，使秦女得為大王箕帚之妾，秦楚娶婦嫁女，長為兄弟之國。
entries.en: Zhang Yi addressed the King of Chu: "If Your Majesty will truly heed my counsel, close your passes and sever your agreements with Qi. I shall present the territory of Shangyu, six hundred li in extent, so that Qin women may serve as Your Majesty's humble attendants. Qin and Chu will exchange brides and become brother states forever.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi persuaded the King of Chu: 'If Your Majesty truly listens to me, close your passes and break your agreements with Qi. I will present the territory of Shangyu, six hundred li in extent, so that Qin women may serve as Your Majesty's humble attendants. Qin and Chu will exchange brides and become brother states forever.

entries.zh: 此北弱齊而西益秦也，計無便此者。」
entries.en: This diminishes Qi northward while enriching Qin westward—no strategy could prove more advantageous."
entries.literal: This weakens Qi to the north while benefiting Qin to the west—no plan could be better.'

entries.zh: 楚王大說而許之。
entries.en: The King of Chu was immensely delighted and consented.
entries.literal: The King of Chu was greatly pleased and agreed.

entries.zh: 群臣皆賀，陳軫獨弔之。
entries.en: All the courtiers offered felicitations, but Chen Zhen alone expressed condolences.
entries.literal: All the ministers congratulated him, but Chen Zhen alone mourned.

entries.zh: 楚王怒曰：「寡人不興師發兵得六百里地，群臣皆賀，子獨弔，何也？」
entries.en: The King of Chu grew furious: "I acquired six hundred li of territory without mobilizing armies or dispatching troops. All my ministers rejoice, yet you alone lament—what is the reason?"
entries.literal: The King of Chu was angry: 'I obtained six hundred li of land without raising troops or sending armies. All ministers congratulate me, yet you alone mourn—why?'

entries.zh: 陳軫對曰：「不然，以臣觀之，商於之地不可得而齊秦合，齊秦合則患必至矣。」
entries.en: Chen Zhen responded: "Not at all. In your minister's view, the territory of Shangyu cannot be obtained, and Qi and Qin will unite. Once Qi and Qin unite, disaster will certainly come."
entries.literal: Chen Zhen replied: 'Not so. In my view, the land of Shangyu cannot be obtained, and Qi and Qin will unite; once Qi and Qin unite, disaster will certainly come.'

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「有說乎？」
entries.en: The King of Chu asked, "Do you have something to say?"
entries.literal: The King of Chu said, 'Do you have an explanation?'

entries.zh: 陳軫對曰：「夫秦之所以重楚者，以其有齊也。
entries.en: Chen Zhen responded: "Qin's esteem for Chu stems from Chu's alliance with Qi.
entries.literal: Chen Zhen replied: 'Qin's reason for valuing Chu is because Chu has Qi as an ally.

entries.zh: 今閉關絕約於齊，則楚孤。
entries.en: Now sealing the passes and severing ties with Qi isolates Chu.
entries.literal: Now closing borders and breaking with Qi leaves Chu isolated.

entries.zh: 秦奚貪夫孤國，而與之商於之地六百里？
entries.en: Why would Qin desire a solitary kingdom and bestow upon it six hundred li of Shangyu territory?
entries.literal: Why would Qin covet an isolated state and give it six hundred li of Shangyu land?

entries.zh: 張儀至秦，必負王，是北絕齊交，西生患於秦也，而兩國之兵必俱至。
entries.en: Zhang Yi will return to Qin and assuredly deceive Your Majesty—this severs alliances with Qi northward and provokes enmity with Qin westward. The armies of both realms will surely advance in concert.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi will return to Qin and certainly betray Your Majesty—this cuts off Qi relations to the north and creates trouble with Qin to the west. The troops of both countries will certainly attack together.

entries.zh: 善為王計者，不若陰合而陽絕於齊，使人隨張儀。
entries.en: A wise strategy for Your Majesty would be to maintain covert concord while overtly rupturing with Qi, dispatching an envoy to accompany Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: A good plan for Your Majesty would be to secretly unite while openly breaking with Qi, sending someone to follow Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 茍與吾地，絕齊未晚也；
entries.en: Should they cede the territory, severing with Qi will not be untimely;
entries.literal: If they give us the land, breaking with Qi is not too late;

entries.zh: 不與吾地，陰合謀計也。」
entries.en: Should they withhold the territory, we preserve the clandestine partnership."
entries.literal: If they don't give us the land, we maintain the secret alliance.'

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「願陳子閉口毋復言，以待寡人得地。」
entries.en: The King of Chu declared, "I would have you seal your lips and cease speaking, awaiting my acquisition of the territory."
entries.literal: The King of Chu said, 'I wish you would shut your mouth and stop speaking, waiting for me to get the land.'

entries.zh: 乃以相印授張儀，厚賂之。
entries.en: He bestowed the premier's seal upon Zhang Yi and lavished gifts upon him.
entries.literal: He gave the prime minister's seal to Zhang Yi and richly bribed him.

entries.zh: 於是遂閉關絕約於齊，使一將軍隨張儀。
entries.en: Chu accordingly sealed its passes and renounced relations with Qi, dispatching a single commander to escort Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: Chu then closed its borders and broke relations with Qi, sending one general to follow Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 張儀至秦，詳失綏墮車，不朝三月。
entries.en: Zhang Yi arrived in Qin, feigning the loss of his reins and tumbling from his chariot, absenting himself from court for three months.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi returned to Qin, pretending to lose his reins and fall from his chariot, not appearing at court for three months.

entries.zh: 楚王聞之，曰：「儀以寡人絕齊未甚邪？」
entries.en: The King of Chu learned of this and exclaimed, "Does Zhang Yi believe my severance from Qi insufficient?"
entries.literal: The King of Chu heard this and said, 'Is Zhang Yi thinking my break with Qi is not complete enough?'

entries.zh: 乃使勇士至宋，借宋之符，北罵齊王。
entries.en: He dispatched valiant warriors to Song, borrowing Song's insignia, to journey north and revile the King of Qi.
entries.literal: He sent brave warriors to Song, borrowing Song's credentials, to go north and curse the King of Qi.

entries.zh: 齊王大怒，折節而下秦。
entries.en: The King of Qi raged furiously and bent his pride to yield to Qin.
entries.literal: The King of Qi was furious and humbled himself to submit to Qin.

entries.zh: 秦齊之交合，張儀乃朝，謂楚使者曰：「臣有奉邑六里，願以獻大王左右。」
entries.en: With Qin and Qi united in alliance, Zhang Yi appeared at court and addressed the Chu envoy: "Your servant possesses a fiefdom of six li—I wish to present it to Your Majesty's retainers."
entries.literal: With Qin and Qi allied, Zhang Yi appeared at court and told the Chu envoy: 'I have a fief of six li— I wish to present it to Your Majesty's attendants.'

entries.zh: 楚使者曰：「臣受令於王，以商於之地六百里，不聞六里。」
entries.en: The Chu envoy replied, "Your servant received the king's command for six hundred li of Shangyu territory, not six li."
entries.literal: The Chu envoy said, 'I received orders from the king for six hundred li of Shangyu land, not six li.'

entries.zh: 還報楚王，楚王大怒，發兵而攻秦。
entries.en: He returned and informed the King of Chu, who erupted in rage and mobilized forces to assault Qin.
entries.literal: He returned and reported to the King of Chu, who was furious and sent troops to attack Qin.

entries.zh: 陳軫曰：「軫可發口言乎？
entries.en: Chen Zhen inquired, "May your servant now open his mouth to speak?
entries.literal: Chen Zhen said, 'May I now speak?

entries.zh: 攻之不如割地反以賂秦，與之并兵而攻齊，是我出地於秦，取償於齊也，王國尚可存。」
entries.en: Assaulting Qin proves inferior to surrendering territory to appease them, combining our armies to strike at Qi—this surrenders land to Qin but exacts recompense from Qi. Your Majesty's realm can yet endure."
entries.literal: Attacking is not as good as ceding land to bribe Qin, uniting troops to attack Qi—this gives land to Qin but takes compensation from Qi. Your Majesty's kingdom can still survive.'

entries.zh: 楚王不聽，卒發兵而使將軍屈丐擊秦。
entries.en: The King of Chu paid no heed and ultimately dispatched forces under General Qu Gai to strike at Qin.
entries.literal: The King of Chu wouldn't listen and sent troops with General Qu Gai to attack Qin.

entries.zh: 秦齊共攻楚，斬首八萬，殺屈丐，遂取丹陽、漢中之地。
entries.en: Qin and Qi jointly assaulted Chu, decapitating eighty thousand, slaying Qu Gai, and seizing the lands of Danyang and Hanzhong.
entries.literal: Qin and Qi together attacked Chu, beheading eighty thousand, killing Qu Gai, and taking Danyang and Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 楚又復益發兵而襲秦，至藍田，大戰，楚大敗，於是楚割兩城以與秦平。
entries.en: Chu once more amassed additional forces to ambush Qin, advancing to Lantian. In a monumental clash, Chu suffered catastrophic defeat. Chu consequently relinquished two cities to reconcile with Qin.
entries.literal: Chu again raised more troops to attack Qin, reaching Lantian. In a great battle, Chu was badly defeated. Chu then ceded two cities to make peace with Qin.

entries.zh: 秦要楚欲得黔中地，欲以武關外易之。
entries.en: Qin coerced Chu into yielding Qianzhong territory, proposing to barter the lands beyond Wuguan.
entries.literal: Qin pressed Chu for Qianzhong land, offering to exchange Wuguan.

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「不願易地，願得張儀而獻黔中地。」
entries.en: The King of Chu declared, "I desire no land exchange—I want Zhang Yi and will surrender Qianzhong territory."
entries.literal: The King of Chu said, 'I don't want to exchange land—I want Zhang Yi and will cede Qianzhong.'

entries.zh: 秦王欲遣之，口弗忍言。
entries.en: The King of Qin desired to dispatch him but could not bring himself to utter the words.
entries.literal: The King of Qin wanted to send him but couldn't bear to say it.

entries.zh: 張儀乃請行。
entries.en: Zhang Yi then requested to proceed.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi volunteered to go.

entries.zh: 惠王曰：「彼楚王怒子之負以商於之地，是且甘心於子。」
entries.en: King Hui cautioned, "The King of Chu is angry that you deceived him over the territory of Shangyu; he will surely vent his anger on you."
entries.literal: King Hui said, 'The King of Chu is angry that you deceived him over the territory of Shangyu; he will surely vent his anger on you.'

entries.zh: 張儀曰：「秦彊楚弱，臣善靳尚，尚得事楚夫人鄭袖，袖所言皆從。
entries.en: Zhang Yi replied, "Qin is mighty while Chu is feeble. Your servant enjoys friendship with Jin Shang, who attends Lady Zheng Xiu of Chu. Whatever she commands is obeyed.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said, 'Qin is strong and Chu weak. I am close to Jin Shang, who serves Lady Zheng Xiu. Whatever she says is followed.

entries.zh: 且臣奉王之節使楚，楚何敢加誅。
entries.en: Your servant bears Your Majesty's insignia on mission to Chu. How would Chu dare punish me?
entries.literal: Moreover, I carry Your Majesty's credentials to Chu—how dare Chu execute me.

entries.zh: 假令誅臣而為秦得黔中之地，臣之上願。」
entries.en: Even should they put me to death and thereby secure Qianzhong for Qin, that would fulfill my supreme desire."
entries.literal: Even if they execute me and Qin gets Qianzhong, that would fulfill my greatest wish.'

entries.zh: 遂使楚。
entries.en: He proceeded to Chu.
entries.literal: He went to Chu.

entries.zh: 楚懷王至則囚張儀，將殺之。
entries.en: The King of Chu imprisoned Zhang Yi upon his arrival and prepared to execute him.
entries.literal: The King of Chu imprisoned Zhang Yi and prepared to kill him.

entries.zh: 靳尚謂鄭袖曰：「子亦知子之賤於王乎？」
entries.en: Jin Shang said to Zheng Xiu: "Are you aware of your lowly status in the king's eyes?"
entries.literal: Jin Shang said to Zheng Xiu: 'Do you know how lowly you are to the king?'

entries.zh: 鄭袖曰：「何也？」
entries.en: Zheng Xiu asked, "How so?"
entries.literal: Zheng Xiu said, 'Why?'

entries.zh: 靳尚曰：「秦王甚愛張儀而不欲出之，今將以上庸之地六縣賂楚，美人聘楚，以宮中善歌謳者為媵。
entries.en: Jin Shang said: "The King of Qin greatly values Zhang Yi and does not want to surrender him. Now he plans to offer six counties of Shangyong territory as a bribe to Chu and send beautiful women as brides, accompanied by palace singers as attendants.
entries.literal: Jin Shang said: 'The King of Qin greatly values Zhang Yi and does not want to send him away. Now he plans to offer six counties of Shangyong territory as a bribe to Chu and send beautiful women as brides, accompanied by palace singers as attendants.

entries.zh: 楚王重地尊秦，秦女必貴而夫人斥矣。
entries.en: The King of Chu prizes the territory and reveres Qin—Qin maidens will surely be exalted while you, my lady, will be discarded.
entries.literal: The King of Chu values the land and respects Qin—Qin women will certainly be honored while you, madam, will be cast aside.

entries.zh: 不若為言而出之。」
entries.en: Better to intercede on his behalf and secure his release."
entries.literal: Better to speak on his behalf to save him.'

entries.zh: 於是鄭袖日夜言懷王曰：「人臣各為其主用。
entries.en: Zheng Xiu then spoke to King Huai day and night: "Ministers each serve their own lord.
entries.literal: Zheng Xiu then spoke to King Huai day and night: 'Ministers each serve their own lord.

entries.zh: 今地未入秦，秦使張儀來，至重王。
entries.en: The territory has not yet passed to Qin, yet Qin dispatches Zhang Yi, demonstrating utmost reverence for the king.
entries.literal: Now the land has not yet gone to Qin, yet Qin sends Zhang Yi, showing great respect for the king.

entries.zh: 王未有禮而殺張儀，秦必大怒攻楚。
entries.en: The king shows no graciousness yet seeks to execute Zhang Yi—Qin will surely rage and assault Chu.
entries.literal: The king has shown no courtesy but wants to kill Zhang Yi—Qin will certainly be furious and attack Chu.

entries.zh: 妾請子母俱遷江南，毋為秦所魚肉也。」
entries.en: I implore you and my son to relocate south of the Yangtze, lest we become Qin's fish and flesh."
entries.literal: I beg you and my son to move to south of the Yangtze, lest we become Qin's fish and meat.'

entries.zh: 懷王後悔，赦張儀，厚禮之如故。
entries.en: King Huai came to regret his actions, pardoned Zhang Yi, and bestowed upon him the same lavish treatment as before.
entries.literal: King Huai regretted it, pardoned Zhang Yi, and treated him with the same generous hospitality.

entries.zh: 張儀既出，未去，聞蘇秦死，乃說楚王曰：「秦地半天下，兵敵四國，被險帶河，四塞以為固。
entries.en: Zhang Yi had left but had not yet gone far when he learned of Su Qin's death. He then addressed the King of Chu: "Qin controls half the world, with troops able to rival four states, protected by dangerous terrain and the Yellow River, and secured by four natural barriers.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi had left but had not yet gone far when he heard Su Qin had died. He then persuaded the King of Chu: 'Qin controls half the world, with troops able to rival four states, protected by dangerous terrain and the Yellow River, and secured by four natural barriers.

entries.zh: 虎賁之士百餘萬，車千乘，騎萬匹，積粟如丘山。
entries.en: Boasting over a million fierce warriors, a thousand chariots, ten thousand cavalry, with grain stockpiled like mountain ranges.
entries.literal: With fierce warriors over a million, a thousand chariots, ten thousand cavalry, grain piled like mountains.

entries.zh: 法令既明，士卒安難樂死，主明以嚴，將智以武，雖無出甲，席卷常山之險，必折天下之脊，天下有後服者先亡。
entries.en: Laws are lucid, soldiers embrace peril and welcome death with joy. The sovereign is enlightened yet stern, commanders wise and valiant. Even without deploying armor, Qin can sweep away the perils of Mount Chang and snap the world's spine. Those who yield belatedly shall perish first.
entries.literal: Laws are clear, soldiers face hardship and death with joy. The ruler is enlightened and strict, generals intelligent and brave. Even without mobilizing troops, Qin can roll up the dangers of Mount Chang and break the world's backbone. Those who submit late will perish first.

entries.zh: 且夫為從者，無以異於驅群羊而攻猛虎，虎之與羊不格明矣。
entries.en: Forming confederations is no different from herding sheep to attack a ferocious tiger. It is obvious that sheep cannot contend with a tiger.
entries.literal: Moreover, forming alliances is no different from driving a flock of sheep to attack a fierce tiger—the tiger and sheep cannot fight, that's clear.

entries.zh: 今王不與猛虎而與群羊，臣竊以為大王之計過也。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty allies not with the ferocious tiger but with the herd of sheep—I humbly deem Your Majesty's strategy misguided.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty does not ally with the fierce tiger but with the flock of sheep—I secretly think Your Majesty's plan is wrong.

entries.zh: 今秦與楚接境壤界，固形親之國也。
entries.en: Now Qin and Chu share borders and territories—they are naturally states that should be close.
entries.literal: Using one deceitful Su Qin to try to manage the world and unite the feudal lords—the impossibility of success is clear.

entries.zh: 大王誠能聽臣，臣請使秦太子入質於楚，楚太子入質於秦，請以秦女為大王箕帚之妾，效萬室之都以為湯沐之邑，長為昆弟之國，終身無相攻伐。
entries.en: If Your Majesty will truly heed my counsel, I shall arrange for the Qin crown prince to serve as hostage in Chu, and the Chu crown prince to serve as hostage in Qin. I shall present Qin maidens as Your Majesty's humble attendants, and cede a city of ten thousand households as Your bathing fief. Let us be fraternal realms forever, never assaulting one another for all our lives.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty truly listens to me, I will have the Qin crown prince become hostage in Chu, the Chu crown prince become hostage in Qin. I will make Qin women become Your Majesty's broom-wielding concubines, present a city of ten thousand households as a bathing town. Let us be brother states forever, never attacking each other.

entries.zh: 臣以為計無便於此者。」
entries.en: I deem no strategy more beneficial than this."
entries.literal: I consider no plan more advantageous than this.'

entries.zh: 於是楚王已得張儀而重出黔中地與秦，欲許之。
entries.en: Thus, the King of Chu, having already secured Zhang Yi, was willing to part with Qianzhong territory to Qin and desired to agree to the terms.
entries.literal: Then Chu Wang already obtain Zhang Yi heavy send Qian Zhong land to Qin, wished permit him.

entries.zh: 屈原曰：「前大王見欺於張儀，張儀至，臣以為大王烹之；
entries.en: Qu Yuan said: "The former king was deceived by Zhang Yi. Now that Zhang Yi has come, I believe Your Majesty should boil him alive.
entries.literal: Qu Yuan said: "Former great wang see cheat Zhang Yi, Zhang Yi arrive, subject think great wang boil him;

entries.zh: 今縱弗忍殺之，又聽其邪說，不可。」
entries.en: Now if you cannot bear to kill him, at least do not listen to his crooked words—it would be unacceptable."
entries.literal: Now release not endure kill him, moreover listen his crooked words, unacceptable."

entries.zh: 懷王曰：「許儀而得黔中，美利也。
entries.en: King Huai said, "If agreeing to Zhang Yi lets us obtain Qianzhong, that is an excellent profit.
entries.literal: King Huai said: "To agree to Zhang Yi and obtain Qianzhong is a fine profit.

entries.zh: 後而倍之，不可。」
entries.en: To betray him afterward would be unacceptable."
entries.literal: After double it, unacceptable."

entries.zh: 故卒許張儀，與秦親。
entries.en: Therefore, they ultimately agreed to Zhang Yi's terms and formed intimate relations with Qin.
entries.literal: Therefore, they finally agreed to Zhang Yi's terms and formed close ties with Qin.

entries.zh: 韓王聽儀計。
entries.en: The King of Han followed Zhang Yi's plan.
entries.literal: Han Wang listen Yi plan.

entries.zh: 張儀歸報，秦惠王封儀五邑，號曰武信君。
entries.en: Zhang Yi returned and reported. King Hui of Qin enfeoffed him with five cities and styled him Lord Wuxin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi return report, Qin Hui Wang enfeoff Yi five cities, number Wu Xin Jun.

entries.zh: 使張儀東說齊湣王曰：「天下彊國無過齊者，大臣父兄殷眾富樂。
entries.en: He sent Zhang Yi east to persuade King Min of Qi: "Among the world's strong states, none surpasses Qi. Your ministers, fathers, and elder brothers are numerous, wealthy, and content.
entries.literal: Make Zhang Yi east advise Qi Min Wang: "World strong states none exceed Qi, ministers fathers elder brothers numerous rich joyful.

entries.zh: 然而為大王計者，皆為一時之說，不顧百世之利。
entries.en: Yet those who plan for Your Majesty all speak of momentary gains, disregarding benefits for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: Yet for great wang planning, all momentary speech, not consider hundred generations profit.

entries.zh: 從人說大王者，必曰『齊西有彊趙，南有韓與梁。
entries.en: Confederation advocates persuading Your Majesty will certainly say: Qi has mighty Zhao to the west, Han and Wei to the south.
entries.literal: Alliance advocates persuading Your Majesty will certainly say: "Qi has strong Zhao to the west, Han and Wei to the south.

entries.zh: 齊，負海之國也，地廣民眾，兵彊士勇，雖有百秦，將無柰齊何』。
entries.en: Qi is a coastal state with vast territory, teeming populace, powerful armies, and valiant soldiers. Even with a hundred Qins, what could they do against Qi?
entries.literal: Qi is a maritime state with broad territory, numerous people, strong troops, and brave soldiers. Even with a hundred Qins, what could they do to Qi?

entries.zh: 大王賢其說而不計其實。
