entries.en: Your Majesty admires their rhetoric but does not calculate the reality.
entries.literal: Great wang worthy their speech not calculate its substance.

entries.zh: 夫從人朋黨比周，莫不以從為可。
entries.en: Confederation advocates form cliques and collude, none failing to deem alliance acceptable.
entries.literal: Alliance people faction close, none not consider alliance acceptable.

entries.zh: 臣聞之，齊與魯三戰而魯三勝，國以危亡隨其後，雖有戰勝之名，而有亡國之實。
entries.en: I have heard it said that Qi fought Lu three times and Lu prevailed three times, yet danger and extinction followed for the state. Though bearing the name of victory, it possessed the reality of a perished state.
entries.literal: I have heard that Qi fought Lu three times and Lu won three times, yet the state faced danger and extinction afterward. Though having the name of victory, it had the reality of a perished state.

entries.zh: 是何也？
entries.en: Why is this?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 齊大而魯小也。
entries.en: Qi is great while Lu is small.
entries.literal: Qi is large and Lu is small.

entries.zh: 今秦之與齊也，猶齊之與魯也。
entries.en: Now Qin's relation to Qi is like Qi's relation to Lu.
entries.literal: Now Qin compared to Qi is like Qi compared to Lu.

entries.zh: 秦趙戰於河漳之上，再戰而趙再勝秦；
entries.en: Qin and Zhao clashed along the He River and Zhang River. In two engagements Zhao defeated Qin twice;
entries.literal: Qin and Zhao fought at the He and Zhang rivers—two battles and Zhao won Qin twice;

entries.zh: 戰於番吾之下，再戰又勝秦。
entries.en: battled below Fanwu—in two more engagements again prevailed against Qin.
entries.literal: fought at Fanwu below—two battles and again won Qin.

entries.zh: 四戰之後，趙之亡卒數十萬，邯鄲僅存，雖有戰勝之名而國已破矣。
entries.en: After four campaigns, Zhao's fallen soldiers numbered several hundred thousand. Handan barely endured. Though bearing victory's reputation, the kingdom was already shattered.
entries.literal: After four battles, Zhao's perished troops numbered several hundred thousand. Handan barely survived. Though having victory's name, the state was already broken.

entries.zh: 是何也？
entries.en: How is this?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 秦彊而趙弱。
entries.en: Qin is mighty while Zhao is feeble.
entries.literal: Qin is strong and Zhao is weak.

entries.zh: 張儀去楚，因遂之韓，說韓王曰：「韓地險惡山居，五穀所生，非菽而麥，民之食大抵［飯］菽［飯］藿羹。
entries.en: Zhang Yi left Chu and proceeded to Han, where he addressed the King of Han: "Han territory is perilous and harsh, suited for mountain dwelling. Of the five grains, it produces mainly beans and wheat; the people's food consists mostly of beans and bean-leaf soup.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi left Chu and proceeded to Han, where he advised the King of Han: "Han territory is perilous and harsh, suited for mountain dwelling. Of the five grains, it produces mainly beans and wheat; the people's food consists mostly of beans and bean-leaf soup.

entries.zh: 一歲不收，民不饜糟糠。
entries.en: If a single year brings no harvest, the people cannot even eat their fill of chaff and bran.
entries.literal: If one year brings no harvest, the people cannot even eat their fill of chaff and bran.

entries.zh: 地不過九百里，無二歲之食。
entries.en: Its territory does not exceed nine hundred li, with no provisions for two years.
entries.literal: Land not exceed nine hundred li, no two years food.

entries.zh: 料大王之卒，悉之不過三十萬，而廝徒負養在其中矣。
entries.en: Estimating Your Majesty's troops, all told they do not exceed three hundred thousand, yet servants and baggage carriers are counted among them.
entries.literal: Estimate great wang troops, all not exceed thirty thousand, yet servants burden support in midst.

entries.zh: 除守徼亭鄣塞，見卒不過二十萬而已矣。
entries.en: Excluding those guarding border towers and barriers, your actual fighting troops do not exceed two hundred thousand at most.
entries.literal: Except guard border towers barriers, see troops not exceed twenty thousand only.

entries.zh: 秦帶甲百餘萬，車千乘，騎萬匹，虎賁之士跿跔科頭貫頤奮戟者，至不可勝計。
entries.en: Qin fields over a million armored warriors, a thousand chariots, ten thousand cavalry mounts, and tiger-brave soldiers who squat and kneel, bareheaded, piercing chins and brandishing halberds, too many to count.
entries.literal: Qin armored hundred thousand, chariots thousand, cavalry ten thousand horses, tiger brave soldiers bend kneel bare head pierce chin wave halberd, to cannot count.

entries.zh: 秦馬之良，戎兵之眾，探前趹後蹄閒三尋騰者，不可勝數。
entries.en: Qin's horses are superb, its barbarian troops numerous; those that probe forward and kick backward with hooves spanning three zhang in their leaps are too many to count.
entries.literal: Qin horses excellent, Rong troops multitude, probe front kick rear hoof between three zhang leap, cannot count.

entries.zh: 山東之士被甲蒙胄以會戰，秦人捐甲徒裼以趨敵，左挈人頭，右挾生虜。
entries.en: Eastern warriors don armor and helmets to meet battle, while Qin soldiers cast off their armor and charge the enemy bare-chested, clutching severed heads in their left hands and dragging living captives with their right.
entries.literal: Shandong scholars don armor cover helmets meet battle, Qin people cast armor bare advance enemy, left grasp people heads, right hold living captives.

entries.zh: 夫秦卒與山東之卒，猶孟賁之與怯夫；
entries.en: Qin's soldiers compared to eastern troops are like Meng Ben to a coward;
entries.literal: Qin troops with Shandong troops, like Meng Ben with coward;

entries.zh: 以重力相壓，猶烏獲之與嬰兒。
entries.en: pressing with overwhelming force, like Wu Huo against an infant.
entries.literal: With heavy strength press, like Wu Huo with infant.

entries.zh: 夫戰孟賁、烏獲之士以攻不服之弱國，無異垂千鈞之重於鳥卵之上，必無幸矣。
entries.en: To deploy soldiers like Meng Ben and Wu Huo against unsubmissive weak states is like suspending a thousand-jun weight above a bird's egg. Surely there will be no survivors.
entries.literal: Battle Meng Ben Wu Huo soldiers attack not submit weak states, no different hang thousand jun weight on bird egg above, certainly no lucky.

entries.zh: 故為大王計，莫如為秦。
entries.en: Therefore, in planning for Your Majesty, nothing surpasses serving Qin.
entries.literal: Therefore, for great wang planning, none better serve Qin.

entries.zh: 秦之所欲莫如弱楚，而能弱楚者如韓。
entries.en: Qin's greatest desire is to weaken Chu, and none can weaken Chu like Han.
entries.literal: Qin desire weaken none like Chu, yet can weaken Chu like Han.

entries.zh: 非以韓能彊於楚也，其地勢然也。
entries.en: Not because Han is stronger than Chu, but because the terrain makes it so.
entries.literal: Not because Han can strong Chu, its land position so.

entries.zh: 今王西面而事秦以攻楚，秦王必喜。
entries.en: If Your Majesty now faces west to serve Qin and attack Chu, the King of Qin will certainly be pleased.
entries.literal: Now wang west face serve Qin attack Chu, Qin Wang certainly happy.

entries.zh: 夫攻楚以利其地，轉禍而說秦，計無便於此者。」
entries.en: If Han attacks Chu, it can profit from Chu territory, turn disaster aside, and please Qin. No plan is more advantageous than this."
entries.literal: By attacking Chu, Han will profit from its territory, turn calamity around, and please Qin; no plan is more advantageous than this."

entries.zh: 今秦楚嫁女娶婦，為昆弟之國。
entries.en: Now Qin and Chu wed their daughters and take brides, becoming fraternal realms.
entries.literal: Now Qin and Chu exchange women as brides, becoming brother states.

entries.zh: 韓獻宜陽；
entries.en: Han tenders Yiyang;
entries.literal: Han offers Yiyang;

entries.zh: 梁效河外；
entries.en: Wei cedes Hedong;
entries.literal: Wei presents Hedong;

entries.zh: 趙入朝澠池，割河閒以事秦。
entries.en: Zhao attends court at Mianchi, surrenders Hejian to submit to Qin.
entries.literal: Zhao enters court at Mianchi, cedes Hejian to serve Qin.

entries.zh: 大王不事秦，秦驅韓梁攻齊之南地，悉趙兵渡清河，指博關，臨菑、即墨非王之有也。
entries.en: Should Your Majesty refuse to serve Qin, Qin will spur Han and Wei to assault Qi's southern territories, dispatch all Zhao forces to ford the Qing River, aim for Bo Pass—Linzi and Jimo will cease to be the king's possessions.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will drive Han and Wei to attack Qi's southern lands, send all Zhao troops to cross Qing River, point to Bo Pass—Linzi and Jimou will not belong to the king.

entries.zh: 國一日見攻，雖欲事秦，不可得也。
entries.en: The kingdom attacked for a single day—even desiring to serve Qin afterward will prove unattainable.
entries.literal: The state attacked for one day, even wishing to serve Qin later will be impossible.

entries.zh: 是故願大王孰計之也。」
entries.en: Therefore, I beseech Your Majesty to deliberate upon this thoroughly."
entries.literal: Therefore, I wish Your Majesty to carefully consider.'

entries.zh: 齊王曰：「齊僻陋，隱居東海之上，未嘗聞社稷之長利也。」
entries.en: The King of Qi said: "Qi is remote and backward, secluded on the eastern sea. I have never heard of the state's long-term benefit."
entries.literal: The King of Qi said: 'Qi is remote and backward, secluded on the eastern sea. I have never heard of the state's long-term benefit.'

entries.zh: 乃許張儀。
entries.en: He consented to Zhang Yi's terms.
entries.literal: He agreed to Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 張儀去，西說趙王曰：「敝邑秦王使使臣效愚計於大王。
entries.en: Zhang Yi departed westward to address the King of Zhao: "My humble state's King of Qin dispatched me to present foolish stratagems to Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi left, going west to persuade the King of Zhao: 'My humble state's King of Qin sent me to present foolish plans to Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 大王收率天下以賓秦，秦兵不敢出函谷關十五年。
entries.en: Your Majesty rallied the realm to subdue Qin—Qin's armies dared not emerge from Hangu Pass for fifteen years.
entries.literal: Your Majesty gathering the world to make Qin submit—Qin troops dared not emerge from Hangu Pass for fifteen years.

entries.zh: 大王之威行於山東，敝邑恐懼懾伏，繕甲厲兵，飾車騎，習馳射，力田積粟，守四封之內，愁居懾處，不敢動搖，唯大王有意督過之也。
entries.en: Your Majesty's awe extended throughout Shandong. My humble state feared and cowered, mended armor, honed weapons, equipped chariots and cavalry, trained in riding and archery, toiled in the fields and stockpiled grain, defended within our four frontiers, dwelling anxiously in terror, not daring to budge—merely awaiting Your Majesty's inclination to chastise our transgressions.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's might spread through Shandong. My humble state feared and trembled, repaired armor, sharpened weapons, prepared chariots and cavalry, practiced riding and shooting, worked fields and stored grain, guarded within the four borders, anxiously dwelling in fear, not daring to stir—only awaiting Your Majesty's intention to chastise.

entries.zh: 趙王曰：「先王之時，奉陽君專權擅勢，蔽欺先王，獨擅綰事，寡人居屬師傅，不與國謀計。
entries.en: The King of Zhao declared: "During my father's reign, Lord Fengyang monopolized authority and influence, deceived my father, solely controlled affairs. I resided as crown prince under tutors, not participating in state deliberations.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao said: 'In my father's time, Lord Yangyang monopolized power and influence, deceived my father, alone controlled affairs. I resided as heir apparent under tutors, not participating in state planning.

entries.zh: 先王棄群臣，寡人年幼，奉祀之日新，心固竊疑焉，以為一從不事秦，非國之長利也。
entries.en: When my father abandoned his ministers in death, I was young and newly responsible for the ancestral sacrifices. In my heart I secretly doubted, believing that joining the alliance and not serving Qin was not the state's long-term interest.
entries.literal: When my father abandoned his ministers in death, I was young and newly responsible for the ancestral sacrifices. In my heart I secretly doubted, believing that joining the alliance and not serving Qin was not the state's long-term benefit.

entries.zh: 乃且願變心易慮，割地謝前過以事秦。
entries.en: I was about to transform my heart and reconsider, cede territory to atone for past transgressions and submit to Qin.
entries.literal: I was about to change heart and thought, cede land to apologize for past errors and serve Qin.

entries.zh: 方將約車趨行，適聞使者之明詔。」
entries.en: I was just preparing chariots to hasten there when I fortunately received the envoy's enlightened proclamation."
entries.literal: Just preparing chariots to hurry there, I fortunately heard the envoy's enlightened decree.'

entries.zh: 趙王許張儀，張儀乃去。
entries.en: The King of Zhao consented to Zhang Yi's terms. Zhang Yi then departed.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao agreed to Zhang Yi. Zhang Yi then left.

entries.zh: 北之燕，說燕昭王曰：「大王之所親莫如趙。
entries.en: He journeyed north to Yan, addressing King Zhao of Yan: "None whom Your Majesty holds dear surpasses Zhao.
entries.literal: He went north to Yan, persuading King Zhao of Yan: 'None whom Your Majesty esteems exceed Zhao.

entries.zh: 昔趙襄子嘗以其姊為代王妻，欲并代，約與代王遇於句注之塞。
entries.en: In former times, Zhao Xiangzi once gave his sister in marriage to the King of Dai, desiring to annex Dai, arranging to meet the King of Dai at the Guju pass.
entries.literal: Formerly Zhao Xiangzi once made his sister wife to the King of Dai, wishing to annex Dai, agreeing to meet the King of Dai at Guju pass.

entries.zh: 乃令工人作為金斗，長其尾，令可以擊人。
entries.en: He commanded artisans to fashion a gold ladle, elongating its handle so it could be used to strike people.
entries.literal: He ordered craftsmen make a gold ladle, lengthening its handle so it could strike people.

entries.zh: 與代王飲，陰告廚人曰：『即酒酣樂，進熱啜，反鬬以擊之。』
entries.en: Feasting with the King of Dai, he secretly instructed the cook: "When wine flows freely and merriment peaks, present hot broth, then turn the ladle to strike him."
entries.literal: Drinking with the King of Dai, secretly told the cook: "When wine is abundant and joy high, advance hot soup, turn the ladle to strike him."

entries.zh: 於是酒酣樂，進熱啜，廚人進斟，因反鬬以擊代王，殺之，王腦涂地。
entries.en: Thus, when wine flowed copiously and revelry peaked, hot soup was presented. The cook advanced to pour, then turned the ladle to strike the King of Dai, killing him, his brains splattering the earth.
entries.literal: Then wine abundant joy high, advance hot soup, cook advances pours, turns ladle strikes King of Dai, kills him, brain splatters ground.

entries.zh: 其姊聞之，因摩笄以自刺，故至今有摩笄之山。
entries.en: His sister heard of this and ground her hairpin to stab herself to death. Therefore, to this day there is Mount Moyaji.
entries.literal: His sister hears, grinds hairpin to stab herself, therefore until now has Moya mountain.

entries.zh: 代王之亡，天下莫不聞。
entries.en: The King of Dai's demise is known throughout the world.
entries.literal: Dai king's extinction, world none not hear.

entries.zh: 燕王曰：「寡人蠻夷僻處，雖大男子裁如嬰兒，言不足以采正計。
entries.en: The King of Yan declared: "I am a barbarian dwelling in remote isolation—though a grown man, my wisdom is but that of an infant, my words insufficient to adopt sound strategy.
entries.literal: Yan wang says: 'My person barbarian remote place, though big man only like infant, words not sufficient to adopt correct plan.

entries.zh: 今上客幸教之，請西面而事秦，獻恒山之尾五城。」
entries.en: Now this honored guest has fortunately instructed me—I beg to face west and serve Qin, offering five cities at the foot of Mount Hengshan."
entries.literal: Now upper guest fortunately teaches, please west faces serves Qin, offers Hengshan tail five cities.'

entries.zh: 燕王聽儀。
entries.en: The King of Yan heeded Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: Yan wang listens Yi.

entries.zh: 儀歸報，未至咸陽而秦惠王卒，武王立。
entries.en: Zhang Yi returned and reported. Before reaching Xianyang, King Hui of Qin died and King Wu ascended the throne.
entries.literal: Yi returns reports, not arrives Xian Yang yet Qin Hui Wang dies, Wu Wang stands.

entries.zh: 武王自為太子時不說張儀，及即位，群臣多讒張儀曰：「無信，左右賣國以取容。
entries.en: King Wu, from his days as crown prince, disliked Zhang Yi. Upon ascending the throne, his ministers frequently slandered Zhang Yi, saying: "He has no trustworthiness, betrays the state on all sides to curry favor.
entries.literal: Wu Wang from is crown prince time not likes Zhang Yi, reaches ascends throne, ministers many slander Zhang Yi: 'No trust, left right sells state takes favor.

entries.zh: 秦必復用之，恐為天下笑。」
entries.en: If Qin employs him again, I fear it will be laughed at by the world."
entries.literal: If Qin certainly employs him again, I fear it will be laughed at by the world.'

entries.zh: 諸侯聞張儀有卻武王，皆畔衡，復合從。
entries.en: The feudal lords, learning that Zhang Yi had offended King Wu, all betrayed the alliance and reformed their confederation.
entries.literal: Feudal lords hear Zhang Yi has rejects Wu Wang, all betrays alliance, again unites vertical.

entries.zh: 今秦發三將軍：其一軍塞午道，告齊使興師渡清河，軍於邯鄲之東；
entries.en: Now Qin dispatches three generals: one army blocks Wudao, instructs the Qi envoy to mobilize troops and ford the Qing River, encamp east of Handan;
entries.literal: Now Qin sends three generals: one army blocks Wudao, tells Qi envoy to raise troops cross Qing River, camp east of Handan;

entries.en: one army encamps at Chenggao, drives Han and Wei forces beyond the Yellow River;
entries.literal: one army camps at Chenggao, drives Han and Wei troops beyond the Yellow River;

entries.zh: 一軍軍於澠池。
entries.en: one army encamps at Mianchi.
entries.literal: one army camps at Mianchi.

entries.zh: 約四國為一以攻趙，趙（服）［破］，必四分其地。
entries.en: They will unite the four states to attack Zhao. Once Zhao is defeated, they will certainly divide its territory into four parts.
entries.literal: They will join four states as one to attack Zhao. Once Zhao is defeated, they will certainly divide its territory into four parts.

entries.zh: 是故不敢匿意隱情，先以聞於左右。
entries.en: Therefore, not presuming to conceal our intentions or hide the situation, we first inform Your Majesty's retainers.
entries.literal: Therefore, not daring to hide intention conceal situation, first inform Your Majesty's attendants.

entries.zh: 臣竊為大王計，莫如與秦王遇於澠池，面相見而口相結，請案兵無攻。
entries.en: I humbly strategize for Your Majesty—nothing surpasses meeting the King of Qin at Mianchi, face-to-face and pledging mutual oaths, requesting that troops stand down without assault.
entries.literal: I secretly plan for Your Majesty, nothing better than meeting the Qin king at Mianchi, face to face and mouth to mouth, requesting to halt troops without attack.

entries.zh: 願大王之定計。」
entries.en: I beseech Your Majesty to settle upon a strategy."
entries.literal: I wish Your Majesty to decide.'

entries.zh: 且今時趙之於秦猶郡縣也，不敢妄舉師以攻伐。
entries.en: At present, Zhao stands toward Qin like a commandery or county, not daring to rashly mobilize troops for conquest.
entries.literal: Moreover, now Zhao to Qin like jun county, not dares rashly raises troops attacks invades.

entries.zh: 今王事秦，秦王必喜，趙不敢妄動，是西有彊秦之援，而南無齊趙之患，是故願大王孰計之。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty serves Qin, the King of Qin will certainly rejoice, and Zhao will not dare to move rashly. This means that to the west you have mighty Qin as support, and to the south you will have no trouble from Qi or Zhao. Therefore, I beseech Your Majesty to deliberate carefully."
entries.literal: Now wang serves Qin, Qin wang certainly happy, Zhao not dares rashly moves, is west has strong Qin aid, south no Qi Zhao trouble, is therefore wishes Your Majesty carefully plans.'

entries.literal: Qin Wu Wang first year, ministers day night dislikes Zhang Yi not stops, Qi rebuke moreover arrives.

entries.en: Zhang Yi, fearing execution, then addressed King Wu of Qin: "I have a foolish stratagem—I wish to present it."
entries.literal: Zhang Yi fears executes, then because tells Qin Wu Wang: 'Yi has foolish plan, wishes presents.'

entries.literal: Wang says: 'How?'

entries.en: He replied: "In planning for Qin's altars of soil and grain, when there is great upheaval in the east, then Your Majesty can carve out and gain much territory.

entries.en: The King of Qin deemed this correct, then prepared thirty chariots and sent Zhang Yi to Liang.

entries.en: Qi indeed mobilized troops and attacked Liang.

entries.en: King Ai of Liang grew fearful.

entries.en: Zhang Yi declared: "Your Majesty need not worry—I shall arrange to halt the Qi troops."
entries.literal: Zhang Yi says: 'Wang not worries, please makes stops Qi troops.'

entries.literal: Then makes his house person Feng Xi to Chu, borrows makes to Qi, tells Qi wang: 'Wang very hates Zhang Yi;

entries.en: Nevertheless, it also shows how deeply Your Majesty trusts Zhang Yi with Qin!"
entries.literal: Although, also thick wang trusts Yi at Qin.'

entries.en: The King of Qi declared: "I detest Zhang Yi—wherever he is, I will certainly mobilize troops to attack him. Why would I trust Zhang Yi?"
entries.literal: Qi wang says: 'My person hates Yi, Yi where, certainly raises troops attacks it, why trusts Yi?'

entries.en: He replied: "This is precisely Your Majesty's trust in Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: Answers: 'Is wang trusts Yi.

entries.en: When Zhang Yi departed, he firmly agreed with the King of Qin: 'In planning for Your Majesty, when there is great upheaval in the east, then Your Majesty can carve out and gain much territory.
entries.literal: Yi emerges, solid with Qin wang agrees: 'As wang plans, east has big change, then wang can many divides obtains land.

entries.literal: Now Qi wang very hates Yi, Yi where, certainly raises troops attacks it.

entries.en: Therefore, I wish to beg permission for my unworthy self to go to Liang—Qi will certainly mobilize troops and attack it.
entries.literal: Therefore, Yi wishes begs his not worthy body to Liang, Qi certainly raises troops attacks Liang.

entries.en: With Qi and Liang's troops locked in battle beneath the city walls and unable to disengage, Your Majesty can exploit the opportunity to attack Han, enter the Sanchuan region, emerge troops from Hangu Pass without battle, confront Zhou directly—the sacrificial vessels will certainly be surrendered.

entries.en: Holding the Son of Heaven hostage and controlling the maps and registers—this is the enterprise of a true king.'

entries.en: The King of Qin deemed this correct, therefore prepared thirty chariots and sent him to Liang.
entries.literal: Qin wang considers correct, therefore prepares leather chariots thirty rides enters to Liang.

entries.en: Now Zhang Yi has entered Liang—if Your Majesty indeed attacks it, this exhausts the state within while attacking allied nations without, broadens neighboring enemies while facing peril within, and demonstrates trust in Zhang Yi to the King of Qin.
entries.literal: Now Yi enters Liang, wang indeed attacks it, is wang inner exhausts state outer attacks ally country, broad neighbor enemy with inner self faces, believes Yi at Qin wang.

entries.zh: 此臣之所謂『託儀』也。」
entries.en: This is what your minister means by 'trusting Zhang Yi.'"
entries.literal: This minister so called trusts Yi.'"

entries.zh: 齊王曰：「善。」
entries.en: The King of Qi declared: "Excellent."
entries.literal: Qi wang says: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 乃使解兵。
entries.en: He then ordered the troops to stand down.
entries.literal: Then makes relieves troops.

entries.zh: 張儀相魏一歲，卒於魏也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi served as prime minister of Wei for one year and died there.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi chancellor Wei one year, dies at Wei.

entries.zh: 陳軫者，游說之士。
entries.en: Chen Zhen was a master of diplomatic persuasion.
entries.literal: Chen Zhen, travel speaks scholar.

entries.zh: 與張儀俱事秦惠王，皆貴重，爭寵。
entries.en: Together with Zhang Yi, he served King Hui of Qin. Both were honored and influential, vying for the king's favor.
entries.literal: With Zhang Yi together serves Qin Hui Wang, all noble heavy, contends favor.

entries.zh: 張儀惡陳軫於秦王曰：「軫重幣輕使秦楚之閒，將為國交也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi slandered Chen Zhen to the King of Qin: "Zhen carries rich gifts and shuttles as an envoy between Qin and Chu, intending to broker alliances for other states.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi slandered Chen Zhen to the King of Qin: 'Zhen carries rich gifts and shuttles as an envoy between Qin and Chu, intending to broker alliances for other states.

entries.zh: 今楚不加善於秦而善軫者，軫自為厚而為王薄也。
entries.en: Now Chu shows no greater favor toward Qin yet favors Zhen—this means Zhen enriches himself while impoverishing Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Now Chu not adds good at Qin yet goods Zhen, Zhen self makes thick for wang thin.

entries.zh: 且軫欲去秦而之楚，王胡不聽乎？」
entries.en: Zhen wishes to leave Qin and go to Chu. Why doesn't Your Majesty permit it?"
entries.literal: Moreover, Zhen wishes departs Qin goes Chu, wang why not listens?'

entries.zh: 王謂陳軫曰：「吾聞子欲去秦之楚，有之乎？」
entries.en: The king addressed Chen Zhen: "I have heard that you wish to depart Qin and go to Chu—is this true?"
entries.literal: Wang tells Chen Zhen: 'I hears you wishes departs my Qin goes Chu, has?'

entries.zh: 軫曰：「然。」
entries.en: Zhen replied: "Yes."
entries.literal: Zhen says: 'Correct.'

entries.zh: 王曰：「儀之言果信矣。」
entries.en: The king declared: "Zhang Yi's words have indeed proven trustworthy."
entries.literal: Wang says: 'Yi words indeed believes.'

entries.zh: 軫曰：「非獨儀知之也，行道之士盡知之矣。
entries.en: Zhen declared: "It is not only Zhang Yi who knows this—all itinerant persuaders understand it.
entries.literal: Zhen says: 'Not only Yi knows, travel road scholars all knows.

entries.zh: 昔子胥忠於其君而天下爭以為臣，曾參孝於其親而天下願以為子。
entries.en: In former times, Wu Zixu was loyal to his lord and the world vied to take him as minister; Zeng Shen was filial to his parents and the world wished to have him as son.
entries.literal: Former Wu Yun loyal to his jun yet world contends considers minister, Zeng Shen filial to his parents yet world wishes considers son.

entries.zh: 故賣僕妾不出閭巷而售者，良僕妾也；
entries.en: Therefore, when selling servants who find buyers without leaving the alleys and lanes, these are good servants;
entries.literal: Therefore, sells male female not emerges alley lane yet sells, good male female;

entries.zh: 出婦嫁於鄉曲者，良婦也。
entries.en: divorced women who remarry in the villages and hamlets—these are good women.
entries.literal: emerges woman marries at village quarter, good woman.

entries.zh: 今軫不忠其君，楚亦何以軫為忠乎？

entries.zh: 王以其言為然，遂善待之。
entries.en: The king deemed his words correct and treated him with favor.

entries.zh: 居秦期年，秦惠王終相張儀，而陳軫奔楚。
entries.en: He remained in Qin for one year. King Hui of Qin ultimately appointed Zhang Yi as prime minister, whereupon Chen Zhen fled to Chu.
entries.literal: Dwells Qin one year, Qin Hui Wang finally chancellor Zhang Yi, Chen Zhen flees Chu.

entries.zh: 楚未之重也，而使陳軫使於秦。
entries.en: Chu did not value him highly but sent Chen Zhen as envoy to Qin.

entries.zh: 過梁，欲見犀首。
entries.en: Passing through Liang, he wished to meet Xi Shou.
entries.literal: Passes Liang, wishes sees Xi Shou.

entries.zh: 犀首謝弗見。
entries.en: Xi Shou declined and refused to see him.
entries.literal: Xi Shou declines not sees.

entries.en: Zhen declared: "I have come on official business. If you do not see me, I shall depart and cannot wait for another day."
entries.literal: Zhen says: 'I for affairs comes, jun not sees Zhen, Zhen will goes, not obtains waits different day.'

entries.zh: 犀首見之。
entries.en: Xi Shou then met with him.
entries.literal: Xi Shou sees him.

entries.en: Chen Zhen asked: "Why do you enjoy drinking so much?"
entries.literal: Chen Zhen says: 'Jun why good drinks?'

entries.zh: 犀首曰：「無事也。」
entries.en: Xi Shou replied: "No particular reason."
entries.literal: Xi Shou says: 'No affairs.'

entries.literal: Says: 'I requests makes jun satiates affairs can?'

entries.zh: 公謂於王曰：『臣與燕、趙之王有故，數使人來，曰：「無事何不相見」，願謁行於王。』
entries.en: Tell the king: "Your minister has old ties with the kings of Yan and Zhao. They have repeatedly sent messengers saying, 'If there is no business, why not meet?' I wish to request permission from Your Majesty to travel."
entries.literal: 'Tell the king: Your minister has old ties with the kings of Yan and Zhao. They have repeatedly sent messengers saying, "If there is no business, why not meet?" I wish to request permission from Your Majesty to travel.'

entries.zh: 王雖許公，公請毋多車，以車三十乘，可陳之於庭，明言之燕、趙。」
entries.en: Though the king permits you, request not many chariots—thirty chariots will suffice, arranged in the courtyard, and openly declare your destination to Yan and Zhao."
entries.literal: Wang though permits jun, jun requests not many chariots, with chariots thirty rides, can arranges at court, bright speaks Yan Zhao.'

entries.zh: 燕、趙客聞之，馳車告其王，使人迎犀首。
entries.en: The Yan and Zhao envoys heard of this, galloped their chariots to inform their kings, who sent emissaries to welcome Xi Shou.
entries.literal: Yan Zhao guests hears, gallops chariots tells their wang, makes person welcomes Xi Shou.

entries.zh: 楚王聞之大怒，曰：「田需與寡人約，而犀首之燕、趙，是欺我也。」
entries.en: The King of Chu heard of this and flew into a great rage: "Tian Xu made covenant with me, yet Xi Shou goes to Yan and Zhao—this is deceiving me!"
entries.literal: Chu wang hears greatly angers: 'Tian Xu with my binds, Xi Shou Yan Zhao, is deceives I.'

entries.zh: 怒而不聽其事。
entries.en: In his anger, he refused to heed their affairs.
entries.literal: Angers not listens his affairs.

entries.zh: 齊聞犀首之北，使人以事委焉。
entries.en: Qi learned of Xi Shou's journey north and sent emissaries to entrust affairs to him.
entries.literal: Qi hears Xi Shou north, makes person with affairs entrusts.

entries.zh: 犀首遂行，三國相事皆斷於犀首。
entries.en: Xi Shou then departed, and all affairs among the three states were decided by Xi Shou.
entries.literal: Xi Shou then goes, three countries mutually affairs all breaks at Xi Shou.

entries.zh: 軫遂至秦。
entries.en: Zhen then arrived in Qin.
entries.literal: Zhen then arrives Qin.

entries.zh: 犀首者，魏之陰晉人也，名衍，姓公孫氏。
entries.en: Xi Shou was a man of Yinjin in Wei, named Yan, of the Gongsun clan.
entries.literal: Xi Shou, Wei Yin Jin person, name Yan, surname Gongsun.

entries.zh: 與張儀不善。
entries.en: He was not on good terms with Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: With Zhang Yi not good.

entries.zh: 張儀為秦之魏，魏王相張儀。
entries.en: Zhang Yi served Qin by going to Wei. The King of Wei appointed Zhang Yi as prime minister.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi for Qin Wei, Wei wang chancellor Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 犀首弗利，故令人謂韓公叔曰：「張儀已合秦魏矣，其言曰『魏攻南陽，秦攻三川』。
entries.en: Xi Shou was not pleased, so he sent someone to tell Han Gongshu: "Zhang Yi has already allied Qin and Wei. His words are: Wei will attack Nanyang, Qin will attack Sanchuan.
entries.literal: Xi Shou not benefits, therefore makes person tells Han Gong Shu: 'Zhang Yi already unites Qin Wei, his words: Wei attacks Nan Yang, Qin attacks Sanchuan.

entries.zh: 魏王所以貴張子者，欲得韓地也。
entries.en: The reason the King of Wei honors Master Zhang is that he wishes to gain Han territory.
entries.literal: Wei wang so nobles Zhang Zi, wishes obtains Han land.

entries.zh: 且韓之南陽已舉矣，子何不少委焉以為衍功，則秦魏之交可錯矣。
entries.en: Han's Nanyang has already been surrendered. Why not yield a small portion and let it count as Yan's achievement? Then the friendship between Qin and Wei can be disrupted.
entries.literal: Moreover, Han Nan Yang already raises, you why not little yields to makes Yan merit, then Qin Wei friendship can mistakes.

entries.zh: 然則魏必圖秦而棄儀，收韓而相衍。」
entries.en: Then Wei will certainly plot against Qin and abandon Yi, reclaim Han territory and appoint Yan as prime minister."
entries.literal: Then Wei certainly schemes Qin abandons Yi, collects Han chancellors Yan.'

entries.zh: 公叔以為便，因委之犀首以為功。
entries.en: Gongshu deemed it advantageous, therefore yielded the territory to Xi Shou to make it his merit.
entries.literal: Gong Shu considers convenient, because yields to Xi Shou makes merit.

entries.zh: 果相魏。
entries.en: He indeed became prime minister of Wei.
entries.literal: Indeed chancellor Wei.

entries.zh: 張儀去。
entries.en: Zhang Yi departed.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi goes.

entries.zh: 義渠君朝於魏。
entries.en: The Lord of Yiqu attended court in Wei.
entries.literal: Yi Qu jun courts at Wei.

entries.zh: 犀首聞張儀復相秦，害之。
entries.en: Xi Shou learned that Zhang Yi had again become prime minister of Qin and resented it.
entries.literal: Xi Shou hears Zhang Yi again chancellor Qin, harms him.

entries.zh: 犀首乃謂義渠君曰：「道遠不得復過，請謁事情。」
entries.en: Xi Shou then addressed the Lord of Yiqu: "The road is far, and I cannot pass this way again. Allow me to request affairs."
entries.literal: Xi Shou then tells Yi Qu jun: 'Road far not obtains again passes, please requests affairs.'

entries.zh: 曰：「中國無事，秦得燒掇焚杅君之國；
entries.en: He said: "When the Central States are at peace, Qin can burn and plunder your domain;
entries.literal: Says: 'China no affairs, Qin obtains burns grasps burns gathers jun country;

entries.en: when there are affairs, Qin will lightly dispatch heavy bribes to serve your domain."
entries.literal: has affairs, Qin will light makes heavy currency serves jun country.'

entries.zh: 其後五國伐秦。
entries.en: Afterward, five states attacked Qin.
entries.literal: After five countries attacks Qin.

entries.zh: 會陳軫謂秦王曰：「義渠君者，蠻夷之賢君也，不如賂之以撫其志。」
entries.en: Just then Chen Zhen addressed the King of Qin: "The Lord of Yiqu is a worthy ruler among the barbarians. It would be better to bribe him and soothe his ambitions."
entries.literal: Meets Chen Zhen tells Qin wang: 'Yi Qu jun, barbarian yi worthy jun, not as bribes with pacifies his ambition.'

entries.zh: 秦王曰：「善。」
entries.en: The King of Qin declared: "Excellent."
entries.literal: Qin wang says: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 乃以文繡千純，婦女百人遺義渠君。
entries.en: They then sent a thousand bolts of embroidered silk and a hundred women to the Lord of Yiqu.
entries.literal: Then with literary embroider thousand pure, women hundred people sends Yi Qu jun.

entries.zh: 義渠君致群臣而謀曰：「此公孫衍所謂邪？」
entries.en: The Lord of Yiqu assembled his ministers and consulted them: "Is this what Gongsun Yan spoke of?"
entries.literal: Yi Qu jun assembles ministers plans: 'This Gongsun Yan so called?'

entries.zh: 乃起兵襲秦，大敗秦人李伯之下。
entries.en: He then mobilized troops to attack Qin, greatly defeating the Qin forces under Li Bo.
entries.literal: Then raises troops attacks Qin, greatly defeats Qin people Li Bo below.

entries.zh: 張儀已卒之後，犀首入相秦。
entries.en: After Zhang Yi had died, Xi Shou entered to serve as prime minister of Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi already dies after, Xi Shou enters chancellor Qin.

entries.zh: 嘗佩五國之相印，為約長。
entries.en: He once wore the prime minister's seal of five states and served as leader of alliances.
entries.literal: Once wears five countries chancellor seal, for binds long.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：三晉多權變之士，夫言從衡彊秦者大抵皆三晉之人也。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: The Three Jin states produced many masters of stratagem and change. Those who spoke of vertical and horizontal alliances to strengthen Qin were for the most part all men of the Three Jin.
entries.literal: Grand Historian says: Three Jin many power changes scholars, speaks vertical horizontal strong Qin generally all three Jin people.

entries.zh: 夫張儀之行事甚於蘇秦，然世惡蘇秦者，以其先死，而儀振暴其短以扶其說，成其衡道。
entries.en: Zhang Yi's conduct of affairs greatly surpassed Su Qin's, yet the world detested Su Qin because he died first, while Yi exposed and denounced his faults to support his own doctrines, completing the way of horizontal alliances.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi conduct affairs very surpasses Su Qin, yet world dislikes Su Qin, with his first dies, Yi vibrates exposes his short supports his says, completes his horizontal way.

entries.zh: 要之，此兩人真傾危之士哉！
entries.en: In sum, these two men were truly masters of perilous stratagems!
entries.literal: Summarizes, this two people true inclines dangerous scholars!

entries.zh: 秦惠王卒，太子武王立，逐張儀、魏章，而以樗里子、甘茂為左右丞相。
entries.en: When King Hui of Qin died, Crown Prince Wu ascended the throne as King Wu. He banished Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang, and appointed Shu Lizi and Gan Mao as left and right prime ministers.
entries.literal: When King Hui of Qin died, Crown Prince Wu ascended the throne as King Wu. He expelled Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang, and appointed Shu Lizi and Gan Mao as left and right chancellors.

entries.zh: 秦使甘茂攻韓，拔宜陽。
entries.en: Qin dispatched Gan Mao to attack Han and seize Yiyang.
entries.literal: Qin sent Gan Mao to attack Han and capture Yiyang.

entries.zh: 使樗里子以車百乘入周。
entries.en: Qin then sent Shu Lizi into Zhou with a hundred chariots.
entries.literal: They sent Shu Lizi with a hundred chariots to enter Zhou.

entries.zh: 周以卒迎之，意甚敬。
entries.en: Zhou welcomed him with armed escort, showing utmost deference.
entries.literal: Zhou welcomed him with troops, showing great respect.

entries.zh: 楚王怒，讓周，以其重秦客。
entries.en: The King of Chu grew furious and upbraided Zhou for favoring the Qin envoy.
entries.literal: The King of Chu was angry and rebuked Zhou for favoring the Qin guest.

entries.zh: 游騰為周說楚王曰：「知伯之伐仇猶，遺之廣車，因隨之以兵，仇猶遂亡。
entries.en: You Teng advised the King of Chu on Zhou's behalf: "When Zhi Bo attacked Qiuyou, he sent them broad chariots, then followed up with troops, and Qiuyou was destroyed.
entries.literal: You Teng for Zhou advised Chu Wang: Zhi Bo attack Qiu You, sent him broad chariot, because followed with troops, Qiu You then perished.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why so?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 無備故也。
entries.en: Because they were unprepared.
entries.literal: Because they were unprepared.

entries.zh: 齊桓公伐蔡，號曰誅楚，其實襲蔡。
entries.en: When Duke Huan of Qi attacked Cai, he proclaimed it was to punish Chu, but in truth he ambushed Cai.
entries.literal: When Duke Huan of Qi attacked Cai, he announced it was to punish Chu, but actually attacked Cai.

entries.zh: 今秦，虎狼之國，使樗里子以車百乘入周，周以仇猶、蔡觀焉，故使長戟居前，彊弩在後，名曰衛疾，而實囚之。
entries.en: Now Qin is a realm of tigers and wolves. If it sends Shu Lizi into Zhou with a hundred chariots, Zhou will remember what happened to Qiuyou and Cai. It will therefore station long lances before him and strong crossbows behind, calling it protection for Ji but in truth holding him prisoner.
entries.literal: Now Qin is a land of tigers and wolves. If it sends Shu Lizi into Zhou with a hundred chariots, Zhou will judge the matter by what happened to Qiuyou and Cai. It will therefore place long halberds before him and strong crossbows behind, calling it protection for Ji but actually imprisoning him.

entries.zh: 且夫周豈能無憂其社稷哉？
entries.en: Moreover, how can Zhou not worry about its altars of soil and grain?
entries.literal: Moreover, Zhou how can not worry its state altars?

entries.zh: 恐一旦亡國以憂大王。」
entries.en: I fear that one day Zhou will perish as a kingdom and cause anxiety for Your Majesty."
entries.literal: I fear that one day Zhou will perish as a state and bring worry to Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 楚王乃悅。
entries.en: The King of Chu was then appeased.

entries.zh: 甘茂者，下蔡人也。
entries.en: Gan Mao was a native of Xiaca.
entries.literal: Gan Mao was a man of Xiaca.

entries.en: He attended Master Shi Ju of Xiaca and mastered the teachings of the Hundred Schools.
entries.literal: He served under Master Shi Ju of Xiaca and studied the doctrines of the Hundred Schools.

entries.zh: 因張儀、樗里子而求見秦惠王。
entries.en: Through Zhang Yi and Shu Lizi, he petitioned for an audience with King Hui of Qin.
entries.literal: Through Zhang Yi and Shu Lizi, he sought an audience with King Hui of Qin.

entries.zh: 王見而說之，使將，而佐魏章略定漢中地。
entries.en: The king saw and delighted in him, appointed him general, and had him assist Wei Zhang in roughly pacifying the Han Zhong territory.
entries.literal: Wang saw pleased him, made general, assisted Wei Zhang roughly pacified Han Zhong land.

entries.zh: 惠王卒，武王立。
entries.en: King Hui passed away, and King Wu ascended the throne.
entries.literal: Hui Wang died, Wu Wang established.

entries.zh: 張儀、魏章去，東之魏。
entries.en: Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang departed and went east to Wei.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi, Wei Zhang departed, east to Wei.

entries.zh: 蜀侯煇、相壯反，秦使甘茂定蜀。
entries.en: The Shu lord Hui and chancellor Zhuang rebelled. Qin dispatched Gan Mao to pacify Shu.
entries.literal: Shu Hou Hui, chancellor Zhuang rebelled, Qin made Gan Mao pacify Shu.

entries.zh: 還，而以甘茂為左丞相，以樗里子為右丞相。
entries.en: Upon his return, they appointed Gan Mao as left prime minister and Shu Lizi as right prime minister.
entries.literal: Returned, made Gan Mao left chancellor, Shu Lizi right chancellor.

entries.zh: 秦武王三年，謂甘茂曰：「寡人欲容車通三川，以窺周室，而寡人死不朽矣。」
entries.en: In the third year of King Wu of Qin, he addressed Gan Mao: "I want to open a chariot road through Sanchuan and look upon the Zhou court; then, though I die, my name will not decay."
entries.literal: Qin Wu Wang three years, told Gan Mao: "I wish broad chariot pass San Chuan, spy Zhou house, I die not rotten."

entries.literal: Gan Mao said: "Request Wei, pact attack Han, make Xiang Shou assist go."

entries.en: Gan Mao arrived and told Xiang Shou: "Return and speak to the king: 'Wei heeds my counsel, yet I wish Your Majesty not to attack.'
entries.literal: Gan Mao arrived, told Xiang Shou: "You return, speak wang: 'Wei listen minister, yet wish wang not attack.'

entries.zh: 事成，盡以為子功。」

entries.literal: Affairs complete, all as you merit."

entries.literal: Replied: "Yi Yang, big county, Shang Dang, Nan Yang store long.

entries.zh: 名曰縣，其實郡也。
entries.en: It is called a county in name, but in reality it is a commandery.

entries.zh: 今王倍數險，行千里攻之，難。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty would cross several dangerous passes and travel a thousand li to attack it; this is difficult.

entries.zh: 昔曾參之處費，魯人有與曾參同姓名者殺人，人告其母曰『曾參殺人』，其母織自若也。
entries.en: In former times, when Zeng Shen dwelt in Fei, a man from Lu with the same name as Zeng Shen committed murder. Someone told his mother, "Zeng Shen has killed a man," but his mother continued weaving undisturbed.
entries.literal: Former Zeng Shen at Fei, Lu man with Zeng Shen same name kill person, person told his mother: Zeng Shen kill person, his mother weave as before.

entries.zh: 頃之，一人又告之曰『曾參殺人』，其母尚織自若也。
entries.en: Shortly after, another person told her, "Zeng Shen has killed a man," and his mother still continued weaving undisturbed.
entries.literal: Shortly, one person again told: Zeng Shen kill person, his mother still weave as before.

entries.zh: 頃又一人告之曰『曾參殺人』，其母投杼下機，踰墻而走。

entries.literal: Shortly again one person told: Zeng Shen kill person, his mother threw shuttle left loom, crossed wall fled.

entries.zh: 夫以曾參之賢與其母信之也，三人疑之，其母懼焉。
entries.en: Though Zeng Shen was worthy and fully trusted by his mother, once three men cast doubt on him, she grew fearful.
entries.literal: Using Zeng Shen worthy with his mother trust him, three men doubt, his mother feared.

entries.en: Now your minister's worthiness does not equal Zeng Shen's, and Your Majesty's trust in your minister does not equal Zeng Shen's mother's trust in Zeng Shen. Those who doubt your minister are not merely three men—I fear Your Majesty will throw down the shuttle.
entries.literal: Now minister worthy not as Zeng Shen, wang trust minister again not as Zeng Shen mother trust Zeng Shen, doubt minister not only three men, minister fear wang throw shuttle.

entries.zh: 始張儀西并巴蜀之地，北開西河之外，南取上庸，天下不以多張子而以賢先王。
entries.en: At first Zhang Yi merged the lands of Bashu to the west, opened the territories north of the Yellow River, and seized Shangyong to the south. The world did not credit Master Zhang with the abundance of these gains but regarded the former king as worthy.
entries.literal: At first Zhang Yi annexed the lands of Ba and Shu in the west, opened the territory beyond the Western River in the north, and took Shangyong in the south. The world did not credit Master Zhang with these abundant gains but instead praised the former king's worthiness.

entries.zh: 魏文侯令樂羊將而攻中山，三年而拔之。

entries.literal: Wei Wen Hou make Yue Yang general attack Zhong Shan, three years take it.

entries.en: Yue Yang returned and sought reward for his merit. Marquis Wen showed him a casket filled with slanderous letters.
entries.literal: When Yue Yang returned and requested reward for his merit, Marquis Wen showed him a box full of slanderous letters.

entries.en: Yue Yang bowed twice and touched his head to the ground: "This is not my merit; it is my lord's strength."
entries.literal: Yue Yang twice bow touched head: This not subject merit, jun effort.

entries.zh: 今臣，羈旅之臣也。

entries.zh: 樗里子、公孫奭二人者挾韓而議之，王必聽之，是王欺魏王而臣受公仲侈之怨也。」

entries.literal: Shu Lizi and Gongsun Shi will argue the matter from Han's side, and the king will certainly listen to them. Thus the king will have deceived the King of Wei, while your minister will incur Gong Zhongchi's resentment."

entries.en: Therefore, he greatly mobilized all troops and dispatched Gan Mao to strike at it.
entries.literal: Because greatly all raised troops, made Gan Mao strike it.

entries.zh: 斬首六萬，遂拔宜陽。

entries.literal: Qin heard Gan Mao Chu, made person tell Chu Wang: "Wish send Gan Mao Qin."

entries.en: The King of Chu asked Fan Quan: 'I wish to place a prime minister in Qin—who would be suitable?'
entries.literal: Chu Wang asked Fan Quan: "I wish place chancellor Qin, who suitable?"

entries.en: He replied: 'Your subject is not qualified to know such matters.'
entries.literal: Replied: "Subject not enough know."

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「寡人欲相甘茂，可乎？」
entries.en: The King of Chu asked: 'I wish to make Gan Mao prime minister—is this acceptable?'
entries.literal: Chu Wang said: "I wish chancellor Gan Mao, acceptable?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「不可。
entries.en: He replied: 'It is not acceptable.
entries.literal: Replied: "Not acceptable.

entries.zh: 夫史舉，下蔡之監門也，大不為事君，小不為家室，以茍賤不廉聞於世，甘茂事之順焉。
entries.en: Shi Ju was a gatekeeper of Xiaca. On the great scale he did not serve his lord; on the small scale he did not maintain his household, and he was known throughout the world as lowly and unprincipled. Yet Gan Mao served him compliantly.
entries.literal: Shi Ju, Xia Cai gate guard, greatly not serve jun, small not family room, with cheap not clean known world, Gan Mao serve him comply.

entries.zh: 故惠王之明，武王之察，張儀之辯，而甘茂事之，取十官而無罪。
entries.en: Thus, though King Hui was discerning, King Wu perceptive, and Zhang Yi eloquent, Gan Mao served them all, holding ten offices without incurring blame.
entries.literal: Therefore, Hui Wang clear, Wu Wang examine, Zhang Yi eloquence, Gan Mao serve them, take ten offices no crime.

entries.zh: 茂誠賢者也，然不可相於秦。
entries.en: Gan Mao is truly a worthy man, yet he cannot serve as prime minister in Qin.
entries.literal: Mao truly worthy, yet not chancellor Qin.

entries.zh: 夫秦之有賢相，非楚國之利也。
entries.en: For Qin to have a worthy prime minister is not advantageous for the state of Chu.
entries.literal: Qin have worthy chancellor, not Chu state profit.

entries.zh: 且王前嘗用召滑於越，而內行章義之難，越國亂，故楚南塞厲門而郡江東。
entries.en: Moreover, Your Majesty once employed Zhao Hua in Yue, where he secretly fomented turmoil while outwardly displaying benevolence and righteousness. Yue fell into chaos, allowing Chu to close the Limen route to the south and establish commanderies in Jiangdong.
entries.literal: Moreover, the king previously employed Zhao Hua in Yue, where he secretly caused disorder while outwardly displaying benevolence and righteousness. Yue fell into chaos; therefore Chu closed the Limen route to the south and established commanderies in Jiangdong.

entries.zh: 計王之功所以能如此者，越國亂而楚治也。
entries.en: The reason Your Majesty's achievements could be so great was that Yue was in chaos while Chu was well governed.
entries.literal: Calculate wang merit so can like this, Yue state chaotic Chu govern.

entries.zh: 今王知用諸越而忘用諸秦，臣以王為鉅過矣。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty knows how to use Yue but forgets how to use Qin—your subject considers this a grave error.
entries.literal: Now wang know use Yue forget use Qin, subject think wang great error.

entries.zh: 然則王若欲置相於秦，則莫若向壽者可。
entries.en: Therefore, if Your Majesty wishes to place a prime minister in Qin, none is better than Xiang Shou.
entries.literal: Then wang if wish place chancellor Qin, then none better Xiang Shou suitable.

entries.zh: 夫向壽之於秦王，親也，少與之同衣，長與之同車，以聽事。
entries.en: Xiang Shou is close to the King of Qin. In youth, he shared the same robes; in adulthood, the same chariot, attending to affairs together.
entries.literal: Xiang Shou to Qin Wang, close, young with same clothes, long with same chariot, listen affairs.

entries.zh: 王必相向壽於秦，則楚國之利也。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty certainly makes Xiang Shou prime minister in Qin, it will benefit the state of Chu.'
entries.literal: Wang certainly chancellor Xiang Shou Qin, then Chu state profit."

entries.zh: 於是使使請秦相向壽於秦。
entries.en: Therefore, they sent an envoy to request that Qin appoint Xiang Shou as prime minister.
entries.literal: Then made envoy request Qin chancellor Xiang Shou Qin.

entries.zh: 秦卒相向壽。
entries.en: Qin ultimately appointed Xiang Shou as prime minister.
entries.literal: Qin finally chancellor Xiang Shou.

entries.zh: 而甘茂竟不得復入秦，卒於魏。
entries.en: Gan Mao was ultimately unable to reenter Qin and died in Wei.
entries.literal: Gan Mao finally not obtain reenter Qin, died Wei.

entries.zh: 樗里子者，名疾，秦惠王之弟也，與惠王異母。
entries.en: Shu Lizi, whose given name was Ji, was the younger half-brother of King Hui of Qin.
entries.literal: Shu Lizi, whose name was Ji, was King Hui of Qin's younger half-brother.

entries.zh: 母，韓女也。
entries.en: His mother was a woman from Han.
entries.literal: His mother was a woman from Han.

entries.zh: 樗里子滑稽多智，秦人號曰「智囊」。
entries.en: Shu Lizi was witty and exceedingly clever. The people of Qin dubbed him the 'Wisdom Satchel.'
entries.literal: Shu Lizi was witty and highly intelligent. The people of Qin called him the "Wisdom Bag."

entries.zh: 昭王三十二年，穰侯為相國，將兵攻魏，走芒卯，入北宅，遂圍大梁。
entries.en: In the thirty-second year of King Zhao, the Marquis of Rang, serving as prime minister, led troops to attack Wei, routed Mang Mao, entered Beizhai, and thereupon besieged Daliang.
entries.literal: In King Zhao's thirty-second year, the Marquis of Rang, serving as chancellor, led troops to attack Wei, routed Mang Mao, entered Bei Zhai, and then surrounded Daliang.

entries.zh: 梁大夫須賈說穰侯曰：「臣聞魏之長吏謂魏王曰：『昔梁惠王伐趙，戰勝三梁，拔邯鄲；
entries.en: Xu Jia, a grandee of Liang, advised the Marquis of Rang: "Your servant has heard Wei's high officials tell the King of Wei: 'Formerly King Hui of Liang attacked Zhao, won a battle at Sanliang, and captured Handan;
entries.literal: Xu Jia, a grandee of Liang, advised the Marquis of Rang: Your servant has heard Wei's high officials tell the King of Wei: Formerly King Hui of Liang attacked Zhao, won a battle at Sanliang, and captured Handan;

entries.zh: 趙氏不割，而邯鄲復歸。
entries.en: Zhao refused to cede land, and Handan was restored to it.
entries.literal: The Zhao clan did not cede land, and Handan returned to them.

entries.zh: 齊人攻衛，拔故國，殺子良；
entries.en: Qi attacked Wey, took its former capital, and killed Ziliang;
entries.literal: Qi attacked Wei, captured Guguo, and killed Ziliang;

entries.zh: 衛人不割，而故地復反。
entries.en: Wey refused to cede land, and its old territory was returned.
entries.literal: The people of Wei did not cede land, and the former territory was returned.

entries.zh: 衛、趙之所以國全兵勁而地不并於諸侯者，以其能忍難而重出地也。
entries.en: The reason Wey and Zhao survive as intact states with vigorous armies and lands not annexed by the feudal lords is that they are able to endure hardship and treat ceding territory as a grave matter.
entries.literal: Wei and Zhao survive as complete states with strong troops and unannexed lands among the feudal lords because they are able to endure hardship and make heavy territorial concessions.

entries.zh: 宋、中山數伐割地，而國隨以亡。
entries.en: Song and Zhongshan were repeatedly attacked for ceding land, and their states perished in consequence.
entries.literal: Song and Zhongshan were attacked several times for ceding land, and their states followed them into extinction.

entries.zh: 臣以為衛、趙可法，而宋、中山可為戒也。
entries.en: Your servant considers Wei and Zhao worthy of emulation, while Song and Zhongshan serve as cautionary examples.
entries.literal: Your servant thinks Wei and Zhao can be models, while Song and Zhongshan serve as warnings.

entries.zh: 秦，貪戾之國也，而毋親。
entries.en: Qin is a rapacious and violent state with no kin relations.
entries.literal: Qin is a greedy and violent state with no kin.

entries.zh: 蠶食魏氏，又盡晉國，戰勝暴子，割八縣，地未畢入，兵復出矣。
entries.en: Qin eats away at Wei like a silkworm and drains the old Jin states dry. After Baozi was defeated and eight counties were ceded, the land had not even been fully delivered before Qin sent troops out again.
entries.literal: Qin nibbles away at the Wei clan and exhausts the Jin states. After defeating Baozi and obtaining the cession of eight counties, the land had not yet been fully handed over before Qin's troops came out again.

entries.zh: 夫秦何厭之有哉！
entries.en: How could Qin ever be satisfied!
entries.literal: How could Qin ever be satisfied!

entries.zh: 今又走芒卯，入北宅，此非敢攻梁也，且劫王以求多割地。
entries.en: Now it has routed Mang Mao once more and entered Beizhai—this is not daring to attack Liang, but rather coercing the king to cede much land.
entries.literal: Now again routed Mang Mao, entered Bei Zhai, this not dare attack Liang, moreover coerce wang seek much cede land.

entries.zh: 王必勿聽也。
entries.en: Your Majesty must not listen to Qin.
entries.literal: Your Majesty must not listen to Qin.

entries.zh: 今王背楚、趙而講秦，楚、趙怒而去王，與王爭事秦，秦必受之。
entries.en: If Your Majesty now abandons Chu and Zhao to negotiate with Qin, Chu and Zhao will grow angry and desert Your Majesty, contending with you to serve Qin, and Qin will certainly accept them.
entries.literal: Now wang back Chu Zhao discuss Qin, Chu Zhao angry depart wang, with wang contend serve Qin, Qin certainly accept.

entries.zh: 秦挾楚、趙之兵以復攻梁，則國求無亡不可得也。
entries.en: If Qin seizes Chu and Zhao's troops to attack Liang once more, then even if our state seeks to avoid destruction, it will not be possible.
entries.literal: Qin grasp Chu Zhao troops again attack Liang, then state seek not perish impossible obtain.

entries.zh: 願王之必無講也。
entries.en: I urge Your Majesty not to negotiate under any circumstances.
entries.literal: I hope Your Majesty will absolutely not negotiate.

entries.zh: 王若欲講，少割而有質；
entries.en: If Your Majesty does negotiate, cede only a little land and take hostages in return;
entries.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to negotiate, cede little and take hostages;

entries.zh: 不然，必見欺。』
entries.en: If not, you will certainly be deceived.'
entries.literal: not so, certainly see deceived.'

entries.zh: 此臣之所聞於魏也，願君［王］之以是慮事也。
entries.en: This is what your servant has heard from Wei. I wish you to consider affairs accordingly.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard this from Wei and wishes you to consider affairs accordingly.

entries.zh: 《周書》曰『惟命不于常』，此言幸之不可數也。
entries.en: The Zhou Book says, 'The mandate does not remain constant.' This means that good fortune cannot be expected again and again.
entries.literal: The Zhou Book says, 'The mandate is not constant'; this means that one cannot count on good fortune again and again.

entries.zh: 夫戰勝暴子，割八縣，此非兵力之精也，又非計之工也，天幸為多矣。
entries.en: The defeat of Baozi and the cession of eight counties came neither from superior military strength nor from brilliant planning; Heaven’s favor played the greater part.
entries.literal: Defeating Baozi in battle and obtaining the cession of eight counties was not due to refined military strength, nor to excellent planning; Heaven's favor had much to do with it.

entries.zh: 今又走芒卯，入北宅，以攻大梁，是以天幸自為常也。
entries.en: Now to rout Mang Mao once more, enter Beizhai, and attack Daliang—this takes heaven's favor as a constant.
entries.literal: Now to rout Mang Mao again, enter Bei Zhai, and attack Daliang - this takes Heaven's good fortune as a constant.

entries.zh: 智者不然。
entries.en: The wise do not act thus.
entries.literal: Wise not so.

entries.zh: 臣聞魏氏悉其百縣勝甲以上戍大梁，臣以為不下三十萬。
entries.en: Your servant has heard that the Wei clan has mobilized the best armored troops from all its hundred counties to garrison Daliang. Your servant thinks they number not less than three hundred thousand.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the Wei clan has mobilized all the best armored troops from its hundred counties and above to garrison Daliang. Your servant thinks they number not less than three hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 以三十萬之眾守梁七仞之城，臣以為湯、武復生，不易攻也。
entries.en: To defend Liang's seven-ren-high walls with three hundred thousand troops—your servant thinks that even if Tang and Wu were revived, they would not easily attack it.
entries.literal: To guard Liang's seven-ren-high city with three hundred thousand troops—your servant thinks that even if Tang and Wu were revived, they would not easily attack it.

entries.zh: 夫輕背楚、趙之兵，陵七仞之城，戰三十萬之眾，而志必舉之，臣以為自天地始分以至于今，未嘗有者也。
entries.en: To turn lightly away from the armies of Chu and Zhao, climb walls seven ren high, fight three hundred thousand men, and insist on taking the city: your servant believes that from the first separation of Heaven and Earth down to the present, such a thing has never happened.
entries.literal: To lightly turn one's back on Chu and Zhao's troops, scale seven-ren walls, battle a force of three hundred thousand, and be determined to take the city: your servant thinks that from the first division of Heaven and Earth until now, there has never been such a thing.

entries.zh: 攻而不拔，秦兵必罷，陶邑必亡，則前功必棄矣。
entries.en: If the attack fails to capture it, Qin troops will certainly be exhausted, Tao city will certainly perish, and then all previous merits will certainly be abandoned.
entries.literal: Attack not pull, Qin troops certainly tired, Tao city certainly perish, then previous merit certainly abandon.

entries.zh: 今魏氏方疑，可以少割收也。
entries.en: Wei is now wavering; it can be brought over with a small concession.
entries.literal: Now the Wei clan is just wavering; it can be won over with a small concession.

entries.zh: 願君逮楚、趙之兵未至於梁，亟以少割收魏。
entries.en: I wish my lord to hasten and make a small territorial concession to win over Wei before Chu and Zhao's troops arrive at Liang.
entries.literal: I wish you to hasten and make a small concession to gather Wei before Chu and Zhao's troops arrive at Liang.

entries.zh: 魏方疑而得以少割為利，必欲之，則君得所欲矣。
entries.en: Since Wei is wavering, if it sees profit in a small concession, it will surely want it, and my lord will obtain what he seeks.
entries.literal: Wei is just wavering, and if it can gain advantage from a small concession, it will certainly desire this; then my lord will obtain what he wishes.

entries.zh: 楚、趙怒於魏之先己也，必爭事秦，從以此散，而君後擇焉。
entries.en: Chu and Zhao will resent Wei for getting ahead of them and will compete to serve Qin. The alliance will break apart, and my lord can then choose among them.
entries.literal: Chu and Zhao will be angry that Wei preceded them and will certainly vie to serve Qin. The alliance will thereby scatter, and my lord can afterward choose among them.

entries.zh: 且君之得地豈必以兵哉！
entries.en: Moreover, must my lord's acquisition of land necessarily be through troops!
entries.literal: Moreover, jun obtain land how must with troops!

entries.zh: 邦晉國，秦兵不攻，而魏必效絳安邑。
entries.en: If you bring peace to the Jin states without sending Qin troops to attack, Wei will surely offer up Jiang and Anyi.
entries.literal: If you stabilize the state of Jin without Qin troops attacking, Wei will certainly cede Jiang and Anyi.

entries.zh: 又為陶開兩道，幾盡故宋，衛必效單父。
entries.en: You will also open two routes to Tao and nearly exhaust the former Song lands; Wey will surely offer up Shanfu.
entries.literal: You will also open two roads for Tao and nearly exhaust the former Song territories; Wei will certainly cede Shanfu.

entries.zh: 秦兵可全，而君制之，何索而不得，何為而不成！
entries.en: Qin troops can be preserved whole while my lord controls them—what is there to seek that cannot be obtained, what to do that cannot be accomplished!
entries.literal: Qin troops can complete, jun control it, what seek not obtain, what do not complete!

entries.zh: 願君熟慮之而無行危。」
entries.en: I wish my lord to deliberate carefully and not pursue danger."
entries.literal: Wish jun carefully consider not do danger."

entries.zh: 穰侯曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Marquis of Rang declared: 'Excellent.'
entries.literal: Marquis of Rang said: Good.

entries.zh: 乃罷梁圍。
entries.en: He then lifted the siege of Liang.
entries.literal: He then stopped the siege of Liang.

entries.zh: 穰侯魏冉者，秦昭王母宣太后弟也。
entries.en: Wei Ran, Marquis of Rang, was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xuan, the mother of King Zhao of Qin.
entries.literal: Wei Ran, Marquis of Rang, was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xuan, mother of King Zhao of Qin.

entries.zh: 其先楚人，姓羋氏。
entries.en: His forebears were Chu people of the Mi clan.
entries.literal: His ancestors were Chu people of the Mi clan.

entries.zh: 王翦者，頻陽東鄉人也。
entries.en: Wang Jian was a man from the eastern village of Pinyang.
entries.literal: Wang Jian was a man from the eastern village of Pinyang.

entries.zh: 少而好兵，事秦始皇。
entries.en: From youth, he delighted in military matters and served Qin Shihuang.
entries.literal: As a youth he loved military affairs and served Qin Shihuang.

entries.zh: 始皇十一年，翦將攻趙閼與，破之，拔九城，十八年，翦將攻趙。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Shihuang, Jian commanded the attack on Zhao's Yanyu and broke it, conquering nine cities. In the eighteenth year, Jian commanded the attack on Zhao.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Shihuang, Jian commanded the attack on Zhao's Yan Yu and broke it, conquering nine cities. In the eighteenth year, Jian commanded the attack on Zhao.

entries.zh: 歲餘，遂拔趙，趙王降，盡定趙地為郡。
entries.en: After more than a year, he conquered Zhao. The King of Zhao surrendered. They pacified all Zhao territory and organized it into commanderies.
entries.literal: After more than a year, he captured Zhao. The King of Zhao surrendered. They completely pacified Zhao territory as commanderies.

entries.zh: 明年，燕使荊軻為賊於秦，秦王使王翦攻燕。
entries.en: The following year, Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate Qin. The King of Qin sent Wang Jian to attack Yan.
entries.literal: The next year, Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate Qin. The King of Qin sent Wang Jian to attack Yan.

entries.zh: 燕王喜走遼東，翦遂定燕薊而還。
entries.en: King Xi of Yan fled to Liaodong. Jian thereupon pacified Yan's Ji and returned.
entries.literal: King Xi of Yan fled to Liaodong. Jian then pacified Yan's Ji and returned.

entries.zh: 秦使翦子王賁擊荊，荊兵敗。
entries.en: Qin sent Jian's son Wang Ben to attack Chu. Chu soldiers were defeated.
entries.literal: Qin sent Jian's son Wang Ben to attack Chu. Chu troops were defeated.

entries.zh: 還擊魏，魏王降，遂定魏地。
entries.en: They returned to attack Wei. The King of Wei surrendered. They thereupon pacified Wei territory.
entries.literal: They returned to attack Wei. The King of Wei surrendered. They then pacified Wei territory.

entries.zh: 秦始皇既滅三晉，走燕王，而數破荊師。
entries.en: Qin Shihuang had already extinguished the Three Jin, driven away the King of Yan, and repeatedly defeated Chu forces.
entries.literal: Qin Shihuang had already extinguished the Three Jin, driven away the King of Yan, and repeatedly broken Chu forces.

entries.zh: 秦將李信者，年少壯勇，嘗以兵數千逐燕太子丹至於衍水中，卒破得丹，始皇以為賢勇。
entries.en: Among Qin's generals was Li Xin, young and vigorous. He once with several thousand soldiers pursued Yan's crown prince Dan to the middle of Yan River, finally breaking through and capturing Dan. Shihuang considered him worthy and brave.
entries.literal: Among Qin's generals was Li Xin, young and vigorous. He once with several thousand troops pursued Yan's crown prince Dan to the middle of Yan River, finally breaking through and capturing Dan. Shihuang considered him worthy and brave.

entries.zh: 於是始皇問李信：「吾欲攻取荊，於將軍度用幾何人而足？」
entries.en: Shihuang then asked Li Xin: 'I wish to attack and conquer Chu. In your estimation, General, how many men will suffice?'
entries.literal: Shihuang asked Li Xin: 'I wish to attack and conquer Chu. In your estimation, how many men will suffice?'

entries.zh: 李信曰：「不過用二十萬人。」
entries.en: Li Xin said: 'No more than two hundred thousand men will suffice.'
entries.literal: Li Xin said: 'No more than 200,000 men.'

entries.zh: 始皇問王翦，王翦曰：「非六十萬人不可。」
entries.en: Shihuang asked Wang Jian. Wang Jian replied: 'Without six hundred thousand men it cannot be accomplished.'
entries.literal: Shihuang asked Wang Jian. Wang Jian said: 'Without 600,000 men it cannot be done.'

entries.zh: 始皇曰：「王將軍老矣，何怯也！
entries.en: Shihuang said: 'General Wang has grown old. Why so timid?
entries.literal: Shihuang said: 'General Wang is old. Why so cowardly?

entries.zh: 李將軍果勢壯勇，其言是也。」
entries.en: General Li is indeed vigorous and courageous. His words are correct.'
entries.literal: General Li is truly vigorous and brave. His words are correct.'

entries.zh: 遂使李信及蒙恬將二十萬南伐荊。
entries.en: He then sent Li Xin and Meng Tian to lead two hundred thousand men south to attack Chu.
entries.literal: He sent Li Xin and Meng Tian to lead 200,000 men south to attack Chu.

entries.zh: 王翦言不用，因謝病，歸老於頻陽。
entries.en: Wang Jian's counsel was not heeded, so he pleaded illness and returned to retire in Pinyang.
entries.literal: Wang Jian's advice was not used, so he claimed illness and returned to retire in Pinyang.

entries.zh: 李信攻平與，蒙恬攻寢，大破荊軍。
entries.en: Li Xin attacked Pingyu, Meng Tian attacked Qin. They greatly defeated Chu forces.
entries.literal: Li Xin assaulted Ping Yu, Meng Tian assaulted Qin. They greatly broke Chu forces.

entries.zh: 信又攻鄢郢，破之，於是引兵而西，與蒙恬會城父。
entries.en: Xin attacked Yanying once more and broke it. He then led his troops west to rendezvous with Meng Tian at Chengfu.
entries.literal: Xin assaulted Yan Ying again and broke it. He then led soldiers west to meet Meng Tian at Chengfu.

entries.zh: 荊人因隨之，三日三夜不頓舍，大破李信軍，入兩壁，殺七都尉，秦軍走。
entries.en: Chu people followed them, three days and nights without resting or camping, greatly broke Li Xin's forces, entered two walls, killed seven commandants, and Qin forces fled.
entries.literal: Chu people followed them, three days and nights without resting or camping, greatly broke Li Xin's army, entered two walls, killed seven commandants, and Qin army fled.

entries.zh: 王翦果代李信擊荊。
entries.en: Wang Jian did in fact replace Li Xin in the attack on Chu.
entries.literal: Wang Jian indeed replaced Li Xin to attack Chu.

entries.zh: 荊聞王翦益軍而來，乃悉國中兵以拒秦。
entries.en: Chu heard that Wang Jian was coming with augmented forces and mobilized all soldiers in their state to resist Qin.
entries.literal: Chu heard Wang Jian was coming with increased forces and mobilized all their national soldiers to resist Qin.

entries.zh: 王翦至，堅壁而守之，不肯戰。
entries.en: Wang Jian arrived and fortified his position stoutly, refusing to give battle.
entries.literal: Wang Jian arrived and built firm fortifications to defend, refusing battle.

entries.zh: 荊兵數出挑戰，終不出。
entries.en: Chu soldiers repeatedly sallied forth to challenge, but he would not emerge.
entries.literal: Chu soldiers repeatedly came out to challenge, but he would not come out.

entries.zh: 王翦日休士洗沐，而善飲食撫循之，親與士卒同食。
entries.en: Wang Jian daily gave his soldiers rest and bathing, treating them well with food and encouragement, personally sharing the same meals as his troops.
entries.literal: Wang Jian daily let his soldiers rest and bathe, treating them well with food and care, personally eating the same as the soldiers.

entries.zh: 久之，王翦使人問軍中戲乎？
entries.en: After a long while, Wang Jian sent someone to ask if the army was engaging in games.
entries.literal: After a long time, Wang Jian sent someone to ask if the forces were playing.

entries.zh: 對曰：「方投石超距。」
entries.en: They replied: 'They are currently throwing stones and leaping.'
entries.literal: They replied: 'They are throwing stones and jumping.'

entries.zh: 於是王翦曰：「士卒可用矣。」
entries.en: Wang Jian then said: 'The troops can be deployed now.'
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: 'The soldiers can be used now.'

entries.zh: 荊數挑戰而秦不出，乃引而東。
entries.en: Chu repeatedly provoked battle, but Qin would not emerge. Chu then withdrew eastward.
entries.literal: Chu repeatedly challenged but Qin would not come out. Chu then withdrew eastward.

entries.zh: 翦因舉兵追之，令壯士擊，大破荊軍。
entries.en: Jian then raised his troops to pursue them, commanding valiant warriors to strike. He greatly routed Chu forces.
entries.literal: Jian raised his soldiers to pursue them, commanding brave warriors to strike. He greatly broke Chu forces.

entries.zh: 至蘄南，殺其將軍項燕，荊兵遂敗走。
entries.en: Reaching south of Qian, he slew their general Xiang Yan. Chu soldiers thereupon fled in rout.
entries.literal: Reaching south of Qian, he killed their general Xiang Yan. Chu soldiers fled in defeat.

entries.zh: 秦因乘勝略定荊地城邑。
entries.en: Qin took advantage of their victory to sweep through and pacify Chu's cities and towns.
entries.literal: Qin took advantage of victory to sweep and pacify Chu cities and towns.

entries.zh: 歲餘，虜荊王負芻，竟平荊地為郡縣。
entries.en: After more than a year, they captured Chu King Fuchu and finally pacified Chu territory as commanderies and counties.
entries.literal: After more than a year, they captured Chu King Fu Chou and finally pacified Chu territory as commanderies and counties.

entries.zh: 因南征百越之君。
entries.en: They then campaigned southward against the lords of the Hundred Yue.
entries.literal: They then campaigned south against the lords of Baiyue.

entries.zh: 而王翦子王賁，與李信破定燕、齊地。
entries.en: Wang Jian's son Wang Ben, together with Li Xin, captured and pacified Yan and Qi territories.
entries.literal: Wang Jian's son Wang Ben, together with Li Xin, conquered and pacified Yan and Qi territories.

entries.zh: 始皇聞之，大怒，自馳如頻陽，見謝王翦曰：「寡人以不用將軍計，李信果辱秦軍。
entries.en: Shihuang heard of it and grew greatly angry. He raced personally to Pinyang and apologized to Wang Jian: 'I did not use your plan. Li Xin has indeed disgraced our Qin forces.
entries.literal: Shihuang heard of it and grew greatly angry. He raced personally to Pinyang and apologized to Wang Jian: 'I did not use your plan. Li Xin has indeed disgraced our Qin army.

entries.zh: 今聞荊兵日進而西，將軍雖病，獨忍棄寡人乎！」
entries.en: Now I hear Chu soldiers advance daily westward. Though you are ill, can you bear to abandon me?'
entries.literal: Now I hear Chu troops advance daily westward. Though you are ill, can you bear to abandon me?'

entries.zh: 王翦謝曰：「老臣罷病悖亂，唯大王更擇賢將。」
entries.en: Wang Jian declined, saying: 'Old minister is exhausted and ill, addled in mind. I ask only that Your Majesty select another worthy general.'
entries.literal: Wang Jian apologized: 'Old minister is tired and ill, confused. I ask only that Your Majesty choose another worthy general.'

entries.zh: 始皇謝曰：「已矣，將軍勿復言！」
entries.en: Shihuang apologized, saying: 'Enough. General, speak no more!'
entries.literal: Shihuang apologized: 'Enough. General, speak no more!'

entries.zh: 王翦曰：「大王必不得已用臣，非六十萬人不可。」
entries.en: Wang Jian said: 'If Your Majesty must needs employ me, six hundred thousand men are indispensable.'
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: 'If Your Majesty must use me, 600,000 men are indispensable.'

entries.zh: 始皇曰：「為聽將軍計耳。」
entries.en: Shihuang said: 'I will heed your counsel.'
entries.literal: Shihuang said: 'I will follow your plan.'

entries.zh: 於是王翦將兵六十萬人，始皇自送至灞上。
entries.en: Wang Jian led 600,000 soldiers. Shihuang personally saw him off to Bashang.
entries.literal: Wang Jian led 600,000 troops. Shihuang personally saw him off to Bashang.

entries.zh: 王翦行，請美田宅園池甚眾。
entries.en: As Wang Jian set out, he requested numerous fine fields, residences, gardens, and ponds.
entries.literal: As Wang Jian departed, he requested many fine fields, houses, and gardens.

entries.zh: 始皇曰：「將軍行矣，何憂貧乎？」
entries.en: Shihuang said: 'General is departing. Why concern yourself with poverty?'
entries.literal: Shihuang said: 'General is departing. Why worry about poverty?'

entries.zh: 王翦曰：「為大王將，有功終不得封侯，故及大王之向臣，臣亦及時以請園池為子孫業耳。」
entries.en: Wang Jian said: 'Serving as Your Majesty's general, even with merit I will never be enfeoffed as marquess. So while Your Majesty looks favorably upon me, I also take this timely opportunity to request gardens and ponds as property for my descendants.'
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: 'As Your Majesty's general, even with merit I will never be enfeoffed as marquess. So while Your Majesty favors me, I also take this opportunity to request gardens and pools as property for my descendants.'

entries.zh: 始皇大笑。
entries.en: Shihuang burst into great laughter.
entries.literal: Shihuang laughed heartily.

entries.zh: 王翦既至關，使使還請善田者五輩。
entries.en: When Wang Jian reached the pass, he sent messengers back five times requesting fine fields.
entries.literal: Wang Jian reached the pass and sent messengers back five times requesting good fields.

entries.zh: 或曰：「將軍之乞貸，亦已甚矣。」
entries.en: Some remarked: 'The general's requests for favors have already gone too far.'
entries.literal: Some said: 'The general's begging is already excessive.'

entries.zh: 王翦曰：「不然。
entries.en: Wang Jian said: 'Not so.
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: 'Not so.

entries.zh: 夫秦王怚而不信人。
entries.en: The King of Qin is mistrustful and does not trust others.
entries.literal: The King of Qin is suspicious and distrusts people.

entries.zh: 今空秦國甲士而專委於我，我不多請田宅為子孫業以自堅，顧令秦王坐而疑我邪？」
entries.en: Now he empties Qin's armored soldiers and entrusts them exclusively to me. If I don't request numerous fields and residences as property for my descendants to fortify myself, won't the King of Qin sit idly by and suspect me?'
entries.literal: Now he empties Qin's armored soldiers and entrusts them all to me. If I don't request many fields and houses as property for my descendants to strengthen myself, won't the King of Qin sit and suspect me?'

entries.zh: 秦二世之時，王翦及其子賁皆已死，而又滅蒙氏。
entries.en: In the time of Qin Ershi, Wang Jian and his son Ben had both already perished, and they also extinguished the Meng clan.
entries.literal: In the time of Qin Ershi, Wang Jian and his son Ben had both already died, and they also extinguished the Meng clan.

entries.zh: 陳勝之反秦，秦使王翦之孫王離擊趙，圍趙王及張耳鉅鹿城。
entries.en: When Chen Sheng rebelled against Qin, Qin sent Wang Jian's grandson Wang Li to attack Zhao, besieging the King of Zhao and Zhang Er at Julu City.
entries.literal: When Chen Sheng rebelled against Qin, Qin sent Wang Jian's grandson Wang Li to attack Zhao, besieging King Zhao and Zhang Er at Julu City.

entries.zh: 或曰：「王離，秦之名將也。
entries.en: Some said: 'Wang Li is Qin's renowned general.
entries.literal: Some said: 'Wang Li is Qin's famous general.

entries.zh: 今將彊秦之兵，攻新造之趙，舉之必矣。」
entries.en: Now commanding strong Qin's soldiers to attack newly founded Zhao—it will certainly succeed.'
entries.literal: Now commanding strong Qin's troops to attack newly founded Zhao—it will certainly succeed.'

entries.zh: 客曰：「不然。
entries.en: A guest said: 'Not so.
entries.literal: A guest said: 'Not so.

entries.zh: 夫為將三世者必敗。
entries.en: Generals of the third generation will certainly meet defeat.
entries.literal: Generals of the third generation will certainly fail.

entries.zh: 必敗者何也？
entries.en: Why will they certainly meet defeat?
entries.literal: Why will they certainly fail?

entries.zh: 必其所殺伐多矣，其後受其不祥。
entries.en: They must have slain and conquered much. Afterward they receive their ill fortune.
entries.literal: They must have killed and captured much. Afterward they receive their misfortune.

entries.zh: 今王離已三世將矣。」
entries.en: Now Wang Li is already a third-generation commander.'
entries.literal: Now Wang Li is already a third-generation general.'

entries.zh: 居無何，項羽救趙，擊秦軍，果虜王離，王離軍遂降諸侯。
entries.en: Before long, Xiang Yu rescued Zhao, assaulted Qin forces, and indeed captured Wang Li. Wang Li's forces surrendered to the feudal lords.
entries.literal: Before long, Xiang Yu rescued Zhao, attacked Qin army, and indeed captured Wang Li. Wang Li's army surrendered to the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：鄙語云「尺有所短，寸有所長」。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: The vulgar proverb says 'A chi has its shortness, a cun has its length.'
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: The common saying goes 'A foot has its shortcomings, an inch has its strengths.'

entries.zh: 白起料敵合變，出奇無窮，聲震天下，然不能救患於應侯。
entries.en: Bai Qi gauged foes and adapted to circumstances, deploying stratagems without bound, his reputation shook the world, yet he could not save himself from Lord Ying's machinations.
entries.literal: Bai Qi assessed enemies and adapted to changes, deploying surprises without limit, his fame shook the world, yet he could not save himself from Lord Ying's schemes.

entries.zh: 王翦為秦將，夷六國，當是時，翦為宿將，始皇師之，然不能輔秦建德，固其根本，偷合取容，以至圽身。
entries.en: Wang Jian as Qin's general extinguished the six states. At that time, Jian was a veteran general whom Shihuang relied upon, yet he could not assist Qin in establishing virtue and consolidating its foundations, but instead sought favor and accommodated himself, leading to his ruin.
entries.literal: Wang Jian as Qin's general extinguished the six states. At that time, Jian was an old general whom Shihuang relied on, yet he could not assist Qin in establishing virtue and strengthening its foundations, but instead curried favor and accommodated himself, leading to his downfall.

entries.zh: 及孫王離為項羽所虜，不亦宜乎！
entries.en: When his grandson Wang Li was captured by Xiang Yu, was it not fitting!
entries.literal: When his grandson Wang Li was captured by Xiang Yu, was it not fitting?

entries.zh: 彼各有所短也。
entries.en: Each has his deficiencies.
entries.literal: They each have their shortcomings.

entries.zh: 白起者，郿人也。
entries.en: Bai Qi was a man of Mei.
entries.literal: Bai Qi was a native of Mei.

entries.zh: 善用兵，事秦昭王。
entries.en: He was adept at warfare and served King Zhao of Qin.
entries.literal: He was skilled in the art of war and served King Zhao of Qin.

entries.zh: 昭王十三年，而白起為左庶長，將而擊韓之新城。
entries.en: In King Zhao's thirteenth year, Bai Qi was appointed Left Senior Minister and led troops to attack Xincheng of Han.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of King Zhao's reign, Bai Qi became left senior minister and led troops to attack Han's Xincheng.

entries.zh: 是歲，穰侯相秦，舉任鄙以為漢中守。
entries.en: That year, the Marquis of Rang became prime minister of Qin and recommended Ren Bi to serve as governor of Hanzhong.
entries.literal: That year, the Marquis of Rang served as Qin's prime minister and appointed Ren Bi as governor of Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 其明年，白起為左更，攻韓、魏於伊闕，斬首二十四萬，又虜其將公孫喜，拔五城。
entries.en: The next year, Bai Qi was appointed Left Minister of the Interior and attacked Han and Wei at Yique, beheading 240,000 men, capturing their general Gongsun Xi, and taking five cities.
entries.literal: The next year, Bai Qi became left minister of the interior and attacked Han and Wei at Yique. He beheaded 240,000 men, captured their general Gongsun Xi, and took five cities.

entries.zh: 起遷為國尉。
entries.en: Qi was advanced to the position of state defender.
entries.literal: Qi was promoted to state defender.

entries.zh: 涉河取韓安邑以東，到乾河。
entries.en: He forded the Yellow River and seized Han's Anyi and eastward to Ganhe.
entries.literal: He crossed the Yellow River and took Han's Anyi and eastward to Ganhe.

entries.zh: 明年，白起為大良造。
entries.en: The following year, Bai Qi was appointed grand master craftsman.
entries.literal: The next year, Bai Qi became grand master craftsman.

entries.zh: 攻魏，拔之，取城小大六十一。
entries.en: He attacked Wei, conquered it, and seized sixty-one cities, large and small.
entries.literal: He attacked Wei, conquered it, and took sixty-one cities of varying sizes.

entries.zh: 明年，起與客卿錯攻垣城，拔之。
entries.en: The following year, Qi and guest minister Cuo attacked Yuan City and conquered it.
entries.literal: The next year, Qi and guest minister Cuo attacked Yuan City and conquered it.

entries.zh: 後五年，白起攻趙，拔光狼城。
entries.en: Five years later, Bai Qi attacked Zhao and seized Guanglang City.
entries.literal: Five years later, Bai Qi attacked Zhao and conquered Guanglang City.

entries.zh: 後七年，白起攻楚，拔鄢、鄧五城。
entries.en: Seven years later, Bai Qi attacked Chu and conquered Yan and Deng—five cities in all.
entries.literal: Seven years later, Bai Qi attacked Chu and conquered Yan and Deng—five cities in total.

entries.zh: 其明年，攻楚，拔郢，燒夷陵，遂東至竟陵。
entries.en: The following year, he attacked Chu once more, conquered Ying, burned Yiling, and advanced eastward to Jingling.
entries.literal: The next year, he attacked Chu again, conquered Ying, burned Yiling, and advanced east to Jingling.

entries.zh: 楚王亡去郢，東走徙陳。
entries.en: The King of Chu abandoned Ying and fled eastward to Chen.
entries.literal: The King of Chu fled Ying and moved east to Chen.

entries.zh: 秦以郢為南郡。
entries.en: Qin established Ying as the Nanjun commandery.
entries.literal: Qin made Ying into Nan Commandery.
