entries.zh: 白起遷為武安君。
entries.en: Bai Qi was elevated to Lord Wu'an.
entries.literal: Bai Qi was promoted to Lord Wu'an.

entries.zh: 武安君因取楚，定巫、黔中郡。
entries.en: Lord Wu'an then took territory from Chu and established Wu and Qianzhong as commanderies.
entries.literal: Lord Wu'an then conquered Chu and established the commanderies of Wu and Qianzhong.

entries.zh: 昭王三十四年，白起攻魏，拔華陽，走芒卯，而虜三晉將，斬首十三萬。
entries.en: In King Zhao's thirty-fourth year, Bai Qi attacked Wei, conquered Huayang, routed Mang Mao, captured three Jin generals, and beheaded 130,000 men.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of King Zhao, Bai Qi attacked Wei, conquered Huayang, routed Mang Mao, captured three Jin generals, and beheaded 130,000 men.

entries.zh: 與趙將賈偃戰，沈其卒二萬人於河中。
entries.en: He fought with Zhao general Jia Yan and drowned 20,000 of his troops in the Yellow River.
entries.literal: He fought with Zhao general Jia Yan and drowned 20,000 of his troops in the river.

entries.zh: 昭王四十三年，白起攻韓陘城，拔五城，斬首五萬。
entries.en: In King Zhao's forty-third year, Bai Qi attacked Han's Xingcheng, conquered five cities, and beheaded 50,000 men.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year of King Zhao, Bai Qi attacked Han's Xingcheng, conquered five cities, and beheaded 50,000 men.

entries.zh: 四十四年，白起攻南陽太行道，絕之。
entries.en: In the forty-fourth year, Bai Qi attacked the Nanyang-Taihang road and severed it.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year, Bai Qi attacked the Nanyang-Taihang road and cut it off.

entries.zh: 是以騶子重於齊。
entries.en: Therefore, Master Zou was honored in Qi.
entries.literal: Therefore, Zou Zi heavy at Qi.

entries.zh: 適梁，惠王郊迎，執賓主之禮。
entries.en: When he went to Liang, King Hui welcomed him at the suburbs and performed the rituals of guest and host.
entries.literal: Go Liang, Hui Wang suburban welcome, hold guest host ritual.

entries.zh: 適趙，平原君側行撇席。
entries.en: When he went to Zhao, Lord Pingyuan stepped aside and personally swept his mat in deference.
entries.literal: When he went to Zhao, Lord Pingyuan sidestepped and swept aside his mat in deference.

entries.zh: 如燕，昭王擁彗先驅，請列弟子之座而受業，筑碣石宮，身親往師之。
entries.en: When he went to Yan, King Zhao embraced a broom and drove ahead, requested to arrange a disciple's seat to receive instruction, built the Jieshi Palace, and personally went to study under him.
entries.literal: Go Yan, Zhao Wang embrace broom first drive, request arrange disciple seat receive teaching, build Jie Shi palace, body personally go teacher.

entries.zh: 作主運。
entries.en: He composed 'Lord of Fate.'
entries.literal: He composed 'Lord of Fate.'

entries.zh: 其游諸侯見尊禮如此，豈與仲尼菜色陳蔡，孟軻困於齊梁同乎哉！
entries.en: Such were his travels among the feudal lords and the honors he received. How could this be compared with Confucius wasting away in Chen and Cai, or Meng Ke suffering hardship in Qi and Liang?
entries.literal: His travels among the feudal lords and the honored rites he received were thus—how can this be compared to Confucius's emaciation in Chen and Cai, or Meng Ke's distress in Qi and Liang!

entries.zh: 笔武王以仁義伐紂而王，伯夷餓不食周粟；
entries.en: Formerly King Wu used benevolence and righteousness to attack Zhou and became king, but Bo Yi starved rather than eat Zhou grain;
entries.literal: Former Wu Wang with benevolence righteousness attack Zhou wang, Bo Yi starve not eat Zhou millet;

entries.zh: 衛靈公問陳，而孔子不答；
entries.en: Duke Ling of Wei asked about battle formations, but Confucius did not answer;
entries.literal: Wei Ling Gong ask array, Confucius not answer;

entries.zh: 梁惠王謀欲攻趙，孟軻稱大王去邠。
entries.en: When King Hui of Liang planned to attack Zhao, Meng Ke cited the Great King’s departure from Bin.
entries.literal: When King Hui of Liang plotted to attack Zhao, Meng Ke cited how the Great King left Bin.

entries.zh: 此豈有意阿世俗茍合而已哉！
entries.en: How could this have been intended merely to flatter the world and casually fit in!
entries.literal: This how have intention flatter world casual match only!

entries.zh: 持方枘欲內圜鑿，其能入乎？
entries.en: To hold a square tenon and wish to insert it into a round socket—can it enter?
entries.literal: Hold square tenon wish enter round hole, can enter?

entries.zh: 或曰，伊尹負鼎而勉湯以王，百里奚飯牛車下而繆公用霸，作先合，然後引之大道。
entries.en: Some say: Yi Yin carried a tripod and urged Tang to become king; Baili Xi fed oxen under a cart and Duke Mu employed him to become hegemon. They made themselves fit first, then led them to the great way.
entries.literal: Some say, Yi Yin carry tripod urge Tang wang, Baili Xi feed cow cart under Mu Gong use hegemon, make first match, then lead great way.

entries.zh: 騶衍其言雖不軌，儻亦有牛鼎之意乎？
entries.en: Although Zou Yan’s words were unorthodox, perhaps he too had Yi Yin’s intention in speaking of cauldrons and tripods.
entries.literal: Though Zou Yan's words were unorthodox, might he also have had yiyin's intention of the cauldron and tripod?

entries.zh: 淳于髡，齊人也。
entries.en: Chunyu Kun was a man of Qi.
entries.literal: Chun Yu Kun, Qi man.

entries.zh: 博聞彊記，學無所主。
entries.en: He was broadly learned and had a strong memory, his studies having no particular master.
entries.literal: Broad hear strong memory, study no master.

entries.zh: 其諫說，慕晏嬰之為人也，然而承意觀色為務。
entries.en: In his remonstrances and persuasions he admired Yan Ying’s conduct, yet his work lay in accommodating a ruler’s intentions and reading his expressions.
entries.literal: In his remonstrances and persuasions he admired Yan Ying's conduct, yet his task was to accommodate intentions and observe expressions.

entries.zh: 客有見髡於梁惠王，惠王屏左右，獨坐而再見之，終無言也。
entries.en: A guest introduced Kun to King Hui of Liang. The king dismissed his attendants, sat alone, and received him twice, but in the end Kun said nothing.
entries.literal: A guest had Kun introduced to King Hui of Liang; the king dismissed his attendants, sat alone, and received him twice, but in the end said nothing.

entries.zh: 惠王怪之，以讓客曰：「子之稱淳于先生，管、晏不及，及見寡人，寡人未有得也。
entries.en: King Hui was astonished and reproached the guest, saying: "You praised Master Chunyu as surpassing Guan and Yan, but when I met him, I gained nothing from it.
entries.literal: Hui Wang strange, with rebuke guest: You praise Chun Yu mister, Guan Yan not reach, reach see my person, my person not have obtain.

entries.zh: 豈寡人不足為言邪？
entries.en: Am I not worth speaking to?
entries.literal: How my person not sufficient speak?

entries.zh: 何故哉？」
entries.en: Why is that?"
entries.literal: Why?"

entries.zh: 客以謂髡。
entries.en: The guest told this to Kun.
entries.literal: The guest told this to Kun.

entries.zh: 髡曰：「固也。
entries.en: Kun replied, "Indeed.
entries.literal: Kun said: Indeed.

entries.zh: 吾前見王，王志在驅逐；
entries.en: The first time I saw the king, his mind was fixed on the hunt;
entries.literal: The first time I saw the king, his mind was on the hunt;

entries.zh: 後復見王，王志在音聲：吾是以默然。」
entries.en: The second time I saw the king, his mind was on music. That is why I remained silent."
entries.literal: After again see wang, wang ambition in sound voice: I therefore silent."

entries.zh: 客具以報王，王大駭，曰：「嗟乎，淳于先生誠聖人也！
entries.en: The guest reported everything to the king, who was greatly astonished and exclaimed, "Alas! Master Chunyu is truly a sage!
entries.literal: Guest all with report wang, wang greatly shocked: Alas, Chun Yu mister truly sage!

entries.zh: 前淳于先生之來，人有獻善馬者，寡人未及視，會先生至。
entries.en: Before Master Chunyu arrived, someone had presented me with a fine horse. I had not yet examined it when the master came.
entries.literal: Before Master Chunyu arrived, someone presented me with a fine horse. I had not yet examined it when the master arrived.

entries.zh: 後先生之來，人有獻謳者，未及試，亦會先生來。
entries.en: On his later visit, someone presented a singer. I had not yet tried her out when the master came again.
entries.literal: On his later visit, someone presented a singer; I had not yet tested her when the master came again.

entries.zh: 寡人雖屏人，然私心在彼，有之。」
entries.en: Although I dismissed my attendants, my private thoughts were still on those things. What he said was true."
entries.literal: Though I dismissed my attendants, my private thoughts were still on those things. It was true."

entries.zh: 後淳于髡見，壹語連三日三夜無倦。
entries.en: After that, when Chunyu Kun was received, he spoke continuously for three days and three nights without tiring.
entries.literal: Afterward, when Chunyu Kun was received, he spoke continuously for three days and three nights without tiring.

entries.zh: 惠王欲以卿相位待之，髡因謝去。
entries.en: King Hui wished to honor him with the rank of minister and chancellor, but Kun declined and departed.
entries.literal: King Hui wished to treat him with the position of minister and chancellor, but Kun declined and left.

entries.zh: 於是送以安車駕駟，束帛加璧，黃金百鎰。
entries.en: He was then sent off with a comfortable four-horse carriage, bolts of silk, jade discs, and one hundred yi of gold.
entries.literal: He was then sent off with a comfortable carriage drawn by four horses, bolts of silk and jade discs, and one hundred yi of gold.

entries.zh: 終身不仕。
entries.en: For the rest of his life he did not serve in office.
entries.literal: He never served in office for the rest of his life.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：余讀孟子書，至梁惠王問「何以利吾國」，未嘗不廢書而嘆也。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: I read the Book of Mengzi, and when I came to King Hui of Liang's question, 'By what means may my state be benefited?' I could never help but set down the book and sigh.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian said: I read the book of Mengzi; when I reached King Hui of Liang asking, 'By what means may my state be benefited?' I never failed to set down the book and sigh.

entries.zh: 曰：嗟乎，利誠亂之始也！
entries.en: He said, "Alas, profit truly is where disorder begins!"
entries.literal: He said: Alas, profit is truly the beginning of disorder!

entries.zh: 夫子罕言利者，常防其原也。
entries.en: The Master rarely spoke of profit because he was constantly on guard against its source.
entries.literal: Master rarely speak profit, constantly guard its source.

entries.zh: 故曰「放於利而行，多怨」。
entries.en: The saying goes: 'To act with profit as one's guide brings much resentment.'
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said, 'To act with profit as one's guide brings much resentment.'

entries.zh: 自天子至於庶人，好利之獘何以異哉！
entries.en: From the Son of Heaven down to commoners, what difference is there in the harm caused by love of profit?
entries.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, what difference is there in the harm of loving profit!

entries.zh: 孟嘗君名文，姓田氏。
entries.en: Lord Mengchang was Tian Wen of the Tian clan.
entries.literal: Lord Mengchang's name was Wen, and his surname was Tian.

entries.zh: 文之父曰靖郭君田嬰。
entries.en: Tian Wen's father was called Lord Jingguo, Tian Ying.
entries.literal: Wen's father was called Lord Jingguo, Tian Ying.

entries.zh: 田嬰者，齊威王少子而齊宣王庶弟也。
entries.en: Tian Ying was King Wei of Qi's youngest son and King Xuan of Qi's half-brother.
entries.literal: Tian Ying was Qi Wei King's youngest son and Qi Xuan King's younger half-brother.

entries.zh: 田嬰自威王時任職用事，與成侯鄒忌及田忌將而救韓伐魏。
entries.en: Tian Ying held office and managed affairs from King Wei's time onward. Together with Lord Cheng Zou Ji and the general Tian Ji, he rescued Han and attacked Wei.
entries.literal: Tian Ying from Wei King time hold office handle affairs, with Cheng Hou Zou Ji and Tian Ji general save Han attack Wei.

entries.zh: 成侯與田忌爭寵，成侯賣田忌。
entries.en: Lord Cheng contended with Tian Ji for favor, and Lord Cheng betrayed Tian Ji.
entries.literal: Cheng Hou with Tian Ji contend favor, Cheng Hou sell out Tian Ji.

entries.zh: 田忌懼，襲齊之邊邑，不勝，亡走。
entries.en: Tian Ji was afraid, attacked Qi's border cities, did not succeed, and fled.
entries.literal: Tian Ji fear, attack Qi border city, not win, flee go.

entries.zh: 會威王卒，宣王立，知成侯賣田忌，乃復召田忌以為將。
entries.en: When King Wei died and King Xuan ascended, King Xuan learned that Lord Cheng had betrayed Tian Ji, and summoned Tian Ji back to serve as general.
entries.literal: Meet Wei King die, Xuan King stand, know Cheng Hou sell out Tian Ji, then again summon Tian Ji as general.

entries.zh: 宣王二年，田忌與孫臏、田嬰俱伐魏，敗之馬陵，虜魏太子申而殺魏將龐涓。
entries.en: In King Xuan's second year, Tian Ji together with Sun Bin and Tian Ying attacked Wei, defeated them at Ma Ling, captured Wei's crown prince Shen, and killed Wei's general Pang Juan.
entries.literal: Xuan King two years, Tian Ji with Sun Bin, Tian Ying together attack Wei, defeat at Ma Ling, capture Wei crown prince Shen kill Wei general Pang Juan.

entries.zh: 宣王七年，田嬰使於韓、魏，韓、魏服於齊。
entries.en: In King Xuan's seventh year, Tian Ying was envoy to Han and Wei, and Han and Wei submitted to Qi.
entries.literal: Xuan King seven years, Tian Ying envoy to Han Wei, Han Wei submit to Qi.

entries.zh: 嬰與韓昭侯、魏惠王會齊宣王東阿南，盟而去。
entries.en: Ying, Marquis Zhao of Han, and King Hui of Wei met King Xuan of Qi south of Dong'e, formed an alliance, and departed.
entries.literal: Ying with Han Zhao Hou, Wei Hui King meet Qi Xuan King Dong E south, alliance depart.

entries.zh: 明年，復與梁惠王會甄。
entries.en: The next year, he again met King Hui of Liang at Zhen.
entries.literal: Next year, again with Liang Hui King meet Zhen.

entries.zh: 是歲，梁惠王卒。
entries.en: This year, King Hui of Liang died.
entries.literal: This year, Liang Hui King die.

entries.zh: 宣王九年，田嬰相齊。
entries.en: In King Xuan's ninth year, Tian Ying became chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: Xuan King nine years, Tian Ying chancellor Qi.

entries.zh: 齊宣王與魏襄王會徐州而相王也。
entries.en: King Xuan of Qi and King Xiang of Wei met at Xuzhou and mutually declared themselves kings.
entries.literal: Qi Xuan King with Wei Xiang King meet Xu Zhou mutually wang.

entries.zh: 楚威王聞之，怒田嬰。
entries.en: When King Wei of Chu heard this, he was angry with Tian Ying.
entries.literal: Chu Wei King hear, angry Tian Ying.

entries.zh: 明年，楚伐敗齊師於徐州，而使人逐田嬰。
entries.en: The next year, Chu attacked and defeated Qi forces at Xuzhou, and sent men to pursue Tian Ying.
entries.literal: Next year, Chu attack defeat Qi forces at Xu Zhou, make person pursue Tian Ying.

entries.zh: 田嬰使張丑說楚威王，威王乃止。
entries.en: Tian Ying sent Zhang Chou to persuade King Wei of Chu, and King Wei then stopped.
entries.literal: Tian Ying make Zhang Chou advise Chu Wei King, Wei King then stop.

entries.zh: 田嬰相齊十一年，宣王卒，湣王即位。
entries.en: Tian Ying served as chancellor of Qi for eleven years. King Xuan died, and King Min ascended the throne.
entries.literal: Tian Ying chancellor Qi eleven years, Xuan King die, Min King ascend throne.

entries.zh: 即位三年，而封田嬰於薛。
entries.en: After three years on the throne, he enfeoffed Tian Ying at Xue.
entries.literal: Ascend throne three years, enfeoff Tian Ying at Xue.

entries.zh: 初，田嬰有子四十餘人。
entries.en: Originally, Tian Ying had over forty sons.
entries.literal: Originally, Tian Ying have son forty more people.

entries.zh: 其賤妾有子名文，文以五月五日生。
entries.en: His lowly concubine bore a son named Tian Wen, and the child was born on the fifth day of the fifth month.
entries.literal: His lowly concubine have son name Wen, Wen with five month five day born.

entries.zh: 嬰告其母曰：「勿舉也。」
entries.en: Ying told the mother: 'Do not raise him.'
entries.literal: Ying tell his mother: Do not raise.

entries.zh: 其母竊舉生之。
entries.en: His mother secretly raised him.
entries.literal: His mother secretly raised him and kept him alive.

entries.zh: 及長，其母因兄弟而見其子文於田嬰。
entries.en: When he grew up, his mother used his brothers as an excuse to present her son Tian Wen to Tian Ying.
entries.literal: Reach grow, his mother because brothers see their son Wen to Tian Ying.

entries.zh: 田嬰怒其母曰：「吾令若去此子，而敢生之，何也？」
entries.en: Tian Ying angrily berated his mother: 'I commanded you to abandon this child, yet you dared to raise him. Why?'
entries.literal: Tian Ying angry at his mother: I commanded you to abandon this child, yet you dared to raise him; why?

entries.zh: 文頓首，因曰：「君所以不舉五月子者，何故？」
entries.en: Tian Wen kowtowed and said: 'My lord, why do you not raise children born in the fifth month?'
entries.literal: Wen kowtow, because say: Jun so not raise five month child, what reason?

entries.zh: 嬰曰：「五月子者，長與戶齊，將不利其父母。」
entries.en: Ying said: 'Children born in the fifth month grow up to be as tall as the door, which will bring harm to their parents.'
entries.literal: Ying say: Five month child, grow with door even, will harm parents.

entries.zh: 文曰：「人生受命於天乎？
entries.en: Tian Wen said: 'Does a person's life receive its mandate from Heaven?
entries.literal: Wen say: Person life receive mandate from heaven?

entries.zh: 將受命於戶邪？」
entries.en: Or does it receive its mandate from the door?'
entries.literal: Will receive mandate from door?"

entries.zh: 嬰默然。
entries.en: Ying fell silent.
entries.literal: Ying silent.

entries.zh: 文曰：「必受命於天，君何憂焉。
entries.en: Tian Wen said: 'If one's mandate comes from Heaven, what does my lord have to worry about?
entries.literal: Wen say: Must receive mandate from heaven, jun what worry.

entries.zh: 必受命於戶，則可高其戶耳，誰能至者！」
entries.en: If it comes from the door, then make the door higher. Who could ever reach it?'
entries.literal: Must receive mandate from door, then can high its door, who can reach!"

entries.zh: 嬰曰：「子休矣。」
entries.en: Ying said: 'Enough, my son.'
entries.literal: Ying say: Son rest.

entries.zh: 久之，文承閒問其父嬰曰：「子之子為何？」
entries.en: After a long time, Tian Wen took the opportunity to ask his father Ying: 'What is a son's son called?'
entries.literal: Long time, Wen take opportunity ask his father Ying: Son son what?

entries.zh: 曰：「為孫。」
entries.en: He said: 'A grandson.'
entries.literal: Say: For grandson.

entries.zh: 「孫之孫為何？」
entries.en: 'What is a grandson's grandson called?'
entries.literal: Grandson grandson what?

entries.zh: 曰：「為玄孫。」
entries.en: He said: 'A great-grandson.'
entries.literal: Say: For great grandson.

entries.zh: 「玄孫之孫為何？」
entries.en: 'What is a great-grandson's grandson called?'
entries.literal: Great grandson grandson what?

entries.zh: 曰：「不能知也。」
entries.en: He said: 'I cannot know.'
entries.literal: Say: Cannot know.

entries.zh: 文曰：「君用事相齊，至今三王矣，齊不加廣而君私家富累萬金，門下不見一賢者。
entries.en: Tian Wen said: 'My lord has handled Qi's affairs as chancellor through three reigns, yet Qi's territory has not expanded while your private household has accumulated wealth by the tens of thousands in gold, and not one worthy man is seen among your retainers.
entries.literal: Wen say: Jun handle affairs chancellor Qi, to now three kings, Qi not add broad yet jun private family rich accumulate ten thousand gold, gate below not see one worthy.

entries.zh: 文聞將門必有將，相門必有相。
entries.en: I have heard that a general's house must produce generals, and a chancellor's house must produce chancellors.
entries.literal: Wen hear will gate must have general, chancellor gate must have chancellor.

entries.zh: 今君後宮蹈綺縠而士不得（短）［裋］褐，仆妾餘粱肉而士不厭糟糠。
entries.en: Now the women of your inner palace tread on silk and gauze, while scholars cannot obtain coarse cloth; servants and concubines have fine grain and meat left over, while scholars cannot fill themselves on bran and chaff.
entries.literal: Now ruler rear palace step silk satin yet scholar not obtain coarse cloth, servant concubine remain fine grain meat yet scholar not satiated bran chaff.

entries.zh: 今君又尚厚積餘藏，欲以遺所不知何人，而忘公家之事日損，文竊怪之。」
entries.en: Now you still pile up surplus stores, intending to leave them to people whose identity you cannot even know, while the affairs of the public house decline day by day. I privately find this strange.'
entries.literal: Now ruler moreover still thick accumulate surplus store, wish leave to not know what person, forget public family affairs day damage, Wen secretly strange it."

entries.zh: 於是嬰乃禮文，使主家待賓客。
entries.en: Ying then treated Tian Wen with courtesy and had him manage the household to receive guests.
entries.literal: Ying then treated Wen with courtesy and made him manage the household to receive guests.

entries.zh: 賓客日進，名聲聞於諸侯。
entries.en: Guests came daily, and his reputation was heard among the feudal lords.
entries.literal: Guests day advance, name sound heard at feudal lords.

entries.zh: 諸侯皆使人請薛公田嬰以文為太子，嬰許之。
entries.en: All the feudal lords sent envoys asking Lord Xue, Tian Ying, to make Tian Wen his heir, and Ying agreed.
entries.literal: Feudal lords all make person request Xue Gong Tian Ying with Wen as crown prince, Ying permit.

entries.zh: 嬰卒，謚為靖郭君。
entries.en: Ying died and was posthumously named Lord Jingguo.
entries.literal: Ying die, posthumous name Jing Guo Jun.

entries.zh: 而文果代立於薛，是為孟嘗君。
entries.en: And Tian Wen indeed succeeded to the position at Xue, becoming Lord Mengchang.
entries.literal: Wen indeed succeed stand at Xue, is Meng Chang Jun.

entries.zh: 高祖始微少時，數聞公子賢。
entries.en: When Gaozu was still of humble and lowly station, he often heard that the prince was worthy.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was still humble and young, he often heard that the prince was worthy.

entries.zh: 及即天子位，每過大梁，常祠公子。
entries.en: When he ascended the imperial throne, whenever he passed through Daliang, he would always make offerings to the prince.
entries.literal: When he ascended the imperial throne, whenever he passed through Daliang, he would always offer sacrifices to the prince.

entries.zh: 高祖十二年，從擊黥布還，為公子置守冢五家，世世歲以四時奉祠公子。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Gaozu's reign, upon returning from the campaign against Qing Bu, he established five families to guard the prince's tomb, with each generation offering seasonal sacrifices to the prince year after year.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Gaozu's reign, upon returning from the campaign against Qing Bu, he established five families to tend the prince's tomb, with each generation offering seasonal sacrifices to the prince.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：吾過大梁之墟，求問其所謂夷門。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: I passed through the ruins of Daliang and asked about what was called the Yi Gate.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: I passed through the ruins of Daliang and inquired about what was called the Yi Gate.

entries.zh: 夷門者，城之東門也。
entries.en: The Yi Gate is the city's eastern gate.
entries.literal: The Yi Gate is the city's east gate.

entries.zh: 天下諸公子亦有喜士者矣，然信陵君之接巖穴隱者，不恥下交，有以也。
entries.en: Though other princes in the world also delight in worthy men, Lord Xinling's willingness to receive recluses from mountain caves and not disdain humble associations has its reasons.
entries.literal: Though the world's princes also have those who love scholars, Lord Xinling's reception of hermits from rocky caves, not ashamed to associate with inferiors, has good reason.

entries.zh: 名冠諸侯，不虛耳。
entries.en: His reputation stands above all the feudal lords—and justly so.
entries.literal: His name crowns the feudal lords, not in vain.

entries.zh: 高祖每過之而令民奉祠不絕也。
entries.en: Whenever Gaozu passed through the place, he ordered the people to keep up the sacrifices without interruption.
entries.literal: Whenever Gaozu passed through, he commanded the people to maintain the sacrifices without interruption.

entries.zh: 魏公子無忌者，魏昭王子少子而魏安釐王異母弟也。
entries.en: Lord Xinling Wuji was the youngest son of King Zhao of Wei and the half-brother of King Anli of Wei.
entries.literal: Lord Xinling Wuji was King Zhao of Wei's youngest son and King Anli's half-brother.

entries.zh: 昭王薨，安釐王即位，封公子為信陵君。
entries.en: When King Zhao died and King Anli ascended the throne, he enfeoffed the prince as Lord Xinling.
entries.literal: After King Zhao died, King Anli ascended the throne and enfeoffed the prince as Lord Xinling.

entries.zh: 是時范睢亡魏相秦，以怨魏齊故，秦兵圍大梁，破魏華陽下軍，走芒卯。
entries.en: At this time, Fan Sui had fled Wei to become Chancellor of Qin, driven by resentment toward Wei Qi. Qin forces besieged Daliang, crushed Wei's army at Huayang, and sent Mang Mao fleeing in defeat.
entries.literal: At this time, Fan Sui had fled from Wei to serve as Chancellor of Qin, bearing resentment toward Wei Qi. Qin troops besieged Daliang, defeated Wei's army at Huayang, and routed Mang Mao.

entries.zh: 魏王及公子患之。
entries.en: The King of Wei and the prince were both deeply troubled by this.
entries.literal: Both the King of Wei and the prince were deeply concerned.

entries.zh: 春申君相二十五年，楚考烈王病。
entries.en: Lord Chunshen had served as prime minister for twenty-five years when King Kaolie of Chu fell gravely ill.
entries.literal: Lord Chunshen served as prime minister for twenty-five years. King Kaolie of Chu fell ill.

entries.zh: 朱英謂春申君曰：「世有毋望之福，又有毋望之禍。
entries.en: Zhu Ying told Lord Chunshen, “In the world there are blessings that come unexpectedly, and disasters that come unexpectedly.
entries.literal: Zhu Ying told Lord Chunshen: 'The world has blessings that come without expectation, and disasters that come without expectation.

entries.zh: 今君處毋望之世，事毋望之主，安可以無毋望之人乎？」
entries.en: Your Lordship now lives in an age without prospects, serving a ruler without prospects. How can you be without a companion who shares your lack of prospects?'
entries.literal: Now Your Lordship lives in a time without expectations, serving a lord without expectations. How can you lack a person without expectations?'

entries.zh: 春申君曰：「何謂毋望之福？」
entries.en: Lord Chunshen said, “What are blessings that come unexpectedly?”
entries.literal: Lord Chunshen said: 'What are blessings without expectation?'

entries.zh: 曰：「君相楚二十餘年矣，雖名相國，實楚王也。
entries.en: “Your Lordship has been prime minister of Chu for more than twenty years. Though nominally prime minister, you are truly the king of Chu.
entries.literal: 'Your Lordship has been prime minister of Chu for over twenty years. Though nominally prime minister, you are truly the king of Chu.

entries.zh: 今楚王病，旦暮且卒，而君相少主，因而代立當國，如伊尹、周公，王長而反政，不即遂南面稱孤而有楚國？
entries.en: The King of Chu now lies ill and will die any day. Your Lordship aids the young ruler, seizes control of the government, and ascends the throne like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. When the king comes of age, you return power to him. If not, you proclaim yourself ruler facing south and take possession of the kingdom of Chu.
entries.literal: Now the King of Chu is ill, will die any day. Your Lordship assists the young ruler and takes over the state, ascending the throne like yiyin and the Duke of Zhou. When the king matures you return power. If not, you face south and proclaim yourself ruler, possessing Chu.

entries.zh: 此所謂毋望之福也。」
entries.en: This is what they call unexpected fortune.'
entries.literal: This is called blessing without expectation.'

entries.zh: 春申君曰：「何謂毋望之禍？」
entries.en: Lord Chunshen said: 'What is unexpected calamity?'
entries.literal: Lord Chunshen said: 'What is disaster without expectation?'

entries.zh: 曰：「李園不治國而君之仇也，不為兵而養死士之日久矣，楚王卒，李園必先入據權而殺君以滅口。
entries.en: 'Li Yuan cares nothing for governing the state, but he is Your Lordship's mortal enemy. Instead of raising armies, he has long been cultivating assassins. When the King of Chu dies, Li Yuan will surely enter first, seize control, and kill Your Lordship to silence the secret.
entries.literal: 'Li Yuan does not govern the state but is Your Lordship's enemy. Not raising troops but nurturing assassins for a long time. When the King of Chu dies, Li Yuan will certainly enter first, seize power and kill Your Lordship to silence him.

entries.zh: 此所謂毋望之禍也。」
entries.en: This is what they call unexpected disaster.'
entries.literal: This is called disaster without expectation.'

entries.zh: 春申君曰：「何謂毋望之人？」
entries.en: Lord Chunshen said: 'What is a companion without prospects?'
entries.literal: Lord Chunshen said: 'What is a person without expectation?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「君置臣郎中，楚王卒，李園必先入，臣為君殺李園。
entries.en: He replied: 'Appoint me as your aide-de-camp. When the King of Chu dies, Li Yuan will surely enter first. I will kill Li Yuan for you.
entries.literal: He replied: 'Appoint me as your attendant. When the King of Chu dies, Li Yuan will certainly enter first. I will kill Li Yuan for Your Lordship.

entries.zh: 此所謂毋望之人也。」
entries.en: This is what they call a companion without prospects.'
entries.literal: This is called a person without expectation.'

entries.zh: 春申君曰：「足下置之，李園，弱人也，仆又善之，且又何至此！」
entries.en: Lord Chunshen said: 'Set that aside for now. Li Yuan is a weakling, and I have treated him kindly. How could matters come to such a pass!'
entries.literal: Lord Chunshen said: 'Set that aside for now. Li Yuan is a weak man, and I have also treated him kindly. How could matters come to such a pass!'

entries.zh: 朱英知言不用，恐禍及身，乃亡去。
entries.en: Zhu Ying realized his advice would be ignored and feared the danger would extend to him, so he fled.
entries.literal: Zhu Ying knew his words would not be used and feared disaster would reach him, so he fled.

entries.zh: 春申君者，楚人也，名歇，姓黃氏。
entries.en: Lord Chunshen was a man of Chu, named Xie, of the Huang clan.
entries.literal: Lord Chunshen was a native of Chu, named Xie, of the Huang clan.

entries.zh: 游學博聞，事楚頃襄王。
entries.en: He traveled widely in his studies, became broadly learned, and served King Qingxiang of Chu.
entries.literal: He traveled widely in his studies and became broadly learned, serving King Qingxiang of Chu.

entries.zh: 頃襄王以歇為辯，使於秦。
entries.en: King Qingxiang valued Xie’s eloquence and sent him as an envoy to Qin.
entries.literal: King Qingxiang valued Xie's eloquence and sent him as envoy to Qin.

entries.zh: 秦昭王使白起攻韓、魏，敗之於華陽，禽魏將芒卯，韓、魏服而事秦。
entries.en: King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Han and Wei, defeating them at Huayang and capturing Wei's general Mang Mao. Han and Wei submitted and served Qin.
entries.literal: King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Han and Wei, defeating them at Huayang, capturing Wei's general Mang Mao. Han and Wei submitted and served Qin.

entries.zh: 秦昭王方令白起與韓、魏共伐楚，未行，而楚使黃歇適至於秦，聞秦之計。
entries.en: King Zhao of Qin was about to order Bai Qi to join forces with Han and Wei to attack Chu, but before the plan could be executed, Chu's envoy Huang Xie arrived in Qin and learned of Qin's strategy.
entries.literal: King Zhao of Qin was about to order Bai Qi to join with Han and Wei to attack Chu, but the plan had not yet been carried out when Chu's envoy Huang Xie arrived in Qin and learned of Qin's plans.

entries.zh: 當是之時，秦已前使白起攻楚，取巫、黔中之郡，拔鄢郢，東至竟陵，楚頃襄王東徙治於陳縣。
entries.en: At this time, Qin had already sent Bai Qi to attack Chu, taking the commanderies of Wu and Qianzhong, capturing Yan and Ying, and advancing east to Jingling. King Qingxiang of Chu moved his capital east to Chen county.
entries.literal: At this time, Qin had already sent Bai Qi to attack Chu earlier, taking the commanderies of Wu and Qianzhong, capturing Ying and Yiling, and advancing east to Jingling. King Qingxiang of Chu moved his capital east to Chen county.

entries.zh: 黃歇見楚懷王之為秦所誘而入朝，遂見欺，留死於秦。
entries.en: Huang Xie witnessed King Huai of Chu being lured by Qin into attending their court, only to be deceived, detained, and die in Qin.
entries.literal: Huang Xie saw that King Huai of Chu had been lured by Qin into attending their court, then deceived, detained, and died in Qin.

entries.zh: 頃襄王，其子也，秦輕之，恐壹舉兵而滅楚。
entries.en: King Qingxiang was his son. Qin held him in contempt and feared that with a single campaign they could destroy Chu entirely.
entries.literal: King Qingxiang was his son. Qin held him in low regard and feared that with one military campaign they could destroy Chu entirely.

entries.zh: 歇乃上書說秦昭王曰：
entries.en: Xie then submitted a memorial advising King Zhao of Qin:
entries.literal: Xie then presented a memorial advising King Zhao of Qin:

entries.zh: 其後二十餘年，高帝過趙，問：「樂毅有後世乎？」
entries.en: Thereafter, more than twenty years later, Gao Di passed through Zhao and asked: 'Does Yue Yi have descendants?'
entries.literal: Thereafter twenty plus years, Gao Di passed Zhao, asked: 'Yue Yi has descendants?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「有樂叔。」
entries.en: Replied: 'There is Yue Shu.'
entries.literal: Replied: 'Has Yue Shu.'

entries.zh: 高帝封之樂卿，號曰華成君。
entries.en: Gao Di enfeoffed him at Yueqing and titled him Lord Huacheng.
entries.literal: Gao Di enfeoffed him at Yueqing and titled him Lord Huacheng.

entries.zh: 華成君，樂毅之孫也。
entries.en: Lord Huacheng was Yue Yi's grandson.
entries.literal: Lord Huacheng was Yue Yi's grandson.

entries.zh: 而樂氏之族有樂瑕公、樂臣公，趙且為秦所滅，亡之齊高密。
entries.en: And the Yue clan had Yue Xiagong, Yue Chengong, Zhao was about to be extinguished by Qin, fled to Qi Gaomi.
entries.literal: Yue clan had Yue Xiagong, Yue Chengong, Zhao about to be extinguished by Qin, fled Qi Gaomi.

entries.zh: 樂臣公善修黃帝、老子之言，顯聞於齊，稱賢師。
entries.en: Yue Chengong was expert in the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi. He became well known in Qi and was regarded as a worthy teacher.
entries.literal: Yue Chengong was skilled at cultivating the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, became prominent and known in Qi, and was called a worthy teacher.

entries.zh: 樂毅者，其先祖曰樂羊。
entries.en: Yue Yi's ancestor was called Yue Yang.
entries.literal: Yue Yi, his ancestor called Yue Yang.

entries.zh: 樂羊為魏文侯將，伐取中山，魏文侯封樂羊以靈壽。
entries.en: Yue Yang was a general under Marquis Wen of Wei. After he attacked and captured Zhongshan, Marquis Wen enfeoffed him at Lingshou.
entries.literal: Yue Yang served as general for Marquis Wen of Wei, attacked and took Zhongshan, and Marquis Wen of Wei enfeoffed Yue Yang at Lingshou.

entries.zh: 樂羊死，葬於靈壽，其後子孫因家焉。
entries.en: Yue Yang died and was buried at Lingshou, and his descendants thereafter made their home there.
entries.literal: Yue Yang died, buried at Lingshou, his later descendants thus made home there.

entries.zh: 中山復國，至趙武靈王時復滅中山，而樂氏後有樂毅。
entries.en: Zhongshan was restored as a state, until Zhao Wu Ling Wang's time when Zhongshan was again extinguished, and the Yue clan later had Yue Yi.
entries.literal: Zhongshan restored state, to Zhao Wu Ling Wang time again extinguished Zhongshan, yet Yue clan later had Yue Yi.

entries.zh: 趙王遷七年，秦使王翦攻趙，趙使李牧、司馬尚御之。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Zhao King Qian, Qin sent Wang Jian to attack Zhao. Zhao sent Li Mu and Sima Shang to defend against him.
entries.literal: Zhao Wang Qian seventh year, Qin sent Wang Jian to attack Zhao; Zhao sent Li Mu and Sima Shang to defend against them.

entries.zh: 秦多與趙王寵臣郭開金，為反閒，言李牧、司馬尚欲反。
entries.en: Qin gave much gold to Zhao king's favorite minister Guo Kai to act as a reverse spy, claiming that Li Mu and Sima Shang wished to rebel.
entries.literal: Qin much gave Zhao king favorite minister Guo Kai gold, made reverse spies, said Li Mu, Sima Shang wished to rebel.

entries.zh: 趙王乃使趙蔥及齊將顏聚代李牧。
entries.en: The Zhao king then sent Zhao Cong and Qi general Yan Ju to replace Li Mu.
entries.literal: Zhao king then sent Zhao Cong and Qi general Yan Ju replaced Li Mu.

entries.zh: 李牧不受命，趙使人微捕得李牧，斬之。
entries.en: Li Mu refused the orders. Zhao sent people to secretly arrest and behead him.
entries.literal: Li Mu not accepted orders, Zhao sent people secretly arrested Li Mu, beheaded him.

entries.zh: 廢司馬尚。
entries.en: Sima Shang was dismissed.
entries.literal: Dismissed Sima Shang.

entries.zh: 後三月，王翦因急擊趙，大破殺趙蔥，虜趙王遷及其將顏聚，遂滅趙。
entries.en: Three months later, Wang Jian urgently attacked Zhao, routed and killed Zhao Cong, captured King Qian of Zhao and his general Yan Ju, thus destroying Zhao.
entries.literal: After three months, Wang Jian thus urgently attacked Zhao, greatly broke killed Zhao Cong, captured Zhao Wang Qian and his general Yan Ju, thus extinguished Zhao.

entries.zh: 廉頗者，趙之良將也。
entries.en: Lian Po was a distinguished general of Zhao.
entries.literal: Lian Po was a fine general of Zhao.

entries.zh: 趙惠文王十六年，廉頗為趙將伐齊，大破之，取陽晉，拜為上卿，以勇氣聞於諸侯。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year of King Huiwen of Zhao, Lian Po served as Zhao's general and attacked Qi. He routed them and took Yangjin, was appointed upper minister, and his bravery became renowned among the feudal lords.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of King Huiwen of Zhao, Lian Po served as Zhao's general and attacked Qi. He routed them and took Yangjin. He was appointed upper minister, and his bravery was renowned among the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 藺相如者，趙人也，為趙宦者令繆賢舍人。
entries.en: Lin Xiangru was a man of Zhao who served as retainer to Miao Xian, the eunuch director of Zhao.
entries.literal: Lin Xiangru was a man of Zhao and served as retainer to Miao Xian, the eunuch director of Zhao.

entries.zh: 且吾聞之，規小睗者不能成榮名，惡小恥者不能立大功。
entries.en: Furthermore, I have heard it said that those who scheme for petty gains cannot achieve a glorious name, and those who cannot endure small humiliations cannot accomplish great deeds.
entries.literal: Moreover, I heard, plan small advantages cannot achieve glorious name, hate small shame cannot establish great merit.

entries.zh: 昔者管夷吾射桓公中其鉤，篡也；
entries.en: In former times, Guan Zhong shot at Duke Huan and struck his belt hook—an act of rebellion.
entries.literal: Formerly Guan Yiwu shot Duke Huan hit his hook, usurpation;

entries.zh: 遺公子糾不能死，怯也；
entries.en: When Prince Jiu was killed, Guan Zhong failed to die alongside him—an act of cowardice.
entries.literal: Abandon Gongzi Jiu cannot die, cowardice;

entries.zh: 束縛桎梏，辱也。
entries.en: He was bound in fetters and shackles—an act of humiliation.
entries.literal: Bound fetters, humiliation.

entries.zh: 若此三行者，世主不臣而鄉里不通。
entries.en: With these three marks against him, no ruler in the world would have employed him, and no village would have associated with him.
entries.literal: Like this three actions, world rulers not employ village not communicate.

entries.zh: 鄉使管子幽囚而不出，身死而不反於齊，則亦名不免為辱人賤行矣。
entries.en: Had Guan Zhong remained in prison and never emerged, had he died there without returning to Qi, his name would never have escaped the stigma of a disgraced man of base conduct.
entries.literal: Suppose make Guan Zi imprisoned not exit, body die not return to Qi, then also name not avoid become humiliated person base conduct.

entries.zh: 臧獲且羞與之同名矣，況世俗乎！
entries.en: Even slaves would have been ashamed to be mentioned in the same breath as him, let alone ordinary people!
entries.literal: Slaves moreover ashamed share his name, moreover ordinary people!

entries.zh: 笔管子不恥身在縲紲之中而恥天下之不治，不恥不死公子糾而恥威之不信於諸侯，故兼三行之過而為五霸首，名高天下而光燭鄰國。
entries.en: But Guan Zhong felt no shame at being in chains—his shame was that the realm was not in order. He felt no shame at failing to die for Prince Jiu—his shame was that his lord's authority was not trusted by the feudal lords. And so, despite bearing the blame of all three transgressions, he rose to become foremost among the Five Hegemons, his name towering over the realm and his glory illuminating the neighboring states.
entries.literal: Guan Zi not ashamed body in prison chains yet ashamed world not orderly, not ashamed not die Gongzi Jiu yet ashamed prestige not trusted by feudal lords, therefore combined three actions faults became Five Hegemons first, name high world light illuminate neighboring states.

entries.zh: 曹子為魯將，三戰三北，而亡地五百里。
entries.en: Cao Mo served as a general of Lu and lost three battles in a row, surrendering five hundred li of territory.
entries.literal: Cao Zi as Lu general, three battles three defeats, yet lost land five hundred li.

entries.zh: 鄉使曹子計不反顧，議不還踵，刎頸而死，則亦名不免為敗軍禽將矣。
entries.en: Had Cao Mo refused to look back, declined to reconsider, and simply cut his own throat, his name would have been forever associated with a defeated army and a captured general.
entries.literal: Suppose make Cao Zi plan not look back, discussion not turn heel, cut throat die, then also name not avoid become defeated army captured general.

entries.zh: 曹子棄三北之恥，而退與魯君計。
entries.en: Instead, Cao Mo set aside the shame of three defeats and withdrew to plan with the lord of Lu.
entries.literal: Cao Zi abandoned three defeats shame, retreated with Lu lord plan.

entries.zh: 桓公朝天下，會諸侯，曹子以一劍之任，枝桓公之心於壇坫之上，顏色不變，辭氣不悖，三戰之所亡一朝而復之，天下震動，諸侯驚駭，威加吳、越。
entries.en: When Duke Huan summoned the lords of the realm to an assembly, Cao Mo advanced with only a dagger, pressing it against Duke Huan's chest upon the altar platform. His expression did not change, and his words did not falter. In a single morning he recovered all the territory lost in three battles. The realm was shaken, the feudal lords stood in awe, and his prestige reached as far as Wu and Yue.
entries.literal: Duke Huan assembled world, met feudal lords, Cao Zi with one sword duty, stabbed Duke Huan heart on altar steps above, color not change, speech not confused, three battles lost land one morning recover, world shake, feudal lords astonished, prestige reach Wu, Yue.

entries.zh: 若此二士者，非不能成小廉而行小睗也，以為殺身亡軀，絕世滅後，功名不立，非智也。
entries.en: These two men were not incapable of preserving petty honor or gaining small advantages, but they understood that to throw away one's life, cut off one's line, and leave no merit behind is not wisdom.
entries.literal: Like this two gentlemen, not cannot achieve small integrity perform small advantages, considered kill body lose form, cut descendants extinguish posterity, merit name not establish, not wise.

entries.zh: 故去感忿之怨，立終身之名；
entries.en: Therefore, they cast aside the resentment born of wounded pride and established names that would endure a lifetime.
entries.literal: Therefore, abandon resentful anger resentment, establish lifelong name;

entries.zh: 棄忿悁之節，定累世之功。
entries.en: They abandoned the stubborn integrity of rage and spite, and secured achievements that would last for generations.
entries.literal: Abandon angry spite integrity, determine generations merit.

entries.zh: 是以業與三王爭流，而名與天壤相獘也。
entries.en: And so their accomplishments vied with those of the Three Kings, and their fame endures as long as heaven and earth.
entries.literal: Therefore, enterprise with Three Kings contend flow, name with heaven earth equal.

entries.zh: 願公擇一而行之。
entries.en: I urge you to choose one and act upon it.
entries.literal: Wish you choose one carry out.

entries.zh: 臣聞明月之珠，夜光之璧，以闇投人於道路，人無不按劍相眄者。
entries.en: Your servant has heard this. If someone hurls a moon-bright pearl or a night-glowing jade disc at a man on the road in the dark, he will clap a hand to his sword and glare.
entries.literal: Minister heard bright moon pearls, night-lighting jade, in darkness throw to people on roads, people none not grip swords glare each other.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why is this?
entries.literal: Why then?

entries.zh: 無因而至前也。
entries.en: Because a treasure that arrives without explanation arouses suspicion.
entries.literal: Without cause come forward.

entries.zh: 蟠木根柢，輪囷離詭，而為萬乘器者。
entries.en: Yet gnarled wood with twisted roots and tangled grain can be fashioned into vessels fit for a king of ten thousand chariots.
entries.literal: Coiled wood roots base, twisted crooked strange, yet become ten thousand chariots vessels.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why is this?
entries.literal: Why then?

entries.zh: 以左右先為之容也。
entries.en: Because someone has already prepared a place for it and presented it properly.
entries.literal: Because attendants first make appearance for it.

entries.zh: 故無因至前，雖出隨侯之珠，夜光之璧，猶結怨而不見德。
entries.en: Thus, when something arrives without introduction, even if one produces the pearl of the Marquis of Sui or a jade disc that glows in the dark, it will still breed resentment rather than gratitude.
entries.literal: Therefore, without cause to front, though produce Sui Hou pearls, night-lighting jade, still harbor resentment not see virtue.

entries.zh: 故有人先談，則以枯木朽株樹功而不忘。
entries.en: But if someone speaks on one's behalf first, then even a withered log and a rotten stump can be used to build merit that will never be forgotten.
entries.literal: Therefore, if someone speaks first, then even withered wood rotten stump can establish merit not forgotten.

entries.zh: 今夫天下布衣窮居之士，身在貧賤，雖蒙堯、舜之術，挾伊、管之辯，懷龍逢、比干之意，欲盡忠當世之君，而素無根柢之容，雖竭精思，欲開忠信，輔人主之治，則人主必有按劍相眄之跡，是使布衣不得為枯木朽株之資也。
entries.en: Now consider the scholars of the realm who dwell in poverty and low estate. Though they may possess the arts of Yao and Shun, wield the eloquence of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, and harbor the devotion of Long Pang and Bi Gan, wishing to devote their utmost loyalty to the ruler of their age—yet lacking anyone to introduce them or vouch for their worth—no matter how they exhaust their minds and seek to offer their faithfulness, the ruler will inevitably greet them with a hand on his sword and a suspicious glare. This is what prevents men of humble birth from gaining even the advantage of the gnarled log and the rotten stump.
entries.literal: Now world commoners poor dwelling scholars, body in poverty lowliness, though have Yao Shun techniques, carry Yi Guan eloquence, harbor Long Peng Bi Gan intentions, wish exhaust loyalty serve current age lord, yet originally without root foundation appearance, though exhaust essence thought, wish open loyalty faithfulness, assist ruler governance, then ruler certainly has grip sword glare traces - this makes commoners unable become withered wood rotten stump resource.

entries.zh: 鄒陽者，齊人也。
entries.en: Zou Yang was a man of Qi.
entries.literal: Zou Yang, Qi person.

entries.zh: 游於梁，與故吳人莊忌夫子、淮陰枚生之徒交。
entries.en: He traveled to Liang, where he associated with Master Zhuang Ji, a former man of Wu, and Mei Sheng of Huaiyin, among others.
entries.literal: Traveled to Liang, with former Wu person Zhuang Ji Fuzi, Huaiyin Mei Sheng others associated.

entries.zh: 上書而介於羊勝、公孫詭之閒。
entries.en: He submitted memorials and found himself drawn into the circle of Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui.
entries.literal: Submitted writings introduced between Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui.

entries.zh: 勝等嫉鄒陽，惡之梁孝王。
entries.en: Yang Sheng and his associates grew envious of Zou Yang and slandered him before King Xiao of Liang.
entries.literal: Sheng etc. envied Zou Yang, slandered him to Liang Xiao Wang.

entries.zh: 孝王怒，下之吏，將欲殺之。
entries.en: King Xiao was furious and had Zou Yang turned over to the officials, intending to have him executed.
entries.literal: Xiao Wang angry, sent to officials, intended kill him.

entries.zh: 鄒陽客游，以讒見禽，恐死而負累，乃從獄中上書曰：
entries.en: Zou Yang, a traveling guest who had been imprisoned on account of slander, feared that his death would leave a burden of shame upon others. And so from prison he submitted a letter that read:
entries.literal: Zou Yang, a traveling guest, was seized on account of slander; fearing death and the burden of shame he would leave upon others, he submitted a letter from prison that read:

entries.zh: 臣聞忠無不報，信不見疑，臣常以為然，徒虛語耳。
entries.en: Your servant has heard it said that loyalty is always repaid and faithfulness is never doubted. I once believed this to be true, but now I see it was nothing but empty words.
entries.literal: Minister heard loyalty none not rewarded, faithfulness not seen doubted, minister often considered true, merely empty words.

entries.zh: 昔者荊軻慕燕丹之義，白虹貫日，太子畏之；
entries.en: In former times, Jing Ke so admired the righteousness of Crown Prince Dan of Yan that a white rainbow pierced the sun as an omen—yet the Crown Prince still harbored doubts about him.
entries.literal: Formerly Jing Ke admired Yan Dan righteousness, white rainbow pierced sun, crown prince feared him;

entries.zh: 衛先生為秦畫長平之事，太白蝕昴，而昭王疑之。
entries.en: Master Wei devised the strategy for the Battle of Changping on behalf of Qin, and Venus eclipsed the Pleiades as a celestial sign—yet King Zhao of Qin doubted him.
entries.literal: Wei mister for Qin planned Changping affair, Venus ate Pleiades, yet Zhao Wang doubted him.

entries.zh: 夫精變天地而信不喻兩主，豈不哀哉！
entries.en: Their sincerity was so profound that it moved heaven and earth, yet their faithfulness could not be understood by their own lords—how sorrowful this is!
entries.literal: That essence changed heaven earth yet faithfulness not understood two lords, how not sorrowful!

entries.zh: 今臣盡忠竭誠，畢議願知，左右不明，卒從吏訊，為世所疑，是使荊軻、衛先生復起，而燕、秦不悟也。
entries.en: Now your servant has exhausted his loyalty and poured out his sincerity, laying all his counsel before you, yet those around Your Majesty fail to understand. In the end I am subjected to interrogation by officials and doubted by the world. It is as though Jing Ke and Master Wei had risen from the dead, and yet Yan and Qin still remained blind.
entries.literal: Now your servant has exhausted loyalty and sincerity, fully expounded my views hoping you would understand, yet those around you do not see clearly; in the end I am subjected to interrogation by officials and doubted by the world—as though Jing Ke and Master Wei had risen again, yet Yan and Qin still did not awaken.

entries.zh: 願大王孰察之。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to examine the matter carefully.
entries.literal: Wish great king carefully examine it.

entries.zh: 昔卞和獻寶，楚王刖之；
entries.en: In ancient times, Bian He offered his precious jade, but the King of Chu had his feet cut off.
entries.literal: Formerly Bian He offered treasure, Chu Wang cut feet;

entries.zh: 李斯竭忠，胡亥極刑。
entries.en: Li Si devoted himself with utmost loyalty, yet Huhai subjected him to the cruelest punishment.
entries.literal: Li Si exhausted loyalty, Hu Hai extreme punishment.

entries.zh: 是以箕子詳狂，接輿辟世，恐遭此患也。
entries.en: This is why Jizi feigned madness and Jieyu withdrew from the world—they feared they would suffer such a fate.
entries.literal: Therefore, jizi feigned madness, Jie Yu avoided world, feared encounter this calamity.

entries.zh: 願大王孰察卞和、李斯之意，而後楚王、胡亥之聽，無使臣為箕子、接輿所笑。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to examine closely the true intentions of Bian He and Li Si, and not to listen as the King of Chu and Huhai did, lest your servant become an object of ridicule alongside Jizi and Jieyu.
entries.literal: Wish great king carefully examine Bian He, Li Si intentions, then not like Chu Wang, Hu Hai listen, not make minister become jizi, Jie Yu laughed at.

entries.zh: 臣聞比干剖心，子胥鴟夷，臣始不信，乃今知之。
entries.en: Your servant had heard that Bi Gan's heart was cut open and that Wu Zixu's body was sewn into a leather sack. I did not believe such things at first, but now I know they can happen.
entries.literal: Minister heard Bi Gan heart cut, Zi Xu leather sack, minister initially not believe, now know it.

entries.zh: 願大王孰察，少加憐焉。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to examine the truth carefully and show a measure of mercy.
entries.literal: Wish great king carefully examine, little add pity.

entries.zh: 故女無美惡，入宮見妒；
entries.en: Thus, it is that women, regardless of beauty, are envied the moment they enter the palace.
entries.literal: Therefore, women no beauty ugliness, enter palace seen envy;

entries.zh: 士無賢不肖，入朝見嫉。
entries.en: And scholars, regardless of merit, are resented the moment they enter the court.
entries.literal: Scholars no worthy unworthy, enter court seen jealousy.

entries.zh: 昔者司馬喜髕腳於宋，卒相中山；
entries.en: In ancient times, Sima Xi had his kneecaps shattered in Song, yet he went on to become chancellor of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Formerly Sima Xi kneecap broken in Song, finally chancellor Zhongshan;

entries.zh: 范睢摺脅折齒於魏，卒為應侯。
entries.en: Fan Sui suffered cracked ribs and broken teeth in Wei, but ultimately became the Marquis of Ying.
entries.literal: Fan Sui ribs broken teeth knocked in Wei, finally became Marquis Ying.

entries.zh: 此二人者，皆信必然之畫，捐朋黨之私，挾孤獨之位，故不能自免於嫉妒之人也。
entries.en: Both of these men trusted in plans they knew to be right, abandoned the private interests of factions, and held themselves apart in isolated positions—and for this reason they could not escape the malice of the envious.
entries.literal: These two people, all trusted inevitable plans, abandoned faction private interests, held isolated positions, therefore could not avoid jealous people.

entries.zh: 是以申徒狄自沈於河，徐衍負石入海。
entries.en: This is why Shentu Di drowned himself in the river and Xu Yan walked into the sea bearing a stone.
entries.literal: Therefore, Shentu Di self drowned in river, Xu Yan carried stone entered sea.

entries.zh: 不容於世，義不茍取，比周於朝，以移主上之心。
entries.en: They could not be tolerated by the world because they would not compromise their principles by forming cliques at court to sway their sovereign's heart.
entries.literal: Not tolerated by world, righteousness not casual take, allied in court to shift lord heart.

entries.zh: 故百里奚乞食於路，繆公委之以政；
entries.en: Baili Xi once begged for food by the roadside, yet Duke Mu of Qin entrusted him with the government.
entries.literal: Therefore, Baili Xi begged food on road, Duke Mu entrusted government;

entries.zh: 甯戚飯牛車下，而桓公任之以國。
entries.en: Ning Qi fed oxen beneath a cart, yet Duke Huan of Qi entrusted him with the affairs of state.
entries.literal: Ning Qi fed oxen cart under, yet Duke Huan entrusted state.

entries.zh: 此二人者，豈借宦於朝，假譽於左右，然後二主用之哉？
entries.en: Did these two men first borrow an office at court or a reputation from the attendants before their lords employed them?
entries.literal: These two, how borrowed office in court, borrowed reputation from attendants, then two lords used them?

entries.zh: 感於心，合於行，親於膠漆，昆弟不能離，豈惑於眾口哉？
entries.en: Their hearts were moved, their conduct aligned; they were bound closer than glue and lacquer, inseparable even by brothers—how could the clamor of the crowd have confused them?
entries.literal: Moved in heart, matched in conduct, close as glue varnish, brothers cannot separate, how confused by crowd mouths?

entries.zh: 故偏聽生姦，獨任成亂。
entries.en: Therefore, listening to only one side breeds treachery, and relying on a single counselor invites chaos.
entries.literal: Therefore, partial listening produces evil, sole reliance creates chaos.

entries.zh: 昔者魯聽季孫之說而逐孔子，宋信子罕之計而囚墨翟。
entries.en: In former times, Lu heeded the words of the Jisun clan and drove out Confucius; Song trusted the schemes of Zi Han and imprisoned Mozi.
entries.literal: Formerly Lu listened Ji Sun words drove Confucius, Song trusted Zi Han plans imprisoned Mo Di.

entries.zh: 夫以孔、墨之辯，不能自免於讒諛，而二國以危。
entries.en: Even with the eloquence of Confucius and Mozi, they could not save themselves from slander and flattery, and both states were brought to the brink of ruin.
entries.literal: That with Confucius, Mo Di eloquence, could not self avoid slander flattery, yet two states endangered.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why was this?
entries.literal: Why then?

entries.zh: 眾口鑠金，積毀銷骨也。
entries.en: Because the mouths of the many can melt gold, and accumulated slander can grind bones to dust.
entries.literal: Crowd mouths melt gold, accumulated slander destroys bone.

entries.zh: 是以秦用戎人由余而霸中國，齊用越人蒙而彊威、宣。
entries.en: This is why Qin employed You Yu, a man of the Rong, and achieved hegemony over the Central States; and Qi employed Meng, a man of Yue, and strengthened itself during the reigns of kings Wei and Xuan.
entries.literal: Therefore, Qin used Rong man You Yu hegemonized central states, Qi used Yue man Meng strengthened Wei, Xuan.

entries.zh: 此二國，豈拘於俗，牽於世，系阿偏之辭哉？
entries.en: Were these two states shackled by convention, swayed by popular opinion, or bound by the words of flatterers?
entries.literal: These two states, how constrained by custom, pulled by world, bound by partial words?

entries.zh: 公聽并觀，垂名當世。
entries.en: They listened broadly and observed impartially, and thus bequeathed their names to posterity.
entries.literal: Public listening parallel viewing, bequeathed names current age.

entries.zh: 故意合則胡越為昆弟，由余、越人蒙是矣；
entries.en: Thus, when minds are in accord, even the Hu and the Yue become brothers—as the cases of You Yu and Meng of Yue attest.
entries.literal: Therefore, when intentions match then Hu Yue become brothers, You Yu, Yue Meng are examples;

entries.zh: 不合，則骨肉出逐不收，朱、象、管、蔡是矣。
entries.en: But when minds are at odds, even flesh and blood are cast out and never recalled—as the cases of Zhu, Xiang, Guan, and Cai demonstrate.
entries.literal: Not match, then bone flesh driven out not recalled, Zhu, Xiang, Guan, Cai are examples.

entries.zh: 今人主誠能用齊、秦之義，後宋、魯之聽，則五伯不足稱，三王易為也。
entries.en: If a ruler today could truly follow the example of Qi and Qin while avoiding the mistakes of Song and Lu, then surpassing the Five Hegemons would be trivial, and matching the Three Kings would be within easy reach.
entries.literal: Now rulers truly can use Qi, Qin righteousness, avoid Song, Lu listening, then Five Hegemons insufficient name, Three Kings easy become.

entries.zh: 臣聞盛飾入朝者不以利汙義，砥厲名號者不以欲傷行，故縣名勝母而曾子不入，邑號朝歌而墨子回車。
entries.en: Your servant has heard that those who enter court in splendid attire do not let profit stain their righteousness, and those who sharpen their reputations do not let desire corrupt their conduct. This is why Zengzi refused to enter a county called Shengmu, and Mozi turned his chariot away from a town named Zhaoge.
entries.literal: Minister heard splendid adorned enter court not use profit soil righteousness, sharpen hone name reputation not use desire injure conduct, therefore county named Sheng Mu yet Zeng Zi not enter, town named Zhao Ge yet Mo Zi turned cart.

entries.zh: 今欲使天下寥廓之士，攝於威重之權，主於位勢之貴，故回面汙行以事諂諛之人而求親近於左右，則士伏死堀穴巖（巖）［藪］之中耳，安肯有盡忠信而趨闕下者哉！
entries.en: If you now force the broad-minded scholars of the realm to cower before the weight of authority, to grovel before the prestige of rank, and to soil their reputations serving flatterers in hopes of gaining access to the inner circle—then the true scholars will sooner hide themselves away and die in caves and rocky marshes than ever come to the palace gates to offer their loyal service!
entries.literal: Now wish make world broad scholars, restrained by awe-inspiring authority power, lorded by position status nobility, therefore turn face soil conduct serve flattering people seek close to attendants, then scholars hide die in burrows holes rocks swamps, how willing have exhaust loyalty faithfulness hurry palace gates!

entries.zh: 書奏梁孝王，孝王使人出之，卒為上客。
entries.en: When the letter was submitted to King Xiao of Liang, the king sent men to release Zou Yang from prison, and in the end made him an honored guest.
entries.literal: Letter submitted Liang Xiao Wang, Xiao Wang sent people release him, finally became honored guest.

entries.zh: 魯仲連者，齊人也。
entries.en: Lu Zhonglian was a man of Qi.
entries.literal: Lu Zhonglian was Qi person.

entries.zh: 好奇偉俶儻之畫策，而不肯仕宦任職，好持高節。
entries.en: He delighted in extraordinary and unconventional stratagems, yet refused to serve in office or hold any official post, preferring to uphold his lofty principles.
entries.literal: Loved grand extraordinary outstanding strategies, yet not willing serve in office hold position, liked maintain high integrity.

entries.zh: 游於趙。
entries.en: He traveled to the state of Zhao.
entries.literal: Traveled in Zhao.

entries.zh: 屈平疾王聽之不聰也，讒諂之蔽明也，邪曲之害公也，方正之不容也，故憂愁幽思而作離騷。
entries.en: Qu Ping was pained that the king's judgment was so easily clouded, that slander and flattery obscured his wisdom, that the crooked and corrupt harmed the public good, and that the upright found no place at court. And so, in deep sorrow and brooding anguish, he composed the 'Encountering Sorrow.'
entries.literal: Qu Ping grieved king listening not wise, slander flattery blocked clarity, crooked harmed justice, upright not tolerated, therefore worried sorrowful deep thought composed Li Sao.

entries.zh: 離騷者，猶離憂也。
entries.en: The title 'Encountering Sorrow' means, in essence, parting from sorrow.
entries.literal: 'Li Sao' is like 'li you' (parting from sorrow).

entries.zh: 夫天者，人之始也；
entries.en: Heaven is the origin of all people;
entries.literal: That heaven, people beginning;

entries.zh: 父母者，人之本也。
entries.en: Parents are the root of every person.
entries.literal: Parents, people root.

entries.zh: 人窮則反本，故勞苦倦極，未嘗不呼天也；
entries.en: When people are driven to extremity, they return to their roots. Thus, in the depths of toil and exhaustion, they never fail to cry out to Heaven;
entries.literal: People poor then return to roots, therefore labor toil exhausted extreme, never not call heaven;

entries.zh: 疾痛慘怛，未嘗不呼父母也。
entries.en: In the anguish of sickness and suffering, they never fail to call out to their parents.
entries.literal: Illness pain bitter sorrow, never not call parents.

entries.zh: 屈平正道直行，竭忠盡智以事其君，讒人閒之，可謂窮矣。
entries.en: Qu Ping walked the straight path and acted with integrity, exhausting his loyalty and wisdom in service to his lord, yet slanderers drove a wedge between them. One may truly say he was driven to the uttermost extremity.
entries.literal: Qu Ping correct path straight conduct, exhausted loyalty wisdom to serve his lord, slanderers separated them, can be called poor indeed.

entries.zh: 信而見疑，忠而被謗，能無怨乎？
entries.en: To be trusted yet met with suspicion, to be loyal yet slandered — how could he not feel resentment?
entries.literal: Faithful yet seen suspicious, loyal yet slandered, can have no resentment?

entries.zh: 屈平之作離騷，蓋自怨生也。
entries.en: Qu Ping's composition of the 'Encountering Sorrow' was born from just such resentment.
entries.literal: Qu Ping's composing Li Sao was probably born from resentment.

entries.zh: 國風好色而不淫，小雅怨誹而不亂。
entries.en: The 'Airs of the States' delights in beauty without becoming licentious; the 'Lesser Odes' expresses resentment without descending into disorder.
entries.literal: Guo Feng loves beauty not licentious, Xiao Ya resents criticizes not chaotic.

entries.zh: 若離騷者，可謂兼之矣。
entries.en: The 'Encountering Sorrow' may be said to unite both these virtues.
entries.literal: As for Li Sao, can be said combines them.

entries.zh: 上稱帝嚳，下道齊桓，中述湯武，以刺世事。
entries.en: It invokes Emperor Ku in the remote past, speaks of Duke Huan of Qi in recent times, and recounts the deeds of Tang and Wu in between — all to cast light on the affairs of the present age.
entries.literal: Above mentions Emperor Ku, below speaks Duke Huan, middle describes Tang Wu, to criticize current affairs.

entries.zh: 明道德之廣崇，治亂之條貫，靡不畢見。
entries.en: It illuminates the breadth and grandeur of moral virtue and the patterns underlying order and chaos, leaving nothing unexamined.
entries.literal: Clarifies morality broad elevation, governance chaos systematic order, nothing not completely seen.

entries.zh: 其文約，其辭微，其志絜，其行廉，其稱文小而其指極大，舉類邇而見義遠。
entries.en: Its language is concise, its diction subtle, its aspirations pure, its conduct unblemished. Its allusions may seem trifling, but their significance is vast; the examples it draws upon are near at hand, yet the principles they illuminate reach far.
entries.literal: Its text concise, its words subtle, its will pure, its conduct clean, its references small yet its meaning extremely great, cites nearby examples yet sees far justice.

entries.zh: 其志絜，故其稱物芳。
entries.en: Because its aspirations are pure, it speaks of fragrant things.
entries.literal: Its will pure, therefore its named things fragrant.

entries.zh: 其行廉，故死而不容自疏。
entries.en: Because its conduct is unblemished, he would sooner die than allow himself to be estranged from virtue.
entries.literal: Its conduct clean, therefore died not allowing self distant.

entries.zh: 濯淖汙泥之中，蟬蛻於濁穢，以浮游塵埃之外，不獲世之滋垢，皭然泥而不滓者也。
entries.en: He cleansed himself amid the mire and filth, shed his skin like a cicada leaving behind corruption, and floated free beyond the dust of the world. He refused to let the grime of his age stain him — a man who passed through the mud yet emerged without a blemish.
entries.literal: Washed mud filth midst, cicada molted foulness, to float roam dust outside, not obtaining world accumulated filth, pure unstained mud not dregs.

entries.zh: 推此志也，雖與日月爭光可也。
entries.en: Judging by such resolve, one may say that his brilliance could rival even the sun and moon.
entries.literal: Pushing this ambition, even with sun moon contend light possible.

entries.zh: 屈平既絀，其後秦欲伐齊，齊與楚從親，惠王患之，乃令張儀詳去秦，厚幣委質事楚，曰：「秦甚憎齊，齊與楚從親，楚誠能絕齊，秦願獻商、於之地六百里。」
entries.en: After Qu Ping had been dismissed, Qin wished to attack Qi. Since Qi and Chu had formed a close alliance, King Hui of Qin grew alarmed. He dispatched Zhang Yi, who feigned departure from Qin's service and arrived in Chu bearing lavish gifts, pledging himself as a vassal. Zhang Yi told the king of Chu: 'Qin despises Qi, and Qi has allied itself closely with Chu. If Chu would truly sever its ties with Qi, Qin is willing to cede six hundred li of the Shang and Yu territories.'
entries.literal: Qu Ping already dismissed, after this Qin wished attack Qi, Qi with Chu allied closely, Hui Wang worried it, then had Zhang Yi pretend leave Qin, thick gifts humble serve Chu, said: 'Qin greatly hates Qi, Qi with Chu allied closely. Chu truly can break Qi, Qin wishes offer Shang Yu lands 600 li.'

entries.zh: 楚懷王貪而信張儀，遂絕齊，使使如秦受地。
entries.en: King Huai of Chu, blinded by greed, believed Zhang Yi. He severed relations with Qi and sent an envoy to Qin to claim the promised territory.
entries.literal: Chu Huai Wang greedy believed Zhang Yi, thus broke Qi, sent envoy to Qin receive land.

entries.zh: 張儀詐之曰：「儀與王約六里，不聞六百里。」
entries.en: Zhang Yi deceived them, saying: 'I agreed with the king on six li. I never heard anything about six hundred.'
entries.literal: Zhang Yi deceived them said: 'Yi with king agreed six li, not heard six hundred li.'

entries.zh: 楚使怒去，歸告懷王。
entries.en: The Chu envoy departed in fury and returned to report to King Huai.
entries.literal: Chu envoy angered left, returned told Huai Wang.

entries.zh: 懷王怒，大興師伐秦。
entries.en: King Huai was enraged and raised a great army to attack Qin.
entries.literal: Huai Wang angered, greatly raised troops attacked Qin.

entries.zh: 秦發兵擊之，大破楚師於丹、淅，斬首八萬，虜楚將屈丐，遂取楚之漢中地。
entries.en: Qin sent its forces to meet them and dealt a crushing defeat to the Chu army at Dan and Xi, beheading eighty thousand soldiers and capturing the Chu general Qu Gai. Qin then seized the Hanzhong territories of Chu.
entries.literal: Qin sent troops struck them, greatly defeated Chu army at Dan Xi, beheaded eighty thousand, captured Chu general Qu Gai, thus took Chu Hanzhong land.

entries.zh: 懷王乃悉發國中兵以深入擊秦，戰於藍田。
entries.en: King Huai then mobilized every soldier in the realm for a deep thrust into Qin, and the two sides clashed at Lantian.
entries.literal: Huai Wang then sent all state troops to deeply attack Qin, battled at Lantian.

entries.zh: 魏聞之，襲楚至鄧。
entries.en: Wei, learning of this, launched a surprise attack on Chu and advanced as far as Deng.
entries.literal: Wei heard it, attacked Chu to Deng.

entries.zh: 楚兵懼，自秦歸。
entries.en: The Chu forces grew fearful and withdrew from Qin.
entries.literal: Chu troops feared, from Qin returned.

entries.zh: 而齊竟怒不救楚，楚大困。
entries.en: Qi, still furious at Chu's betrayal, refused to come to its aid, and Chu was left in dire straits.
entries.literal: And Qi finally angered not rescued Chu, Chu greatly distressed.

entries.zh: 明年，秦割漢中地與楚以和。
entries.en: The following year, Qin offered to cede the Hanzhong territory to Chu in exchange for peace.
entries.literal: Next year, Qin ceded Hanzhong land to Chu for peace.

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「不願得地，願得張儀而甘心焉。」
entries.en: The king of Chu declared: 'I do not want the land. I want Zhang Yi — only then will my heart be satisfied.'
entries.literal: Chu Wang said: 'Not wish get land, wish get Zhang Yi satisfy hatred.'

entries.zh: 張儀聞，乃曰：「以一儀而當漢中地，臣請往如楚。」
entries.en: When Zhang Yi heard this, he said: 'If one Zhang Yi is worth the Hanzhong territory, then let me go to Chu.'
entries.literal: Zhang Yi heard, then said: 'With one Zhang Yi match Hanzhong land, minister requests go to Chu.'

entries.zh: 如楚，又因厚幣用事者臣靳尚，而設詭辯於懷王之寵姬鄭袖。
entries.en: He went to Chu and bribed the powerful minister Jin Shang with lavish gifts, then contrived through cunning arguments to win over King Huai's favored consort, Zheng Xiu.
entries.literal: Went to Chu, moreover used thick gifts influential minister Jin Shang, set up deceptive arguments with Huai Wang favored concubine Zheng Xiu.

entries.zh: 懷王竟聽鄭袖，復釋去張儀。
entries.en: In the end, King Huai heeded Zheng Xiu and released Zhang Yi once again.
entries.literal: Huai Wang finally listened Zheng Xiu, again released Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 是時屈平既疏，不復在位，使於齊，顧反，諫懷王曰：「何不殺張儀？」
entries.en: At that time, Qu Ping had already been estranged and was no longer in office. He had been sent on a mission to Qi, and upon his return, he remonstrated with King Huai: 'Why not execute Zhang Yi?'
entries.literal: This time Qu Ping already alienated, no longer in position, sent to Qi; upon returning, advised Huai Wang said: 'Why not kill Zhang Yi?'

entries.zh: 懷王悔，追張儀不及。
entries.en: King Huai was filled with regret and sent men to pursue Zhang Yi, but they could not catch him.
entries.literal: Huai Wang regretted, pursued Zhang Yi could not catch.

entries.zh: 屈平既嫉之，雖放流，睠顧楚國，系心懷王，不忘欲反，冀幸君之一悟，俗之一改也。
entries.en: Qu Ping loathed Zi Lan. Though banished, he remained devoted to the state of Chu. His heart was bound to King Huai, and he never ceased longing for his return to court, hoping that the king might one day awaken to the truth and that the corruption of the age might be reformed.
entries.literal: Qu Ping already hated him, though banished, fondly regarded Chu state, tied heart Huai Wang, not forget wished return, hoped king one awakening, customs one change.

entries.zh: 其存君興國而欲反覆之，一篇之中三致志焉。
entries.en: His desire to preserve his lord and restore the state, to reverse its decline — this resolve is expressed three times within a single poem.
entries.literal: His preserve lord revive country wish reverse it, one chapter three times expressed will.

entries.zh: 然終無可柰何，故不可以反，卒以此見懷王之終不悟也。
entries.en: Yet in the end, nothing could be done. He could not return to court, and so he came to see at last that King Huai would never awaken.
entries.literal: Yet finally nothing could be done, therefore could not return, finally thus saw Huai Wang final lack of awakening.

entries.zh: 人君無愚智賢不肖，莫不欲求忠以自為，舉賢以自佐，然亡國破家相隨屬，而聖君治國累世而不見者，其所謂忠者不忠，而所謂賢者不賢也。
entries.en: Every ruler, whether foolish or wise, worthy or unworthy, wishes to find loyal ministers to serve him and to elevate the worthy to assist him. Yet states collapse and families are ruined in unbroken succession, while sage rulers who bring lasting order are not seen for generations on end. This is because those they called loyal were not truly loyal, and those they called worthy were not truly worthy.
entries.literal: Rulers regardless foolish wise worthy unworthy, none not wish seek loyal for themselves, raise worthy assist themselves, yet ruined states broken families follow succession, yet sage kings govern states generations not appear - what they called loyal not loyal, what they called worthy not worthy.

entries.zh: 懷王以不知忠臣之分，故內惑於鄭袖，外欺於張儀，疏屈平而信上官大夫、令尹子蘭。
entries.en: Because King Huai could not distinguish a loyal minister from a false one, he was beguiled within by Zheng Xiu and deceived without by Zhang Yi. He cast aside Qu Ping and placed his trust in Grand Master Shangguan and the Prime Minister Zi Lan.
entries.literal: Huai Wang because not know loyal ministers distinction, therefore internally confused by Zheng Xiu, externally deceived by Zhang Yi, alienated Qu Ping trusted Chamberlain Shangguan, Prime Minister Zi Lan.

entries.zh: 兵挫地削，亡其六郡，身客死於秦，為天下笑。
entries.en: His armies were routed, his territory stripped away, and six commanderies were lost. He himself died a captive in Qin, and became a laughingstock to all under Heaven.
entries.literal: Army defeated land reduced, lost six commanderies, body died as guest in Qin, became world laughingstock.

entries.zh: 此不知人之禍也。
entries.en: Such is the calamity of failing to know men.
entries.literal: This not know people calamity.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「井泄不食，為我心惻，可以汲。
entries.en: The Book of Changes says: 'The well seeps but none drink from it — this grieves my heart. Yet water may still be drawn.
entries.literal: The 'Yi' says: 'The well is cleared yet none drink from it — this grieves my heart; water may still be drawn.

entries.zh: 王明，并受其福。」
entries.en: When the king is wise, all share in his blessings.'
entries.literal: King enlightened, all receive its blessing.'

entries.zh: 王之不明，豈足福哉！
entries.en: But when the king lacks wisdom, how can there be any blessing at all!
entries.literal: King lack of enlightenment, how sufficient blessing!

entries.zh: 賈生以為漢興至孝文二十餘年，天下和洽，而固當改正朔，易服色，法制度，定官名，興禮樂，乃悉草具其事儀法，色尚黃，數用五，為官名，悉更秦之法。
entries.en: Jia Sheng believed that more than twenty years had passed since the founding of the Han, and that the realm was now at peace. It was therefore time to reform the calendar, change the ritual colors, revise the laws and institutions, establish proper official titles, and promote the rites and music. He drafted a comprehensive plan for all of these measures, proposing yellow as the dynastic color, the number five as the governing numeral, and new official titles — entirely replacing the old Qin system.
entries.literal: Jia Sheng thought Han rise to Filial Wen twenty plus years, world peaceful harmonious, should change calendar, change colors, establish laws systems, fix official names, promote rites music, then completely drafted all matters ceremonies laws, color esteem yellow, number use five, for official names, completely changed Qin laws.

entries.zh: 孝文帝初即位，謙讓未遑也。
entries.en: Emperor Wen had only recently ascended the throne and, out of modesty and restraint, had not yet found the occasion to act.
entries.literal: Filial Wen Emperor initially ascended, modest yielding not leisure.

entries.zh: 諸律令所更定，及列侯悉就國，其說皆自賈生發之。
entries.en: The various reforms to the statutes and ordinances, as well as the policy of sending all the marquises to their fiefdoms, all originated from Jia Sheng's proposals.
entries.literal: Various statutes orders what changed fixed, and marquises all go to states, these theories all from Jia Sheng originated.

entries.zh: 於是天子議以為賈生任公卿之位。
entries.en: The emperor then considered promoting Jia Sheng to the rank of one of the great ministers of state.
entries.literal: Then emperor discussed make Jia Sheng assume duke ministers position.

entries.zh: 絳、灌、東陽侯、馮敬之屬盡害之，乃短賈生曰：「雒陽之人，年少初學，專欲擅權，紛亂諸事。」
entries.en: But the Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying, the Marquis of Dongyang, Feng Jing, and others all opposed him. They slandered Jia Sheng, saying: 'This man from Luoyang is young and has barely begun his studies, yet he seeks to monopolize power and throw everything into confusion.'
entries.literal: Jiang, Guan, Dongyang Hou, Feng Jing and others all harmed him, then slandered Jia Sheng said: 'Luoyang person, young just studied, monopolize want seize power, confuse various matters.'

entries.zh: 於是天子後亦疏之，不用其議，乃以賈生為長沙王太傅。
entries.en: The emperor afterward also distanced himself from Jia Sheng and ceased to follow his counsel. He appointed Jia Sheng as Grand Tutor to the King of Changsha.
entries.literal: Then emperor afterward also distanced him, not used his proposals, then made Jia Sheng Changsha King Taifu.

entries.zh: 賈生名誼，雒陽人也。
entries.en: Jia Sheng, whose given name was Yi, was a native of Luoyang.
entries.literal: Jia Sheng named Yi, Luoyang person.

entries.zh: 年十八，以能誦詩屬書聞於郡中。
entries.en: By the age of eighteen, he was renowned throughout his commandery for his ability to recite the Odes and compose fine prose.
entries.literal: Age eighteen, able recite poetry compose writings famous in commandery.

entries.zh: 吳廷尉為河南守，聞其秀才，召置門下，甚幸愛。
entries.en: Wu, the Commandant of Justice, was serving as Governor of Henan. When he heard of Jia Yi's talent, he summoned him into his household and treated him with great favor and affection.
entries.literal: Wu the Commandant of Justice as Henan governor, heard his talent, summoned placed under his patronage, greatly favored and cherished.

entries.zh: 孝文皇帝初立，聞河南守吳公治平為天下第一，故與李斯同邑而常學事焉，乃徵為廷尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen first ascended the throne, he heard that Wu Gong, the Governor of Henan, governed so well that he was reckoned the finest administrator in the realm. Wu Gong had come from the same town as Li Si and had often studied under him. The emperor summoned Wu Gong to serve as Commandant of Justice.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Han first ascended throne, heard Henan governor Wu Gong governed peacefully ranked first under heaven, formerly from same town as Li Si and often studied under him, then summoned as Commandant of Justice.

entries.zh: 廷尉乃言賈生年少，頗通諸子百家之書。
entries.en: The Commandant of Justice then spoke of Jia Sheng, saying that though he was young, he was deeply versed in the writings of the various philosophers and the Hundred Schools of thought.
entries.literal: The Commandant of Justice then spoke of Jia Sheng, young, quite versed in the writings of the various philosophers and the Hundred Schools.

entries.zh: 文帝召以為博士。
entries.en: Emperor Wen summoned him and appointed him as an Erudite.
entries.literal: Wen Emperor summoned as erudite.

entries.zh: 萬物變化兮，固無休息。
entries.en: The myriad things are ever-changing — there is never any rest.
entries.literal: Myriad things change, indeed no rest.

entries.zh: 斡流而遷兮，或推而還。
entries.en: They revolve and flow and shift; pushed forward, they circle back again.
entries.literal: Rotate flow migrate, or push return.

entries.zh: 形氣轉續兮，變化而嬗。
entries.en: Form and breath pass on in ceaseless succession, changing and transforming without end.
entries.literal: Form qi transfer continue, change transform.

entries.zh: 沕穆無窮兮，胡可勝言！
entries.en: Boundless and unfathomable — how could words ever encompass it!
entries.literal: Swim silent no end, how can exhaust speak!

entries.zh: 禍兮福所倚，福兮禍所伏；
entries.en: Misfortune — that is where fortune leans; fortune — that is where misfortune hides;
entries.literal: Calamity fortune depend on each other, fortune calamity lie hidden;

entries.zh: 憂喜聚門兮，吉凶同域。
entries.en: sorrow and joy gather at the same gate, the auspicious and the dire share the same ground.
entries.literal: Worry joy gather gate, auspicious inauspicious same region.

entries.zh: 彼吳彊大兮，夫差以敗；
entries.en: The state of Wu was mighty and strong, yet Fu Chai met defeat;
entries.literal: That Wu strong great, Fu Chai with defeat;

entries.zh: 越棲會稽兮，句踐霸世。
entries.en: Yue cowered at Kuaiji, yet Goujian rose to dominate the age.
entries.literal: Yue dwell Kuaiji, Gou Jian hegemon world.

entries.zh: 斯游遂成兮，卒被五刑；
entries.en: Li Si roamed and achieved success, yet in the end he suffered the Five Punishments;
entries.literal: Si You finally succeed, finally received five punishments;

entries.zh: 傅說胥靡兮，乃相武丁。
entries.en: Fu Yue toiled as a convict laborer, yet rose to become chief minister to King Wu Ding.
entries.literal: Fu Yue slave labor, then became minister Wu Ding.

entries.zh: 夫禍之與福兮，何異糾纆。
entries.en: Misfortune and fortune — how are they any different from the strands of a twisted rope?
entries.literal: That calamity and fortune, what different twisted rope.

entries.zh: 命不可說兮，孰知其極？
entries.en: Fate cannot be explained — who knows where it will end?
entries.literal: Fate cannot explain, who knows its limit?

entries.zh: 水激則旱兮，矢激則遠。
entries.en: Water forced through a narrow channel shoots high; an arrow released from a drawn bow flies far.
entries.literal: Water forced through a narrow channel shoots upward; an arrow released from a drawn bow flies far.

entries.zh: 萬物回薄兮，振蕩相轉。
entries.en: The myriad things surge and press upon one another, buffeted and turning without cease.
entries.literal: Myriad things return press, shake sway transfer each other.

entries.zh: 雲蒸雨降兮，錯繆相紛。
entries.en: Clouds rise as steam and rain descends; all is tangled and interwoven.
entries.literal: Cloud steam rain fall, wrong error mix confused.

entries.zh: 大專槃物兮，坱軋無垠。
entries.en: The great Way encompasses all things, vast and boundless, without limit.
entries.literal: Great concentrated encompass things, vast press no border.

entries.zh: 天不可與慮兮，道不可與謀。
entries.en: Heaven cannot be reasoned with; the Way cannot be plotted against.
entries.literal: Heaven cannot with deliberate, way cannot with plan.

entries.zh: 遲數有命兮，惡識其時？
entries.en: Whether slow or swift, all is fated — who can know the appointed hour?
entries.literal: Slow hasten have fate, how know its time?

entries.zh: 居數年，懷王騎，墮馬而死，無後。
entries.en: A few years later, King Huai went riding, fell from his horse, and died. He left no heir.
entries.literal: Dwell several years, Huai King ride horse, fall horse die, no posterity.

entries.zh: 賈生自傷為傅無狀，哭泣歲餘，亦死。
