entries.en: Jia Sheng blamed himself bitterly for having failed as a tutor. He wept for more than a year, and then he too died.
entries.literal: Jia Sheng self blame as tutor without achievement, cry weep year plus, also die.

entries.zh: 賈生之死時年三十三矣。
entries.en: At the time of his death, Jia Sheng was only thirty-three years old.
entries.literal: Jia Sheng death time age thirty three.

entries.zh: 及孝文崩，孝武皇帝立，舉賈生之孫二人至郡守，而賈嘉最好學，世其家，與余通書。
entries.en: After Emperor Wen passed away and Emperor Wu ascended the throne, two of Jia Sheng's grandsons were promoted to the rank of commandery governor. Among them, Jia Jia was the most devoted to learning. He carried on the family tradition and exchanged letters with me.
entries.literal: When Filial Wen passed, Filial Wu Emperor established, raise Jia Sheng two grandsons to commandery governors, Jia Jia most good learning, inherit family, with me communicate writings.

entries.zh: 至孝昭時，列為九卿。
entries.en: By the time of Emperor Zhao, he had risen to the rank of one of the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: To Filial Zhao time, listed as nine ministers.

entries.zh: 屈原者，名平，楚之同姓也。
entries.en: Qu Yuan, whose given name was Ping, shared the royal surname of the state of Chu.
entries.literal: Qu Yuan, named Ping, Chu same clan.

entries.zh: 為楚懷王左徒。
entries.en: He served as Left Minister to King Huai of Chu.
entries.literal: Served Chu Huai Wang Left Tutor.

entries.zh: 博聞彊志，明於治亂，嫻于辭令。
entries.en: He was widely learned with a powerful memory, well versed in the principles of governance and disorder, and eloquent in speech and composition.
entries.literal: Broad learning strong will, clear on order chaos, skilled in rhetoric.

entries.zh: 入則與王圖議國事，以出號令；
entries.en: At court, he deliberated affairs of state with the king and drafted royal edicts;
entries.literal: Enter then with king plan discuss state affairs, to issue commands;

entries.zh: 出則接遇賓客，應對諸侯。
entries.en: Abroad, he received envoys and conducted diplomacy with the feudal lords.
entries.literal: Exit then receive guests, respond to feudal lords.

entries.zh: 王甚任之。
entries.en: The king placed great trust in him.
entries.literal: King greatly relied on him.

entries.zh: 蒙恬者，其先齊人也。
entries.en: Meng Tian's ancestors were originally from the state of Qi.
entries.literal: Meng Tian, his ancestors were Qi people.

entries.zh: 恬大父蒙驁，自齊事秦昭王，官至上卿。
entries.en: Tian's grandfather Meng Ao left Qi to serve King Zhao of Qin and rose to the rank of High Minister.
entries.literal: Tian's grandfather Meng Ao, from Qi served King Zhao of Qin; his office reached High Minister.

entries.zh: 秦莊襄王元年，蒙驁為秦將，伐韓，取成皋、滎陽，作置三川郡。
entries.en: In the first year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, Meng Ao served as a Qin general, attacked the state of Han, seized Chenggao and Yingyang, and established Sanchuan Commandery.
entries.literal: In the first year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, Meng Ao served as a Qin general, attacked Han, took Chenggao and Yingyang, and established Sanchuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 二年，蒙驁攻趙，取三十七城。
entries.en: In the second year, Meng Ao attacked the state of Zhao and captured thirty-seven cities.
entries.literal: Second year, Meng Ao attacked Zhao, took thirty-seven cities.

entries.zh: 始皇三年，蒙驁攻韓，取十三城。
entries.en: In the third year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao attacked Han and captured thirteen cities.
entries.literal: Shihuang third year, Meng Ao attacked Han, took thirteen cities.

entries.zh: 五年，蒙驁攻魏，取二十城，作置東郡。
entries.en: In the fifth year, Meng Ao attacked the state of Wei, captured twenty cities, and established Dong Commandery.
entries.literal: Fifth year, Meng Ao attacked Wei, took twenty cities, established Dong Commandery.

entries.zh: 始皇七年，蒙驁卒。
entries.en: In the seventh year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Ao died.
entries.literal: Shihuang seventh year, Meng Ao died.

entries.zh: 驁子曰武，武子曰恬。
entries.en: Ao's son was named Wu, and Wu's son was named Tian.
entries.literal: Ao's son was called Wu, Wu's son was called Tian.

entries.zh: 恬嘗書獄典文學。
entries.en: Tian studied the penal codes and the classics in his youth.
entries.literal: Tian once studied penal law classics and literature.

entries.zh: 始皇二十三年，蒙武為秦裨將軍，與王翦攻楚，大破之，殺項燕。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year of the First Emperor's reign, Meng Wu served as a deputy general of Qin and joined Wang Jian in an attack on the state of Chu, inflicting a devastating defeat and killing the Chu general Xiang Yan.
entries.literal: Shihuang twenty-third year, Meng Wu as Qin secondary general, with Wang Jian attacked Chu, greatly defeated it, killed Xiang Yan.

entries.zh: 二十四年，蒙武攻楚，虜楚王。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year, Meng Wu attacked Chu and captured the King of Chu.
entries.literal: Twenty-fourth year, Meng Wu attacked Chu, captured the King of Chu.

entries.zh: 蒙恬弟毅。
entries.en: Meng Tian had a younger brother named Yi.
entries.literal: Meng Tian's younger brother was Yi.

entries.zh: 子嬰進諫曰：「臣聞故趙王遷殺其良臣李牧而用顏聚，燕王喜陰用荊軻之謀而倍秦之約，齊王建殺其故世忠臣而用后勝之議。
entries.en: Ziying came forward to remonstrate: "Your servant has heard that King Qian of Zhao executed his able minister Li Mu and relied instead on the mediocre Yan Ju; that King Xi of Yan secretly adopted Jing Ke's assassination plot and thereby violated his treaty with Qin; and that King Jian of Qi executed his loyal ministers of many generations and followed the counsel of the treacherous Hou Sheng.
entries.literal: Ziying came forward to remonstrate, saying: 'Your servant has heard that King Qian of Zhao killed his able minister Li Mu and employed Yan Ju instead; King Xi of Yan secretly adopted Jing Ke's plot and violated the treaty with Qin; King Jian of Qi killed his long-serving loyal ministers and followed the counsel of Hou Sheng.

entries.zh: 此三君者，皆各以變古者失其國而殃及其身。
entries.en: Each of these three rulers abandoned the ways of antiquity, lost his state, and brought ruin upon himself.
entries.literal: These three rulers each, for changing from antiquity, lost their states and brought calamity upon themselves.

entries.zh: 今蒙氏，秦之大臣謀士也，而主欲一旦棄去之，臣竊以為不可。
entries.en: The Meng clan are among the greatest ministers and strategists Qin has ever known. Yet now the sovereign wishes to cast them aside overnight. Your servant humbly submits that this must not be done.
entries.literal: Now the Meng clan are great ministers and strategists of Qin, yet the ruler wishes to discard them overnight. Your servant humbly believes this must not be done.

entries.zh: 臣聞輕慮者不可以治國，獨智者不可以存君。
entries.en: Your servant has heard it said that those who deliberate carelessly cannot govern a state, and those who rely on their own judgment alone cannot safeguard their sovereign.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that those who deliberate carelessly cannot govern a state, and those who rely on their own wisdom alone cannot preserve their sovereign.

entries.zh: 誅殺忠臣而立無節行之人，是內使群臣不相信而外使鬬士之意離也，臣竊以為不可。」
entries.en: To execute loyal ministers and elevate men without integrity would sow distrust among the officials at court and disillusion the soldiers in the field. Your servant humbly submits that this must not be done."
entries.literal: To execute loyal ministers and elevate men of no integrity is to cause the court ministers to lose trust in one another within, and the fighting men to lose heart without. Your servant humbly believes this must not be done.'

entries.zh: 秦之滅大梁也，張耳家外黃。
entries.en: When Qin destroyed Daliang, Zhang Er was living in Waihuang.
entries.literal: When Qin destroyed Daliang, Zhang Er's home was in Waihuang.

entries.zh: 高祖為布衣時，嘗數從張耳游，客數月。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Gaozu was still a commoner, he visited Zhang Er on several occasions and stayed as his guest for months at a time.
entries.literal: When the future Emperor Gaozu was still a commoner, he once stayed with Zhang Er several times, lodging for several months.

entries.zh: 秦滅魏數歲，已聞此兩人魏之名士也，購求有得張耳千金，陳餘五百金。
entries.en: Some years after Qin conquered Wei, word reached the court that these two men were celebrated figures of the former state. Qin posted bounties of a thousand gold pieces for Zhang Er and five hundred for Chen Yu.
entries.literal: Several years after Qin destroyed Wei, having heard that these two men were famous gentlemen of Wei, it offered a reward of a thousand gold for capturing Zhang Er and five hundred gold for Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 張耳、陳餘乃變名姓，俱之陳，為里監門以自食。
entries.en: Zhang Er and Chen Yu assumed false names and fled together to the city of Chen, where they took positions as village gatekeepers to earn their keep.
entries.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu then changed their names and surnames, both went to Chen, and became village gate-watchers to feed themselves.

entries.zh: 兩人相對。
entries.en: The two stood opposite each other at the gate.
entries.literal: The two men stood facing each other.

entries.zh: 里吏嘗有過笞陳餘，陳餘欲起，張耳躡之，使受笞。
entries.en: Once, a village official flogged Chen Yu for some petty infraction. Chen Yu was about to leap up in fury, but Zhang Er trod on his foot and forced him to endure the beating.
entries.literal: A village official once came by and flogged Chen Yu for some offense; Chen Yu was about to rise up, but Zhang Er stepped on his foot and made him endure the flogging.

entries.zh: 吏去，張耳乃引陳餘之桑下而數之曰：「始吾與公言何如？
entries.en: After the official had gone, Zhang Er pulled Chen Yu under a mulberry tree and rebuked him. 'What did I tell you at the start?
entries.literal: After the official left, Zhang Er led Chen Yu under a mulberry tree and rebuked him, saying: 'What did I say to you at the beginning?

entries.zh: 今見小辱而欲死一吏乎？」
entries.en: Would you throw your life away over a petty official's insult?'
entries.literal: Now you face a small humiliation and want to fight a petty official to the death?'

entries.zh: 陳餘然之。
entries.en: Chen Yu acknowledged he was right.
entries.literal: Chen Yu agreed with him.

entries.zh: 秦詔書購求兩人，兩人亦反用門者以令里中。
entries.en: Even as Qin circulated warrants for their arrest, the two men turned their role as gatekeepers to their advantage, exercising authority over the village.
entries.literal: Qin issued edicts offering bounties for the two men, but the two men in turn used their position as gatekeepers to give orders within the village.

entries.zh: 漢二年，東擊楚，使使告趙，欲與俱。
entries.en: In the second year of Han, the King of Han marched east against Chu and sent envoys to Zhao, inviting them to join the campaign.
entries.literal: In the second year of Han, the King of Han marched east to attack Chu and sent envoys to inform Zhao, wishing them to join him.

entries.zh: 陳餘曰：「漢殺張耳乃從。」
entries.en: Chen Yu replied, 'We will join you only after Han puts Zhang Er to death.'
entries.literal: Chen Yu said: 'We will join you only if Han kills Zhang Er.'

entries.zh: 於是漢王求人類張耳者斬之，持其頭遺陳餘。
entries.en: The King of Han found a man who resembled Zhang Er, had him beheaded, and sent the head to Chen Yu.
entries.literal: Thereupon the King of Han found a man who resembled Zhang Er, had him beheaded, and sent his head to Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 陳餘乃遣兵助漢。
entries.en: Chen Yu then dispatched troops to assist Han.
entries.literal: Chen Yu then sent troops to assist Han.

entries.zh: 漢之敗於彭城西，陳餘亦復覺張耳不死，即背漢。
entries.en: After Han's defeat west of Pengcheng, Chen Yu discovered that Zhang Er was in fact still alive, and he immediately turned against Han.
entries.literal: When Han was defeated west of Pengcheng, Chen Yu also discovered that Zhang Er was not dead, and immediately turned against Han.

entries.zh: 漢三年，韓信已定魏地，遣張耳與韓信擊破趙井陘，斬陳餘泜水上，追殺趙王歇襄國。
entries.en: In the third year of Han, after Han Xin had pacified the territory of Wei, he and Zhang Er were sent to attack Zhao. They shattered the Zhao army at Jingxing, beheaded Chen Yu on the banks of the Zhi River, and pursued King Zhao Xie to Xiangguo, where he was killed.
entries.literal: In the third year of Han, Han Xin had already pacified the land of Wei. Zhang Er was sent with Han Xin to attack and defeat Zhao at Jingxing. Chen Yu was beheaded on the banks of the Zhi River, and King Zhao Xie was pursued and killed at Xiangguo.

entries.zh: 漢立張耳為趙王。
entries.en: Han then established Zhang Er as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: Han established Zhang Er as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 漢五年，張耳薨，謚為景王。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Han, Zhang Er died. He was given the posthumous title King Jing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Han, Zhang Er died, and he was posthumously titled King Jing.

entries.zh: 子敖嗣立為趙王。
entries.en: His son Zhang Ao succeeded him as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: His son Ao succeeded him and was established as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 高祖長女魯元公主為趙王敖后。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Luyuan, became Queen of Zhao.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Luyuan, became the queen of King Ao of Zhao.

entries.zh: 漢七年，高祖從平城過趙，趙王朝夕袒韛蔽，自上食，禮甚卑，有子婿禮。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Han, Emperor Gaozu passed through Zhao on his return from Pingcheng. The King of Zhao attended him morning and evening, baring his arms and tying on an apron to serve the food himself. His deference was extreme, befitting a son-in-law rather than a king.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Han, Emperor Gaozu passed through Zhao on his return from Pingcheng. The King of Zhao waited on him morning and evening, baring his arms and wearing an apron, personally serving food. His manner was extremely humble, observing the etiquette of a son-in-law.

entries.zh: 高祖箕踞詈，甚慢易之。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu sat sprawled with his legs apart, swearing and berating him. He treated the King of Zhao with open contempt.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu sat with his legs spread wide, cursing freely, and treated him with great contempt.

entries.zh: 趙相貫高、趙午等年六十餘，故張耳客也。
entries.en: The chancellor of Zhao, Guan Gao, along with Zhao Wu and other men over sixty years of age, had all been retainers of Zhang Er.
entries.literal: The Chancellor of Zhao, Guan Gao, Zhao Wu, and others, all over sixty years old, were former retainers of Zhang Er.

entries.zh: 生平為氣，乃怒曰：「吾王孱王也！」
entries.en: These were men of fierce pride, and they said in fury, 'Our king is a weakling!'
entries.literal: They were men of spirit by nature, and they said angrily: 'Our king is a weak king!'

entries.zh: 說王曰：「夫天下豪桀并起，能者先立。
entries.en: They went to the king and said, 'Heroes have risen across the realm, and the capable are the first to stake their claim.
entries.literal: They addressed the king, saying: 'Heroes throughout the realm have risen together; the capable are the first to establish themselves.

entries.zh: 今王事高祖甚恭，而高祖無禮，請為王殺之！」
entries.en: Your Majesty serves Emperor Gaozu with the deepest reverence, yet the Emperor shows you nothing but contempt. Allow us to kill him for you!'
entries.literal: Now the King serves Emperor Gaozu with the utmost respect, yet Gaozu shows no courtesy. We beg to kill him for the King!'

entries.zh: 張敖齧其指出血，曰：「君何言之誤！
entries.en: Zhang Ao bit his finger until it bled and cried, 'What terrible things you say!
entries.literal: Zhang Ao bit his finger until it bled and said: 'How wrong your words are!

entries.zh: 且先人亡國，賴高祖得復國，德流子孫，秋豪皆高祖力也。
entries.en: My father lost his kingdom, and it was Emperor Gaozu who restored it. This grace extends to his descendants—every last bit of it was Gaozu's doing.
entries.literal: My father lost his kingdom, and it was thanks to Emperor Gaozu that it was restored. This grace flows down to his descendants—every particle of it was through Gaozu's power.

entries.zh: 願君無復出口。」
entries.en: I beg you, never speak of this again.'
entries.literal: I beg you never to speak of this again.'

entries.zh: 貫高、趙午等十餘人皆相謂曰：「乃吾等非也。
entries.en: Guan Gao, Zhao Wu, and more than ten others conferred among themselves: 'We were wrong to involve the king.
entries.literal: Guan Gao, Zhao Wu, and more than ten others all said to one another: 'We were wrong.

entries.zh: 吾王長者，不倍德。
entries.en: Our king is a man of integrity. He will not betray a debt of gratitude.
entries.literal: Our king is a man of virtue; he would not betray a kindness.

entries.zh: 且吾等義不辱，今怨高祖辱我王，故欲殺之，何乃汙王為乎？
entries.en: Our code of honor will not suffer insult. We resent Gaozu for humiliating our king, and so we wish to kill him. Why should we drag the king into this disgrace?
entries.literal: Moreover, by our code of honor we cannot endure insult. Now we resent Gaozu for humiliating our king, so we wish to kill him—why should we drag the king into disgrace?

entries.zh: 令事成歸王，事敗獨身坐耳。」
entries.en: If we succeed, the credit goes to the king. If we fail, we alone will bear the consequences.'
entries.literal: If we succeed, the credit goes to the king; if we fail, we alone will bear the punishment.'

entries.zh: 漢八年，上從東垣還，過趙，貫高等乃壁人柏人，要之置廁。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Han, as the Emperor was returning from Dongyuan and passing through Zhao, Guan Gao and his conspirators hid assassins in the walls at Bairen, intending to waylay him at the privy.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Han, when the Emperor was returning from Dongyuan and passing through Zhao, Guan Gao and the others concealed men in the walls at Bairen, planning to waylay him at the privy.

entries.zh: 上過欲宿，心動，問曰：「縣名為何？」
entries.en: The Emperor was about to spend the night there when he felt a sudden unease. He asked, 'What is the name of this county?'
entries.literal: The Emperor was passing through and was about to stay the night when his heart stirred. He asked: 'What is the name of this county?'

entries.zh: 曰：「柏人。」
entries.en: The answer came: 'Bairen.'
entries.literal: They replied: 'Bairen.'

entries.zh: 「柏人者，迫於人也！」
entries.en: 'Bairen!' he exclaimed. 'That sounds like "pressed by men"!'
entries.literal: 'Bairen—"pressed by men"!'

entries.zh: 不宿而去。
entries.en: He refused to spend the night and departed at once.
entries.literal: He did not stay the night and left.

entries.zh: 漢九年，貫高怨家知其謀，乃上變告之。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Han, enemies of Guan Gao learned of the plot and reported it to the throne.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Han, enemies of Guan Gao learned of his plot and reported it to the throne.

entries.zh: 於是上皆并逮捕趙王、貫高等。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered the arrest of the King of Zhao along with Guan Gao and all the other conspirators.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor had the King of Zhao, Guan Gao, and the others all arrested together.

entries.zh: 十餘人皆爭自剄，貫高獨怒罵曰：「誰令公為之？
entries.en: More than ten of the conspirators tried to slit their own throats, but Guan Gao alone raged at them: 'Who told you to do this?
entries.literal: More than ten of the conspirators all vied to cut their own throats, but Guan Gao alone cursed angrily, saying: 'Who told you to do this?

entries.zh: 今王實無謀，而并捕王；
entries.en: The king truly had no part in our plot, yet they have arrested him too.
entries.literal: The king truly had no part in the plot, yet the king has been arrested too;

entries.zh: 公等皆死，誰白王不反者！」
entries.en: If all of you die now, who will be left to prove that the king is innocent?'
entries.literal: If you all die, who will clear the king of the charge of rebellion!'

entries.zh: 乃轞車膠致，與王詣長安。
entries.en: They were loaded into sealed prison carts and transported to Chang'an along with the king.
entries.literal: They were then placed in sealed prison carts and taken together with the king to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 治張敖之罪。
entries.en: An investigation was opened into Zhang Ao's crimes.
entries.literal: Zhang Ao's crimes were investigated.

entries.zh: 上乃詔趙群臣賓客有敢從王皆族。
entries.en: The Emperor then issued an edict declaring that any minister or retainer of Zhao who dared follow the king would have their entire clan put to death.
entries.literal: The Emperor then decreed that any minister or guest of Zhao who dared to follow the king would have their entire clan exterminated.

entries.zh: 貫高與客孟舒等十餘人，皆自髡鉗，為王家奴，從來。
entries.en: Guan Gao, along with Meng Shu and more than ten other retainers, shaved their heads and clamped iron collars around their necks, disguising themselves as the king's household slaves in order to follow him.
entries.literal: Guan Gao and guests such as Meng Shu, more than ten men in all, all shaved their heads and placed iron collars around their necks, becoming household slaves of the king, and followed him.

entries.zh: 貫高至，對獄，曰：「獨吾屬為之，王實不知。」
entries.en: When Guan Gao was brought to trial, he declared, 'We alone are responsible. The king truly knew nothing of it.'
entries.literal: When Guan Gao arrived and faced trial, he said: 'Only we did this; the king truly did not know.'

entries.zh: 吏治榜笞數千，刺剟，身無可擊者，終不復言。
entries.en: The officials flogged him thousands of times and pricked his flesh with needles until there was not a spot left on his body to strike, but he never changed his testimony.
entries.literal: The officials beat him with clubs and bamboo thousands of times and stabbed him with needles until there was no spot left on his body to strike, but he never changed his statement.

entries.zh: 呂后數言張王以魯元公主故，不宜有此。
entries.en: Empress Lu repeatedly argued that Zhang Ao, as the husband of Princess Luyuan, should not be treated this way.
entries.literal: Empress Lu repeatedly said that King Zhang, because of Princess Luyuan, should not be treated this way.

entries.zh: 上怒曰：「使張敖據天下，豈少而女乎！」
entries.en: The Emperor said in a fury, 'If Zhang Ao held the whole realm, do you think he would lack for women? Your daughter would mean nothing to him!'
entries.literal: The Emperor said angrily: 'If Zhang Ao held the whole realm, would he lack for your daughter!'

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: He refused to relent.
entries.literal: He did not listen.

entries.zh: 廷尉以貫高事辭聞，上曰：「壯士！
entries.en: When the Commandant of Justice presented the details of Guan Gao's testimony, the Emperor exclaimed, 'A brave man indeed!
entries.literal: When the Commandant of Justice reported the details of Guan Gao's testimony, the Emperor said: 'A brave man!

entries.zh: 誰知者，以私問之。」
entries.en: Does anyone know him? Have someone question him in private.'
entries.literal: Who knows him? Have someone question him privately.'

entries.zh: 中大夫泄公曰：「臣之邑子，素知之。
entries.en: The Palace Grandee Xie Gong said, 'He is from my hometown. I have known him all my life.
entries.literal: The Palace Grandee Xie Gong said: 'He is a fellow townsman of mine; I have always known him.

entries.zh: 此固趙國立名義不侵為然諾者也。」
entries.en: He is one of those men of Zhao renowned for their honor and for keeping their word at any cost.'
entries.literal: He is one of those men from Zhao who are famous for upholding honor and keeping their word without fail.'

entries.zh: 上使泄公持節問之箯輿前。
entries.en: The Emperor sent Xie Gong, bearing the imperial staff of authority, to question Guan Gao before his prison litter.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Xie Gong, bearing the imperial staff, to question him before the prisoner's litter.

entries.zh: 仰視曰：「泄公邪？」
entries.en: Guan Gao looked up and said, 'Is that Xie Gong?'
entries.literal: Guan Gao looked up and said: 'Is that Xie Gong?'

entries.zh: 泄公勞苦如生平驩，與語，問張王果有計謀不。
entries.en: Xie Gong consoled him warmly, speaking as though they were old friends, and asked whether King Zhang had truly been involved in the plot.
entries.literal: Xie Gong comforted him as if they were old friends, spoke with him, and asked whether King Zhang had truly been involved in the plot.

entries.zh: 高曰：「人情寧不各愛其父母妻子乎？
entries.en: Guan Gao said, 'Is it not human nature to love one's own parents, wife, and children?
entries.literal: Gao said: 'Is it not human nature for everyone to love their parents, wife, and children?

entries.zh: 今吾三族皆以論死，豈以王易吾親哉！
entries.en: All three branches of my clan have been condemned to death. Do you think I would sacrifice my own family to shield the king?
entries.literal: Now my three clans have all been condemned to death—would I trade my own family for the king!

entries.zh: 顧為王實不反，獨吾等為之。」
entries.en: But the truth is that the king did not rebel. We alone are responsible.'
entries.literal: But the truth is that the king did not rebel; only we did it.'

entries.zh: 具道本指所以為者王不知狀。
entries.en: He then gave a full account of the original plot and the circumstances proving that the king had known nothing of it.
entries.literal: He then explained in full the original plan and how the king had no knowledge of it.

entries.zh: 於是泄公入，具以報，上乃赦趙王。
entries.en: Xie Gong returned to the palace and reported everything. The Emperor thereupon pardoned the King of Zhao.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xie Gong entered the palace, reported everything in full, and the Emperor pardoned the King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 張敖已出，以尚魯元公主故，封為宣平侯。
entries.en: After his release, Zhang Ao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping on account of his marriage to Princess Luyuan.
entries.literal: After Zhang Ao was released, because he was married to Princess Luyuan, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping.

entries.zh: 於是上賢張王諸客，以鉗奴從張王入關，無不為諸侯相、郡守者。
entries.en: The Emperor admired the retainers of King Zhang who had disguised themselves as collared slaves to follow the king to the capital. Every one of them was eventually appointed chancellor of a feudal state or governor of a commandery.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor admired the retainers of King Zhang, who as collared slaves had followed the king through the Pass—not one of them failed to become a chancellor of a feudal lord or a commandery governor.

entries.zh: 及孝惠、高后、文帝、孝景時，張王客子孫皆得為二千石。
entries.en: Through the reigns of Emperor Hui, Empress Dowager Gao, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing, the descendants of King Zhang's retainers all attained the rank of two-thousand-bushel officials.
entries.literal: Through the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui, Empress Dowager Gao, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Xiaojing, the descendants of King Zhang's retainers all attained the rank of two-thousand-bushel officials.

entries.zh: 張耳者，大梁人也。
entries.en: Zhang Er was a native of Daliang.
entries.literal: Zhang Er was a person from Daliang.

entries.zh: 其少時，及魏公子毋忌為客。
entries.en: In his youth, he served as a retainer to Lord Xinling of Wei.
entries.literal: In his youth, he was a retainer of the Wei prince Wuji.

entries.zh: 張耳嘗亡命游外黃。
entries.en: Zhang Er once fled as a fugitive and wandered to Waihuang.
entries.literal: Zhang Er once fled for his life and traveled to Waihuang.

entries.zh: 外黃富人女甚美，嫁庸奴，亡其夫，去抵父客。
entries.en: A wealthy man's daughter in Waihuang was a great beauty. She had been married to a worthless man, but after her husband died, she went to lodge with one of her father's guests.
entries.literal: A rich man's daughter in Waihuang was very beautiful; she had married a common slave, but her husband died, and she went to stay with a guest of her father.

entries.zh: 父客素知張耳，乃謂女曰：「必欲求賢夫，從張耳。」
entries.en: This guest had long been acquainted with Zhang Er, and he told the woman, 'If you want a husband of true worth, then marry Zhang Er.'
entries.literal: The father's guest had long known Zhang Er, and so he said to the woman: 'If you truly wish to find a worthy husband, follow Zhang Er.'

entries.zh: 女聽，乃卒為請決，嫁之張耳。
entries.en: The woman consented, and the guest arranged everything and wed her to Zhang Er.
entries.literal: The woman agreed, and he finally arranged the matter and married her to Zhang Er.

entries.zh: 張耳是時脫身游，女家厚奉給張耳，張耳以故致千里客。
entries.en: Zhang Er was then a wandering adventurer. His wife's family lavished resources upon him, and with these means he attracted followers from a thousand li around.
entries.literal: Zhang Er at that time was wandering freely; the woman's family generously provided for Zhang Er, and Zhang Er thereby attracted guests from a thousand li away.

entries.zh: 乃宦魏為外黃令。
entries.en: He then entered the service of Wei and was appointed Magistrate of Waihuang.
entries.literal: He then entered service in Wei and became the Magistrate of Waihuang.

entries.zh: 名由此益賢。
entries.en: His fame grew steadily as a man of virtue.
entries.literal: His reputation thus grew ever more worthy.

entries.zh: 陳餘者，亦大梁人也，好儒術，數游趙苦陘。
entries.en: Chen Yu was also a native of Daliang. He was devoted to Confucian learning and often traveled to Kuxing in the state of Zhao.
entries.literal: Chen Yu was also a person from Daliang; he was fond of Confucian learning and frequently traveled to Kuxing in Zhao.

entries.zh: 富人公乘氏以其女妻之，亦知陳餘非庸人也。
entries.en: A wealthy man of the Gongcheng clan gave him his daughter in marriage, recognizing that Chen Yu was no ordinary man.
entries.literal: A rich man of the Gongcheng clan gave him his daughter in marriage, also knowing that Chen Yu was no ordinary man.

entries.zh: 餘年少，父事張耳，兩人相與為刎頸交。
entries.en: Chen Yu was the younger of the two and looked up to Zhang Er as a father. Together they became the closest of friends, each willing to die for the other.
entries.literal: Yu was younger, and he served Zhang Er as a father; the two became sworn brothers willing to die for each other.

entries.zh: 漢王還定三秦，渡臨晉，魏王豹以國屬焉，遂從擊楚於彭城。
entries.en: When the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin and crossed the river at Linjin, King Bao of Wei submitted his kingdom and joined in the attack on Chu at Pengcheng.
entries.literal: When the King of Han returned to pacify the Three Qin, and crossed at Linjin, King Bao of Wei submitted his state to him, and then followed him to attack Chu at Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 漢敗，還至滎陽，豹請歸視親病，至國，即絕河津畔漢。
entries.en: After the Han defeat, when they had retreated to Xingyang, Bao asked for leave to visit an ailing parent. Upon reaching his own domain, he promptly severed the river crossings and turned against Han.
entries.literal: After the Han defeat, when they had returned to Xingyang, Bao requested leave to visit a sick parent; upon reaching his own state, he immediately cut off the river crossings and rebelled against Han.

entries.zh: 漢王聞魏豹反，方東憂楚，未及擊，謂酈生曰：「緩頰往說魏豹，能下之，吾以萬戶封若。」
entries.en: When the King of Han learned of Wei Bao's rebellion, he was preoccupied with the threat from Chu to the east and could not spare forces for an attack. He said to Li Yiji, "Go and talk Wei Bao into submission. If you succeed, I shall grant you a fief of ten thousand households."
entries.literal: When the King of Han heard that Wei Bao had rebelled, he was preoccupied with Chu to the east and had no time to attack, so he said to Li Yiji: 'Go and use your eloquence to persuade Wei Bao; if you can make him submit, I will enfeoff you with ten thousand households.'

entries.zh: 酈生說豹。
entries.en: Li Yiji went to persuade Bao.
entries.literal: Li Yiji tried to persuade Bao.

entries.zh: 豹謝曰：「人生一世閒，如白駒過隙耳。
entries.en: Bao rebuffed him, saying, "A man's life in this world passes as swiftly as a white colt glimpsed through a crack in the wall.
entries.literal: Bao declined, saying: 'A man's life in this world is like a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall.

entries.zh: 今漢王慢而侮人，罵詈諸侯群臣如罵奴耳，非有上下禮節也，吾不忍復見也。」
entries.en: The King of Han is arrogant and abusive, cursing his lords and ministers as though they were slaves, with no regard for the proprieties between ruler and subject. I cannot bear to face him again."
entries.literal: Now the King of Han is arrogant and insults people, cursing the lords and ministers as if cursing slaves, with no regard for the proprieties between superior and subordinate; I cannot bear to see him again.'

entries.zh: 於是漢王遣韓信擊虜豹於河東，傳詣滎陽，以豹國為郡。
entries.en: The King of Han then dispatched Han Xin to attack and capture Bao in Hedong. Bao was escorted under guard to Xingyang, and his kingdom was converted into a commandery.
entries.literal: Thereupon the King of Han dispatched Han Xin to attack and capture Bao in Hedong, had him transported under escort to Xingyang, and converted Bao's kingdom into a commandery.

entries.zh: 漢王令豹守滎陽。
entries.en: The King of Han assigned Bao to the defense of Xingyang.
entries.literal: The King of Han ordered Bao to guard Xingyang.

entries.zh: 楚圍之急，周苛遂殺魏豹。
entries.en: When Chu pressed the siege fiercely, Zhou Ke put Wei Bao to death.
entries.literal: When Chu besieged it urgently, Zhou Ke then killed Wei Bao.

entries.zh: 沛公之從碭北擊昌邑，彭越助之。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei marched north from Dang to attack Changyi, Peng Yue came to his aid.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Pei marched north from Dang to attack Changyi, Peng Yue assisted him.

entries.zh: 昌邑未下，沛公引兵西。
entries.en: Before Changyi fell, the Lord of Pei withdrew his forces and headed west.
entries.literal: Changyi had not yet fallen, and the Lord of Pei led his troops westward.

entries.zh: 彭越亦將其眾居鉅野中，收魏散卒。
entries.en: Peng Yue likewise kept his men in the Juye marshes, gathering Wei soldiers who had been scattered.
entries.literal: Peng Yue also led his followers to remain in the Juye marshes, collecting scattered Wei soldiers.

entries.zh: 項籍入關，王諸侯，還歸，彭越眾萬餘人毋所屬。
entries.en: When Xiang Ji entered the passes, installed the lords as kings, and departed, Peng Yue's force of more than ten thousand men remained without allegiance to any lord.
entries.literal: When Xiang Ji entered the Pass, made kings of the lords, and returned, Peng Yue's force of over ten thousand men had no one to whom they belonged.

entries.zh: 漢元年秋，齊王田榮畔項王，（漢）乃使人賜彭越將軍印，使下濟陰以擊楚。
entries.en: In the autumn of the first year of Han, when King Tian Rong of Qi rebelled against the King of Xiang, Han sent an envoy to bestow upon Peng Yue the seal of a general and ordered him to take Jiyin and attack Chu.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Han, King Tian Rong of Qi rebelled against the King of Xiang, and Han sent a man to bestow upon Peng Yue a general's seal, ordering him to take Jiyin to attack Chu.

entries.zh: 楚命蕭公角將兵擊越，越大破楚軍。
entries.en: Chu dispatched Lord Xiao Jiao to lead forces against Yue, but Yue routed the Chu army.
entries.literal: Chu ordered Lord Xiao Jiao to lead troops to attack Yue, but Yue greatly defeated the Chu army.

entries.zh: 漢王二年春，與魏王豹及諸侯東擊楚，彭越將其兵三萬餘人歸漢於外黃。
entries.en: In the spring of the King of Han's second year, when he marched east with King Bao of Wei and the other lords to attack Chu, Peng Yue led his thirty thousand troops to submit to Han at Waihuang.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year of the King of Han, when he marched east with King Bao of Wei and the other lords to attack Chu, Peng Yue led his troops of over thirty thousand men to submit to Han at Waihuang.

entries.zh: 漢王曰：「彭將軍收魏地得十餘城，欲急立魏後。
entries.en: The King of Han said, "General Peng has recovered the Wei territories and taken more than ten cities, and he is eager to see a descendant of Wei restored to the throne.
entries.literal: The King of Han said: 'General Peng has recovered the Wei territory and taken more than ten cities, and wishes urgently to establish a descendant of Wei.

entries.zh: 今西魏王豹亦魏王咎從弟也，真魏後。」
entries.en: King Bao of Western Wei is a cousin of King Jiu of Wei and a true heir of the Wei royal line."
entries.literal: Now King Bao of Western Wei is also a cousin of King Jiu of Wei, a true descendant of Wei.'

entries.zh: 乃拜彭越為魏相國，擅將其兵，略定梁地。
entries.en: He then appointed Peng Yue as the Chancellor of Wei, granting him sole command of his forces to conquer and pacify the Liang region.
entries.literal: He then appointed Peng Yue as Chancellor of Wei, giving him full command of his own troops, to seize and pacify the Liang territory.

entries.zh: 十年秋，陳豨反代地，高帝自往擊，至邯鄲，徵兵梁王。
entries.en: In the autumn of the tenth year, Chen Xi rebelled in the region of Dai. The Emperor himself marched to attack, and upon reaching Handan, he summoned the King of Liang to send troops.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year, Chen Xi rebelled in the Dai region; the Supreme Emperor went in person to attack him, reached Handan, and summoned troops from the King of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁王稱病，使將將兵詣邯鄲。
entries.en: The King of Liang pleaded illness and sent a general to lead his troops to Handan in his stead.
entries.literal: The King of Liang pleaded illness and sent a general to lead troops to Handan.

entries.zh: 高帝怒，使人讓梁王。
entries.en: The Emperor was furious and sent an envoy to rebuke the King of Liang.
entries.literal: The Supreme Emperor was angered and sent someone to rebuke the King of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁王恐，欲自往謝。
entries.en: The King of Liang grew fearful and wished to go in person to offer his apologies.
entries.literal: The King of Liang was afraid and wished to go in person to apologize.

entries.zh: 其將扈輒曰：「王始不往，見讓而往，往則為禽矣。
entries.en: His general Hu Zhe said, "Your Majesty chose not to go at first. Now that you have been rebuked, if you go, you will be seized.
entries.literal: His general Hu Zhe said: 'Your Majesty did not go at first; now that you have been rebuked, if you go, you will be captured.

entries.zh: 不如遂發兵反。」
entries.en: It would be better to raise your army and rebel outright."
entries.literal: It would be better to raise troops and rebel.'

entries.zh: 梁王不聽，稱病。
entries.en: The King of Liang refused to listen and continued to plead illness.
entries.literal: The King of Liang did not listen and continued to plead illness.

entries.zh: 梁王怒其太仆，欲斬之。
entries.en: The King of Liang grew enraged at his Grand Coachman and wanted to have him executed.
entries.literal: The King of Liang was angry with his Grand Coachman and wished to behead him.

entries.zh: 太仆亡走漢，告梁王與扈輒謀反。
entries.en: The Grand Coachman fled to the Han court and reported that the King of Liang and Hu Zhe were plotting rebellion.
entries.literal: The Grand Coachman fled to Han and reported that the King of Liang and Hu Zhe were plotting rebellion.

entries.zh: 於是上使使掩梁王，梁王不覺，捕梁王，囚之雒陽。
entries.en: The Emperor sent men to seize the King of Liang by surprise. Caught unawares, the King of Liang was arrested and imprisoned at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor sent an envoy to seize the King of Liang by surprise; the King of Liang was unaware, and was captured and imprisoned at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 有司治反形己具，請論如法。
entries.en: The officials assembled the evidence of rebellion and petitioned for him to be sentenced according to the law.
entries.literal: The officials had completed their investigation and the evidence of rebellion was assembled; they requested that he be sentenced according to the law.

entries.zh: 上赦以為庶人，傳處蜀青衣。
entries.en: The Emperor pardoned him, reduced him to a commoner, and banished him to Qingyi in Shu.
entries.literal: The Emperor pardoned him and reduced him to a commoner, to be banished and resettled at Qingyi in Shu.

entries.zh: 西至鄭，逢呂后從長安來，欲之雒陽，道見彭王。
entries.en: As he was being escorted westward and reached Zheng, he chanced upon Empress Lu, who was traveling from Chang'an toward Luoyang. She encountered King Peng on the road.
entries.literal: Traveling west, when he reached Zheng, he encountered Empress Lu coming from Chang'an, intending to go to Luoyang; on the road she met King Peng.

entries.zh: 彭王為呂后泣涕，自言無罪，願處故昌邑。
entries.en: King Peng wept before Empress Lu, protesting his innocence and begging to be allowed to live out his days in his old home of Changyi.
entries.literal: King Peng wept before Empress Lu, declaring himself innocent and asking to be allowed to live in his old home of Changyi.

entries.zh: 呂后許諾，與俱東至雒陽。
entries.en: Empress Lu agreed and brought him east with her to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Empress Lu agreed and traveled east with him to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 呂后白上曰：「彭王壯士，今徙之蜀，此自遺患，不如遂誅之。
entries.en: Empress Lu told the Emperor, "King Peng is a formidable warrior. Banishing him to Shu will only leave us with a future menace. It would be better to execute him outright.
entries.literal: Empress Lu said to the Emperor: 'King Peng is a mighty warrior; to banish him to Shu now is to store up trouble for ourselves. It would be better to put him to death at once.

entries.zh: 妾謹與俱來。」
entries.en: I have taken the precaution of bringing him back with me."
entries.literal: I have taken the liberty of bringing him back with me.'

entries.zh: 於是呂后乃令其舍人彭越復謀反。
entries.en: Empress Lu then had one of Peng Yue's own retainers accuse him of plotting a fresh rebellion.
entries.literal: Thereupon Empress Lu had one of his retainers accuse Peng Yue of plotting rebellion again.

entries.zh: 廷尉王恬開奏請族之。
entries.en: The Commandant of Justice, Wang Tiankai, petitioned for the extermination of Peng Yue's entire clan.
entries.literal: The Commandant of Justice, Wang Tiankai, submitted a memorial requesting the extermination of his entire clan.

entries.zh: 上乃可，遂夷越宗族，國除。
entries.en: The Emperor approved the petition. Yue's clan was wiped out, and his kingdom was abolished.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved, and Yue's clan was exterminated, and his kingdom was abolished.

entries.zh: 魏豹亡走楚。
entries.en: Wei Bao fled to Chu.
entries.literal: Wei Bao fled to Chu.

entries.zh: 楚懷王予魏豹數千人，復徇魏地。
entries.en: King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao several thousand troops to reclaim the Wei territories.
entries.literal: King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao several thousand men to again make a circuit through the Wei territories.

entries.zh: 項羽已破秦，降章邯。
entries.en: After Xiang Yu had defeated Qin and accepted Zhang Han's surrender.
entries.literal: After Xiang Yu had defeated Qin and accepted the surrender of Zhang Han.

entries.zh: 豹下魏二十餘城，立豹為魏王。
entries.en: Bao captured more than twenty cities in the Wei lands, and he was established as King of Wei.
entries.literal: Bao took more than twenty cities in Wei, and Bao was established as King of Wei.

entries.zh: 豹引精兵從項羽入關。
entries.en: Bao led his best troops to follow Xiang Yu through the passes into the heartland of Qin.
entries.literal: Bao led elite troops to follow Xiang Yu into the Pass.

entries.zh: 漢元年，項羽封諸侯，欲有梁地，乃徙魏王豹於河東，都平陽，為西魏王。
entries.en: In the first year of the Han dynasty, when Xiang Yu parceled out domains among the lords, he coveted the Liang territory for himself and relocated King Bao of Wei to Hedong, with his capital at Pingyang, designating him King of Western Wei.
entries.literal: In the first year of Han, Xiang Yu enfeoffed the lords; wanting to possess the Liang territory himself, he moved King Bao of Wei to Hedong, with his capital at Pingyang, as King of Western Wei.

entries.zh: 漢王之敗彭城解而西也，彭越皆復亡其所下城，獨將其兵北居河上。
entries.en: When the King of Han was defeated at Pengcheng and fell back to the west, Peng Yue lost all the cities he had captured and withdrew his forces northward to take up a position along the Yellow River.
entries.literal: When the King of Han was defeated at Pengcheng and retreated westward, Peng Yue lost all the cities he had taken, and led his troops alone to the north to station them along the Yellow River.

entries.zh: 漢王三年，彭越常往來為漢游兵，擊楚，絕其後糧於梁地。
entries.en: In the King of Han's third year, Peng Yue ranged back and forth as a mobile force for Han, raiding Chu and severing its supply lines in the Liang region.
entries.literal: In the third year of the King of Han, Peng Yue constantly went back and forth as a roving force for Han, striking at Chu and cutting off its supply lines in the Liang territory.

entries.zh: 漢四年冬，項王與漢王相距滎陽，彭越攻下睢陽、外黃十七城。
entries.en: In the winter of the King of Han's fourth year, while the King of Xiang and the King of Han were locked in a standoff at Xingyang, Peng Yue attacked and captured seventeen cities, including Suiyang and Waihuang.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Han, when the King of Xiang and the King of Han were facing each other at Xingyang, Peng Yue attacked and took seventeen cities including Suiyang and Waihuang.

entries.zh: 項王聞之，乃使曹咎守成皋，自東收彭越所下城邑，皆復為楚。
entries.en: When the King of Xiang learned of this, he left Cao Jiu to hold Chenggao and marched east in person to reclaim the cities Peng Yue had taken, restoring them all to Chu.
entries.literal: When the King of Xiang heard of this, he ordered Cao Jiu to hold Chenggao, and went east himself to recover the cities Peng Yue had taken, all of which returned to Chu.

entries.zh: 越將其兵北走穀城。
entries.en: Yue led his forces northward and withdrew to Gucheng.
entries.literal: Yue led his troops north and withdrew to Gucheng.

entries.zh: 漢五年秋，項王之南走陽夏，彭越復下昌邑旁二十餘城，得穀十餘萬斛，以給漢王食。
entries.en: In the autumn of the fifth year of Han, when the King of Xiang retreated south to Yangxia, Peng Yue once again captured more than twenty cities around Changyi and seized over a hundred thousand bushels of grain to provision the King of Han.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Han, when the King of Xiang went south to Yangxia, Peng Yue again took more than twenty cities around Changyi, and captured over a hundred thousand bushels of grain to supply the King of Han with provisions.

entries.zh: 漢王敗，使使召彭越并力擊楚。
entries.en: After the King of Han suffered a defeat, he sent a messenger to summon Peng Yue to join forces against Chu.
entries.literal: The King of Han was defeated and sent a messenger to summon Peng Yue to combine forces and attack Chu.

entries.zh: 越曰：「魏地初定，尚畏楚，未可去。」
entries.en: Yue replied, "The Wei territory has only just been pacified. We still fear Chu and cannot yet afford to leave."
entries.literal: Yue said: 'The Wei territory has only just been pacified; we still fear Chu and cannot leave yet.'

entries.zh: 漢王追楚，為項籍所敗碧陵。
entries.en: The King of Han pursued Chu but was defeated by Xiang Ji at Guling.
entries.literal: The King of Han pursued Chu and was defeated by Xiang Ji at Guling.

entries.zh: 乃謂留侯曰：「諸侯兵不從，為之柰何？」
entries.en: He said to the Marquis of Liu, "The armies of the other lords will not come to my aid. What should I do?"
entries.literal: He then said to the Marquis of Liu: 'The armies of the lords do not follow me; what should I do?'

entries.zh: 留侯曰：「齊王信之立，非君王之意，信亦不自堅。
entries.en: The Marquis of Liu replied, "The King of Qi, Han Xin, was installed without Your Majesty's approval, and he himself feels insecure in his position.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Liu said: 'The installation of the King of Qi, Xin, was not Your Majesty's intention, and Xin himself is also not secure in his position.

entries.zh: 彭越本定梁地，功多，始君王以魏豹故，拜彭越為魏相國。
entries.en: Peng Yue was the one who originally pacified the Liang territory and rendered great service, yet because of Wei Bao, Your Majesty initially appointed Peng Yue merely as Chancellor of Wei.
entries.literal: Peng Yue originally pacified the Liang territory with great merit; at first, Your Majesty on account of Wei Bao appointed Peng Yue as Chancellor of Wei.

entries.zh: 今豹死毋後，且越亦欲王，而君王不蚤定。
entries.en: Now that Bao is dead and has left no heir, Yue naturally desires a kingship of his own, yet Your Majesty has not moved to settle the matter.
entries.literal: Now Bao is dead and has no heir; moreover, Yue also desires to be a king, yet Your Majesty has not settled the matter early.

entries.zh: 與此兩國約：即勝楚，睢陽以北至穀城，皆以王彭相國；
entries.en: Make a compact with these two men: once Chu is defeated, all the territory from Suiyang northward to Gucheng shall be granted to Chancellor Peng as his kingdom;
entries.literal: Make a pact with these two men: if we defeat Chu, all the territory from Suiyang north to Gucheng shall be given to make Chancellor Peng a king;

entries.zh: 從陳以東傅海，與齊王信。
entries.en: and the territory from Chen eastward to the sea shall be given to the King of Qi, Han Xin.
entries.literal: from Chen eastward to the sea shall be given to the King of Qi, Xin.

entries.zh: 齊王信家在楚，此其意欲復得故邑。
entries.en: The King of Qi's ancestral home is in Chu, and his heart's desire is to recover his old homeland.
entries.literal: The King of Qi, Xin, has his family home in Chu; his desire is to recover his old homeland.

entries.zh: 君王能出捐此地許二人，二人今可致；
entries.en: If Your Majesty can part with these territories and promise them to these two men, both can be won over;
entries.literal: If Your Majesty can relinquish these territories and promise them to these two men, the two of them can be brought to your side;

entries.zh: 即不能，事未可知也。」
entries.en: If you cannot bring yourself to do this, the outcome of the war remains uncertain."
entries.literal: If you cannot, then the outcome of things cannot be known.'

entries.zh: 於是漢王乃發使使彭越，如留侯策。
entries.en: The King of Han accordingly dispatched an envoy to Peng Yue, following the strategy of the Marquis of Liu.
entries.literal: Thereupon the King of Han dispatched an envoy to Peng Yue, following the Marquis of Liu's plan.

entries.zh: 使者至，彭越乃悉引兵會垓下，遂破楚。
entries.en: When the envoy arrived, Peng Yue marshaled all his forces and converged on Gaixia, where they defeated Chu.
entries.literal: When the envoy arrived, Peng Yue then led all his troops to assemble at Gaixia, and they defeated Chu.

entries.zh: （五年）項籍已死。
entries.en: By the fifth year, Xiang Ji was dead.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Xiang Ji was already dead.

entries.zh: 春，立彭越為梁王，都定陶。
entries.en: In the spring, Peng Yue was installed as the King of Liang, with his capital at Dingtao.
entries.literal: In the spring, Peng Yue was established as King of Liang, with his capital at Dingtao.

entries.zh: 彭越者，昌邑人也，字仲。
entries.en: Peng Yue was a native of Changyi, and his courtesy name was Zhong.
entries.literal: Peng Yue was a man of Changyi, with the courtesy name Zhong.

entries.zh: 常漁鉅野澤中，為群盜。
entries.en: He often fished in the marshes of Juye and led a band of outlaws.
entries.literal: He regularly fished in the marshes of Juye, and was a bandit leader.

entries.zh: 陳勝、項梁之起，少年或謂越曰：「諸豪桀相立畔秦，仲可以來，亦效之。」
entries.en: When Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose in revolt, some young men said to Yue, "The heroes everywhere are setting themselves up and rebelling against Qin. You could join them and follow their example, Zhong."
entries.literal: When Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose in revolt, some young men said to Yue: 'The various heroes are establishing themselves and rebelling against Qin; Zhong, you could come and do the same.'

entries.zh: 彭越曰：「兩龍方鬬，且待之。」
entries.en: Peng Yue replied, "Two dragons are locked in battle. Let us wait and see how it turns out."
entries.literal: Peng Yue said: 'Two dragons are just now fighting; wait for the outcome.'

entries.zh: 居歲餘，澤閒少年相聚百餘人，往從彭越，曰：「請仲為長。」
entries.en: After more than a year, over a hundred young men from the marshes banded together and went to Peng Yue, saying, "We ask that you be our leader, Zhong."
entries.literal: After more than a year, over a hundred young men from the marshes gathered together and went to follow Peng Yue, saying: 'We ask that Zhong be our leader.'

entries.zh: 越謝曰：「臣不願與諸君。」
entries.en: Yue declined, saying, "I have no wish to join you."
entries.literal: Yue declined, saying: 'I do not wish to join you gentlemen.'

entries.zh: 少年彊請，乃許。
entries.en: The young men persisted in their entreaties until he finally agreed.
entries.literal: The young men pressed their request, and he finally agreed.

entries.zh: 與期旦日日出會，後期者斬。
entries.en: He set a time for them to assemble at sunrise the following day, declaring that anyone who arrived late would be beheaded.
entries.literal: He arranged with them to assemble at sunrise the next day; those who arrived late would be beheaded.

entries.zh: 旦日日出，十餘人后，後者至日中。
entries.en: At sunrise the next day, more than ten men arrived late, with the last straggler appearing at noon.
entries.literal: The next day at sunrise, more than ten men were late, the last arriving at noon.

entries.zh: 於是越謝曰：「臣老，諸君彊以為長。
entries.en: Yue then addressed them: "I am getting old, and you insisted on making me your leader.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yue said apologetically: 'I am old, and you gentlemen insisted on making me your leader.

entries.zh: 今期而多後，不可盡誅，誅最後者一人。」
entries.en: Now many of you arrived late. I cannot execute all of you, so I shall execute the one who arrived last."
entries.literal: Now many were late for the appointed time; I cannot execute them all, so I will execute the one who arrived last.'

entries.zh: 令校長斬之。
entries.en: He ordered his adjutant to behead the man.
entries.literal: He ordered the squad leader to behead him.

entries.zh: 皆笑曰：「何至是？
entries.en: They all laughed and said, "Surely there is no need for that?
entries.literal: They all laughed, saying: 'Why go so far?

entries.zh: 請後不敢。」
entries.en: We swear we will never be late again."
entries.literal: We promise we will not dare to be late again.'

entries.zh: 於是越乃引一人斬之，設壇祭，乃令徒屬。
entries.en: Yue had the man dragged out and beheaded, set up an altar to make a sacrifice, and then issued orders to his followers.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yue had the one man dragged out and beheaded, set up an altar and made a sacrifice, and then issued orders to his followers.

entries.zh: 徒屬皆大驚，畏越，莫敢仰視。
entries.en: His followers were all terrified. They feared Yue so deeply that none dared to look up at him.
entries.literal: The followers were all greatly alarmed, feared Yue, and none dared to raise their eyes to look at him.

entries.zh: 乃行略地，收諸侯散卒，得千餘人。
entries.en: He then set out to seize territory, rallying scattered soldiers from across the land until he had gathered more than a thousand men.
entries.literal: He then went out to seize territory, gathering scattered soldiers of the various lords, and obtained more than a thousand men.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：魏豹、彭越雖故賤，然已席卷千里，南面稱孤，喋血乘勝日有聞矣。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Though Wei Bao and Peng Yue were once men of low station, they swept across a thousand li of territory, faced south as sovereign lords, and won renown through victory after blood-soaked victory.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: Although Wei Bao and Peng Yue were originally of low station, they swept across a thousand li, faced south and styled themselves lords, wading through blood and riding on victory until their fame grew with each passing day.

entries.zh: 懷畔逆之意，及敗，不死而虜囚，身被刑戮，何哉？
entries.en: Yet when they harbored rebellious intent and met with defeat, they did not die fighting but were taken captive and subjected to execution. Why was this?
entries.literal: Yet when they harbored thoughts of rebellion and treason, and upon their defeat, did not die but were captured and imprisoned, and suffered execution, why was this?

entries.zh: 中材已上且羞其行，況王者乎！
entries.en: Even a man of middling ability would be ashamed of such conduct, let alone one who had been a king!
entries.literal: Even a person of middling talent and above would be ashamed of such conduct, how much more so a king!

entries.zh: 彼無異故，智略絕人，獨患無身耳。
entries.en: There was no other reason for this: their cunning and strategic brilliance surpassed those of ordinary men, and their sole concern was to preserve their own lives.
entries.literal: There was no other reason for this; their intelligence and strategy surpassed other men, and their only worry was for the preservation of their own persons.

entries.zh: 得攝尺寸之柄，其雲蒸龍變，欲有所會其度，以故幽囚而不辭云。
entries.en: Having once grasped even a sliver of power, they had soared like clouds and transformed like dragons, always hoping for some chance to fulfill their grand designs. That is why they submitted to imprisonment without protest.
entries.literal: Having grasped even an inch of the handle of power, they transformed like clouds rising and dragons changing, desiring to find some opportunity to fulfill their ambitions; therefore they endured imprisonment without demurring.

entries.zh: 魏豹者，故魏諸公子也。
entries.en: Wei Bao was a prince of the royal house of Wei.
entries.literal: Wei Bao was a former scion of the house of Wei.

entries.zh: 其兄魏咎，故魏時封為寧陵君。
entries.en: His elder brother, Wei Jiu, had been enfeoffed as the Lord of Ningling during the days of the old Wei state.
entries.literal: His elder brother Wei Jiu had in the old Wei times been enfeoffed as Lord of Ningling.

entries.zh: 秦滅魏，遷咎為家人。
entries.en: When Qin conquered Wei, Jiu was reduced to the status of a commoner.
entries.literal: When Qin destroyed Wei, it reduced Jiu to the status of a commoner.

entries.zh: 陳勝之起王也，咎往從之。
entries.en: When Chen Sheng rose in rebellion and declared himself king, Jiu went to join him.
entries.literal: When Chen Sheng rose up and proclaimed himself king, Jiu went to follow him.

entries.zh: 陳王使魏人周市徇魏地，魏地已下，欲相與立周市為魏王。
entries.en: The King of Chen sent Zhou Shi, a man of Wei, to pacify the old Wei territories. Once those lands had submitted, the people wished to make Zhou Shi the King of Wei.
entries.literal: The King of Chen sent the Wei man Zhou Shi to make a circuit through the Wei territories; after the Wei territories had all submitted, the people wished together to set up Zhou Shi as King of Wei.

entries.zh: 周市曰：「天下昏亂，忠臣乃見。
entries.en: Zhou Shi said, "It is only when the world falls into darkness and chaos that loyal ministers make themselves known.
entries.literal: Zhou Shi said, "When all under heaven is in darkness and chaos, only then are loyal ministers revealed.

entries.zh: 今天下共畔秦，其義必立魏王後乃可。」
entries.en: Now all the world has risen against Qin. By any measure of righteousness, we must first restore a descendant of the Wei royal line to the throne."
entries.literal: Now all under heaven together rebel against Qin; by righteousness, one must first establish a descendant of the Wei kings, only then will it be permissible."

entries.zh: 齊、趙使車各五十乘，立周市為魏王。
entries.en: Qi and Zhao each sent fifty chariots in support of installing Zhou Shi as King of Wei.
entries.literal: Qi and Zhao each sent fifty chariots to establish Zhou Shi as King of Wei.

entries.zh: 市辭不受，迎魏咎於陳。
entries.en: Zhou Shi refused the title and traveled to Chen to welcome Wei Jiu.
entries.literal: Zhou Shi declined and did not accept, and went to welcome Wei Jiu from Chen.

entries.zh: 五反，陳王乃遣立咎為魏王。
entries.en: After five round trips of entreaty, the King of Chen finally released Jiu and established him as King of Wei.
entries.literal: After five round trips, the King of Chen then authorized the establishment of Jiu as King of Wei.

entries.zh: 陳勝之起也，布乃見番君，與其眾叛秦，聚兵數千人。
entries.en: When Chen Sheng raised the banner of revolt, Bu sought out Lord Fan of Poyang and joined forces with his followers to rebel against Qin, assembling an army of several thousand men.
entries.literal: When Chen Sheng rose in revolt, Bu went to see Lord Fan, and together with his followers rebelled against Qin, gathering several thousand soldiers.

entries.zh: 番君以其女妻之。
entries.en: Lord Fan gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Lord Fan gave his daughter to him in marriage.

entries.zh: 章邯之滅陳勝，破呂臣軍，布乃引兵北擊秦左右校，破之清波，引兵而東。
entries.en: After Zhang Han destroyed Chen Sheng and routed the army of Lü Chen, Bu led his forces northward to attack the Qin left and right battalions. He defeated them at Qingbo, then marched his army eastward.
entries.literal: When Zhang Han destroyed Chen Sheng and defeated Lü Chen's army, Bu led his troops north to attack the Qin left and right battalions, defeated them at Qingbo, and marched his army eastward.

entries.zh: 聞項梁定江東會稽，涉江而西。
entries.en: Upon hearing that Xiang Liang had established control over Jiangdong and Kuaiji, he crossed the Yangtze and headed west to join him.
entries.literal: Hearing that Xiang Liang had pacified Jiangdong and Kuaiji, he crossed the Yangtze River and went west.

entries.zh: 陳嬰以項氏世為楚將，乃以兵屬項梁，渡淮南，英布、蒲將軍亦以兵屬項梁。
entries.en: Chen Ying, recognizing that the Xiang family had served as generals of Chu for generations, placed his forces under Xiang Liang's command and crossed south of the Huai River. Ying Bu and General Pu likewise pledged their troops to Xiang Liang.
entries.literal: Chen Ying, because the Xiang clan had served as Chu generals for generations, submitted his troops to Xiang Liang and crossed south of the Huai River. Ying Bu and General Pu also submitted their troops to Xiang Liang.

entries.zh: 十一年，高后誅淮陰侯，布因心恐。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, Empress Gao had the Marquis of Huaiyin executed, and Bu grew fearful in his heart.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, Empress Dowager Gao executed the Marquis of Huaiyin, and Bu became fearful at heart.

entries.zh: 夏，漢誅梁王彭越，醢之，盛其醢遍賜諸侯。
entries.en: That summer, Han executed Peng Yue, the King of Liang, had his flesh minced into a paste, and sent portions of it to every feudal lord in the realm.
entries.literal: In the summer, Han executed Peng Yue, the King of Liang, minced his flesh into paste, placed the paste in vessels, and distributed it to all the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 至淮南，淮南王方獵，見醢，因大恐，陰令人部聚兵，候伺旁郡警急。
entries.en: When the parcel arrived in Huainan, the King of Huainan was out hunting. Upon seeing the flesh paste, he was seized with terror. He secretly ordered his men to assemble troops and keep watch for signs of military action in the neighboring commanderies.
entries.literal: When the paste arrived in Huainan, the King of Huainan was hunting. Upon seeing the paste, he was seized with great terror. He secretly ordered men to assemble troops and watch for any alarms or emergencies in the neighboring commanderies.

entries.zh: 上召諸將問曰：「布反，為之柰何？」
entries.en: The Emperor summoned his generals and asked, "Bu has rebelled. What is to be done?"
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned his generals and asked: 'Bu has rebelled. What shall we do about it?'

entries.zh: 皆曰；
entries.en: They all replied,
entries.literal: They all said,

entries.zh: 「發兵擊之，阬豎子耳。
entries.en: "Send troops to crush him and bury the wretch alive.
entries.literal: 'Send troops to attack him and bury the wretch alive.

entries.zh: 何能為乎！」
entries.en: What can he possibly do!"
entries.literal: What can he possibly do!'

entries.zh: 汝陰侯滕公召故楚令尹問之。
entries.en: The Marquis of Ruyin, Lord Teng, summoned the former Chief Minister of Chu and consulted him on the matter.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Ruyin, Lord Teng, summoned the former Chu Chief Minister and asked his opinion.

entries.zh: 令尹曰：「是故當反。」
entries.en: The Chief Minister said, "That is why he was bound to rebel."
entries.literal: The Chief Minister said: 'That is why he was bound to rebel.'

entries.zh: 滕公曰：「上裂地而王之，疏爵而貴之，南面而立萬乘之主，其反何也？」
entries.en: Lord Teng asked, "The Emperor carved out territory and made him a king, bestowed a noble title upon him, and set him up as a ruler of ten thousand chariots. Why would he rebel?"
entries.literal: Lord Teng said: 'The Emperor carved out territory and made him a king, bestowed a noble title to honor him, and set him up as ruler of ten thousand chariots facing south. Why then did he rebel?'

entries.zh: 令尹曰：「往年殺彭越，前年殺韓信，此三人者，同功一體之人也。
entries.en: The Chief Minister replied, "Last year Peng Yue was killed; the year before that, Han Xin was killed. These three men shared the same achievements and the same fate.
entries.literal: The Chief Minister said: 'Last year Peng Yue was killed; the year before, Han Xin was killed. These three men shared the same achievements and were of one body.

entries.zh: 自疑禍及身，故反耳。」
entries.en: He feared that catastrophe would come for him next, and so he rebelled."
entries.literal: He suspected that disaster would reach him as well, so he rebelled.'

entries.zh: 滕公言之上曰：「臣客故楚令尹薛公者，其人有籌筴之計，可問。」
entries.en: Lord Teng reported to the Emperor, "My retainer, the former Chu Chief Minister known as the Duke of Xue, is a man of great strategic insight. He should be consulted."
entries.literal: Lord Teng reported to the Emperor: 'My retainer, the former Chu Chief Minister Duke of Xue, is a man of great strategic ability. He may be consulted.'

entries.zh: 上乃召見問薛公。
entries.en: The Emperor summoned the Duke of Xue for an audience and questioned him.
entries.literal: The Emperor then summoned and questioned the Duke of Xue.

entries.zh: 薛公對曰：「布反不足怪也。
entries.en: The Duke of Xue replied, "Bu's rebellion should come as no surprise.
entries.literal: The Duke of Xue replied: 'Bu's rebellion is nothing to be surprised at.

entries.zh: 使布出於上計，山東非漢之有也；
entries.en: If Bu adopts the best strategy, the lands east of the mountains will be lost to Han.
entries.literal: If Bu follows the best strategy, the lands east of the mountains will no longer belong to Han;

entries.zh: 出於中計，勝敗之數未可知也；
entries.en: If he follows the middle strategy, the outcome will be uncertain.
entries.literal: If he follows the middle strategy, the outcome of victory or defeat cannot be predicted;

entries.zh: 出於下計，陛下安枕而臥矣。」
entries.en: If he follows the worst strategy, Your Majesty may sleep soundly."
entries.literal: If he follows the worst strategy, Your Majesty may rest your head on the pillow and sleep peacefully.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「何謂上計？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, "What would the best strategy be?"
entries.literal: The Emperor asked: 'What is the best strategy?'

entries.zh: 令尹對曰：「東取吳，西取楚，并齊取魯，傳檄燕、趙，固守其所，山東非漢之有也。」
entries.en: The Chief Minister replied, "Seize Wu to the east, take Chu to the west, annex Qi and conquer Lu, send proclamations rallying Yan and Zhao, then hold his ground. The lands east of the mountains would be lost to Han."
entries.literal: The Chief Minister replied: 'Take Wu in the east, take Chu in the west, annex Qi and seize Lu, send proclamations to Yan and Zhao, and hold firm where he stands. The lands east of the mountains would no longer belong to Han.'

entries.zh: 「何謂中計？」
entries.en: "What would the middle strategy be?"
entries.literal: 'What is the middle strategy?'

entries.zh: 「東取吳，西取楚，并韓取魏，據敖庾之粟，塞成皋之口，勝敗之數未可知也。」
entries.en: "Seize Wu to the east, take Chu to the west, annex Han and conquer Wei, secure the grain stores at Ao Granary, and block the pass at Chenggao. Then the outcome would hang in the balance."
entries.literal: 'Take Wu in the east, take Chu in the west, annex Han and seize Wei, seize the grain stores at Ao Granary, and block the pass at Chenggao. Then the outcome of victory or defeat cannot be known.'

entries.zh: 「何謂下計？」
entries.en: "And the worst strategy?"
entries.literal: 'What is the worst strategy?'

entries.zh: 「東取吳，西取下蔡，歸重於越，身歸長沙，陛下安枕而臥，漢無事矣。」
entries.en: "Seize Wu to the east, take Xiacai to the west, send his treasures to Yue for safekeeping, and retreat to Changsha himself. In that case, Your Majesty may sleep soundly, and the Han empire will be secure."
entries.literal: 'Take Wu in the east, take Xiacai in the west, send his valuables south to Yue, and retreat personally to Changsha. Then Your Majesty may rest your head on the pillow and sleep, and Han will have nothing to worry about.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「是計將安出？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, "Which strategy will he choose?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'Which strategy will he adopt?'

entries.zh: 令尹對曰：「出下計。」
entries.en: The Chief Minister replied, "He will choose the worst one."
entries.literal: The Chief Minister replied: 'He will adopt the worst strategy.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「何謂廢上中計而出下計？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, "Why would he pass over the best and middle strategies and choose the worst?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'Why would he abandon the best and middle strategies and adopt the worst?'

entries.zh: 令尹曰：「布故麗山之徒也，自致萬乘之主，此皆為身，不顧後為百姓萬世慮者也，故曰出下計。」
entries.en: The Chief Minister said, "Bu was once a convict laborer at Mount Li who raised himself to become the ruler of ten thousand chariots. Everything he has done has been for himself alone—he has never given a thought to the welfare of the people or planned for future generations. This is why I say he will choose the worst strategy."
entries.literal: The Chief Minister said: 'Bu was originally a convict laborer at Mount Li who raised himself to become the lord of ten thousand chariots. All of this was done for himself alone; he has never thought of the people or planned for ten thousand generations. Therefore, I say he will adopt the worst strategy.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "Well spoken."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 封薛公千戶。
entries.en: He rewarded the Duke of Xue with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed the Duke of Xue with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 乃立皇子長為淮南王。
entries.en: He then installed the imperial prince Chang as the new King of Huainan.
entries.literal: He then established the imperial prince Chang as King of Huainan.

entries.zh: 上遂發兵自將東擊布。
entries.en: The Emperor then raised an army and personally led the campaign eastward against Bu.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon raised troops and personally led them eastward to attack Bu.

entries.zh: 布之初反，謂其將曰：「上老矣，厭兵，必不能來。
entries.en: When Bu first raised his rebellion, he told his generals, "The Emperor is old and weary of war. He will certainly not come in person.
entries.literal: When Bu first rebelled, he told his generals: 'The Emperor is old and weary of war. He certainly will not come in person.

entries.zh: 使諸將，諸將獨患淮陰、彭越，今皆已死，餘不足畏也。」
entries.en: If he sends his generals, the only ones to fear were the Marquis of Huaiyin and Peng Yue—both are now dead. The rest are not worth worrying about."
entries.literal: If he sends his generals, the only generals to worry about were the Marquis of Huaiyin and Peng Yue—both are now dead. The rest are not worth fearing.'

entries.zh: 故遂反。
entries.en: And so he went ahead with the rebellion.
entries.literal: Therefore, he proceeded to rebel.

entries.zh: 果如薛公籌之，東擊荊，荊王劉賈走死富陵。
entries.en: Just as the Duke of Xue had predicted, Bu struck eastward against Jing. The King of Jing, Liu Jia, fled and met his death at Fuling.
entries.literal: Indeed, just as the Duke of Xue had predicted, Bu struck eastward against Jing. The King of Jing, Liu Jia, fled and died at Fuling.

entries.zh: 盡劫其兵，渡淮擊楚。
entries.en: He commandeered all of Jing's soldiers, crossed the Huai River, and launched an attack on the kingdom of Chu.
entries.literal: He seized all of Jing's troops, crossed the Huai River, and attacked Chu.

entries.zh: 楚發兵與戰徐、僮閒，為三軍，欲以相救為奇。
entries.en: The kingdom of Chu raised an army and engaged him between Xu and Tong, dividing their forces into three columns with a plan of mutual reinforcement as a surprise stratagem.
entries.literal: Chu raised troops and fought between Xu and Tong, forming three armies with the intention of using mutual reinforcement as a surprise tactic.

entries.zh: 或說楚將曰：「布善用兵，民素畏之。
entries.en: Someone warned the Chu general, saying, "Bu is a master of warfare, and the people have long feared him.
entries.literal: Someone advised the Chu general, saying: 'Bu is skilled at using troops, and the people have long feared him.

entries.zh: 且兵法，諸侯戰其地為散地。
entries.en: Moreover, the art of war teaches that when lords fight on their own territory, it is called dispersed ground.
entries.literal: Moreover, according to the art of war, when lords fight on their own territory, it is called 'dispersed ground.

entries.zh: 今別為三，彼敗吾一軍，餘皆走，安能相救！」
entries.en: If we split into three, and he routs just one of our columns, the others will scatter and run. How could they possibly come to one another's rescue?"
entries.literal: Now if we divide into three and he defeats one of our armies, the rest will all flee. How could they come to each other's rescue!'

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: The general did not heed this advice.
entries.literal: They did not listen.

entries.zh: 布果破其一軍，其二軍散走。
entries.en: Sure enough, Bu routed one of the columns, and the other two scattered and fled.
entries.literal: Bu indeed defeated one of their armies, and the other two scattered and fled.

entries.zh: 黥布者，六人也，姓英氏。
entries.en: Qing Bu was a native of Liu, with the surname Ying.
entries.literal: Qing Bu was a man of Liu, surnamed Ying.

entries.zh: 秦時為布衣。
entries.en: During the Qin era, he lived as a commoner.
entries.literal: During the Qin dynasty he was a commoner.

entries.zh: 少年，有客相之曰：「當刑而王。」
entries.en: In his youth, a traveling physiognomist examined his features and declared, "You shall first suffer punishment, and then become a king."
entries.literal: When young, a traveling physiognomist read his features and said: 'You shall be punished and then become a king.'

entries.zh: 及壯，坐法黥。
entries.en: When he reached manhood, he was convicted of a crime and branded with the convict's tattoo.
entries.literal: When he reached manhood, he was convicted of a crime and tattooed on the face.

entries.zh: 布欣然笑曰；
entries.en: Bu laughed with delight and said,
entries.literal: Bu happily laughed and said,

entries.zh: 「人相我當刑而王，幾是乎？」
entries.en: "Someone once read my face and foretold that I would suffer punishment before becoming a king. Could this be the start of that prophecy?"
entries.literal: 'Someone read my physiognomy and said I would be punished and then become king—could this be the beginning?'

entries.zh: 人有聞者，共俳笑之。
entries.en: Those who overheard him mocked and laughed at his words.
entries.literal: Those who heard this all mocked and laughed at him.

entries.zh: 布已論輸麗山，麗山之徒數十萬人，布皆與其徒長豪桀交通，乃率其曹偶，亡之江中為群盜。
entries.en: After Bu was sentenced to hard labor at Mount Li, he found himself among hundreds of thousands of convicts. There he befriended every leader and formidable figure among the laborers, and eventually led a band of his companions to escape to the Yangtze River region, where they turned to banditry.
entries.literal: Bu had already been sentenced to labor at Mount Li. Among the hundreds of thousands of convicts at Mount Li, Bu associated with all the leaders and outstanding men among the convicts, and then led his group of companions to flee to the Yangtze River area to become bandits.

entries.zh: 盧綰者，豐人也，與高祖同里。
entries.en: Lu Wan was a native of Feng and came from the same village as the High Ancestor.
entries.literal: Lu Wan was a man of Feng, from the same village as the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 盧綰親與高祖太上皇相愛，及生男，高祖、盧綰同日生，里中持羊酒賀兩家。
entries.en: Lu Wan's parents were close friends with the High Ancestor's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor. When both families had sons, the High Ancestor and Lu Wan were born on the same day, and the villagers brought lamb and wine to congratulate both households.
entries.literal: Lu Wan's parents and the High Ancestor's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, were close friends. When their sons were born, the High Ancestor and Lu Wan were born on the same day, and the villagers brought lamb and wine to congratulate both families.

entries.zh: 及高祖、盧綰壯，俱學書，又相愛也。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor and Lu Wan came of age, they studied together and grew fond of each other.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor and Lu Wan grew up, they studied together, and they were fond of each other.

entries.zh: 里中嘉兩家親相愛，生子同日，壯又相愛，復賀兩家羊酒。
entries.en: The villagers marveled that the two families had been close friends, that their sons were born on the same day, and that the boys grew up devoted to each other. Once again they brought lamb and wine to congratulate both households.
entries.literal: The villagers, delighted that the two families were close and their sons born on the same day grew up fond of each other, again congratulated both families with lamb and wine.

entries.zh: 高祖為布衣時，有吏事辟匿，盧綰常隨出入上下。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor was still a commoner and had to go into hiding over legal troubles, Lu Wan always accompanied him wherever he went.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor was a commoner and had to flee and hide because of legal troubles, Lu Wan always accompanied him wherever he went.

entries.zh: 及高祖初起沛，盧綰以客從，入漢中為將軍，常侍中。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor first rose in revolt at Pei, Lu Wan followed as a retainer. He entered Hanzhong, was made a general, and attended constantly at court.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor first rose in revolt at Pei, Lu Wan followed as a retainer, entered Hanzhong and was made a general, and constantly attended at court.

entries.zh: 從東擊項籍，以太尉常從，出入臥內，衣被飲食賞賜，群臣莫敢望，雖蕭曹等，特以事見禮，至其親幸，莫及盧綰。
entries.en: He followed the eastward campaign against Xiang Ji, serving as Grand Commandant and constantly at the Emperor's side, even entering the private chambers. In clothing, bedding, food, drink, and gifts bestowed, no minister dared aspire to his level. Even Xiao He and Cao Shen were only accorded respect on account of their official duties—when it came to intimate favor, none could match Lu Wan.
entries.literal: He followed the eastward campaign against Xiang Ji, and as Grand Commandant he constantly attended, going in and out of the bedchamber. In clothing, bedding, food, drink, and gifts, no minister dared aspire to his level. Even Xiao He and Cao Shen were only treated with ceremony on account of their duties; as for intimate favor, none could match Lu Wan.

entries.zh: 綰封為長安侯。
entries.en: Lu Wan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an.
entries.literal: Wan was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Chang'an.

entries.zh: 長安，故咸陽也。
entries.en: Chang'an was the site of the former Xianyang.
entries.literal: Chang'an was the former Xianyang.

entries.zh: 韓王信者，故韓襄王孽孫也，長八尺五寸。
entries.en: Han Xin, the King of Han, was a descendant of the former King Xiang of Han through a concubine's line. He stood eight feet five inches tall.
entries.literal: Han King Xin was a descendant through a concubine's line of the former King Xiang of Han, and was eight chi five cun tall.

entries.zh: 及項梁之立楚後懷王也，燕、齊、趙、魏皆已前王，唯韓無有後，故立韓諸公子橫陽君成為韓王，欲以撫定韓故地。
entries.en: When Xiang Liang installed the later King Huai of Chu, the states of Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had all already restored their former royal lines. Only Han had no surviving heir, so they established Cheng, the Lord of Hengyang and a prince of the Han royal house, as King of Han, intending to pacify and settle the former Han territories.
entries.literal: When Xiang Liang established the later King Huai of Chu, Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei had all already restored their former kings; only Han had no heir, so they established the Lord of Hengyang, Cheng, one of the princes of Han, as King of Han, wishing to pacify and settle the former territory of Han.

entries.zh: 項梁敗死定陶，成奔懷王。
entries.en: When Xiang Liang was defeated and killed at Dingtao, Cheng fled to King Huai.
entries.literal: Xiang Liang was defeated and died at Dingtao; Cheng fled to King Huai.

entries.zh: 沛公引兵擊陽城，使張良以韓司徒降下韓故地，得信，以為韓將，將其兵從沛公入武關。
entries.en: The Lord of Pei led his forces to attack Yangcheng and dispatched Zhang Liang, serving as the Minister of Education of Han, to secure the surrender of the former Han territories. There he obtained Han Xin's services, appointed him as a general of Han, and had him lead his troops to follow the Lord of Pei through the Wu Pass.
entries.literal: The Lord of Pei led troops to attack Yangcheng, sent Zhang Liang as the Han Minister of Education to receive the surrender of Han's former territory, obtained Xin, made him a Han general, and had him lead troops following the Lord of Pei through Wu Pass.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，韓信從入漢中，乃說漢王曰：「項王王諸將近地，而王獨遠居此，此左遷也。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei was established as King of Han, Han Xin followed him into Hanzhong. He counseled the King of Han, saying: 'The King of Xiang has enfeoffed all his other generals with territories close at hand, yet Your Majesty alone has been banished to this remote place. This is a demotion.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Pei was established as King of Han, Han Xin followed into Hanzhong and counseled the King of Han saying: 'The King of Xiang enfeoffed all his generals with nearby territories, yet Your Majesty alone dwells far away here; this is a demotion.

entries.zh: 士卒皆山東人，跂而望歸，及其鋒東鄉，可以爭天下。」
entries.en: Your soldiers are all men from east of the mountains who stand on tiptoe gazing homeward. If you harness their eagerness and march east, you can contend for the empire.'
entries.literal: The soldiers are all men from east of the mountains; they stand on tiptoe gazing homeward. If you take advantage of their sharp eagerness and turn east, you can contend for the realm.'

entries.zh: 漢王還定三秦，乃許信為韓王，先拜信為韓太尉，將兵略韓地。
entries.en: When the King of Han returned to conquer the Three Qin kingdoms, he promised to make Han Xin the King of Han. First, he appointed Xin as Grand Commandant of Han and sent him to lead troops to take the Han territories.
