entries.literal: When the King of Han returned and pacified the Three Qin, he then promised Xin the title of King of Han, first appointing Xin as Grand Commandant of Han, and had him lead troops to take the Han territory.

entries.zh: 七年冬，上自往擊，破信軍銅鞮，斬其將王喜。
entries.en: In the winter of the seventh year, the Emperor personally led a campaign against him, defeating Xin's army at Tongdi and beheading his general Wang Xi.
entries.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, the Emperor personally went to attack, defeated Xin's army at Tongdi, and beheaded his general Wang Xi.

entries.zh: 信亡走匈奴。
entries.en: Xin fled to the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Xin fled to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: （與）其與白土人曼丘臣、王黃等立趙苗裔趙利為王，復收信敗散兵，而與信及冒頓謀攻漢。
entries.en: Together with Manqiu Chen and Wang Huang, men of Baitu, they set up Zhao Li, a scion of the Zhao royal house, as king. They rallied Xin's defeated and scattered troops and, together with Xin and Modu, plotted to attack Han.
entries.literal: He and Manqiu Chen and Wang Huang, men of Baitu, established Zhao Li, a descendant of the Zhao royal line, as king, gathered Xin's defeated and scattered troops, and together with Xin and Modu plotted to attack Han.

entries.zh: 匈奴仗左右賢王將萬餘騎與王黃等屯廣武以南，至晉陽，與漢兵戰，漢大破之，追至于離石，復破之。
entries.en: The Xiongnu deployed their Wise Kings of the Left and Right with more than ten thousand cavalry, who joined Wang Huang's forces and encamped south of Guangwu, advancing as far as Jinyang. They engaged the Han army, but Han won a decisive victory, pursuing them to Lishi and defeating them once more.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu deployed the Wise Kings of the Left and Right leading more than ten thousand cavalry with Wang Huang and others to encamp south of Guangwu, reaching Jinyang, where they fought the Han army. Han inflicted a great defeat on them, pursued them to Lishi, and defeated them again.

entries.zh: 匈奴復聚兵樓煩西北，漢令車騎擊破匈奴。
entries.en: The Xiongnu reassembled their forces to the northwest of Loufan, but Han sent its chariots and cavalry to attack and rout them.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu reassembled their troops northwest of Loufan; Han ordered chariots and cavalry to attack and defeat the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 匈奴常敗走，漢乘勝追北，聞冒頓居代（上）谷，高皇帝居晉陽，使人視冒頓，還報曰「可擊」。
entries.en: The Xiongnu suffered defeat after defeat and retreated. Han pressed its advantage and pursued northward. Hearing that Modu was encamped in the Dai Valley, the High Emperor, based at Jinyang, sent scouts to assess his forces. They returned and reported: 'He can be attacked.'
entries.literal: The Xiongnu were constantly defeated and fled; Han pursued in victory. Hearing that Modu was stationed in the Dai Valley, the High Emperor, staying at Jinyang, sent scouts to observe Modu; they returned and reported: 'He can be attacked.'

entries.zh: 上遂至平城。
entries.en: The Emperor then advanced to Pingcheng.
entries.literal: The Emperor then advanced to Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 上出白登，匈奴騎圍上，上乃使人厚遺閼氏。
entries.en: The Emperor rode out to Baideng, where the Xiongnu cavalry surrounded him. He then sent an envoy to present lavish gifts to the Chanyu's consort.
entries.literal: The Emperor went out to Baideng, and the Xiongnu cavalry surrounded him. The Emperor then sent someone to present lavish gifts to the Chanyu's consort.

entries.zh: 閼氏乃說冒頓曰：「今得漢地，猶不能居；
entries.en: The consort persuaded Modu, saying: 'Even if you were to seize the Han lands, you could not hold them.
entries.literal: The consort then persuaded Modu, saying: 'Even if you take the Han lands, you still could not dwell there;

entries.zh: 且兩主不相緱」居七日，胡騎稍引去。
entries.en: Moreover, two rulers should not press each other into a corner.' After seven days, the Xiongnu cavalry gradually withdrew.
entries.literal: Moreover, two rulers should not corner each other.' After seven days, the Hu cavalry gradually withdrew.

entries.zh: 時天大霧，漢使人往來，胡不覺。
entries.en: A thick fog had descended, and the Han envoys were able to pass back and forth without the Xiongnu noticing.
entries.literal: At the time there was a great fog; Han sent people to come and go, and the Hu did not notice.

entries.zh: 護軍中尉陳平言上曰：「胡者全兵，請令彊弩傅兩矢外向，徐行出圍。」
entries.en: Chen Ping, the Commandant of the Guard, advised the Emperor: 'The Xiongnu still have their forces intact around us. I suggest we order our strongest crossbowmen to load two bolts apiece, facing outward, and march slowly out of the encirclement.'
entries.literal: The Commandant of the Guard, Chen Ping, said to the Emperor: 'The Hu keep their troops intact; I request that we order the strong crossbowmen to load two bolts facing outward and slowly march out of the encirclement.'

entries.zh: 入平城，漢救兵亦到，胡騎遂解去。
entries.en: They reached Pingcheng, where the Han relief forces had also arrived, and the Xiongnu cavalry broke off and withdrew.
entries.literal: They entered Pingcheng; the Han relief forces also arrived, and the Hu cavalry thereupon dispersed and withdrew.

entries.zh: 漢亦罷兵歸。
entries.en: The Han forces withdrew as well.
entries.literal: Han also withdrew its troops and returned.

entries.zh: 韓信為匈奴將兵往來擊邊。
entries.en: Han Xin now served as a general for the Xiongnu, leading raids back and forth along the border.
entries.literal: Han Xin served as a Xiongnu general, leading troops back and forth to attack the border.

entries.zh: 明年春，上以韓信材武，所王北近鞏、洛，南迫宛、葉，東有淮陽，皆天下勁兵處，乃詔徙韓王信王太原以北，備御胡，都晉陽。
entries.en: The following spring, the Emperor, noting that Han Xin was a man of martial talent and that his kingdom lay close to Gong and Luoyang in the north, bordered Wan and Ye in the south, and included Huaiyang in the east—all strategic positions for the empire's most formidable troops—issued a decree transferring the King of Han to rule north of Taiyuan, charged with defending against the Hu nomads, with his capital at Jinyang.
entries.literal: The next spring, the Emperor, considering that Han Xin was talented and martial, and that his kingdom was close to Gong and Luo in the north, bordered Wan and Ye in the south, and held Huaiyang in the east—all locations of the realm's crack troops—issued a decree to transfer the King of Han to rule north of Taiyuan, to defend against the Hu, with his capital at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 信上書曰：「國被邊，匈奴數入，晉陽去塞遠，請治馬邑。」
entries.en: Xin submitted a memorial saying: 'My kingdom lies along the frontier, and the Xiongnu invade frequently. Jinyang is too far from the border passes. I request permission to govern from Mayi.'
entries.literal: Xin submitted a memorial saying: 'The kingdom borders the frontier; the Xiongnu frequently invade; Jinyang is far from the border passes. I request to administer from Mayi.'

entries.zh: 上許之，信乃徙治馬邑。
entries.en: The Emperor granted his request, and Xin moved his seat of government to Mayi.
entries.literal: The Emperor permitted it, and Xin thereupon moved to administer from Mayi.

entries.zh: 秋，匈奴冒頓大圍信，信數使使胡求和解。
entries.en: That autumn, the Xiongnu Chanyu Modu besieged Xin with a massive force. Xin sent envoy after envoy to the Xiongnu to negotiate peace.
entries.literal: In autumn, the Xiongnu Chanyu Modu laid a great siege around Xin; Xin repeatedly sent envoys to the Hu to seek a peace settlement.

entries.zh: 漢發兵救之，疑信數閒使，有二心，使人責讓信。
entries.en: Han dispatched troops to relieve him, but suspected that Xin's frequent secret embassies meant he harbored divided loyalties, and sent a messenger to rebuke him.
entries.literal: Han dispatched troops to rescue him, but suspected Xin of frequently sending secret envoys and harboring divided loyalties, and sent someone to rebuke and reproach Xin.

entries.zh: 信恐誅，因與匈奴約共攻漢，反，以馬邑降胡，擊太原。
entries.en: Xin, fearing execution, made a pact with the Xiongnu to jointly attack Han. He rebelled, surrendered Mayi to the Xiongnu, and struck at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Xin, fearing execution, thereupon made a pact with the Xiongnu to jointly attack Han, rebelled, surrendered Mayi to the Hu, and attacked Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 上還至洛陽。
entries.en: The Emperor returned to Luoyang.
entries.literal: The Emperor returned to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 上曰：「代居常山北，趙乃從山南有之，遠。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: 'Dai lies north of the Changshan Mountains, yet Zhao governs it from south of the range—too distant.'
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'Dai lies north of Changshan, yet Zhao governs it from south of the mountains; this is too far.'

entries.zh: 乃立子恒為代王，都中都，代、鴈門皆屬代。
entries.en: He thereupon established his son Heng as King of Dai, with the capital at Zhongdu. The territories of Dai and Yanmen were both placed under his authority.
entries.literal: He then established his son Heng as King of Dai, with his capital at Zhongdu; Dai and Yanmen were both placed under Dai.

entries.zh: 漢十二年，東擊黥布，豨常將兵居代，漢使樊噲擊斬豨。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, while the Emperor campaigned east against Qing Bu, Chen Xi continued to hold Dai with his forces. Han sent Fan Kuai to attack and behead Chen Xi.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Han, during the eastern campaign against Qing Bu, Xi continued to command troops in Dai. Han sent Fan Kuai to attack and behead Xi.

entries.zh: 其裨將降，言燕王綰使范齊通計謀於豨所。
entries.en: One of Chen Xi's subordinate generals surrendered and revealed that the King of Yan had sent Fan Qi to coordinate plots with Chen Xi.
entries.literal: One of Xi's subordinate generals surrendered and reported that the King of Yan, Wan, had sent Fan Qi to communicate plots with Xi.

entries.zh: 高祖使使召盧綰，綰稱病。
entries.en: The High Ancestor sent a messenger to summon Lu Wan, but Wan pleaded illness.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor sent an envoy to summon Lu Wan; Wan pleaded illness.

entries.zh: 上又使辟陽侯審食其、御史大夫趙堯往迎燕王，因驗問左右。
entries.en: The Emperor then sent the Marquis of Biyang, Shen Shiqi, and the Grand Censor Zhao Yao to receive the King of Yan and to investigate and interrogate his attendants.
entries.literal: The Emperor also sent the Marquis of Biyang, Shen Shiqi, and the Grand Censor Zhao Yao to go and receive the King of Yan, and to investigate and question those around him.

entries.zh: 綰愈恐，閉匿，謂其幸臣曰：「非劉氏而王，獨我與長沙耳。
entries.en: Wan grew even more fearful and shut himself away. He confided to his trusted ministers: 'Of those who bear the title of king without being of the Liu surname, only I and the King of Changsha remain.
entries.literal: Wan grew more afraid and shut himself away in hiding. He said to his favored ministers: 'Among those who are kings but not of the Liu surname, only I and the King of Changsha remain.

entries.zh: 往年春，漢族淮陰，夏，誅彭越，皆呂后計。
entries.en: Last spring, the court destroyed the clan of the Marquis of Huaiyin. That summer, Peng Yue was executed. Both were the schemes of Empress Lu.
entries.literal: Last year in spring, Han exterminated the clan of the Marquis of Huaiyin; in summer, Peng Yue was executed—all were Empress Lu's schemes.

entries.zh: 今上病，屬任呂后。
entries.en: Now the Emperor is ill and has entrusted affairs of state to Empress Lu.
entries.literal: Now the Emperor is ill and has entrusted affairs to Empress Lu.

entries.zh: 呂后婦人，專欲以事誅異姓王者及大功臣。」
entries.en: Empress Lu is a woman bent on finding pretexts to execute kings of other surnames and great meritorious ministers.'
entries.literal: Empress Lu is a woman who desires only to find pretexts to execute kings of different surnames and great meritorious ministers.'

entries.zh: 乃遂稱病不行。
entries.en: And so he continued to plead illness and refused to go.
entries.literal: He thereupon continued to plead illness and did not go.

entries.zh: 其左右皆亡匿。
entries.en: His attendants all fled and went into hiding.
entries.literal: All those around him fled and went into hiding.

entries.zh: 語頗泄，辟陽侯聞之，歸具報上，上益怒。
entries.en: Word of this leaked out. The Marquis of Biyang heard the report, returned to court, and relayed everything to the Emperor. The Emperor's anger only deepened.
entries.literal: Word of this leaked; the Marquis of Biyang heard of it, returned and reported everything to the Emperor, and the Emperor grew more angry.

entries.zh: 又得匈奴降者，降者言張勝亡在匈奴，為燕使。
entries.en: Furthermore, a Xiongnu defector was captured, and the defector reported that Zhang Sheng had fled to the Xiongnu, where he was serving as an envoy of Yan.
entries.literal: Moreover, a Xiongnu defector was captured, and the defector said Zhang Sheng had fled and was among the Xiongnu, serving as an envoy of Yan.

entries.zh: 於是上曰：「盧綰果反矣！」
entries.en: At this, the Emperor declared: 'Lu Wan has indeed rebelled!'
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor said: 'Lu Wan has indeed rebelled!'

entries.zh: 使樊噲擊燕。
entries.en: He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan.
entries.literal: He sent Fan Kuai to attack Yan.

entries.zh: 燕王綰悉將其宮人家屬騎數千居長城下，侯伺，幸上病愈，自入謝。
entries.en: The King of Yan gathered all his palace women and family members, along with several thousand horsemen, and camped below the Great Wall, watching and waiting, hoping that the Emperor would recover so he could go in person to beg forgiveness.
entries.literal: The King of Yan, Wan, took all his palace women and family members with several thousand cavalry to camp below the Great Wall, waiting and watching, hoping the Emperor would recover from his illness so he could personally go and offer his apologies.

entries.zh: 四月，高祖崩，盧綰遂將其眾亡入匈奴，匈奴以為東胡盧王。
entries.en: In the fourth month, the High Ancestor died. Lu Wan then led his followers across the border into Xiongnu territory. The Xiongnu made him King Lu of the Eastern Hu.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, the High Ancestor died. Lu Wan thereupon led his followers to flee into the Xiongnu lands. The Xiongnu made him King Lu of the Eastern Hu.

entries.zh: 綰為蠻夷所侵奪，常思復歸。
entries.en: Among the barbarians, Wan was constantly harassed and plundered, and he never stopped longing to return home.
entries.literal: Wan was encroached upon and plundered by the barbarians, and he constantly thought of returning.

entries.zh: 居歲餘，死胡中。
entries.en: After little more than a year, he died among the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: After more than a year, he died among the Hu.

entries.zh: 上聞，乃赦趙、代吏人為豨所詿誤劫略者，皆赦之。
entries.en: When the Emperor heard the news, he pardoned all the officials and common people of Zhao and Dai who had been misled, deceived, or coerced by Chen Xi.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard, he pardoned the officials and people of Zhao and Dai who had been misled, deceived, or coerced by Xi; he pardoned them all.

entries.zh: 上自往，至邯鄲，喜曰：「豨不南據漳水，北守邯鄲，知其無能為也。」
entries.en: The Emperor went in person, and upon reaching Handan said with satisfaction: 'Chen Xi failed to hold the Zhang River to the south or defend Handan to the north. I know now that he is incapable of accomplishing anything.'
entries.literal: The Emperor went in person, and upon reaching Handan said with pleasure: 'Xi did not hold the Zhang River in the south or defend Handan in the north; I know he is incapable of accomplishing anything.'

entries.zh: 趙相奏斬常山守、尉，曰：「常山二十五城，豨反，亡其二十城。」
entries.en: The Chancellor of Zhao memorialized requesting the execution of the Governor and Commandant of Changshan, saying: 'Changshan has twenty-five cities, and when Chen Xi rebelled, twenty of them were lost.'
entries.literal: The Chancellor of Zhao memorialized requesting the execution of the Governor and Commandant of Changshan, saying: 'Changshan has twenty-five cities; when Xi rebelled, they lost twenty of them.'

entries.zh: 上問曰：「守、尉反乎？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, 'Had the Governor and Commandant rebelled?'
entries.literal: The Emperor asked: 'Did the Governor and Commandant rebel?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「不反。」
entries.en: The reply was: 'They did not rebel.'
entries.literal: The reply was: 'They did not rebel.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「是力不足也。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: 'Then they simply lacked the strength to resist.'
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'Then their strength was insufficient.'

entries.zh: 赦之，復以為常山守、尉。
entries.en: The Emperor pardoned them and restored them as Governor and Commandant of Changshan.
entries.literal: He pardoned them and reappointed them as Governor and Commandant of Changshan.

entries.zh: 上問周昌曰：「趙亦有壯士可令將者乎？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked Zhou Chang: 'Does Zhao have any brave men who could serve as generals?'
entries.literal: The Emperor asked Zhou Chang: 'Does Zhao also have brave men who could serve as generals?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「有四人。」
entries.en: Zhou Chang replied: 'There are four men.'
entries.literal: He replied: 'There are four men.'

entries.zh: 四人謁，上謾罵曰：「豎子能為將乎？」
entries.en: The four men came for an audience. The Emperor berated them, saying: 'Can rascals like you really serve as generals?'
entries.literal: The four men came for an audience. The Emperor abused them, saying: 'Can scoundrels like you serve as generals?'

entries.zh: 四人慚伏。
entries.en: The four men hung their heads in shame.
entries.literal: The four men bowed their heads in shame.

entries.zh: 上封之各千戶，以為將。
entries.en: The Emperor granted each of them a thousand-household fief and made them generals.
entries.literal: The Emperor enfeoffed each of them with a thousand households and appointed them as generals.

entries.zh: 左右諫曰：「從入蜀、漢，伐楚，功未遍行，今此何功而封？」
entries.en: His advisors remonstrated: 'Many who followed you into Shu and Han and campaigned against Chu have not yet been rewarded. What merits have these men earned to deserve enfeoffment?'
entries.literal: Those around him remonstrated, saying: 'Those who followed you into Shu and Han and campaigned against Chu have not all been rewarded; what merits do these men have to be enfeoffed?'

entries.zh: 上曰：「非若所知！
entries.en: The Emperor said, 'You do not understand this!
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'This is not something you understand!

entries.zh: 陳豨反，邯鄲以北皆豨有，吾以羽檄徵天下兵，未有至者，今唯獨邯鄲中兵耳。
entries.en: Chen Xi has rebelled, and everything north of Handan is in his hands. I sent urgent dispatches summoning troops from across the empire, but none have arrived. All I have now is the garrison of Handan.
entries.literal: Chen Xi has rebelled, and everything north of Handan is under his control. I sent urgent dispatches summoning troops from the realm, but none have arrived. Now I have only the garrison of Handan.

entries.zh: 吾胡愛四千戶封四人，不以慰趙子弟！」
entries.en: How could I begrudge four thousand households to enfeoff four men, if it serves to hearten the men of Zhao!'
entries.literal: How could I begrudge four thousand households to enfeoff four men, rather than use them to hearten the men of Zhao!'

entries.zh: 皆曰：「善。」
entries.en: Everyone agreed: 'Well said.'
entries.literal: All said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 於是上曰：「陳豨將誰？」
entries.en: The Emperor then asked: 'Who are Chen Xi's generals?'
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor asked: 'Who are Chen Xi's generals?'

entries.zh: 曰：「王黃、曼丘臣，皆故賈人。」
entries.en: Those present replied: 'Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen. Both are former merchants.'
entries.literal: The reply was: 'Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen; both are former merchants.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾知之矣。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, 'I understand the matter now.'
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'I know what to do.'

entries.zh: 乃各以千金購黃、臣等。
entries.en: He then placed a bounty of a thousand catties of gold each on the heads of Wang Huang, Manqiu Chen, and the others.
entries.literal: He then offered a bounty of a thousand catties of gold each for Wang Huang, Manqiu Chen, and the others.

entries.zh: 項籍之封諸王皆就國，韓王成以不從無功，不遣就國，更以為列侯。
entries.en: When Xiang Ji enfeoffed all the kings and they went to their domains, King Cheng of Han had not accompanied Xiang Ji and had no merit to his name, so he was not allowed to proceed to his domain. Instead, he was demoted to the rank of marquis.
entries.literal: When Xiang Ji enfeoffed all the kings and they each went to their kingdoms, King Cheng of Han, because he had not followed and had no merit, was not sent to his kingdom and was instead made a marquis.

entries.zh: 及聞漢遣韓信略韓地，乃令故項籍游吳時吳令鄭昌為韓王以距漢。
entries.en: When Xiang Ji heard that Han had dispatched Han Xin to take the Han territories, he appointed Zheng Chang, who had served as the Magistrate of Wu when Xiang Ji was traveling in Wu, as King of Han to resist the Han forces.
entries.literal: When he heard that Han had sent Han Xin to take the Han territory, he appointed Zheng Chang, who had been the Magistrate of Wu when Xiang Ji traveled in Wu, as King of Han to resist Han.

entries.zh: 漢二年，韓信略定韓十餘城。
entries.en: In the second year of the Han dynasty, Han Xin conquered more than ten cities in the Han territory.
entries.literal: In the second year of Han, Han Xin conquered and pacified more than ten cities of Han.

entries.zh: 漢王至河南，韓信急擊韓王昌陽城。
entries.en: When the King of Han arrived at Henan, Han Xin launched a swift attack on King Chang of Han at Yangcheng.
entries.literal: When the King of Han reached Henan, Han Xin urgently attacked King Chang of Han at Yangcheng.

entries.zh: 昌降，漢王乃立韓信為韓王，常將韓兵從。
entries.en: Chang surrendered, and the King of Han thereupon established Han Xin as King of Han. Xin regularly led the Han troops in the king's service.
entries.literal: Chang surrendered, and the King of Han then established Han Xin as King of Han; he constantly led Han troops in service.

entries.zh: 三年，漢王出滎陽，韓王信、周苛等守滎陽。
entries.en: In the third year, when the King of Han left Xingyang, Han Xin the King of Han, along with Zhou Ke and others, was left to defend Xingyang.
entries.literal: In the third year, the King of Han left Xingyang; Han King Xin, Zhou Ke, and others defended Xingyang.

entries.zh: 及楚敗滎陽，信降楚，已而得亡，復歸漢，漢復立以為韓王，竟從擊破項籍，天下定。
entries.en: When Chu defeated Xingyang, Xin surrendered to Chu. Later he managed to escape and returned to Han, and the Han court restored him as King of Han. He ultimately joined in the campaign that defeated Xiang Ji, and the realm was settled.
entries.literal: When Chu defeated Xingyang, Xin surrendered to Chu; afterward he managed to escape, returned to Han, and Han again established him as King of Han. He ultimately followed in defeating Xiang Ji, and the realm was settled.

entries.zh: 五年春，遂與剖符為韓王，王潁川。
entries.en: In the spring of the fifth year, he was formally invested as King of Han with the splitting of the tally, and he ruled over Yingchuan.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, he was thereupon invested as King of Han with the splitting of the tally, and ruled over Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 漢五年冬，以破項籍，乃使盧綰別將，與劉賈擊臨江王共尉，破之。
entries.en: In the winter of the fifth year of the Han dynasty, after the defeat of Xiang Ji, the Emperor dispatched Lu Wan to command a separate force. Together with Liu Jia, he attacked and defeated Gong Wei, the King of Linjiang.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Han, after defeating Xiang Ji, he sent Lu Wan to command a separate force, joining Liu Jia to attack Gong Wei, the King of Linjiang, and defeated him.

entries.zh: 七月還，從擊燕王臧荼，臧荼降。
entries.en: In the seventh month he returned and joined the campaign against Zang Tu, the King of Yan. Zang Tu surrendered.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he returned, and joined in attacking Zang Tu, the King of Yan; Zang Tu surrendered.

entries.zh: 高祖已定天下，諸侯非劉氏而王者七人。
entries.en: After the High Ancestor had settled the realm, there were seven men who held the title of king yet were not of the Liu surname.
entries.literal: After the High Ancestor had settled the realm, there were seven lords who were kings but not of the Liu surname.

entries.zh: 欲王盧綰，為群臣觖望。
entries.en: He wished to make Lu Wan a king, but this aroused resentment among his ministers.
entries.literal: He wished to make Lu Wan a king, but this caused resentment among his ministers.

entries.zh: 及虜臧荼，乃下詔諸將相列侯，擇群臣有功者以為燕王。
entries.en: After Zang Tu's capture, the Emperor issued a decree to his generals, ministers, and marquises, directing them to select a meritorious minister to serve as King of Yan.
entries.literal: After capturing Zang Tu, he issued a decree to the generals, ministers, and marquises, to select a meritorious minister to be King of Yan.

entries.zh: 群臣知上欲王盧綰，皆言曰：「太尉長安侯盧綰常從平定天下，功最多，可王燕。」
entries.en: The ministers, knowing the Emperor wished to make Lu Wan king, all declared: 'The Grand Commandant, the Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Wan, has followed the Emperor throughout the pacification of the realm and has the greatest merit. He should be made King of Yan.'
entries.literal: The ministers, knowing the Emperor wished to make Lu Wan king, all said: 'The Grand Commandant, the Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Wan, has constantly followed in pacifying the realm and has the most merit; he may be made King of Yan.'

entries.zh: 詔許之。
entries.en: The Emperor issued an edict granting the request.
entries.literal: An edict approved it.

entries.zh: 漢五年八月，乃立虜綰為燕王。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the fifth year of the Han dynasty, Lu Wan was established as King of Yan.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Han, Lu Wan was established as King of Yan.

entries.zh: 諸侯王得幸莫如燕王。
entries.en: Of all the vassal kings, none enjoyed greater imperial favor than the King of Yan.
entries.literal: Among the lords who were kings, none was as favored as the King of Yan.

entries.zh: 漢十一年秋，陳豨反代地，高祖如邯鄲擊豨兵，燕王綰亦擊其東北。
entries.en: In the autumn of the eleventh year, Chen Xi rebelled in the territory of Dai. The High Ancestor marched to Handan to attack Chen Xi's forces, and the King of Yan, Wan, also struck at his northeastern flank.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year of Han, Chen Xi rebelled in the territory of Dai. The High Ancestor went to Handan to attack Xi's forces, and the King of Yan, Wan, also attacked his northeast.

entries.zh: 當是時，陳豨使王黃求救匈奴。
entries.en: At this time, Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to request assistance from the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: At that time, Chen Xi sent Wang Huang to seek aid from the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 燕王綰亦使其臣張勝於匈奴，言豨等軍破。
entries.en: The King of Yan also sent his minister Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu to report that Chen Xi's army had been defeated.
entries.literal: The King of Yan, Wan, also sent his minister Zhang Sheng to the Xiongnu to announce that Xi's army had been defeated.

entries.zh: 張勝至胡，故燕王臧茶子衍出亡在胡，見張勝曰：「公所以重於燕者，以習胡事也。
entries.en: When Zhang Sheng reached the Xiongnu lands, Yan, the son of the former King of Yan Zang Tu, who had fled and was living among the Xiongnu, met him and said: 'The reason you are valued in Yan is that you understand the affairs of the northern peoples.
entries.literal: When Zhang Sheng reached the Hu lands, Yan, the son of the former King of Yan Zang Tu, who had fled and was living among the Hu, met Zhang Sheng and said: 'The reason you are valued by Yan is that you understand the affairs of the Hu.

entries.zh: 燕所以久存者，以諸侯數反，兵連不決也。
entries.en: The reason Yan has survived so long is that the various lords have frequently rebelled, keeping the armies tied down without a decisive resolution.
entries.literal: The reason Yan has long survived is that the lords have frequently rebelled, keeping the armies engaged without resolution.

entries.zh: 今公為燕欲急滅豨等，豨等已盡，次亦至燕，公等亦且為虜矣。
entries.en: Now you act on Yan's behalf, eager to destroy Chen Xi and his allies. But once they are finished, the court will turn its attention to Yan, and you and the others will become prisoners.
entries.literal: Now you act on Yan's behalf and wish to quickly destroy Xi and the rest; once Xi and the rest are finished, the next target will be Yan, and you and the others will become prisoners.

entries.zh: 公何不令燕且緩陳豨而與胡和？
entries.en: Why not have Yan ease up on the campaign against Chen Xi and make peace with the Xiongnu?
entries.literal: Why don't you have Yan slow its campaign against Chen Xi and make peace with the Hu?

entries.zh: 事寬，得長王燕；
entries.en: If the situation relaxes, you can remain king of Yan for a long time.
entries.literal: If things ease, you can long remain king of Yan;

entries.zh: 即有漢急，可以安國。」
entries.en: And should Han press you, you will have the means to keep the state secure.'
entries.literal: If there is urgency from Han, you can keep the state secure.'

entries.zh: 張勝以為然，豨私令匈奴助豨等擊燕。
entries.en: Zhang Sheng found this reasoning persuasive. Chen Xi secretly ordered the Xiongnu to assist his forces in raiding Yan.
entries.literal: Zhang Sheng thought this was right; Chen Xi secretly ordered the Xiongnu to help Xi and the others attack Yan.

entries.zh: 燕王綰疑張勝與胡反，上書請族張勝。
entries.en: The King of Yan suspected Zhang Sheng of conspiring with the Xiongnu to rebel and submitted a memorial requesting that Zhang Sheng's entire clan be executed.
entries.literal: The King of Yan, Wan, suspected Zhang Sheng of conspiring with the Hu to rebel, and submitted a memorial requesting the execution of Zhang Sheng's entire clan.

entries.zh: 勝還，具道所以為者。
entries.en: When Zhang Sheng returned, he explained the full reasoning behind his actions.
entries.literal: Sheng returned and fully explained the reasons for his actions.

entries.zh: 燕王寤，乃詐論它人，脫勝家屬，使得為匈奴閒，而陰使范齊之陳豨所，欲令久亡，連兵勿決。
entries.en: The King of Yan came to understand and so framed another man in Zhang Sheng's place, freed Sheng's family, and had Sheng serve as a liaison with the Xiongnu. Meanwhile, he secretly sent Fan Qi to Chen Xi's camp, intending to prolong the conflict and keep the armies locked in an unresolved stalemate.
entries.literal: The King of Yan understood, and so fraudulently convicted another person, freed Sheng's family, and had Sheng serve as an agent between the Xiongnu, while secretly sending Fan Qi to Chen Xi's camp, wishing to prolong the conflict and keep the armies engaged without resolution.

entries.zh: 高后時，盧綰妻子亡降漢，會高后病，不能見，舍燕邸，為欲置酒見之。
entries.en: During Empress Gao's regency, Lu Wan's wife and children fled and surrendered to Han. But as it happened, Empress Gao was ill and could not receive them. She lodged them at the Yan residence, intending to hold a banquet to meet them.
entries.literal: During the time of Empress Gao, Lu Wan's wife and children fled and surrendered to Han. It happened that Empress Gao was ill and could not receive them, so she lodged them at the Yan residence, intending to arrange a banquet to meet them.

entries.zh: 高祖竟崩，不得見。
entries.en: The High Ancestor was already dead, and so they never met him.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor had already died, and they could not meet him.

entries.zh: 盧綰妻亦病死。
entries.en: Lu Wan's wife also became ill and died.
entries.literal: Lu Wan's wife also fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 陳豨者，宛朐人也，不知始所以得從。
entries.en: Chen Xi was a man of Wanqu. It is not known how he first came to enter service.
entries.literal: Chen Xi was a man of Wanqu. It is not known how he first came to serve.

entries.zh: 及高祖七年冬，韓王信反，入匈奴，上至平城還，乃封豨為列侯，以趙相國將監趙、代邊兵，邊兵皆屬焉。
entries.en: In the winter of the High Ancestor's seventh year, after Han Xin the King of Han rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu and the Emperor had gone to Pingcheng and returned, Chen Xi was enfeoffed as a marquis and appointed Chancellor of Zhao with command over the border troops of Zhao and Dai. All the border forces were placed under his authority.
entries.literal: In the winter of the High Ancestor's seventh year, when Han King Xin rebelled and went over to the Xiongnu and the Emperor went to Pingcheng and returned, Chen Xi was enfeoffed as a marquis, appointed as Chancellor of Zhao to command and supervise the border troops of Zhao and Dai; all the border troops were placed under his authority.

entries.zh: 豨常告歸過趙，趙相周昌見豨賓客隨之者千餘乘，邯鄲官舍皆滿。
entries.en: Chen Xi frequently took leave and passed through Zhao. The Chancellor of Zhao, Zhou Chang, observed that more than a thousand carriages of retainers accompanied him, and the official guesthouses of Handan were all full to overflowing.
entries.literal: Xi often took leave and passed through Zhao. The Chancellor of Zhao, Zhou Chang, observed that more than a thousand carriages of retainers followed Xi, and the official guesthouses in Handan were all full.

entries.zh: 豨所以待賓客布衣交，皆出客下。
entries.en: Chen Xi treated his retainers with the humility of a man among equals, always placing himself below his guests in courtesy.
entries.literal: Xi treated his retainers with the deference of a commoner's friendship, always placing himself beneath his guests.

entries.zh: 豨還之代，周昌乃求入見。
entries.en: When Chen Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang sought an audience with the Emperor.
entries.literal: When Xi returned to Dai, Zhou Chang sought an audience with the Emperor.

entries.zh: 見上，具言豨賓客盛甚，擅兵於外數歲，恐有變。
entries.en: He had an audience with the Emperor and reported in full that Chen Xi's retinue was enormously large, that he had held military command far from the capital for several years, and that he feared trouble was brewing.
entries.literal: He saw the Emperor and fully reported that Xi's retainers were exceedingly numerous, that he had held military authority outside for several years, and that he feared there would be trouble.

entries.zh: 上乃令人覆案豨客居代者財物諸不法事，多連引豨。
entries.en: The Emperor then ordered an investigation into the finances and illegal activities of Chen Xi's retainers residing in Dai. Many of the cases implicated Chen Xi.
entries.literal: The Emperor then sent people to investigate and examine the finances and illegal activities of Xi's retainers residing in Dai; many of the cases implicated Xi.

entries.zh: 豨恐，陰令客通使王黃、曼丘臣所。
entries.en: Chen Xi grew fearful and secretly sent retainers to make contact with Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen.
entries.literal: Xi grew afraid and secretly sent retainers to communicate with Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen.

entries.zh: 及高祖十年七月，太上皇崩，使人召豨，豨稱病甚。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the tenth year, the Grand Supreme Emperor died. A messenger was sent to summon Chen Xi, but he claimed he was gravely ill.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the High Ancestor's tenth year, the Grand Supreme Emperor died. A messenger was sent to summon Xi, but Xi claimed he was gravely ill.

entries.zh: 九月，遂與王黃等反，自立為代王，劫略趙、代。
entries.en: In the ninth month, he rebelled together with Wang Huang and the others, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and plundered the territories of Zhao and Dai.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, he then rebelled with Wang Huang and others, proclaimed himself King of Dai, and plundered Zhao and Dai.

entries.zh: 十一年冬，漢兵擊斬陳豨將侯敞、王黃於曲逆下，破豨將張春於聊城，斬首萬餘。
entries.en: In the winter of the eleventh year, the Han army attacked and beheaded Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang below the walls of Quni, and defeated his general Zhang Chun at Liaocheng, taking more than ten thousand heads.
entries.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, the Han army attacked and beheaded Chen Xi's generals Hou Chang and Wang Huang below Quni, defeated Xi's general Zhang Chun at Liaocheng, and took more than ten thousand heads.

entries.zh: 太尉勃入定太原、代地。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant Bo marched in and pacified the territories of Taiyuan and Dai.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant Bo entered and pacified the territories of Taiyuan and Dai.

entries.zh: 十二月，上自擊東垣，東垣不下，卒罵上；
entries.en: In the twelfth month, the Emperor personally attacked Dongyuan. The city did not fall, and its soldiers hurled insults at the Emperor.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the Emperor personally attacked Dongyuan. Dongyuan did not fall, and the soldiers cursed the Emperor.

entries.zh: 東垣降，卒罵者斬之，不罵者黥之。
entries.en: When Dongyuan surrendered, those soldiers who had hurled insults were beheaded, and those who had not hurled insults were branded.
entries.literal: When Dongyuan surrendered, those soldiers who had cursed were beheaded, and those who had not cursed were branded.

entries.zh: 更命東垣為真定。
entries.en: He renamed Dongyuan as Zhending.
entries.literal: He changed the name of Dongyuan to Zhending.

entries.zh: 王黃、曼丘臣其麾下受購賞之，皆生得，以故陳豨軍遂敗。
entries.en: Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen were captured alive by their own subordinates, who had been lured by the bounties. With their generals gone, Chen Xi's army collapsed.
entries.literal: Wang Huang and Manqiu Chen were captured alive by those under their own command who had accepted the bounty reward; for this reason Chen Xi's army was ultimately defeated.

entries.zh: 高祖十二年冬，樊噲軍卒追斬豨於靈丘。
entries.en: In the winter of the twelfth year, soldiers under Fan Kuai's command pursued and beheaded Chen Xi at Lingqiu.
entries.literal: In the winter of the High Ancestor's twelfth year, soldiers of Fan Kuai's army pursued and beheaded Xi at Lingqiu.

entries.zh: 漢十年，信令王黃等說誤陳豨。
entries.en: In the tenth year of the Han dynasty, Xin had Wang Huang and others persuade and lead Chen Xi astray.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Han, Xin had Wang Huang and others persuade and mislead Chen Xi.

entries.zh: 十一年春，故韓王信復與胡騎入居參合，距漢。
entries.en: In the spring of the eleventh year, the former King of Han, Xin, once again rode in with Xiongnu cavalry and occupied Canhe, defying Han.
entries.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, the former King of Han, Xin, again entered with Hu cavalry and occupied Canhe, resisting Han.

entries.zh: 漢使柴將軍擊之，遺信書曰：「陛下寬仁，諸侯雖有畔亡，而復歸，輒復故位號，不誅也。
entries.en: Han sent General Chai to attack him. Chai sent a letter to Xin, saying: 'His Majesty is generous and benevolent. When lords have rebelled and fled but later returned, he has always restored their former titles and ranks without executing them.
entries.literal: Han sent General Chai to attack him. He sent Xin a letter saying: 'His Majesty is generous and benevolent; when lords have rebelled and fled but returned, he has always restored their former titles and ranks, without executing them.

entries.zh: 大王所知。
entries.en: As you well know, Great King.
entries.literal: This the Great King knows.

entries.zh: 今王以敗亡走胡，非有大罪，急自歸！」
entries.en: Now you fled to the Xiongnu after a defeat—this is not a grave crime. Return at once!'
entries.literal: Now the King, having been defeated and fled to the Hu, has not committed a great crime; hurry and return of your own accord!'

entries.zh: 韓王信報曰：「陛下擢仆起閭巷，南面稱孤，此仆之幸也。
entries.en: Han Xin the King of Han replied: 'His Majesty raised me from the common lanes to sit upon a throne facing south and bear the title of king. That was my great fortune.
entries.literal: Han King Xin replied: 'His Majesty raised me from the common lanes, to face south and be addressed as the Solitary One; this was my good fortune.

entries.zh: 滎陽之事，仆不能死，囚於項籍，此一罪也。
entries.en: At the siege of Xingyang, I could not manage to die but was taken prisoner by Xiang Ji. That is my first crime.
entries.literal: In the affair at Xingyang, I was unable to die but was captured by Xiang Ji; this is my first crime.

entries.zh: 及寇攻馬邑，仆不能堅守，以城降之，此二罪也。
entries.en: When the enemy attacked Mayi, I could not hold the city and surrendered it to them. That is my second crime.
entries.literal: When the enemy attacked Mayi, I was unable to defend it firmly and surrendered the city to them; this is my second crime.

entries.zh: 今反為寇將兵，與將軍爭一旦之命，此三罪也。
entries.en: Now I have turned to lead enemy troops and contend with you, General, for our lives in a single morning's battle. That is my third crime.
entries.literal: Now I have turned to lead enemy troops, contending with the General for survival on a single morning; this is my third crime.

entries.zh: 夫種、蠡無一罪，身死亡；
entries.en: Wen Zhong and Fan Li bore not a single crime, yet one was put to death and the other forced to flee.
entries.literal: Wen Zhong and Fan Li had not a single crime, yet they died or fled.

entries.zh: 今仆有三罪於陛下，而欲求活於世，此伍子胥所以僨於吳也。
entries.en: Now I bear three crimes against His Majesty and yet wish to go on living. This is precisely what brought Wu Zixu to his destruction in Wu.
entries.literal: Now I bear three crimes against His Majesty, yet wish to seek to live in the world; this is the reason Wu Zixu met his ruin in Wu.

entries.zh: 今仆亡匿山谷閒，旦暮乞貸蠻夷，仆之思歸，如痿人不忘起，盲者不忘視也，勢不可耳。」
entries.en: Now I hide among the mountain valleys, begging sustenance from the barbarians morning and evening. My longing to return home is like the cripple who never stops dreaming of walking, or the blind man who never stops dreaming of sight—but my circumstances will not permit it.'
entries.literal: Now I hide in the mountain valleys, begging from the barbarians morning and evening. My longing to return is like the lame who never forget walking, or the blind who never forget sight—but circumstances will not allow it.'

entries.zh: 遂戰。
entries.en: And so they fought.
entries.literal: They then fought.

entries.zh: 柴將軍屠參合，斬韓王信。
entries.en: General Chai stormed Canhe and beheaded Han Xin, the King of Han.
entries.literal: General Chai sacked Canhe and beheaded Han King Xin.

entries.zh: 信之入匈奴，與太子俱；
entries.en: When Xin went over to the Xiongnu, he brought his crown prince with him.
entries.literal: When Xin entered the Xiongnu lands, he brought the Crown Prince with him;

entries.zh: 及至穨當城，生子，因名曰穨當。
entries.en: When they reached the city of Tuidang, a son was born, and the boy was named Tuidang after the place.
entries.literal: When they reached the city of Tuidang, a son was born, and so he was named Tuidang.

entries.zh: 韓太子亦生子，命曰嬰。
entries.en: The Han crown prince also had a son, whom he named Ying.
entries.literal: The Han Crown Prince also had a son, whom he named Ying.

entries.zh: 至孝文十四年，穨當及嬰率其眾降漢。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Tuidang and Ying led their followers in submitting to Han.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Xiaowen, Tuidang and Ying led their followers to surrender to Han.

entries.zh: 漢封穨當為弓高侯，嬰為襄城侯。
entries.en: Han enfeoffed Tuidang as the Marquis of Gonggao and Ying as the Marquis of Xiangcheng.
entries.literal: Han enfeoffed Tuidang as Marquis of Gonggao and Ying as Marquis of Xiangcheng.

entries.zh: 吳楚軍時，弓高侯功冠諸將。
entries.en: During the Rebellion of Wu and Chu, the Marquis of Gonggao's achievements surpassed those of all the other generals.
entries.literal: During the war against Wu and Chu, the Marquis of Gonggao's merits were foremost among all the generals.

entries.zh: 傳子至孫，孫無子，失侯。
entries.en: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson, but the grandson had no heir, and the marquisate was lost.
entries.literal: The title passed to his son and then to his grandson; the grandson had no son, and the marquisate was lost.

entries.zh: 嬰孫以不敬失侯。
entries.en: Ying's grandson lost his marquisate on grounds of disrespect.
entries.literal: Ying's grandson lost the marquisate for disrespect.

entries.zh: 穨當孽孫韓嫣，貴幸，名富顯於當世。
entries.en: Tuidang's descendant through a concubine's line, Han Yan, became a court favorite, and his name and wealth were renowned in his generation.
entries.literal: Tuidang's descendant through a concubine's line, Han Yan, was honored and favored, and his name, wealth, and prominence were known in his time.

entries.zh: 其弟說，再封，數稱將軍，卒為案道侯。
entries.en: His younger brother Yue was enfeoffed a second time, served several times as general, and ultimately became the Marquis of Andao.
entries.literal: His younger brother Yue was twice enfeoffed, served as general several times, and ultimately became the Marquis of Andao.

entries.zh: 子代，歲餘坐法死。
entries.en: His son succeeded him, but within a year was convicted of a crime and put to death.
entries.literal: His son succeeded him; after more than a year, he was convicted of a crime and executed.

entries.zh: 後歲餘，說孫曾拜為龍頟侯，續說後。
entries.en: More than a year later, Yue's grandson Zeng was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Longe to continue Yue's line.
entries.literal: More than a year later, Yue's grandson Zeng was appointed Marquis of Longe, continuing Yue's line.

entries.zh: 孝景中六年，盧綰孫他之，以東胡王降，封為亞谷侯。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing, Lu Wan's grandson Tazhi surrendered in his capacity as King of the Eastern Hu and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yagu.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Lu Wan's grandson Tazhi surrendered as King of the Eastern Hu and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yagu.

entries.zh: 齊人聞王田儋死，乃立故齊王建之弟田假為齊王、田角為相、田間為將，以距諸侯。
entries.en: When the people of Qi heard that King Tian Dan was dead, they set up Tian Jia, younger brother of the former Qi king Jian, as king of Qi; appointed Tian Jiao chancellor; and made Tian Jian general, so as to resist the feudal lords.
entries.literal: When the people of Qi heard that King Tian Dan had died, they installed Tian Jia, younger brother of the former Qi king Jian, as king of Qi, made Tian Jiao chancellor, and made Tian Jian general, in order to resist the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 項羽既存趙，降章邯等，西屠咸陽，滅秦而立侯王也，乃徙齊王田市更王膠東，治即墨。
entries.en: After Xiang Yu saved Zhao and accepted the surrender of Zhang Han and his forces, he marched west to sack Xianyang, destroyed Qin, and parceled out the realm among the lords. He transferred King Tian Shi of Qi to the Kingdom of Jiaodong, with his seat at Jimo.
entries.literal: After Xiang Yu preserved Zhao and Zhang Han and others surrendered, he went west to slaughter Xianyang, extinguished Qin, and established the various lords and kings. He then moved King Tian Shi of Qi to be king of Jiaodong, governing from Jimo.

entries.zh: 齊將田都從共救趙，因入關，故立都為齊王，治臨淄。
entries.en: The Qi general Tian Du had joined the campaign to rescue Zhao and afterward entered the passes with the allied forces. For this he was made King of Qi, with his seat at Linzi.
entries.literal: The Qi general Tian Du followed and helped save Zhao, and then entered the pass. Therefore, he was established as King of Qi, governing from Linzi.

entries.zh: 故齊王建孫田安，項羽方渡河救趙，田安下濟北數城，引兵降項羽，項羽立田安為濟北王，治博陽。
entries.en: Tian An, a grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, had seized several cities in Jibei while Xiang Yu was crossing the river to relieve Zhao, and brought his forces over in submission. For this, Xiang Yu made him King of Jibei, with his seat at Boyang.
entries.literal: The grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, Tian An, when Xiang Yu was crossing the river to save Zhao, took several cities in Jibei and led troops to surrender to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu established Tian An as King of Jibei, governing from Boyang.

entries.zh: 田榮以負項梁不肯出兵助楚、趙攻秦，故不得王；
entries.en: Tian Rong, because he had failed Xiang Liang and refused to send troops to aid Chu and Zhao against Qin, was denied a kingdom.
entries.literal: Tian Rong, because he had failed Xiang Liang and refused to send troops to aid Chu and Zhao in attacking Qin, was not made a king.

entries.zh: 趙將陳餘亦失職，不得王：二人俱怨項王。
entries.en: The Zhao general Chen Yu had likewise been passed over and denied a kingdom. Both men harbored a deep resentment toward King Xiang.
entries.literal: The Zhao general Chen Yu likewise failed to obtain a kingdom. Both men resented King Xiang.

entries.zh: 項王聞之，大怒，乃北伐齊。
entries.en: When King Xiang learned of this, he flew into a rage and marched north to punish Qi.
entries.literal: King Xiang heard of it and was greatly angered. He then attacked Qi to the north.

entries.zh: 齊王田榮兵敗，走平原，平原人殺榮。
entries.en: King Tian Rong of Qi was defeated in battle and fled to Pingyuan, where the people of that place killed him.
entries.literal: King Tian Rong of Qi suffered defeat, fled to Pingyuan, and the people of Pingyuan killed Rong.

entries.zh: 項王遂燒夷齊城郭，所過者盡屠之。
entries.en: King Xiang then burned and leveled the cities of Qi, putting to the sword everyone in his path.
entries.literal: King Xiang then burned and razed the cities and walls of Qi, slaughtering all those he passed.

entries.zh: 齊人相聚畔之。
entries.en: The people of Qi banded together and rose against him.
entries.literal: The people of Qi gathered together and rebelled against him.

entries.zh: 榮弟橫，收齊散兵，得數萬人，反擊項羽於城陽。
entries.en: Rong's younger brother Tian Heng rallied the scattered soldiers of Qi, assembling tens of thousands of men, and struck back against Xiang Yu at Chengyang.
entries.literal: Rong's younger brother Heng gathered Qi's scattered troops, obtaining tens of thousands of men, and counterattacked Xiang Yu at Chengyang.

entries.zh: 而漢王率諸侯敗楚，入彭城。
entries.en: Meanwhile, the King of Han led a coalition of lords to defeat Chu and seized Pengcheng.
entries.literal: But the Han king led the various lords, defeated Chu, and entered Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 項羽聞之，乃醳齊而歸，擊漢於彭城，因連與漢戰，相距滎陽。
entries.en: When Xiang Yu learned of this, he abandoned the Qi campaign and rushed south to strike the Han forces at Pengcheng. From then on, the two sides fought a protracted war, facing off at Xingyang.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu heard of it and abandoned Qi to return, striking Han at Pengcheng. He then continuously battled with Han, confronting each other at Xingyang.

entries.zh: 以故田橫復得收齊城邑，立田榮子廣為齊王，而橫相之，專國政，政無巨細皆斷於相。
entries.en: With Xiang Yu's attention diverted, Tian Heng recovered the cities of Qi. He installed Tian Rong's son Guang as King of Qi and served as his chancellor, concentrating all power in his own hands. Every affair of state, great or small, was decided by the chancellor.
entries.literal: Therefore, Tian Heng was again able to gather Qi's cities and towns. He established Tian Rong's son Guang as King of Qi, while Heng served as his chancellor, monopolizing the state's government. All matters of government, great and small, were decided by the chancellor.

entries.zh: 橫定齊三年，漢王使酈生往說下齊王廣及其相國橫。
entries.en: After Heng had held Qi for three years, the King of Han sent the persuader Li Yiji to talk King Guang of Qi and his Chancellor Heng into surrendering.
entries.literal: After Heng had pacified Qi for three years, the Han king sent Li Sheng to go and persuade the submission of King Guang of Qi and his prime minister Heng.

entries.zh: 橫以為然，解其歷下軍。
entries.en: Heng found the arguments persuasive and stood down his garrison at Lixia.
entries.literal: Heng thought this was right and disbanded his army at Lixia.

entries.zh: 漢將韓信引兵且東擊齊。
entries.en: Meanwhile, the Han general Han Xin was leading his army east to attack Qi.
entries.literal: The Han general Han Xin led troops and was about to attack Qi to the east.

entries.zh: 齊初使華無傷、田解軍於歷下以距漢，漢使至，乃罷守戰備，縱酒，且遣使與漢平。
entries.en: Qi had previously stationed Hua Wushang and Tian Jie with troops at Lixia to hold off Han. But after the Han envoy arrived, they relaxed their defenses, gave themselves over to drinking, and dispatched envoys to negotiate peace with Han.
entries.literal: Qi had initially sent Hua Wushang and Tian Jie to station troops at Lixia to resist Han. When the Han envoy arrived, they stopped their guard and battle preparations, indulged in drinking wine, and moreover sent envoys to make peace with Han.

entries.zh: 漢將韓信已平趙、燕，用蒯通計，度平原，襲破齊歷下軍，因入臨淄。
entries.en: Han Xin, having already subdued Zhao and Yan, adopted Kuai Tong's stratagem and crossed the plains to launch a surprise attack on the Qi forces at Lixia. He then marched straight into Linzi.
entries.literal: The Han general Han Xin had already pacified Zhao and Yan. Using Kuai Tong's plan, he crossed the Pingyuan, attacked and broke the Qi army at Lixia, and then entered Linzi.

entries.zh: 齊王廣、相橫怒，以酈生賣己，而亨酈生。
entries.en: King Guang and Chancellor Heng were furious, convinced that Li Yiji had sold them out. They had him boiled alive.
entries.literal: King Guang of Qi and Chancellor Heng were angry, thinking Li Sheng had betrayed them, and cooked Li Sheng.

entries.zh: 齊王廣東走高密，相橫走博（陽），守相田光走城陽，將軍田既軍於膠東。
entries.en: King Guang fled east to Gaomi; Chancellor Heng escaped to Boyang; the Deputy Chancellor Tian Guang retreated to Chengyang; and General Tian Ji encamped with his forces in Jiaodong.
entries.literal: King Guang of Qi fled east to Gaomi; Chancellor Heng fled to Boyang; the defending chancellor Tian Guang fled to Chengyang; General Tian Ji encamped his army in Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 楚使龍且救齊，齊王與合軍高密。
entries.en: Chu dispatched Long Ju to rescue Qi, and the King of Qi joined forces with him at Gaomi.
entries.literal: Chu sent Long Ju to save Qi, and the King of Qi combined forces with him at Gaomi.

entries.zh: 漢將韓信與曹參破殺龍且，虜齊王廣。
entries.en: The Han general Han Xin, together with Cao Shen, defeated and killed Long Ju and took King Guang of Qi prisoner.
entries.literal: The Han general Han Xin, together with Cao Shen, broke and killed Long Ju, capturing King Guang of Qi.

entries.zh: 漢將灌嬰追得齊守相田光。
entries.en: The Han general Guan Ying pursued and captured the Qi Deputy Chancellor Tian Guang.
entries.literal: The Han general Guan Ying pursued and captured Qi's defender chancellor Tian Guang.

entries.zh: 至博（陽），而橫聞齊王死，自立為齊王，還擊嬰，嬰敗橫之軍於嬴下。
entries.en: When word reached Boyang that the King of Qi was dead, Heng proclaimed himself King of Qi and turned to attack Guan Ying. But Guan Ying routed Heng's forces below Ying.
entries.literal: When he reached Boyang, Heng heard that the King of Qi was dead. He proclaimed himself King of Qi, turned back to attack Guan Ying, and Guan Ying defeated Heng's army below Ying.

entries.zh: 田橫亡走梁，歸彭越。
entries.en: Tian Heng fled to Liang and took refuge with Peng Yue.
entries.literal: Tian Heng fled and went to Liang, joining Peng Yue.

entries.zh: 彭越是時居梁地，中立，且為漢，且為楚。
entries.en: At this time Peng Yue occupied the territory of Liang and maintained a position of neutrality, siding now with Han, now with Chu.
entries.literal: Peng Yue at this time resided in Liang territory, maintaining neutrality, sometimes for Han, sometimes for Chu.

entries.zh: 韓信已殺龍且，因令曹參進兵破殺田既於膠東，使灌嬰破殺齊將田吸於千乘。
entries.en: After Han Xin killed Long Ju, he sent Cao Shen to advance into Jiaodong and destroy Tian Ji, and dispatched Guan Ying to defeat and kill the Qi general Tian Xi at Qiancheng.
entries.literal: After Han Xin had killed Long Ju, he ordered Cao Shen to advance troops and break and kill Tian Ji at Jiaodong, and had Guan Ying break and kill the Qi general Tian Xi at Qiancheng.

entries.zh: 韓信遂平齊，乞自立為齊假王，漢因而立之。
entries.en: Han Xin thus completed the conquest of Qi and petitioned to be made its Acting King. The King of Han granted his request.
entries.literal: Han Xin then pacified Qi and begged to establish himself as acting King of Qi, and Han therefore established him as such.

entries.zh: 後歲餘，漢滅項籍，漢王立為皇帝，以彭越為梁王。
entries.en: More than a year later, Han destroyed Xiang Ji. The King of Han ascended as Emperor and made Peng Yue King of Liang.
entries.literal: After more than a year, Han extinguished Xiang Ji, and the Han king established himself as emperor, making Peng Yue King of Liang.

entries.zh: 田橫懼誅，而與其徒屬五百餘人入海，居島中。
entries.en: Tian Heng, fearing execution, sailed out to sea with more than five hundred of his followers and took up residence on an island.
entries.literal: Tian Heng feared execution and, together with over five hundred of his followers, entered the sea and resided on an island.

entries.zh: 高帝聞之，以為田橫兄弟本定齊，齊人賢者多附焉，今在海中不收，後恐為亂，乃使使赦田橫罪而召之。
entries.en: Emperor Gao heard of this and reflected that the Tian brothers had been the ones to pacify Qi, and that many of the ablest men in Qi were devoted to them. If they were left at large on the sea, they might one day stir up trouble. He therefore sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng and summon him to court.
entries.literal: The Gao Emperor heard of this and thought that the Tian Heng brothers had originally pacified Qi, and many worthy men of Qi were attached to them. If they were not brought in from the sea now, he feared they might cause chaos later. He then sent an envoy to pardon Tian Heng's crime and summon him.

entries.zh: 田橫因謝曰：「臣亨陛下之使酈生，今聞其弟酈商為漢將而賢，臣恐懼，不敢奉詔，請為庶人，守海島中。」
entries.en: Tian Heng declined, saying, "I boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji alive. Now I hear that his younger brother Li Shang serves as a Han general and is a man of ability. I am terrified and dare not obey the summons. I beg leave to remain a commoner and keep to my island."
entries.literal: Tian Heng thereupon declined, saying, "Your servant boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear that his younger brother Li Shang is a Han general and a man of ability. Your servant is afraid and dares not obey the summons. I beg to remain a commoner and guard my island in the sea."

entries.zh: 使還報，高皇帝乃詔衛尉酈商曰：「齊王田橫即至，人馬從者敢動搖者致族夷！」
entries.en: When the envoy returned with this reply, Emperor Gao issued an edict to Li Shang, the Commandant of Guards: "Tian Heng, the former King of Qi, is about to arrive. If anyone among his retinue so much as stirs, the offender's entire clan shall be exterminated!"
entries.literal: When the envoy returned and reported, Emperor Gao issued an edict to the Commandant of Guards, Li Shang, saying, "When Tian Heng, King of Qi, arrives, if any man or horse among his followers dares to stir, his clan shall be exterminated to the last!"

entries.zh: 乃復使使持節具告以詔商狀，曰：「田橫來，大者王，小者乃侯耳；
entries.en: He then sent another envoy bearing the imperial tally to inform Tian Heng in full of the edict restraining Li Shang, adding, "If Tian Heng comes, at best he shall be made a king, at least a marquis.
entries.literal: He then sent another envoy bearing the imperial tally to inform Tian Heng fully of the edict to Li Shang, saying, "If Tian Heng comes, at most he will be made a king, at least a marquis.

entries.zh: 不來，且舉兵加誅焉。」
entries.en: If he does not come, troops will be sent to destroy him."
entries.literal: If he does not come, troops will be raised to punish him."

entries.zh: 田橫乃與其客二人乘傳詣雒陽。
entries.en: Tian Heng then set out with two of his retainers, traveling by relay carriage toward Luoyang.
entries.literal: Tian Heng then, together with two of his guests, rode a relay chariot to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 未至三十里，至尸鄉廄置，橫謝使者曰：「人臣見天子當洗沐。」
entries.en: When they were still thirty li from the capital, they reached the relay station at Shixiang. Heng addressed the envoy, "A subject about to be received by the Son of Heaven ought first to bathe and purify himself."
entries.literal: Before they had gone thirty li, they reached the relay station at Shixiang. Heng declined to the envoy, saying, "When a subject is to see the Son of Heaven, he ought to bathe and purify himself."

entries.zh: 止留。
entries.en: He halted there and remained.
entries.literal: He stopped and stayed.

entries.zh: 謂其客曰：「橫始與漢王俱南面稱孤，今漢王為天子，而橫乃為亡虜而北面事之，其恥固已甚矣。
entries.en: He said to his retainers, "At first I and the King of Han both faced south and styled ourselves sovereign. Now the King of Han is Son of Heaven, and I am nothing but a fugitive who must face north and serve him. The shame of it is already beyond bearing.
entries.literal: He said to his guests, "At first I and the King of Han both faced south and styled ourselves sovereigns; now the King of Han is Son of Heaven, while I am a fugitive captive who must face north and serve him—the shame is already very great.

entries.zh: 且吾亨人之兄，與其弟并肩而事其主，縱彼畏天子之詔，不敢動我，我獨不愧於心乎？
entries.en: Moreover, I boiled a man's elder brother alive, and now I am to stand shoulder to shoulder with his younger brother in serving the same lord. Even if Li Shang fears the imperial edict and dares not touch me, can I alone feel no shame in my heart?
entries.literal: Moreover, I boiled a man's elder brother alive, and am to stand shoulder to shoulder with his younger brother in serving the same lord. Even if he fears the Son of Heaven's edict and dares not touch me, can I alone feel no shame in my heart?

entries.zh: 且陛下所以欲見我者，不過欲一見吾面貌耳。
entries.en: Moreover, the only reason His Majesty wishes to see me is to look upon my face once.
entries.literal: Moreover, the reason Your Majesty wishes to see me is no more than to look upon my face once.

entries.zh: 今陛下在洛陽，今斬吾頭，馳三十里閒，形容尚未能敗，猶可觀也。」
entries.en: His Majesty is in Luoyang. If my head is cut off now and rushed there at a gallop—a mere thirty li—my features will not yet have decayed. He may still look upon them."
entries.literal: His Majesty is now in Luoyang. If my head is cut off now and rushed thirty li, my features will not yet have decayed—he may still look upon them."

entries.zh: 遂自剄，令客奉其頭，從使者馳奏之高帝。
entries.en: With that he cut his own throat. He ordered his guest to present his head; the guest followed the envoy and rode at a gallop to present it to Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: He then slit his own throat and ordered his guest to present his head, following the envoy to gallop and present it to the Gao Emperor.

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「嗟乎，有以也夫！
entries.en: Emperor Gao exclaimed, "Alas! There was something to this man indeed!
entries.literal: Emperor Gao said, "Alas! There was reason in it!

entries.zh: 起自布衣，兄弟三人更王，豈不賢乎哉！」
entries.en: Rising from common cloth, three brothers took the throne in turn—were they not men of surpassing worth!"
entries.literal: Rising from common cloth, three brothers took the throne in turn—were they not worthy men!"

entries.zh: 為之流涕，而拜其二客為都尉，發卒二千人，以王者禮葬田橫。
entries.en: He wept for Tian Heng, appointed the two retainers as commandants, and dispatched two thousand soldiers to bury Tian Heng with the rites due a king.
entries.literal: He shed tears for him and appointed his two guests as commandants, sending two thousand troops to bury Tian Heng with the rites of a king.

entries.zh: 既葬，二客穿其冢旁孔，皆自剄，下從之。
entries.en: After the burial, the two retainers dug openings beside his tomb, slit their own throats, and fell into the earth to follow their lord in death.
entries.literal: After the burial, the two guests dug holes beside his tomb, all slit their throats, and descended to follow him.

entries.zh: 高帝聞之，乃大驚，大田橫之客皆賢。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao heard of this, he was deeply shaken and declared that all of Tian Heng's followers were men of the highest worth.
entries.literal: The Gao Emperor heard of this and was greatly astonished, praising that all of Tian Heng's guests were worthy.

entries.zh: 吾聞其餘尚五百人在海中，使使召之。
entries.en: He learned that some five hundred followers still remained on the island and sent envoys to summon them.
entries.literal: He heard that more than five hundred of them still remained at sea and sent envoys to summon them.

entries.zh: 至則聞田橫死，亦皆自殺。
entries.en: When the envoys arrived and the followers learned that Tian Heng was dead, every one of them took his own life.
entries.literal: When they arrived and heard that Tian Heng had died, they all committed suicide as well.

entries.zh: 於是乃知田橫兄弟能得士也。
entries.en: Only then did the world understand the power the Tian brothers had to command the loyalty of men.
entries.literal: Then he knew that the Tian Heng brothers were able to attract worthy men.

entries.zh: 田儋者，狄人也，故齊王田氏族也。
entries.en: Tian Dan was a native of Di and a descendant of the Tian clan, the former royal house of Qi.
entries.literal: Tian Dan was a man of Di. He was of the clan of the former kings of Qi, the Tian family.

entries.zh: 儋從弟田榮，榮弟田橫，皆豪，宗彊，能得人。
entries.en: His cousin Tian Rong and Rong's younger brother Tian Heng were both bold and formidable men. Their clan wielded great power and could rally followers to their cause.
entries.literal: Dan's cousin Tian Rong, and Rong's younger brother Tian Heng, were all bold and formidable. Their clan was powerful and they could win men over.

entries.zh: 張丞相蒼者，陽武人也。
entries.en: Chancellor Zhang Cang was a native of Yangwu.
entries.literal: Zhang Cang, the Chancellor, was a man from Yangwu.

entries.zh: 好書律歷。
entries.en: He had a passion for written records, legal codes, and calendrical calculations.
entries.literal: He was fond of books, laws, and calendars.

entries.zh: 秦時為御史，主柱下方書。
entries.en: During the Qin dynasty, he served as a Censor and was responsible for the official documents stored beneath the pillar.
entries.literal: During Qin times he served as a censor in charge of the square books below the pillar.

entries.zh: 有罪，亡歸。
entries.en: Having been found guilty of an offense, he fled and returned home.
entries.literal: He committed a crime and fled back home.

entries.zh: 及沛公略地過陽武，蒼以客從攻南陽。
entries.en: When the Duke of Pei was campaigning through the region and passed through Yangwu, Cang joined him as a retainer and followed him to attack Nanyang.
entries.literal: When the Duke of Pei was raiding territory and passed through Yangwu, Cang followed as a guest to attack Nanyang.

entries.zh: 蒼坐法當斬，解衣伏質，身長大，肥白如瓠，時王陵見而怪其美士，乃言沛公，赦勿斬。
entries.en: Cang was later convicted of a crime and sentenced to execution. When he stripped off his robes and lay upon the chopping block, his tall frame and skin as plump and white as a gourd caught the eye of Wang Ling, who marveled at such a fine specimen of a man. Wang Ling spoke to the Duke of Pei on his behalf, and Cang was pardoned.
entries.literal: Cang was convicted by law and should be beheaded. He loosened his clothes and lay on the execution block. His body was tall and large, fat and white like a gourd. At the time Wang Ling saw him and marveled at this beautiful gentleman, so he spoke to the Duke of Pei, who pardoned him and did not behead him.

entries.zh: 遂從西入武關，至咸陽。
entries.en: He then followed the army westward through Wuguan Pass and on to Xianyang.
entries.literal: He then followed west through Wuguan and arrived at Xianyang.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，入漢中，還定三秦。
entries.en: After the Duke of Pei was established as King of Han, he withdrew to Hanzhong and then returned to subdue the Three Qin kingdoms.
entries.literal: The Duke of Pei was established as King of Han, entered Hanzhong, and returned to settle the Three Qin.

entries.zh: 陳餘擊走常山王張耳，耳歸漢，漢乃以張蒼為常山守。
entries.en: When Chen Yu attacked and drove out Zhang Er, the King of Changshan, Er sought refuge with Han. Han then appointed Zhang Cang as the Governor of Changshan.
entries.literal: Chen Yu struck and drove away Changshan king Zhang Er. Er returned to Han, and Han then made Zhang Cang Changshan governor.

entries.zh: 從淮陰侯擊趙，蒼得陳餘。
entries.en: He accompanied the Marquis of Huaiyin in the campaign against Zhao, and Cang captured Chen Yu.
entries.literal: He followed Marquis Huaiyin in striking Zhao, and Cang captured Chen Yu.

entries.zh: 趙地已平，漢王以蒼為代相，備邊寇。
entries.en: Once the lands of Zhao were pacified, the King of Han appointed Cang as Chancellor of Dai to defend against raids from the northern frontier.
entries.literal: Once Zhao lands were pacified, the Han king made Cang chancellor of Dai to prepare against border bandits.

entries.zh: 已而徙為趙相，相趙王耳。
entries.en: Before long, he was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Zhao under King Zhang Er.
entries.literal: Soon after he was moved to serve as chancellor of Zhao, chancellor to Zhao king Er.

entries.zh: 耳卒，相趙王敖。
entries.en: After Er died, he continued as Chancellor under King Ao of Zhao.
entries.literal: Er died, and he served as chancellor to Zhao king Ao.

entries.zh: 復徙相代王。
entries.en: He was then transferred again to serve as chancellor to the King of Dai.
entries.literal: He was again moved to serve as chancellor to the Dai king.

entries.zh: 燕王臧荼反，高祖往擊之。
entries.en: When Zang Tu, the King of Yan, rose in rebellion, Emperor Gaozu personally led a campaign against him.
entries.literal: Yan king Zang Tu rebelled, and Gaozu went to strike him.

entries.zh: 蒼以代相從攻臧荼有功，以六年中封為北平侯，食邑千二百戶。
entries.en: For his meritorious service as Chancellor of Dai in the campaign against Zang Tu, he was enfeoffed in the middle of the sixth year as Marquis of Beiping, with a fief of twelve hundred households.
entries.literal: Cang as Dai chancellor followed in attacking Zang Tu with merit. In the middle of the sixth year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beiping, with a food fief of one thousand two hundred households.

entries.zh: 周昌者，沛人也。
entries.en: Zhou Chang was a native of Pei.
entries.literal: Zhou Chang was a man from Pei.

entries.zh: 其從兄曰周苛，秦時皆為泗水卒史。
entries.en: His elder cousin was named Zhou Ke. During the Qin dynasty, both of them served as junior clerks in the Sishui commandery.
entries.literal: His elder cousin was called Zhou Ke. During Qin times they both served as soldier secretaries in Sishui.

entries.zh: 及高祖起沛，擊破泗水守監，於是周昌、周苛自卒史從沛公，沛公以周昌為職志，周苛為客。
entries.en: When Gaozu rose at Pei and defeated the Sishui Guardian and Inspector, Zhou Chang and Zhou Ke left their positions as junior clerks to follow the Duke of Pei. The Duke appointed Zhou Chang as a duty recorder and Zhou Ke as a retainer.
entries.literal: When Gaozu rose at Pei and struck and broke the Sishui guard and supervisor, then Zhou Chang and Zhou Ke followed the Duke of Pei from their positions as soldier secretaries. The Duke of Pei made Zhou Chang duty recorder and Zhou Ke a guest.

entries.zh: 從入關，破秦。
entries.en: They followed him through the passes and helped bring down the Qin dynasty.
entries.literal: They followed in entering the pass and breaking Qin.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，以周苛為御史大夫，周昌為中尉。
entries.en: When the Duke of Pei was established as King of Han, he appointed Zhou Ke as Censor Grand Master and Zhou Chang as Commandant of the Capital.
entries.literal: The Duke of Pei was established as King of Han. He made Zhou Ke Censor Grand Master and Zhou Chang Central Commandery Captain.

entries.zh: 遷為計相，一月，更以列侯為主計四歲。
entries.en: He was promoted to the position of Accounting Chancellor. After one month, he was reassigned to serve as Chief Accountant for four years while retaining his rank as a marquis.
entries.literal: He was moved to serve as accounting chancellor. After one month, he was changed to serve as chief accountant for four years as a ranked marquis.

entries.zh: 是時蕭何為相國，而張蒼乃自秦時為柱下史，明習天下圖書計籍。
entries.en: At this time Xiao He served as Prime Minister, while Zhang Cang, who had served as the Historian Beneath the Pillar since the Qin dynasty, was thoroughly versed in the empire's maps, documents, and accounting records.
entries.literal: At this time Xiao He served as prime minister, but Zhang Cang had since Qin times served as the historian below the pillar, clearly versed in the world's maps, books, and accounting records.

entries.zh: 蒼又善用算律歷，故令蒼以列侯居相府，領主郡國上計者。
entries.en: Since Cang was also skilled in mathematics, legal codes, and calendrical science, he was ordered to reside in the Prime Minister's office as a ranked marquis, overseeing the account submissions from the commanderies and kingdoms.
entries.literal: Cang was again skilled in using calculations, laws, and calendars, so he was ordered to reside in the prime minister's mansion as a ranked marquis, leading those in charge of commandery and state account submissions.

entries.zh: 黥布反亡，漢立皇子長為淮南王，而張蒼相之。
entries.en: After Qing Bu rebelled and was destroyed, Han established the imperial prince Chang as King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang served as his chancellor.
entries.literal: Qing Bu rebelled and was destroyed. Han established imperial son Chang as King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang served as his chancellor.

entries.zh: 十四年，遷為御史大夫。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year, he was promoted to the position of Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was moved to serve as Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 漢王四年，楚圍漢王滎陽急，漢王遁出去，而使周苛守滎陽城。
entries.en: In the fourth year of the King of Han's reign, Chu laid a desperate siege to the King of Han at Xingyang. The King of Han escaped, leaving Zhou Ke behind to defend the city.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of the Han king, Chu urgently surrounded the Han king at Xingyang. The Han king fled out, but sent Zhou Ke to guard Xingyang city.

entries.zh: 楚破滎陽城，欲令周苛將。
entries.en: When Chu breached the walls of Xingyang, they tried to compel Zhou Ke to serve as a general on their side.
entries.literal: Chu broke Xingyang city and wished to make Zhou Ke lead.

entries.zh: 苛罵曰：「若趣降漢王！
entries.en: Zhou Ke cursed him: "You should surrender to the King of Han at once!
entries.literal: Zhou Ke cursed and said, "Hurry and surrender to the King of Han!

entries.zh: 不然，今為虜矣！」
entries.en: If not, you will soon be captives!"
entries.literal: If not, you will soon be captives!"

entries.zh: 項羽怒，亨周苛。
entries.en: Xiang Yu, enraged, had Zhou Ke boiled alive.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu was angry and cooked Zhou Ke.

entries.zh: 於是乃拜周昌為御史大夫。
entries.en: Zhou Chang was then appointed as the new Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: Then he appointed Zhou Chang as Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 常從擊破項籍。
entries.en: He regularly accompanied the campaigns that defeated Xiang Ji.
entries.literal: He often followed in striking and breaking Xiang Ji.

entries.zh: 以六年中與蕭、曹等俱封：封周昌為汾陰侯；
entries.en: In the sixth year, he was enfeoffed along with Xiao He, Cao Shen, and the others, becoming Marquis of Fenyin.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed together with Xiao He, Cao Shen, and the others; Zhou Chang was made Marquis of Fenyin.

entries.zh: 周苛子周成以父死事，封為高景侯。
entries.en: Zhou Ke's son Zhou Cheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaojing in recognition of his father's death in the line of duty.
entries.literal: Zhou Ke's son Zhou Cheng, for his father's death in service, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaojing.

entries.zh: 是後戚姬子如意為趙王，年十歲，高祖憂即萬歲之後不全也。
entries.en: After this, Consort Qi's son Ruyi was made King of Zhao at the age of ten. Gaozu worried that after his own death, the boy would not be able to preserve himself.
entries.literal: After this, Consort Qi's son Ruyi became Zhao king, aged ten. Gaozu worried that after his ten thousand years he would not be whole.

entries.zh: 趙堯年少，為符璽御史。
entries.en: Zhao Yao, though young, was serving as the Censor in Charge of Tallies and Seals.
entries.literal: Zhao Yao was young in years, serving as tally and seal censor.

entries.zh: 趙人方與公謂御史大夫周昌曰：「君之史趙堯，年雖少，然奇才也，君必異之，是且代君之位。」
entries.en: A man of Zhao named Fang Yugong said to Censor-in-Chief Zhou Chang, "Your secretary Zhao Yao, though still young, is nevertheless a man of exceptional talent. You must treat him differently—he will one day take your place."
entries.literal: A man of Zhao named Fang Yugong said to Censor-in-Chief Zhou Chang, "Your secretary Zhao Yao, though young in years, is nevertheless an exceptional talent. You must treat him differently. He will one day take your place."

entries.zh: 周昌笑曰；
entries.en: Zhou Chang laughed and said,
entries.literal: Zhou Chang laughed and said,

entries.zh: 「堯年少，刀筆吏耳，何能至是乎！」
entries.en: "Yao is young—a mere clerk. How could he rise so high!"
entries.literal: "Yao is young—a mere clerk with brush and knife. How could he reach this!"

entries.zh: 居頃之，趙堯侍高祖。
entries.en: Before long, Zhao Yao was attending upon Gaozu.
entries.literal: After a short time, Zhao Yao attended Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖獨心不樂，悲歌，群臣不知上之所以然。
entries.en: Gaozu was troubled at heart and sang melancholy songs, but none of his ministers understood the reason for the emperor's sorrow.
entries.literal: Gaozu alone was unhappy in heart, sang sadly. The group of ministers did not know the cause of the sovereign's sadness.

entries.zh: 趙堯進請問曰：「陛下所為不樂，非為趙王年少而戚夫人與呂后有卻邪？
entries.en: Zhao Yao stepped forward and asked, "Your Majesty is unhappy—is it not because the King of Zhao is still young, and because Consort Qi and Empress Lü are estranged?
entries.literal: Zhao Yao advanced and asked, "Your Majesty is unhappy—is it not because the King of Zhao is young and because Consort Qi and Empress Lü are at odds?

entries.zh: 備萬歲之後而趙王不能自全乎？」
entries.en: Are you worried that after Your Majesty passes away the King of Zhao will not be able to preserve himself?"
entries.literal: Are you worried that after Your Majesty's death the King of Zhao will not be able to preserve himself?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「然。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "That is so.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "That is so.

entries.zh: 吾私憂之，不知所出。」
entries.en: I have been worrying about this in private and cannot find a way out."
entries.literal: I privately worry about it, and do not know what to do."

entries.zh: 堯曰：「陛下獨宜為趙王置貴彊相，及呂后、太子、群臣素所敬憚乃可。」
entries.en: Yao said, "Your Majesty should establish for the King of Zhao a noble and powerful chancellor, one whom Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the ministers have always revered and feared. Only then will it be possible."
entries.literal: Yao said, "Your Majesty should appoint a noble and powerful chancellor for the King of Zhao, one whom Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the ministers have always revered and feared. Only such a man will do."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「然。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Correct.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Correct.

entries.zh: 吾念之欲如是，而群臣誰可者？」
entries.en: I have thought about it and want to do this, but which of the ministers would be suitable?"
entries.literal: I think it want like this, but group ministers who suitable ones?"

entries.zh: 堯曰：「御史大夫周昌，其人堅忍質直，且自呂后、太子及大臣皆素敬憚之。
entries.en: Yao said, "Censor Grand Master Zhou Chang is firm, enduring, simple, and upright. Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the great ministers have all always revered and feared him.
entries.literal: Yao said, "Censor Grand Master Zhou Chang is firm, resolute, honest, and upright. Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the great ministers have all long revered and feared him.

entries.zh: 獨昌可。」
entries.en: Chang alone would be equal to the task."
entries.literal: Chang alone is suitable."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「善。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Good."
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Good."

entries.zh: 於是乃召周昌，謂曰：「吾欲固煩公，公彊為我相趙王。」
entries.en: He then summoned Zhou Chang and told him, "I truly must trouble you: force yourself to go on my behalf and serve as chancellor to the King of Zhao."
entries.literal: Then he summoned Zhou Chang and said, "I wish indeed to trouble you. You must go and serve as chancellor to the King of Zhao on my behalf."

entries.zh: 周昌泣曰：「臣初起從陛下，陛下獨柰何中道而棄之於諸侯乎？」
entries.en: Zhou Chang wept and said, "When I first rose and followed Your Majesty, how can Your Majesty abandon me midway among the feudal lords?"
entries.literal: Zhou Chang wept and said, "When this minister first rose and followed Your Majesty, how can Your Majesty alone abandon me midway among the feudal lords?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「吾極知其左遷，然吾私憂趙王，念非公無可者。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "I know perfectly well that this is a demotion for you, but I am privately worried about the King of Zhao, and I can think of no one suitable except you.
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "I know full well this is a demotion for you, but I worry privately for the King of Zhao. I think there is no one suitable except you.

entries.zh: 公不得已彊行！」
entries.en: You have no choice but to go!"
entries.literal: You have no choice but to go!"

entries.zh: 於是徙御史大夫周昌為趙相。
entries.en: And so Censor Grand Master Zhou Chang was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Zhao.
entries.literal: Then he moved Censor Grand Master Zhou Chang to serve as Zhao chancellor.

entries.zh: 昌為人彊力，敢直言，自蕭、曹等皆卑下之。
entries.en: Chang was a man of great strength and force of character, unafraid to speak his mind. Even Xiao He, Cao Shen, and the other ministers all deferred to him.
entries.literal: Chang as a person was strong and forceful, daring to speak directly. Even Xiao, Cao, and others all treated him with deference.

entries.zh: 昌嘗燕時入奏事，高帝方擁戚姬，昌還走，高帝逐得，騎周昌項，問曰：「我何如主也？」
entries.en: Once during a feast Chang came in to present a memorial. Emperor Gaozu was embracing Consort Qi. Chang turned and fled. The emperor chased him down, climbed onto Zhou Chang's neck, and asked, "What kind of ruler am I?"
entries.literal: Once at a feast Chang entered to present a memorial. Emperor Gaozu was just embracing Consort Qi. Chang turned and ran. The emperor chased and caught him, climbed onto Zhou Chang's neck, and asked, "What kind of ruler am I?"

entries.zh: 昌仰曰：「陛下即桀紂之主也。」
entries.en: Chang looked up and said, "Your Majesty is just the sort of ruler Jie and Zhou were."
entries.literal: Chang looked up and said, "Your Majesty is a ruler like Jie and Zhou."

entries.zh: 於是上笑之，然尤憚周昌。
entries.en: The emperor laughed at this, yet he held Zhou Chang in particular awe.
entries.literal: Then the sovereign laughed at it, but especially feared Zhou Chang.

entries.zh: 及帝欲廢太子，而立戚姬子如意為太子，大臣固爭之，莫能得；
entries.en: When the emperor wished to depose the crown prince and establish Consort Qi's son Ruyi as crown prince, the great ministers remonstrated firmly, but none could prevail.
