entries.literal: When the emperor wished to depose the crown prince and establish Consort Qi's son Ruyi as crown prince, the great ministers firmly remonstrated, but none could prevail.

entries.zh: 上以留侯策即止。
entries.en: The emperor abandoned the plan on account of the stratagem devised by the Marquis of Liu.
entries.literal: The sovereign stopped because of Marquis Liu's strategy.

entries.zh: 而周昌廷爭之彊，上問其說，昌為人吃，又盛怒，曰：「臣口不能言，然臣期期知其不可。
entries.en: But Zhou Chang opposed the plan fiercely in court. When the emperor asked him to explain, Chang, who stuttered and was now beside himself with anger, said, "My mouth cannot speak well, but I k-k-know this must not be done.
entries.literal: But Zhou Chang disputed it forcefully at court. The emperor asked for his reasoning. Chang, who stuttered, was greatly angered again and said, "This minister's mouth cannot speak, yet this minister qi-qi knows it is impossible.

entries.zh: 陛下雖欲廢太子，臣期期不奉詔。」
entries.en: Even if Your Majesty wishes to depose the crown prince, this minister will s-s-steadfastly refuse to obey the decree."
entries.literal: Even if Your Majesty wishes to depose the crown prince, this minister qi-qi will not accept the decree."

entries.zh: 上欣然而笑。
entries.en: The emperor broke into a delighted laugh.
entries.literal: The sovereign laughed happily.

entries.zh: 既罷，呂后側耳於東箱聽，見周昌，為跪謝曰：「微君，太子幾廢。」
entries.en: After the audience ended, Empress Lu, who had been listening from the eastern chamber, saw Zhou Chang and knelt to thank him, saying, "Without you, the crown prince would nearly have been deposed."
entries.literal: When the audience ended, Empress Lü listened from the eastern chamber. Seeing Zhou Chang, she knelt and thanked him, saying, "But for you, the crown prince would almost have been deposed."

entries.zh: 既行久之，高祖持御史大夫印弄之，曰：「誰可以為御史大夫者？」
entries.en: After he had gone for a long time, Gaozu held the Censor Grand Master seal and played with it, saying, "Who can serve as Censor Grand Master?"
entries.literal: Already go long time, Gao Zu hold censor grand master seal play it, say: Who can be censor grand master ones?

entries.zh: 孰視趙堯，曰：「無以易堯。」
entries.en: He looked closely at Zhao Yao and said, "No one can take Yao's place."
entries.literal: He fixed his gaze on Zhao Yao and said, "There is no one who can replace Yao."

entries.zh: 遂拜趙堯為御史大夫。
entries.en: He then appointed Zhao Yao as the new Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: Then he appointed Zhao Yao as Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 堯亦前有軍功食邑，及以御史大夫從擊陳豨有功，封為江邑侯。
entries.en: Yao had already earned military merit and a fief, and for his meritorious service accompanying the campaign against Chen Xi as Censor Grand Master, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangyi.
entries.literal: Yao also previously had military merit with a food fief, and as Censor Grand Master followed in striking Chen Xi with merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangyi.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，呂太后使使召趙王，其相周昌令王稱疾不行。
entries.en: After Gaozu died, Empress Dowager Lu sent a messenger to summon the King of Zhao. His chancellor Zhou Chang instructed the king to plead illness and refuse the summons.
entries.literal: Gaozu collapsed. Empress Dowager Lu sent a messenger to summon Zhao king. His chancellor Zhou Chang commanded the king to claim illness and not go.

entries.zh: 使者三反，周昌固為不遣趙王。
entries.en: The messenger went back and forth three times, but Zhou Chang steadfastly refused to send the King of Zhao.
entries.literal: The messenger returned three times. Zhou Chang firmly refused to send Zhao king.

entries.zh: 於是高后患之，乃使使召周昌。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Gao grew vexed by this and sent a messenger to summon Zhou Chang himself.
entries.literal: Then Empress Dowager Gao worried about it and sent a messenger to summon Zhou Chang.

entries.zh: 周昌至，謁高后，高后怒而罵周昌曰：「爾不知我之怨戚氏乎？
entries.en: Zhou Chang arrived and presented himself to Empress Dowager Gao. Furious, she cursed him, saying, "Do you not know of my grudge against the Qi clan?
entries.literal: Zhou Chang arrive, announce Gao empress dowager, Gao empress dowager angry and curse Zhou Chang say: You not know I of grudge Qi clan?

entries.zh: 而不遣趙王，何？」
entries.en: And yet you will not send the King of Zhao. Why?"
entries.literal: But not send Zhao wang, what?"

entries.zh: 昌既徵，高后使使召趙王，趙王果來。
entries.en: Once Chang had been called away, Empress Dowager Gao sent another messenger for the King of Zhao, and the King of Zhao duly came.
entries.literal: After Chang was summoned, Empress Dowager Gao sent a messenger to summon Zhao king. Zhao king indeed came.

entries.zh: 至長安月餘，飲藥而死。
entries.en: A little over a month after arriving in Chang'an, he was poisoned and died.
entries.literal: He arrived at Chang'an after more than a month and died from drinking medicine.

entries.zh: 周昌因謝病不朝見，三歲而死。
entries.en: Zhou Chang withdrew on the pretext of illness and never appeared at court again. Three years later, he died.
entries.literal: Zhou Chang because of claiming illness did not appear at court audiences. After three years he died.

entries.zh: 後五歲，高后聞御史大夫江邑侯趙堯高祖時定趙王如意之畫，乃抵堯罪，以廣阿侯任敖為御史大夫。
entries.en: Five years later, Empress Dowager Gao learned that Censor Grand Master Zhao Yao, the Marquis of Jiangyi, had been the one who devised the plan to protect King Ruyi of Zhao during Gaozu's reign. She had Yao charged with a crime and replaced him with Ren Ao, the Marquis of Guang'a, as Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: After five years, Empress Dowager Gao heard that Censor Grand Master Jiangyi marquis Zhao Yao had during Gaozu's time decided on the plan for Zhao king Ruyi. Then she charged Yao with a crime and made Guang A marquis Ren Ao Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 任敖者，故沛獄吏。
entries.en: Ren Ao had formerly been a prison official in Pei.
entries.literal: Ren Ao was a former Pei prison official.

entries.zh: 高祖嘗辟吏，吏系呂后，遇之不謹。
entries.en: When Gaozu was once evading the authorities, an official arrested Empress Lu and treated her with disrespect.
entries.literal: Gaozu once avoided an official. The official arrested Empress Lu and treated her disrespectfully.

entries.zh: 任敖素善高祖，怒，擊傷主呂后吏。
entries.en: Ren Ao, who had long been on good terms with Gaozu, flew into a rage and struck and wounded the official who had charge of Empress Lu.
entries.literal: Ren Ao had always been on good terms with Gaozu. He was angry and struck and injured the official in charge of Empress Lu.

entries.zh: 及高祖初起，敖以客從為御史，守豐二歲，高祖立為漢王，東擊項籍，敖遷為上黨守。
entries.en: When Gaozu first rose in rebellion, Ao joined him as a retainer and served as a censor. He defended Feng for two years. After Gaozu was established as King of Han and marched east against Xiang Ji, Ao was transferred to serve as Governor of Shangdang.
entries.literal: When Gaozu initially rose, Ao followed as a guest to serve as censor. He guarded Feng for two years. Gaozu was established as Han king and went east to strike Xiang Ji. Ao was moved to serve as Shangdang governor.

entries.zh: 陳豨反時，敖堅守，封為廣阿侯，食千八百戶。
entries.en: During the rebellion of Chen Xi, Ao held his ground with determination and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guang'a, with a fief of eighteen hundred households.
entries.literal: During Chen Xi's rebellion, Ao firmly guarded his position and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guang A, with a food fief of one thousand eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 高后時為御史大夫。
entries.en: During the reign of Empress Dowager Gao, he served as Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: During Empress Dowager Gao's time he served as Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 三歲免，以平陽侯曹窋為御史大夫。
entries.en: After three years he was dismissed, and Cao Zhu, the Marquis of Pingyang, was appointed Censor Grand Master in his place.
entries.literal: After three years he was dismissed, and Cao Zhu, Marquis of Pingyang, was made Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 高后崩，（不）與大臣共誅呂祿等。
entries.en: After Empress Dowager Gao died, he did not join the great ministers in executing Lü Lu and the other members of the Lü clan.
entries.literal: After Empress Dowager Gao died, he did not join the great ministers in executing Lü Lu and the others.

entries.zh: 免，以淮南相張蒼為御史大夫。
entries.en: He was dismissed from office, and Zhang Cang, the Chancellor of Huainan, was appointed Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: He was dismissed, and Huainan chancellor Zhang Cang was made Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 自漢興至孝文二十餘年，會天下初定，將相公卿皆軍吏。
entries.en: From the founding of Han through more than twenty years into Emperor Wen's reign, as the empire was still settling after the wars, the generals, chancellors, and high officials had all risen from military service.
entries.literal: From Han's rise to over twenty years into Xiaowen's reign, as the world was initially settling, the generals, chancellors, dukes, and ministers were all military officials.

entries.zh: 張蒼為計相時，緒正律歷。
entries.en: When Zhang Cang served as Accounting Chancellor, he took up the task of revising the legal codes and the calendar.
entries.literal: When Zhang Cang served as accounting chancellor, he continued to correct the laws and calendars.

entries.zh: 以高祖十月始至霸上，因故秦時本以十月為歲首，弗革。
entries.en: Because Gaozu had first arrived at Bashang in the tenth month, and because the Qin dynasty had originally designated the tenth month as the start of the year, he did not alter this practice.
entries.literal: Because Gaozu in the tenth month began arriving at Bashang, following the old Qin practice which originally used the tenth month as the year's beginning, he did not change it.

entries.zh: 推五德之運，以為漢當水德之時，尚黑如故。
entries.en: He calculated the cycle of the Five Phases and concluded that the Han dynasty corresponded to the phase of Water, and so continued to honor black as its ceremonial color.
entries.literal: He calculated the progression of the Five Virtues, thinking that Han was in the time of water virtue, esteeming black as before.

entries.zh: 吹律調樂，入之音聲，及以比定律令。
entries.en: He blew the pitch-pipes to tune the court music, integrated their tones into the musical system, and used their proportions to establish the standard measures and regulations.
entries.literal: He blew the pitchpipes to tune music, incorporated them into the musical sounds, and used comparisons to determine the laws and commands.

entries.zh: 若百工，天下作程品。
entries.en: As for the various trades and crafts, he set the standards and specifications for the entire empire.
entries.literal: Like the hundred artisans, he made standards and grades for the world.

entries.zh: 至於為丞相，卒就之，故漢家言律歷者，本之張蒼。
entries.en: By the time he became chancellor, he had finally brought this work to completion. For this reason, whenever the Han court discussed legal codes and the calendar, they traced the foundations back to Zhang Cang.
entries.literal: Until he became chancellor, he finally completed it. Therefore, when the Han family spoke of laws and calendars, they based it on Zhang Cang.

entries.zh: 蒼本好書，無所不觀，無所不通，而尤善律歷。
entries.en: Cang had always been a lover of learning, with nothing he had not examined and nothing he did not understand, but he was especially accomplished in legal codes and calendrical science.
entries.literal: Cang was originally fond of books, observing nothing without seeing it, passing through nothing without understanding it, but he was especially skilled in laws and calendars.

entries.zh: 蒼與絳侯等尊立代王為孝文皇帝。
entries.en: Cang, together with the Marquis of Jiang and the other ministers, honored and enthroned the King of Dai as Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Cang together with the Jiang marquis and others honored and established the Dai king as Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 四年，丞相灌嬰卒，張蒼為丞相。
entries.en: In the fourth year, Chancellor Guan Ying died, and Zhang Cang was appointed chancellor in his place.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Chancellor Guan Ying died, and Zhang Cang became chancellor.

entries.zh: 蒼為丞相十餘年，魯人公孫臣上書言漢土德時，其符有黃龍當見。
entries.en: After Cang had served as chancellor for more than ten years, a man from Lu named Gongsun Chen submitted a memorial arguing that Han corresponded to the phase of Earth, and that its confirming omen would be the appearance of a yellow dragon.
entries.literal: Cang served as chancellor for over ten years. A man from Lu named Gongsun Chen submitted a memorial saying Han was in the time of earth virtue, and its omen was that a yellow dragon should appear.

entries.zh: 詔下其議張蒼，張蒼以為非是，罷之。
entries.en: An imperial decree referred the matter to Zhang Cang for deliberation. Zhang Cang judged the argument to be unfounded and dismissed it.
entries.literal: The decree sent it down for Zhang Cang to discuss. Zhang Cang thought it was not correct and dismissed it.

entries.zh: 其後黃龍見成紀，於是文帝召公孫臣以為博士，草土德之歷制度，更元年。
entries.en: Later, a yellow dragon was sighted at Chengji. Emperor Wen thereupon summoned Gongsun Chen and appointed him an Erudite, directing him to draft a new calendar and institutional system based on the phase of Earth, and proclaimed a new first year.
entries.literal: Afterward, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Emperor Wen then summoned Gongsun Chen, appointed him an Erudite, ordered him to draft a calendar and institutions based on the virtue of Earth, and inaugurated a new first year.

entries.zh: 張丞相由此自絀，謝病稱老。
entries.en: Chancellor Zhang was humiliated by these events and withdrew from public life, pleading illness and old age.
entries.literal: From this, Chancellor Zhang diminished himself, claimed illness, and professed old age.

entries.zh: 蒼任人為中候，大為姦利，上以讓蒼，蒼遂病免。
entries.en: Cang had appointed a man as a palace guard who engaged in extensive corruption. The emperor rebuked Cang over this, and Cang subsequently resigned on the grounds of illness.
entries.literal: Cang appointed someone as middle guard who greatly engaged in evil profiteering. The sovereign reprimanded Cang for this, and Cang then claimed illness and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 蒼為丞相十五歲而免。
entries.en: In all, Cang served as chancellor for fifteen years before his dismissal.
entries.literal: Cang served as chancellor for fifteen years and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 孝景前五年，蒼卒，謚為文侯。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Emperor Jing's first reign period (152 BC), Cang died and was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Wen.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xiaojing's first reign period, Cang died and was posthumously titled Marquis Wen.

entries.zh: 子康侯代，八年卒。
entries.en: His son, who received the posthumous title Marquis Kang, succeeded him and died after eight years.
entries.literal: His son Marquis Kang succeeded him and died after eight years.

entries.zh: 子類代為侯，八年，坐臨諸侯喪後就位不敬，國除。
entries.en: His son Lei succeeded as marquis. After eight years, he was convicted of behaving disrespectfully upon assuming his seat after attending a feudal lord's funeral, and his marquisate was abolished.
entries.literal: His son Lei succeeded as marquis. After eight years, convicted of taking his position disrespectfully after attending feudal lords' mourning, the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 嘉為人廉直，門不受私謁。
entries.en: Jia was a man of integrity and directness. His gate was closed to private petitioners.
entries.literal: Jia as a person was incorruptible and straightforward. His gate did not accept private visits.

entries.zh: 是時太中大夫鄧通方隆愛幸，賞賜累巨萬。
entries.en: At this time, the Grand Palace Gentleman Deng Tong was at the height of imperial favor, with rewards and gifts lavished upon him that accumulated to enormous sums.
entries.literal: At this time, Grand Central Gentleman Deng Tong was greatly favored and fortunate, with rewards accumulating to great tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 文帝嘗燕飲通家，其寵如是。
entries.en: Emperor Wen even went so far as to feast and drink at Tong's home; such was the extent of his favor.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen once feasted and drank at Tong's home - his favor was like this.

entries.zh: 是時丞相入朝，而通居上傍，有怠慢之禮。
entries.en: Once when the chancellor entered the court, Tong was seated beside the emperor and conducted himself with a negligent lack of ceremony.
entries.literal: At this time, the chancellor entered court, but Tong sat beside the sovereign with disrespectful ritual.

entries.zh: 丞相奏事畢，因言曰：「陛下愛幸臣，則富貴之；
entries.en: When the chancellor had finished presenting his business, he then said, "Your Majesty loves and favors this minister—then make him wealthy and noble;
entries.literal: When the chancellor had finished memorializing affairs, he then said, "Your Majesty loves and favors this minister—then make him wealthy and noble;

entries.zh: 至於朝廷之禮，不可以不肅！」
entries.en: But as for court ritual, it must be solemn!"
entries.literal: As for the rites of court, they cannot but be kept solemn!"

entries.zh: 上曰：「君勿言，吾私之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Say no more. I am partial to him."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Say no more. I favor him privately."

entries.zh: 罷朝坐府中，嘉為檄召鄧通詣丞相府，不來，且斬通。
entries.en: After court was dismissed, Jia sat in his office and issued an official summons ordering Deng Tong to appear at the chancellor's mansion, with the threat that if he did not come, he would be beheaded.
entries.literal: After dismissing court, he sat in his mansion. Jia issued a dispatch summoning Deng Tong to the chancellor's mansion. If he did not come, he would behead Tong.

entries.zh: 通恐，入言文帝。
entries.en: Tong was terrified and hurried to plead his case before Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Tong was afraid and entered to speak to Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 文帝曰：「汝第往，吾今使人召若。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen said, "Go ahead. I will send someone presently to summon you."
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said, "Just go. I will now send someone to summon you."

entries.zh: 通至丞相府，免冠，徒跣，頓首謝。
entries.en: Tong arrived at the chancellor's mansion, removed his cap, went barefoot, and kowtowed in abject apology.
entries.literal: Tong arrived at the chancellor's mansion, removed his hat, went barefoot, and kowtowed in apology.

entries.zh: 嘉坐自如，故不為禮，責曰：「夫朝廷者，高皇帝之朝廷也。
entries.en: Jia remained seated as before, deliberately withholding the courtesy due him, and rebuked him: "This court is the court of Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: Jia sat as usual and deliberately did not perform the courtesy. He reproached him, saying, "The court is the court of Emperor Gao.

entries.zh: 通小臣，戲殿上，大不敬，當斬。
entries.en: Tong is a petty minister who behaved frivolously in the great hall, a gross act of disrespect, and should be beheaded.
entries.literal: Tong is a small minister who played in the hall - greatly disrespectful, should be beheaded.

entries.zh: 吏今行斬之！」
entries.en: Let the official carry out the execution now!"
entries.literal: The official shall now carry out the beheading!"

entries.zh: 通頓首，首盡出血，不解。
entries.en: Tong beat his head on the ground until blood ran freely, but Jia would not relent.
entries.literal: Tong kowtowed until his head bled completely, but did not stop.

entries.zh: 文帝度丞相已困通，使使者持節召通，而謝丞相曰：「此吾弄臣，君釋之。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen judged that the chancellor had already humiliated Tong, so he sent a messenger bearing an imperial tally to summon Tong, and apologized to the chancellor, saying, "This is my favorite jester. Release him."
entries.literal: Emperor Wen judged that the chancellor had already humiliated Tong, so he sent a messenger holding an imperial tally to summon Tong, and apologized to the chancellor, saying, "This is my favorite jester. Release him."

entries.zh: 鄧通既至，為文帝泣曰：「丞相幾殺臣。」
entries.en: When Deng Tong arrived, he wept to Emperor Wen and said, "The chancellor nearly killed me."
entries.literal: When Deng Tong arrived, he wept to Emperor Wen and said, "The chancellor nearly killed this minister."

entries.zh: 嘉為丞相五歲，孝文帝崩，孝景帝即位。
entries.en: Jia served as chancellor for five years. When Emperor Wen died, Emperor Jing ascended the throne.
entries.literal: Jia served as chancellor for five years. Emperor Xiaowen collapsed, and Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne.

entries.zh: 二年，晁錯為內史，貴幸用事，諸法令多所請變更，議以謫罰侵削諸侯。
entries.en: In the second year, Chao Cuo was serving as Prefect of the Capital. Highly favored and wielding great influence, he proposed numerous changes to the laws and regulations, advocating the use of censure and punishment to encroach upon and diminish the feudal lords.
entries.literal: In the second year, Chao Cuo served as inner secretary, was noble and fortunate, handled affairs. He requested many changes to various laws and commands, discussing using demotion and punishment to erode and cut back the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 而丞相嘉自絀所言不用，疾錯。
entries.en: Chancellor Jia found himself marginalized, his counsel ignored, and he grew to despise Cuo.
entries.literal: But Chancellor Jia diminished himself, and what he said was not used. He hated Cuo.

entries.zh: 錯為內史，門東出，不便，更穿一門南出。
entries.en: As Prefect of the Capital, Cuo's gate opened to the east, which he found inconvenient. He had a new gate cut through to open to the south.
entries.literal: Cuo as inner secretary had his gate exit east, which was inconvenient, so he changed it to dig another gate exiting south.

entries.zh: 南出者，太上皇廟堧垣。
entries.en: But the south gate opened through the outer wall of the temple of the Grand Supreme Emperor.
entries.literal: The south exit was beside the Great Supreme Emperor's temple wall.

entries.zh: 嘉聞之，欲因此以法錯擅穿宗廟垣為門，奏請誅錯。
entries.en: When Jia learned of this, he saw an opportunity to bring charges against Cuo for having unlawfully breached the wall of an ancestral temple to make a gate, and prepared a memorial requesting Cuo's execution.
entries.literal: Jia heard this and wished to use this to accuse Cuo by law of presumptuously digging the ancestral temple wall as a gate, memorializing to request executing Cuo.

entries.zh: 錯客有語錯，錯恐，夜入宮上謁，自歸景帝。
entries.en: One of Cuo's retainers warned him of the plot. Frightened, Cuo stole into the palace by night for an audience and threw himself upon the mercy of Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: Cuo's guest spoke to Cuo. Cuo was afraid and entered the palace at night to have audience, surrendering himself to Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 至朝，丞相奏請誅內史錯。
entries.en: The next morning at court, the chancellor submitted his memorial requesting the execution of Prefect Cuo.
entries.literal: When court arrived, the chancellor memorialized requesting to execute Inner Secretary Cuo.

entries.zh: 景帝曰：「錯所穿非真廟垣，乃外堧垣，故他官居其中，且又我使為之，錯無罪。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing said, "The wall Cuo cut through was not the actual temple wall, but the outer side wall. Other offices occupy the space within it, and besides, I ordered him to do it. Cuo is not guilty."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said, "What Cuo breached was not the true temple wall but the outer side wall. Other officials dwell within it, and moreover I had him do it. Cuo is not guilty."

entries.zh: 罷朝，嘉謂長史曰：「吾悔不先斬錯，乃先請之，為錯所賣。」
entries.en: After court was dismissed, Jia said to his chief clerk, "I regret not beheading Cuo first and asking permission afterward. Cuo has outmaneuvered me."
entries.literal: After court was dismissed, Jia told the chief clerk, "I regret that I did not behead Cuo first but asked permission first—I was outmaneuvered by Cuo."

entries.zh: 至舍，因歐血而死。
entries.en: Upon returning to his residence, he vomited blood and died.
entries.literal: He arrived at his residence and died from vomiting blood.

entries.zh: 謚為節侯。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Jie, the Steadfast.
entries.literal: He was posthumously titled Marquis Jie.

entries.zh: 子共侯蔑代，三年卒。
entries.en: His son Mie, known posthumously as Marquis Gong, succeeded him and died after three years.
entries.literal: His son Marquis Gong Mie succeeded him and died after three years.

entries.zh: 子侯去病代，三十一年卒。
entries.en: His son, the Marquis Qubing, succeeded him and died after thirty-one years.
entries.literal: His son Marquis Qubing succeeded him and died after thirty-one years.

entries.zh: 子侯臾代，六歲，坐為九江太守受故官送有罪，國除。
entries.en: His son, the Marquis Yu, succeeded him. After six years, he was convicted of accepting gifts from former officials while serving as Governor of Jiujiang, and his marquisate was abolished.
entries.literal: His son Marquis Yu succeeded him. After six years, convicted of accepting bribes as Jiu Jiang governor from former officials, the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 自申屠嘉死之後，景帝時開封侯陶青、桃侯劉舍為丞相。
entries.en: After the death of Shentu Jia, during Emperor Jing's reign, Tao Qing, Marquis of Kaifeng, and Liu She, Marquis of Tao, each served in turn as chancellor.
entries.literal: After Shentu Jia died, during Emperor Jing's time Kaifeng marquis Tao Qing and Tao marquis Liu She served as chancellor.

entries.zh: 及今上時，柏至侯許昌、平棘侯薛澤、武彊侯莊青翟、高陵侯趙周等為丞相。
entries.en: In the time of the present emperor, Xu Chang the Marquis of Baizhi, Xue Ze the Marquis of Pingji, Zhuang Qingdi the Marquis of Wuqiang, Zhao Zhou the Marquis of Gaoling, and others have each served as chancellor.
entries.literal: When it reached the present sovereign's time, Baizhi marquis Xu Chang, Pingji marquis Xue Ze, Wuqiang marquis Zhuang Qingdi, Gaoling marquis Zhao Zhou, and others served as chancellor.

entries.zh: 皆以列侯繼嗣，娖娖廉謹，為丞相備員而已，無所能發明功名有著於當世者。
entries.en: All of them succeeded to the position as ranked marquises by inheritance. They were meticulous and incorruptible, but merely filled the chancellorship as seat-warmers, with none achieving any distinction or accomplishment worthy of note in their own age.
entries.literal: All succeeded as ranked marquises through inheritance, were cautious and incorruptible, merely filling the chancellor position, with none able to invent merits and fame that manifested in the current world.

entries.zh: 孝武時丞相多甚，不記，莫錄其行起居狀略，且紀征和以來。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Wu, the chancellors were exceedingly numerous. I shall not record them all here, as no one set down even a brief account of their conduct and daily affairs. Instead, I shall record only from the Zhenghe era onward.
entries.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's time the chancellors were very many. I do not record them, and none recorded their conduct and daily life conditions briefly. Moreover, I record from Zhenghe onwards.

entries.zh: 魏丞相相者，濟陰人也。
entries.en: Chancellor Wei Xiang was a native of Jiyin.
entries.literal: Chancellor Wei Xiang was a man from Jiyin.

entries.zh: 以文吏至丞相。
entries.en: He rose through the civil service to become chancellor.
entries.literal: He reached chancellor as a literary official.

entries.zh: 其人好武，皆令諸吏帶劍，帶劍前奏事。
entries.en: He was a man who admired military ways. He ordered all his officials to wear swords and to present their reports before him wearing swords.
entries.literal: His person was fond of martial affairs. He commanded all officials to wear swords, wearing swords before memorializing affairs.

entries.zh: 或有不帶劍者，當入奏事，至乃借劍而敢入奏事。
entries.en: If any official happened not to be carrying a sword, upon arriving for an audience he would have to borrow one before daring to enter and present his report.
entries.literal: If there were those who did not wear swords, when they should enter to memorialize affairs, they would arrive and borrow swords before daring to enter and memorialize affairs.

entries.zh: 其時京兆尹趙君，丞相奏以免罪，使人執魏丞相，欲求脫罪而不聽。
entries.en: At that time, Zhao Jun, the Prefect of the Capital, was the subject of a memorial by the chancellor requesting his removal for offenses. Zhao sent men to seize Chancellor Wei, hoping to escape punishment, but Wei refused to yield.
entries.literal: At that time the Prefect of the Capital, Zhao Jun, was memorialized by the chancellor for removal on criminal charges. He sent men to seize Chancellor Wei, hoping to escape punishment, but Wei would not yield.

entries.zh: 復使人脅恐魏丞相，以夫人賊殺待婢事而私獨奏請驗之，發吏卒至丞相舍，捕奴婢笞擊問之，實不以兵刃殺也。
entries.en: Zhao then sent men to threaten and intimidate Chancellor Wei, and privately submitted a memorial accusing the chancellor's wife of murdering a maidservant, requesting an investigation. He dispatched officials and soldiers to the chancellor's residence, where they seized the household slaves and interrogated them under the lash, yet in truth no blade had been used to kill her.
entries.literal: He again sent people to threaten and frighten Chancellor Wei, using the matter of his wife bandit-killing a waiting maid, privately memorializing alone to request verification. He sent officials and soldiers to the chancellor's residence, captured the slaves and maids, caned and struck them in questioning - in reality they had not killed with weapons.

entries.zh: 而丞相司直繁君奏京兆尹趙君迫脅丞相，誣以夫人賊殺婢，發吏卒圍捕丞相舍，不道；
entries.en: But the chancellor's superintendent of justice Fan Jun memorialized that the Prefect of the Capital Zhao Jun had coerced and threatened the chancellor. Zhao had falsely accused the chancellor's wife of murdering a maidservant and sent officials and soldiers to surround and seize the chancellor's residence—conduct contrary to propriety;
entries.literal: But the chancellor's superintendent of justice Fan Jun memorialized that the Prefect of the Capital Zhao Jun coerced and threatened the chancellor, falsely accusing his wife of murdering a maidservant, and sent officials and soldiers to surround and seize the chancellor's residence—conduct contrary to propriety;

entries.zh: 又得擅屏騎士事，趙京兆坐要斬。
entries.en: Additionally, charges were brought regarding his unauthorized dismissal of cavalry officers. Zhao, the Prefect of the Capital, was convicted and sentenced to execution.
entries.literal: Moreover, he obtained matters of presumptuously dismissing cavalry gentlemen. Zhao Jing Zhao was convicted and warranted beheading.

entries.zh: 又有使掾陳平等劾中尚書，疑以獨擅劫事而坐之，大不敬，長史以下皆坐死，或下蠶室。
entries.en: Furthermore, Zhao had dispatched his assistants Chen Ping and others to impeach an official of the Imperial Secretariat, suspecting him of unauthorized seizure of property and convicting him of gross disrespect. The Chief Clerk and all those below him were sentenced to death, or remanded to the silkworm chamber for castration.
entries.literal: Moreover, he had assistants Chen Ping and others impeach the central secretary, suspecting him of alone presumptuously conducting robbery matters and convicting him - greatly disrespectful. The chief clerk and below were all convicted to die, or sent to the silkworm room.

entries.zh: 而魏丞相竟以丞相病死。
entries.en: Chancellor Wei, however, ultimately died of illness while still in office.
entries.literal: But Chancellor Wei ultimately died as chancellor from illness.

entries.zh: 子嗣。
entries.en: His son inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son succeeded him.

entries.zh: 後坐騎至廟，不敬，有詔奪爵一級，為關內侯，失列侯，得食其故國邑。
entries.en: Later the son was found guilty of disrespectfully riding his horse to the temple. By imperial decree his rank was reduced one degree to Marquis Within the Pass, losing his full marquisate, though he retained the revenues from his former fief.
entries.literal: Later he was convicted of riding to the temple disrespectfully. By decree his rank was reduced one level, becoming Guan Nei marquis, losing his ranked marquis status, and obtaining the food from his former state's fief.

entries.zh: 魏丞相卒，以御史大夫邴吉代。
entries.en: After Chancellor Wei died, Censor Grand Master Bing Ji was appointed to succeed him.
entries.literal: Chancellor Wei died, and Censor Grand Master Bing Ji replaced him.

entries.zh: 邴丞相吉者，魯國人也。
entries.en: Chancellor Bing Ji was a native of the state of Lu.
entries.literal: Chancellor Bing Ji was a man from Lu state.

entries.zh: 以讀書好法令至御史大夫。
entries.en: Through his scholarship and mastery of the laws and regulations, he rose to the position of Censor Grand Master.
entries.literal: Through reading books and being fond of laws and commands, he reached Censor Grand Master.

entries.zh: 孝宣帝時，以有舊故，封為列侯，而因為丞相。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Xuan, on account of an old connection, he was enfeoffed as a ranked marquis and subsequently appointed chancellor.
entries.literal: During Emperor Xiaoxuan's time, because of old acquaintance, he was enfeoffed as a ranked marquis, and therefore became chancellor.

entries.zh: 明於事，有大智，後世稱之。
entries.en: He was perceptive in his handling of affairs and possessed great wisdom. Later generations spoke of him with admiration.
entries.literal: Clear about affairs, he had great wisdom. Later generations praised him.

entries.zh: 以丞相病死。
entries.en: He died of illness while still serving as chancellor.
entries.literal: He died as chancellor from illness.

entries.zh: 子顯嗣。
entries.en: His son Xian inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Xian succeeded him.

entries.zh: 後坐騎至廟，不敬，有詔奪爵一級，失列侯，得食故國邑。
entries.en: Later he was found guilty of disrespectfully riding his horse to the temple. By imperial decree his rank was reduced one degree, losing his full marquisate, though he retained the revenues from his former fief.
entries.literal: Later he was convicted of riding to the temple disrespectfully. By decree his rank was reduced one level, losing his ranked marquis status, and obtaining the food from his former state's fief.

entries.zh: 顯為吏至太仆，坐官秏亂，身及子男有姦贓，免為庶人。
entries.en: Xian rose through the civil service to the position of Grand Coachman. He was convicted of malfeasance and administrative disorder, and both he and his sons were found guilty of corruption and bribery. He was stripped of his rank and reduced to the status of a commoner.
entries.literal: Xian served as an official and reached Tai Pu. Convicted of official waste and disorder, his person and sons and males having corrupt bribes, he was exempted and became a commoner.

entries.zh: 漢三年秋，項羽擊漢，拔滎陽，漢兵遁保鞏、洛。
entries.en: In the autumn of the third year of Han, Xiang Yu attacked Han and took Xingyang. The Han forces retreated to hold Gong and Luo.
entries.literal: In the autumn of Han's third year, Xiang Yu attacked Han, capturing Xingyang. Han forces fled to defend Gong and Luo.

entries.zh: 楚人聞淮陰侯破趙，彭越數反梁地，則分兵救之。
entries.en: When the Chu forces heard that the Marquis of Huaiyin had defeated Zhao and that Peng Yue was raiding Liang territory repeatedly, they divided their troops to deal with these threats.
entries.literal: The Chu people heard that the Marquis of Huaiyin had defeated Zhao and that Peng Yue had repeatedly rebelled in Liang territory, so they divided their troops to relieve it.

entries.zh: 淮陰方東擊齊，漢王數困滎陽、成皋，計欲捐成皋以東，屯鞏、洛以拒楚。
entries.en: The Marquis of Huaiyin was then striking east against Qi. The King of Han had been in dire straits at Xingyang and Chenggao time and again, and was planning to abandon Chenggao and all the territory east of it, garrisoning Gong and Luo to resist Chu.
entries.literal: Huaiyin was just attacking Qi to the east. The King of Han was repeatedly in distress at Xingyang and Chenggao, and planned to abandon Chenggao and the territory to its east, garrisoning Gong and Luo to resist Chu.

entries.zh: 酈生因曰：「臣聞知天之天者，王事可成；
entries.en: Li Sheng then said: 'I have heard that he who understands the heaven of Heaven can accomplish the king's affairs;
entries.literal: Li Sheng then said: 'I heard he who knows heaven's heaven, king's affairs can be accomplished;

entries.zh: 不知天之天者，王事不可成。
entries.en: he who does not understand the heaven of Heaven cannot accomplish the king's affairs.
entries.literal: He who does not know the heaven of Heaven cannot accomplish the king's affairs.

entries.zh: 王者以民人為天，而民人以食為天。
entries.en: The king takes the people as his heaven, and the people take food as their heaven.
entries.literal: The king takes the people as heaven, and the people take food as heaven.

entries.zh: 夫敖倉，天下轉輸久矣，臣聞其下乃有藏粟甚多。
entries.en: Indeed, Aocang has long been the empire's transport hub. I hear that below it there is a vast amount of stored grain.
entries.literal: Indeed Aocang, all under heaven's transport long time, I heard below it actually has stored grain very much.

entries.zh: 楚人拔滎陽，不堅守敖倉，乃引而東，令適卒分守成皋，此乃天所以資漢也。
entries.en: The Chu people took Xingyang but did not firmly defend Aocang. Instead, they withdrew eastward, ordering suitable troops to divide and defend Chenggao. This is truly Heaven's way of assisting Han.
entries.literal: Chu people took Xingyang, did not firmly defend Aocang, then withdrew and went east, ordered suitable troops divide defend Chenggao, this is heaven's means to assist Han.

entries.zh: 方今楚易取而漢反卻，自奪其便，臣竊以為過矣。
entries.en: Now, Chu is easy to take, yet Han instead retreats, depriving itself of this advantage. I secretly believe this is a mistake.
entries.literal: Now Chu easy to take yet Han instead retreats, self-deprives its advantage, I secretly think it is a mistake.

entries.zh: 且兩雄不俱立，楚漢久相持不決，百姓騷動，海內搖蕩，農夫釋耒，工女下機，天下之心未有所定也。
entries.en: Moreover, two heroes cannot stand together. Chu and Han have long contended without resolution, the common people are agitated, the realm is shaken, farmers have abandoned their plows, and weaving women have left their looms. The hearts of the people are not yet settled.
entries.literal: Moreover, two heroes cannot stand together, Chu Han long mutually contend undecided, common people agitated, within seas shaken, farmers abandon plows, weaving women leave looms, all under heaven's heart not yet settled.

entries.zh: 願足下急復進兵，收取滎陽，據敖倉之粟，塞成皋之險，杜大行之道，距蜚狐之口，守白馬之津，以示諸侯效實形制之勢，則天下知所歸矣。
entries.en: I wish your excellency to urgently advance troops again, take Xingyang, occupy Aocang's grain, block Chenggao's defiles, cut off the road through Taihang, hold the mouth of Feihu, and guard Baima's ford. Show the feudal lords the force of real control, and then the whole realm will know where to turn.
entries.literal: Wish your excellency urgently again advance troops, receive Xingyang, occupy Aocang's grain, block Chenggao's defiles, dam Daxing's road, distance Feihu's mouth, guard Baima's ford, to show feudal lords imitate reality form control power, then all under heaven know where to return.

entries.zh: 方今燕、趙已定，唯齊未下。
entries.en: Now, Yan and Zhao are already settled; only Qi has not yet submitted.
entries.literal: Now Yan, Zhao already settled, only Qi not yet submitted.

entries.zh: 今田廣據千里之齊，田閒將二十萬之眾，軍於歷城，諸田宗彊，負海阻河濟，南近楚，人多變詐，足下雖遣數十萬師，未可以歲月破也。
entries.en: Now, Tian Guang occupies a thousand li of Qi, and Tian Jian leads an army of two hundred thousand, encamped at Licheng. The Tian clans are strong, relying on the sea and shielded by the Yellow and Ji Rivers. To the south, they are close to Chu, and their people are often deceitful. Even if your excellency sends hundreds of thousands of troops, you cannot break them in months or years.
entries.literal: Now Tian Guang occupies thousand li of Qi, Tian Jian leads two hundred thousand troops, encamped at Licheng, various Tian clans strong, relying on sea obstructed by Yellow River Ji River, south near Chu, people many deceitful, your excellency even if sends hundreds of thousands troops, cannot in months years break it.

entries.zh: 臣請得奉明詔說齊王，使為漢而稱東藩。」
entries.en: I request to be allowed to respectfully carry out a clear edict to persuade the King of Qi, to make him serve Han and be called an eastern vassal.'
entries.literal: I request to be allowed respectfully carry out clear edict persuade Qi king, make him serve Han and be called eastern vassal.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: 'Good.'
entries.literal: The Sovereign said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 乃從其畫，復守敖倉，而使酈生說齊王曰：「王知天下之所歸乎？」
entries.en: Then, following his plan, Liu Bang again defended Aocang and sent Li Sheng to persuade the King of Qi, saying: 'Does the King know where the realm is turning?'
entries.literal: Then followed his plan, again defended Aocang, and sent Li Sheng persuade Qi king said: 'Does the king know where all under heaven returns?'

entries.zh: 王曰：「不知也。」
entries.en: The King replied: 'I do not know.'
entries.literal: King said: 'Do not know.'

entries.zh: 曰：「王知天下之所歸，則齊國可得而有也；
entries.en: Li Sheng said: 'If the King knows where the realm is turning, then the state of Qi can be taken and held;
entries.literal: Li Yiji said: 'If the King knows where all under heaven is turning, then the state of Qi can be obtained and possessed;

entries.zh: 若不知天下之所歸，即齊國未可得保也。」
entries.en: if you do not know where the realm is turning, then the state of Qi cannot be preserved.'
entries.literal: if does not know where all under heaven returns, then Qi state cannot be preserved.'

entries.zh: 齊王曰：「天下何所歸？」
entries.en: The King of Qi asked: 'Where is the realm turning?'
entries.literal: Qi king said: 'Where does all under heaven return?'

entries.zh: 曰：「歸漢。」
entries.en: Li Sheng replied: 'Submit to Han.'
entries.literal: Li Yiji replied: 'Submit to Han.'

entries.zh: 曰：「先生何以言之？」
entries.en: The king asked, 'On what grounds do you say this, sir?'
entries.literal: The King asked: 'Sir, why do you speak thus?'

entries.zh: 曰：「漢王與項王力西面擊秦，約先入咸陽者王之。
entries.en: Li Sheng explained: 'The Han King and Xiang Yu jointly attacked Qin from the west, agreeing that whoever entered Xianyang first would become king.
entries.literal: Li Yiji said: 'The King of Han and Xiang Yu jointly attacked Qin from the west, agreeing that whoever entered Xianyang first would become king.

entries.zh: 漢王先入咸陽，項王負約不與而王之漢中。
entries.en: The King of Han was the first to enter Xianyang, but the King of Xiang broke the covenant and, instead of granting him that kingship, made him king of Hanzhong.
entries.literal: The Han King entered Xianyang first, but Xiang Yu broke the agreement and did not grant him the kingship, instead enfeoffing him in Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 項王遷殺義帝，漢王聞之，起蜀漢之兵擊三秦，出關而責義帝之處，收天下之兵，立諸侯之後。
entries.en: Xiang Yu relocated and assassinated the Righteous Emperor. When the Han King heard of this, he raised troops from Shu and Han to attack the Three Qins, emerged from the pass to demand justice for the Righteous Emperor's death, gathered armies from all quarters, and restored the descendants of the feudal lords to their positions.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu moved and killed Righteous Emperor, Han King heard it, raised Shu-Han troops to attack San Qin, came out of pass and demanded Righteous Emperor's place, gathered all-under-heaven's troops, established feudal lords' descendants.

entries.zh: 降城即以侯其將，得賂即以分其士，與天下同其利，豪英賢才皆樂為之用。
entries.en: When a city surrendered, he immediately enfeoffed its commanders as marquises. When he seized spoils, he shared them at once with his soldiers. He shared the empire's benefits broadly, and so the brave, the talented, and the worthy all gladly served him.
entries.literal: When cities surrendered, he immediately enfeoffed their generals as marquises. When he obtained booty, he immediately shared it with his soldiers. He shared benefits equally with all under heaven, so that heroic elites and worthy talents were all glad to serve him.

entries.zh: 諸侯之兵四面而至，蜀漢之粟方船而下。
entries.en: The troops of the feudal lords arrived from all four directions, while grain from Shu and Han was transported downriver in large square boats.
entries.literal: Feudal lords' troops arrived from four directions, Shu-Han grain came down in square boats.

entries.zh: 項王有倍約之名，殺義帝之負；
entries.en: Xiang Yu bore the reputation of breaking agreements and the burden of assassinating the Righteous Emperor;
entries.literal: Xiang Yu had name of breaking agreements, burden of killing Righteous Emperor;

entries.zh: 於人之功無所記，於人之罪無所忘；
entries.en: he remembered no one's merits but forgot no one's faults;
entries.literal: regarding people's merits remembered nothing, regarding people's faults forgot nothing;

entries.zh: 戰勝而不得其賞，拔城而不得其封；
entries.en: those who won battles received no rewards, those who captured cities received no enfeoffments;
entries.literal: won battles but received no rewards, captured cities but received no enfeoffments;

entries.zh: 非項氏莫得用事；
entries.en: only members of the Xiang clan could hold positions of authority;
entries.literal: only Xiang clan could hold office;

entries.zh: 為人刻印，刓而不能授；
entries.en: he had seals carved for people but kept them blunted and would not grant them;
entries.literal: carved seals for people, blunted them and could not grant;

entries.zh: 攻城得賂，積而不能賞：天下畔之，賢才怨之，而莫為之用。
entries.en: when he captured cities and obtained booty, he hoarded it without distributing rewards. All under heaven rebelled against him, worthy talents resented him, and no one would serve him.
entries.literal: attacked cities obtained booty, accumulated it and could not reward: all-under-heaven rebelled against him, worthy talents resented him, and none would serve him.

entries.zh: 故天下之士歸於漢王，可坐而策也。
entries.en: Therefore, all the scholars under heaven have turned to the Han King. Victory can be achieved without leaving one's seat.
entries.literal: Therefore, all-under-heaven's scholars returned to Han King, can be determined while seated.

entries.zh: 夫漢王發蜀漢，定三秦；
entries.en: Now the Han King marched forth from Shu and Han and pacified the Three Qins;
entries.literal: Now Han King issued from Shu-Han, pacified San Qin;

entries.zh: 涉西河之外，援上黨之兵；
entries.en: he crossed beyond the Xi River and drew in troops from Shangdang;
entries.literal: crossed beyond Xi River, drew Shangdang's troops;

entries.zh: 下井陘，誅成安君；
entries.en: he descended through the Jingxing Pass and executed Lord Cheng'an;
entries.literal: descended Jingxing, executed Cheng An Jun;

entries.zh: 破北魏，舉三十二城：此蚩尤之兵也，非人之力也，天之福也。
entries.en: he defeated the Wei of the north and captured thirty-two cities. This was the army of Chiyou, not achieved through human effort but through heaven's blessing.
entries.literal: defeated Northern Wei, raised thirty-two cities: this was Chiyou's army, not human strength, heaven's blessing.

entries.zh: 今已據敖倉之粟，塞成皋之險，守白馬之津，杜大行之阪，距蜚狐之口，天下後服者先亡矣。
entries.en: Now he has already seized the grain stores of Aocang, blocked the strategic passes at Chenggao, guards the ford at Baima, blocked the Taihang slopes, and confronts Feihu Pass. Those under heaven who submit late will perish first.
entries.literal: Now already occupied Aocang's grain, blocked Chenggao's defiles, guarded Baima's ford, blocked Taihang's slopes, confronted Feihu's mouth, all-under-heaven late submitters first perish.

entries.zh: 王疾先下漢王，齊國社稷可得而保也；
entries.en: Your Majesty, hasten to submit first to the Han King, and the altars of soil and grain of the state of Qi can be preserved;
entries.literal: King quickly first submit to Han King, Qi state's altars of soil and grain can be preserved;

entries.zh: 不下漢王，危亡可立而待也。」
entries.en: If you do not submit to the King of Han, ruin and destruction will come upon you before you can draw another breath.'
entries.literal: if you do not submit to the Han King, peril and extinction await you immediately.'

entries.zh: 田廣以為然，乃聽酈生，罷歷下兵守戰備，與酈生日縱酒。
entries.en: Tian Guang found this persuasive. He heeded Li Yiji, stood down the garrison at Lixia and disbanded his war preparations, and spent his days drinking freely with Li Yiji.
entries.literal: Tian Guang considered this correct, so he heeded Li Sheng, dismissed the troops guarding Lixia and their battle preparations, and indulged daily in drinking with Li Sheng.

entries.zh: 酈生食其者，陳留高陽人也。
entries.en: Li Yiji was a man of Gaoyang in Chenliu.
entries.literal: Li Sheng Shiqi was from Gaoyang in Chenliu.

entries.zh: 好讀書，家貧落魄，無以為衣食業，為里監門吏。
entries.en: He loved reading, but his family was destitute. Unable to earn a living, he took a position as a gatekeeper in his village.
entries.literal: He was fond of reading books. His family was poor and downfallen, with nothing to make a living providing clothing and food, so he became the neighborhood gate watch official.

entries.zh: 然縣中賢豪不敢役，縣中皆謂之狂生。
entries.en: However, the county's worthy nobles did not dare employ him. Everyone in the county called him the mad scholar.
entries.literal: However, the county's worthy and powerful did not dare employ him. Everyone in the county called him the mad scholar.

entries.zh: 陽陵侯傅寬，以魏五大夫騎將從，為舍人，起橫陽。
entries.en: The Marquis of Yangling, Fu Kuan, had held the Wei rank of Fifth-Rank Grandee and served as a cavalry general. He joined as a retainer, first rising at Hengyang.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Yangling, Fu Kuan, followed as a Wei cavalry general holding the rank of Fifth-Rank Grandee, became a retainer, and first rose at Hengyang.

entries.zh: 從攻安陽、杠裏，擊趙賁軍於開封，及擊楊熊曲遇、陽武，斬首十二級，賜爵卿。
entries.en: Fu Kuan took part in the attacks on Anyang and Gangli, engaged Zhao Ben's army at Kaifeng, and fought Yang Xiong at Quyu and Yangwu. He took twelve heads and was granted the rank of Minister.
entries.literal: He followed in attacking Anyang and Gangli, struck Zhao Ben's army at Kaifeng, and also struck Yang Xiong at Quyu and Yangwu. He took twelve heads and was granted the noble rank of Minister (qing).

entries.zh: 從至霸上。
entries.en: The army then reached Bashang.
entries.literal: He followed and arrived at Bashang.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，漢王賜寬封號共德君。
entries.en: When the Lord of Pei was made King of Han, the king bestowed upon Fu Kuan the title Lord of Shared Virtue.
entries.literal: When Pei Gong was established as Han King, the Han King granted Fu Kuan the title Lord Gongde.

entries.zh: 從入漢中，遷為右騎將。
entries.en: From there he followed the king into Hanzhong and was promoted to General of the Right Cavalry.
entries.literal: He followed in entering Hanzhong and was promoted to Right Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 從定三秦，賜食邑雕陰。
entries.en: During the pacification of the Three Qin kingdoms, he was granted the revenue fief of Diaoyin.
entries.literal: He followed in pacifying the Three Qins and was granted the fief of Diaoyin.

entries.zh: 從擊項籍，待懷，賜爵通德侯。
entries.en: In the campaign against Xiang Ji, he was stationed at Huai and granted the title Marquis of Tongde.
entries.literal: He followed in attacking Xiang Ji, waited at Huai, and was granted the title Marquis of Tongde.

entries.zh: 從擊項冠、周蘭、龍且，所將卒斬騎將一人敖下，益食邑。
entries.en: He took part in the campaigns against Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Ju. The troops under his command beheaded a cavalry general at Ao, and his fief was enlarged.
entries.literal: He followed in attacking Xiang Guan, Zhou Lan, and Long Ju. The troops he led beheaded one cavalry general below Ao, and his fief was increased.

entries.zh: 信武侯靳歙，以中涓從，起宛朐。
entries.en: The Marquis of Xinwu, Jin Xi, joined as an inner attendant, first rising at Wanqu.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Xinwu, Jin Xi, followed as an inner attendant and arose from Wanqu.

entries.zh: 攻濟陽。
entries.en: Jin Xi attacked Jiyang.
entries.literal: He attacked Jiyang.

entries.zh: 破李由軍。
entries.en: He then defeated the army of Li You.
entries.literal: He broke Li You's army.

entries.zh: 擊秦軍亳南、開封東北，斬騎千人將一人，首五十七級，捕虜七十三人，賜爵封號臨平君。
entries.en: Against the Qin army south of Bo and northeast of Kaifeng, he beheaded a commander of a thousand cavalry, took fifty-seven heads, and captured seventy-three prisoners. For this he was granted a noble rank and the title Lord of Linping.
entries.literal: He struck the Qin army south of Bo and northeast of Kaifeng, beheaded one commander of a thousand cavalry, took fifty-seven heads, captured seventy-three prisoners, and was granted a noble rank and the title Lord of Linping.

entries.zh: 又戰藍田北，斬車司馬二人，騎長一人，首二十八級，捕虜五十七人。
entries.en: He fought again north of Lantian, beheading two chariot marshals and one cavalry captain, taking twenty-eight heads, and capturing fifty-seven prisoners.
entries.literal: He again battled north of Lantian, beheaded two chariot assistant directors and one cavalry captain, took twenty-eight heads, and captured fifty-seven prisoners.

entries.zh: 至霸上。
entries.en: He reached Bashang.
entries.literal: He arrived at Bashang.

entries.zh: 沛公立為漢王，賜歙爵建武侯，遷為騎都尉。
entries.en: After the Lord of Pei was installed as King of Han, Jin Xi received the rank of Marquis of Jianwu and was promoted to Cavalry Commandant.
entries.literal: When the Lord of Pei was made King of Han, he granted Jin Xi the title Marquis of Jianwu and promoted him to Cavalry Commandant.

entries.zh: 蒯成侯緤者，沛人也，姓周氏。
entries.en: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Xie, was a man of Pei, surnamed Zhou.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Zhou Xie, was a man of Pei and bore the surname Zhou.

entries.zh: 常為高祖參乘，以舍人從起沛。
entries.en: He regularly served as Gaozu's chariot companion and followed him as a retainer when he first rose at Pei.
entries.literal: He often served Gaozu as chariot companion and followed him as a retainer when he arose from Pei.

entries.zh: 至霸上，西入蜀、漢，還定三秦，食邑池陽。
entries.en: The campaign carried him to Bashang, west into Shu and Han, and back to pacify the Three Qin kingdoms; he then received the revenue fief of Chiyang.
entries.literal: He arrived at Bashang, went west into Shu and Han, returned and pacified the Three Qins, and received the fief of Chiyang.

entries.zh: 東絕甬道，從出度平陰，遇淮陰侯兵襄國，軍乍利乍不利，終無離上心。
entries.en: After cutting the eastern corridor road, he crossed Pingyin on campaign and met the Marquis of Huaiyin's forces at Xiangguo. Though the army's fortunes swung between victory and defeat, he never wavered in his devotion to the sovereign.
entries.literal: He cut off the eastern Yongdao, followed and emerged crossing Pingyin, encountered the Marquis of Huaiyin's troops at Xiangguo. The army was now advantageous, now disadvantageous, but he finally had no heart that departed from the Sovereign.

entries.zh: 以緤為信武侯，食邑三千三百戶。
entries.en: Xie was made Marquis of Xinwu and granted a revenue fief of three thousand three hundred households.
entries.literal: Xie was made Marquis of Xinwu, with a food fief of three thousand three hundred households.

entries.zh: 高祖十二年，以緤為蒯成侯，除前所食邑。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Gaozu's reign, Xie was made Marquis of Kuaicheng, superseding all previous fiefs.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's twelfth year, Xie was made Marquis of Kuaicheng, with previous fiefs eliminated.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：陽陵侯傅寬、信武侯靳歙皆高爵，從高祖起山東，攻項籍，誅殺名將，破軍降城以十數，未嘗困辱，此亦天授也。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: The Marquis of Yangling, Fu Kuan, and the Marquis of Xinwu, Jin Xi, both held high noble ranks. They followed Gaozu in rising from Shandong, attacked Xiang Ji, executed famous generals, broke armies, and induced the surrender of cities numbering in the tens, and never experienced distress or humiliation. This too was heaven's bestowal.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: The Marquis of Yangling Fu Kuan and the Marquis of Xinwu Jin Xi both held high noble ranks. They followed Gaozu in rising from Shandong, attacked Xiang Ji, executed famous generals, broke armies, and induced the surrender of cities numbering in the tens, and never experienced distress or humiliation. This too was heaven's bestowal.

entries.zh: 蒯成侯周緤操心堅正，身不見疑，上欲有所之，未嘗不垂涕，此有傷心者然，可謂篤厚君子矣。
entries.en: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Zhou Xie, was steadfast and upright in his convictions, and his loyalty was never called into question. Whenever the sovereign intended to take the field, Xie never failed to weep. His was the bearing of one whose heart truly ached for his lord. He may well be called a man of deep and genuine devotion.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Kuaicheng, Zhou Xie, held a heart that was firm and upright, and his person was never suspected. Whenever the emperor intended to go on campaign, he never failed to shed tears. This was the bearing of one whose heart was wounded for his lord. He may be called a man of deep and genuine devotion.

entries.zh: 上欲自擊陳豨，蒯成侯泣曰：「始秦攻破天下，未嘗自行。
entries.en: When the emperor wanted to lead the attack on Chen Xi himself, the Marquis of Kuaicheng wept and said, "When Qin first conquered the realm, its ruler never personally took the field.
entries.literal: When the emperor wished to attack Chen Xi in person, the Marquis of Kuaicheng wept and said, "When Qin first overran the realm, its ruler never took the field in person.

entries.zh: 今上常自行，是為無人可使者乎？」
entries.en: Yet now Your Majesty is forever campaigning in person. Are there truly no men who can be sent instead?"
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty constantly campaigns in person—does this mean there is no one who can be sent to do the work?"

entries.zh: 上以為「愛我」，賜入殿門不趨，殺人不死。
entries.en: The emperor took this as "loving me" and granted him entry through the palace gate without quick-stepping, and immunity from the death penalty for homicide.
entries.literal: The emperor took this as "love for me" and granted him entry through the palace gate without quick-stepping, and that homicide would not be punishable by death.

entries.zh: 孝惠五年卒，謚為景侯。
entries.en: He died in the fifth year of Emperor Xiaohui's reign and was posthumously titled Marquis Jing.
entries.literal: He died in the fifth year of Xiaohui and was posthumously named Marquis Jing.

entries.zh: 子頃侯精立，二十四年卒。
entries.en: His son Jing succeeded him as Marquis Qing and died after twenty-four years.
entries.literal: His son Marquis Qing Jing succeeded him and died after twenty-four years.

entries.zh: 子共侯則立，十二年卒。
entries.en: His son Ze succeeded him as Marquis Gong and died after twelve years.
entries.literal: His son Marquis Gong Ze succeeded him and died after twelve years.

entries.zh: 子侯偃立，三十一年，坐與淮南王謀反，死，國除。
entries.en: His son Yan succeeded as marquis. After thirty-one years, he was convicted of conspiring with the King of Huainan to rebel, was put to death, and his state was abolished.
entries.literal: His son Yan succeeded him as marquis. After thirty-one years, he was implicated in plotting rebellion with the King of Huainan, was put to death, and his state was abolished.

entries.zh: 至孝文五年，緤以壽終，謚為貞侯。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Xie died of old age and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhen.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Emperor Wen's reign, Xie died of old age and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhen.

entries.zh: 子昌代侯，有罪，國除。
entries.en: His son Chang succeeded to the marquisate but was found guilty of a crime, and his state was abolished.
entries.literal: His son Chang succeeded as marquis, but had a crime and his state was eliminated.

entries.zh: 至孝景中二年，封緤子居代侯。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Jing's middle reign period, Xie's son Ju was enfeoffed to continue the marquisate.
entries.literal: In the second year of the middle reign period of Emperor Jing, Xie's son Ju was enfeoffed as successor marquis.

entries.zh: 至元鼎三年，居為太常，有罪，國除。
entries.en: In the third year of the Yuanding era, Ju was serving as Grand Master of Ceremonies when he was found guilty of a crime, and his state was abolished.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yuanding, Ju served as Grand Supplicator but had a crime, and his state was eliminated.

entries.zh: 劉敬者，齊人也。
entries.en: Liu Jing was a native of Qi.
entries.literal: Liu Jing was a man of Qi.

entries.zh: 漢五年，戍隴西，過洛陽，高帝在焉。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Han dynasty, while on garrison duty in Longxi, he passed through Luoyang, where Emperor Gao was residing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Han, he was garrisoned in Longxi and passed through Luoyang where the Gao Emperor was.

entries.zh: 婁敬脫輓輅，衣其羊裘，見齊人虞將軍曰：「臣願見上言便事。」
entries.en: Lou Jing stepped down from his cart, put on his sheepskin coat, and went to see Yu the General, a fellow man of Qi. He said, 'I wish to see the Sovereign and present a matter of advantage.'
entries.literal: Lou Jing stepped down from the draught cart, put on his sheepskin coat, went to see Yu the General, a man of Qi, and said, 'I wish to see the Sovereign and speak on a matter of advantage.'

entries.zh: 虞將軍欲與之鮮衣，婁敬曰：「臣衣帛，衣帛見；
entries.en: General Yu wished to give him fine clothes. Lou Jing said, 'If I wear silk, I shall go to audience in silk;
entries.literal: General Yu wished to give him fine clothes. Lou Jing said, 'If I wear silk, I shall appear in silk;

entries.zh: 衣褐，衣褐見：終不敢易衣。」
entries.en: if I wear coarse cloth, I shall go to audience in coarse cloth—I ultimately dare not change my clothes.'
entries.literal: if I wear coarse cloth, I shall appear in coarse cloth. I ultimately dare not change clothes.'

entries.zh: 於是虞將軍入言上。
entries.en: General Yu then went in and reported this to the Emperor.
entries.literal: Thereupon General Yu entered and spoke to the Sovereign.

entries.zh: 上召入見，賜食。
entries.en: The Emperor summoned him for an audience and bestowed a meal upon him.
entries.literal: The Sovereign summoned him to enter and see him, granting him food.

entries.zh: 高帝問群臣，群臣皆山東人，爭言周王數百年，秦二世即亡，不如都周。
entries.en: Emperor Gao consulted his ministers, but they were all men from east of the mountains. They argued that the Zhou had reigned for several hundred years while the Qin fell after just two generations, making it far better to establish the capital at the old Zhou site.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao asked the assembled ministers. The ministers, all being men from east of the mountains, contended that the Zhou had ruled for several hundred years while the Qin perished after two generations—it would be better to establish the capital at Zhou.

entries.zh: 上疑未能決。
entries.en: The Emperor was uncertain and could not reach a decision.
entries.literal: The Sovereign doubted and could not decide.

entries.zh: 及留侯明言入關便，即日車駕西都關中。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Liu clearly stated the advantages of entering the passes, that very day the imperial carriage set out westward to establish the capital in Guanzhong.
entries.literal: When Liu Hou clearly spoke of the convenience of entering the pass, that very day the carriage drove west to make Guanzhong the capital.

entries.zh: 漢九年，高帝徙叔孫通為太子太傅。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Han, Emperor Gao transferred Shusun Tong to the position of Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Han, the High Emperor transferred Shusun Tong to serve as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 漢十二年，高祖欲以趙王如意易太子，叔孫通諫上曰：「昔者晉獻公以驪姬之故廢太子，立奚齊，晉國亂者數十年，為天下笑。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Han, Gaozu wished to replace the Crown Prince with King Ruyi of Zhao. Shusun Tong admonished the High Emperor, saying, 'Formerly, Duke Xian of Jin deposed the crown prince because of Li Ji and established Xi Qi, plunging Jin into disorder for several decades and making it the laughingstock of the empire.
entries.literal: Han twelfth year, Gaozu wished with Zhao King Ruyi change Crown Prince, Shusun Tong admonished High Emperor said: 'Formerly Jin Xian Gong because of Li Ji's sake deposed Crown Prince, established Xi Qi, Jin state in chaos several decades, became tianxia's laughingstock.

entries.zh: 秦以不蚤定扶蘇，令趙高得以詐立胡亥，自使滅祀，此陛下所親見。
entries.en: Because the Qin failed to designate Fusu early, Zhao Gao was able to fraudulently enthrone Huhai, bringing about the extinction of the Qin sacrificial line—this is something Your Majesty witnessed personally.
entries.literal: Qin failed to establish Fusu early, allowing Zhao Gao to fraudulently establish Hu Hai, which caused the Qin sacrifices to be extinguished—this is something Your Majesty witnessed personally.

entries.zh: 今太子仁孝，天下皆聞之；
entries.en: The current Crown Prince is benevolent and filial—everyone in the empire has heard of this;
entries.literal: Now Crown Prince benevolent filial, tianxia all heard of it;

entries.zh: 呂后與陛下攻苦食啖，其可背哉！
entries.en: Empress Lu shared hardship and coarse food with Your Majesty. How can you turn your back on her?
entries.literal: Empress Lü endured hardship and ate meager food with Your Majesty—how can you turn your back on her!

entries.zh: 陛下必欲廢適而立少，臣願先伏誅，以頸血汙地。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty insists on deposing the rightful heir and establishing a younger son, I wish to be executed first, staining the ground with my neck blood.'
entries.literal: Your Majesty must wish depose proper and establish young, minister wishes first receive execution, with neck blood stain ground.'

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「公罷矣，吾直戲耳。」
entries.en: The High Emperor said, 'Enough, you. I was only joking.'
entries.literal: High Emperor said: 'You stop, I only joking.'

entries.zh: 叔孫通曰：「太子天下本，本一搖天下振動，柰何以天下為戲！」
entries.en: Shusun Tong said, 'The Crown Prince is the root of the empire. If the root shakes even once, the whole empire shakes. How can you treat the empire as a joke!'
entries.literal: Shusun Tong said: 'Crown Prince tianxia root, root one shake tianxia shakes, how with tianxia as joke!'

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「吾聽公言。」
entries.en: The High Emperor said, 'I will listen to your words.'
entries.literal: High Emperor said: 'I listen to your words.'

entries.zh: 及上置酒，見留侯所招客從太子入見，上乃遂無易太子志矣。
entries.en: When the High Emperor held a banquet, he saw the guests recruited by Liu Hou following the Crown Prince in for an audience, and the High Emperor finally abandoned any intention to change the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: When High Emperor placed wine, saw Liu Hou's recruited guests follow Crown Prince enter audience, High Emperor then finally had no change Crown Prince intention.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：語曰「千金之裘，非一狐之腋也；
entries.en: The Grand Historian said: As the proverb goes, 'A fur coat worth a thousand pieces of gold is not made from the armpit of a single fox;
entries.literal: Grand Historian said: Proverb says 'Thousand gold fur coat, not one fox armpit;

entries.zh: 臺榭之榱，非一木之枝也；
entries.en: The rafters of a pavilion or terrace are not made from the branch of a single tree;
entries.literal: Pavilion terrace rafters, not one tree branch;

entries.zh: 三代之際，非一士之智也。」
entries.en: The governance of the Three Dynasties was not the wisdom of a single scholar.'
entries.literal: Three dynasties governance, not one scholar's wisdom.'

entries.zh: 信哉！
entries.en: How true!
entries.literal: Truly!

entries.zh: 夫高祖起微細，定海內，謀計用兵，可謂盡之矣。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu rose from the humblest origins to pacify the realm within the seas, exhausting every stratagem and military art.
entries.literal: Indeed, Gaozu rose from humble origins, pacified the empire, and exhausted all stratagems and military uses.

entries.zh: 然而劉敬脫輓輅一說，建萬世之安，智豈可專邪！
entries.en: Yet Liu Jing, after stepping down from his cart, secured peace for ten thousand generations with a single proposal. How could wisdom belong to one class alone?
entries.literal: Yet Liu Jing, with one counsel after stepping down from his cart, secured peace for ten thousand generations—how can wisdom be monopolized!

entries.zh: 叔孫通希世度務，制禮進退，與時變化，卒為漢家儒宗。
entries.en: Shusun Tong gauged the spirit of the age and measured affairs of state, crafting the rites of advancement and withdrawal to suit each change of the times, and in the end became the Confucian patriarch of the Han house.
entries.literal: Shusun Tong gauged the spirit of the age and measured affairs of state, formulated the rites of advancement and retreat, changed with the times, and finally became the Confucian patriarch of the Han house.

entries.zh: 「大直若詘，道固委蛇」，蓋謂是乎？
entries.en: 'The great straight appears bent; the Way is indeed winding'—is this not what it speaks of?
entries.literal: 'Great straight like bent, Way indeed winding', probably speaking of this?

entries.zh: 叔孫通者，薛人也。
entries.en: Shusun Tong was a native of Xue.
entries.literal: Shusun Tong was a man of Xue.

entries.zh: 秦時以文學徵，待詔博士。
entries.en: During the Qin dynasty, he was summoned for his learning and served as an erudite awaiting imperial orders.
entries.literal: During Qin times he was summoned for his literature and awaited decrees as an erudite.

entries.zh: 數歲，陳勝起山東，使者以聞，二世召博士諸儒生問曰：「楚戍卒攻蘄入陳，於公如何？」
entries.en: Several years later, Chen Sheng rose east of the mountains. When an envoy reported this, the Second Emperor summoned the erudites and scholar-students and asked, "Chu garrison soldiers have attacked Qi and entered Chen. What do you gentlemen make of this?"
entries.literal: After several years Chen Sheng arose east of the mountains. An envoy reported it. The Second Emperor summoned the erudites and scholar-students and asked, 'Chu garrison soldiers have attacked Qi and entered Chen—what do you gentlemen make of this?'

entries.zh: 博士諸生三十餘人前曰：「人臣無將，將即反，罪死無赦。
entries.en: The erudites and students, more than thirty men, came forward and said: 'Subjects may not command troops; if they do, they are rebelling. The crime is death with no pardon.
entries.literal: The erudites and students, more than thirty men, advanced and said: 'Subject ministers may not command troops; if they do, then they are rebelling. The crime is death with no pardon.

entries.zh: 願陛下急發兵擊之。」
entries.en: We wish Your Majesty to urgently send troops and strike them.'
entries.literal: Wish Your Majesty urgently send troops strike them.'

entries.zh: 二世怒，作色。
entries.en: The Second Emperor was enraged, his expression darkening.
entries.literal: The Second Generation was angered and changed color.

entries.zh: 叔孫通前曰：「諸生言皆非也。
entries.en: Shusun Tong stepped forward and said, "The scholars' words are all wrong.
entries.literal: Shusun Tong stepped forward and said, 'The scholars' words are all wrong.

entries.zh: 夫天下合為一家，毀郡縣城，鑠其兵，示天下不復用。
entries.en: All under heaven has been united as one family. The walls of the commanderies and counties have been torn down, their weapons melted, to show the realm they will never be used again.
entries.literal: Now all under heaven is united as one family. The commandery and county walls have been destroyed, their weapons melted, showing all under heaven they will not be used again.

entries.zh: 且明主在其上，法令具於下，使人人奉職，四方輻輳，安敢有反者！
entries.en: Moreover, an enlightened ruler is at the top; below, the laws are complete, making everyone fulfill their duties. The four directions converge like spokes to a hub—how dare there be any who rebel!
entries.literal: Moreover, enlightened ruler at top, laws commands complete at bottom, makes everyone fulfill duty, four directions spokes converge, how dare have rebel persons!

entries.zh: 此特群盜鼠竊狗盜耳，何足置之齒牙閒。
entries.en: These are merely a pack of petty thieves—rats pilfering and dogs stealing—hardly worth mentioning.
entries.literal: This is only a group of bandits—rat stealing, dog stealing—what is worth placing between the teeth.

entries.zh: 郡守尉今捕論，何足憂。」
entries.en: The commandery governor and commandant's assistant will now capture and judge them—what is there to worry about."
entries.literal: Commandery governor and commandant's assistant now capture and judge them, what is there worth worrying.'

entries.zh: 二世喜曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Second Generation was pleased and said: 'Good.'
entries.literal: Second Generation pleased said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 盡問諸生，諸生或言反，或言盜。
entries.en: He questioned all the scholars, and some called it rebellion while others called it banditry.
entries.literal: He asked all the various students, and the various students either said it was rebellion or said it was bandits.

entries.zh: 於是二世令御史案諸生言反者下吏，非所宜言。
entries.en: The Second Emperor then ordered the Imperial Secretary to investigate those scholars who had called it rebellion and hand them over to the authorities, for speaking what was improper.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Second Generation ordered the imperial secretary to investigate the various students who said it was rebellion and send them to the officials, as they had not spoken what was proper.

entries.zh: 諸言盜者皆罷之。
entries.en: All those who had called it banditry were dismissed from their posts.
entries.literal: All those who said it was bandits were dismissed.

entries.zh: 乃賜叔孫通帛二十匹，衣一襲，拜為博士。
entries.en: He bestowed upon Shusun Tong twenty bolts of silk and a set of clothes, and appointed him as a court erudite.
entries.literal: He then granted Shusun Tong twenty bolts of silk, one set of clothes, and appointed him as an erudite.

entries.zh: 叔孫通已出宮，反舍，諸生曰：「先生何言之諛也？」
entries.en: After Shusun Tong left the palace and returned to his lodging, the students said: 'Sir, why did you speak so flatteringly?'
entries.literal: Shusun Tong had left the palace and returned to his lodging when the students said: 'Sir, why were your words so flattering?'

entries.zh: 通曰：「公不知也，我幾不脫於虎口！」
entries.en: Tong said, "You gentlemen do not understand. I nearly failed to escape the tiger's mouth!"
entries.literal: Tong said, 'You gentlemen do not understand—I nearly did not escape the tiger's mouth!'

entries.zh: 乃亡去，之薛，薛已降楚矣。
entries.en: He then fled to Xue, but Xue had already surrendered to Chu.
entries.literal: He then fled and went to Xue, but Xue had already submitted to Chu.

entries.zh: 及項梁之薛，叔孫通從之。
entries.en: When Xiang Liang came to Xue, Shusun Tong attached himself to him.
entries.literal: When Xiang Liang went to Xue, Shusun Tong followed him.

entries.zh: 敗於定陶，從懷王。
entries.en: After the defeat at Dingtao, he followed King Huai.
entries.literal: After the defeat at Dingtao, he followed the Huai King.

entries.zh: 懷王為義帝，徙長沙，叔孫通留事項王。
entries.en: When King Huai was made the Righteous Emperor and relocated to Changsha, Shusun Tong remained behind to serve King Xiang.
entries.literal: The Huai King became the Righteous Emperor and moved to Changsha, while Shusun Tong stayed and served Xiang Wang.

entries.zh: 漢二年，漢王從五諸侯入彭城，叔孫通降漢王。
entries.en: In the second year of the Han dynasty, the King of Han entered Pengcheng with the forces of five feudal lords, and Shusun Tong surrendered to the King of Han.
entries.literal: In the second year of Han, the Han King followed the five feudal lords into Pengcheng, and Shusun Tong submitted to the Han King.

entries.zh: 漢王敗而西，因竟從漢。
entries.en: When the King of Han was defeated and retreated westward, Shusun Tong followed and ultimately committed himself to the Han cause.
entries.literal: The Han King was defeated and fled west, and thus ultimately joined the Han cause.

entries.zh: 叔孫通之降漢，從儒生弟子百餘人，然通無所言進，專言諸故群盜壯士進之。
entries.en: When Shusun Tong submitted to Han, he was followed by over a hundred Confucian scholar disciples, but Tong made no recommendations for them. Instead, he specifically recommended the former bandit leaders and warriors for advancement.
entries.literal: Shusun Tong's submission to Han, followed Confucian scholar disciples over hundred people, but Tong nothing said advanced, specially spoke various former bandit group strong men advanced them.

entries.zh: 弟子皆竊罵曰：「事先生數歲，幸得從降漢，今不能進臣等，專言大猾，何也？」
entries.en: All the disciples secretly cursed and said, 'We served the master for several years and were fortunate enough to follow him in submitting to Han. Now he cannot advance us, but instead only speaks of promoting those big rogues—what is the reason?'
entries.literal: Disciples all secretly cursed said: 'Served master several years, fortunately got follow submit Han, now cannot advance us ministers, specially speak big cunning ones, why?'

entries.zh: 叔孫通聞之，乃謂曰：「漢王方蒙矢石爭天下，諸生寧能鬬乎？
entries.en: Shusun Tong heard this and then said to them, 'The Han King is currently braving arrows and stones to contend for the empire—how can you Confucian scholars fight?
entries.literal: Shusun Tong heard this, then said to them: 'Han King currently braves arrows stones contends for tianxia, various scholars how can fight?

entries.zh: 故先言斬將搴旗之士。
entries.en: That is why I first recommended warriors who behead enemy generals and seize their banners.
entries.literal: Therefore, I first speak of promoting those warriors who behead generals and seize enemy banners.

entries.zh: 諸生且待我，我不忘矣。」
entries.en: You scholars should wait for me—I will not forget you.'
entries.literal: Various scholars temporarily wait for me, I will not forget you.'

entries.zh: 漢王拜叔孫通為博士，號稷嗣君。
entries.en: The King of Han appointed Shusun Tong as an erudite and bestowed on him the title Lord Successor of Ji.
entries.literal: The Han King appointed Shusun Tong as a Doctor and gave him the title 'Successor to Ji.'

entries.zh: 孝惠帝為東朝長樂宮，及閒往，數蹕煩人，乃作複道，方筑武庫南。
entries.en: Emperor Hui held court at the Changle Palace to the east, and when he traveled there, the repeated clearing of the roads troubled the people. He therefore had a covered walkway constructed, just south of the armory.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui went to court at the eastern Changle Palace, and when he went there, repeatedly clearing the way troubled the people. So he built a covered walkway, which was just south of the armory.

entries.zh: 叔孫生奏事，因請閒曰：「陛下何自筑複道高寢，衣冠月出游高廟？
entries.en: Master Shusun memorialized on affairs, then requested a private audience and said, 'Why does Your Majesty personally build a covered walkway to the high chamber and, wearing court robes, go out monthly to tour the High Temple?
entries.literal: Shusun Sheng memorialized affairs, then requested private audience said: 'Your Majesty why personally build covered walkway high chamber, in robes monthly go out tour high temple?

entries.zh: 高廟，漢太祖，柰何令後世子孫乘宗廟道上行哉？」
entries.en: The High Temple is the temple of Han's Great Ancestor. How can we allow descendants in later generations to travel along the ancestral-temple road?"
entries.literal: The High Temple is Han's Great Ancestor—how can we let future generations' descendants travel along the ancestral temple road!'

entries.zh: 孝惠帝大懼，曰：「急壞之。」
entries.en: Emperor Hui was greatly terrified and said, 'Destroy it immediately.'
entries.literal: Filial Hui Emperor greatly feared, said: 'Urgently destroy it.'

entries.zh: 叔孫生曰：「人主無過舉。
entries.en: Master Shusun said, 'A ruler makes no mistaken actions.
entries.literal: Shusun Sheng said: 'Ruler has no mistaken actions.

entries.zh: 今已作，百姓皆知之，今壞此，則示有過舉。
entries.en: Now that it has already been built and all the people know of it, if we were to tear it down, it would reveal a misstep.
entries.literal: Now it has already been built and all the common people know about it. If we destroy it now, it will show that there was a mistaken action.

entries.zh: 願陛下原廟渭北，衣冠月出游之，益廣多宗廟，大孝之本也。」
entries.en: I wish Your Majesty would establish a temple north of the Wei River and, wearing court robes, go out monthly to tour it. Moreover, expand and increase the ancestral temples—this is the root of great filial piety.'
entries.literal: Wish Your Majesty establish temple Wei north, in robes monthly go out tour it, moreover expand many ancestral temples, great filial piety's root.'

entries.zh: 上乃詔有司立原廟。
entries.en: The Emperor then ordered the responsible officials to establish a branch temple.
entries.literal: The Emperor then decreed that the responsible officials establish a branch temple.

entries.zh: 原廟起，以複道故。
entries.en: The branch temple was established on account of the covered walkway.
entries.literal: The Yuan Temple was established because of the covered walkway.

entries.zh: 漢五年，已并天下，諸侯共尊漢王為皇帝於定陶，叔孫通就其儀號。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Han, the empire having been unified, the feudal lords together honored the King of Han as Emperor at Dingtao, and Shusun Tong arranged the ceremonies and titles for the occasion.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Han, having already unified the empire, the feudal lords together honored the Han King as emperor at Dingtao, and Shusun Tong arranged the ceremonies and titles.

entries.zh: 高帝悉去秦苛儀法，為簡易。
entries.en: Emperor Gao abolished all the harsh ceremonies and regulations of Qin, replacing them with simplicity.
entries.literal: The High Emperor completely abolished the harsh Qin ceremonies and laws, making them simple and easy.

entries.zh: 群臣飲酒爭功，醉或妄呼，拔劍擊柱，高帝患之。
entries.en: The ministers would drink and quarrel over their merits; some, in their drunkenness, would shout wildly, draw their swords, and hack at the pillars. Emperor Gao found this deeply troubling.
entries.literal: The assembled ministers drank wine and argued about their merits. Some got drunk and shouted wildly, drew their swords and struck the pillars. The High Emperor was troubled by this.

entries.zh: 叔孫通知上益厭之也，說上曰：「夫儒者難與進取，可與守成。
entries.en: Shusun Tong knew the High Emperor increasingly disliked this and persuaded him, saying, 'Confucian scholars are difficult to use for conquest, but they can be used for maintaining what has been achieved.
entries.literal: Shusun Tong knew High Emperor increasingly disliked it, persuaded High Emperor said: 'Indeed Confucian scholars difficult with for advancement, can with for maintaining achievement.

entries.zh: 臣願徵魯諸生，與臣弟子共起朝儀。」
