entries.en: I wish to summon the Confucian scholars of Lu and, together with my disciples, establish court ceremonies.'
entries.literal: Minister wishes summon Lu various scholars, with minister's disciples together establish court ceremony.'

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「得無難乎？」
entries.en: The High Emperor said, 'Will it not be difficult?'
entries.literal: High Emperor said: 'Will it not be difficult?'

entries.zh: 叔孫通曰：「五帝異樂，三王不同禮。
entries.en: Shusun Tong said, 'The Five Emperors had different music, and the Three Kings had different rites.
entries.literal: Shusun Tong said: 'Five Emperors different music, Three Kings different rites.

entries.zh: 禮者，因時世人情為之節文者也。
entries.en: Rites are the formal patterns shaped by the times and by human nature.
entries.literal: Rites are ritual patterns created following the times, generations, and human feelings.

entries.zh: 故夏、殷、周之禮所因損益可知者，謂不相復也。
entries.en: Thus, the ways in which the rites of the Xia, Yin, and Zhou dynasties adapted, subtracted, and added can be traced—they did not simply repeat one another.
entries.literal: Therefore, what was followed, added, or subtracted in the rites of Xia, Yin, and Zhou can be known—they do not simply repeat each other.

entries.zh: 臣願頗采古禮與秦儀雜就之。」
entries.en: I wish to somewhat collect ancient rites and mix them together with Qin ceremonies to complete them.'
entries.literal: Minister wishes somewhat collect ancient rites with Qin ceremonies mix complete them.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「可試為之，令易知，度吾所能行為之。」
entries.en: The High Emperor said, 'We can try doing it—make it easy to understand and within my ability to perform.'
entries.literal: High Emperor said: 'Can try do it, make easy know, measure my ability to do it.'

entries.zh: 高帝崩，孝惠即位，乃謂叔孫生曰：「先帝園陵寢廟，群臣莫（能）習。」
entries.en: After the High Emperor passed away and Emperor Hui ascended the throne, he said to Master Shusun, 'The assembled ministers are not familiar with the rituals for the late emperor's park tomb and ancestral temple.'
entries.literal: High Emperor collapsed, Filial Hui ascended throne, then said to Shusun Sheng: 'Late Emperor park tomb sleeping temple, assembled ministers none able practice.'

entries.zh: 徙為太常，定宗廟儀法。
entries.en: He was transferred to the post of Grand Master of Ceremonies, where he established the ceremonial regulations for the ancestral temples.
entries.literal: He was transferred to serve as Grand Master of Ceremonies and established the ceremonial regulations for the ancestral temples.

entries.zh: 及稍定漢諸儀法，皆叔孫生為太常所論箸也。
entries.en: As Han's ceremonial regulations were gradually established, they were all discussed and codified by Master Shusun during his tenure as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: When Han's ceremonial regulations were gradually established, they were all discussed and recorded by Master Shusun while serving as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 高帝罷平城歸，韓王信亡入胡。
entries.en: After Emperor Gao withdrew from Pingcheng and returned, King Xin of Han fled to the Hu.
entries.literal: The Gao Emperor dismissed Pingcheng and returned, while Han King Xin fled and entered the Hu.

entries.zh: 當是時，冒頓為單于，兵彊，控弦三十萬，數苦北邊。
entries.en: At that time, Modu was the Chanyu. His forces were formidable—he commanded three hundred thousand mounted archers and repeatedly ravaged the northern frontier.
entries.literal: At this time, Modun served as Chanyu, his troops were strong, he controlled three hundred thousand archers, and frequently pained the northern borders.

entries.zh: 上患之，問劉敬。
entries.en: The Emperor was troubled by this and consulted Liu Jing.
entries.literal: The Sovereign worried about it and asked Liu Jing.

entries.zh: 劉敬曰：「天下初定，士卒罷於兵，未可以武服也。
entries.en: Liu Jing said: 'The empire has newly been pacified, the officers and soldiers are fatigued by warfare, and it cannot yet be subjugated with martial means.
entries.literal: Liu Jing said: 'All-under-heaven newly pacified, officers soldiers fatigued by warfare, not yet can with martial subjugate.

entries.zh: 冒頓殺父代立，妻群母，以力為威，未可以仁義說也。
entries.en: Modu killed his father and seized the throne, took his father's widows as wives, and rules by force and intimidation—he cannot be won over with benevolence and righteousness.
entries.literal: Modu killed his father and replaced him, took his father's widows as wives, uses strength to create awe, and cannot be persuaded with benevolence and righteousness.

entries.zh: 獨可以計久遠子孫為臣耳，然恐陛下不能為。」
entries.en: Only with a plan for the long term can their descendants serve as ministers, but I fear Your Majesty cannot do it.'
entries.literal: Only can with plan long distant descendants serve as ministers, yet fear Your Majesty cannot do.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「誠可，何為不能！
entries.en: The Sovereign said: 'If it truly can be done, why cannot I do it!
entries.literal: Sovereign said: 'Truly can, why cannot!

entries.zh: 顧為柰何？」
entries.en: But how should it be done?'
entries.literal: But do how?'

entries.zh: 劉敬對曰：「陛下誠能以適長公主妻之，厚奉遺之，彼知漢適女送厚，蠻夷必慕以為閼氏，生子必為太子。
entries.en: Liu Jing replied, "If Your Majesty can truly give him the legitimate eldest princess as his wife and send her with generous gifts, then when he knows that Han has sent a legitimate daughter with such wealth, the barbarians will surely esteem her as Yanzhi, and any son she bears will certainly become crown prince.
entries.literal: Liu Jing replied, 'If Your Majesty can truly give him the legitimate eldest princess as wife, with rich gifts sent along, when he knows that Han sends a legitimate daughter with such generosity, the barbarians will surely esteem her as Yanzhi, and any son born will certainly become crown prince.

entries.zh: 代單于。
entries.en: He will succeed the Chanyu.
entries.literal: He will replace the Chanyu.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why is this so?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 貪漢重幣。
entries.en: Because they covet the lavish gifts of Han.
entries.literal: They are greedy for Han's heavy gifts.

entries.zh: 陛下以歲時漢所餘彼所鮮數問遺，因使辯士風諭以禮節。
entries.en: Your Majesty should regularly send them, according to the seasons, whatever goods are abundant in Han and scarce among them, and dispatch eloquent envoys to instruct them gently in ritual propriety.
entries.literal: Your Majesty should frequently bestow upon them what Han has in surplus and they lack according to the seasons, and following this send eloquent scholars to gently exhort them with rites and propriety.

entries.zh: 冒頓在，固為子婿；
entries.en: While Modun is present, he firmly serves as son-in-law;
entries.literal: Modun present, firmly serves as son-in-law;

entries.zh: 死，則外孫為單于。
entries.en: When he dies, your grandson will become the Chanyu.
entries.literal: When he dies, then the grandson will become Chanyu.

entries.zh: 豈嘗聞外孫敢與大父抗禮者哉？
entries.en: Have you ever heard of a grandson who dares to contend in rites with his grandfather?
entries.literal: How ever heard grandson dares with grandfather contend rites?

entries.zh: 兵可無戰以漸臣也。
entries.en: Without a battle, the Xiongnu could gradually be brought to submission.
entries.literal: The troops can without battle gradually make them ministers.

entries.zh: 若陛下不能遣長公主，而令宗室及後宮詐稱公主，彼亦知，不肯貴近，無益也。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty cannot send the eldest princess, but orders the imperial clan and rear palace to falsely call someone princess, they will also know, and will not be willing to honor and approach her. It will be of no benefit.'
entries.literal: If Your Majesty cannot send eldest princess, yet orders imperial clan and rear palace falsely call princess, they also know, not willing honor approach, no benefit.'

entries.zh: 高帝曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Gao Emperor said: 'Good.'
entries.literal: Gao Emperor said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 欲遣長公主。
entries.en: He wished to send the eldest princess.
entries.literal: He desired to send the eldest princess.

entries.zh: 呂后日夜泣，曰：「妾唯太子、一女，柰何棄之匈奴！」
entries.en: Empress Lu wept day and night, saying, "I have only the Crown Prince and one daughter. How can I cast her away to the Xiongnu?"
entries.literal: Empress Lü wept day and night, saying, 'I have only the crown prince and one daughter—how can I abandon her to the Xiongnu!'

entries.zh: 上竟不能遣長公主，而取家人子名為長公主，妻單于。
entries.en: In the end, the Emperor could not bring himself to send the eldest princess. Instead, he took a girl from a common family, bestowed on her the title of eldest princess, and married her to the Chanyu.
entries.literal: The Sovereign finally could not send the eldest princess, but took a child from a commoner family and named her the eldest princess to be wife to the Chanyu.

entries.zh: 使劉敬往結和親約。
entries.en: He sent Liu Jing to negotiate and conclude the marriage alliance.
entries.literal: He sent Liu Jing to go and tie the peaceful kinship covenant.

entries.zh: 漢七年，韓王信反，高帝自往擊之。
entries.en: In the seventh year of the Han dynasty, King Xin of Han rebelled, and Emperor Gao personally led a campaign against him.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Han, King Xin of Han rebelled, and the Gao Emperor personally went to strike him.

entries.zh: 至晉陽，聞信與匈奴欲共擊漢，上大怒，使人使匈奴。
entries.en: Upon reaching Jinyang, he learned that Xin intended to join forces with the Xiongnu to attack Han. The Emperor was furious and sent envoys to the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: He arrived at Jinyang and heard that Xin, together with the Xiongnu, intended to attack Han together. The Emperor was greatly angered and sent envoys to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 匈奴匿其壯士肥牛馬，但見老弱及羸畜。
entries.en: The Xiongnu hid their finest warriors and fattest cattle and horses, displaying only the old and weak along with emaciated livestock.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu hid their strong warriors and fat oxen and horses, only showing old and weak people and emaciated livestock.

entries.zh: 使者十輩來，皆言匈奴可擊。
entries.en: Envoys returned in ten successive groups, all reporting that the Xiongnu could be attacked.
entries.literal: Envoys came in ten groups, all saying the Xiongnu could be struck.

entries.zh: 上使劉敬復往使匈奴，還報曰：「兩國相擊，此宜夸矜見所長。
entries.en: The Emperor again sent Liu Jing as envoy to the Xiongnu. Jing returned and reported, "When two states are about to fight, each ought to boast and show off its strengths.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Liu Jing again as envoy to the Xiongnu. He returned and reported, 'When two states are about to fight, each should boast and display its strengths.

entries.zh: 今臣往，徒見羸瘠老弱，此必欲見短，伏奇兵以爭利。
entries.en: When I went, all I saw were the emaciated, the old, and the weak. They are surely displaying their weaknesses while concealing crack troops to seize the advantage.
entries.literal: Now when I went, I only saw emaciated, old, and weak people. This certainly means they desire to show weaknesses while hiding crack troops to contend for advantage.

entries.zh: 愚以為匈奴不可擊也。」
entries.en: In my humble opinion, the Xiongnu must not be attacked."
entries.literal: In my foolish opinion, the Xiongnu cannot be attacked.'

entries.zh: 是時漢兵已踰句注，二十餘萬兵已業行。
entries.en: By this time, the Han forces had already crossed the Gouzhu Pass, and over two hundred thousand troops were already on the march.
entries.literal: At this time Han troops had already crossed Gouzhu, and more than two hundred thousand soldiers were already on the march.

entries.zh: 上怒，罵劉敬曰：「齊虜！
entries.en: The Sovereign was angered and cursed Liu Jing, saying: 'Qi captive!
entries.literal: Sovereign angered, cursed Liu Jing said: 'Qi captive!

entries.zh: 以口舌得官，今乃妄言沮吾軍。」
entries.en: You gained office with your tongue, and now you make reckless claims to obstruct my army."
entries.literal: You got your office with your tongue—now you speak reckless words to obstruct my army.'

entries.zh: 械系敬廣武。
entries.en: He had Liu Jing shackled and imprisoned at Guangwu.
entries.literal: He shackled and bound Jing at Guangwu.

entries.zh: 遂往，至平城，匈奴果出奇兵圍高帝白登，七日然後得解。
entries.en: He pressed onward to Pingcheng, where the Xiongnu indeed unleashed their hidden forces and surrounded Emperor Gao at Baideng. Only after seven days was the siege lifted.
entries.literal: He then went, arrived at Pingcheng, and the Xiongnu indeed sent crack troops that surrounded the Gao Emperor at Baideng. Only after seven days did he get release.

entries.zh: 高帝至廣武，赦敬，曰：「吾不用公言，以困平城。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao reached Guangwu, he pardoned Jing and said, "Because I did not use your advice, I was trapped at Pingcheng.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao arrived at Guangwu, pardoned Jing, and said, 'I did not heed your words and was trapped at Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 吾皆已斬前使十輩言可擊者矣。」
entries.en: I have already beheaded all ten earlier groups of envoys who said the Xiongnu could be attacked."
entries.literal: I have already beheaded all ten groups of the earlier envoys who said they could be attacked.'

entries.zh: 乃封敬二千戶，為關內侯，號為建信侯。
entries.en: He then enfeoffed Liu Jing with two thousand households, granted him the rank of Marquis Within the Passes, and titled him the Marquis of Jianxin.
entries.literal: He then enfeoffed Jing with two thousand households, served as Guannei Hou, and titled him Jianxin Hou.

entries.zh: 已而問婁敬，婁敬說曰：「陛下都洛陽，豈欲與周室比隆哉？」
entries.en: Then he questioned Lou Jing. Lou Jing said, 'Your Majesty is establishing the capital at Luoyang—do you wish to rival the Zhou in splendor?'
entries.literal: Then he asked Lou Jing. Lou Jing said, 'Your Majesty is making Luoyang the capital—do you wish to rival the Zhou in glory?'

entries.zh: 上曰：「然。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, 'Yes.'
entries.literal: The Emperor said, 'Yes.'

entries.zh: 婁敬曰：「陛下取天下與周室異。
entries.en: Lou Jing said: "Your Majesty took the empire differently from the Zhou house.
entries.literal: Lou Jing said: 'Your Majesty took all-under-heaven differently from the Zhou house.

entries.zh: 周之先自后稷，堯封之邰，積德累善十有餘世。
entries.en: The Zhou ancestors began with Hou Ji, whom Yao enfeoffed at Tai, accumulating virtue and goodness for more than ten generations.
entries.literal: Zhou's ancestors from Hou Ji, Yao enfeoffed him Tai, accumulated virtue piled goodness ten plus generations.

entries.zh: 公劉避桀居豳。
entries.en: Duke Liu fled from Jie and settled at Bin.
entries.literal: Duke Liu fled from Jie and dwelt at Bin.

entries.zh: 太王以狄伐故，去豳，杖馬箠居岐，國人爭隨之。
entries.en: Because of Di attacks, King Tai left Bin. Leaning on his riding crop, he settled at Qiyi, and the people of his state vied to follow him.
entries.literal: Because of Di attacks, King Tai left Bin, leaned on his horse whip and dwelt at Qiyi, and the people of the state contended to follow him.

entries.zh: 及文王為西伯，斷虞芮之訟，始受命，呂望、伯夷自海濱來歸之。
entries.en: When Wen Wang became Western Bo, he adjudicated the dispute between Yu and Rui, began receiving the mandate, and Lü Wang and Bo Yi came from the seacoast to submit to him.
entries.literal: When Wen Wang became Western Bo, adjudicated Yu Rui's dispute, began received mandate, Lü Wang, Bo Yi from seacoast came submitted to him.

entries.zh: 武王伐紂，不期而會孟津之上八百諸侯，皆曰紂可伐矣，遂滅殷。
entries.en: When King Wu marched against Zhou, eight hundred lords gathered unbidden at Mengjin. All said, 'Zhou can be attacked,' and he then destroyed the Yin dynasty.
entries.literal: King Wu attacked Zhou. Without prior arrangement, eight hundred feudal lords met him above Mengjin; all said, 'Zhou can be attacked,' and he then extinguished Yin.

entries.zh: 成王即位，周公之屬傅相焉，乃營成周洛邑，以此為天下之中也，諸侯四方納貢職，道裏均矣，有德則易以王，無德則易以亡。
entries.en: When King Cheng ascended the throne, Zhou Gong's kinsmen served as his tutors and ministers. They then built Chengzhou at Luoyi, making it the center of the realm, so that the feudal lords from the four directions could submit tribute and service over balanced routes. With virtue, one could easily become king; without virtue, one could easily perish.
entries.literal: Cheng Wang ascended the throne, and Zhou Gong's kinsmen served as tutors and ministers to him. They then built Chengzhou at Luoyi, making it the center of the realm, so that the feudal lords from the four directions submitted tribute and duties at equal road distances. With virtue one could easily become king; without virtue one could easily perish.

entries.zh: 凡居此者，欲令周務以德致人，不欲依阻險，令後世驕奢以虐民也。
entries.en: All who chose to reside there wished the Zhou to devote themselves to attracting the people through virtue, not to rely on natural defenses, lest future generations grow arrogant and extravagant and oppress the people.
entries.literal: All who dwelt here desired to make Zhou attend to attracting people with virtue, not desiring to rely on strategic defiles, so as to prevent later generations from becoming arrogant and extravagant in oppressing the people.

entries.zh: 及周之盛時，天下和洽，四夷鄉風，慕義懷德，附離而并事天子，不屯一卒，不戰一士，八夷大國之民莫不賓服，效其貢職。
entries.en: When Zhou was flourishing, the realm was harmonious and at peace. The four Yi turned toward its customs, admired righteousness, cherished virtue, attached themselves to it though far away, and together served the Son of Heaven. Without stationing a single soldier or fighting a single warrior, the people of the eight Yi and the great states all submitted and presented their tribute and service.
entries.literal: When Zhou was flourishing, the realm was harmonious and at peace. The four Yi turned toward its customs, admired righteousness, cherished virtue, attached themselves to it though far away, and together served the Son of Heaven. Without stationing a single soldier or fighting a single warrior, the people of the eight Yi and the great states all submitted and presented their tribute and duties.

entries.zh: 及周之衰也，分而為兩，天下莫朝，周不能制也。
entries.en: When Zhou declined, it split in two. None in the realm came to court, and Zhou could no longer control them.
entries.literal: When Zhou declined, it divided into two, none in the realm came to court, and Zhou could no longer control them.

entries.zh: 非其德薄也，而形勢弱也。
entries.en: It was not that their virtue was lacking, but that their strategic position was weak.
entries.literal: It was not that their virtue was thin, but that their strategic position was weak.

entries.zh: 今陛下起豐沛，收卒三千人，以之徑往而卷蜀漢，定三秦，與項羽戰滎陽，爭成皋之口，大戰七十，小戰四十，使天下之民肝腦涂地，父子暴骨中野，不可勝數，哭泣之聲未絕，傷痍者未起，而欲比隆於成康之時，臣竊以為不侔也。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty arose from Feng and Pei, gathered three thousand soldiers, and with them swept through Shu and Han, pacified the Three Qins, battled Xiang Yu at Xingyang, and fought for the pass at Chenggao. In seventy great battles and forty small battles, the people of the realm had their livers and brains smeared on the ground, and fathers and sons exposed their bones in the fields beyond counting. The sound of weeping has not ceased, the wounded have not yet risen, and yet you wish to compare your flourishing age with the time of Cheng and Kang. I privately think they are not equal.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty arose from Feng and Pei, gathered three thousand soldiers, and with them went straight on to sweep through Shu and Han, pacify the Three Qins, battle Xiang Yu at Xingyang, and contend for the pass at Chenggao. In seventy great battles and forty small battles, the people of the realm had their livers and brains smeared on the ground, and fathers and sons exposed their bones in the fields beyond counting. The sounds of weeping have not ceased, the wounded have not yet risen, yet you wish to compare your flourishing age with the time of Cheng and Kang. I privately think they are not equal.

entries.zh: 且夫秦地被山帶河，四塞以為固，卒然有急，百萬之眾可具也。
entries.en: Moreover, the land of Qin is flanked by mountains and belted by the Yellow River, secured on all four sides by strategic passes. Should an emergency suddenly arise, an army of a million could be assembled.
entries.literal: Moreover, Qin territory is covered by mountains and girded by rivers, with four strategic passes making it firm. If suddenly there is an emergency, a million multitudes can be prepared.

entries.zh: 因秦之故，資甚美膏腴之地，此所謂天府者也。
entries.en: Building on the foundations of Qin, it commands lands of exceptional fertility—this is what men call the Heavenly Storehouse.
entries.literal: Following Qin's example, it has resources of very beautiful fertile lands—this is what is called the heavenly storehouse.

entries.zh: 陛下入關而都之，山東雖亂，秦之故地可全而有也。
entries.en: If Your Majesty enters the passes and establishes the capital there, then even should the lands east of the mountains fall into chaos, the old territories of Qin can be held in their entirety.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty enters the pass and makes it the capital, even if Shandong is chaotic, Qin's old lands can be completely preserved.

entries.zh: 夫與人鬬，不搤其亢，拊其背，未能全其勝也。
entries.en: When wrestling an opponent, if you do not seize him by the throat but merely pat his back, you cannot secure a complete victory.
entries.literal: Now when fighting with a person, if you do not grasp his throat but pat his back, you cannot complete your victory.

entries.zh: 今陛下入關而都，案秦之故地，此亦搤天下之亢而拊其背也。」
entries.en: Now if Your Majesty enters the passes and establishes the capital there, holding Qin's old territories, this too seizes the realm by the throat while pressing on its back."
entries.literal: Now if Your Majesty enters the passes and establishes the capital there, holding Qin's old lands, this too is seizing the realm by the throat while pressing on its back.'

entries.zh: 於是上曰：「本言都秦地者婁敬，『婁』者乃『劉』也。」
entries.en: The Emperor then said, "The one who originally spoke of establishing the capital in Qin territory was Lou Jing; Lou is Liu."
entries.literal: The Emperor then said, 'The one who originally spoke of establishing the capital in Qin territory was Lou Jing—"Lou" is "Liu."'

entries.zh: 賜姓劉氏，拜為郎中，號為奉春君。
entries.en: He was granted the imperial surname Liu, appointed as a Palace Attendant, and given the title Lord of Fengchun.
entries.literal: He was granted the surname Liu, appointed as Palace Attendant, and titled Lord Fengchun.

entries.zh: 劉敬從匈奴來，因言「匈奴河南白羊、樓煩王，去長安近者七百里，輕騎一日一夜可以至秦中。
entries.en: When Liu Jing returned from the Xiongnu, he said, "The Xiongnu kings Baiyang and Loufan south of the Yellow River are, at their nearest point, only seven hundred li from Chang'an; light cavalry could reach the Qin heartland in a single day and night.
entries.literal: When Liu Jing returned from the Xiongnu, he then said, 'The Xiongnu kings Baiyang and Loufan south of the Yellow River are, at nearest, seven hundred li from Chang'an; light cavalry can reach the heart of Qin in one day and one night.

entries.zh: 秦中新破，少民，地肥饒，可益實。
entries.en: The heartland of Qin has been recently devastated and is sparsely populated, yet the land is fertile and abundant—it can be further settled and filled.
entries.literal: Qin central has newly been broken, has few people, the land is fertile and abundant, and can be increased and filled.

entries.zh: 夫諸侯初起時，非齊諸田，楚昭、屈、景莫能興。
entries.en: When the feudal lords first rose in rebellion, none could have succeeded without the Tian clans of Qi and the Zhao, Qu, and Jing clans of Chu.
entries.literal: Now when the feudal lords initially arose, without the various Tian of Qi and the Zhao, Qu, Jing of Chu, none could rise.

entries.zh: 今陛下雖都關中，實少人。
entries.en: Now, though Your Majesty has established the capital in Guanzhong, the population there is in truth too sparse.
entries.literal: Now although Your Majesty has the capital in Guanzhong, in reality it has few people.

entries.zh: 北近胡寇，東有六國之族，宗彊，一日有變，陛下亦未得高枕而臥也。
entries.en: To the north, Hu raiders are close by; to the east are the clans of the six states, with powerful lineages. If one day disorder breaks out, Your Majesty still will not be able to sleep soundly.
entries.literal: To the north the Hu raiders are near; to the east are the clans of the six states, strong in lineage. If one day there is trouble, Your Majesty cannot yet sleep soundly either.

entries.zh: 臣願陛下徙齊諸田，楚昭、屈、景，燕、趙、韓、魏後，及豪桀名家居關中。
entries.en: I request that Your Majesty relocate the Tian clans of Qi, the Zhao, Qu, and Jing clans of Chu, the descendants of the Yan, Zhao, Han, and Wei ruling houses, and all the powerful and prominent families to reside in Guanzhong.
entries.literal: I wish Your Majesty to move the various Tian of Qi, the Zhao, Qu, Jing of Chu, the descendants of Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei, and the heroic stalwart famous families to dwell in Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 無事，可以備胡；
entries.en: In peacetime, it can serve to guard against the Hu;
entries.literal: In peacetime it can serve to guard against the Hu;

entries.zh: 諸侯有變，亦足率以東伐。
entries.en: Should the feudal lords rebel, these relocated families would also serve as a ready force to lead eastward in a punitive campaign.
entries.literal: If the feudal lords rebel, it is also sufficient to lead them in attacking eastward.

entries.zh: 此彊本弱末之術也」。
entries.en: This is the method of strengthening the root and weakening the branches.'
entries.literal: This strengthen root weaken branches method.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: The Sovereign said: 'Good.'
entries.literal: Sovereign said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 乃使劉敬徙所言關中十餘萬口。
entries.en: He then dispatched Liu Jing to relocate over a hundred thousand people to Guanzhong, as he had advised.
entries.literal: He then sent Liu Jing to move what he had spoken of—ten-plus ten thousand people—to Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 叔孫通儒服，漢王憎之；
entries.en: Shusun Tong wore Confucian robes, and the King of Han disliked them;
entries.literal: Shusun Tong wore Confucian robes, which the King of Han disliked;

entries.zh: 乃變其服，服短衣，楚製，漢王喜。
entries.en: So he changed his attire, adopting a short jacket in the Chu fashion, which pleased the King of Han.
entries.literal: So he changed his clothing and wore a short jacket in Chu style, which pleased the Han King.

entries.zh: 遂與所徵三十人西，及上左右為學者與其弟子百餘人為綿蕞野外。
entries.en: So he went west with the thirty summoned scholars, along with the High Emperor's attendants who were scholars and his own disciples—over a hundred people total—and they practiced in a continuous tent in the open fields.
entries.literal: Then with summoned thirty people west, and High Emperor's left right learned ones with his disciples hundred more people made continuous tent open country outside.

entries.zh: 習之月餘，叔孫通曰：「上可試觀。」
entries.en: After practicing for over a month, Shusun Tong said, 'Your Majesty can try observing.'
entries.literal: Practiced it month more, Shusun Tong said: 'High Emperor can try observe.'

entries.zh: 上既觀，使行禮，曰：「吾能為此。」
entries.en: After the High Emperor observed, he had them perform the rites and said, 'I can do this.'
entries.literal: High Emperor already observed, made perform rites, said: 'I can do this.'

entries.zh: 乃令群臣習肄，會十月。
entries.en: He then ordered all the ministers to practice and rehearse, scheduling the assembly for the tenth month.
entries.literal: He then ordered all the ministers to practice and drill, scheduling the assembly for the tenth month.

entries.zh: 漢七年，長樂宮成，諸侯群臣皆朝十月。
entries.en: In the seventh year of the Han dynasty, when the Changle Palace was completed, all the feudal lords and ministers gathered for the court assembly in the tenth month.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Han, when the Changle Palace was completed, all the feudal lords and ministers assembled for court in the tenth month.

entries.zh: 儀：先平明，謁者治禮，引以次入殿門，廷中陳車騎步卒衛宮，設兵張旗志。
entries.en: The ceremony: Before dawn, the ye zhe arranged the rites and led them in proper order to enter the hall gate. In the courtyard were arrayed chariots, cavalry, and infantry guarding the palace, with weapons displayed and banners and insignia unfurled.
entries.literal: Ceremony: First dawn, ye zhe arranged rites, led in order enter hall gate, courtyard middle arranged chariots cavalry infantry guarded palace, set weapons displayed banners insignia.

entries.zh: 傳言「趨」。
entries.en: The command was transmitted: 'Hurry!'
entries.literal: Transmitted words 'hurry'.

entries.zh: 殿下郎中俠陛，陛數百人。
entries.en: Below the hall, the Palace Attendants flanked the steps, with several hundred men lining the stairway.
entries.literal: Below the hall, the lang zhong flanked the stairs, with several hundred people upon the stairs.

entries.zh: 功臣列侯諸將軍軍吏以次陳西方，東鄉；
entries.en: The meritorious ministers, ranked marquises, generals, and army officials were arrayed in order on the western side, facing east;
entries.literal: Meritorious ministers, ranked marquises, generals, and army officials were arranged in sequence on the western side, facing east;

entries.zh: 文官丞相以下陳東方，西鄉。
entries.en: The civil officials, from the Chancellor on down, were arrayed on the eastern side, facing west.
entries.literal: The civil officials, from the prime minister down, were arrayed on the eastern side, facing west.

entries.zh: 大行設九賓，臚傳。
entries.en: The Grand Usher arranged the nine ranks of guests, and the heralds relayed the announcements.
entries.literal: The grand usher arranged the nine ranks of guests, and the lu proclaimed.

entries.zh: 於是皇帝輦出房，百官執職傳警，引諸侯王以下至吏六百石以次奉賀。
entries.en: Then the Emperor emerged from his chamber on the imperial carriage. The hundred officials performed their duties and relayed the ceremonial alerts, leading the feudal lords and kings down to officials ranked at six hundred bushels to offer their congratulations in order of precedence.
entries.literal: Then the emperor's chariot emerged from the chamber. The hundred officials held their duties and transmitted alarms, leading the feudal lords and kings down to officials of six hundred dan to offer congratulations in order.

entries.zh: 自諸侯王以下莫不振恐肅敬。
entries.en: From the feudal lords and kings on down, all trembled with awe and solemn reverence.
entries.literal: From the feudal lords and kings down, none were not trembling with fear and solemn respect.

entries.zh: 至禮畢，復置法酒。
entries.en: When the ceremonies were concluded, the ritual wine was served once more.
entries.literal: When the rites were finished, ritual wine was again placed.

entries.zh: 諸侍坐殿上皆伏抑首，以尊卑次起上壽。
entries.en: All those seated in attendance in the hall bowed low and pressed their heads to the ground, then rose in order of rank to offer toasts of longevity.
entries.literal: All those attending and seated in the hall above prostrated themselves and lowered their heads, rising in order of nobility to offer long life toasts.

entries.zh: 觴九行，謁者言「罷酒」。
entries.en: Nine rounds of cups circulated, and the ye zhe announced, 'Dismiss the wine.'
entries.literal: Cups nine circulated, ye zhe said 'dismiss wine'.

entries.zh: 御史執法舉不如儀者輒引去。
entries.en: The censors enforced the rules and immediately escorted out anyone who failed to observe proper ceremony.
entries.literal: The imperial secretaries enforced the law and immediately led away anyone who did not conform to the ceremony.

entries.zh: 竟朝置酒，無敢讙譁失禮者。
entries.en: Throughout the entire court session and banquet, not a single person dared to cause a disturbance or breach propriety.
entries.literal: Throughout the morning while wine was placed, none dared make a clamor or lose propriety.

entries.zh: 於是高帝曰：「吾乃今日知為皇帝之貴也。」
entries.en: Emperor Gao then said, "Only today do I understand the dignity of being emperor."
entries.literal: Then Emperor Gao said, 'Only today do I understand how noble it is to be emperor.'

entries.zh: 乃拜叔孫通為太常，賜金五百斤。
entries.en: He then appointed Shusun Tong as Grand Master of Ceremonies and bestowed upon him five hundred catties of gold.
entries.literal: Then he appointed Shusun Tong as Grand Master of Ceremonies and granted him five hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 叔孫通因進曰：「諸弟子儒生隨臣久矣，與臣共為儀，願陛下官之。」
entries.en: Shusun Tong then stepped forward and said, 'These disciples and Confucian scholars have followed me for a long time and helped me create the ceremonies. I wish Your Majesty would give them official positions.'
entries.literal: Shusun Tong then advanced said: 'Various disciples Confucian scholars followed minister long already, with minister together made ceremonies, wish Your Majesty official them.'

entries.zh: 高帝悉以為郎。
entries.en: Emperor Gao appointed every one of them as court attendants.
entries.literal: The High Emperor appointed them all as lang (court attendants).

entries.zh: 叔孫通出，皆以五百斤金賜諸生。
entries.en: When Shusun Tong left the court, he distributed all five hundred catties of gold among the scholars.
entries.literal: When Shusun Tong went out, he gave the five hundred jin of gold to the scholars.

entries.zh: 諸生乃皆喜曰：「叔孫生誠聖人也，知當世之要務。」
entries.en: The scholars were all delighted and said, 'Master Shusun is truly a sage—he understands the essential affairs of our time.'
entries.literal: Various scholars then all pleased said: 'Shusun Sheng truly sage person, knows current age's essential affairs.'

entries.zh: 孝惠帝曾春出游離宮，叔孫生曰：「古者有春嘗果，方今櫻桃孰，可獻，願陛下出，因取櫻桃獻宗廟。」
entries.en: Once in spring, Emperor Hui went out to tour a detached palace. Master Shusun said, 'In ancient times there was the spring tasting of fruits. Right now the cherries are ripe and can be offered. I wish Your Majesty would go out and thereby take cherries to offer at the ancestral temple.'
entries.literal: Filial Hui Emperor once spring went out toured detached palace, Shusun Sheng said: 'Ancient ones had spring tasting fruits, right now cherry ripe, can offer, wish Your Majesty go out, thereby take cherry offer ancestral temple.'

entries.zh: 上乃許之。
entries.en: The Emperor then granted permission.
entries.literal: The Emperor then granted permission.

entries.zh: 諸果獻由此興。
entries.en: The practice of offering fruits and produce arose from this.
entries.literal: The offering of various fruits arose from this.

entries.zh: 於是叔孫通使徵魯諸生三十餘人。
entries.en: Shusun Tong then sent for more than thirty Confucian scholars from Lu.
entries.literal: So Shusun Tong sent to summon over thirty Confucian scholars from Lu.

entries.zh: 魯有兩生不肯行，曰：「公所事者且十主，皆面諛以得親貴。
entries.en: Lu had two scholars who were unwilling to go and said, 'You, sir, have served nearly ten rulers, and each time you flattered them to gain closeness and nobility.
entries.literal: Lu had two scholars unwilling go, said: 'You sir served ones nearly ten rulers, all flattered to face to obtain close nobility.

entries.zh: 今天下初定，死者未葬，傷者未起，又欲起禮樂。
entries.en: The empire has only just been settled—the dead are not yet buried, the wounded have not yet risen—and already you wish to institute rites and music.
entries.literal: Now the empire has just been settled, the dead are not yet buried, the wounded have not yet recovered, and yet you wish to establish rites and music.

entries.zh: 禮樂所由起，積德百年而後可興也。
entries.en: Rites and music can only flourish after virtue has been accumulated for a hundred years.
entries.literal: Rites and music arise only after virtue has been accumulated for a hundred years before they can flourish.

entries.zh: 吾不忍為公所為。
entries.en: We cannot bring ourselves to do what you advocate.
entries.literal: We cannot bear to do what you, sir, are doing.

entries.zh: 公所為不合古，吾不行。
entries.en: What you propose does not accord with antiquity—we will not participate.
entries.literal: What you, sir, are doing does not accord with antiquity—we will not go.

entries.zh: 公往矣，無汙我！」
entries.en: You, sir, may go—do not defile us!'
entries.literal: You sir go, do not defile us!'

entries.zh: 叔孫通笑曰：「若真鄙儒也，不知時變。」
entries.en: Shusun Tong laughed and said, 'You are truly narrow-minded Confucian scholars who do not understand how times change.'
entries.literal: Shusun Tong laughed said: 'You are truly narrow Confucian scholars, do not know times change.'

entries.zh: 季布者，楚人也。
entries.en: Ji Bu was a native of Chu.
entries.literal: Ji Bu was a man of Chu.

entries.zh: 為氣任俠，有名於楚。
entries.en: A man of fierce spirit who lived as a knight-errant, he was famed throughout Chu.
entries.literal: He was spirited and acted as a knight-errant, gaining great renown in Chu.

entries.zh: 項籍使將兵，數窘漢王。
entries.en: Xiang Ji appointed him to command troops, and on multiple occasions he drove the King of Han into desperate straits.
entries.literal: Xiang Ji sent him to command troops, and he repeatedly put the Han King in dire straits.

entries.zh: 及項羽滅，高祖購求布千金，敢有舍匿，罪及三族。
entries.en: After the fall of Xiang Yu, Emperor Gaozu posted a bounty of a thousand gold pieces for Ji Bu's capture, decreeing that anyone who dared shelter or conceal him would have the punishment extended to three generations of their clan.
entries.literal: When Xiang Yu was destroyed, Gaozu offered a thousand pieces of gold for Ji Bu's capture; anyone who dared harbor or conceal him would have the crime extend to three generations of his clan.

entries.zh: 季布匿濮陽周氏。
entries.en: Ji Bu went into hiding with the Zhou family in Puyang.
entries.literal: Ji Bu hid with the Zhou family in Puyang.

entries.zh: 周氏曰：「漢購將軍急，跡且至臣家，將軍能聽臣，臣敢獻計；
entries.en: The Zhou family said, "The Han search for you, General, is urgent, and your trail will soon reach my house. If you, General, will heed me, I dare offer a plan;
entries.literal: The Zhou family said, "The Han search for the general is urgent, and traces will soon reach my household. If the general can heed me, I dare offer a plan;

entries.zh: 即不能，願先自剄。」
entries.en: if not, I will slit my own throat first."
entries.literal: if you cannot, I wish first to slit my own throat."

entries.zh: 季布許之。
entries.en: Ji Bu consented.
entries.literal: Ji Bu agreed to this.

entries.zh: 乃髡鉗季布，衣褐衣，置廣柳車中，并與其家僮數十人，之魯朱家所賣之。
entries.en: They shaved Ji Bu's head, clamped an iron collar around his neck, dressed him in coarse cloth, and placed him in a broad-sided cart. Together with dozens of household slaves, they transported him to the estate of Zhu Jia in Lu and sold him there.
entries.literal: They shaved Ji Bu's head, fitted him with an iron collar, dressed him in coarse hemp clothing, placed him in a wide willow cart, and along with several dozen of his household slaves, took him to be sold to Zhu Jia of Lu.

entries.zh: 朱家心知是季布，乃買而置之田。
entries.en: Zhu Jia secretly recognized that this was Ji Bu. He purchased him and set him to work in the fields.
entries.literal: Zhu Jia recognized in his heart that this was Ji Bu, so he bought him and put him to work in the fields.

entries.zh: 誡其子曰：「田事聽此奴，必與同食。」
entries.en: He admonished his son, saying, "In the fields, take orders from this slave; you must eat at the same table with him."
entries.literal: He admonished his son, saying, "In field affairs obey this slave; you must eat with him."

entries.zh: 朱家乃乘軺車之洛陽，見汝陰侯滕公。
entries.en: Zhu Jia then rode a light carriage to Luoyang, where he called upon Xiahou Ying, the Marquis of Ruyin.
entries.literal: Zhu Jia then rode in a light carriage to Luoyang and saw the Marquis of Ruyin, Teng Gong.

entries.zh: 滕公留朱家飲數日。
entries.en: The Marquis kept Zhu Jia as his guest and drank with him for several days.
entries.literal: Teng Gong detained Zhu Jia and feasted him for several days.

entries.zh: 因謂滕公曰：「季布何大罪，而上求之急也？」
entries.en: He then asked Teng Gong, "What grave offense has Ji Bu committed, for the Sovereign to pursue him with such urgency?"
entries.literal: Then he said to Teng Gong, "What great crime has Ji Bu committed, that the Sovereign seeks him so urgently?"

entries.zh: 滕公曰：「布數為項羽窘上，上怨之，故必欲得之。」
entries.en: Teng Gong said, "Ji Bu repeatedly put the Sovereign in dire straits while serving Xiang Yu; the Sovereign resents him, and therefore is determined to capture him."
entries.literal: Teng Gong said, "Ji Bu repeatedly put the Sovereign in dire straits while serving Xiang Yu; the Sovereign resents him, and therefore is determined to have him."

entries.zh: 朱家曰：「君視季布何如人也？」
entries.en: Zhu Jia said, 'What kind of man do you consider Ji Bu to be?'
entries.literal: Zhu Jia said, 'What kind of man do you consider Ji Bu to be?'

entries.zh: 曰：「賢者也。」
entries.en: Teng Gong said, "A worthy man."
entries.literal: He said, "A worthy man."

entries.zh: 朱家曰：「臣各為其主用，季布為項籍用，職耳。
entries.en: Zhu Jia said, 'Each minister serves his own lord. Ji Bu served Xiang Ji—that was merely his duty.
entries.literal: Zhu Jia said, 'Each minister serves his own lord. Ji Bu served Xiang Ji—that was merely his duty.

entries.zh: 項氏臣可盡誅邪？
entries.en: Should all Xiang Yu's ministers be executed?
entries.literal: Xiang clan ministers can all execute?

entries.zh: 今上始得天下，獨以己之私怨求一人，何示天下之不廣也！
entries.en: Now that the Sovereign has just won the empire, to hunt one man solely out of private resentment—what a display of narrow-mindedness to all under heaven!
entries.literal: Now that the Sovereign has just obtained the empire, to seek one man solely out of private resentment—what a display of lack of magnanimity to all under heaven!

entries.zh: 且以季布之賢而漢求之急如此，此不北走胡即南走越耳。
entries.en: Moreover, with a man as worthy as Ji Bu sought by Han with such urgency, he will either flee north to the Xiongnu or south to the Yue.
entries.literal: Moreover, with Ji Bu's worthiness and Han seek him urgent like this, this not north flee Hu then south flee Yue only.

entries.zh: 夫忌壯士以資敵國，此伍子胥所以鞭荊平王之墓也。
entries.en: To drive away stalwart warriors and thereby strengthen enemy states—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.
entries.literal: To drive away stalwart warriors and thereby aid enemy states—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.

entries.zh: 君何不從容為上言邪？」
entries.en: Why not find a calm moment to speak to the Sovereign about this?"
entries.literal: Why do you not speak to the Sovereign about this at your leisure?"

entries.zh: 汝陰侯滕公心知朱家大俠，意季布匿其所，乃許曰：「諾。」
entries.en: The Marquis of Ruyin, Teng Gong, knew in his heart that Zhu Jia was a great knight-errant, and suspected that Ji Bu was hiding in his home. He then agreed, saying, 'Very well.'
entries.literal: Ruyin Hou Teng Gong heart knew Zhu Jia great knight-errant, suspected Ji Bu concealed his place, then promised said: 'Yes.'

entries.zh: 待閒，果言如朱家指。
entries.en: When he had a suitable moment, he spoke to the Emperor exactly as Zhu Jia had urged.
entries.literal: He waited for a leisurely moment, and indeed spoke as Zhu Jia had directed.

entries.zh: 上乃赦季布。
entries.en: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Ji Bu.
entries.literal: The Sovereign then pardoned Ji Bu.

entries.zh: 當是時，諸公皆多季布能摧剛為柔，朱家亦以此名聞當世。
entries.en: At that time, everyone praised Ji Bu for his ability to bend the unyielding and make it yielding, and Zhu Jia likewise won renown throughout the age for this.
entries.literal: At this time, all the nobles praised Ji Bu for his ability to bend the unyielding and make it yielding, and Zhu Jia also gained fame in the present age through this.

entries.zh: 季布召見，謝，上拜為郎中。
entries.en: Ji Bu was summoned for an audience and expressed his gratitude. The Emperor appointed him as a Gentleman of the Palace.
entries.literal: Ji Bu was summoned for an audience and expressed thanks. The Sovereign appointed him as a lang zhong (court attendant).

entries.zh: 孝惠時，為中郎將。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Hui, he served as Commander of the Palace Guard.
entries.literal: During Emperor Hui's reign, he served as zhong lang jiang (lieutenant general).

entries.zh: 單于嘗為書嫚呂后，不遜，呂后大怒，召諸將議之。
entries.en: The Chanyu once wrote a letter insulting Empress Lü in disrespectful terms. Empress Lü was greatly angered and summoned all the generals to discuss it.
entries.literal: The Chanyu once wrote a letter insulting Empress Lü in disrespectful terms; Empress Lü was greatly angered and summoned the generals to discuss it.

entries.zh: 上將軍樊噲曰：「臣願得十萬眾，橫行匈奴中。」
entries.en: The Supreme General, Fan Kuai, said, 'I wish to obtain a force of 100,000 men and march unchecked through the Xiongnu lands.'
entries.literal: Supreme General Fan Kuai said, "Your servant wishes to have a force of one hundred thousand and rampage through the Xiongnu lands."

entries.zh: 諸將皆阿呂后意，曰「然」。
entries.en: All the generals flattered Empress Lü's wishes and said, 'Yes.'
entries.literal: Various generals all flattered Empress Lü's intention, said 'Yes'.

entries.zh: 季布曰：「樊噲可斬也！
entries.en: Ji Bu said, 'Fan Kuai should be executed!
entries.literal: Ji Bu said: 'Fan Kuai can behead!

entries.zh: 夫高帝將兵四十餘萬眾，困於平城，今噲柰何以十萬眾橫行匈奴中，面欺！
entries.en: Indeed, when the Gao Emperor led over 400,000 troops, he was trapped at Pingcheng. Now how can Kuai march unchecked through the Xiongnu lands with 100,000 men? This is barefaced deception!
entries.literal: Indeed Gao Emperor led troops forty more myriad multitude, trapped at Pingcheng, now Kuai how with ten myriad multitude rampage Xiongnu midst, face deceive!

entries.zh: 且秦以事於胡，陳勝等起。
entries.en: Moreover, when Qin was occupied with campaigns against the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose in revolt.
entries.literal: Moreover, when Qin was occupied with campaigns against the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose up.

entries.zh: 于今創痍未瘳，噲又面諛，欲搖動天下。」
entries.en: Even now our wounds are not yet healed, yet Fan Kuai again flatters you to your face, wishing to shake the empire.'
entries.literal: Even now our wounds are not yet healed, yet Kuai again flatters to your face, wishing to shake the empire.'

entries.zh: 是時殿上皆恐，太后罷朝，遂不復議擊匈奴事。
entries.en: At this, everyone in the hall fell silent with fear. The Empress Dowager dismissed the court, and the matter of attacking the Xiongnu was never raised again.
entries.literal: At this time, all in the hall were terrified. The Empress Dowager dismissed the court, and they never again discussed attacking the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 季布母弟丁公，為楚將。
entries.en: Ji Bu's mother's younger brother Ding Gong served as a Chu general.
entries.literal: Ji Bu mother's younger brother Ding Gong, served as Chu general.

entries.zh: 丁公為項羽逐窘高祖彭城西，短兵接，高祖急，顧丁公曰：「兩賢豈相戹哉！」
entries.en: Ding Gong, serving Xiang Yu, pursued and cornered Emperor Gaozu west of Pengcheng. They met in close combat; the Emperor was in peril and looked back at Ding Gong, saying, "How can two worthy men afflict each other!"
entries.literal: Ding Gong, serving Xiang Yu, pursued and cornered Gaozu west of Pengcheng. They met in close combat; Gaozu was in peril and looked back at Ding Gong, saying, "How can two worthy men afflict each other!"

entries.zh: 於是丁公引兵而還，漢王遂解去。
entries.en: At this, Ding Gong withdrew his troops, and the King of Han was able to escape.
entries.literal: So Ding Gong led his troops back, and the Han King thus escaped.

entries.zh: 及項王滅，丁公謁見高祖。
entries.en: After the fall of Xiang Yu, Ding Gong sought an audience with Emperor Gaozu.
entries.literal: When Xiang Yu was destroyed, Ding Gong went for an audience with Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖以丁公徇軍中，曰：「丁公為項王臣不忠，使項王失天下者，乃丁公也。」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded through the army and said, "Ding Gong served King Xiang as a minister without loyalty; the one who caused King Xiang to lose the empire is Ding Gong."
entries.literal: Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded through the army and said, "Ding Gong served as King Xiang's minister without loyalty; the one who caused King Xiang to lose the empire is Ding Gong."

entries.zh: 遂斬丁公，曰：「使後世為人臣者無效丁公！」
entries.en: Gaozu then had Ding Gong beheaded, saying, "Let no minister in later generations follow Ding Gong's example!"
entries.literal: He then beheaded Ding Gong, saying, "Let no minister in future generations imitate Ding Gong!"

entries.zh: 使於齊，未還，漢召彭越，責以謀反，夷三族。
entries.en: Luan Bu was sent on a diplomatic mission to Qi and had not yet returned when the Han court summoned Peng Yue, charged him with plotting rebellion, and exterminated his three clans.
entries.literal: He was sent on a mission to Qi and had not yet returned when Han summoned Peng Yue, blamed him for plotting rebellion, and exterminated his three clans.

entries.zh: 已而梟彭越頭於雒陽下，詔曰：「有敢收視者，輒捕之。」
entries.en: Soon after, Peng Yue's head was displayed below Luoyang, and an edict said, "Anyone who dares to gather or look upon it will be arrested at once."
entries.literal: Soon Peng Yue's head was displayed below Luoyang, and an edict said, "Anyone who dares to gather or look upon it will be arrested at once."

entries.zh: 布從齊還，奏事彭越頭下，祠而哭之。
entries.en: When Luan Bu returned from Qi, he reported on his mission beneath Peng Yue's severed head, made offerings, and wept for him.
entries.literal: When Bu returned from Qi, he reported on his mission beneath Peng Yue's head, made offerings, and wept for him.

entries.zh: 吏捕布以聞。
entries.en: The officials arrested Luan Bu and reported the matter to the throne.
entries.literal: The officials captured Bu and reported it.

entries.zh: 上召布，罵曰：「若與彭越反邪？
entries.en: The Emperor summoned Luan Bu and cursed him, saying, "Did you rebel with Peng Yue?
entries.literal: The Sovereign summoned Bu and cursed him, saying, "Did you rebel with Peng Yue?

entries.zh: 吾禁人勿收，若獨祠而哭之，與越反明矣。
entries.en: I forbade anyone to attend to his remains, yet you alone made offerings and wept for him—it is clear you were part of Yue's rebellion.
entries.literal: I prohibited people from collecting it, but you alone sacrificed and wept for him—it's clear you rebelled with Yue.

entries.zh: 趣亨之。」
entries.en: Hurry and execute him.'
entries.literal: Hurry execute him.'

entries.zh: 方提趣湯，布顧曰：「願一言而死。」
entries.en: Just as they were leading him to hurry to the cauldron, Bu looked back and said, 'I wish to speak one word before I die.'
entries.literal: Just as they were leading him in haste to the cauldron, Bu looked back and said, "I wish to speak one word before I die."

entries.zh: 上曰：「何言？」
entries.en: The Sovereign said, 'What words?'
entries.literal: Sovereign said: 'What words?'

entries.zh: 布曰：「方上之困於彭城，敗滎陽、成皋閒，項王所以（遂）不能［遂］西，徒以彭王居梁地，與漢合從苦楚也。
entries.en: Bu said, 'When the Sovereign was distressed at Pengcheng and defeated between Xingyang and Chenggao, the reason Xiang Yu could not advance west was only because the Peng King dwelt in Liang lands and allied with Han to afflict Chu.
entries.literal: Bu said: 'Just Sovereign's distress at Pengcheng, defeated between Xingyang, Chenggao, Xiang Wang reason not able west, only because Peng King dwelt Liang lands, with Han allied together afflicted Chu.

entries.zh: 當是之時，彭王一顧，與楚則漢破，與漢而楚破。
entries.en: At that moment, the fate of the empire hung on a single decision by the King of Peng: had he sided with Chu, Han would have been destroyed; because he sided with Han, Chu was destroyed.
entries.literal: At this time, with just one glance from the Peng King, if he allied with Chu then Han would be broken, if he allied with Han then Chu would be broken.

entries.zh: 且垓下之會，微彭王，項氏不亡。
entries.en: Moreover, at the battle of Gaixia, without the King of Peng, the house of Xiang would never have fallen.
entries.literal: Moreover, at the Gaixia meeting, without the Peng King, the Xiang clan would not have perished.

entries.zh: 天下已定，彭王剖符受封，亦欲傳之萬世。
entries.en: After the empire was settled, the King of Peng received his tally and his fief, and naturally wished to pass them down for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: The empire was already settled, the Peng King had his tally divided and received his fief, and he also wished to transmit it to ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 今陛下一徵兵於梁，彭王病不行，而陛下疑以為反，反形未見，以苛小案誅滅之，臣恐功臣人人自危也。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty levied troops from Liang just once, and when the King of Peng was too ill to comply, Your Majesty suspected him of rebellion. No evidence of rebellion was ever found, yet he was destroyed on a trivial pretext. I fear that every minister who has rendered meritorious service now feels his own life is in danger.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty summoned troops just once from Liang, the Peng King was ill and did not go, yet Your Majesty suspected him of rebellion. The shape of rebellion was not seen, but you exterminated him with a harsh and petty case. I fear all the merit ministers will each feel endangered.

entries.zh: 今彭王已死，臣生不如死，請就亨。」
entries.en: Now that the Peng King is already dead, living is not as good as dying for me. Please proceed with the boiling.'
entries.literal: Now Peng King already dead, minister living not as dying, please proceed boil.'

entries.zh: 於是上乃釋布罪，拜為都尉。
entries.en: Thereupon the Emperor released Luan Bu from guilt and appointed him District Commandant.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Sovereign released Bu from guilt and appointed him District Commandant.

entries.zh: 欒布者，梁人也。
entries.en: Luan Bu was a native of Liang.
entries.literal: Luan Bu was a man of Liang.

entries.zh: 始梁王彭越為家人時，嘗與布游。
entries.en: In the early days, when Peng Yue—who would later become King of Liang—was still a commoner, he and Luan Bu had been companions.
entries.literal: When the Liang King Peng Yue was still a commoner, he once roamed with Bu.

entries.zh: 窮困，賃傭於齊，為酒人保。
entries.en: Destitute, Luan Bu hired himself out as a laborer in Qi and worked as a guard at a tavern.
entries.literal: He was impoverished and distressed, hired himself out as labor in Qi, and served as security at a tavern.

entries.zh: 數歲，彭越去之巨野中為盜，而布為人所略賣，為奴於燕。
entries.en: After several years, Peng Yue departed for the Juye marshes to become a bandit, while Luan Bu was kidnapped and sold into slavery in Yan.
entries.literal: After several years, Peng Yue went into the Juye marshes to become a bandit, while Bu was abducted and sold by people, becoming a slave in Yan.

entries.zh: 為其家主報仇，燕將臧荼舉以為都尉。
entries.en: He avenged his master's death, and the Yan general Zang Tu, impressed, recommended him to the rank of District Commandant.
entries.literal: He avenged his household master, and the Yan general Zang Tu recommended him to serve as du wei.

entries.zh: 臧荼後為燕王，以布為將。
entries.en: When Zang Tu later became King of Yan, he appointed Luan Bu as one of his generals.
entries.literal: Zang Tu later became King of Yan and appointed Bu as his general.

entries.zh: 及臧荼反，漢擊燕，虜布。
entries.en: When Zang Tu rebelled, the Han forces attacked Yan and took Luan Bu prisoner.
entries.literal: When Zang Tu rebelled, Han attacked Yan and captured Bu.

entries.zh: 梁王彭越聞之，乃言上，請贖布以為梁大夫。
entries.en: When the King of Liang, Peng Yue, heard of this, he petitioned the Emperor to ransom Luan Bu and appoint him as a Minister of Liang.
entries.literal: The Liang King Peng Yue heard this and then spoke to the Sovereign, requesting to redeem Bu to serve as a Liang daifu (minister).

entries.zh: 太史公曰：以項羽之氣，而季布以勇顯於楚，身屨（典）軍搴旗者數矣，可謂壯士。
entries.en: The Grand Historian said: In the age of Xiang Yu's fierce power, Ji Bu became renowned in Chu for his bravery; he personally commanded troops and seized enemy banners several times. He can indeed be called a stalwart warrior.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian said: Under Xiang Yu's authority, Ji Bu nonetheless became famed in Chu for bravery; he personally led troops and seized enemy banners on several occasions—he may be called a stalwart warrior.

entries.zh: 然至被刑戮，為人奴而不死，何其下也！
entries.en: Yet when he reached the point of punishment and branding, became another man's slave, and still did not die, how low he sank!
entries.literal: Yet when it came to suffering punishment and branding, becoming another man's slave and not dying—how base!

entries.zh: 彼必自負其材，故受辱而不羞，欲有所用其未足也，故終為漢名將。
entries.en: He must have been confident in his own abilities, and therefore accepted humiliation without shame, knowing that his talents had not yet been fully employed. In the end, he became one of the celebrated generals of Han.
entries.literal: He certainly relied upon his own talents, therefore accepted humiliation without feeling shame, wishing to have some use for what was still insufficient, and therefore finally became a famous general of Han.

entries.zh: 賢者誠重其死。
entries.en: A truly worthy man weighs his death carefully.
entries.literal: Truly, the worthy value their death.

entries.zh: 夫婢妾賤人感慨而自殺者，非能勇也，其計畫無復之耳。
entries.en: When slave girls, concubines, and people of low station kill themselves in a moment of passion, it is not because they are brave—it is because they see no way forward.
entries.literal: Indeed, when concubines and base people are emotionally moved and commit suicide, it is not that they are able to be brave—their plans simply have no recovery.

entries.zh: 欒布哭彭越，趣湯如歸者，彼誠知所處，不自重其死。
entries.en: When Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue and walked toward the boiling cauldron as calmly as if he were going home, it was because he truly understood his situation and did not cling to his own life.
entries.literal: Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue and hurried to the cauldron as if returning home—he truly knew his situation and did not value his own death.

entries.zh: 雖往古烈士，何以加哉！
entries.en: Even among the fierce warriors of antiquity, who could surpass this?
entries.literal: Even the martyred warriors of old—how could one surpass this!

entries.zh: 景帝中五年薨。
entries.en: He died in the fifth year of the Zhongyuan reign of Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Zhongyuan reign of Emperor Jing, he died.

entries.zh: 子賁嗣，為太常，犧牲不如令，國除。
entries.en: His son Ben inherited the title and served as the Grand Master of Ceremonies, but because the sacrificial animals he provided did not meet the prescribed standards, his fief was abolished.
entries.literal: His son Ben succeeded him and served as Grand Master of Ceremonies, but his sacrifices did not conform to regulations, so his fief was eliminated.

entries.zh: 袁盎常引大體慨。
entries.en: Yuan Ang always spoke of matters of great principle with impassioned conviction.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang always drew upon matters of great principle and spoke with impassioned concern.

entries.zh: 宦者趙同以數幸，常害袁盎，袁盎患之。
entries.en: The eunuch Zhao Tong, who had long enjoyed the Emperor's favor, constantly sought to undermine Yuan Ang, and Ang was troubled by this.
entries.literal: The eunuch Zhao Tong, who enjoyed frequent imperial favor, constantly sought to harm Yuan Ang, and Yuan Ang was troubled by this.

entries.zh: 盎兄子種為常侍騎，持節夾乘，說盎曰：「君與鬬，廷辱之，使其毀不用。」
entries.en: Ang's nephew Zhong served as an Attendant Cavalry officer who rode beside the imperial carriage bearing a tally. He advised Ang, 'Pick a fight with him and humiliate him at court, so that his slanders lose their sting.'
entries.literal: Ang's nephew Zhong served as an Attendant Cavalry officer and rode alongside the imperial carriage bearing a tally. He advised Ang: 'You should clash with him and humiliate him at court, so that his slanders lose their effect.'

entries.zh: 孝文帝出，趙同參乘，袁盎伏車前曰：「臣聞天子所與共六尺輿者，皆天下豪英。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen went out, Zhao Tong rode as a companion in the imperial carriage. Yuan Ang threw himself before the carriage and said, 'I have heard that those who share the Son of Heaven's carriage should be the finest heroes of the realm.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen went out, Zhao Tong rode as a companion in the imperial carriage. Yuan Ang prostrated himself before the carriage and said: 'I have heard that those who share the six-foot carriage with the Son of Heaven should all be the outstanding heroes of the realm.

entries.zh: 今漢雖乏人，陛下獨奈何與刀鋸餘人載！」
entries.en: Though the Han may be short of men, how can Your Majesty ride with the leavings of the knife and saw!'
entries.literal: Although the Han dynasty may lack men, how can Your Majesty alone ride with a remnant of the knife and saw!'

entries.zh: 於是上笑，下趙同。
entries.en: The Emperor laughed and ordered Zhao Tong to get off.
entries.literal: At this the Emperor laughed and ordered Zhao Tong to step down.

entries.zh: 趙同泣下車。
entries.en: Zhao Tong climbed down from the carriage in tears.
entries.literal: Zhao Tong wept as he descended from the carriage.

entries.zh: 然袁盎亦以數直諫，不得久居中，調為隴西都尉。
entries.en: Yet because Yuan Ang had so often spoken bluntly in remonstrance, he could not remain long at court and was transferred to serve as Commandant of Longxi.
entries.literal: However, because Yuan Ang had so often spoken bluntly in remonstrance, he could not remain long at the capital and was transferred to serve as Commandant of Longxi.

entries.zh: 仁愛士卒，士卒皆爭為死。
entries.en: He treated his soldiers with kindness and generosity, and they all competed for the chance to die for him.
entries.literal: He treated the soldiers with benevolence and love, and the soldiers all vied to die for him.

entries.zh: 遷為齊相。
entries.en: He was then promoted to Chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of Qi.

entries.zh: 徙為吳相，辭行，種謂盎曰：「吳王驕日久，國多姦。
entries.en: He was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Wu. When he took his leave to depart, Zhong said to Ang, 'The King of Wu has been arrogant for years, and his kingdom is rife with sedition.
entries.literal: He was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Wu. When he took his leave, Zhong said to Ang: 'The King of Wu has been arrogant for a long time, and his kingdom harbors many treacherous elements.

entries.zh: 今茍欲劾治，彼不上書告君，即利劍刺君矣。
entries.en: If you try to investigate and prosecute him, he will either submit a memorial denouncing you, or run you through with a sword.
entries.literal: If you now try to impeach and bring order, he will either submit a memorial accusing you, or stab you with a sharp sword.

entries.zh: 南方卑溼，君能日飲，毋何，時說王曰毋反而已。
entries.en: The south is low and damp. Just drink every day, do nothing of consequence, and from time to time urge the king not to rebel. That is all you need to do.
entries.literal: The south is low-lying and damp. You should just drink every day, do nothing, and from time to time persuade the king not to rebel—that is all.

entries.zh: 如此幸得脫。」
entries.en: If you do this, you may be lucky enough to escape with your life.'
entries.literal: In this way you may be fortunate enough to escape with your life.'

entries.zh: 盎用種之計，吳王厚遇盎。
entries.en: Ang followed Zhong's advice, and the King of Wu treated him well.
entries.literal: Ang followed Zhong's plan, and the King of Wu treated Ang generously.

entries.zh: 盎素不好鼂錯，鼂錯所居坐，盎去；
entries.en: Ang had always disliked Chao Cuo. Whenever Chao Cuo was present, Ang would leave.
entries.literal: Ang had always disliked Chao Cuo. Whenever Chao Cuo was present and seated, Ang would leave.

entries.zh: 盎坐，錯亦去：兩人未嘗同堂語。
entries.en: When Ang was present, Cuo would likewise depart. The two never spoke in the same room.
entries.literal: When Ang was seated, Cuo would likewise leave. The two never exchanged a word in the same hall.

entries.zh: 及孝文帝崩，孝景帝即位，鼂錯為御史大夫，使吏案袁盎受吳王財物，抵罪，詔赦以為庶人。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo was appointed Imperial Secretary. He sent officials to investigate Yuan Ang for accepting gifts from the King of Wu, and Ang was convicted. By imperial edict he was pardoned but reduced to a commoner.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died and Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne, Chao Cuo became the Imperial Secretary. He dispatched officials to investigate Yuan Ang for accepting gifts from the King of Wu, and Ang was convicted. By imperial edict he was pardoned but reduced to the status of a commoner.

entries.zh: 錯為人陗直刻深。
entries.en: Cuo was by nature severe, blunt, and unsparing.
entries.literal: Cuo was by nature harsh, blunt, exacting, and unforgiving.

entries.zh: 孝文帝時，天下無治尚書者，獨聞濟南伏生故秦博士，治尚書，年九十餘，老不可徵，乃詔太常使人往受之。
entries.en: In the time of Emperor Wen, no one in the realm still studied the Book of Documents. The only master known to survive was Fu Sheng of Jinan, a former Erudite of the Qin, who was over ninety and too old to be summoned to court. An edict was issued ordering the Grand Master of Ceremonies to send someone to study under him.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowen, there was no one in the realm who studied the Book of Documents. It was heard only that Fu Sheng of Jinan, a former Erudite of the Qin, had mastered it. He was over ninety years old and too aged to be summoned to court, so an edict was issued ordering the Grand Master of Ceremonies to send someone to receive his teachings.

entries.zh: 太常遣錯受尚書伏生所。
entries.en: The Grand Master of Ceremonies dispatched Cuo to study the Book of Documents under Fu Sheng.
entries.literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies sent Cuo to study the Book of Documents under Fu Sheng.

entries.zh: 還，因上便宜事，以書稱說。
entries.en: Upon his return, he submitted proposals on matters of governance, citing the Book of Documents to support his arguments.
entries.literal: Upon his return, he submitted proposals on expedient measures, citing the Book of Documents to support his arguments.

entries.zh: 詔以為太子舍人、門大夫、家令。
entries.en: By imperial edict, he was successively appointed Retainer of the Heir Apparent, Gentleman of the Gate, and Steward of the Household.
entries.literal: By imperial edict, he was appointed successively as Retainer of the Heir Apparent, Gentleman of the Gate, and Steward of the Household.

entries.zh: 以其辯得幸太子，太子家號曰「智囊」。
entries.en: Through his eloquence he won the favor of the Heir Apparent, and the household dubbed him the 'Bag of Wisdom.'
entries.literal: Through his eloquence he won the favor of the Heir Apparent, and in the Heir Apparent's household he was called the 'Bag of Wisdom.'

entries.zh: 數上書孝文時，言削諸侯事，及法令可更定者。
entries.en: He submitted numerous memorials during Emperor Wen's reign, arguing for the reduction of the feudal lords' territories and proposing revisions to the laws.
entries.literal: He submitted numerous memorials during Emperor Xiaowen's reign, arguing for the reduction of the feudal lords' territories and proposing revisions to the laws and regulations.

entries.zh: 書數十上，孝文不聽，然奇其材，遷為中大夫。
entries.en: He submitted dozens of memorials, but Emperor Wen did not adopt his proposals. The Emperor admired his talent, however, and promoted him to Palace Grandee.
entries.literal: He submitted dozens of memorials, but Emperor Xiaowen did not adopt his proposals. Nevertheless, the Emperor admired his talents and promoted him to the rank of Palace Grandee.

entries.zh: 當是時，太子善錯計策，袁盎諸大功臣多不好錯。
entries.en: At that time, the Heir Apparent approved of Cuo's plans and strategies, but Yuan Ang and many of the senior meritorious ministers disliked him.
entries.literal: At that time, the Heir Apparent approved of Cuo's plans and strategies, but Yuan Ang and many of the great meritorious ministers disliked Cuo.

entries.zh: 遷為御史大夫，請諸侯之罪過，削其地，收其枝郡。
entries.en: He was promoted to Imperial Secretary. He proposed charging the feudal lords with their offenses, reducing their territories, and confiscating their outlying commanderies.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Imperial Secretary. He requested that the feudal lords be charged with their offenses, their territories reduced, and their outlying commanderies confiscated.

entries.zh: 奏上，上令公卿列侯宗室集議，莫敢難，獨竇嬰爭之，由此與錯有卻。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor ordered the senior officials, marquises, and members of the imperial clan to deliberate. None dared object, except Dou Ying, who contested it. From this a rift grew between him and Cuo.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor ordered the senior officials, marquises, and members of the imperial clan to deliberate on it. None dared to object, except Dou Ying, who contested it. From this a rift developed between Dou Ying and Cuo.

entries.zh: 錯所更令三十章，諸侯皆諠譁疾鼂錯。
entries.en: Cuo revised thirty articles of law. The feudal lords all raised an outcry and despised Chao Cuo.
entries.literal: Cuo's revised laws amounted to thirty articles. The feudal lords all protested loudly and despised Chao Cuo.

entries.zh: 錯父聞之，從潁川來，謂錯曰：「上初即位，公為政用事，侵削諸侯，別疏人骨肉，人口議多怨公者，何也？」
entries.en: When Cuo's father heard of this, he came from Yingchuan and said to Cuo, 'The Emperor has only just come to the throne, and you are the one directing affairs of state. You encroach upon the feudal lords, reduce their lands, and drive a wedge between the Emperor's own kin. People everywhere are speaking against you with resentment. Why?'
entries.literal: When Cuo's father heard of this, he came from Yingchuan and said to Cuo: 'The Emperor has only just come to the throne, and you are the one directing affairs of state. You encroach upon and reduce the feudal lords, separating and estranging the Emperor's own flesh and blood. People's talk is full of resentment toward you. Why is this?'

entries.zh: 鼂錯曰：「固也。
entries.en: Chao Cuo replied, 'That is to be expected.
entries.literal: Chao Cuo said: 'That is to be expected.

entries.zh: 不如此，天子不尊，宗廟不安。」
entries.en: Without this, the Son of Heaven cannot be honored, and the ancestral temples will never be secure.'
entries.literal: Without this, the Son of Heaven cannot be honored, and the ancestral temples cannot be secure.'

entries.zh: 錯父曰：「劉氏安矣，而鼂氏危矣，吾去公歸矣！」
entries.en: Cuo's father said, 'The House of Liu may be secure, but the House of Chao is in peril. I will leave you and go home!'
entries.literal: Cuo's father said: 'The House of Liu is secure, but the House of Chao is in peril. I shall leave you and go home!'

entries.zh: 遂飲藥死，曰：「吾不忍見禍及吾身。」
entries.en: He then drank poison and died, saying, 'I cannot bear to live to see disaster fall upon me.'
entries.literal: He then drank poison and died, saying: 'I cannot bear to see disaster reach my own person.'

entries.zh: 死十餘日，吳楚七國果反，以誅錯為名。
entries.en: A little over ten days after his death, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in rebellion, using the demand to execute Cuo as their pretext.
entries.literal: More than ten days after his death, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu did indeed rebel, using the demand to execute Cuo as their pretext.

entries.zh: 及竇嬰、袁盎進說，上令鼂錯衣朝衣斬東市。
entries.en: When Dou Ying and Yuan Ang pressed their case, the Emperor ordered Chao Cuo beheaded in his court robes at the Eastern Market.
entries.literal: When Dou Ying and Yuan Ang came forward with their arguments, the Emperor ordered Chao Cuo to be beheaded in his court robes at the Eastern Market.

entries.zh: 吳楚反，聞，鼂錯謂丞史曰：「夫袁盎多受吳王金錢，專為蔽匿，言不反。
entries.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, upon hearing the news, Chao Cuo said to the Chancellor's Clerk, 'Yuan Ang accepted large sums from the King of Wu and deliberately covered for him, insisting he would not rebel.
entries.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, upon hearing the news, Chao Cuo said to the Chancellor's Clerk: 'Yuan Ang accepted large sums of gold and money from the King of Wu and deliberately concealed and covered for him, claiming he would not rebel.

entries.zh: 今果反，欲請治盎宜知計謀。」
entries.en: Now that the rebellion has come, I intend to request an investigation of Ang, who surely knew of the plot.'
entries.literal: Now he has indeed rebelled. I wish to request an investigation of Ang, who must have known of the plot.'

entries.zh: 丞史曰：「事未發，治之有絕。
entries.en: The Chancellor's Clerk replied, 'Before the rebellion broke out, an investigation might have nipped it in the bud.
entries.literal: The Chancellor's Clerk said: 'Before the affair broke out, pursuing it might have put an end to it.

entries.zh: 今兵西鄉，治之何益！
entries.en: Now that their armies are marching west, what good would an investigation do!
entries.literal: Now that the armies are marching westward, what good would an investigation do!

entries.zh: 且袁盎不宜有謀。」
entries.en: Besides, it is unlikely that Yuan Ang was party to the conspiracy.'
entries.literal: Moreover, Yuan Ang is unlikely to have been party to the plot.'

entries.zh: 鼂錯猶與未決。
entries.en: Chao Cuo hesitated and could not make up his mind.
entries.literal: Chao Cuo still hesitated and had not yet decided.

entries.zh: 人有告袁盎者，袁盎恐，夜見竇嬰，為言吳所以反者，願至上前口對狀。
entries.en: Someone warned Yuan Ang. Alarmed, Ang went to see Dou Ying that night. He explained the reasons for Wu's rebellion and expressed his wish to present his case in person before the Emperor.
entries.literal: Someone informed Yuan Ang of this. Ang was alarmed and went to see Dou Ying by night. He explained the reasons for Wu's rebellion and expressed his wish to present an oral defense before the Emperor.

entries.zh: 竇嬰入言上，上乃召袁盎入見。
entries.en: Dou Ying went in and spoke to the Emperor, who summoned Yuan Ang for an audience.
entries.literal: Dou Ying went in and spoke to the Emperor, and the Emperor thereupon summoned Yuan Ang for an audience.

entries.zh: 鼂錯在前，及盎請辟人賜閒，錯去，固恨甚。
entries.en: Chao Cuo was present at the audience. When Ang asked that others be dismissed for a private word, Cuo had to leave, and his resentment deepened.
entries.literal: Chao Cuo was present at the time. When Ang requested that others be dismissed for a private audience, Cuo was forced to withdraw, and his resentment deepened greatly.

entries.zh: 袁盎具言吳所以反狀，以錯故，獨急斬錯以謝吳，吳兵乃可罷。
entries.en: Yuan Ang laid out in full the reasons for Wu's rebellion, arguing that Cuo was the cause, and that the only way to halt the Wu armies was to execute Cuo at once as a gesture of appeasement to Wu.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang laid out in full the reasons for Wu's rebellion, arguing that it was on account of Cuo, and that the only course was to swiftly execute Cuo as an apology to Wu, after which the Wu armies could be halted.

entries.zh: 其語具在吳事中。
entries.en: The full account of his words can be found in the chapter on the affairs of Wu.
entries.literal: The full account of his words is in the chapter on the affairs of Wu.

entries.zh: 使袁盎為太常，竇嬰為大將軍。
entries.en: The emperor made Yuan Ang Grand Master of Ceremonies and Dou Ying Grand General.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies, and Dou Ying was made Grand General.

entries.zh: 兩人素相與善。
entries.en: The two had always been close.
entries.literal: The two had always been on good terms with each other.

entries.zh: 逮吳反。
entries.en: Then Wu rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: This was at the time of the Wu rebellion.

entries.zh: 諸陵長者長安中賢大夫爭附兩人，車隨者日數百乘。
entries.en: The elders of the mausoleum towns and the eminent officials of Chang'an vied to attach themselves to the two men, and hundreds of carriages trailed them each day.
entries.literal: The elders of the various imperial mausoleum towns and the worthy officials of Chang'an all vied to attach themselves to the two men. Hundreds of carriages followed them each day.

entries.zh: 吳楚已破，上更以元王子平陸侯禮為楚王，袁盎為楚相。
entries.en: After Wu and Chu were defeated, the Emperor installed the Marquis of Pinglu, Li, a son of the former King Yuan, as the new King of Chu, and Yuan Ang was appointed Chancellor of Chu.
entries.literal: After Wu and Chu had been defeated, the Emperor installed the Marquis of Pinglu, Li, son of the former King Yuan, as the new King of Chu, and Yuan Ang was made Chancellor of Chu.

entries.zh: 嘗上書有所言，不用。
entries.en: He once submitted a memorial with proposals, but they were not adopted.
entries.literal: He once submitted a memorial speaking on certain matters, but his proposals were not adopted.

entries.zh: 袁盎病免居家，與閭里浮沈，相隨行，鬬雞走狗。
entries.en: Yuan Ang was dismissed on grounds of illness and retired to his home. He drifted along with his neighbors, joining them in cockfights and dog races.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang was dismissed due to illness and lived at home. He drifted along with his neighbors, going about with them, cockfighting and dog-racing.

entries.zh: 雒陽劇孟嘗過袁盎，盎善待之。
entries.en: Ju Meng of Luoyang once paid Yuan Ang a visit, and Ang received him warmly.
entries.literal: Ju Meng of Luoyang once visited Yuan Ang, and Ang treated him well.

entries.zh: 安陵富人有謂盎曰：「吾聞劇孟博徒，將軍何自通之？」
entries.en: A wealthy man of Anling said to Ang, 'I hear that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why do you associate with such a man, General?'
entries.literal: A wealthy man of Anling said to Ang: 'I have heard that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why does the General associate with such a man?'

entries.zh: 盎曰：「劇孟雖博徒，然母死，客送葬車千餘乘，此亦有過人者。
entries.en: Ang replied, 'Though Ju Meng is a gambler, when his mother died, over a thousand carriages of guests attended the funeral. A man who commands such loyalty has qualities that surpass the ordinary.
entries.literal: Ang said: 'Though Ju Meng is a gambler, when his mother died, more than a thousand carriages of guests attended the funeral procession. This shows he has qualities that surpass those of ordinary men.

entries.zh: 且緩急人所有。
entries.en: After all, crises come to every man.
entries.literal: Moreover, emergencies are something that everyone faces.

entries.zh: 夫一旦有急叩門，不以親為解，不以存亡為辭，天下所望者，獨季心、劇孟耳。
entries.en: When a crisis comes knocking, men who will not hide behind family ties or plead for their own lives—men whom all under heaven look to—are only Ji Xin and Ju Meng.
entries.literal: When one day a crisis comes knocking at the door, those who will not use family ties as an excuse and will not plead concerns of life and death—the men whom all under heaven look to—are only Ji Xin and Ju Meng.

entries.zh: 今公常從數騎，一旦有緩急，寧足恃乎！」
entries.en: You ride with only a few horsemen. If a crisis comes, can you rely on them!'
entries.literal: Now you go about with only a few horsemen. If one day a crisis comes, can they be relied upon!'

entries.zh: 罵富人，弗與通。
entries.en: He berated the rich man and cut off all contact with him.
entries.literal: He berated the wealthy man and refused to associate with him.

entries.zh: 諸公聞之，皆多袁盎。
entries.en: When word of this spread, everyone praised Yuan Ang.
entries.literal: When the various gentlemen heard of this, they all praised Yuan Ang.

entries.zh: 袁盎雖家居，景帝時時使人問籌策。
entries.en: Although Yuan Ang was living in retirement, Emperor Jing would from time to time send someone to consult him on matters of policy.
entries.literal: Although Yuan Ang was living at home, Emperor Jing would from time to time send people to consult him for counsel and strategies.

entries.zh: 梁王欲求為嗣，袁盎進說，其後語塞。
entries.en: When the King of Liang sought to be named heir, Yuan Ang spoke against it, and the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: When the King of Liang sought to be named heir, Yuan Ang spoke out against it, and thereafter the discussion was silenced.

entries.zh: 梁王以此怨盎，曾使人刺盎。
entries.en: The King of Liang bore a grudge against Ang and sent assassins after him.
entries.literal: The King of Liang bore a grudge against Ang for this and sent someone to assassinate him.

entries.zh: 刺者至關中，問袁盎，諸君譽之皆不容口。
entries.en: When the assassin arrived in Guanzhong and asked about Yuan Ang, everyone he met praised Ang so effusively they could scarcely contain themselves.
entries.literal: When the assassin arrived at Guanzhong and inquired about Yuan Ang, everyone praised him so effusively that they could hardly contain themselves.

entries.zh: 乃見袁盎曰：「臣受梁王金來刺君，君長者，不忍刺君。
entries.en: He went to see Yuan Ang and said, 'I was paid by the King of Liang to assassinate you. But you are an honorable man, and I cannot bring myself to do it.
entries.literal: He then went to see Yuan Ang and said: 'I accepted gold from the King of Liang and came to assassinate you. But you are an honorable man, and I cannot bring myself to do it.

entries.zh: 然後刺君者十餘曹，備之！」
entries.en: But there are more than ten other teams of assassins coming for you. Be on your guard!'
entries.literal: However, more than ten other teams of assassins are coming after you. Be on your guard!'

entries.zh: 袁盎心不樂，家又多怪，乃之棓生所問占。
entries.en: Yuan Ang was deeply troubled, and strange omens had been plaguing his household. He went to consult the diviner Master Pou.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang was troubled at heart, and his household had been plagued by many strange occurrences. He went to consult the diviner Master Pou.

entries.zh: 還，梁刺客後曹輩果遮刺殺盎安陵郭門外。
entries.en: On his way back, the later teams of Liang assassins ambushed and killed Ang outside the outer gate of Anling.
entries.literal: On his way back, the later teams of Liang assassins indeed ambushed and stabbed Ang to death outside the outer gate of Anling.

entries.zh: 景帝即位，以錯為內史。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he appointed Cuo as Prefect of the Capital.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he appointed Cuo as Prefect of the Capital.

entries.zh: 錯常數請閒言事，輒聽，寵幸傾九卿，法令多所更定。
entries.en: Cuo frequently requested private audiences to discuss affairs, and the Emperor always listened. His favor eclipsed that of the Nine Ministers, and many laws and regulations were revised at his behest.
