entries.literal: Cuo frequently requested private audiences to discuss affairs, and the Emperor invariably heeded him. His favor eclipsed that of the Nine Ministers, and many laws and regulations were revised.

entries.zh: 丞相申屠嘉心弗便，力未有以傷。
entries.en: Chancellor Shentu Jia resented this but lacked the means to bring Cuo down.
entries.literal: Chancellor Shentu Jia was displeased in his heart but did not yet have the power to harm Cuo.

entries.zh: 內史府居太上廟壖中，門東出，不便，錯乃穿兩門南出，鑿廟壖垣。
entries.en: The offices of the Prefect of the Capital stood within the precincts of the Supreme Temple. The gate faced east, which was inconvenient, so Cuo opened two gates facing south, cutting through the temple precinct wall.
entries.literal: The offices of the Prefect of the Capital were located within the precincts of the Supreme Temple. The gate opened to the east, which was inconvenient. Cuo therefore opened two gates to the south, cutting through the precinct wall of the temple.

entries.zh: 丞相嘉聞，大怒，欲因此過為奏請誅錯。
entries.en: When Chancellor Jia heard of this, he was furious and resolved to use the offense as grounds for a memorial requesting Cuo's execution.
entries.literal: When Chancellor Jia heard of this, he was furious and intended to use this transgression as the basis for a memorial requesting Cuo's execution.

entries.zh: 錯聞之，即夜請閒，具為上言之。
entries.en: When Cuo learned of the Chancellor's plan, he immediately sought a private audience that night and laid the whole matter before the Emperor.
entries.literal: When Cuo heard of this, he immediately requested a private audience that very night and laid the entire matter before the Emperor.

entries.zh: 丞相奏事，因言錯擅鑿廟垣為門，請下廷尉誅。
entries.en: When the Chancellor presented his memorial, he charged Cuo with arbitrarily cutting through the temple wall to make a gate and requested that the case be referred to the Commandant of Justice for execution.
entries.literal: When the Chancellor presented his memorial, he accused Cuo of arbitrarily cutting through the temple wall to make a gate and requested that the case be referred to the Commandant of Justice for execution.

entries.zh: 上曰：「此非廟垣，乃壖中垣，不致於法。」
entries.en: The Emperor replied, 'That is not the temple wall itself but merely the precinct wall. No law applies.'
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'This is not the temple wall itself, but rather the precinct wall. The law does not apply.'

entries.zh: 丞相謝。
entries.en: The Chancellor apologized.
entries.literal: The Chancellor apologized.

entries.zh: 罷朝，怒謂長史曰：「吾當先斬以聞，乃先請，為兒所賣，固誤。」
entries.en: After court was dismissed, he angrily said to the Chief Clerk, 'I should have had him beheaded first and reported afterward. Instead, I asked permission first and was outmaneuvered by that boy. A terrible blunder.'
entries.literal: After court was dismissed, he angrily said to the Chief Clerk: 'I should have had him beheaded first and reported afterward. Instead I asked permission first and was outmaneuvered by that boy. It was a great blunder.'

entries.zh: 丞相遂發病死。
entries.en: The Chancellor soon fell ill and died.
entries.literal: The Chancellor thereupon fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 錯以此愈貴。
entries.en: After this, Cuo's power only grew.
entries.literal: Cuo became even more influential because of this.

entries.zh: 鼂錯已死，謁者仆射鄧公為校尉，擊吳楚軍為將。
entries.en: After Chao Cuo was dead, Deng Gong, the Chief Receptionist, served as a Colonel and led troops against the Wu and Chu armies.
entries.literal: After Chao Cuo was dead, Deng Gong, the Chief Receptionist, was serving as a Colonel and led troops as a general to attack the Wu and Chu armies.

entries.zh: 還，上書言軍事，謁見上。
entries.en: Upon his return, he submitted a memorial on military affairs and was granted an audience with the Emperor.
entries.literal: Upon his return, he submitted a memorial on military affairs and requested an audience with the Emperor.

entries.zh: 上問曰：「道軍所來，聞鼂錯死，吳楚罷不？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, 'On your way back from the front, did you hear whether Wu and Chu ceased hostilities after Chao Cuo's death?'
entries.literal: The Emperor asked: 'On your way back from the army, did you hear whether, after Chao Cuo's death, Wu and Chu have ceased hostilities?'

entries.zh: 鄧公曰：「吳王為反數十年矣，發怒削地，以誅錯為名，其意非在錯也。
entries.en: Deng Gong replied, 'The King of Wu has been plotting rebellion for decades. He exploded in fury over the reduction of his territory and used the execution of Cuo as his pretext. His true aim was never about Cuo.
entries.literal: Deng Gong said: 'The King of Wu has been plotting rebellion for decades. He erupted in fury over the reduction of his territory and used the demand to execute Cuo as his pretext. His true intention was never about Cuo.

entries.zh: 且臣恐天下之士噤口，不敢復言也！」
entries.en: Moreover, I fear that the scholars of the realm will seal their lips and never dare speak again!'
entries.literal: Moreover, I fear that the scholars of the realm will clamp their mouths shut and never dare to speak again!'

entries.zh: 上曰：「何哉？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, 'Why?'
entries.literal: The Emperor said: 'Why is that?'

entries.zh: 鄧公曰：「夫鼂錯患諸侯彊大不可制，故請削地以尊京師，萬世之利也。
entries.en: Deng Gong said, 'Chao Cuo saw that the feudal lords had grown too powerful to control, and so he proposed reducing their territories to strengthen the capital. This was a policy to benefit ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: Deng Gong said: 'Chao Cuo was concerned that the feudal lords had grown too strong to be controlled, and so he proposed reducing their territories to enhance the authority of the capital. This was a policy that would benefit ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 計畫始行，卒受大戮，內杜忠臣之口，外為諸侯報仇，臣竊為陛下不取也。」
entries.en: His plans had barely begun when he met a terrible end. At home, this has sealed the mouths of loyal ministers. Abroad, it has served as the feudal lords' revenge. I venture to say that this was not a wise course for Your Majesty.'
entries.literal: His plans had only just begun to be carried out when he met with terrible execution. Internally, this has sealed the mouths of loyal ministers. Externally, it has served as revenge for the feudal lords. I venture to say that this was inadvisable for Your Majesty.'

entries.zh: 於是景帝默然良久，曰：「公言善，吾亦恨之。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing fell silent for a long while, then said, 'You speak well. I, too, regret it.'
entries.literal: At this, Emperor Jing was silent for a long time and then said: 'Your words are well spoken. I too regret it.'

entries.zh: 乃拜鄧公為城陽中尉。
entries.en: Deng Gong was then appointed Commandant of Chengyang.
entries.literal: He then appointed Deng Gong as Commandant of Chengyang.

entries.zh: 鄧公，成固人也，多奇計。
entries.en: Deng Gong was a native of Chenggu, known for his many brilliant stratagems.
entries.literal: Deng Gong was a native of Chenggu and was known for his many remarkable stratagems.

entries.zh: 建元中，上招賢良，公卿言鄧公，時鄧公免，起家為九卿。
entries.en: During the Jianyuan period, when the Emperor sought worthy men, the senior officials recommended Deng Gong. At the time he was out of office, but he was recalled and appointed as one of the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: During the Jianyuan period, when the Emperor sought worthy and talented men, the senior officials recommended Deng Gong. At that time Deng Gong was out of office. He was recalled from private life and appointed as one of the Nine Ministers.

entries.zh: 一年，復謝病免歸。
entries.en: After a year, he again pleaded illness and retired.
entries.literal: After one year, he again pleaded illness and was dismissed, returning home.

entries.zh: 其子章以修黃老言顯於諸公閒。
entries.en: His son Zhang became prominent among the senior officials through his devotion to the teachings of Huang-Lao.
entries.literal: His son Zhang became prominent among the senior officials through his study and practice of the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.

entries.zh: 袁盎者，楚人也，字絲。
entries.en: Yuan Ang was a native of Chu, and his courtesy name was Si.
entries.literal: Yuan Ang was a man of Chu, with the courtesy name Si.

entries.zh: 父故為群盜，徙處安陵。
entries.en: His father had once been a bandit and was later resettled in Anling.
entries.literal: His father had formerly been among a band of robbers, and was relocated to settle in Anling.

entries.zh: 高后時，盎嘗為呂祿舍人。
entries.en: During the reign of Empress Dowager Gao, Ang served as a retainer in the household of Lü Lu.
entries.literal: During the time of Empress Dowager Gao, Ang once served as a retainer of Lü Lu.

entries.zh: 及孝文帝即位，盎兄噲任盎為中郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Ang's elder brother Kuai secured him a position as Gentleman of the Palace.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, Ang's elder brother Kuai recommended Ang to serve as a Gentleman of the Palace.

entries.zh: 張廷尉釋之者，堵陽人也，字季。
entries.en: Zhang Shizhi, the Commandant of Justice, was a native of Duyang. His courtesy name was Ji.
entries.literal: Zhang Shizhi, the Commandant of Justice, was from Duyang and his courtesy name was Ji.

entries.zh: 有兄仲同居。
entries.en: He had an elder brother named Zhong, with whom he shared a household.
entries.literal: He had an elder brother Zhong with whom he lived.

entries.zh: 以訾為騎郎，事孝文帝，十歲不得調，無所知名。
entries.en: He purchased a position as a mounted attendant and served Emperor Wen, but for ten years received no promotion and remained entirely unknown.
entries.literal: He became a mounted attendant through purchase and served Emperor Wen, but for ten years received no promotion and remained unknown.

entries.zh: 釋之曰：「久宦減仲之產，不遂。」
entries.en: Shizhi said: "Long service in office has been depleting Zhong's property—I cannot make a success of this."
entries.literal: Shizhi said: "Long service in office diminishes Zhong's property—I cannot succeed this way."

entries.zh: 欲自免歸。
entries.en: He wanted to resign his post and return home.
entries.literal: He wished to resign and return home.

entries.zh: 中郎將袁盎知其賢，惜其去，乃請徙釋之補謁者。
entries.en: The Colonel of the Guard Yuan Ang recognized his talent and was reluctant to see him leave, so he petitioned to have Shizhi transferred to fill a vacancy as an usher.
entries.literal: The Colonel Yuan Ang knew his worth and regretted his departure, so he requested to transfer Shizhi to fill the position of usher.

entries.zh: 釋之既朝畢，因前言便宜事。
entries.en: After Shizhi completed his court duties, he stepped forward to speak on matters of practical governance.
entries.literal: After Shizhi finished his court duties, he stepped forward to speak of matters of advantage.

entries.zh: 文帝曰：「卑之，毋甚高論，令今可施行也。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen said: "Keep it modest—do not discourse too loftily; speak of what can be put into practice now."
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Keep it low—do not discourse too loftily; make it something that can be put into practice now."

entries.zh: 於是釋之言秦漢之閒事，秦所以失而漢所以興者久之。
entries.en: Shizhi then spoke at length about the transition from Qin to Han—why the Qin fell and why the Han rose.
entries.literal: Then Shizhi spoke at length of affairs between Qin and Han, why Qin lost and why Han rose.

entries.zh: 文帝稱善，乃拜釋之為謁者仆射。
entries.en: Emperor Wen praised his discourse and appointed him Chief Usher.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen praised it as good and appointed Shizhi as Chief Usher.

entries.zh: 頃之，太子與梁王共車入朝，不下司馬門，於是釋之追止太子、梁王無得入殿門。
entries.en: Soon afterward, the Crown Prince and the King of Liang rode together in one carriage to attend court, failing to dismount at the Marshal's Gate. Shizhi gave chase and barred them from entering the palace gates.
entries.literal: Soon after, the crown prince and King Liang entered the court together in the same carriage without descending at the Marshal's Gate, so Shizhi pursued and stopped the crown prince and King Liang from entering the palace gate.

entries.zh: 遂劾不下公門不敬，奏之。
entries.en: He then impeached them for failing to dismount at the palace gate—a breach of protocol—and submitted a formal memorial.
entries.literal: He then impeached them for not descending at the public gate, a sign of disrespect, and memorialized it.

entries.zh: 薄太后聞之，文帝免冠謝曰：「教兒子不謹。」
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Bo heard of it, Emperor Wen removed his cap and apologized, saying, "I have failed to teach my sons carefully enough."
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Bo heard of it. Emperor Wen removed his cap and apologized, saying: "I have not taught my sons with sufficient care."

entries.zh: 薄太后乃使使承詔赦太子、梁王，然後得入。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Bo then dispatched messengers bearing an imperial edict to pardon the Crown Prince and the King of Liang, after which they were permitted to enter.
entries.literal: Empress Bo then sent messengers to pardon the crown prince and King Liang according to the imperial command, after which they were allowed to enter.

entries.zh: 文帝由是奇釋之，拜為中大夫。
entries.en: From this, Emperor Wen came to regard Shizhi as remarkable and appointed him Palace Counselor.
entries.literal: From this Emperor Wen regarded Shizhi as extraordinary and appointed him Palace Counselor.

entries.zh: 後文帝崩，景帝立，釋之恐，稱病。
entries.en: After Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing ascended the throne, Shizhi grew fearful and feigned illness.
entries.literal: After Emperor Wen passed away and Emperor Jing ascended, Shizhi was fearful and claimed illness.

entries.zh: 欲免去，懼大誅至；
entries.en: He wanted to resign and leave, fearing that severe punishment would follow.
entries.literal: He wished to resign and leave, fearing that severe punishment would come.

entries.zh: 欲見謝，則未知何如。
entries.en: He wished to seek an audience and apologize, but did not know how it would be received.
entries.literal: He wished to see and apologize, but did not know how it would be received.

entries.zh: 用王生計，卒見謝，景帝不過也。
entries.en: Following Wang Sheng's counsel, he finally obtained an audience and offered his apology. Emperor Jing did not hold it against him.
entries.literal: Using Wang Sheng's plan, he finally saw and apologized, and Emperor Jing did not punish him.

entries.zh: 張廷尉事景帝歲餘，為淮南王相，猶尚以前過也。
entries.en: Zhang the Commandant of Justice served Emperor Jing for over a year before being transferred to serve as Chancellor to the King of Huainan—still bearing the taint of his earlier offense.
entries.literal: Zhang the Commandant of Justice served Emperor Jing for over a year, became chancellor to the King of Huainan, but still bore the previous offense.

entries.zh: 久之，釋之卒。
entries.en: In time, Shizhi died.
entries.literal: After a long time, Shizhi passed away.

entries.zh: 其子曰張摯，字長公，官至大夫，免。
entries.en: His son was Zhang Zhi, courtesy name Changgong. He rose to the rank of Grand Master but was then dismissed.
entries.literal: His son was named Zhang Zhi, courtesy name Changgong, served as grand master, then was dismissed.

entries.zh: 以不能取容當世，故終身不仕。
entries.en: Unable to ingratiate himself with the powers of his day, he never held office again for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: Because he could not accommodate the current age, he never served in office throughout his life.

entries.zh: 七年，景帝立，以唐為楚相，免。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Emperor Jing ascended the throne, appointed Tang Chancellor of Chu, and later dismissed him.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Jing ascended the throne, made Tang Chancellor of Chu, and dismissed him.

entries.zh: 武帝立，求賢良，舉馮唐。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne and sought out men of worth, Feng Tang was recommended.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu ascended, sought worthy and good officials, recommended Feng Tang.

entries.zh: 唐時年九十餘，不能復為官，乃以唐子馮遂為郎。
entries.en: By that time, Tang was over ninety years old and could no longer serve. His son Feng Sui was appointed as a mounted attendant in his stead.
entries.literal: Tang at that time was over ninety years old, could no longer serve as official, so made Tang son Feng Sui a mounted attendant.

entries.zh: 遂字王孫，亦奇士，與余善。
entries.en: Sui, courtesy name Wangsun, was also a remarkable man, and he and I became good friends.
entries.literal: Sui courtesy name Wangsun, also an extraordinary gentleman, befriended me well.

entries.zh: 萬石君名奮，其父趙人也，姓石氏。
entries.en: The Marquis of Wanshi was named Fen. His father was a man of Zhao, surnamed Shi.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi was named Fen, his father was from Zhao, surname Shi.

entries.zh: 趙亡，徙居溫。
entries.en: When Zhao fell, he moved to Wen.
entries.literal: After Zhao perished, he moved to reside in Wen.

entries.zh: 高祖東擊項籍，過河內，時奮年十五，為小吏，侍高祖。
entries.en: When Gaozu marched east to attack Xiang Ji and passed through Henei, Fen was fifteen years old, serving as a minor functionary in attendance on Gaozu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu struck east against Xiang Ji, passing through Henei, at that time Fen was fifteen years old, serving as a minor official attending Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖與語，愛其恭敬，問曰：「若何有？」
entries.en: Gaozu spoke with him and was pleased by his respectful bearing. He asked, "What do you have?"
entries.literal: Gaozu spoke with him and was pleased by his respectful bearing, and asked, "What do you have?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「奮獨有母，不幸失明。
entries.en: He replied, "I have only my mother, who has unfortunately gone blind.
entries.literal: He replied, "Fen has only a mother, who has unfortunately gone blind.

entries.zh: 家貧。
entries.en: His family was poor.
entries.literal: The family is poor.

entries.zh: 有姊，能鼓琴。」
entries.en: I also have an elder sister who can play the zither."
entries.literal: I have an elder sister who can play the zither."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「若能從我乎？」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Can you follow me?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "Can you follow me?"

entries.zh: 曰：「願盡力。」
entries.en: He said, "I will do my utmost."
entries.literal: He said, "I wish to serve with all my strength."

entries.zh: 於是高祖召其姊為美人，以奮為中涓，受書謁，徙其家長安中戚裏，以姊為美人故也。
entries.en: Thereupon Gaozu summoned his elder sister to serve as a court beauty, appointed Fen as a palace attendant in charge of receiving documents and audiences, and relocated his family to the Zhongqi quarter in Chang'an—all on account of his sister becoming a court beauty.
entries.literal: Then Gaozu summoned his elder sister to become a beauty, made Fen a palace attendant receiving documents and audiences, moved his family to the Zhongqi quarter in Chang'an, because his elder sister became a beauty.

entries.zh: 其官至孝文時，積功勞至大中大夫。
entries.en: By the time of Emperor Wen, he had accumulated enough merit to rise to the rank of Grand Palace Counselor.
entries.literal: His official position reached during Emperor Wen's time, accumulating merit he reached Grand Palace Counselor.

entries.zh: 無文學，恭謹無與比。
entries.en: He had no literary learning, but in respectful caution he was without equal.
entries.literal: Without literary learning, his respectful caution had no equal.

entries.zh: 文帝時，東陽侯張相如為太子太傅，免。
entries.en: During Emperor Wen's reign, the Marquis of Dongyang, Zhang Xiangru, served as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince but was dismissed.
entries.literal: During Emperor Wen's time, the Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiangru served as crown prince's Grand Tutor, was dismissed.

entries.zh: 選可為傅者，皆推奮，奮為太子太傅。
entries.en: When a suitable replacement was being selected, all recommended Fen, and so Fen became Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: When selecting someone suitable as tutor, all recommended Fen, so Fen became crown prince's Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 及孝景即位，以為九卿；
entries.en: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he was appointed one of the Nine Ministers;
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, [Fen] was appointed one of the Nine Ministers;

entries.zh: 迫近，憚之，徙奮為諸侯相。
entries.en: Being too close to the throne, others feared him, and so Fen was transferred to serve as chancellor of a feudal kingdom.
entries.literal: Pressing close, they feared him, transferred Fen to become chancellor of feudal lords.

entries.zh: 奮長子建，次子甲，次子乙，次子慶，皆以馴行孝謹，官皆至二千石。
entries.en: Fen's eldest son Jian, second son Jia, third son Yi, and fourth son Qing all attained the rank of two-thousand-bushel official through their disciplined conduct, filial piety, and caution.
entries.literal: Fen's eldest son Jian, second son Jia, third son Yi, fourth son Qing, all through their tame conduct filial piety and caution, their official positions all reached two thousand dan.

entries.zh: 於是景帝曰：「石君及四子皆二千石，人臣尊寵乃集其門。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing therefore said, "Lord Shi and his four sons all hold offices of two thousand bushels. The honor and favor due to ministers are gathered at his gate."
entries.literal: Thereupon Emperor Jing said, "Lord Shi and his four sons are all two-thousand-bushel officials—ministerial honor and favor all gather at his gate."

entries.zh: 號奮為萬石君。
entries.en: He bestowed upon Fen the title Marquis of Wanshi.
entries.literal: He titled Fen the Marquis of Wan Shi.

entries.zh: 建陵侯衛綰者，代大陵人也。
entries.en: The Marquis of Jianling, Wei Wan, was a man of Daling in Dai.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Jianling Wei Wan was a person from Daling in Dai.

entries.zh: 綰以戲車為郎，事文帝，功次遷為中郎將，醇謹無他。
entries.en: Wan entered service as a mounted attendant through his skill in chariot games, serving Emperor Wen. Through accumulated merit he was successively promoted to Colonel of the Palace Guard—upright and cautious, with no other notable qualities.
entries.literal: Wan became a mounted attendant through chariot games, served Emperor Wen, merit successively promoted to Colonel, pure and cautious without other qualities.

entries.zh: 孝景為太子時，召上左右飲，而綰稱病不行。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing was still Crown Prince, he summoned Emperor Wen's attendants to drink with him, but Wan pleaded illness and did not go.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing was Crown Prince, he summoned the attendants of the emperor [Wen] to drink, but Wan pleaded illness and did not go.

entries.zh: 文帝且崩時，屬孝景曰：「綰長者，善遇之。」
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was near death, he charged Emperor Jing, saying, "Wan is a man of mature character. Treat him well."
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was about to die, he entrusted Emperor Jing, saying, "Wan is a man of mature character—treat him well."

entries.zh: 及文帝崩，景帝立，歲餘不噍呵綰，綰日以謹力。
entries.en: After Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing ascended the throne, more than a year passed without his ever scolding or rebuking Wan. Wan redoubled his cautious diligence each day.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen passed away and Emperor Jing ascended, over a year did not scold or berate Wan, Wan daily exerted himself cautiously.

entries.zh: 景帝幸上林，詔中郎將參乘，還而問曰：「君知所以得參乘乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Jing visited Shanglin Park and ordered the Colonel of the Palace Guard to ride beside him in the imperial carriage. On the return, he asked, "Do you know why you were given this place beside me?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing visited Shanglin Park and ordered the Colonel of the Palace Guard to ride beside him as attendant. On the return he asked, "Do you know why you were granted the place of attendant in the carriage?"

entries.zh: 綰曰：「臣從車士幸得以功次遷為中郎將，不自知也。」
entries.en: Wan said, "Your servant began as a chariot soldier and was fortunate enough to be promoted by degrees to Colonel of the Palace Guard. I do not know the reason."
entries.literal: Wan said, "Your servant followed as a chariot warrior and was fortunate to be promoted step by step to Colonel of the Palace Guard—I do not know [why]."

entries.zh: 上問曰：「吾為太子時召君，君不肯來，何也？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "When I was Crown Prince, I summoned you, but you refused to come. Why?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked, "When I was Crown Prince I summoned you, but you were unwilling to come—why?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「死罪，實病！」
entries.en: He replied, "I deserve death, but I truly was ill!"
entries.literal: He replied, "A capital offense—I was truly ill!"

entries.zh: 上賜之劍。
entries.en: The emperor bestowed a sword upon him.
entries.literal: The emperor granted him a sword.

entries.zh: 綰曰：「先帝賜臣劍凡六，劍不敢奉詔。」
entries.en: Wan said, "The former emperor granted me six swords in all; I dare not comply with the edict [to wear this one]."
entries.literal: Wan said, "The former emperor granted your servant six swords in all; your servant dares not comply with the edict [to wear this one]."

entries.zh: 上曰：「劍，人之所施易，獨至今乎？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Swords are things people readily give away. Can it be that you alone have kept yours down to the present?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Swords are what men part with readily—have you alone kept yours until now?"

entries.zh: 綰曰：「具在。」
entries.en: Wan said, "They are all here."
entries.literal: Wan said, "They are all here."

entries.zh: 上使取六劍，劍尚盛，未嘗服也。
entries.en: The emperor had the six swords brought out. They were still in pristine condition—he had never once worn them.
entries.literal: The emperor had the six swords taken, the swords were still abundant, he had never used them.

entries.zh: 郎官有譴，常蒙其罪，不與他將爭；
entries.en: When palace attendants were reprimanded, he often shielded them by taking the blame himself, and he did not quarrel with other commanders;
entries.literal: When palace attendants were blamed, he would regularly shield them and bear their guilt, and would not dispute with other commanders;

entries.zh: 有功，常讓他將。
entries.en: When there was merit to be claimed, he always deferred to the other generals.
entries.literal: When there was merit, he constantly yielded to other generals.

entries.zh: 上以為廉，忠實無他腸，乃拜綰為河閒王太傅。
entries.en: The emperor considered him incorruptible, loyal, and sincere, without any ulterior motives, and so appointed Wan as Grand Tutor to the King of Hejian.
entries.literal: The emperor considered him clean, loyal and real without other intentions, then appointed Wan as Hejian King's Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 吳楚反，詔綰為將，將河閒兵擊吳楚有功，拜為中尉。
entries.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, an edict appointed Wan as general. He led the troops of Hejian against Wu and Chu with distinction, and was appointed Commandant.
entries.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, an edict appointed Wan as general; he led the troops of Hejian against Wu and Chu with merit and was appointed Commandant of the Palace Guard.

entries.zh: 三歲，以軍功，孝景前六年中封綰為建陵侯。
entries.en: Three years later, on account of his military merit, in the sixth year of Emperor Jing's first reign period, Wan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianling.
entries.literal: Three years, through army merit, in the middle of the sixth year of Emperor Jing's reign before his death, sealed Wan as Marquis of Jianling.

entries.zh: 孝景帝季年，萬石君以上大夫祿歸老于家，以歲時為朝臣。
entries.en: In the later years of Emperor Jing's reign, the Marquis of Wanshi retired to his home on the salary of a Senior Grand Counselor, attending court only at seasonal assemblies.
entries.literal: In the later years of Emperor Jing, the Marquis of Wan Shi returned home to retire on the salary of Grand Palace Counselor, serving as court minister by season.

entries.zh: 過宮門闕，萬石君必下車趨，見路馬必式焉。
entries.en: Whenever he passed the gate-towers of the palace, the Marquis of Wanshi would invariably step down from his carriage and walk briskly past. Whenever he saw the imperial carriage horses on the road, he would bow in salute.
entries.literal: Passing the palace gate towers, the Marquis of Wan Shi would certainly descend his chariot and hasten, seeing road horses he would certainly salute.

entries.zh: 子孫為小吏，來歸謁，萬石君必朝服見之，不名。
entries.en: When his sons and grandsons who served as minor officials came home to pay their respects, the Marquis of Wanshi would invariably receive them in full court dress, never addressing them by name.
entries.literal: When sons and grandsons serving as minor officials came home to visit, the Marquis of Wan Shi would certainly wear court robes to see them, not using names.

entries.zh: 子孫有過失，不譙讓，為便坐，對案不食。
entries.en: When his sons and grandsons committed errors, he would not scold or reproach them but would take his seat, face the table, and refuse to eat.
entries.literal: When sons and grandsons had faults, he would not scold or reproach them but would take his seat, face the table, and not eat.

entries.zh: 然後諸子相責，因長老肉袒固謝罪，改之，乃許。
entries.en: Then the sons would reproach one another, and the elders would bare their shoulders and earnestly beg forgiveness. Only when the offender had reformed would he relent.
entries.literal: Then the various sons would mutually reproach each other, because of the elders stripping to the waist and firmly apologizing for the offense, changing it, then he would allow it.

entries.zh: 子孫勝冠者在側，雖燕居必冠，申申如也。
entries.en: When sons and grandsons who had undergone the capping ceremony were at his side, he would always wear his cap even in private, bearing himself with grave composure.
entries.literal: When sons and grandsons who had undergone the capping ceremony were at his side, even in private he would always wear his cap, grave and composed.

entries.zh: 僮仆訢訢如也，唯謹。
entries.en: His servants and attendants went about cheerfully, all with the utmost caution.
entries.literal: The servants and attendants were cheerful and only cautious.

entries.zh: 上時賜食於家，必稽首俯伏而食之，如在上前。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor bestowed food upon his household, he would invariably bow his head to the ground and prostrate himself before eating it, as though he were in the emperor's presence.
entries.literal: When the emperor occasionally granted food at home, he would certainly bow his head and prostrate to eat it, as if before the emperor.

entries.zh: 其執喪，哀戚甚悼。
entries.en: When the family observed mourning, their grief was profound and deeply sorrowful.
entries.literal: Their observance of mourning was sorrowfully sad and deeply mournful.

entries.zh: 子孫遵教，亦如之。
entries.en: His sons and grandsons followed his teachings and conducted themselves in the same manner.
entries.literal: Sons and grandsons followed the teachings, also like this.

entries.zh: 萬石君家以孝謹聞乎郡國，雖齊魯諸儒質行，皆自以為不及也。
entries.en: The household of the Marquis of Wanshi was renowned for filial piety and caution throughout the commanderies and kingdoms. Even the Confucian scholars of Qi and Lu, known for their upright conduct, all considered themselves his inferiors.
entries.literal: The Wan Shi Jun household was known for filial piety and caution throughout commanderies and kingdoms, though the various Confucian scholars of Qi and Lu in solid conduct, all considered themselves not equal.

entries.zh: 為丞相三歲，景帝崩，武帝立。
entries.en: After three years as Chancellor, Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu ascended the throne.
entries.literal: Served as Chancellor three years, Emperor Jing passed away, Emperor Wu ascended.

entries.zh: 建元年中，丞相以景帝疾時諸官囚多坐不辜者，而君不任職，免之。
entries.en: In the first year of the Jianyuan era, the Chancellor was dismissed on the grounds that during Emperor Jing's illness many imprisoned officials had been wrongly convicted, and he had failed to fulfill his duties.
entries.literal: In the middle of the first year of Jianyuan, the Chancellor, because during Emperor Jing's illness various official prisoners many sat not guilty, yet he did not bear his duty, dismissed him.

entries.zh: 其後綰卒，子信代。
entries.en: Afterward Wan died, and his son Xin succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: Afterward Wan died, son Xin succeeded.

entries.zh: 坐酎金失侯。
entries.en: He was convicted of providing impure ritual gold for the suburban sacrifice and lost his marquisate.
entries.literal: He was convicted on account of the tribute gold for the suburban sacrifice and lost his marquisate.

entries.zh: 吳楚反時，不疑以二千石將兵擊之。
entries.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Buyi led troops against them in his capacity as a two-thousand-bushel official.
entries.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Buyi with two thousand dan led troops to strike them.

entries.zh: 景帝後元年，拜為御史大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Emperor Jing's latter reign, he was appointed Imperial Secretary.
entries.literal: In the first year of Emperor Jing's reign after Emperor Wen's death, appointed as Imperial Secretary.

entries.zh: 天子修吳楚時功，乃封不疑為塞侯。
entries.en: The emperor reviewed the merits earned in the Wu-Chu campaign and enfeoffed Buyi as Marquis of Sai.
entries.literal: The emperor reviewed the merits from the Wu and Chu campaign and enfeoffed Buyi as Marquis of Sai.

entries.zh: 武帝建元年中，與丞相綰俱以過免。
entries.en: In the first year of Emperor Wu's Jianyuan era, he was dismissed along with Chancellor Wan on account of their offenses.
entries.literal: In the middle of the first year of Emperor Wu's Jianyuan, together with Chancellor Wan both dismissed due to faults.

entries.zh: 郎中令周文者，名仁，其先故任城人也。
entries.en: The Palace Steward Zhou Wen, whose given name was Ren, had ancestors originally from Rencheng.
entries.literal: The Palace Steward Zhou Wen, named Ren, his ancestors were formerly from Rencheng.

entries.zh: 以醫見。
entries.en: He first came to notice through his skill in medicine.
entries.literal: Appeared through medicine.

entries.zh: 景帝為太子時，拜為舍人，積功稍遷，孝文帝時至太中大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing was still Crown Prince, Ren was appointed as a retainer. Through accumulated merit he was gradually promoted, reaching the rank of Grand Palace Counselor by Emperor Wen's time.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing was crown prince, appointed as retainer, accumulating merit gradually promoted, during Emperor Wen's time reached Grand Palace Counselor.

entries.zh: 景帝初即位，拜仁為郎中令。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing first ascended the throne, he appointed Ren as Palace Steward.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing first ascended, appointed Ren as Palace Steward.

entries.zh: 仁為人陰重不泄，常衣敝補衣溺袴，期為不絜清，以是得幸。
entries.en: Ren was by nature secretive and discreet, never divulging anything. He habitually wore threadbare patched clothes and soiled trousers, deliberately making himself appear unkempt, and thus won the emperor's favor.
entries.literal: Ren as person was deep and heavy not leaking, constantly wore worn patched clothes urine pants, pretended to be not clean and pure, thus obtained favor.

entries.zh: 景帝入臥內，於後宮祕戲，仁常在旁。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing retired to his private chambers and engaged in secret amusements in the rear palace, Ren was always at his side.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing entered sleeping quarters, in the rear palace secret games, Ren constantly at side.

entries.zh: 至景帝崩，仁尚為郎中令，終無所言。
entries.en: Until Emperor Jing's death, Ren still served as Palace Steward, and to the end he never uttered a word about what he had seen.
entries.literal: Until Emperor Jing passed away, Ren still served as Palace Steward, ultimately had nothing to say.

entries.zh: 上時問人，仁曰：「上自察之。」
entries.en: When the emperor occasionally asked his opinion of people, Ren would say, "Your Majesty should examine them yourself."
entries.literal: When the emperor sometimes asked about people, Ren would say, "Your Majesty should examine them yourself."

entries.zh: 然亦無所毀。
entries.en: Yet neither did he ever slander anyone.
entries.literal: Yet also had nothing to slander.

entries.zh: 以此景帝再自幸其家。
entries.en: For this reason, Emperor Jing twice personally visited his home.
entries.literal: With this Emperor Jing twice personally visited his home.

entries.zh: 家徙陽陵。
entries.en: His family relocated to Yangling.
entries.literal: The home moved to Yangling.

entries.zh: 上所賜甚多，然常讓，不敢受也。
entries.en: The emperor's gifts to him were many, yet he always declined, not daring to accept.
entries.literal: What the emperor granted was very many, yet he constantly yielded, not daring to receive.

entries.zh: 諸侯群臣賂遺，終無所受。
entries.en: Gifts and offerings from feudal lords and ministers he would never accept.
entries.literal: Feudal lords and assembled ministers' gifts and remembrances, ultimately received none.

entries.zh: 御史大夫張叔者，名歐，安丘侯說之庶子也。
entries.en: The Imperial Secretary Zhang Shu, whose given name was Ou, was a concubine's son of the Marquis of Anqiu, Yue.
entries.literal: The Imperial Secretary Zhang Shu, named Ou, was the illegitimate son of the Marquis of Anqiu, Yue.

entries.zh: 孝文時以治刑名言事太子。
entries.en: During Emperor Wen's reign, Ou was known for his command of penal law and legal terminology and reported on affairs to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: During Emperor Wen's reign he was known for expertise in penal law and terminology and presented affairs to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 然歐雖治刑名家，其人長者。
entries.en: Yet although Ou was a practitioner of the Legalist school, he was himself a man of integrity.
entries.literal: Yet though Ou governed penal codes school, his person was a venerable elder.

entries.zh: 景帝時尊重，常為九卿。
entries.en: During Emperor Jing's reign he was respected and honored, regularly serving as one of the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: During Emperor Jing's time respected and honored, constantly became one of the Nine Ministers.

entries.zh: 至武帝元朔四年，韓安國免，詔拜歐為御史大夫。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Emperor Wu's Yuanshuo era, Han Anguo was dismissed, and an edict was issued appointing Ou as Imperial Secretary.
entries.literal: Reached Emperor Wu's the fourth year of Yuanshuo, Han Anguo dismissed, commanded to appoint Ou as Imperial Secretary.

entries.zh: 自歐為吏，未嘗言案人，專以誠長者處官。
entries.en: From the time Ou first became an official, he never once spoke of prosecuting anyone, devoting himself entirely to administering his office with sincerity and the manner of a man of integrity.
entries.literal: Since Ou became official, never once spoke of prosecuting people, specialized in sincerely as venerable elder administering office.

entries.zh: 官屬以為長者，亦不敢大欺。
entries.en: His subordinates regarded him as a man of integrity and did not dare to deceive him greatly.
entries.literal: Subordinates considered him venerable elder, also dared not greatly deceive.

entries.zh: 上具獄事，有可卻，卻之；
entries.en: When the emperor had prison cases prepared, Ou sent them back whenever they could be returned;
entries.literal: When the emperor had prepared prison cases, if they could be sent back, Ou sent them back;

entries.zh: 不可者，不得已，為涕泣面對而封之。
entries.en: When they could not be sent back, then, having no alternative, he would weep as he faced the prisoner and sealed the verdict.
entries.literal: if they could not be sent back, then, having no alternative, he would weep as he faced the prisoner and sealed the verdict.

entries.zh: 其愛人如此。
entries.en: Such was his compassion for others.
entries.literal: His loving people was like this.

entries.zh: 建元二年，郎中令王臧以文學獲罪。
entries.en: In the second year of the Jianyuan era, the Palace Steward Wang Zang was convicted on account of his literary activities.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, the Palace Steward Wang Zang was convicted for literary matters.

entries.zh: 皇太后以為儒者文多質少，今萬石君家不言而躬行，乃以長子建為郎中令，少子慶為內史。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager considered that Confucian scholars were long on rhetoric but short on substance, whereas the household of the Marquis of Wanshi spoke little but practiced virtue in person. She therefore appointed the eldest son Jian as Palace Steward and the youngest son Qing as Interior Minister.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager considered scholars have much text but little substance, now the Wan Shi Jun household does not speak but practices with their bodies, so she made the eldest son Jian Palace Steward, the youngest son Qing Interior Minister.

entries.zh: 萬石君徙居陵裏。
entries.en: The Marquis of Wanshi moved his residence to the Ling quarter.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi moved to reside in Ling quarter.

entries.zh: 內史慶醉歸，入外門不下車。
entries.en: The Interior Minister Qing returned home drunk and entered the outer gate without descending from his carriage.
entries.literal: The Interior Minister Qing returned drunk, entering the outer gate without descending his chariot.

entries.zh: 萬石君聞之，不食。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Wanshi heard of this, he refused to eat.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi heard of it and would not eat.

entries.zh: 慶恐，肉袒請罪，不許。
entries.en: Qing was frightened and bared his shoulders to beg forgiveness, but the Marquis would not accept.
entries.literal: Qing feared, stripped to the waist and apologized for the offense, but was not allowed.

entries.zh: 舉宗及兄建肉袒，萬石君讓曰：「內史貴人，入閭里，里中長老皆走匿，而內史坐車中自如，固當！」
entries.en: The whole clan, together with his elder brother Jian, bared their shoulders. The Marquis of Wanshi rebuked him, saying, "The Interior Minister is an exalted man: when he enters the lane, the elders there all run and hide, while the Interior Minister sits calmly in his carriage. Quite proper!"
entries.literal: The whole clan and his elder brother Jian bared their shoulders. The Marquis of Wanshi rebuked him, saying, "The Interior Minister is a man of rank. When he enters the lane, the elders of the lane all flee and hide, yet the Interior Minister sits at ease in his carriage—as he ought!"

entries.zh: 乃謝罷慶。
entries.en: Only then did he forgive and dismiss Qing.
entries.literal: Then he thanked and dismissed Qing.

entries.zh: 慶及諸子弟入里門，趨至家。
entries.en: From then on, Qing and all the sons and younger brothers would enter the quarter gate and hasten home on foot.
entries.literal: Qing and the various sons and younger brothers entered the quarter gate, hastening home.

entries.zh: 萬石君以元朔五年中卒。
entries.en: The Marquis of Wanshi died in the fifth year of the Yuanshuo era.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi died in the middle of the fifth year of Yuanshuo.

entries.zh: 長子郎中令建哭泣哀思，扶杖乃能行。
entries.en: His eldest son, the Palace Steward Jian, wept so piteously in his grief that he could walk only by leaning on a staff.
entries.literal: The eldest son Palace Steward Jian wept and mourned sorrowfully, supporting a staff he could then walk.

entries.zh: 歲餘，建亦死。
entries.en: A little over a year later, Jian too died.
entries.literal: Over a year later, Jian also died.

entries.zh: 諸子孫咸孝，然建最甚，甚於萬石君。
entries.en: All the sons and grandsons were filial, but Jian was the most extreme of all—surpassing even the Marquis of Wanshi himself.
entries.literal: All the sons and grandsons were filial, but Jian was most extreme, even more than the Marquis of Wan Shi.

entries.zh: 建老白首，萬石君尚無恙。
entries.en: By the time Jian had grown old and white-haired, the Marquis of Wanshi was still in good health.
entries.literal: Jian grew old with white hair, the Marquis of Wan Shi was still without illness.

entries.zh: 建為郎中令，每五日洗沐歸謁親，入子舍，竊問侍者，取親中帬廁牏，身自浣滌，復與侍者，不敢令萬石君知，以為常。
entries.en: While serving as Palace Steward, Jian would return home every five days during his rest period to visit his parents. He would slip into the servants' quarters, secretly ask for his father's undergarments and chamber-pot linings, wash them himself, then return them to the servants—never daring to let the Marquis of Wanshi know. This became his constant practice.
entries.literal: Jian served as Palace Steward, every five days he would wash and bathe then return home to visit his parents, entering the children's quarters, secretly asking the servants, taking the parents' jackets and toilet mats, personally washing and cleaning them, then returning them to the servants, not daring to let the Marquis of Wan Shi know, making it his constant practice.

entries.zh: 建為郎中令，事有可言，屏人恣言，極切；
entries.en: While serving as Palace Steward, when there was something worth saying on state affairs, he would dismiss attendants and speak with utmost frankness and force;
entries.literal: As Palace Steward, when there was something worth saying on state affairs, he would dismiss attendants and speak with unrestrained frankness, extremely pointed;

entries.zh: 至廷見，如不能言者。
entries.en: Yet at court audiences, he appeared as though he could not speak a word.
entries.literal: When reaching court audiences, he was like one unable to speak.

entries.zh: 是以上乃親尊禮之。
entries.en: For this reason, the emperor personally honored him and treated him with the highest respect.
entries.literal: Therefore, the emperor personally honored and ritualized him.

entries.zh: 建為郎中令，書奏事，事下，建讀之，曰：「誤書！
entries.en: While Jian was serving as Palace Steward, memorials on affairs came down to him. He read one and said, "There is an error in the writing!
entries.literal: While serving as Palace Steward, when memorials on affairs came down, Jian read them and said, "An error in the document!

entries.zh: 『馬』者與尾當五，今乃四，不足一。
entries.en: The graph for 'horse' ought to have five strokes in the tail, but here there are only four; one is missing.
entries.literal: The character for 'horse' should have five strokes in the tail; now there are only four—one stroke short.

entries.zh: 上譴死矣！」
entries.en: The emperor will blame me to death!"
entries.literal: The emperor will blame me to death!"

entries.zh: 甚惶恐。
entries.en: He was greatly alarmed and fearful.
entries.literal: He was greatly panicked and fearful.

entries.zh: 其為謹慎，雖他皆如是。
entries.en: Such was his caution—and in all other matters he was just the same.
entries.literal: His being cautious and careful, though others were all like this.

entries.zh: 其明年，上廢太子，誅栗卿之屬。
entries.en: The following year, the emperor deposed the Crown Prince and executed Li Qing and his associates.
entries.literal: The next year, the emperor deposed the crown prince, executed Li Qing and his group.

entries.zh: 上以為綰長者，不忍，乃賜綰告歸，而使郅都治捕栗氏。
entries.en: The emperor regarded Wan as a venerable elder who could not bear such matters, and so granted Wan leave to retire. He then dispatched Zhi Du to arrest the Li clan.
entries.literal: The emperor considered Wan a venerable elder, could not bear it, so granted Wan to announce retirement, and had Zhi Du govern and catch the Li clan.

entries.zh: 既已，上立膠東王為太子，召綰，拜為太子太傅。
entries.en: When this was done, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as Crown Prince, summoned Wan, and appointed him Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Afterward, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince, summoned Wan, appointed him crown prince's Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 久之，遷為御史大夫。
entries.en: After a long while, he was promoted to Imperial Secretary.
entries.literal: After a long time, promoted to Imperial Secretary.

entries.zh: 五歲，代桃侯舍為丞相，朝奏事如職所奏。
entries.en: Five years later, he succeeded She, Marquis of Tao, as Chancellor, and presented memorials at court according to the duties of his office.
entries.literal: After five years, he replaced the Marquis of Tao, She, as Chancellor, presenting memorials at court as the duties of his office required.

entries.zh: 然自初官以至丞相，終無可言。
entries.en: Yet from his first appointment as an official all the way to the chancellorship, he ultimately had nothing worth saying.
entries.literal: Yet from beginning as official until Chancellor, ultimately had nothing to say.

entries.zh: 天子以為敦厚，可相少主，尊寵之，賞賜甚多。
entries.en: The emperor considered him sincere and steadfast, fit to serve as Chancellor for a young ruler, and honored and favored him greatly, bestowing many rewards and gifts.
entries.literal: The emperor considered him sincere and substantial, able to be Chancellor for the young ruler, honored and favored him, rewards and grants very many.

entries.zh: 元鼎五年秋，丞相有罪，罷。
entries.en: In the autumn of the fifth year of the Yuanding era, the Chancellor was found guilty and dismissed.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuanding, the Chancellor had crime, was dismissed.

entries.zh: 制詔御史：「萬石君先帝尊之，子孫孝，其以御史大夫慶為丞相，封為牧丘侯。」
entries.en: The emperor issued an edict to the Imperial Secretary: "The Marquis of Wanshi was honored by the former emperor, and his sons and grandsons are filial. Let the Imperial Secretary Qing become Chancellor, and let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Muqiu."
entries.literal: An imperial edict to the Imperial Secretary: "The Marquis of Wanshi was honored by the former emperor, and his sons and grandsons are filial. Let the Imperial Secretary Qing be made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Muqiu."

entries.zh: 是時漢方南誅兩越，東擊朝鮮，北逐匈奴，西伐大宛，中國多事。
entries.en: At this time, the Han was campaigning against the two Yue kingdoms in the south, striking Chaoxian in the east, pursuing the Xiongnu in the north, and attacking Dayuan in the west. The empire was beset with affairs.
entries.literal: At this time Han was just punishing the two Yue in the south, striking Chaoxian in the east, pursuing the Xiongnu in the north, attacking Dayuan in the west, China had many affairs.

entries.zh: 天子巡狩海內，修上古神祠，封禪，興禮樂。
entries.en: The emperor toured and hunted throughout the realm, restored the ancient divine shrines, performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices, and revived the rites and music.
entries.literal: The emperor toured and hunted within the seas, repaired the ancient god temples, performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices, raised rites and music.

entries.zh: 公家用少，桑弘羊等致利，王溫舒之屬峻法，兒寬等推文學至九卿，更進用事，事不關決於丞相，丞相醇謹而已。
entries.en: The state coffers were running low. Sang Hongyang and his like raised revenue, Wang Wenshu and his sort enforced harsh laws, and Er Kuan and others advanced through scholarship to the rank of the Nine Ministers. Those who handled affairs were the ones promoted, and decisions were no longer referred to the Chancellor. The Chancellor was simply upright and cautious, nothing more.
entries.literal: Public family expenditures were few, Sang Hongyang and others achieved profits, Wang Wenshu and others enforced severe laws, Er Kuan and others promoted literature to reach the Nine Ministers, changing to advance those who handled affairs, affairs not closely decided by the Chancellor, the Chancellor was pure and cautious only.

entries.zh: 在位九歲，無能有所匡言。
entries.en: In nine years in office, he was never able to offer a single word of correction.
entries.literal: In position nine years, unable to have any rectifying words.

entries.zh: 嘗欲請治上近臣所忠、九卿咸宣罪，不能服，反受其過，贖罪。
entries.en: He once sought to have the emperor's close minister Suo Zhong prosecuted and the crimes of the Nine Ministers publicly declared, but could not prevail; instead he himself bore the blame and had to ransom his offense.
entries.literal: He once wished to request prosecution of the emperor's close minister Suo Zhong and public announcement of the crimes of the Nine Ministers, but could not prevail; instead he himself bore the blame and had to ransom his offense.

entries.zh: 元封四年中，關東流民二百萬口，無名數者四十萬，公卿議欲請徙流民於邊以適之。
entries.en: In the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, there were two million displaced refugees east of the passes, with another four hundred thousand unregistered. The ministers debated whether to petition for the refugees to be relocated to the frontier.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, there were two million displaced people east of the passes, with another four hundred thousand unregistered; the ministers debated petitioning to relocate the refugees to the frontier.

entries.zh: 上以為丞相老謹，不能與其議，乃賜丞相告歸，而案御史大夫以下議為請者。
entries.en: The emperor considered the Chancellor old and overly cautious, unable to take part in such deliberations, and so granted the Chancellor leave to retire. He then investigated the Imperial Secretary and those below who had proposed the petition.
entries.literal: The emperor considered the Chancellor old and cautious, could not discuss with him, so granted the Chancellor to announce his retirement, and investigated the Imperial Secretary and below who had discussed and requested this.

entries.zh: 丞相慚不任職，乃上書曰：「慶幸得待罪丞相，罷駑無以輔治，城郭倉庫空虛，民多流亡，罪當伏斧質，上不忍致法。
entries.en: The Chancellor, ashamed that he could not fulfill his duties, submitted a memorial saying, "Qing has had the good fortune to serve as Chancellor while awaiting punishment; I am worn out and incapable of assisting in governance. The walled cities and storehouses are empty, and the people are fleeing in great numbers. My crime deserves execution by axe, yet Your Majesty has been unwilling to apply the law.
entries.literal: The Chancellor, ashamed that he could not bear his duties, submitted a memorial saying, "Qing has had the good fortune to serve as Chancellor while awaiting punishment; I am worn out and incapable of assisting in governance. The walled cities and storehouses are empty, and the people are fleeing in great numbers. My crime deserves execution by axe, yet Your Majesty has been unwilling to apply the law.

entries.zh: 願歸丞相侯印，乞骸骨歸，避賢者路。」
entries.en: I wish to return the Chancellor's seal and my marquisate, beg leave to retire, and make way for worthier men."
entries.literal: I wish to return the Chancellor's seal and the marquisate, beg to retire with my bones, and yield the road to the worthy."

entries.zh: 天子曰：「倉廩既空，民貧流亡，而君欲請徙之，搖蕩不安，動危之，而辭位，君欲安歸難乎？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "The granaries are already empty and the people poor and displaced—yet you wished to petition to relocate them, which would shake and unsettle them and expose them to danger; yet you resign your post—where do you intend to go to escape difficulty?"
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "The granaries are already empty and the people poor and displaced—yet you wished to petition to relocate them, which would shake and unsettle them and expose them to danger; yet you resign your post—where do you intend to go to escape difficulty?"

entries.zh: 以書讓慶，慶甚慚，遂復視事。
entries.en: He rebuked Qing by letter. Qing was deeply ashamed and thereupon resumed his duties.
entries.literal: He rebuked Qing by letter; Qing was very ashamed, then again oversaw affairs.

entries.zh: 武帝立，以為先帝臣，重之。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he regarded Ren as a minister of the former emperor and treated him with great respect.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu ascended, considered him former emperor's minister, honored him.

entries.zh: 仁乃病免，以二千石祿歸老，子孫咸至大官矣。
entries.en: Ren eventually fell ill and was relieved of his duties, retiring on a salary of two thousand bushels. His sons and grandsons all rose to high office.
entries.literal: Ren then fell ill and was dismissed, with two thousand dan salary returned to retire, sons and grandsons all reached high office.

entries.zh: 老病甐，請免。
entries.en: When he grew old and fell ill with dropsy, he requested to be relieved of his duties.
entries.literal: Old and ill with dropsy, requested dismissal.

entries.zh: 於是天子亦策罷，以上大夫祿歸老于家。
entries.en: Thereupon the emperor also issued an edict relieving him of office, and he retired to his home on the salary of a Senior Grand Counselor.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven also issued an edict dismissing him, and he retired home on the salary of a Senior Grand Counselor.

entries.zh: 家於陽陵。
entries.en: He made his home in Yangling.
entries.literal: Made home at Yangling.

entries.zh: 子孫咸至大官矣。
entries.en: His sons and grandsons all rose to high office.
entries.literal: Sons and grandsons all reached high office.

entries.zh: 會陳豨反代，漢七年，高祖往誅之，過趙，趙王張敖自持案進食，禮恭甚，高祖箕踞罵之。
entries.en: It happened that Chen Xi raised a rebellion in the territory of Dai. In the seventh year of the Han dynasty, Emperor Gaozu set out to suppress him and passed through Zhao along the way. King Zhang Ao personally held the serving tray to present food to the emperor, his courtesy exceedingly respectful. But the emperor sat sprawled with his legs apart and berated the king.
entries.literal: It happened that Chen Xi rebelled in Dai; in the seventh year of Han, the High Ancestor went to punish him and passed through Zhao, where the King of Zhao, Zhang Ao, personally held the serving tray to present food, his ritual courtesy being extremely respectful, but the High Ancestor sat with legs spread and berated him.

entries.zh: 是時趙相趙午等數十人皆怒，謂張王曰：「王事上禮備矣，今遇王如是，臣等請為亂。」
entries.en: At this, the state chancellor Zhao Wu and some dozens of other officials were all outraged. They addressed King Zhang Ao: "Your Majesty has served the emperor with every proper courtesy, yet he treats you in this manner. We, your servants, beg leave to rise in revolt."
entries.literal: At that time, Zhao's chancellor Zhao Wu and dozens of others were all furious and said to King Zhang: "Your Majesty has served His Majesty with complete ritual courtesy, yet now he treats you like this; we your servants request permission to cause a disturbance."

entries.zh: 趙王齧指出血，曰：「先人失國，微陛下，臣等當蟲出。
entries.en: The King of Zhao bit his own finger until it bled and said: "Our forefathers lost the kingdom. Were it not for His Majesty, we would be no better than worms crawling from the earth.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao bit his finger until it bled and said: "Our ancestors lost the state; without His Majesty, we your servants would be like worms crawling forth.

entries.zh: 公等柰何言若是！
entries.en: How dare you speak in such a way!
entries.literal: How can you gentlemen speak like this!

entries.zh: 毋復出口矣！」
entries.en: Never let such words leave your lips again!"
entries.literal: Do not let this come from your mouths again!"

entries.zh: 於是貫高等曰：「王長者，不倍德。」
entries.en: At this, Guan Gao and the others said among themselves: "The king is a man of honor who would never repay kindness with treachery."
entries.literal: Thereupon Guan Gao and others said: "The king is a man of virtue and will not betray kindness."

entries.zh: 卒私相與謀弒上。
entries.en: In the end, they secretly plotted among themselves to assassinate the emperor.
entries.literal: In the end they privately conspired together to assassinate the sovereign.

entries.zh: 會事發覺，漢下詔捕趙王及群臣反者。
entries.en: The conspiracy was eventually exposed, and the Han court issued an edict ordering the arrest of the King of Zhao along with all the ministers involved in the plot.
entries.literal: It happened that the affair was discovered, and the Han court issued an edict to arrest the King of Zhao and the rebellious ministers.

entries.zh: 於是趙午等皆自殺，唯貫高就系。
entries.en: Zhao Wu and the other conspirators all took their own lives. Only Guan Gao submitted himself to arrest.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zhao Wu and the others all killed themselves; only Guan Gao submitted to arrest.

entries.zh: 是時漢下詔書：「趙有敢隨王者罪三族。」
entries.en: At that time, the Han court issued a decree: "Any person of Zhao who dares follow the king shall be punished together with all three branches of their clan."
entries.literal: At that time the Han court issued an edict: "Anyone in Zhao who dares follow the king shall have their three clans punished."

entries.zh: 唯孟舒、田叔等十餘人赭衣自髡鉗，稱王家奴，隨趙王敖至長安。
entries.en: Only Meng Shu, Tian Shu, and some ten others donned the red garments of convicts, shaved their heads and clamped iron collars around their own necks. Calling themselves slaves of the royal household, they followed King Ao of Zhao all the way to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Only Meng Shu, Tian Shu, and more than ten others wore prisoner's red garments, shaved their own heads and placed iron collars on themselves, calling themselves slaves of the king's household, and followed King Ao of Zhao to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 貫高事明白，趙王敖得出，廢為宣平侯，乃進言田叔等十餘人。
entries.en: When Guan Gao's testimony cleared the king's name, King Ao of Zhao was released but demoted to the rank of Marquis of Xuanping. He then put forward the names of Tian Shu and more than ten others.
entries.literal: When Guan Gao's affair was made clear, King Ao of Zhao was allowed to go free and was demoted to the Marquis of Xuanping; he then recommended Tian Shu and more than ten others.

entries.zh: 上盡召見，與語，漢廷臣毋能出其右者，上說，盡拜為郡守、諸侯相。
entries.en: The emperor summoned them all for an audience and conversed with each in turn. He found that none of the ministers at the Han court could surpass them in ability. Delighted, the emperor appointed every one of them as either a commandery governor or a chancellor to one of the feudal kings.
entries.literal: The emperor summoned and received them all, and conversed with them; none among the Han court ministers could surpass them. The emperor was pleased and appointed them all as commandery governors or chancellors of feudal kingdoms.

entries.zh: 叔為漢中守十餘年，會高后崩，諸呂作亂，大臣誅之，立孝文帝。
entries.en: Tian Shu served as Governor of Hanzhong for more than ten years. Then Empress Dowager Gao died, and the Lü clan attempted to seize power. The senior ministers suppressed the Lü faction and placed Emperor Wen on the throne.
entries.literal: Shu served as governor of Hanzhong for more than ten years. It happened that Empress Dowager Gao died, the various Lü clan members caused a rebellion, the great ministers executed them, and established Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 孝文帝既立，召田叔問之曰：「公知天下長者乎？」
entries.en: After Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he summoned Tian Shu and asked: "Do you know who the truly worthy men of the realm are?"
entries.literal: After Emperor Xiaowen was established, he summoned Tian Shu and asked him: "Do you know who the men of virtue in the empire are?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣何足以知之！」
entries.en: Tian Shu replied: "How could your humble servant presume to know such a thing!"
entries.literal: He replied: "How could your servant be sufficient to know this!"

entries.zh: 上曰：「公，長者也，宜知之。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "You yourself are a man of worth. Surely you would know."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "You, sir, are a man of virtue yourself, and should know them."

entries.zh: 叔頓首曰：「故雲中守孟舒，長者也。」
entries.en: Tian Shu pressed his forehead to the ground and said: "The former Governor of Yunzhong, Meng Shu—he is truly a man of worth."
entries.literal: Shu bowed his head to the ground and said: "The former governor of Yunzhong, Meng Shu, is a man of virtue."

entries.zh: 是時孟舒坐虜大入塞盜劫，雲中尤甚，免。
entries.en: At that time, Meng Shu had been dismissed from office because barbarian raiders had broken through the frontier defenses on a massive scale, with the Yunzhong commandery suffering the worst of it.
entries.literal: At that time Meng Shu had been dismissed for the crime of barbarians making a great incursion past the frontier to raid and plunder, with Yunzhong being hit especially hard.

entries.zh: 上曰：「先帝置孟舒雲中十餘年矣，虜曾一人，孟舒不能堅守，毋故士卒戰死者數百人。
entries.en: The emperor said: "The late emperor posted Meng Shu at Yunzhong for more than ten years. When the barbarians once raided in force, Meng Shu failed to hold his ground, and several hundred soldiers died in battle without cause.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "The former emperor placed Meng Shu in Yunzhong for more than ten years; when the barbarians once invaded, Meng Shu could not hold the defense, and for no good reason several hundred soldiers died in battle.

entries.zh: 長者固殺人乎？
entries.en: Does a worthy man send people to their deaths like this?
entries.literal: Does a man of virtue truly cause people to be killed?

entries.zh: 公何以言孟舒為長者也？」
entries.en: On what basis do you call Meng Shu a man of worth?"
entries.literal: On what grounds do you say that Meng Shu is a man of virtue?"

entries.zh: 叔叩頭對曰：「是乃孟舒所以為長者也。
entries.en: Tian Shu kowtowed and replied: "This is precisely the reason Meng Shu is a man of worth.
entries.literal: Shu knocked his head on the ground and replied: "This is precisely why Meng Shu is a man of virtue.

entries.zh: 夫貫高等謀反，上下明詔，趙有敢隨張王，罪三族。
entries.en: When Guan Gao and the others plotted their rebellion, the throne issued a clear decree that anyone in Zhao who dared follow King Zhang Ao would be punished along with all three branches of their clan.
entries.literal: When Guan Gao and the others plotted rebellion, a clear edict was issued from above: anyone in Zhao who dared follow King Zhang would have the three clans punished.

entries.zh: 然孟舒自髡鉗，隨張王敖之所在，欲以身死之，豈自知為雲中守哉！
entries.en: Yet Meng Shu shaved his head and clamped an iron collar around his own neck, following King Zhang Ao wherever he went, willing to lay down his life for his lord—how could he have foreseen that he would one day become Governor of Yunzhong!
entries.literal: Yet Meng Shu shaved his own head and put on an iron collar, followed King Zhang Ao wherever he was, willing to die for him with his own body—how could he have known he would become governor of Yunzhong!

entries.zh: 漢與楚相距，士卒罷敝。
entries.en: While Han and Chu were locked in their great struggle, the soldiers had been worn down to exhaustion.
entries.literal: Han and Chu confronted each other, and the soldiers were exhausted and worn out.

entries.zh: 匈奴冒頓新服北夷，來為邊害，孟舒知士卒罷敝，不忍出言，士爭臨城死敵，如子為父，弟為兄，以故死者數百人。
entries.en: The Xiongnu under Modu Chanyu, having recently subjugated the northern tribes, came to raid the frontier. Meng Shu knew his soldiers were utterly spent and could not bring himself to order them out to battle. Yet the men fought of their own accord, mounting the walls and throwing themselves at the enemy as sons would for their fathers and younger brothers for their elders. For this reason several hundred perished.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu under Modu had newly subjugated the northern barbarians and came to harry the borders. Meng Shu knew the soldiers were exhausted and could not bear to drive them out to fight, yet the soldiers vied with one another to mount the walls and fight the enemy to the death, as sons would for fathers and younger brothers for elder brothers, and for this reason several hundred died.

entries.zh: 孟舒豈故驅戰之哉！
entries.en: How could Meng Shu have willfully driven them to fight!
entries.literal: How could Meng Shu have deliberately driven them into battle!

entries.zh: 是乃孟舒所以為長者也。」
entries.en: This is precisely what makes Meng Shu a man of worth."
entries.literal: This is why Meng Shu is a man of virtue."

entries.zh: 於是上曰：「賢哉孟舒！」
entries.en: At this, the emperor exclaimed: "What a worthy man Meng Shu is!"
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor said: "How worthy is Meng Shu!"

entries.zh: 復召孟舒以為雲中守。
entries.en: He summoned Meng Shu back and reappointed him as Governor of Yunzhong.
entries.literal: He recalled Meng Shu and again appointed him as governor of Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 後數歲，叔坐法失官。
entries.en: Several years later, Tian Shu was convicted of a legal offense and stripped of his post.
entries.literal: Several years later, Shu was found guilty of a legal offense and lost his position.

entries.zh: 梁孝王使人殺故吳相袁盎，景帝召田叔案梁，具得其事，還報。
entries.en: King Xiao of Liang sent assassins to murder Yuan Ang, the former chancellor of Wu. Emperor Jing dispatched Tian Shu to investigate the affair in Liang. Tian Shu uncovered all the details and returned to deliver his report.
entries.literal: King Xiao of Liang sent people to assassinate the former chancellor of Wu, Yuan Ang. Emperor Jing summoned Tian Shu to investigate Liang, and he obtained full details of the affair and returned to report.

entries.zh: 景帝曰：「梁有之乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Jing asked: "Is Liang truly responsible?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: "Did Liang do this?"

entries.zh: 叔對曰：「死罪！
entries.en: Tian Shu replied: "I deserve death for what I must say!
entries.literal: Tian Shu replied: "A capital offense to say so!

entries.zh: 有之。」
entries.en: It is true."
entries.literal: It is so."

entries.zh: 上曰：「其事安在？」
entries.en: The emperor asked: "Where is the evidence of the case?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Where is the evidence?"

entries.zh: 田叔曰：「上毋以梁事為也。」
entries.en: Tian Shu said: "Your Majesty must not pursue the matter of Liang any further."
entries.literal: Tian Shu said: "Your Majesty should not pursue the Liang matter."

entries.zh: 上曰：「何也？」
entries.en: The emperor asked: "Why not?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Why?"

entries.zh: 曰：「今梁王不伏誅，是漢法不行也；
entries.en: He replied: "If the King of Liang is not brought to justice, it means the laws of the Han dynasty hold no authority.
entries.literal: He said: "If the King of Liang is not put to death, then Han law is not being carried out;

entries.zh: 如其伏法，而太后食不甘味，臥不安席，此憂在陛下也。」
entries.en: But should he be made to face the law, the Empress Dowager will find no pleasure in her meals and no rest in her bed—and that burden will fall squarely upon Your Majesty."
entries.literal: But if he submits to the law, then the Empress Dowager will find no flavor in her food and no comfort in her bed—this worry would rest upon Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 景帝大賢之，以為魯相。
entries.en: Emperor Jing was deeply impressed by his wisdom and appointed him as the Chancellor of Lu.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing greatly esteemed him as worthy and appointed him as chancellor of Lu.

entries.zh: 其後有詔募擇衛將軍舍人以為郎，將軍取舍人中富給者，令具鞌馬絳衣玉具劍，欲入奏之。
entries.en: Later, an imperial edict was issued to recruit and select retainers of the General of the Guard for appointment as Gentlemen at court. The general chose the wealthiest among his retainers and ordered them to furnish themselves with saddled horses, crimson robes, and jade-hilted swords, intending to present them before the emperor.
entries.literal: Afterwards there was an imperial edict to recruit and select retainers of the General of the Guard to serve as gentlemen at court. The general chose the wealthy and well-provisioned among his retainers, ordering them to prepare saddled horses, crimson robes, and jade-handled swords, intending to present them to the emperor.

entries.zh: 會賢大夫少府趙禹來過衛將軍，將軍呼所舉舍人以示趙禹。
entries.en: It happened that the esteemed official Zhao Yu, who served as Privy Treasurer, paid a visit to the General of the Guard. The general summoned the retainers he had selected and presented them for Zhao Yu's inspection.
entries.literal: It happened that the worthy senior official Zhao Yu, the Privy Treasurer, came to visit the General of the Guard. The general called forth the retainers he had selected to show them to Zhao Yu.

entries.zh: 趙禹以次問之，十餘人無一人習事有智略者。
entries.en: Zhao Yu questioned them one by one, and among the ten or more candidates, not a single one showed any experience in administration or possessed any measure of wit and strategic ability.
entries.literal: Zhao Yu questioned them one by one, and among the ten or more men, not a single one was experienced in affairs or possessed wisdom and strategic ability.

entries.zh: 趙禹曰：「吾聞之，將門之下必有將類。
entries.en: Zhao Yu said: "I have always heard it said that under the roof of a great general, one is sure to find men of a general's caliber.
entries.literal: Zhao Yu said: "I have heard that beneath the gates of a general, there must be men of a general's caliber.

entries.zh: 傳曰『不知其君視其所使，不知其子視其所友』。
entries.en: As the saying goes, 'To know a lord, observe whom he employs; to know a son, observe whom he befriends.'
entries.literal: The tradition says, 'If you do not know a lord, look at whom he employs; if you do not know a son, look at who his friends are.'

entries.zh: 今有詔舉將軍舍人者，欲以觀將軍而能得賢者文武之士也。
entries.en: The purpose of this edict to select retainers from the general's household is to evaluate the general himself—to see whether he has the ability to identify worthy men of both civil and military talent.
entries.literal: Now there is an edict to select retainers of the general, the purpose being to observe the general and see whether he can identify worthy men of both civil and military ability.

entries.zh: 今徒取盎人子上之，又無智略，如木偶人衣之綺繡耳，將柰之何？」
entries.en: Yet you have merely picked the sons of the wealthy to put forward, and they lack any wit or strategic ability—they are nothing more than wooden puppets dressed in fine silk. What purpose will they serve?"
entries.literal: Now you have merely taken the sons of wealthy men and put them forward, yet they lack wisdom and strategy—they are like wooden puppets dressed in fine silks. What good will this do?"

entries.zh: 於是趙禹悉召衛將軍舍人百餘人，以次問之，得田仁、任安，曰：「獨此兩人可耳，餘無可用者。」
entries.en: Zhao Yu then summoned all the general's retainers—over a hundred—and questioned them one after another. He singled out Tian Ren and Ren An, declaring: "Only these two are fit for service. The rest are of no use whatsoever."
entries.literal: Thereupon Zhao Yu summoned all of the General of the Guard's retainers, over a hundred of them, and questioned them one by one. He identified Tian Ren and Ren An, saying: "Only these two will do; the rest are of no use."

entries.zh: 衛將軍見此兩人貧，意不平。
entries.en: The General of the Guard, seeing how poor the two men were, was not at all pleased.
entries.literal: When the General of the Guard saw that these two men were poor, he was displeased.

entries.zh: 趙禹去，謂兩人曰：「各自具樾象絳衣。」
entries.en: After Zhao Yu departed, the general told the two men: "Each of you must furnish your own saddled horses and crimson robes yourselves."
entries.literal: After Zhao Yu left, the general told the two men: "Each of you must prepare your own saddled horses and crimson robes at your own expense."

entries.zh: 兩人對曰：「家貧無用具也。」
entries.en: The two men replied: "Our families are too poor. We have no means to provide such equipment."
entries.literal: The two men replied: "Our families are poor, and we have no means to furnish such things."

entries.zh: 將軍怒曰：「今兩君家自為貧，何為出此言？
entries.en: The general said angrily: "So your families are poor—why then do you speak like this?
entries.literal: The general said angrily: "If your families are truly poor, why do you speak such words?

entries.zh: 鞅鞅如有移德於我者，何也？」
entries.en: You carry yourselves with such resentment, as though I owed you some debt of gratitude you had earned—why is that?"
entries.literal: You act resentful, as though you had bestowed some favor on me that I have failed to repay—why is that?"

entries.zh: 將軍不得已，上籍以聞。
entries.en: With no other option, the general submitted their names to the throne for consideration.
entries.literal: The general had no choice but to submit their names on the register for the emperor to hear of.

entries.zh: 有詔召見衛將軍舍人，此二人前見，詔問能略相推第也。
entries.en: An imperial edict summoned the General of the Guard's retainers for an audience. The two men stepped forward, and the emperor commanded them to assess and rank each other's abilities.
entries.literal: An edict was issued to summon the General of the Guard's retainers for an audience. These two came forward, and by imperial command were asked to evaluate and rank each other's abilities.

entries.zh: 田仁對曰；
entries.en: Tian Ren answered:
entries.literal: Tian Ren replied:

entries.zh: 「提桴鼓立軍門，使士大夫樂死戰鬬，仁不及任安。」
entries.en: "When it comes to taking up the drumstick at the camp gate and inspiring officers and soldiers to fight gladly to the death—in this, I am no match for Ren An."
entries.literal: "In taking up the drumstick to beat the war drum, standing at the gate of the camp, and inspiring officers and soldiers to gladly fight to the death—I, Ren, am no match for Ren An."

entries.zh: 任安對曰：「夫決嫌疑，定是非，辯治官，使百姓無怨心，安不及仁也。」
entries.en: Ren An replied: "When it comes to resolving doubts, determining right from wrong, evaluating the competence of officials, and ensuring that the common people harbor no resentment—in these things, I am no match for Tian Ren."
entries.literal: Ren An replied: "In resolving doubts and suspicions, determining right and wrong, discerning the governance of officials, and ensuring the people harbor no resentment—I, An, am no match for Tian Ren."

entries.zh: 武帝大笑曰：「善。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu laughed heartily and said: "Well spoken."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu laughed greatly and said: "Excellent."

entries.zh: 使任安護北軍，使田仁護邊田穀於河上。
entries.en: He assigned Ren An to oversee the Northern Army, and dispatched Tian Ren to supervise the frontier agricultural colonies along the Yellow River.
entries.literal: He sent Ren An to oversee the Northern Army, and sent Tian Ren to oversee the border agricultural colonies along the Yellow River.

entries.zh: 此兩人立名天下。
entries.en: Through these appointments, both men made their names known throughout the empire.
entries.literal: These two men established their reputations throughout the empire.

entries.zh: 其後逢太子有兵事，丞相自將兵，使司直主城門。
entries.en: Later, the crisis came when the Crown Prince took up arms. The Chancellor personally led troops and ordered the Director of Justice to take charge of guarding the city gates.
entries.literal: Afterwards it happened that the Crown Prince was involved in a military affair. The Chancellor personally led troops and ordered the Director of Justice to take charge of the city gates.

entries.zh: 司直以為太子骨肉之親，父子之閒不甚欲近，去之諸陵過。
entries.en: The Director of Justice felt that since the Crown Prince was the emperor's own flesh and blood, this was a dispute between father and son that he had no wish to be drawn into. He left his post and detoured past the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: The Director of Justice considered that since the Crown Prince was of the emperor's own flesh and blood, and the matter between father and son was not something he greatly wished to involve himself in, he departed and passed by the imperial tombs.

entries.zh: 是時武帝在甘泉，使御史大夫暴君下責丞相「何為縱太子」，丞相對言「使司直部守城門而開太子」。
entries.en: At the time, Emperor Wu was at the Ganquan Palace. He dispatched Grand Censor Bao Shengzhi to reprimand the Chancellor: "Why did you allow the Crown Prince to escape?" The Chancellor replied in his defense: "I assigned the Director of Justice to guard the city gates, but he opened them and let the Crown Prince through."
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was at Ganquan. He sent Grand Censor Bao Shengzhi down to reprimand the Chancellor: "Why did you let the Crown Prince escape?" The Chancellor replied: "I ordered the Director of Justice to guard the city gates, but he opened them for the Crown Prince."

entries.zh: 上書以聞，請捕系司直。
entries.en: A memorial was submitted to the emperor requesting the arrest and imprisonment of the Director of Justice.
entries.literal: A memorial was submitted to bring the matter to the emperor's attention, requesting the arrest and imprisonment of the Director of Justice.

entries.zh: 司直下吏，誅死。
entries.en: The Director of Justice was handed over to the judicial officials and put to death.
entries.literal: The Director of Justice was handed over to officials and executed.

entries.zh: 是時任安為北軍使者護軍，太子立車北軍南門外，召任安，與節令發兵。
entries.en: At that time, Ren An was serving as the Protector General dispatched to the Northern Army. The Crown Prince halted his carriage outside the south gate of the Northern Army camp, summoned Ren An, and presented him with an imperial tally ordering him to mobilize the troops.
entries.literal: At that time Ren An was serving as the Protector General dispatched to the Northern Army. The Crown Prince stopped his carriage outside the south gate of the Northern Army camp, summoned Ren An, and gave him a tally commanding him to mobilize troops.

entries.zh: 安拜受節，入，閉門不出。
entries.en: Ren An bowed and accepted the tally, then entered the camp, shut the gates behind him, and did not come out.
entries.literal: An bowed and accepted the tally, entered the camp, closed the gates, and did not come out.

entries.zh: 武帝聞之，以為任安為詳邪，不傅事，何也？
entries.en: When Emperor Wu heard of this, he suspected Ren An of feigning loyalty: the man had accepted the tally yet taken no action and reported nothing to the throne—why?
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu heard of this, he thought Ren An had been feigning righteousness and had not reported the matter—why?

entries.zh: 任安笞辱北軍錢官小吏，小吏上書言之，以為受太子節，言「幸與我其鮮好者」。
entries.en: Ren An had previously flogged and humiliated a minor financial clerk of the Northern Army. The aggrieved clerk submitted a memorial denouncing him, testifying that Ren An had accepted the Crown Prince's tally and had demanded to be given "the freshest and finest goods."
entries.literal: Ren An had flogged and humiliated a minor financial official of the Northern Army. The minor official submitted a memorial reporting this, saying that An had accepted the Crown Prince's tally and had said, "Please give me the freshest and finest goods."

entries.zh: 書上聞，武帝曰：「是老吏也，見兵事起，欲坐觀成敗，見勝者欲合從之，有兩心。
entries.en: When the memorial came to the emperor's attention, Emperor Wu declared: "He is a wily old official. When the fighting broke out, he wanted to sit back and watch how things unfolded, intending to side with whichever faction won. He harbors a divided heart.
entries.literal: When the memorial reached the emperor's ears, Emperor Wu said: "This is an old and cunning official. When the military conflict arose, he wanted to sit and watch the outcome, intending to join whichever side prevailed. He harbors divided loyalties.

entries.zh: 安有當死之罪甚眾，吾常活之，今懷詐，有不忠之心。」
