entries.en: Ren An has committed many offenses deserving death, yet I have always spared his life. Now he harbors treachery in his breast and is disloyal at heart."
entries.literal: An has accumulated many crimes deserving of death, yet I have always spared his life. Now he harbors deceit and has a disloyal heart."

entries.zh: 下安吏，誅死。
entries.en: Ren An was handed over to the judicial officials and put to death.
entries.literal: An was handed over to officials and executed.

entries.zh: 夫月滿則虧，物盛則衰，天地之常也。
entries.en: When the moon reaches fullness, it begins to wane; when things reach their zenith, they begin to decline. Such is the immutable law of heaven and earth.
entries.literal: When the moon is full it wanes; when things reach their peak they decline—this is the constant way of heaven and earth.

entries.zh: 知進而不知退，久乘富貴，禍積為祟。
entries.en: Those who know only how to advance and never how to retreat, who cling to wealth and honor too long, find that their misfortunes pile up until disaster strikes.
entries.literal: Knowing how to advance but not how to retreat, riding wealth and honor for too long—calamity accumulates and becomes a curse.

entries.zh: 故范蠡之去越，辭不受官位，名傳後世，萬歲不忘，豈可及哉！
entries.en: Thus, did Fan Li, when he departed from Yue and refused all titles and offices, leave a name that would be passed down through the ages, unforgotten for ten thousand years. Who could ever rival such a man!
entries.literal: Thus, Fan Li's departure from Yue—declining office and refusing rank—caused his name to be transmitted to later generations, never forgotten for ten thousand years. How can anyone match him!

entries.zh: 後進者慎戒之。
entries.en: Let those who come after take heed and learn from this lesson.
entries.literal: Those who come after should take careful warning from this.

entries.zh: 田仁上書言：「天下郡太守多為姦利，三河尤甚，臣請先刺舉三河。
entries.en: Tian Ren submitted a memorial to the throne: "Many commandery governors throughout the empire engage in corruption for personal gain, and the Three Rivers region is the worst offender. I request permission to begin by investigating and impeaching the officials of the Three Rivers.
entries.literal: Tian Ren submitted a memorial saying: "Many commandery governors throughout the empire engage in corrupt profiteering, and the Three Rivers region is the worst. I request permission to investigate and impeach the Three Rivers first.

entries.zh: 三河太守皆內倚中貴人，與三公有親屬，無所畏憚，宜先正三河以警天下姦吏。」
entries.en: The governors of the Three Rivers all rely on the backing of powerful palace favorites and are related by kinship to the Three Excellencies. They know no fear. We should first set the Three Rivers right as a warning to corrupt officials across the empire."
entries.literal: The governors of the Three Rivers all rely internally on powerful court favorites and are related to the Three Excellencies; they fear nothing. We should first rectify the Three Rivers to serve as a warning to corrupt officials throughout the empire."

entries.zh: 是時河南、河內太守皆御史大夫杜父兄子弟也，河東太守石丞相子孫也。
entries.en: At that time, the governors of Henan and Henei were all kinsmen—fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews—of Grand Censor Du, and the Governor of Hedong was a descendant of the former Chancellor Shi.
entries.literal: At that time, the governors of Henan and Henei were all fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews of Grand Censor Du, and the governor of Hedong was a descendant of Chancellor Shi.

entries.zh: 是時石氏九人為二千石，方盛貴。
entries.en: At that time, nine members of the Shi clan held offices at the two-thousand-bushel rank, and the family was at the very peak of its power and prestige.
entries.literal: At that time, nine members of the Shi clan held positions at the two-thousand-bushel rank, and the family was at the height of its power and prestige.

entries.zh: 田仁數上書言之。
entries.en: Tian Ren submitted memorial after memorial pressing the case.
entries.literal: Tian Ren repeatedly submitted memorials speaking of this matter.

entries.zh: 杜大夫及石氏使人謝，謂田少卿曰：「吾非敢有語言也，願少卿無相誣汙也。」
entries.en: Grand Censor Du and the Shi clan sent intermediaries to plead with him, telling Tian Ren: "We would not dare utter a word against you. We only hope that you will not level false accusations against us."
entries.literal: Grand Censor Du and the Shi clan sent people to make apologies, telling Tian Shaoqing: "We would not dare say anything against you; we only hope that you, Shaoqing, will not falsely accuse and defame us."

entries.zh: 仁已刺三河，三河太守皆下吏誅死。
entries.en: Tian Ren carried out his investigation of the Three Rivers, and all three governors were handed over to the judicial officials and put to death.
entries.literal: Ren investigated the Three Rivers, and all three governors were handed over to officials and executed.

entries.zh: 仁還奏事，武帝說，以仁為能不畏彊御，拜仁為丞相司直，威振天下。
entries.en: Tian Ren returned and delivered his report. Emperor Wu was delighted, judging Tian Ren to be a man who feared no authority however powerful. He appointed him as the Chancellor's Director of Justice, and his renown shook the entire empire.
entries.literal: Ren returned and reported on the matter. Emperor Wu was pleased, considered Ren capable and unafraid of the powerful, and appointed him as the Chancellor's Director of Justice; his authority shook the empire.

entries.zh: 田叔者，趙陘城人也。
entries.en: Tian Shu was a native of Xingcheng in the state of Zhao.
entries.literal: Tian Shu was a person from Xingcheng in Zhao.

entries.zh: 其先，齊田氏苗裔也。
entries.en: His forebears were descendants of the Tian clan of the state of Qi.
entries.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Tian clan of Qi.

entries.zh: 叔喜劍，學黃老術於樂巨公所。
entries.en: Tian Shu delighted in swordsmanship and studied the teachings of Huang-Lao philosophy under the master Yue Jugong.
entries.literal: Shu enjoyed swordsmanship, and studied the arts of Huang-Lao at the place of Yue Jugong.

entries.zh: 叔為人刻廉自喜，喜游諸公。
entries.en: By nature, Tian Shu was rigorously principled and incorruptible, taking pride in these qualities, and he enjoyed keeping company with distinguished men.
entries.literal: Shu as a person was strict, incorruptible, and self-possessed, and enjoyed associating with various notables.

entries.zh: 趙人舉之趙相趙午，午言之趙王張敖所，趙王以為郎中。
entries.en: The people of Zhao recommended him to the state chancellor Zhao Wu, who in turn spoke of him to King Zhang Ao of Zhao. The king appointed him as a Gentleman of the Palace.
entries.literal: People of Zhao recommended him to Zhao's chancellor Zhao Wu, and Wu spoke of him to the King of Zhao, Zhang Ao, and the King of Zhao appointed him as a court gentleman.

entries.zh: 數歲，切直廉平，趙王賢之，未及遷。
entries.en: Over the course of several years, Tian Shu proved himself forthright, incorruptible, and even-handed. The King of Zhao esteemed him as a man of worth, though he had not yet found occasion to promote him.
entries.literal: After several years, being earnest, upright, incorruptible, and fair, the King of Zhao regarded him as worthy, but had not yet promoted him.

entries.zh: 御史大夫韓安國者，梁成安人也，後徙睢陽。
entries.en: The Grand Censor Han Anguo was a native of Cheng'an in the kingdom of Liang, and later moved to Suiyang.
entries.literal: Imperial censor Han Anguo, Liang Cheng'an person, later moved Suiyang.

entries.zh: 嘗受韓子、雜家說於騶田生所。
entries.en: He once studied the writings of Han Feizi and the teachings of the Eclectic School under Master Zou Tian.
entries.literal: Once received Hanzi, miscellaneous learning from Zou Tiansheng place.

entries.zh: 事梁孝王為中大夫。
entries.en: He served King Xiao of Liang as a Palace Grandee.
entries.literal: Served Liang Xiao wang as central grand master.

entries.zh: 吳楚反時，孝王使安國及張羽為將，捍吳兵於東界。
entries.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, King Xiao dispatched Anguo and Zhang Yu as generals to defend the eastern border against the forces of Wu.
entries.literal: Wu Chu rebellion time, Xiao wang sent Anguo and Zhang Yu as generals, defended Wu troops at eastern border.

entries.zh: 張羽力戰，安國持重，以故吳不能過梁。
entries.en: Zhang Yu fought with fierce determination while Anguo held a steady defensive position, and so the armies of Wu were unable to advance past Liang.
entries.literal: Zhang Yu vigorously fought, Anguo held steady, therefore Wu could not pass Liang.

entries.zh: 吳楚已破，安國、張羽名由此顯。
entries.en: After Wu and Chu were defeated, the names of Anguo and Zhang Yu became renowned throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Wu Chu already broken, Anguo, Zhang Yu fame from this prominent.

entries.zh: 梁孝王，景帝母弟，竇太后愛之，令得自請置相、二千石，出入游戲，僭於天子。
entries.en: King Xiao of Liang was Emperor Jing's younger brother by the same mother. Empress Dowager Dou doted on him, allowing him to appoint his own chancellor and officials of two-thousand-shi rank, to come and go at his pleasure, and to adopt ceremonies that exceeded those appropriate for anyone but the Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Liang Xiao wang, Emperor Jing younger brother, Empress Dowager Dou loved him, ordered got self request appoint chancellor, two thousand shi, enter leave play games, exceeded emperor.

entries.zh: 天子聞之，心弗善也。
entries.en: When the Emperor heard of this, he was displeased.
entries.literal: Emperor heard it, heart not good.

entries.zh: 太后知帝不善，乃怒梁使者，弗見，案責王所為。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager learned of the Emperor's displeasure, she turned her anger upon the envoys from Liang, refusing to grant them audience and instead investigating and censuring the king's conduct.
entries.literal: Empress dowager knew emperor not good, then angered Liang envoys, not saw, examined blamed wang conduct.

entries.zh: 韓安國為梁使，見大長公主而泣曰：「何梁王為人子之孝，為人臣之忠，太后曾弗省也？
entries.en: Han Anguo, as envoy of Liang, went to see the Grand Princess and wept, saying, "How can it be that the King of Liang's filial piety as a son and loyalty as a minister have never won the Empress Dowager's regard?
entries.literal: Han Anguo as Liang envoy, saw Grand Princess and wept, saying: "How can it be that the King of Liang's filial piety as a son and loyalty as a minister have never won the Empress Dowager's regard?

entries.zh: 夫前日吳、楚、齊、趙七國反時，自關以東皆合從西鄉，惟梁最親為艱難。
entries.en: In the past, when the Seven Kingdoms of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao rebelled, all the lands east of the passes united and marched westward, yet it was Liang alone—the kingdom closest to the throne—that bore the hardest fighting.
entries.literal: Because previous Wu, Chu, Qi, Zhao seven kingdoms rebellion time, from pass eastward all united following west direction, only Liang most intimate for difficulties.

entries.zh: 梁王念太后、帝在中，而諸侯擾亂，一言泣數行下，跪送臣等六人，將兵擊卻吳楚，吳楚以故兵不敢西，而卒破亡，梁王之力也。
entries.en: The King of Liang, mindful that the Empress Dowager and the Emperor stood at the center while the feudal lords threw the realm into chaos, wept with every word he spoke, tears streaming down his face. He knelt and sent off six of us as generals, who led troops to drive back Wu and Chu. Because of this, the armies of Wu and Chu dared not advance westward and were ultimately destroyed—all through the efforts of the King of Liang.
entries.literal: Liang wang thought empress dowager, emperor in center, but feudal lords disturbance chaos, one word wept several rows down, knelt sent us six people, led troops repelled Wu Chu, Wu Chu therefore troops not dared west, and finally broken perished, Liang wang effort.

entries.zh: 今太后以小睗苛禮責望梁王。
entries.en: Now the Empress Dowager, on account of minor suspicions and rigid protocols, censures and finds fault with the King of Liang.
entries.literal: Now empress dowager with small suspicion harsh etiquette blamed expected Liang wang.

entries.zh: 梁王父兄皆帝王，所見者大，故出稱蹕，入言警，車旗皆帝所賜也，即欲以侘鄙縣，驅馳國中，以夸諸侯，令天下盡知太后、帝愛之也。
entries.en: The King of Liang's father and brothers were all emperors, so naturally his vision is grand. When he goes abroad he calls for the roads to be cleared, and when he returns he commands the imperial alert—but his carriages and banners were all bestowed upon him by the Emperor himself. He merely wished to display them through the humble counties and ride throughout his kingdom, to impress the feudal lords and let all under heaven know that the Empress Dowager and the Emperor loved him.
entries.literal: Liang wang father brothers all emperors, what saw great, therefore out used imperial way, enter spoke imperial alert, carriages banners all emperor granted, immediately wanted with lowly county, drive in country, to boast feudal lords, make realm all know empress dowager, emperor loved him.

entries.zh: 今梁使來，輒案責之。
entries.en: Yet now, whenever envoys arrive from Liang, they are immediately subjected to interrogation and blame.
entries.literal: Now Liang envoys come, immediately examined blamed them.

entries.zh: 梁王恐，日夜涕泣思慕，不知所為。
entries.en: The King of Liang is terrified, weeping day and night with longing, not knowing what to do.
entries.literal: Liang wang feared, day night wept thought longed, not knew what to do.

entries.zh: 何梁王之為子孝，為臣忠，而太后弗恤也？」
entries.en: How can the King of Liang be so filial as a son and so loyal as a minister, yet the Empress Dowager show him no compassion?"
entries.literal: How Liang King's conduct as son filial, as minister loyal, yet Empress Dowager not show compassion?"

entries.zh: 大長公主具以告太后，太后喜曰：「為言之帝。」
entries.en: The Grand Princess told the Empress Dowager everything. The Empress Dowager was pleased and said, "Speak of this to the Emperor."
entries.literal: Grand Princess fully reported to Empress Dowager; Empress Dowager pleased, said: "Speak of this to the Emperor."

entries.zh: 言之，帝心乃解，而免冠謝太后曰：「兄弟不能相教，乃為太后遺憂。」
entries.en: When she did so, the Emperor's mind was eased. He removed his cap and apologized to the Empress Dowager, saying, "We brothers could not instruct one another, and thus caused Your Majesty sorrow."
entries.literal: When she spoke of it, Emperor's mind then eased; he removed cap and apologized to Empress Dowager, saying: "We brothers could not instruct one another, and thus caused Your Majesty sorrow."

entries.zh: 悉見梁使，厚賜之。
entries.en: He received all the envoys from Liang and bestowed generous gifts upon them.
entries.literal: All saw Liang envoys, thickly granted them.

entries.zh: 其後梁王益親驩。
entries.en: After this, the King of Liang enjoyed even closer and warmer relations with the court.
entries.literal: Its after Liang wang increasingly intimate close.

entries.zh: 太后、長公主更賜安國可直千餘金。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager and the Grand Princess in turn rewarded Anguo with gifts worth over a thousand pieces of gold.
entries.literal: Empress dowager, grand princess moreover granted Anguo value thousand remainder gold.

entries.zh: 名由此顯，結於漢。
entries.en: His name became illustrious from this, and he forged ties with the Han court.
entries.literal: Name from this prominent, attached to Han.

entries.zh: 公孫詭、羊勝說孝王求為帝太子及益地事，恐漢大臣不聽，乃陰使人刺漢用事謀臣。
entries.en: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng persuaded King Xiao to seek designation as the Emperor's heir apparent and to petition for additional territory. Fearing that the great ministers of Han would not comply, they secretly sent assassins to murder the influential advisors at the Han court.
entries.literal: Gongsun Gui, Yang Sheng persuaded Xiao wang seek be emperor crown prince and increase territory matters, feared Han great ministers not listen, then secretly sent people assassinated Han in power plotting ministers.

entries.zh: 及殺故吳相袁盎，景帝遂聞詭、勝等計畫，乃遣使捕詭、勝，必得。
entries.en: When they murdered Yuan Ang, the former Chancellor of Wu, Emperor Jing at last learned of the plots of Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng. He dispatched envoys to arrest them, with orders that they must be captured.
entries.literal: And killed former Wu chancellor Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing then heard Gui, Sheng etc. plans, then sent envoys arrest Gui, Sheng, must obtain.

entries.zh: 漢使十輩至梁，相以下舉國大索，月餘不得。
entries.en: Ten groups of Han envoys arrived in Liang, and the Chancellor and all officials below him mobilized the entire kingdom in a great search, but after more than a month they could not find them.
entries.literal: Han sent ten groups to Liang, chancellor below mobilized whole country great search, month remainder not obtained.

entries.zh: 內史安國聞詭、勝匿孝王所，安國入見王而泣曰：「主辱臣死。
entries.en: Prefect Anguo learned that Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng were hidden at King Xiao's residence. Anguo entered to see the king and wept, saying, "When the lord is disgraced, his minister must die.
entries.literal: Prefect Anguo heard Gui and Sheng were hidden at King Xiao's place; Anguo entered to see the king and wept, saying: "When the lord is disgraced, his minister must die.

entries.zh: 大王無良臣，故事紛紛至此。
entries.en: Your Majesty has no worthy ministers, and so affairs have descended into this chaos.
entries.literal: Great wang without good ministers, therefore matters confused to this.

entries.zh: 今詭、勝不得，請辭賜死。」
entries.en: Since Gui and Sheng cannot be captured, I ask to withdraw and receive death."
entries.literal: Since Gui and Sheng cannot be captured, I beg to resign and accept death."

entries.zh: 王曰：「何至此？」
entries.en: The king said, "How has it come to this?"
entries.literal: The king said: "How has it come to this?"

entries.zh: 安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與太上皇之與高皇帝及皇帝之與臨江王親？」
entries.en: Anguo wept, his tears streaming down several lines, and said, "Your Majesty, compare for yourself your closeness to the Emperor—which is greater, the relation between the Grand Emperor Father and Emperor Gaozu, or that between the Emperor and the King of Linjiang?"
entries.literal: Anguo wept, tears streaming down several lines, and said: "Your Majesty, compare for yourself your closeness to the Emperor—which is greater, the relation between the Grand Emperor Father and Emperor Gaozu, or that between the Emperor and the King of Linjiang?"

entries.zh: 孝王曰：「弗如也。」
entries.en: King Xiao said, "It does not compare."
entries.literal: King Xiao said: "It does not compare."

entries.zh: 安國曰：「夫太上、臨江親父子之閒，然而高帝曰『提三尺劍取天下者朕也』，故太上皇終不得制事，居于櫟陽。
entries.en: Anguo said, "The Grand Emperor Father and the King of Linjiang both stood within the closest bonds of father and son. Yet Emperor Gaozu said, 'It was I who took the empire with a three-foot sword,' and so the Grand Emperor Father in the end could not direct affairs, but lived at Liyang.
entries.literal: Anguo said: "Between the Grand Emperor Father and the King of Linjiang there was the closest bond of father and son, yet Emperor Gaozu said, 'It is I who took the empire with a three-foot sword,' so the Grand Emperor Father in the end could not control affairs and lived at Liyang.

entries.zh: 臨江王，適長太子也，以一言過，廢王臨江；
entries.en: The King of Linjiang was the legitimate eldest crown prince, yet because of a single verbal fault he was deposed and made King of Linjiang;
entries.literal: The King of Linjiang was the legitimate eldest heir apparent; for one slip of the tongue he was deposed and made King of Linjiang;

entries.zh: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。
entries.en: On account of the incident at the palace walls, he ended by taking his own life in the Commandant's office.
entries.literal: Used palace wall matter, finally suicide in commandants office.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 治天下終不以私亂公。
entries.en: In governing the realm, he never allowed private interests to disrupt public affairs.
entries.literal: Governing realm finally not with private confuse public.

entries.zh: 語曰：『雖有親父，安知其不為虎？
entries.en: The saying goes, 'Even with a close father, who can be sure he will not become a tiger?
entries.literal: The saying goes: 'Even with a close father, who can be sure he will not become a tiger?

entries.zh: 雖有親兄，安知其不為狼？』
entries.en: Even with a close elder brother, who can know that he will not become a wolf?'
entries.literal: Even with a close elder brother, who can be sure he will not become a wolf?'

entries.zh: 今大王列在諸侯，悅一邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty ranks among the feudal lords, yet you have delighted in the reckless counsel of a treacherous minister, violated the Emperor's prohibitions, and subverted the clear laws.
entries.literal: Now great wang ranked among feudal lords, pleased one wicked minister empty talk, violated emperor prohibition, bent clear law.

entries.zh: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於王。
entries.en: The Emperor, out of regard for the Empress Dowager, cannot bring himself to enforce the law against the king.
entries.literal: Emperor because empress dowager reason, not bear apply law to wang.

entries.zh: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，而大王終不覺寤。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager weeps day and night, hoping that Your Majesty will reform on your own, yet Your Majesty never comes to his senses.
entries.literal: Empress dowager day night wept, hoped great wang self change, but great wang finally not aware enlightened.

entries.zh: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？」
entries.en: If the Empress Dowager's palace carriage should depart on its final journey, whom would Your Majesty still have to cling to?"
entries.literal: If the Empress Dowager's carriage should set out on its final journey, whom will Your Majesty still have to rely upon?"

entries.zh: 語未卒，孝王泣數行下，謝安國曰：「吾今出詭、勝。」
entries.en: Before Anguo had finished speaking, King Xiao wept, tears streaming down several lines, and apologized to Anguo, saying, "I will now hand over Gui and Sheng."
entries.literal: Before Anguo had finished speaking, King Xiao wept, tears streaming down several lines, and apologized to Anguo, saying: "I will now hand over Gui and Sheng."

entries.zh: 詭、勝自殺。
entries.en: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng took their own lives.
entries.literal: Gui, Sheng suicide.

entries.zh: 漢使還報，梁事皆得釋，安國之力也。
entries.en: When the Han envoys returned with their report, all charges against Liang were dropped—this was entirely through Anguo's efforts.
entries.literal: Han envoys returned report, Liang matters all got released, Anguo effort.

entries.zh: 於是景帝、太后益重安國。
entries.en: From then on, Emperor Jing and the Empress Dowager valued Anguo even more highly.
entries.literal: Thereupon Emperor Jing, empress dowager increasingly valued Anguo.

entries.zh: 孝王卒，共王即位，安國坐法失官，居家。
entries.en: When King Xiao died and King Gong succeeded him, Anguo was convicted of an offense and stripped of his position, retiring to his home.
entries.literal: Xiao wang died, Gong wang ascended throne, Anguo sat law lost office, resided home.

entries.zh: 梁內史之缺也，孝王新得齊人公孫詭，說之，欲請以為內史。
entries.en: When the position of Prefect fell vacant, King Xiao had recently taken a liking to Gongsun Gui, a man from Qi who had won the king's favor through persuasive counsel, and wished to request his appointment as Prefect.
entries.literal: Liang internal affairs vacancy, Xiao wang newly got Qi person Gongsun Gui, persuaded him, wanted request appoint as internal affairs.

entries.zh: 竇太后聞，乃詔王以安國為內史。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Dou heard of this, she issued a decree commanding the king to appoint Anguo as Prefect instead.
entries.literal: Dou empress dowager heard, then decreed wang with Anguo as internal affairs.

entries.zh: 及孝景初立，廣為隴西都尉，徙為騎郎將。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing first ascended the throne, Guang was appointed Commandant of Longxi and later transferred to the post of Captain of the Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing initially established, Guang became Longxi commandery governor, moved became cavalry captain.

entries.zh: 吳楚軍時，廣為驍騎都尉，從太尉亞夫擊吳楚軍，取旗，顯功名昌邑下。
entries.en: During the Rebellion of Wu and Chu, Guang served as Commandant of the Brave Cavalry. He followed Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu in the attack against the rebel armies, captured an enemy battle standard, and won renown at the walls of Changyi.
entries.literal: Wu-Chu army time, Guang became brave-cavalry commandant, followed Grand Commandant Yafu attacking Wu-Chu armies, took a flag, and displayed merit and fame below Changyi.

entries.zh: 以梁王授廣將軍印，還，賞不行。
entries.en: But because the King of Liang had bestowed upon him a general's seal, he received no reward from the court upon his return.
entries.literal: Because Liang wang gave Guang general seal, return, reward not carried out.

entries.zh: 徙為上谷太守，匈奴日以合戰。
entries.en: He was transferred to serve as Governor of Shanggu, where he fought the Xiongnu in battle day after day.
entries.literal: Moved became Shanggu governor, Xiongnu daily with engage battle.

entries.zh: 典屬國公孫昆邪為上泣曰：「李廣才氣，天下無雙，自負其能，數與虜敵戰，恐亡之。」
entries.en: Gongsun Kunye, Director of Attendants for Dependent States, wept before the emperor and said, "General Li Guang's talent and spirit are unmatched under Heaven. He is so confident in his own ability that he repeatedly engages the enemy in battle, and I fear we shall lose him."
entries.literal: Gongsun Kunye, Director of Attendants for Dependent States, wept before the emperor and said, "General Li Guang's talent and spirit are unmatched in the realm. Trusting in his ability, he repeatedly fights the enemy in person—I fear we shall lose him."

entries.zh: 於是乃徙為上郡太守。
entries.en: He was thereupon transferred to serve as Governor of Shangjun.
entries.literal: Thereupon then moved became Shangjun governor.

entries.zh: 後廣轉為邊郡太守，徙上郡。
entries.en: Later Guang was rotated through the border commanderies, and was transferred to Shangjun.
entries.literal: Later Guang transferred became border commandery governor, moved Shangjun.

entries.zh: 嘗為隴西、北地、鴈門、代郡、雲中太守，皆以力戰為名。
entries.en: At one time or another he served as Governor of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Dai, and Yunzhong, winning fame at each post through fierce combat.
entries.literal: Once became Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Daijun, Yunzhong governors, all with vigorous battle for fame.

entries.zh: 居久之，孝景崩，武帝立，左右以為廣名將也，於是廣以上郡太守為未央衛尉，而程不識亦為長樂衛尉。
entries.en: Some time later, Emperor Jing passed away, and Emperor Wu ascended the throne. The Emperor's advisors considered Guang a renowned general, and so he was transferred from his post as Governor of Shangjun to become Commander of the Weiyang Palace Guard, while Cheng Bushi was made Commander of the Changle Palace Guard.
entries.literal: Resided long time, Emperor Jing passed, Emperor Wu established, attendants considered Guang famous general, thereupon Guang with Shangjun governor became Weiyang guard wei, and Cheng Bushi also became Changle guard wei.

entries.zh: 程不識故與李廣俱以邊太守將軍屯。
entries.en: Cheng Bushi had formerly served alongside Li Guang as a border governor and garrison commander.
entries.literal: Cheng Bushi originally with Li Guang both as border governors generals garrisoned.

entries.zh: 及出擊胡，而廣行無部伍行陳，就善水草屯，舍止，人人自便，不擊刀鬬以自衛，莫府省約文書籍事，然亦遠斥候，未嘗遇害。
entries.en: When they marched out to fight the barbarians, Guang imposed no formal ranks or battle formations. He camped wherever there was good water and grass, and let each man see to his own needs. He did not use sentries beating watch clappers for defense, and his headquarters kept its paperwork to a minimum. Yet he always sent scouts far afield and was never taken by surprise.
entries.literal: When out attacked Hu, and Guang marched without divisions rows arrayed, approached good water grass garrisoned, resided stopped, people each self convenient, not beat drums fought to self defend, headquarters office reduced simplified documents books matters, but also far sent scouts, never encountered harm.

entries.zh: 程不識正部曲行伍營陳，擊刀鬬，士吏治軍簿至明，軍不得休息，然亦未嘗遇害。
entries.en: Cheng Bushi, by contrast, maintained strict formations and encampments, posted sentries with watch clappers, and kept his officers working on military records until dawn. His troops got little rest, but he too was never taken by surprise.
entries.literal: Cheng Bushi corrected divisions rows arrayed garrisoned, beat drums fought, officers officials managed army registers to dawn, army not got rest, but also never encountered harm.

entries.zh: 不識曰：「李廣軍極簡易，然虜卒犯之，無以禁也；
entries.en: Cheng Bushi said, "General Li Guang’s army is exceedingly loose and simple; if the enemy suddenly falls upon it, there is no way to restrain them.
entries.literal: Cheng Bushi said, "General Li Guang's army is extremely lax, yet if the enemy suddenly attacks it, there is no way to stop them;

entries.zh: 而其士卒亦佚樂，咸樂為之死。
entries.en: Yet his soldiers lived at their ease and were content, and every one of them would gladly have died for him.
entries.literal: And his soldiers also relaxed happy, all happy for him die.

entries.zh: 我軍雖煩擾，然虜亦不得犯我。」
entries.en: My army may be burdensome and exacting, but the enemy cannot break into it."
entries.literal: My army is troublesome and exacting, yet the enemy also cannot break through us."

entries.zh: 是時漢邊郡李廣、程不識皆為名將，然匈奴畏李廣之略，士卒亦多樂從李廣而苦程不識。
entries.en: At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi were both renowned generals of the Han border commanderies. But the Xiongnu feared Li Guang's cunning, and the soldiers too preferred to serve under Li Guang, finding service under Cheng Bushi a hardship.
entries.literal: At time Han border commanderies Li Guang, Cheng Bushi all were famous generals, but Xiongnu feared Li Guang strategy, soldiers also many happy followed Li Guang but suffered Cheng Bushi.

entries.zh: 程不識孝景時以數直諫為太中大夫。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Jing, Cheng Bushi had been appointed Grand Palace Master for his repeated candid remonstrances.
entries.literal: Cheng Bushi Emperor Jing time with repeatedly straight advised became palace grand master.

entries.zh: 為人廉，謹於文法。
entries.en: He was a man of integrity who was scrupulous in his adherence to regulations.
entries.literal: As person incorrupt, careful with written law.

entries.zh: 廣子三人，曰當戶、椒、敢，為郎。
entries.en: Guang had three sons, named Danghu, Jiao, and Gan, all of whom served as Imperial Attendants.
entries.literal: Guang sons three people, named Danghu, Jiao, Gan, became imperial attendants.

entries.zh: 天子與韓嫣戲，嫣少不遜，當戶擊嫣，嫣走。
entries.en: Once, when the Emperor was amusing himself with his favorite Han Yan, Yan behaved disrespectfully. Danghu struck Yan, who fled.
entries.literal: Emperor with Han Yan played, Yan young not respectful, Danghu hit Yan, Yan fled.

entries.zh: 於是天子以為勇。
entries.en: The Emperor regarded Danghu as a man of courage for this.
entries.literal: Thereupon emperor considered brave.

entries.zh: 當戶早死，拜椒為代郡太守，皆先廣死。
entries.en: Danghu died young. Jiao was appointed Governor of Dai Commandery. Both sons died before their father.
entries.literal: Danghu early died, appointed Jiao as Daijun governor, all before Guang died.

entries.zh: 當戶有遺腹子名陵。
entries.en: Danghu left behind a posthumous son named Li Ling.
entries.literal: Danghu had posthumous son named Ling.

entries.zh: 廣死軍時，敢從驃騎將軍。
entries.en: At the time of Guang's death in the field, his son Gan was serving under the General of the Swift Cavalry.
entries.literal: Guang died army time, Gan followed flying cavalry general.

entries.zh: 廣死明年，李蔡以丞相坐侵孝景園壖地，當下吏治，蔡亦自殺，不對獄，國除。
entries.en: The year after Guang died, Li Cai, then serving as Imperial Chancellor, was charged with encroaching on the land around Emperor Jing's funerary park. Facing prosecution, Cai too took his own life rather than submit to interrogation, and his fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Guang died next year, Li Cai with chancellor sat encroached Emperor Jing garden wall land, should sent officials treated, Cai also suicide, not responded prison, fief removed.

entries.zh: 李敢以校尉從驃騎將軍擊胡左賢王，力戰，奪左賢王鼓旗，斬首多，賜爵關內侯，食邑二百戶，代廣為郎中令。
entries.en: Li Gan, serving as a colonel under the General of the Swift Cavalry, had fought valiantly against the Left Worthy King of the Xiongnu, seizing the enemy's war drums and battle standards and taking many heads. He was granted the title of Marquis Within the Passes with a fief of two hundred households, and succeeded his father as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: Li Gan with colonel followed flying cavalry general attacked Hu left worthy king, vigorously fought, took left worthy king drum flags, beheaded heads many, granted nobility Guannei hou, ate fief two hundred households, replaced Guang became palace secretary.

entries.zh: 頃之，怨大將軍青之恨其父，乃擊傷大將軍，大將軍匿諱之。
entries.en: Before long, Gan, harboring resentment against Grand General Qing for having driven his father to his death, attacked and wounded the Grand General. The Grand General concealed the incident.
entries.literal: Short time, resented grand general Qing hated his father, then hit injured grand general, grand general hid covered it.

entries.zh: 居無何，敢從上雍，至甘泉宮獵。
entries.en: Not long afterward, Gan accompanied the Emperor on a journey to Yong and went hunting at the Ganquan Palace.
entries.literal: Resided no long, Gan followed emperor Yong, arrived Ganquan palace hunted.

entries.zh: 驃騎將軍去病與青有親，射殺敢。
entries.en: The General of the Swift Cavalry, Huo Qubing, who was related to Wei Qing, shot and killed Gan.
entries.literal: Flying cavalry general Huo Qubing with Qing had relation, shot killed Gan.

entries.zh: 去病時方貴幸，上諱云鹿觸殺之。
entries.en: Huo Qubing was at the height of imperial favor at the time, and the Emperor covered up the deed, declaring that Gan had been killed by a charging deer.
entries.literal: Qubing at time just noble favored, emperor hid said deer bumped killed him.

entries.zh: 居歲餘，去病死。
entries.en: A little more than a year later, Huo Qubing died.
entries.literal: Resided year remainder, Qubing died.

entries.zh: 而敢有女為太子中人，愛幸，敢男禹有寵於太子，然好利，李氏陵遲衰微矣。
entries.en: Gan had a daughter who served in the Crown Prince's household and was favored by him. Gan's son Li Yu also enjoyed the Crown Prince's patronage, but he was a man who cared only for profit, and the Li family gradually declined.
entries.literal: But Gan had a daughter who was a palace woman of the Crown Prince and was favored; Gan's son Yu had favor with the Crown Prince, but liked profit, and the Li clan gradually declined and weakened.

entries.zh: 初，廣之從弟李蔡與廣俱事孝文帝。
entries.en: Earlier, Guang's younger cousin Li Cai had entered service alongside Guang under Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Initially, Guang younger cousin Li Cai with Guang together served Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 景帝時，蔡積功勞至二千石。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jing, Cai had accumulated enough merit to attain the rank of two thousand shi.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing time, Cai accumulated merit labor to two thousand shi.

entries.zh: 孝武帝時，至代相。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu, he rose to become Chancellor of Dai.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu time, to Dai chancellor.

entries.zh: 以元朔五年為輕車將車，從大將軍擊右賢王，有功中率，封為樂安侯。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Yuanshuo era, he served as General of the Light Chariots and followed the Grand General in an attack on the Right Worthy King. He met the required kill quota and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Le'an.
entries.literal: With the fifth year of Yuanshuo became light chariot general, followed grand general attacked right worthy king, had merit hit rate, sealed as Lean hou.

entries.zh: 元狩二年中，代公孫弘為丞相。
entries.en: In the second year of the Yuanshou era, he succeeded Gongsun Hong as Imperial Chancellor.
entries.literal: The second year of Yuanshou middle, replaced Gongsun Hong became chancellor.

entries.zh: 蔡為人在下中，名聲出廣下甚遠，然廣不得爵邑，官不過九卿，而蔡為列侯，位至三公。
entries.en: Cai was a man of middling ability at best, and his reputation fell far below Guang's. Yet Guang never received a noble title or a fief, and his office never rose above that of one of the Nine Ministers, while Cai became a full marquis and attained the rank of one of the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Cai as person in lower middle, fame reputation out Guang below very far, but Guang not got nobility fief, office not passed nine ministers, but Cai became marquises, position to three dukes.

entries.zh: 諸廣之軍吏及士卒或取封侯。
entries.en: Even officers and soldiers who had served under Guang were among those enfeoffed as marquises.
entries.literal: Various Guang army officers and soldiers or took sealed marquises.

entries.zh: 廣嘗與望氣王朔燕語，曰：「自漢擊匈奴而廣未嘗不在其中，而諸部校尉以下，才能不及中人，然以擊胡軍功取侯者數十人，而廣不為後人，然無尺寸之功以得封邑者，何也？
entries.en: Guang once conversed at leisure with the diviner Wang Shuo and said, "Since the Han began attacking the Xiongnu, I have never failed to be in the field. Yet among the colonels and commanders and those below them, men whose abilities do not reach the middling level have, through merit in fighting the barbarians, become marquises by the dozens. I am not behind others, yet I have not the slightest merit by which to receive a fief—why is this?
entries.literal: Guang once conversed at leisure with the diviner Wang Shuo and said, "Since the Han began attacking the Xiongnu, I have never failed to be among them. Yet among the colonels and commanders and those below them, men whose abilities do not reach the middling level have, through merit in fighting the barbarians, become marquises by the dozens. I am not behind others, yet I have not the slightest merit by which to receive a fief—why is this?

entries.zh: 豈吾相不當侯邪？
entries.en: Can it be that my features are not those of a man destined for a marquisate?
entries.literal: Is it that my physiognomy is not suited to be a marquis?

entries.zh: 且固命也？」
entries.en: Or is it simply fate?"
entries.literal: Or is it simply fate?"

entries.zh: 朔曰：「將軍自念，豈嘗有所恨乎？」
entries.en: Shuo said, "General, think back for yourself. Is there anything you have regretted?"
entries.literal: Shuo said, "General, reflect for yourself—have you ever had something you regret?"

entries.zh: 廣曰：「吾嘗為隴西守，羌嘗反，吾誘而降，降者八百餘人，吾詐而同日殺之。
entries.en: Guang said, "I once served as Governor of Longxi. When the Qiang rebelled, I enticed them into surrender; more than eight hundred surrendered, and I deceived them and killed them all on the same day.
entries.literal: Guang said, "I once served as Governor of Longxi. When the Qiang rebelled, I lured them to surrender; more than eight hundred who surrendered I deceived and killed on the same day.

entries.zh: 至今大恨獨此耳。」
entries.en: To this day, that alone is my deepest regret."
entries.literal: To this day my greatest regret is this alone."

entries.zh: 朔曰：「禍莫大於殺已降，此乃將軍所以不得侯者也。」
entries.en: Shuo said, "There is no greater disaster than killing men who have already surrendered. This is why the general has never become a marquis."
entries.literal: Shuo said, "No calamity is greater than killing men who have already surrendered—this is why the general has not become a marquis."

entries.zh: 匈奴大入上郡，天子使中貴人從廣勒習兵擊匈奴。
entries.en: When the Xiongnu launched a major invasion into Shangjun, the Emperor sent a palace eunuch to join Guang in drilling the troops and leading the attack against the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Xiongnu greatly entered Shangjun, emperor sent palace favorite followed Guang drilled practiced troops attacked Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 中貴人將騎數十縱，見匈奴三人，與戰。
entries.en: The eunuch, leading several dozen riders on a foray, encountered three Xiongnu horsemen and engaged them in combat.
entries.literal: Palace favorite led cavalry several ten released, saw Xiongnu three people, with battle.

entries.zh: 三人還射，傷中貴人，殺其騎且盡。
entries.en: The three men wheeled around and shot back, wounding the eunuch and killing nearly all of his cavalry.
entries.literal: Three people returned shot, injured palace favorite, killed his cavalry almost all.

entries.zh: 中貴人走廣。
entries.en: The eunuch fled back to Guang.
entries.literal: Palace favorite fled to Guang.

entries.zh: 廣曰：「是必射雕者也。」
entries.en: Guang said, "Those must be eagle hunters."
entries.literal: Guang said, "Those must be eagle-shooters."

entries.zh: 廣乃遂從百騎往馳三人。
entries.en: Guang thereupon took a hundred horsemen and rode out in pursuit of the three men.
entries.literal: Guang then from hundred cavalry went galloped pursue three people.

entries.zh: 三人亡馬步行，行數十里。
entries.en: The three men had lost their horses and were traveling on foot. After Guang had chased them for a few dozen li,
entries.literal: The three men had lost their horses and were traveling on foot; they had gone several tens of li.

entries.zh: 廣令其騎張左右翼，而廣身自射彼三人者，殺其二人，生得一人，果匈奴射雕者也。
entries.en: Guang ordered his horsemen to fan out to the left and right while he himself shot at the three men, killing two and taking one alive. They were indeed Xiongnu eagle shooters.
entries.literal: Guang ordered his cavalry spread left right wings, and Guang personally shot those three people, killed their two people, alive captured one person, indeed Xiongnu shooting eagle ones.

entries.zh: 已縛之上馬，望匈奴有數千騎，見廣，以為誘騎，皆驚，上山陳。
entries.en: After they had bound the prisoner and mounted their horses, they spotted several thousand Xiongnu cavalry in the distance. The Xiongnu saw Guang's men and, taking them for a decoy force, were alarmed and drew up in battle formation on the hillside.
entries.literal: Already bound placed on horse, looked Xiongnu had several thousand cavalry, saw Guang, considered lure cavalry, all alarmed, ascended mountain arrayed.

entries.zh: 廣之百騎皆大恐，欲馳還走。
entries.en: Guang's hundred horsemen were seized with terror and wanted to gallop back to safety.
entries.literal: Guang his hundred cavalry all greatly feared, wanted gallop return flee.

entries.zh: 廣曰：「吾去大軍數十里，今如此以百騎走，匈奴追射我立盡。
entries.en: Guang said, "We are dozens of li from the main army. If we now flee with only a hundred horsemen like this, the Xiongnu will pursue and shoot us down to the last man.
entries.literal: Guang said, "We are several tens of li from the main army. If we now flee with only a hundred horsemen like this, the Xiongnu will pursue and shoot us down to the last man.

entries.zh: 今我留，匈奴必以我為大軍［之］誘（之），必不敢擊我。」
entries.en: If we remain here, the Xiongnu will surely think we are a decoy for the main army and will not dare attack us."
entries.literal: If we stay now, the Xiongnu are sure to take us for a decoy force of the main army and will not dare attack us."

entries.zh: 廣令諸騎曰：「前！」
entries.en: Guang ordered his men, saying, "Forward!"
entries.literal: Guang ordered the horsemen, saying, "Forward!"

entries.zh: 前未到匈奴陳二里所，止，令曰：「皆下馬解鞍！」
entries.en: They advanced until they were only about two li from the Xiongnu formation, then halted, and Guang ordered, "All of you, dismount and loosen your saddles!"
entries.literal: They advanced to within about two li of the Xiongnu battle line, halted, and he ordered, "All dismount and loosen your saddles!"

entries.zh: 其騎曰：「虜多且近，即有急，柰何？」
entries.en: His horsemen said, "The enemy are numerous and close. If something urgent happens, what will we do?"
entries.literal: His horsemen said, "The enemy are many and near; if there is an emergency, what then?"

entries.zh: 廣曰：「彼虜以我為走，今皆解鞍以示不走，用堅其意。」
entries.en: Guang said, "Those barbarians think we are men about to run. If we all loosen our saddles now, we show that we will not flee, and so make them more certain of what they believe."
entries.literal: Guang said, "Those barbarians take us for men who would flee. By loosening our saddles now we show that we do not flee, to strengthen their belief."

entries.zh: 於是胡騎遂不敢擊。
entries.en: And so the barbarian cavalry did not dare to attack.
entries.literal: Thereupon Hu cavalry then not dared attack.

entries.zh: 有白馬將出護其兵，李廣上馬與十餘騎奔射殺胡白馬將，而復還至其騎中，解鞍，令士皆縱馬臥。
entries.en: A barbarian general on a white horse rode out to marshal his troops. Li Guang mounted up and, with a dozen or so riders, galloped forward and shot the white-horse general dead. He then returned to his own men, unsaddled the horses, and ordered the soldiers to release the horses and lie down.
entries.literal: Had white horse general out protected their troops, Li Guang mounted horse with ten remainder cavalry galloped shot killed Hu white horse general, and again returned to his cavalry middle, loosened saddles, ordered soldiers all released horses lay down.

entries.zh: 是時會暮，胡兵終怪之，不敢擊。
entries.en: By then dusk had fallen. The barbarian troops, deeply suspicious, still did not dare to attack.
entries.literal: At time met dusk, Hu troops finally wondered it, not dared attack.

entries.zh: 夜半時，胡兵亦以為漢有伏軍於旁欲夜取之，胡皆引兵而去。
entries.en: At midnight, the barbarian troops, now convinced that the Han had an ambush force hidden nearby waiting to strike under cover of darkness, withdrew their forces and departed.
entries.literal: Midnight time, Hu troops also considered Han had ambush army at side wanted night take them, Hu all led troops left.

entries.zh: 平旦，李廣乃歸其大軍。
entries.en: At dawn, Li Guang led his men back to the main army.
entries.literal: Dawn, Li Guang then returned his main army.

entries.zh: 大軍不知廣所之，故弗從。
entries.en: The main army, not knowing where Guang had gone, had been unable to provide support.
entries.literal: Main army not knew Guang where went, therefore not followed.

entries.zh: 頃之，家居數歲。
entries.en: Before long, he retired to his home, where he lived for some years.
entries.literal: Short time, resided home several years.

entries.zh: 廣家與故潁陰侯孫屏野居藍田南山中射獵。
entries.en: Guang lived with a grandson of the former Marquis of Yingyin in the mountains south of Lantian, where they went hunting.
entries.literal: Guang's household lived in seclusion with a grandson of the former Marquis of Yingyin in the mountains south of Lantian, where they went hunting.

entries.zh: 嘗夜從一騎出，從人田間飲。
entries.en: One night, he rode out with a single companion and drank with some people in the fields.
entries.literal: Once night from one cavalry out, followed people field between drank.

entries.zh: 還至霸陵亭，霸陵尉醉，呵止廣。
entries.en: On the way back, when they reached the Baling postal station, the duty officer, who was drunk, shouted at Guang to halt.
entries.literal: Returned to Baling pavilion, Baling wei drunk, shouted stopped Guang.

entries.zh: 廣騎曰：「故李將軍。」
entries.en: Guang's companion said, "It is the former General Li."
entries.literal: Guang's rider said, "The former General Li."

entries.zh: 尉曰：「今將軍尚不得夜行，何乃故也！」
entries.en: The commandant said, "Even a current general may not travel at night. How much less an old one!"
entries.literal: The duty officer said, "Even a serving general may not travel by night—how much less a former one!"

entries.zh: 止廣宿亭下。
entries.en: He detained Guang and made him spend the night at the station.
entries.literal: Stopped Guang stayed pavilion below.

entries.zh: 居無何，匈奴入殺遼西太守，敗韓將軍，後韓將軍徙右北平。
entries.en: Not long afterward, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the Governor of Liaoxi, defeated General Han Anguo, and Han Anguo was transferred to Youbeiping.
entries.literal: Resided no long, Xiongnu entered killed Liaoxi governor, defeated Han general, after Han general moved right Beiping.

entries.zh: 於是天子乃召拜廣為右北平太守。
entries.en: The Emperor thereupon summoned Guang and appointed him Governor of Youbeiping.
entries.literal: Thereupon emperor then summoned appointed Guang as right Beiping governor.

entries.zh: 廣即請霸陵尉與俱，至軍而斬之。
entries.en: Guang immediately requested that the Baling duty officer accompany him to his post, and upon reaching the army, had the man beheaded.
entries.literal: Guang immediately requested Baling wei with together go, arrived army and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 後二歲，大將軍、驃騎將軍大出擊匈奴，廣數自請行。
entries.en: Two years later, the Grand General and the General of the Swift Cavalry launched a major campaign against the Xiongnu. Guang repeatedly petitioned to join them.
entries.literal: After two years, grand general, flying cavalry general greatly out attacked Xiongnu, Guang repeatedly self requested go.

entries.zh: 天子以為老，弗許；
entries.en: The emperor thought him too old and would not allow it;
entries.literal: The emperor considered him too old and did not permit it;

entries.zh: 良久乃許之，以為前將軍。
entries.en: After a long delay, the Emperor relented and appointed him General of the Vanguard.
entries.literal: Long time then permitted him, appointed as front general.

entries.zh: 是歲，元狩四年也。
entries.en: This was the fourth year of the Yuanshou era.
entries.literal: This year, the fourth year of Yuanshou.

entries.zh: 居頃之，石建卒，於是上召廣代建為郎中令。
entries.en: Shortly afterward, Shi Jian died, and the Emperor summoned Guang to replace him as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: Resided short time, Shi Jian died, thereupon emperor summoned Guang replaced Jian became palace secretary.

entries.zh: 元朔六年，廣復為後將軍，從大將軍軍出定襄，擊匈奴。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the Yuanshuo era, Guang was again appointed General of the Rear and followed the Grand General's army out of Dingxiang to attack the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: The sixth year of Yuanshuo, Guang again became rear general, followed grand general army out Dingxiang, attacked Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 諸將多中首虜率，以功為侯者，而廣軍無功。
entries.en: Many of the other generals met the required kill quotas and were enfeoffed as marquises for their achievements, but Guang's forces earned no distinction.
entries.literal: Various generals many hit enemy leaders rates, with merit became marquises, but Guang army no merit.

entries.zh: 後二歲，廣以郎中令將四千騎出右北平，博望侯張騫將萬騎與廣俱，異道。
entries.en: Two years later, Guang, in his capacity as Superintendent of the Imperial Household, led four thousand cavalry out of Youbeiping. The Marquis of Bowang, Zhang Qian, led ten thousand cavalry on a parallel route.
entries.literal: After two years, Guang with palace secretary led four thousand cavalry out right Beiping, Bowang marquis Zhang Qian led ten thousand cavalry with Guang together, different roads.

entries.zh: 行可數百里，匈奴左賢王將四萬騎圍廣，廣軍士皆恐，廣乃使其子敢往馳之。
entries.en: After they had advanced several hundred li, the Left Worthy King of the Xiongnu descended upon them with forty thousand cavalry and surrounded Guang. His soldiers were all terrified. Guang sent his son Li Gan to ride out against the enemy.
entries.literal: Marched could several hundred li, Xiongnu left worthy king led four ten thousand cavalry surrounded Guang, Guang army soldiers all feared, Guang then sent his son Gan go galloped them.

entries.zh: 敢獨與數十騎馳，直貫胡騎，出其左右而還，告廣曰：「胡虜易與耳。」
entries.en: Gan rode out alone with several dozen horsemen, charged straight through the barbarian cavalry, emerged on their flanks, and returned. He reported to Guang, "The Hu cavalry are easy to handle."
entries.literal: Gan rode out alone with several dozen horsemen, charged straight through the barbarian cavalry, broke out to their left and right, and returned. He reported to Guang, saying, "The barbarian enemy are easy to deal with."

entries.zh: 軍士乃安。
entries.en: Only then did the soldiers' courage steady.
entries.literal: Army soldiers then calm.

entries.zh: 廣為圜陳外向，胡急擊之，矢下如雨。
entries.en: Guang formed his men into a circular formation facing outward. The barbarians attacked furiously, and arrows fell like rain.
entries.literal: Guang made circular array outward facing, Hu urgently attacked it, arrows fell like rain.

entries.zh: 漢兵死者過半，漢矢且盡。
entries.en: More than half the Han soldiers were killed, and their arrows were nearly exhausted.
entries.literal: Han troops died over half, Han arrows almost exhausted.

entries.zh: 廣乃令士持滿毋發，而廣身自以大黃射其裨將，殺數人，胡虜益解。
entries.en: Guang ordered his soldiers to draw their bows fully but hold their fire, while he himself took up a powerful crossbow and shot at the enemy's deputy commanders, killing several. The barbarian assault gradually slackened.
entries.literal: Guang then ordered soldiers hold full not fire, and Guang personally with big yellow shot their deputy generals, killed several people, Hu enemy increasingly loosened.

entries.zh: 會日暮，吏士皆無人色，而廣意氣自如，益治軍。
entries.en: As dusk fell, every officer and soldier had gone pale with fear, but Guang remained as composed as ever, rallying his troops with ever greater resolve.
entries.literal: Met dusk, officers soldiers all without human color, but Guang spirit energy self like, increasingly governed army.

entries.zh: 軍中自是服其勇也。
entries.en: From that time on, every man in the army admired his courage.
entries.literal: Army middle from this submitted his courage.

entries.zh: 明日，復力戰，而博望侯軍亦至，匈奴軍乃解去。
entries.en: The next day, they fought on fiercely, and the army of the Marquis of Bowang arrived at last. The Xiongnu withdrew.
entries.literal: Next day, again vigorously fought, and Bowang marquis army also arrived, Xiongnu army then withdrew left.

entries.zh: 漢軍罷，弗能追。
entries.en: The Han army was too exhausted to give chase.
entries.literal: Han army dismissed, not able pursue.

entries.zh: 是時廣軍幾沒，罷歸。
entries.en: Guang's army had been all but annihilated, and the survivors straggled home.
entries.literal: At time Guang army almost perished, dismissed returned.

entries.zh: 漢法，博望侯留遲後期，當死，贖為庶人。
entries.en: Under Han law, the Marquis of Bowang was charged with arriving late past the appointed rendezvous, a crime punishable by death. He was allowed to ransom himself and was reduced to the status of a commoner.
entries.literal: Han law, Bowang marquis stayed late after period, should die, redeemed as commoner.

entries.zh: 廣軍功自如，無賞。
entries.en: As for Guang, his army's gains and losses canceled each other out, and he received no reward.
entries.literal: Guang army merit self like, no reward.

entries.zh: 廣既從大將軍青擊匈奴，既出塞，青捕虜知單于所居，乃自以精兵走之，而令廣并於右將軍軍，出東道。
entries.en: Guang marched with Grand General Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu. After they had crossed the frontier, Qing learned from captured prisoners where the Chanyu was camped. He took his best troops to go after the Chanyu himself and ordered Guang to merge his forces with the General of the Right and advance by the eastern route.
entries.literal: Guang already followed grand general Qing attacked Xiongnu, already out pass, Qing captured captives knew chanyu residence, then self with elite troops went it, and ordered Guang merged with right general army, out east road.

entries.zh: 東道少回遠，而大軍行水草少，其勢不屯行。
entries.en: The eastern route was circuitous and far, with little water or grass along the way, making it difficult for a large force to march and encamp.
entries.literal: East road few winding distant, but main army marched water grass few, its situation not garrison march.

entries.zh: 廣自請曰：「臣部為前將軍，今大將軍乃徙令臣出東道，且臣結發而與匈奴戰，今乃一得當單于，臣願居前，先死單于。」
entries.en: Guang pleaded on his own behalf, saying, "My command is the Vanguard. Now the Grand General has shifted me to the eastern route. I have fought the Xiongnu since I first bound up my hair, and now, for once, I have the chance to face the Chanyu. I wish to stand in the front and be the first to die before him."
entries.literal: Guang petitioned on his own behalf, saying, "My command is that of General of the Vanguard. Now the Grand General has reassigned me to the eastern route. Moreover, I have fought the Xiongnu since I first bound up my hair. Now at last I have a chance to face the Chanyu—I wish to take the front rank and be the first to meet the Chanyu in death."

entries.zh: 大將軍青亦陰受上誡，以為李廣老，數奇，毋令當單于，恐不得所欲。
entries.en: Grand General Qing had also received secret instructions from the Emperor: Li Guang was old and had always been unlucky; he must not be allowed to face the Chanyu, for fear that the desired result would not be achieved.
entries.literal: Grand general Qing also secretly received emperor instruction, considered Li Guang old, repeatedly unlucky, not let face chanyu, feared not get desired.

entries.zh: 而是時公孫敖新失侯，為中將軍從大將軍，大將軍亦欲使敖與俱當單于，故徙前將軍廣。
entries.en: Moreover, Gongsun Ao had recently lost his marquisate and was serving as General of the Center under the Grand General. The Grand General wished to give Ao the chance to face the Chanyu alongside him, and so he reassigned Guang from the vanguard.
entries.literal: And at time Gongsun Ao newly lost marquis, became middle general followed grand general, grand general also wanted make Ao with together face chanyu, therefore moved front general Guang.

entries.zh: 廣時知之，固自辭於大將軍。
entries.en: Guang understood what was happening and firmly protested to the Grand General.
entries.literal: Guang at time knew it, firmly self declined with grand general.

entries.zh: 大將軍不聽，令長史封書與廣之莫府，曰：「急詣部，如書。」
entries.en: The Grand General would not listen. He ordered the chief clerk to seal a letter to Guang’s headquarters, saying, "Report at once to the command assigned in the letter."
entries.literal: The Grand General would not listen. He had the chief clerk seal a letter to Guang's headquarters, saying, "Proceed at once to your command as written."

entries.zh: 廣不謝大將軍而起行，意甚慍怒而就部，引兵與右將軍食其合軍出東道。
entries.en: Guang departed without taking leave of the Grand General, seething with resentment. He went to take up his command and led his troops eastward with the General of the Right, Zhao Shiqi.
entries.literal: Guang not thanked grand general and rose marched, intent very resentful angered and went command, led troops with right general Shiqi combined army out east road.

entries.zh: 軍亡導，或失道，後大將軍。
entries.en: The army had no guide and lost its way, falling behind the Grand General's schedule.
entries.literal: Army lacked guide, or lost road, after grand general.

entries.zh: 大將軍與單于接戰，單于遁走，弗能得而還。
entries.en: The Grand General engaged the Chanyu in battle, but the Chanyu escaped and could not be captured, so the Grand General turned back.
entries.literal: Grand general with chanyu engaged battle, chanyu fled ran, not able get and returned.

entries.zh: 南絕幕，遇前將軍、右將軍。
entries.en: As he crossed south through the desert, he encountered the General of the Vanguard and the General of the Right.
entries.literal: South cut off tent, met front general, right general.

entries.zh: 廣已見大將軍，還入軍。
entries.en: After Guang had met with the Grand General, he returned to his own camp.
entries.literal: Guang already saw grand general, returned entered army.

entries.zh: 大將軍使長史持糒醪遺廣，因問廣、食其失道狀，青欲上書報天子軍曲折。
entries.en: The Grand General sent his chief clerk to bring Guang dried rations and wine, and at the same time to question Guang and Zhao Shiqi about how they had lost their way, for Qing wished to submit a report to the Emperor on the course of the campaign.
entries.literal: Grand general sent chancellor secretary held dried grains wine gifted Guang, because asked Guang, Shiqi lost road condition, Qing wanted memorial reported emperor army twists turns.

entries.zh: 廣未對，大將軍使長史急責廣之幕府對簿。
entries.en: Guang made no reply. The Grand General then sent his chief clerk to summon Guang urgently to headquarters to answer formal charges.
entries.literal: Guang not responded, grand general sent chancellor secretary urgently blamed Guang headquarters respond trial.

entries.zh: 廣曰：「諸校尉無罪，乃我自失道。
entries.en: Guang said, "The colonels are not at fault. I myself lost the road.
entries.literal: Guang said, "The colonels are not guilty—it was I who lost the way.

entries.zh: 吾今自上簿。」
entries.en: I will now present myself and answer for it."
entries.literal: I will now go up and answer the charges myself."

entries.zh: 李陵既壯，選為建章監，監諸騎。
entries.en: When Li Ling came of age, he was selected to serve as Superintendent of the Jianzhang Palace, in charge of the cavalry.
entries.literal: Li Ling already grown, selected became Jianzhang monitor, monitored various cavalry.

entries.zh: 善射，愛士卒。
entries.en: He was a skilled archer who treated his soldiers with care.
entries.literal: Good shooting, loved soldiers.

entries.zh: 天子以為李氏世將，而使將八百騎。
entries.en: The Emperor, considering the Li family a line of hereditary generals, gave him command of eight hundred cavalry.
entries.literal: Emperor considered Li clan world generals, and made lead eight hundred cavalry.

entries.zh: 嘗深入匈奴二千餘里，過居延視地形，無所見虜而還。
entries.en: He once penetrated more than two thousand li into Xiongnu territory, passing through Juyan to survey the terrain, but encountered no enemy and returned.
entries.literal: Once deeply entered Xiongnu two thousand remainder li, passed Juyan viewed terrain, nothing saw enemy returned.

entries.zh: 拜為騎都尉，將丹陽楚人五千人，教射酒泉、張掖以屯衛胡。
entries.en: He was appointed Commandant of Cavalry and given command of five thousand men from Danyang and Chu, whom he trained in archery at Jiuquan and Zhangye to garrison the frontier against the barbarians.
entries.literal: Appointed became cavalry commandery governor, led Danyang Chu people five thousand people, taught shooting Jiuquan, Zhangye to garrison guard Hu.

entries.zh: 李將軍廣者，隴西成紀人也。
entries.en: General Li Guang was a native of Chengji in Longxi.
entries.literal: General Li Guang, Longxi Chengji person.

entries.zh: 其先曰李信，秦時為將，逐得燕太子丹者也。
entries.en: His ancestor Li Xin had served as a general under the Qin and was the man who pursued and captured Dan, the Crown Prince of Yan.
entries.literal: His ancestor named Li Xin, Qin time became general, pursued captured Yan crown prince Dan.

entries.zh: 故槐裏，徙成紀。
entries.en: The family was originally from Huaili but later moved to Chengji.
entries.literal: Originally Huaili, moved to Chengji.

entries.zh: 廣家世世受射。
entries.en: For generations, the Li family had handed down the art of archery.
entries.literal: Guang family generation generation received archery.

entries.zh: 孝文帝十四年，匈奴大入蕭關，而廣以良家子從軍擊胡，用善騎射，殺首虜多，為漢中郎。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Xiongnu launched a major invasion through the Xiao Pass. Guang, as the son of a respectable family, joined the army to fight the barbarians. His skill in horsemanship and archery allowed him to kill a great many of the enemy, and he was appointed as an Attendant at the Han court.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen fourteenth year, Xiongnu greatly entered Xiaoguan, and Guang with good family son followed army attacked Hu, used good horsemanship archery, killed enemy leaders many, became Han imperial attendant.

entries.zh: 廣從弟李蔡亦為郎，皆為武騎常侍，秩八百石。
entries.en: Guang's younger cousin Li Cai also served as an Attendant. Both were appointed as Regular Attendants of the Martial Cavalry, with a salary rank of eight hundred shi.
entries.literal: Guang younger cousin Li Cai also became imperial attendant, all became martial cavalry regular attendants, rank eight hundred shi.

entries.zh: 嘗從行，有所衝陷折關及格猛獸，而文帝曰：「惜乎，子不遇時！
entries.en: Once, while accompanying the Emperor on campaign, Guang charged through barriers and grappled with fierce beasts, and Emperor Wen said, "What a pity that you were not born in your season!
entries.literal: Once on campaign in attendance, there were charges through barriers and grappling with fierce beasts, and Emperor Wen said, "What a pity—you were not born in your season!

entries.zh: 如令子當高帝時，萬戶侯豈足道哉！」
entries.en: Had you lived in the age of Emperor Gao, a marquisate of ten thousand households would scarcely be worth mentioning!"
entries.literal: If you had been in the time of Emperor Gao, would a marquis of ten thousand households not be spoken of with ease!"

entries.zh: 建元元年，天子初即位，招賢良文學之士。
entries.en: In the first year of the Jianyuan era, the newly enthroned Emperor issued a call for men of worth and scholarly talent.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Jianyuan era, the Son of Heaven had just ascended the throne and summoned men of virtue and learning.

entries.zh: 是時弘年六十，徵以賢良為博士。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong was already sixty by then; he was summoned as a worthy scholar and appointed Academician.
entries.literal: At that time Hong was sixty years old, and was summoned as a man of worth to serve as an Academician.

entries.zh: 使匈奴，還報，不合上意，上怒，以為不能，弘乃病免歸。
entries.en: He was dispatched on a mission to the Xiongnu, but upon his return, his report displeased the Emperor. Furious, the Emperor deemed him incompetent. Gongsun Hong pleaded illness, secured his release, and went home.
entries.literal: He was sent on a mission to the Xiongnu, returned and reported, but it did not accord with the Emperor's wishes. The Emperor was angered and deemed him incompetent, so Hong claimed illness and was dismissed, returning home.

entries.zh: 元光五年，有詔徵文學，菑川國復推上公孫弘。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Yuanguang era, an imperial edict went out summoning men of learning, and once again the State of Zichuan put forward Gongsun Hong's name.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Yuanguang era, there was an edict summoning men of learning, and the State of Zichuan again recommended Gongsun Hong.

entries.zh: 弘讓謝國人曰：「臣已嘗西應命，以不能罷歸，願更推選。」
entries.en: Gongsun Hong demurred, telling his countrymen: 'I once answered the summons to the capital, only to be sent home for incompetence. Please select another candidate.'
entries.literal: Hong declined and apologized to the people of the state, saying: 'I have already once gone west to answer the summons, but was dismissed for incompetence and sent home. I wish you would recommend someone else.'

entries.zh: 國人固推弘，弘至太常。
entries.en: But the people of his state insisted on putting him forward, and so Gongsun Hong presented himself before the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: The people of the state insisted on recommending Hong, and Hong went to the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 太常令所徵儒士各對策，百餘人，弘第居下。
entries.en: The Grand Master of Ceremonies ordered all the summoned scholars to submit policy essays. Among more than a hundred candidates, Gongsun Hong was ranked last.
entries.literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies ordered all the summoned Confucian scholars to answer policy questions. Among over a hundred men, Hong's ranking was at the bottom.

entries.zh: 策奏，天子擢弘對為第一。
entries.en: Yet when the essays reached the Emperor, the Son of Heaven himself elevated Gongsun Hong's response to first place.
entries.literal: When the essays were submitted to the throne, the Son of Heaven promoted Hong's response to first place.

entries.zh: 召入見，狀貌甚麗，拜為博士。
entries.en: Summoned for an audience, his appearance and bearing greatly impressed the court, and he was appointed Academician.
entries.literal: He was summoned for an audience; his appearance was most impressive, and he was appointed Academician.

entries.zh: 是時通西南夷道，置郡，巴蜀民苦之，詔使弘視之。
entries.en: At that time, the court was opening roads into the lands of the southwestern tribes and establishing new commanderies. The people of Ba and Shu groaned under the burden, and the Emperor dispatched Gongsun Hong to investigate.
entries.literal: At that time roads were being opened to the southwestern barbarians and commanderies established. The people of Ba and Shu suffered from this, and an edict sent Hong to inspect the situation.

entries.zh: 還奏事，盛毀西南夷無所用，上不聽。
entries.en: Upon his return, he reported vigorously that the southwestern tribes were of no use to the empire, but the Emperor would not heed his counsel.
entries.literal: He returned and reported on the matter, strongly criticizing the southwestern barbarians as useless, but the Emperor did not listen.

entries.zh: 汲黯曰：「弘位在三公，奉祿甚多。
entries.en: Ji An declared: 'Gongsun Hong holds one of the highest offices in the realm, and his salary is exceedingly generous.
entries.literal: Ji An said: 'Hong holds a position among the Three Excellencies, and his salary is very generous.

entries.zh: 然為布被，此詐也。」
entries.en: Yet he sleeps under coarse cloth quilts—this is nothing but fraud.'
entries.literal: Yet he uses cloth quilts—this is fraud.'

entries.zh: 上問弘。
entries.en: The Emperor put the question to Gongsun Hong.
entries.literal: The Emperor asked Hong about it.

entries.zh: 弘謝曰：「有之。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong bowed and replied: 'It is true.
entries.literal: Hong apologized and said: 'It is so.

entries.zh: 夫九卿與臣善者無過黯，然今日庭詰弘，誠中弘之病。
entries.en: Among all the Nine Ministers, none is closer to me than Ji An, yet today he has confronted me before the court and truly struck at the heart of my failing.
entries.literal: Among the Nine Ministers, none is on better terms with me than Ji An, yet today he has confronted me at court, and truly hit upon my fault.

entries.zh: 夫以三公為布被，誠飾詐欲以釣名。
entries.en: For one of the Three Excellencies to sleep under coarse cloth is indeed an affectation designed to fish for a reputation.
entries.literal: For one of the Three Excellencies to use cloth quilts is indeed a deceitful affectation to fish for a good name.

entries.zh: 且臣聞管仲相齊，有三歸，侈擬於君，桓公以霸，亦上僭於君。
entries.en: Moreover, I have heard that when Guan Zhong served as chief minister of Qi, he possessed the Three Gui estates and lived in extravagance rivaling his lord's. Duke Huan achieved hegemony through him, yet Guan Zhong also overstepped the ruler's prerogatives.
entries.literal: Moreover, I have heard that when Guan Zhong served as minister of Qi, he possessed the Three Gui estates, his extravagance rivaling the ruler's. Duke Huan achieved hegemony through him, yet Guan Zhong also encroached upon the ruler's prerogatives.

entries.zh: 晏嬰相景公，食不重肉，妾不衣絲，齊國亦治，此下比於民。
entries.en: When Yanzi served as minister to Duke Jing, he ate no more than a single dish of meat, and his concubines wore no silk, yet Qi was equally well governed—he had lowered himself to the level of the common people.
entries.literal: When Yan Ying served as minister to Duke Jing, he ate no more than one meat dish, his concubines did not wear silk, and Qi was also well governed—this was lowering himself to the level of commoners.

entries.zh: 今臣弘位為御史大夫，而為布被，自九卿以下至於小吏，無差，誠如汲黯言。
entries.en: Now I hold the office of Imperial Secretary, yet I sleep under the same coarse cloth quilts as everyone from the Nine Ministers down to the lowliest clerk. It is exactly as Ji An says.
entries.literal: Now I, Hong, hold the position of Imperial Secretary, yet I use cloth quilts—no different from the Nine Ministers down to the lowest clerks. It is truly as Ji An says.

entries.zh: 且無汲黯忠，陛下安得聞此言。」
entries.en: And yet, were it not for Ji An's loyalty, how would Your Majesty ever have heard such words?'
entries.literal: Moreover, without Ji An's loyalty, how would Your Majesty have heard these words?'

entries.zh: 天子以為謙讓，愈益厚之。
entries.en: The Emperor regarded this as a display of modesty and self-effacement, and favored him all the more.
entries.literal: The Emperor considered him modest and self-effacing, and treated him with ever greater favor.

entries.zh: 卒以弘為丞相，封平津侯。
entries.en: In the end, Gongsun Hong was elevated to Chancellor and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Pingjin.
entries.literal: In the end, Hong was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Pingjin.

entries.zh: 元朔三年，張歐免，以弘為御史大夫。
entries.en: In the third year of the Yuanshuo era, Zhang Ou was removed from office, and Gongsun Hong was appointed Imperial Secretary.
entries.literal: In the third year of the Yuanshuo era, Zhang Ou was dismissed, and Hong was made Imperial Secretary.

entries.zh: 是時通西南夷，東置滄海，北筑朔方之郡。
entries.en: At that time, the court was opening routes to the southwestern tribes, establishing the Canghai Commandery in the east, and constructing the Shuofang Commandery in the north.
entries.literal: At that time, routes were being opened to the southwestern barbarians, the Canghai Commandery was established in the east, and the Shuofang Commandery was being built in the north.

entries.zh: 弘數諫，以為罷敝中國以奉無用之地，願罷之。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong remonstrated repeatedly, arguing that these ventures were exhausting the heartland in service of worthless territories, and urged that they be abandoned.
entries.literal: Hong repeatedly remonstrated, arguing that it was exhausting the heartland to serve useless territories, and wished to abandon them.

entries.zh: 於是天子乃使朱買臣等難弘置朔方之便。
entries.en: The Emperor then dispatched Zhu Maichen and others to debate Gongsun Hong on the merits of establishing the Shuofang Commandery.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor ordered Zhu Maichen and others to challenge Hong on the advantages of establishing Shuofang.

entries.zh: 發十策，弘不得一。
entries.en: They put forward ten arguments, and Gongsun Hong could not counter a single one.
entries.literal: They raised ten arguments, and Hong could not refute a single one.

entries.zh: 弘乃謝曰：「山東鄙人，不知其便若是，願罷西南夷、滄海而專奉朔方。」
entries.en: Gongsun Hong conceded: 'I am but a rustic from east of the mountains and did not realize the advantages were so compelling. I would propose abandoning the southwestern tribes and Canghai to devote our resources entirely to Shuofang.'
entries.literal: Hong then apologized and said: 'I am a rustic man from east of the mountains and did not know the advantages were so great. I wish to abandon the southwestern barbarians and Canghai and focus on supporting Shuofang.'

entries.zh: 上乃許之。
entries.en: The Emperor granted his request.
entries.literal: The Emperor then approved his proposal.

entries.zh: 弘為人恢奇多聞，常稱以為人主病不廣大，人臣病不儉節。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong was a man of wide and remarkable learning. He was fond of saying that a ruler's failing lay in a lack of magnanimity, while a minister's failing lay in a lack of frugality.
entries.literal: Hong was a man of broad and extraordinary learning. He often said that the fault of a ruler lies in not being magnanimous enough, and the fault of a minister lies in not being frugal enough.

entries.zh: 弘為布被，食不重肉。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong slept under coarse cloth quilts and never had more than a single dish of meat at his table.
entries.literal: Hong used cloth quilts and did not eat more than one meat dish.

entries.zh: 后母死，服喪三年。
entries.en: When his stepmother passed away, he observed the full three years of mourning.
entries.literal: When his stepmother died, he observed mourning for three years.

entries.zh: 每朝會議，開陳其端，令人主自擇，不肯面折庭爭。
entries.en: In every court deliberation, he would lay out the essential issues and let the Emperor decide, never once confronting anyone or arguing openly before the assembled officials.
entries.literal: At every court deliberation, he would lay out the key points and let the ruler choose for himself, never willing to openly oppose or argue at court.

entries.zh: 於是天子察其行敦厚，辯論有餘，習文法吏事，而又緣飾以儒術，上大說之。
entries.en: The Emperor thus observed that his conduct was sincere and generous, his reasoning more than persuasive, and that he was well versed in legal and administrative matters, all of which he deftly adorned with Confucian learning. The Emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: Thus, the Son of Heaven observed that his conduct was sincere and generous, his arguments more than adequate, he was versed in legal and clerical affairs, and moreover adorned these with Confucian learning. The Emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 二歲中，至左內史。
entries.en: Within two years, he had risen to the rank of Left Prefect of the Capital.
entries.literal: Within two years, he rose to the position of Left Prefect of the Capital.

entries.zh: 弘奏事，有不可，不庭辯之。
entries.en: Whenever one of Gongsun Hong's proposals was rejected, he never argued about it at court.
entries.literal: When Hong submitted proposals and something was rejected, he did not argue about it at court.

entries.zh: 嘗與主爵都尉汲黯請閒，汲黯先發之，弘推其後，天子常說，所言皆聽，以此日益親貴。
entries.en: On one occasion, he and Ji An, the Commandant of Noble Ranks, jointly sought a private audience. Ji An spoke first, and Gongsun Hong followed up with supporting arguments. The Emperor was invariably pleased and accepted everything they said. In this way, Gongsun Hong's standing grew day by day.
entries.literal: Once, together with the Commandant of Noble Ranks Ji An, they sought a private audience. Ji An spoke first, and Hong followed up after him. The Emperor was always pleased, and everything they said was accepted. Because of this, Hong grew daily in the Emperor's favor.

entries.zh: 嘗與公卿約議，至上前，皆倍其約以順上旨。
entries.en: There were times when he would reach an agreement with the other ministers beforehand, only to abandon the consensus once before the Emperor, aligning himself instead with the imperial will.
entries.literal: He once agreed with the ministers on a joint proposal, but when they came before the Emperor, he went back on the agreement to follow the Emperor's wishes.

entries.zh: 汲黯庭詰弘曰：「齊人多詐而無情實，始與臣等建此議，今皆倍之，不忠。」
entries.en: Ji An confronted him before the entire court: 'Men of Qi are full of deceit and devoid of sincerity. Gongsun Hong joined us in drafting this proposal, and now he has reversed himself entirely. This is disloyalty.'
entries.literal: Ji An confronted Hong at court and said: 'The people of Qi are full of deceit and lack sincerity. Hong first joined us ministers in crafting this proposal, and now he has gone back on all of it. This is disloyal.'

entries.zh: 上問弘。
entries.en: The Emperor turned to Gongsun Hong for his response.
entries.literal: The Emperor asked Hong about it.

entries.zh: 弘謝曰：「夫知臣者以臣為忠，不知臣者以臣為不忠。」
entries.en: Gongsun Hong replied: 'Those who truly know me regard me as loyal; those who do not know me regard me as disloyal.'
entries.literal: Hong replied: 'Those who understand your servant consider me loyal; those who do not understand me consider me disloyal.'

entries.zh: 上然弘言。
entries.en: The Emperor accepted his answer.
entries.literal: The Emperor agreed with Hong's words.

entries.zh: 左右幸臣每毀弘，上益厚遇之。
entries.en: Though the imperial favorites continually maligned Gongsun Hong, the Emperor only treated him with greater generosity.
entries.literal: The favored ministers on the left and right often slandered Hong, but the Emperor treated him with ever greater favor.

entries.zh: 主父偃者，齊臨菑人也。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan hailed from Linzi in the land of Qi.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan was a man from Linzi in Qi.

entries.zh: 學長短縱橫之術，晚乃學易、春秋、百家言。
entries.en: He first studied the arts of persuasion and diplomatic strategy, and only later turned to the Book of Changes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the writings of the Hundred Schools.
entries.literal: He studied the arts of rhetoric and alliance-building, and only later studied the Book of Changes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the writings of the Hundred Schools.

entries.zh: 游齊諸生閒，莫能厚遇也。
entries.en: He traveled among the scholars of Qi, but none would offer him patronage.
entries.literal: He traveled among the scholars of Qi, but none would receive him generously.

entries.zh: 齊諸儒生相與排擯，不容於齊。
entries.en: The Confucian scholars of Qi banded together to ostracize him, and he found no welcome in the land of Qi.
entries.literal: The Confucian scholars of Qi collectively excluded and rejected him, and he was not tolerated in Qi.

entries.zh: 家貧，假貸無所得，乃北游燕、趙、中山，皆莫能厚遇，為客甚困。
entries.en: His family was destitute, and he could obtain no loans. He traveled north to the states of Yan, Zhao, and Zhongshan, but nowhere did he find generous patronage, and his life as a wandering guest was one of great hardship.
entries.literal: His family was poor, and he could not obtain loans. So he traveled north to Yan, Zhao, and Zhongshan, but none would receive him generously, and as a guest he was in great hardship.

entries.zh: 孝武元光元年中，以為諸侯莫足游者，乃西入關見衛將軍。
entries.en: Midway through the first year of the Yuanguang era under Emperor Wu, he concluded that no feudal lord was worth his service, and so he traveled west through the passes to seek out General Wei Qing.
entries.literal: In the middle of the first year of the Yuanguang era under Emperor Wu, he concluded that none of the feudal lords was worth seeking out, so he went west through the passes to see General Wei.

entries.zh: 衛將軍數言上，上不召。
entries.en: General Wei recommended him to the Emperor on several occasions, but the Emperor would not summon him.
entries.literal: General Wei spoke to the Emperor about him several times, but the Emperor did not summon him.

entries.zh: 資用乏，留久，諸公賓客多厭之，乃上書闕下。
entries.en: His funds ran dry, and after lingering so long, the patrons and their guests had grown weary of him. At last, he submitted a memorial directly at the palace gate.
entries.literal: His funds were exhausted, and having stayed a long time, the various lords' guests had mostly grown tired of him. So he submitted a memorial at the palace gate.

entries.zh: 朝奏，暮召入見。
entries.en: He submitted his memorial in the morning, and by evening the Emperor had summoned him for an audience.
entries.literal: He submitted his memorial in the morning and was summoned for an audience that evening.

entries.zh: 所言九事，其八事為律令，一事諫伐匈奴。
entries.en: His memorial addressed nine topics: eight concerned laws and regulations, and one was an argument against waging war on the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: He addressed nine matters: eight concerned laws and regulations, and one was a remonstrance against attacking the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The memorial ran as follows:
entries.literal: His words ran as follows:
