entries.zh: 淮南、衡山謀反，治黨與方急。
entries.en: When the Kings of Huainan and Hengshan plotted rebellion, the investigation of their co-conspirators was pressed with great urgency.
entries.literal: The Kings of Huainan and Hengshan plotted rebellion, and the investigation of their conspirators was being pursued urgently.

entries.zh: 弘病甚，自以為無功而封，位至丞相，宜佐明主填撫國家，使人由臣子之道。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong's illness grew grave. He reflected that he had been enfeoffed without merit and had risen to the rank of Chancellor; it was his duty to assist the wise sovereign in pacifying the realm and guiding the people along the path of loyal subjects.
entries.literal: Hong's illness was severe. He felt that he had been enfeoffed without merit and had risen to the position of Chancellor; he should have assisted the wise ruler in pacifying the state and guiding the people along the path of loyal subjects.

entries.zh: 今諸侯有畔逆之計，此皆宰相奉職不稱，恐竊病死，無以塞責。
entries.en: Now feudal lords had hatched treasonous plots—all because he, as Chancellor, had failed in his duties. He feared that if he died quietly of illness, he would have no way to atone for his failure.
entries.literal: Now the feudal lords harbored treasonous plans—this was all because the Chancellor had failed in his duties. He feared that should he die quietly of illness, he would have no way to fulfill his responsibilities.

entries.zh: 乃上書曰：「臣聞天下之通道五，所以行之者三。
entries.en: He therefore submitted a memorial: 'Your servant has heard that there are five universal principles governing all under Heaven, and three virtues by which they are put into practice.
entries.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: 'I have heard that there are five universal principles under Heaven, and three means by which to put them into practice.

entries.zh: 曰君臣，父子，兄弟，夫婦，長幼之序，此五者天下之通道也。
entries.en: They are: the bond between ruler and subject, between father and son, between elder and younger brother, between husband and wife, and the proper ordering of seniors and juniors. These five constitute the universal principles of all under Heaven.
entries.literal: They are: ruler and subject, father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and the proper order between elders and juniors. These five are the universal principles of the world.

entries.zh: 智，仁，勇，此三者天下之通德，所以行之者也。
entries.en: Wisdom, benevolence, and courage—these three are the universal virtues of all under Heaven, and the means by which the five principles are carried out.
entries.literal: Wisdom, benevolence, and courage—these three are the universal virtues of the world, the means by which the principles are put into practice.

entries.zh: 故曰『力行近乎仁，好問近乎智，知恥近乎勇』。
entries.en: Thus, it is said: "To act with diligence approaches benevolence; to love inquiry approaches wisdom; to know shame approaches courage."
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said: 'To practice with vigor is close to benevolence; to love inquiry is close to wisdom; to know shame is close to courage.'

entries.zh: 知此三者，則知所以自治；
entries.en: One who understands these three virtues understands how to govern himself;
entries.literal: He who knows these three also knows how to govern himself;

entries.zh: 知所以自治，然後知所以治人。
entries.en: And one who knows how to govern himself will then know how to govern others.
entries.literal: and he who knows how to govern himself will then know how to govern others.

entries.zh: 天下未有不能自治而能治人者也，此百世不易之道也。
entries.en: Never in all the world has there been a man unable to govern himself who could govern others. This is a principle unchanged through a hundred generations.
entries.literal: There has never been anyone under Heaven who could not govern himself yet could govern others. This is an unchanging principle through a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 今陛下躬行大孝，鑒三王，建周道，兼文武，厲賢予祿，量能授官。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty personally exemplifies the highest filial piety, takes the Three Kings as his mirror, follows the Way of Zhou, unites the virtues of both the civil and the martial, rewards the worthy with emoluments, and assigns office according to ability.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty personally practices the greatest filial piety, takes the Three Kings as a mirror, establishes the Way of Zhou, combines the virtues of the civil and martial, encourages the worthy with emoluments, and assigns offices according to ability.

entries.zh: 今臣弘罷駑之質，無汗馬之勞，陛下過意擢臣弘卒伍之中，封為列侯，致位三公。
entries.en: Your servant Hong is a man of worn and mediocre talent, with no battlefield merit to his name. Yet Your Majesty has, beyond all reason, raised me from the common ranks, enfeoffed me as a marquis, and elevated me to the highest echelons of government.
entries.literal: Now your servant Hong is of a worn-out and dull nature, with no meritorious military service. Yet Your Majesty has, beyond all expectation, raised me from among the common soldiers, enfeoffed me as a marquis, and elevated me to the position of one of the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 臣弘行能不足以稱，素有負薪之病，恐先狗馬填溝壑，終無以報德塞責。
entries.en: My conduct and ability fall far short of the honor bestowed upon me. I have long suffered from an ailment of the back, and I fear I shall die like a worn-out beast discarded in a ditch, never having repaid Your Majesty's grace or discharged my responsibilities.
entries.literal: Your servant Hong's conduct and ability are insufficient to match this honor. I have long suffered from the ailment of carrying firewood on my back, and I fear I will die like a dog or horse cast into a ditch, never able to repay Your Majesty's grace or fulfill my responsibilities.

entries.zh: 願歸侯印，乞骸骨，避賢者路。」
entries.en: I beg to return the seal of my marquisate and retire in my old age, clearing the path for worthier men.'
entries.literal: I wish to return the marquis's seal, beg to retire with my old bones, and make way for the worthy.'

entries.zh: 天子報曰：「古者賞有功，襃德，守成尚文，遭遇右武，未有易此者也。
entries.en: The Emperor replied: 'Since antiquity, the meritorious have been rewarded and the virtuous honored. In times of stability, the civil arts are prized; in times of crisis, martial valor is exalted. This has never changed.
entries.literal: The Emperor replied: 'In ancient times, merit was rewarded and virtue honored. In times of stability, civil virtues were esteemed; in times of crisis, martial virtues were favored. This has never changed.

entries.zh: 朕宿昔庶幾獲承尊位，懼不能寧，惟所與共為治者，君宜知之。
entries.en: Ever since I was fortunate enough to inherit this exalted throne, I have lived in fear of failing to bring peace. It is only through those who share the burden of governance with me that the realm can be ordered—and this you should know well.
entries.literal: From the time I was fortunate enough to inherit the exalted throne, I have feared I could not bring tranquility. Only through those who share in governance with me can this be achieved—this you should know.

entries.zh: 蓋君子善善惡惡，（君宜知之）君若謹行，常在朕躬。
entries.en: A true gentleman commends the good and condemns the wicked—you should know this well. If you continue to conduct yourself with care, you shall always remain at my side.
entries.literal: A true gentleman commends the good and condemns the wicked—you should know this. If you conduct yourself with care, you will always remain at my side.

entries.zh: 君不幸罹霜露之病，何恙不已，乃上書歸侯，乞骸骨，是章朕之不德也。
entries.en: You have had the misfortune of falling ill from exposure to the elements. Why has the ailment not yet healed? Yet to submit a memorial returning your marquisate and begging to retire would only proclaim my lack of virtue to the world.
entries.literal: You have unfortunately contracted an illness from the frost and dew. Why does the ailment not heal? Yet you submit a memorial to return your marquisate and retire—this would only display my lack of virtue.

entries.zh: 今事少閒，君其省思慮，一精神，輔以醫藥。」
entries.en: Now that the press of affairs has eased somewhat, you should set aside your anxieties, gather your strength, and attend to your recovery with the help of physicians.'
entries.literal: Now that affairs are somewhat less pressing, you should reduce your worries, concentrate your spirit, and supplement this with medicine.'

entries.zh: 因賜告牛酒雜帛。
entries.en: The Emperor thereupon granted him leave and presented him with gifts of cattle, wine, and assorted silks.
entries.literal: He thereupon granted him leave and bestowed upon him cattle, wine, and various silks.

entries.zh: 居數月，病有瘳，視事。
entries.en: After several months, his condition improved and he resumed his duties.
entries.literal: After several months, his illness improved, and he returned to his duties.

entries.zh: 臣聞明主不惡切諫以博觀，忠臣不敢避重誅以直諫，是故事無遺策而功流萬世。
entries.en: I have heard that a wise ruler does not resent blunt counsel, for it broadens his perspective, and a loyal minister does not shrink from the threat of execution to speak the truth. In this way, no policy goes unconsidered and achievements endure through the ages.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that a wise ruler does not resent frank remonstrance, for it broadens his vision, and a loyal minister does not shrink from the threat of severe punishment to offer straight counsel. Thus, no policy is overlooked and achievements endure for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 今臣不敢隱忠避死以效愚計，願陛下幸赦而少察之。
entries.en: Now I dare not conceal my loyalty or shrink from death as I present my humble counsel. I beg Your Majesty to pardon my boldness and give these words some consideration.
entries.literal: Now your servant does not dare conceal his loyalty or avoid death, and offers his humble plan. I hope Your Majesty will graciously pardon me and give it some consideration.

entries.zh: 元狩二年，弘病，竟以丞相終。
entries.en: In the second year of the Yuanshou era, Gongsun Hong fell ill once more and died in office as Chancellor.
entries.literal: In the second year of the Yuanshou era, Hong fell ill and ultimately died while still serving as Chancellor.

entries.zh: 子度嗣為平津侯。
entries.en: His son Du inherited the title of Marquis of Pingjin.
entries.literal: His son Du succeeded him as the Marquis of Pingjin.

entries.zh: 度為山陽太守十餘歲，坐法失侯。
entries.en: Du served as the Governor of Shanyang for more than ten years before being convicted of a legal offense and stripped of his marquisate.
entries.literal: Du served as Governor of Shanyang for over ten years, but was convicted of a legal offense and lost his marquisate.

entries.zh: 及至高皇帝定天下，略地於邊，聞匈奴聚於代谷之外而欲擊之。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu had pacified the realm and was campaigning along the frontier, he learned that the Xiongnu had massed beyond the valley of Dai and wished to strike them.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu pacified the realm and was campaigning along the frontier, he heard that the Xiongnu had massed beyond the valley of Dai and wished to attack them.

entries.zh: 御史成進諫曰：「不可。
entries.en: The Imperial Censor Cheng remonstrated: 'This must not be done.
entries.literal: The Imperial Censor Cheng remonstrated and said: 'This must not be done.

entries.zh: 夫匈奴之性，獸聚而鳥散，從之如搏影。
entries.en: The Xiongnu gather like herds of beasts and scatter like flocks of birds. To pursue them is like trying to catch a shadow.
entries.literal: The nature of the Xiongnu is to gather like beasts and scatter like birds. Pursuing them is like trying to grasp a shadow.

entries.zh: 今以陛下盛德攻匈奴，臣竊危之。」
entries.en: For Your Majesty to risk his great virtue by attacking the Xiongnu—I secretly tremble at the danger of it.'
entries.literal: To use Your Majesty's great virtue to attack the Xiongnu—your servant privately fears the danger of this.'

entries.zh: 高帝不聽，遂北至於代谷，果有平城之圍。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu would not listen and marched north to the valley of Dai, where he was indeed trapped in the siege of Pingcheng.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu did not listen and proceeded north to the valley of Dai, where he was indeed besieged at Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 高皇帝蓋悔之甚，乃使劉敬往結和親之約，然後天下忘干戈之事。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu bitterly regretted his decision and sent Liu Jing to negotiate a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu. Only then did the empire at last set aside the business of war.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu bitterly regretted it and sent Liu Jing to negotiate a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu. Only then did the empire put aside the affairs of war.

entries.zh: 故兵法曰「興師十萬，日費千金」。
entries.en: As the military classics say: "To mobilize an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand in gold each day."
entries.literal: Therefore, the military treatises say: 'To raise an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand pieces of gold per day.'

entries.zh: 夫秦常積眾暴兵數十萬人，雖有覆軍殺將系虜單于之功，亦適足以結怨深讎，不足以償天下之費。
entries.en: Qin regularly deployed hundreds of thousands of troops under the harshest conditions. Even had they destroyed armies, slain enemy generals, and captured the Chanyu himself, it would only have deepened the enmity and blood feuds—it could never have repaid the cost to the empire.
entries.literal: Qin regularly amassed hundreds of thousands of troops and exposed them to hardship. Even if they achieved the feat of destroying armies, killing generals, and capturing the Chanyu, it would only be enough to deepen enmity and grudges, not enough to repay the cost to the empire.

entries.zh: 夫上虛府庫，下敝百姓，甘心於外國，非完事也。
entries.en: To drain the treasury above and exhaust the common people below, all for the satisfaction of punishing foreign nations—this is no sound course of action.
entries.literal: To empty the state treasury above and exhaust the common people below, all to indulge one's heart against foreign nations—this is not a sound course of action.

entries.zh: 夫匈奴難得而制，非一世也。
entries.en: The Xiongnu have been impossible to subdue—and not just for a single generation.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu have been difficult to capture and control—this has not been the case for just one generation.

entries.zh: 行盜侵驅，所以為業也，天性固然。
entries.en: Raiding, invading, and plundering are their livelihood—it is their very nature.
entries.literal: Raiding, invading, and plundering—this is their livelihood, their inborn nature.

entries.zh: 上及虞夏殷周，固弗程督，禽獸畜之，不屬為人。
entries.en: Going back to the reigns of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, the Xiongnu were never governed or supervised; they were treated as wild animals, not reckoned among civilized peoples.
entries.literal: Going back to the reigns of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, they were never regulated or supervised but were treated as birds and beasts, not counted among civilized peoples.

entries.zh: 夫上不觀虞夏殷周之統，而下（修）［循］近世之失，此臣之所大憂，百姓之所疾苦也。
entries.en: To ignore the precedents of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou and instead repeat the mistakes of more recent times—this is what I fear most deeply, and what inflicts the greatest suffering upon the people.
entries.literal: To fail to look up to the traditions of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, and instead to follow the mistakes of recent ages—this is what your servant greatly fears, and what causes the people the greatest suffering.

entries.zh: 且夫兵久則變生，事苦則慮易。
entries.en: Moreover, when war drags on, upheaval follows; when hardship deepens, loyalties waver.
entries.literal: Moreover, when military campaigns drag on, turmoil arises; when hardships increase, loyalties shift.

entries.zh: 乃使邊境之民獘靡愁苦而有離心，將吏相疑而外市，故尉佗、章邯得以成其私也。
entries.en: The border people are driven to exhaustion and despair, breeding disaffection, while generals and officials suspect one another and seek advantage for themselves abroad. It was precisely this that allowed Zhao Tuo and Zhang Han to carve out their own domains.
entries.literal: This causes the border people to become exhausted, miserable, and disaffected, while generals and officials suspect one another and seek advantage abroad. Thus, Zhao Tuo and Zhang Han were able to pursue their private ambitions.

entries.zh: 夫秦政之所以不行者，權分乎二子，此得失之效也。
entries.en: The reason Qin's authority collapsed was that power had been divided between these two men. This is the very lesson of success and failure.
entries.literal: The reason Qin's governance failed was that power was divided between these two men. This is the lesson of success and failure.

entries.zh: 故《周書》曰「安危在出令，存亡在所用」。
entries.en: Thus, the Book of Zhou declares: "Safety and peril depend upon the orders a ruler issues; survival and ruin depend upon the men he employs."
entries.literal: Therefore, the Book of Zhou says: 'Safety and peril depend on the orders issued; survival and destruction depend on the men employed.'

entries.zh: 願陛下詳察之，少加意而熟慮焉。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to examine this matter with care, to give it due attention, and to deliberate thoroughly.
entries.literal: I hope Your Majesty will examine this carefully, pay it some attention, and consider it thoroughly.

entries.zh: 閒者關東五穀不登，年歲未復，民多窮困，重之以邊境之事，推數循理而觀之，則民且有不安其處者矣。
entries.en: In recent years, the five grains have failed east of the passes and the harvests have not recovered. The people are sinking into poverty, burdened further by the ongoing border campaigns. If one traces the pattern and follows the logic, there will soon be people who can no longer remain content where they are.
entries.literal: Recently, the five grains have failed east of the passes, the harvests have not recovered, and many people are impoverished. On top of this, the border campaigns continue. If one follows the numbers and examines the logic, there will be people who can no longer rest easy where they are.

entries.zh: 不安故易動。
entries.en: Those who are not content are easily stirred to revolt.
entries.literal: Those who are not content are easily stirred to action.

entries.zh: 易動者，土崩之勢也。
entries.en: When the people are easily stirred, the conditions for the foundation to crumble are already in place.
entries.literal: Those who are easily stirred—this is the situation of 'earth collapse.'

entries.zh: 故賢主獨觀萬化之原，明於安危之機，修之廟堂之上，而銷未形之患。
entries.en: A wise ruler therefore discerns the origins of all change, grasps the pivotal moment between safety and peril, addresses the matter from the court, and eliminates threats before they take shape.
entries.literal: Therefore, a wise ruler alone discerns the origins of all transformations, understands the critical moment of safety and danger, addresses matters from the court above, and eliminates troubles before they take shape.

entries.zh: 其要，期使天下無土崩之勢而已矣。
entries.en: The essence of his task is simply to ensure that the empire's foundations never crumble.
entries.literal: The essence is simply to ensure that the empire does not face a situation of 'earth collapse.'

entries.zh: 故雖有彊國勁兵，陛下逐走獸，射蜚鳥，弘游燕之囿，淫縱恣之觀，極馳騁之樂，自若也。
entries.en: Thus, even were there powerful states with formidable armies, Your Majesty could chase running game, shoot at soaring birds, roam the vast royal hunting parks, indulge in the most extravagant spectacles, and revel in the thrill of the hunt—all without a care.
entries.literal: Thus, even if there were powerful states with strong armies, Your Majesty could pursue running beasts, shoot at flying birds, roam broadly through parks of excursion and banquet, indulge in the most extravagant spectacles, and enjoy the full thrill of riding—all without concern.

entries.zh: 金石絲竹之聲不絕於耳，帷帳之私俳優侏儒之笑不乏於前，而天下無宿憂。
entries.en: The music of bells, chimes, strings, and flutes would never leave your ears; the pleasures of the bedchamber and the laughter of jesters and entertainers would never be lacking—and the empire would have no lingering worries.
entries.literal: The sounds of bells, stones, strings, and flutes would never cease in your ears; the private delights behind the curtains and the laughter of jesters and dwarfs would never be lacking before you—and the empire would have no lingering worries.

entries.zh: 名何必湯武，俗何必成康！
entries.en: Why would your fame need to match that of Kings Tang and Wu? Why would your customs need to rival those of the reigns of Cheng and Kang?
entries.literal: Why must your fame match Tang and Wu? Why must your customs match those of Cheng and Kang?

entries.zh: 雖然，臣竊以為陛下天然之聖，寬仁之資，而誠以天下為務，則湯武之名不難侔，而成康之俗可復興也。
entries.en: Even so, I privately believe that with Your Majesty's natural sagacity and generous nature, if you truly take the welfare of the realm as your foremost concern, then the fame of Tang and Wu would not be hard to match, and the prosperous customs of the Cheng and Kang reigns could yet be revived.
entries.literal: Nevertheless, your servant privately believes that with Your Majesty's natural sagacity and your generous and benevolent nature, if you truly take the empire as your foremost concern, it would not be difficult to match the fame of Tang and Wu, and the customs of the reigns of Cheng and Kang could be revived.

entries.zh: 此二體者立，然後處尊安之實，揚名廣譽於當世，親天下而服四夷，餘恩遺德為數世隆，南面負扆攝袂而揖王公，此陛下之所服也。
entries.en: Once these two paradigms are established, Your Majesty will enjoy the substance of a secure and exalted throne, spread renown and glory across the age, win the devotion of all under Heaven and the submission of the four barbarian peoples. The blessings of your benevolence and virtue will endure through the generations. Facing south with your back to the imperial screen, you will graciously receive the salutations of lords and dukes—this is what Your Majesty truly deserves.
entries.literal: Once these two paradigms are established, Your Majesty will enjoy the substance of a secure and exalted position, spread fame and glory throughout the age, win the devotion of the empire and the submission of the four barbarian peoples. The surplus of your benevolence and virtue will endure for generations. Facing south with your back to the screen, adjusting your sleeves and saluting the lords and dukes—this is what Your Majesty is worthy of.

entries.zh: 臣聞圖王不成，其敝足以安。
entries.en: I have heard that even if the pursuit of true kingship does not fully succeed, its lesser effects are still sufficient to bring stability.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that even if the plan for true kingship does not fully succeed, its lesser effects are still sufficient to bring stability.

entries.zh: 安則陛下何求而不得，何為而不成，何征而不服乎哉！
entries.en: With stability, what could Your Majesty seek and not obtain? What could you undertake and not accomplish? What campaign could you wage that would not end in submission?
entries.literal: With stability, what could Your Majesty seek and not obtain? What could you attempt and not achieve? What expedition could you launch and not see submission?

entries.zh: 嚴安上書曰：
entries.en: Yan An submitted a memorial that read:
entries.literal: Yan An submitted a memorial that said:

entries.zh: 書奏天子，天子召見三人，謂曰：「公等皆安在？
entries.en: When these memorials reached the Emperor, he summoned all three men and exclaimed: 'Where have you all been hiding?
entries.literal: When the memorials were submitted to the Emperor, the Emperor summoned all three men and said: 'Where have you all been?

entries.zh: 何相見之晚也！」
entries.en: Why has it taken so long for us to meet!'
entries.literal: Why have we met so late!'

entries.zh: 於是上乃拜主父偃、徐樂、嚴安為郎中。
entries.en: The Emperor then appointed Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An as Gentlemen of the Palace.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor appointed Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An as Gentlemen of the Palace.

entries.zh: 偃數見，上疏言事，詔拜偃為謁者，遷為中大夫。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan was received in audience several times and submitted memorials on affairs of state. By imperial decree, he was first appointed Receptionist and then promoted to Palace Grandee.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan was received in audience several times and submitted memorials on affairs of state. By imperial decree he was appointed Receptionist, then promoted to Palace Grandee.

entries.zh: 一歲中四遷偃。
entries.en: In the span of a single year, Zhufu Yan was promoted four times.
entries.literal: Within a single year, Zhufu Yan was promoted four times.

entries.zh: 偃說上曰：「古者諸侯不過百里，彊弱之形易制。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan advised the Emperor: 'In ancient times, a feudal lord's domain extended no more than a hundred li, and the balance of power between the strong and the weak was easy to control.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan advised the Emperor: 'In ancient times, feudal lords held no more than a hundred li. The balance of power between strong and weak was easy to maintain.

entries.zh: 今諸侯或連城數十，地方千里，緩則驕奢易為淫亂，急則阻其彊而合從以逆京師。
entries.en: Now some feudal lords command dozens of linked cities and territories stretching a thousand li. If the court is lenient, they grow arrogant and dissolute; if the court presses them, they rely on their strength and form alliances to resist the capital.
entries.literal: Now some feudal lords command dozens of linked cities, with territories of a thousand li. If the court is lenient, they grow arrogant and dissolute; if the court is strict, they rely on their strength and form alliances to resist the capital.

entries.zh: 今以法割削之，則逆節萌起，前日晁錯是也。
entries.en: Should we now try to reduce them through legal measures, rebellious impulses will flare up—is the fate of Chao Cuo in the past not proof enough?
entries.literal: If we now try to reduce them by law, rebellion will sprout—the case of Chao Cuo in the past proves this.

entries.zh: 今諸侯子弟或十數，而適嗣代立，餘雖骨肉，無尺寸地封，則仁孝之道不宣。
entries.en: Now some feudal lords have ten or more sons, yet only the legitimate heir inherits. The rest, though they are flesh and blood of the same family, receive not a foot of territory—and so the principles of benevolence and filial piety go unfulfilled.
entries.literal: Now some feudal lords have ten or more sons, yet only the legitimate heir succeeds. The rest, though flesh and blood, receive not a foot of territory—thus the principles of benevolence and filial piety are not upheld.

entries.zh: 願陛下令諸侯得推恩分子弟，以地侯之。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to decree that the feudal lords be permitted to extend their grace and divide their lands among all their sons, enfeoffing each with his own domain.
entries.literal: I wish Your Majesty would decree that the feudal lords be permitted to extend their grace and divide territory among their sons, enfeoffing each with land.

entries.zh: 彼人人喜得所願，上以德施，實分其國，不削而稍弱矣。」
entries.en: Every son would be delighted to receive his portion. From above, it would appear a generous bestowal of imperial grace; in reality, it would divide their kingdoms. Without a single decree of reduction, they would gradually weaken.'
entries.literal: Each of them would be delighted to receive what he desires. Above, it would appear as a bestowal of grace; in reality, it divides their kingdoms. Without any formal reduction, they would gradually weaken.'

entries.zh: 於是上從其計。
entries.en: The Emperor adopted his plan.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon adopted his plan.

entries.zh: 又說上曰：「茂陵初立，天下豪桀并兼之家，亂眾之民，皆可徙茂陵，內實京師，外銷姦猾，此所謂不誅而害除。」
entries.en: He further advised the Emperor: 'The Maoling estate has just been established. The powerful families and the land-engrossing houses across the empire, along with the troublemakers among the common people, could all be relocated there. This would strengthen the capital region from within and eliminate subversive elements from without—removing the danger without shedding a drop of blood.'
entries.literal: He also advised the Emperor: 'The Maoling estate has just been established. The powerful families and land-engrossing houses throughout the empire, as well as the troublemakers among the common people, could all be relocated to Maoling. This would strengthen the capital region internally and eliminate cunning and lawlessness externally—what is called removing harm without resorting to execution.'

entries.zh: 上又從其計。
entries.en: Once again, the Emperor adopted his plan.
entries.literal: The Emperor again adopted his plan.

entries.zh: 元朔二年，主父言齊王內淫佚行僻，上拜主父為齊相。
entries.en: In the second year of the Yuanshuo era, Zhufu Yan reported that the King of Qi was privately dissolute and of perverse conduct. The Emperor appointed Zhufu Yan as the Chancellor of Qi.
entries.literal: In the second year of the Yuanshuo era, Zhufu Yan reported that the King of Qi was privately licentious and of deviant conduct. The Emperor appointed Zhufu Yan as Chancellor of Qi.

entries.zh: 至齊，遍召昆弟賓客，散五百金予之，數之曰：「始吾貧時，昆弟不我衣食，賓客不我內門；
entries.en: Upon arriving in Qi, he summoned all his brothers and former acquaintances, distributed five hundred pieces of gold among them, and rebuked them: 'When I was destitute, my brothers would not clothe or feed me, and my friends barred their doors to me;
entries.literal: Upon arriving in Qi, he summoned all his brothers and former acquaintances, distributed five hundred pieces of gold among them, and rebuked them, saying: 'When I was poor, my brothers would not clothe or feed me, and my friends would not let me through their doors;

entries.zh: 今吾相齊，諸君迎我或千里。
entries.en: Now that I am Chancellor of Qi, some of you have traveled a thousand li to welcome me.
entries.literal: now that I am Chancellor of Qi, some of you have come a thousand li to greet me.

entries.zh: 吾與諸君絕矣，毋復入偃之門！」
entries.en: I am severing all ties with you. Never set foot through my door again!'
entries.literal: I sever all ties with you—do not set foot in my door again!'

entries.zh: 乃使人以王與姊姦事動王，王以為終不得脫罪，恐效燕王論死，乃自殺。
entries.en: He then sent an agent to confront the King with the scandal of his incestuous affair with his sister. The King, convinced he could never escape punishment and fearing he would be sentenced to death as the King of Yan had been, took his own life.
entries.literal: He then sent someone to pressure the King with the matter of his incestuous affair with his sister. The King, believing he would never escape punishment and fearing he would be sentenced to death like the King of Yan, killed himself.

entries.zh: 有司以聞。
entries.en: The officials duly reported the matter to the throne.
entries.literal: The officials reported this to the throne.

entries.zh: 偃盛言朔方地肥饒，外阻河，蒙恬城之以逐匈奴，內省轉輸戍漕，廣中國，滅胡之本也。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan argued enthusiastically that the land of Shuofang was fertile and abundant, shielded on the outside by the Yellow River—Meng Tian had once fortified it to drive out the Xiongnu. Holding it would reduce the burden of supply transport and frontier garrisons, expand the heartland, and lay the foundation for defeating the northern barbarians.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan enthusiastically argued that the land of Shuofang was fertile and rich, externally protected by the Yellow River. Meng Tian had once fortified it to drive out the Xiongnu. It would reduce the need for transporting supplies and garrisoning troops internally, expand the heartland, and serve as the foundation for defeating the Hu.

entries.zh: 上覽其說，下公卿議，皆言不便。
entries.en: The Emperor reviewed his proposal and referred it to the ministers for deliberation. They unanimously declared it impractical.
entries.literal: The Emperor reviewed his proposal and sent it to the ministers for deliberation. They all said it was not advantageous.

entries.zh: 公孫弘曰：「秦時常發三十萬眾筑北河，終不可就，已而棄之。」
entries.en: Gongsun Hong objected: 'In the Qin era, three hundred thousand men were deployed to build the northern river fortifications, yet the project could never be completed and was ultimately abandoned.'
entries.literal: Gongsun Hong said: 'In the Qin era, three hundred thousand men were regularly deployed to build the northern river defenses, but it could never be completed, and was eventually abandoned.'

entries.zh: 主父偃盛言其便，上竟用主父計，立朔方郡。
entries.en: But Zhufu Yan argued forcefully for its merits, and in the end the Emperor adopted his plan and established the Shuofang Commandery.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan argued forcefully for its advantages. In the end, the Emperor adopted Zhufu Yan's plan and established the Shuofang Commandery.

entries.zh: 尊立衛皇后，及發燕王定國陰事，蓋偃有功焉。
entries.en: In the elevation of Empress Wei and the exposure of the secret crimes of Liu Dingguo, King of Yan, Zhufu Yan had played a significant role.
entries.literal: In the elevation of Empress Wei and the exposure of the secret crimes of the King of Yan, Dingguo, Zhufu Yan played a meritorious role.

entries.zh: 大臣皆畏其口，賂遺累千金。
entries.en: Every great minister feared the sharpness of his tongue and showered him with bribes totaling thousands in gold.
entries.literal: All the great ministers feared his sharp tongue and bribed him with gifts totaling thousands of pieces of gold.

entries.zh: 人或說偃曰：「太橫矣。」
entries.en: Someone warned Zhufu Yan: 'You are being far too overbearing.'
entries.literal: Someone warned Zhufu Yan: 'You are being too arrogant.'

entries.zh: 主父曰：「臣結發游學四十餘年，身不得遂，親不以為子，昆弟不收，賓客棄我，我阸日久矣。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan replied: 'Since I first bound up my hair as a youth, I have wandered as a scholar for more than forty years. I never achieved anything. My own parents refused to acknowledge me as their son, my brothers turned their backs on me, and my friends abandoned me. I have endured this hardship for a very long time.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan replied: 'I have wandered as a scholar since I first bound my hair—over forty years. I never achieved success. My parents did not regard me as a son, my brothers refused to take me in, and my friends abandoned me. I have suffered this hardship for a very long time.

entries.zh: 且丈夫生不五鼎食，死即五鼎烹耳。
entries.en: A real man—if he cannot dine from the five ceremonial cauldrons while alive, then let him be boiled in the five cauldrons when he dies.
entries.literal: Moreover, a real man—if he cannot eat from the five cauldrons in life, then let him be boiled in the five cauldrons in death.

entries.zh: 吾日暮途遠，故倒行暴施之。」
entries.en: The sun is setting, and the road ahead is long—so I act recklessly and without restraint.'
entries.literal: My sun is setting and the road ahead is long, so I walk backward and act recklessly.'

entries.zh: 主父始為布衣時，嘗游燕、趙，及其貴，發燕事。
entries.en: When Zhufu Yan was still a commoner, he had traveled through the states of Yan and Zhao. After rising to prominence, he exposed the crimes of the King of Yan.
entries.literal: When Zhufu Yan was still a commoner, he had once traveled through Yan and Zhao. After he rose to prominence, he exposed the crimes of the King of Yan.

entries.zh: 趙王恐其為國患，欲上書言其陰事，為偃居中，不敢發。
entries.en: The King of Zhao, fearing that Zhufu Yan would become a threat to his own state, wished to submit a memorial exposing his secret transgressions. But with Zhufu Yan positioned at the heart of the court, he dared not act.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao feared that Zhufu Yan might become a threat to his own state and wished to submit a memorial revealing his secret crimes, but because Zhufu Yan held a position at court, he did not dare act.

entries.zh: 及為齊相，出關，即使人上書，告言主父偃受諸侯金，以故諸侯子弟多以得封者。
entries.en: As soon as Zhufu Yan was appointed Chancellor of Qi and departed from the capital through the passes, the King of Zhao immediately dispatched someone to submit a memorial accusing Zhufu Yan of taking gold from the feudal lords, which was why so many of their sons had obtained fiefs.
entries.literal: When Zhufu Yan was appointed Chancellor of Qi and left the passes, the King of Zhao immediately sent someone to submit a memorial, accusing Zhufu Yan of accepting gold from the feudal lords, and that because of this, many of the lords' sons had obtained fiefs.

entries.zh: 及齊王自殺，上聞大怒，以為主父劫其王令自殺，乃徵下吏治。
entries.en: When the King of Qi took his own life, the Emperor was furious upon hearing the news, convinced that Zhufu Yan had coerced the King into killing himself. He ordered Zhufu Yan arrested and handed over to the judicial officials for trial.
entries.literal: When the King of Qi killed himself, the Emperor heard of it and was furious, believing that Zhufu Yan had coerced the King into suicide. He ordered Zhufu Yan arrested and turned over to the judicial officials for trial.

entries.zh: 主父服受諸侯金，實不劫王令自殺。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan confessed to accepting gold from the feudal lords but maintained that he had not coerced the King into taking his own life.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan confessed to accepting gold from the feudal lords, but maintained that he had not coerced the King into suicide.

entries.zh: 上欲勿誅，是時公孫弘為御史大夫，乃言曰：「齊王自殺無後，國除為郡，入漢，主父偃本首惡，陛下不誅主父偃，無以謝天下。」
entries.en: The Emperor was inclined to spare him. But at that time Gongsun Hong was serving as Imperial Secretary, and he spoke up: 'The King of Qi killed himself and left no heir. His kingdom has been abolished and absorbed as a commandery of the Han. Zhufu Yan was the root cause of it all. If Your Majesty does not execute Zhufu Yan, there will be no way to answer to the empire.'
entries.literal: The Emperor was inclined not to execute him. At that time Gongsun Hong was serving as Imperial Secretary, and he spoke up: 'The King of Qi killed himself and left no heir. His kingdom has been abolished and converted into a commandery under Han. Zhufu Yan was the chief instigator. If Your Majesty does not execute Zhufu Yan, there will be no way to satisfy the expectations of the empire.'

entries.zh: 乃遂族主父偃。
entries.en: And so Zhufu Yan and his entire clan were put to death.
entries.literal: Thus Zhufu Yan was executed along with his entire clan.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：公孫弘行義雖修，然亦遇時。
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Though Gongsun Hong cultivated his conduct and principles, he also benefited from fortunate timing.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian remarks: Although Gongsun Hong cultivated his conduct and righteousness, he also met with favorable times.

entries.zh: 漢興八十餘年矣，上方鄉文學，招俊乂，以廣儒墨，弘為舉首。
entries.en: The Han dynasty had been established for over eighty years, and the Emperor was just then turning his attention to men of learning, recruiting the talented and the distinguished, and broadening the influence of the Confucian and Mohist traditions. Gongsun Hong stood at the head of those recommended.
entries.literal: The Han dynasty had been established for over eighty years. The Emperor was just then turning toward men of learning, recruiting the talented and distinguished, and expanding the Confucian and Mohist traditions. Hong was the foremost among those recommended.

entries.zh: 主父偃當路，諸公皆譽之，及名敗身誅，士爭言其惡。
entries.en: When Zhufu Yan held power, every man of rank sang his praises. But when his reputation was destroyed, and he was executed, the scholars fell over one another to denounce his wickedness.
entries.literal: When Zhufu Yan was in power, all the lords praised him. But when his reputation was ruined and he was executed, the scholars vied with one another to speak of his wickedness.

entries.zh: 悲夫！
entries.en: How sorrowful it all is!
entries.literal: How sad!

entries.zh: 主父方貴幸時，賓客以千數，及其族死，無一人收者，唯獨洨孔車收葬之。
entries.en: When Zhufu Yan was at the height of his favor, his guests and followers numbered in the thousands. Yet when his clan was executed, not a single person came to claim his body—only Kong Che of Xiao collected his remains and gave him a proper burial.
entries.literal: When Zhufu Yan was at the height of his favor, his guests numbered in the thousands. Yet when his clan was executed, not a single one came to claim the body—only Kong Che of Xiao collected and buried him.

entries.zh: 天子后聞之，以為孔車長者也。
entries.en: When the Emperor later learned of this, he regarded Kong Che as a man of true integrity.
entries.literal: The Emperor later heard of this and considered Kong Che to be a man of integrity.

entries.zh: 太皇太后詔大司徒大司空：「蓋聞治國之道，富民為始；
entries.en: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an edict to the Grand Minister of Education and the Grand Minister of Works: 'I have heard that the way to govern a state begins with enriching its people;
entries.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an edict to the Grand Minister of Education and the Grand Minister of Works: 'It is said that the way of governing a state begins with enriching the people;

entries.zh: 富民之要，在於節儉。
entries.en: And the key to enriching the people lies in frugality.
entries.literal: the key to enriching the people lies in frugality.

entries.zh: 《孝經》曰『安上治民，莫善於禮』。
entries.en: The Classic of Filial Piety states: "For securing peace among those above and governing the people below, nothing surpasses ritual propriety."
entries.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "For securing the repose of superiors and governing the people, nothing surpasses ritual propriety."

entries.zh: 『禮，與奢也寧儉』。
entries.en: In matters of ritual, better to err on the side of frugality than extravagance.
entries.literal: In matters of ritual, rather than be extravagant, it is better to be frugal.

entries.zh: 昔者管仲相齊桓，霸諸侯，有九合一匡之功，而仲尼謂之不知禮，以其奢泰侈擬於君故也。
entries.en: In ages past, Guan Zhong served as chief minister to Duke Huan of Qi, achieved hegemony over the feudal lords, and accomplished the feat of nine alliances and the restoration of order. Yet Confucius said Guan Zhong did not understand ritual propriety, for his extravagance rivaled that of his sovereign.
entries.literal: In the past, Guan Zhong served as minister to Duke Huan of Qi, achieved hegemony over the feudal lords, and accomplished the feat of uniting the lords nine times and rectifying the realm. Yet Confucius said he did not understand ritual propriety, because his extravagance rivaled that of his sovereign.

entries.zh: 夏禹卑宮室，惡衣服，后聖不循。
entries.en: The Great Yu of Xia kept his palaces humble and his garments plain—a standard that later sages failed to uphold.
entries.literal: The Great Yu of Xia kept his palaces humble and his clothing plain—later sages did not follow this standard.

entries.zh: 由此言之，治之盛也，德優矣，莫高於儉。
entries.en: From this we may conclude that for the flourishing of good governance and the perfection of virtue, nothing surpasses frugality.
entries.literal: From this we may conclude: for the flourishing of good governance, for the excellence of virtue, nothing surpasses frugality.

entries.zh: 儉化俗民，則尊卑之序得，而骨肉之恩親，爭訟之原息。
entries.en: When frugality transforms the customs of the people, the proper order between high and low is upheld, the bonds among kinfolk are strengthened, and the sources of conflict and litigation dry up.
entries.literal: When frugality transforms customs and the people, the proper order of high and low is maintained, the bonds of kinship among flesh and blood are strengthened, and the roots of conflict and litigation are extinguished.

entries.zh: 斯乃家給人足，刑錯之本也歟？
entries.en: Is this not the very foundation upon which every household is well provided, every person content, and punishments may at last be set aside?
entries.literal: Is this not the very foundation upon which every household is provided for, every person is content, and punishments may be set aside?

entries.zh: 可不務哉！
entries.en: How can we fail to devote ourselves to this!
entries.literal: How can this not be striven for!

entries.zh: 夫三公者，百寮之率，萬民之表也。
entries.en: The Three Excellencies are the leaders of all officials and the standard by which the people measure themselves.
entries.literal: The Three Excellencies are the leaders of all officials and the example for the myriad people.

entries.zh: 未有樹直表而得曲影者也。
entries.en: No one has ever planted a straight pole and obtained a crooked shadow.
entries.literal: There has never been a case where a straight pole was planted and a crooked shadow was cast.

entries.zh: 孔子不云乎，『子率而正，孰敢不正』。
entries.en: Did not Confucius say: "If you lead by setting a straight example, who would dare to go crooked?"
entries.literal: Did not Confucius say: "If you lead by being upright, who would dare not be upright?"

entries.zh: 『舉善而教不能則勸』。
entries.en: If you elevate the good and instruct those who fall short, the people will be encouraged.
entries.literal: If you raise up the good and teach those who are unable, they will be encouraged.

entries.zh: 維漢興以來，股肱宰臣身行儉約，輕財重義，較然著明，未有若故丞相平津侯公孫弘者也。
entries.en: Since the founding of the Han dynasty, among all the chief ministers who personally practiced frugality, prized righteousness over wealth, and stood out as shining examples, none has equaled the late Chancellor Gongsun Hong, the Marquis of Pingjin.
entries.literal: Since the founding of the Han dynasty, among the chief ministers who personally practiced frugality, valued righteousness over wealth, and were clearly illustrious, none has matched the late Chancellor, the Marquis of Pingjin, Gongsun Hong.

entries.zh: 位在丞相而為布被，脫粟之飯，不過一肉。
entries.en: Though he held the highest office in the land, he slept under cloth quilts, ate coarsely hulled millet, and never had more than a single dish of meat.
entries.literal: Though he held the position of Chancellor, he used cloth quilts, ate coarsely hulled millet, and had no more than a single dish of meat.

entries.zh: 故人所善賓客皆分奉祿以給之，無有所餘。
entries.en: He distributed his entire salary among his old friends and the guests he favored, leaving nothing for himself.
entries.literal: He shared his entire salary with his old friends and favored guests, leaving nothing for himself.

entries.zh: 誠內自克約而外從制。
entries.en: He was truly a man who restrained himself within, while outwardly adhering to the proper regulations.
entries.literal: He was truly self-disciplined and restrained within, while outwardly he followed the established regulations.

entries.zh: 汲黯詰之，乃聞于朝，此可謂減於制度而可施行者也。
entries.en: When Ji An confronted him and the matter became known at court, it was recognized as practicing frugality below what his rank prescribed—yet entirely worthy of emulation.
entries.literal: When Ji An confronted him, the matter became known at court. This may be called falling below what regulations prescribe, yet still worthy of being put into practice.

entries.zh: 德優則行，否則止，與內奢泰而外為詭服以釣虛譽者殊科。
entries.en: When a man's virtue is genuine, he acts upon it; when it is not, he refrains. This is altogether different from those who live in private luxury while putting on a deceptive show of austerity to fish for empty praise.
entries.literal: When virtue excels, one acts; otherwise, one refrains. This is entirely different from those who are privately extravagant yet outwardly adopt deceptive garments to fish for empty praise.

entries.zh: 以病乞骸骨，孝武皇帝即制曰『賞有功，褒有德，善善惡惡，君宜知之。
entries.en: When he pleaded illness and begged to retire, Emperor Wu immediately issued an edict: "The meritorious are to be rewarded, the virtuous honored. To commend the good and condemn the wicked—this you should know well.
entries.literal: When he pleaded illness and begged to retire, Emperor Wu immediately issued an edict saying: "The meritorious should be rewarded, the virtuous honored. To commend the good and condemn the wicked—this you should know.

entries.zh: 其省思慮，存精神，輔以醫藥』。
entries.en: Set aside your worries, conserve your strength, and attend to your recovery with the aid of physicians."
entries.literal: Set aside your worries, preserve your spirit, and attend to your recovery with the help of medicine."

entries.zh: 賜告治病，牛酒雜帛。
entries.en: The Emperor granted him leave to recover and presented him with gifts of cattle, wine, and assorted silks.
entries.literal: He was granted leave to convalesce and presented with cattle, wine, and assorted silks.

entries.zh: 居數月，有瘳，視事。
entries.en: After several months, his condition improved and he resumed his duties.
entries.literal: After several months, he recovered somewhat and returned to his duties.

entries.zh: 至元狩二年，竟以善終于相位。
entries.en: In the second year of the Yuanshou era, he died peacefully while still holding the office of Chancellor.
entries.literal: In the second year of the Yuanshou era, he ultimately died peacefully in the office of Chancellor.

entries.zh: 夫知臣莫若君，此其效也。
entries.en: No one knows a minister better than his sovereign—and this is the proof.
entries.literal: No one knows a minister better than his sovereign—this is the proof of it.

entries.zh: 弘子度嗣爵，后為山陽太守，坐法失侯。
entries.en: Gongsun Hong's son Du inherited the title. He later served as the Governor of Shanyang, but was convicted of a legal offense and stripped of his marquisate.
entries.literal: Hong's son Du inherited the title, and later served as Governor of Shanyang, but was convicted of a legal offense and lost the marquisate.

entries.zh: 夫表德章義，所以率俗厲化，聖王之制，不易之道也。
entries.en: To display virtue and make righteousness manifest, thereby leading customs and inspiring moral transformation—this is the system of the sage kings, a principle that never changes.
entries.literal: To display virtue and make righteousness manifest, so as to lead customs and inspire moral transformation—this is the system of the sage kings, an unchanging principle.

entries.zh: 其賜弘後子孫之次當為後者爵關內侯，食邑三百戶，徵詣公車，上名尚書，朕親臨拜焉。」
entries.en: Let the next descendant of Gongsun Hong in the line of succession be granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes, with an estate of three hundred households. He is to be summoned to the imperial carriage office, his name presented to the Imperial Secretariat, and I shall personally preside over his investiture.'
entries.literal: Let the next descendant in Hong's line who is due to carry on as heir be granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes, with an estate of three hundred households. He shall be summoned to the imperial carriage office, his name submitted to the Imperial Secretariat, and I shall personally preside over the investiture.'

entries.zh: 班固稱曰：公孫弘、卜式、兒寬皆以鴻漸之翼困於燕雀，遠跡羊豕之閒，非遇其時，焉能致此位乎？
entries.en: Ban Gu remarked: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi, and Er Kuan all possessed the wings of the great wild goose but languished among sparrows, their footprints lost among sheep and swine. Had they not been born at the right moment, how could they ever have risen to such positions?
entries.literal: Ban Gu remarked: Gongsun Hong, Bu Shi, and Er Kuan all possessed the wings of the soaring swan but were trapped among sparrows and swallows, leaving their traces far off among the sheep and swine. Had they not met with their time, how could they have attained such positions?

entries.zh: 是時漢興六十餘載，海內乂安，府庫充實，而四夷未賓，制度多闕，上方欲用文武，求之如弗及。
entries.en: At that time, the Han had been established for more than sixty years. The realm was peaceful, and the treasury full, yet the four barbarian peoples had not submitted, and the institutional framework remained incomplete. The Emperor was eager to employ men of both civil and martial talent, pursuing them as though he could never find enough.
entries.literal: At that time, the Han had been established for over sixty years. The land within the seas was peaceful and secure, the state treasury was full. Yet the four barbarian peoples had not yet submitted, and the institutional framework had many gaps. The Emperor was eager to employ men of both civil and martial talent, seeking them as though he could never find enough.

entries.zh: 始以蒲輪迎枚生，見主父而嘆息。
entries.en: He first dispatched a rush-cushioned carriage to welcome Master Mei, and upon meeting Zhufu Yan, sighed with admiration.
entries.literal: He first sent a rush-cushioned carriage to welcome Master Mei, and upon meeting Zhufu Yan, sighed with admiration.

entries.zh: 群臣慕向，異人并出。
entries.en: The ministers were inspired to follow this example, and extraordinary men came forward from every quarter.
entries.literal: All the ministers aspired to emulate this, and extraordinary men came forward together.

entries.zh: 卜式試於芻牧，弘羊擢於賈豎，衛青奮於奴仆，日磾出於降虜，斯亦曩時版筑飯牛之朋矣。
entries.en: Bu Shi proved himself among the shepherds, Sang Hongyang was raised from the ranks of merchants, Wei Qing rose from the condition of a slave, and Jin Midi emerged from among surrendered captives. They were the heirs of those ancient men of humble station who pounded earthen walls and fed cattle.
entries.literal: Bu Shi was tested among the shepherds, Sang Hongyang was raised from among the merchants, Wei Qing rose from servitude, and Jin Midi emerged from among surrendered captives. These were the counterparts of those ancient men who pounded walls and fed cattle.

entries.zh: 漢之得人，於茲為盛。
entries.en: Never was the Han dynasty's gathering of talent more abundant than during this era.
entries.literal: The Han's acquisition of talented men reached its zenith at this time.

entries.zh: 儒雅則公孫弘、董仲舒、兒寬，篤行則石建、石慶，質直則汲黯、卜式，推賢則韓安國、鄭當時，定令則趙禹、張湯，文章則司馬遷、相如，滑稽則東方朔、枚皋，應對則嚴助、朱買臣，歷數則唐都、落下閎，協律則李延年，運籌則桑弘羊，奉使則張騫、蘇武，將帥則衛青、霍去病，受遺則霍光、金日磾。
entries.en: In Confucian scholarship, there were Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, and Er Kuan. In steadfast conduct, Shi Jian and Shi Qing. In forthright character, Ji An and Bu Shi. In advancing the worthy, Han Anguo and Zheng Dangshi. In codifying laws, Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang. In literary achievement, Sima Qian and Sima Xiangru. In wit and humor, Dongfang Shuo and Mei Gao. In eloquent debate, Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen. In astronomy and calendrical science, Tang Du and Luoxia Hong. In harmonizing music, Li Yannian. In strategic finance, Sang Hongyang. In diplomatic missions, Zhang Qian and Su Wu. In military command, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing. In receiving the imperial testamentary charge, Huo Guang and Jin Midi.
entries.literal: In Confucian learning: Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, and Er Kuan. In steadfast conduct: Shi Jian and Shi Qing. In forthright character: Ji An and Bu Shi. In recommending the worthy: Han Anguo and Zheng Dangshi. In codifying laws: Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang. In literature: Sima Qian and Sima Xiangru. In wit: Dongfang Shuo and Mei Gao. In debate: Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen. In astronomy and mathematics: Tang Du and Luoxia Hong. In harmonizing music: Li Yannian. In strategic planning: Sang Hongyang. In diplomatic missions: Zhang Qian and Su Wu. In generalship: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing. In receiving the testamentary charge: Huo Guang and Jin Midi.

entries.zh: 其餘不可勝紀。
entries.en: The rest are far too numerous to record.
entries.literal: The rest are too numerous to record.

entries.zh: 是以興造功業，制度遺文，後世莫及。
entries.en: For this reason, the achievements accomplished, the institutions established, and the literary legacy bequeathed were unmatched by any later generation.
entries.literal: For this reason, the achievements accomplished, the institutions established, and the literary legacy left behind were unmatched by later generations.

entries.zh: 孝宣承統，纂修洪業，亦講論六藝，招選茂異，而蕭望之、梁丘賀、夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖、尹更始以儒術進，劉向、王褒以文章顯。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan inherited the line and continued the great work. He, too, lectured on the Six Arts and selected outstanding scholars. Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi rose through Confucian learning, while Liu Xiang and Wang Bao distinguished themselves through their literary accomplishments.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan inherited the dynastic line and continued to cultivate the great enterprise. He too lectured on the Six Arts and selected outstanding men. Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning, while Liu Xiang and Wang Bao achieved fame through their literary works.

entries.zh: 將相則張安世、趙充國、魏相、邴吉、于定國、杜延年，治民則黃霸、王成、龔遂、鄭弘、邵信臣、韓延壽、尹翁歸、趙廣漢之屬，皆有功跡見述於後。
entries.en: Among the generals and chief ministers were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian. Among those skilled in governing the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Zhao Guanghan, and others. All had notable achievements recorded in later accounts.
entries.literal: Among the generals and ministers were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian. Among those skilled in governing the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, and Zhao Guanghan, among others. All had achievements recorded and described in later accounts.

entries.zh: 累其名臣，亦其次也。
entries.en: The long roster of illustrious ministers that followed also merits mention, though they rank a step below.
entries.literal: The accumulated roster of illustrious ministers also ranks next after them.

entries.zh: 丞相公孫弘者，齊菑川國薛縣人也，字季。
entries.en: Chancellor Gongsun Hong hailed from Xue County in the State of Zichuan, within the lands of Qi. His courtesy name was Ji.
entries.literal: The Chancellor Gongsun Hong was a man from Xue County in the State of Zichuan in Qi, with the courtesy name Ji.

entries.zh: 少時為薛獄吏，有罪，免。
entries.en: As a young man, he served as a prison clerk in Xue, but was dismissed after committing some offense.
entries.literal: In his youth he served as a prison clerk in Xue, committed an offense, and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 家貧，牧豕海上。
entries.en: His family was destitute, and he made his living herding pigs along the seashore.
entries.literal: His family was poor, and he herded swine by the sea.

entries.zh: 年四十餘，乃學春秋雜說。
entries.en: Only after he had passed forty did he begin studying the Spring and Autumn Annals and various commentaries.
entries.literal: At over forty years of age, he then studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and miscellaneous commentaries.

entries.zh: 養後母孝謹。
entries.en: He cared for his stepmother with devoted filial piety.
entries.literal: He supported his stepmother with filial piety and care.

entries.zh: 南越王尉佗者，真定人也，姓趙氏。
entries.en: The King of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was a native of Zhending. His surname was Zhao.
entries.literal: The King of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was a man of Zhending, surnamed Zhao.

entries.zh: 秦時已并天下，略定楊越，置桂林、南海、象郡，以謫徙民，與越雜處十三歲。
entries.en: After Qin unified the realm, it conquered the Yangyue region and established the commanderies of Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiang. Exiled settlers were sent to live among the Yue people, and the two groups dwelt together for thirteen years.
entries.literal: When Qin had already unified all under heaven, it conquered and pacified Yangyue, established the commanderies of Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiang, and relocated exiled settlers there, who lived intermixed with the Yue for thirteen years.

entries.zh: 佗，秦時用為南海龍川令。
entries.en: During the Qin dynasty, Tuo served as the Magistrate of Longchuan in the Nanhai commandery.
entries.literal: Tuo was employed by Qin as the Magistrate of Longchuan in Nanhai.

entries.zh: 至二世時，南海尉任囂病且死，召龍川令趙佗語曰：「聞陳勝等作亂，秦為無道，天下苦之，項羽、劉季、陳勝、吳廣等州郡各共興軍聚眾，虎爭天下，中國擾亂，未知所安，豪傑畔秦相立。
entries.en: When the Second Emperor's reign began, the Commandant of Nanhai, Ren Xiao, fell gravely ill and lay near death. He summoned Zhao Tuo, the Magistrate of Longchuan, and told him: "I have heard that Chen Sheng and the others have risen in revolt. Qin has ruled without the Way, and the whole realm suffers for it. Xiang Yu, Liu Ji, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, and men across the commanderies and districts have all raised armies and gathered followers, fighting over the empire like tigers. The Central Plains are thrown into chaos, and no one knows where peace will come from. Great men everywhere have turned against Qin and set themselves up as rival lords.
entries.literal: When the time of the Second Emperor came, the Commandant of Nanhai, Ren Xiao, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned the Magistrate of Longchuan, Zhao Tuo, and said: "I have heard that Chen Sheng and others have raised rebellion, that Qin practices lawlessness and all under heaven suffer from it. Xiang Yu, Liu Ji, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, and others in their commanderies and districts have each raised armies and gathered followers, contending like tigers for the realm. The Central States are in turmoil, and no one knows where safety lies. Heroes have rebelled against Qin and established themselves as rulers.

entries.zh: 南海僻遠，吾恐盜兵侵地至此，吾欲興兵絕新道，自備，待諸侯變，會病甚。
entries.en: Nanhai is remote and far from the center. I fear that rebel forces may push their attacks all the way here. I had intended to raise troops and seal off the mountain passes, fortify our defenses, and wait to see how the situation among the feudal lords develops—but now I have fallen gravely ill.
entries.literal: Nanhai is remote and distant. I fear that rebel soldiers will invade and reach this place. I wished to raise troops and cut off the new roads, to prepare our own defenses, and to await changes among the feudal lords, but then I fell gravely ill.

entries.zh: 且番禺負山險，阻南海，東西數千里，頗有中國人相輔，此亦一州之主也，可以立國。
entries.en: Furthermore, Panyu is backed by rugged mountains and fronted by the Southern Sea, with territory stretching thousands of li from east to west. A fair number of people from the Central Plains are here to lend their support. This land can certainly sustain a regional lord, and a kingdom may well be founded here.
entries.literal: Moreover, Panyu has its back to steep mountains, is bordered by the Southern Sea, stretches thousands of li from east to west, and has quite a number of people from the Central States to assist. This too can be the domain of a provincial lord, and a kingdom can be established here.

entries.zh: 郡中長吏無足與言者，故召公告之。」
entries.en: Among the senior officials of the commandery, none are fit to discuss such matters. That is why I summoned you to tell you all this."
entries.literal: Among the senior officials in the commandery, there is none worthy of discussing this with, so I have summoned you to inform you of this."

entries.zh: 即被佗書，行南海尉事。
entries.en: He then issued Tuo a formal commission, entrusting him with the duties of the Commandant of Nanhai.
entries.literal: He then conferred upon Tuo a written mandate, appointing him to carry out the duties of the Commandant of Nanhai.

entries.zh: 囂死，佗即移檄告橫浦、陽山、湟谿關曰：「盜兵且至，急絕道聚兵自守！」
entries.en: After Ren Xiao died, Tuo immediately dispatched orders to the passes at Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxi: "Rebel forces are on their way! Cut off the roads at once, muster your troops, and hold your positions!"
entries.literal: When Xiao died, Tuo immediately sent dispatches to the passes at Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxi, saying: "Rebel soldiers are approaching! Urgently cut off the roads, gather troops, and defend yourselves!"

entries.zh: 因稍以法誅秦所置長吏，以其黨為假守。
entries.en: He then found legal pretexts to gradually eliminate the senior officials Qin had installed, replacing them with his own associates as acting administrators.
entries.literal: He then gradually used legal pretexts to execute the senior officials that Qin had appointed, and replaced them with his own followers as acting administrators.

entries.zh: 秦已破滅，佗即擊并桂林、象郡，自立為南越武王。
entries.en: Once Qin had fallen, Tuo attacked and absorbed the commanderies of Guilin and Xiang, then proclaimed himself the Martial King of Nanyue.
entries.literal: After Qin was destroyed, Tuo attacked and annexed the commanderies of Guilin and Xiang, and proclaimed himself the Martial King of Nanyue.

entries.zh: 高帝已定天下，為中國勞苦，故釋佗弗誅。
entries.en: After Emperor Gaozu had pacified the realm, the people of the Central Plains were exhausted from years of war, so he pardoned Tuo and refrained from punishing him.
entries.literal: After Emperor Gaozu had settled all under heaven, because the people of the Central States were weary and suffering, he pardoned Tuo and did not punish him.

entries.zh: 漢十一年，遣陸賈因立佗為南越王，與剖符通使，和集百越，毋為南邊患害，與長沙接境。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of the Han dynasty, the emperor dispatched Lu Jia to formally install Tuo as the King of Nanyue. The two sides exchanged tallies and established diplomatic relations, with the goal of pacifying the various Yue peoples so they would not cause trouble along the southern border, where Nanyue adjoined the Kingdom of Changsha.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Han, he dispatched Lu Jia to formally install Tuo as King of Nanyue, exchanged tallies and established diplomatic relations, pacified the many Yue peoples so they would not become a threat on the southern frontier, where Nanyue bordered the Kingdom of Changsha.

entries.zh: 高后時，有司請禁南越關市鐵器。
entries.en: During the reign of Empress Dowager Gao, officials petitioned to ban the sale of iron implements to Nanyue through the border markets.
entries.literal: During the time of Empress Dowager Gao, officials requested a ban on selling iron implements to Nanyue at the border markets.

entries.zh: 佗曰：「高帝立我，通使物，今高後聽讒臣，別異蠻夷，隔絕器物，此必長沙王計也，欲倚中國，擊滅南越而并王之，自為功也。」
entries.en: Tuo declared: "Emperor Gaozu installed me as king and opened trade and diplomatic relations. Now Empress Dowager Gao heeds the words of slanderous ministers, treats us as foreign barbarians, and cuts off our access to iron goods and implements. This is surely a plot by the King of Changsha, who wishes to lean on the might of the Central Plains to destroy Nanyue, annex our territory, and claim the glory for himself."
entries.literal: Tuo said: "Emperor Gaozu installed me and opened trade and envoy exchanges. Now Empress Dowager Gao listens to slanderous ministers, treats us differently as barbarians, and cuts off our access to goods and implements. This must be a scheme of the King of Changsha, who wants to rely on the Central States to attack and destroy Nanyue, annex it, and claim the credit for himself."

entries.zh: 於是佗乃自尊號為南越武帝，發兵攻長沙邊邑，敗數縣而去焉。
entries.en: At this, Tuo elevated his own title to Martial Emperor of Nanyue. He raised an army, attacked the border towns of Changsha, sacked several counties, and then withdrew.
entries.literal: Thereupon Tuo elevated his own title to Martial Emperor of Nanyue, raised troops to attack the border towns of Changsha, defeated several counties, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 高後遣將軍隆慮侯灶往擊之。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Gao dispatched General Zao, the Marquis of Longlü, to lead a campaign against him.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Gao dispatched the general, the Marquis of Longlü, Zao, to go and attack him.

entries.zh: 會暑溼，士卒大疫，兵不能踰嶺。
entries.en: As it happened, the summer heat and humidity brought a devastating plague among the troops, and the army was unable to cross the mountain passes.
entries.literal: It happened that the summer heat and humidity caused a great plague among the soldiers, and the army could not cross the mountain passes.

entries.zh: 歲餘，高后崩，即罷兵。
entries.en: Over a year later, Empress Dowager Gao died, and the campaign was promptly abandoned.
entries.literal: After more than a year, Empress Dowager Gao died, and the campaign was immediately called off.

entries.zh: 佗因此以兵威邊，財物賂遺閩越、西甌、駱，役屬焉，東西萬餘里。
entries.en: Tuo then used military might to cow the borderlands. He lavished gifts of wealth and goods upon the Minyue, the Western Ou, and the Luo, bringing them all under his dominion. His territory stretched more than ten thousand li from east to west.
entries.literal: Tuo then used military force to intimidate the border regions, and bribed Minyue, the Western Ou, and the Luo with wealth and goods, bringing them under his subordination. His territory stretched over ten thousand li from east to west.

entries.zh: 乃乘黃屋左纛，稱制，與中國侔。
entries.en: He rode in a carriage with the yellow canopy and left-side pennant reserved for an emperor, issued imperial edicts, and styled himself as the equal of the Han court.
entries.literal: He then rode in a carriage with a yellow canopy and left-side pennant, issued imperial edicts, and rivaled the Central States in status.

entries.zh: 及孝文帝元年，初鎮撫天下，使告諸侯四夷從代來即位意，喻盛德焉。
entries.en: In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, he set about bringing stability to the realm. He dispatched envoys to inform the feudal lords and the peoples of the four quarters that he had come from the Kingdom of Dai to take the throne, proclaiming his benevolent virtue.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen ascended to the throne in his first year, he first calmed and pacified the realm. He sent messengers to inform the feudal lords and the barbarians of the four quarters that he had come from Dai to take the throne, proclaiming his great virtue.

entries.zh: 乃為佗親冢在真定，置守邑，歲時奉祀。
entries.en: Since Tuo's family tombs lay in Zhending, the emperor appointed custodians for the burial grounds and ordered that sacrificial rites be performed there at the proper seasons.
entries.literal: For Tuo, whose ancestral tombs were in Zhending, the emperor appointed guardians for the settlement and had sacrificial rites performed at the proper seasons.

entries.zh: 召其從昆弟，尊官厚賜寵之。
entries.en: He summoned Tuo's cousins and kinsmen, granted them high offices and generous gifts, and treated them with great favor.
entries.literal: He summoned Tuo's cousins and relatives, bestowed high offices and generous gifts upon them, and showed them favor.

entries.zh: 詔丞相陳平等舉可使南越者，平言好畤陸賈，先帝時習使南越。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Chancellor Chen Ping and others to recommend a suitable envoy to Nanyue. Chen Ping put forward Lu Jia of Haozhi, who had previously served as envoy to Nanyue under the former emperor.
entries.literal: He ordered Chancellor Chen Ping and others to recommend someone suitable to send as envoy to Nanyue. Ping recommended Lu Jia of Haozhi, who had served as envoy to Nanyue during the previous emperor's reign.

entries.zh: 乃召賈以為太中大夫，往使。
entries.en: Lu Jia was accordingly summoned, appointed to the rank of Grand Palace Grandee, and dispatched as envoy.
entries.literal: Lu Jia was then summoned and appointed Grand Palace Grandee, and sent as envoy.

entries.zh: 因讓佗自立為帝，曾無一介之使報者。
entries.en: Lu Jia also reproached Tuo for having proclaimed himself emperor without ever sending so much as a single envoy to inform the Han court.
entries.literal: Lu Jia also reproached Tuo for having proclaimed himself emperor without ever sending even a single envoy to report it.

entries.zh: 陸賈至南越，王甚恐，為書謝，稱曰：「蠻夷大長老夫臣佗，前日高后隔異南越，竊疑長沙王讒臣，又遙聞高后盡誅佗宗族，掘燒先人冢，以故自棄，犯長沙邊境。
entries.en: When Lu Jia reached Nanyue, the king was deeply alarmed. He composed a letter of apology, which read: "Your humble barbarian subject, the Great Elder Tuo: when Empress Dowager Gao cut off relations with Nanyue, I privately suspected the King of Changsha of slandering me at court. Then I heard from afar that the Empress Dowager had executed all of my kinsmen and dug up and burned the ancestral tombs. In my despair, I cast aside all restraint and raided the Changsha border.
entries.literal: When Lu Jia arrived in Nanyue, the king was greatly alarmed. He composed a letter of apology, which read: "I, Tuo, your barbarian great chieftain and old subject: previously, when Empress Dowager Gao cut off Nanyue, I secretly suspected it was the King of Changsha slandering me. Then I heard from afar that the Empress Dowager had executed all of my kinsmen and dug up and burned the ancestral tombs. For this reason I abandoned restraint and attacked the border of Changsha.

entries.zh: 且南方卑溼，蠻夷中閒，其東閩越千人眾號稱王，其西甌駱裸國亦稱王。
entries.en: Moreover, the south is low-lying and damp, surrounded by barbarian peoples on all sides. To the east, the Minyue, with a mere thousand followers, style themselves kings. To the west, the Ou and the Luo, peoples of the naked realm, likewise call themselves kings.
entries.literal: Moreover, the south is low-lying and damp, situated among the barbarians. To the east, the Minyue, with a population of merely a thousand, style themselves king. To the west, the Ou and Luo, peoples of the naked realm, also style themselves kings.

entries.zh: 老臣妄竊帝號，聊以自娛，豈敢以聞天王哉！」
entries.en: This old subject rashly assumed the imperial title merely to amuse himself. How would I dare bring such a matter to the attention of Your Heavenly Majesty!"
entries.literal: This old subject rashly usurped the imperial title merely to amuse himself. How would I dare bring this to the attention of the Heavenly King!"

entries.zh: 乃頓首謝，願長為藩臣，奉貢職。
entries.en: He then prostrated himself in apology and pledged to serve forever as a loyal vassal, faithfully fulfilling his tribute obligations.
entries.literal: He then bowed his head to the ground in apology and expressed his wish to remain a vassal forever, fulfilling his tribute obligations.

entries.zh: 於是乃下令國中曰：「吾聞兩雄不俱立，兩賢不并世。
entries.en: He then issued a decree throughout his kingdom: "I have heard it said that two heroes cannot both stand, nor can two sages share the same age.
entries.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict throughout his kingdom, saying: "I have heard that two heroes cannot both stand, and two sages cannot coexist in the same age.

entries.zh: 皇帝，賢天子也。
entries.en: The Emperor is a virtuous Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: The Emperor is a worthy Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 自今以後，去帝制黃屋左纛。」
entries.en: From this day forward, I shall abandon the imperial title and relinquish the yellow canopy and left-side pennant."
entries.literal: From this day forward, I shall abolish the imperial style and relinquish the yellow canopy and left-side pennant."

entries.zh: 陸賈還報，孝文帝大說。
entries.en: When Lu Jia returned with this report, Emperor Wen was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: When Lu Jia returned and reported, Emperor Xiaowen was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 遂至孝景時，稱臣，使人朝請。
entries.en: Throughout the reign of Emperor Jing, Tuo continued to style himself a subject of the Han and sent envoys to pay tribute at court.
entries.literal: Continuing through the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, Tuo called himself a subject and sent envoys to present tribute at court.

entries.zh: 然南越其居國竊如故號名，其使天子，稱王朝命如諸侯。
entries.en: Within his own domain, however, Nanyue still secretly retained its former imperial titles and customs. When dealing with the Son of Heaven, Tuo styled himself merely a king and received court orders as the other feudal lords did.
entries.literal: However, within his own kingdom, Nanyue still secretly used the old imperial titles. When sending envoys to the Son of Heaven, he styled himself king and received court orders like the other feudal lords.

entries.zh: 至建元四年卒。
entries.en: Tuo lived until the fourth year of the Jianyuan era.
entries.literal: He died in the fourth year of the Jianyuan era.

entries.zh: 佗孫胡為南越王。
entries.en: Tuo's grandson Hu succeeded him as King of Nanyue.
entries.literal: Tuo's grandson Hu became the King of Nanyue.

entries.zh: 此時閩越王郢興兵擊南越邊邑，胡使人上書曰：「兩越俱為藩臣，毋得擅興兵相攻擊。
entries.en: At this time, King Ying of Minyue raised an army and attacked the border towns of Nanyue. Hu sent a memorial to the throne, stating: "Both Yue kingdoms serve as vassals of the empire. Neither should be permitted to raise troops and attack the other without authorization.
entries.literal: At this time, the King of Minyue, Ying, raised troops to attack the border towns of Nanyue. Hu sent someone to present a memorial, saying: "Both Yue kingdoms are vassal states and should not be allowed to raise troops on their own initiative to attack each other.

entries.zh: 今閩越興兵侵臣，臣不敢興兵，唯天子詔之。」
entries.en: Now Minyue has raised an army to invade my territory. I dare not take up arms on my own, and respectfully await the Son of Heaven's command."
entries.literal: Now Minyue has raised troops to invade my territory. I dare not raise troops on my own, and await only the Son of Heaven's decree."

entries.zh: 於是天子多南越義，守職約，為興師，遣兩將軍往討閩越。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven commended Nanyue's righteous adherence to its obligations. He mobilized an army and dispatched two generals to march against Minyue.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven greatly commended Nanyue for its righteousness in keeping to its duty. He raised an army and dispatched two generals to go and punish Minyue.

entries.zh: 兵未踰嶺，閩越王弟餘善殺郢以降，於是罷兵。
entries.en: Before the Han forces had even crossed the mountain passes, King Ying's younger brother Yu Shan killed him and surrendered. The campaign was thereupon called off.
entries.literal: Before the troops had crossed the mountain passes, the King of Minyue's younger brother Yu Shan killed Ying and surrendered, and the army was disbanded.

entries.zh: 天子使莊助往諭意南越王，胡頓首曰：「天子乃為臣興兵討閩越，死無以報德！」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven sent Zhuang Zhu to convey his intentions to the King of Nanyue. Hu prostrated himself and declared: "The Son of Heaven raised an army on my behalf to punish Minyue. Even in death, I could never repay such a kindness!"
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Zhuang Zhu to go and convey his intentions to the King of Nanyue. Hu bowed his head to the ground and said: "The Son of Heaven raised an army on my behalf to punish Minyue. Even in death I could not repay this kindness!"

entries.zh: 遣太子嬰齊入宿衛。
entries.en: He dispatched his crown prince, Yingqi, to serve in the palace guard at the Han capital.
entries.literal: He sent his crown prince Yingqi to serve in the palace guard at the capital.

entries.zh: 謂助曰：「國新被寇，使者行矣。
entries.en: He told Zhuang Zhu: "Our kingdom has only just been invaded. You may take your leave now.
entries.literal: He said to Zhuang Zhu: "The kingdom has just suffered an invasion. You may take your leave now.

entries.zh: 胡方日夜裝入見天子。」
entries.en: I am making preparations day and night to travel to court and present myself before the Son of Heaven."
entries.literal: I am preparing day and night to go and present myself before the Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 助去後，其大臣諫胡曰：「漢興兵誅郢，亦行以驚動南越。
entries.en: After Zhuang Zhu departed, the senior ministers remonstrated with Hu: "The Han raised an army to punish Ying, but their purpose was also to intimidate Nanyue.
entries.literal: After Zhu left, the senior ministers remonstrated with Hu, saying: "The Han raised an army to punish Ying, but also did so to intimidate Nanyue.

entries.zh: 且先王昔言，事天子期無失禮，要之不可以說好語入見。
entries.en: Moreover, the former king once warned that in serving the Son of Heaven, the key is never to fail in courtesy—but under no circumstances should one be sweet-talked into appearing at court in person.
entries.literal: Moreover, the former king once said that in serving the Son of Heaven, one should aim not to fail in propriety, but above all must not be lured by sweet words into going to court in person.

entries.zh: 入見則不得復歸，亡國之勢也。」
entries.en: Once you go to court, you will never be permitted to return. That would mean the ruin of our kingdom."
entries.literal: If you go to court, you will never be allowed to return. This would mean the end of our kingdom."

entries.zh: 於是胡稱病，竟不入見。
entries.en: At this, Hu pleaded illness and ultimately never went to court.
entries.literal: Thereupon Hu claimed illness and in the end never went to court.

entries.zh: 後十餘歲，胡實病甚，太子嬰齊請歸。
entries.en: More than ten years later, Hu genuinely fell gravely ill. Crown Prince Yingqi asked permission to return home.
entries.literal: More than ten years later, Hu truly fell seriously ill, and Crown Prince Yingqi requested permission to return home.

entries.zh: 胡薨，謚為文王。
entries.en: When Hu died, he was given the posthumous title of King Wen, the Cultured King.
entries.literal: Hu died and was posthumously titled King Wen.

entries.zh: 太子興代立，其母為太后。
entries.en: Crown Prince Xing succeeded to the throne, and his mother was elevated to the rank of Queen Dowager.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Xing succeeded to the throne, and his mother became the Queen Dowager.

entries.zh: 太后自未為嬰齊姬時，嘗與霸陵人安國少季通。
entries.en: Even before the Queen Dowager had become Yingqi's consort, she had carried on an affair with a man named An Guoshaoji from Baling.
entries.literal: Before the Queen Dowager had become Yingqi's consort, she had once had an affair with An Guoshaoji, a man of Baling.

entries.zh: 及嬰齊薨後，元鼎四年，漢使安國少季往諭王、王太后以入朝，比內諸侯；
entries.en: After Yingqi's death, in the fourth year of the Yuanding era, the Han court dispatched An Guoshaoji to persuade the king and the Queen Dowager to present themselves at court and accept the status of inner feudal lords.
entries.literal: After Yingqi died, in the fourth year of the Yuanding era, the Han sent An Guoshaoji to persuade the king and the Queen Dowager to come to court and accept the status of inner feudal lords.

entries.zh: 令辯士諫大夫終軍等宣其辭，勇士魏臣等輔其缺，衛尉路博德將兵屯桂陽，待使者。
entries.en: The court also ordered the eloquent Remonstrance Grandee Zhong Jun and others to present the arguments, the brave warrior Wei Chen and others to assist where needed, and the Commandant of Guards Lu Bode to station troops at Guiyang in readiness for the envoys.
entries.literal: The eloquent Remonstrance Grandee Zhong Jun and others were ordered to deliver the persuasive arguments, the brave warrior Wei Chen and others to supplement their shortcomings, and the Commandant of Guards Lu Bode to station troops at Guiyang and await the envoys.
