entries.zh: 王年少，太後中國人也，嘗與安國少季通，其使復私焉。
entries.en: The king was young, and the Queen Dowager, who was originally from the Central Plains, had previously been An Guoshaoji's lover. When he arrived as envoy, the two resumed their affair.
entries.literal: The king was young. The Queen Dowager was originally from the Central States and had previously had an affair with An Guoshaoji. When he came as envoy, she resumed their private relationship.

entries.zh: 國人頗知之，多不附太后。
entries.en: The people of the kingdom were well aware of the affair, and many withheld their support from the Queen Dowager.
entries.literal: The people of the kingdom became quite aware of this and many did not support the Queen Dowager.

entries.zh: 太后恐亂起，亦欲倚漢威，數勸王及群臣求內屬。
entries.en: The Queen Dowager, fearing that unrest might break out, sought to rely on the might of the Han dynasty. She repeatedly urged the king and his ministers to petition for the status of inner subjects of the Han.
entries.literal: The Queen Dowager feared that disorder would break out. She also wished to rely on the power of the Han, and repeatedly urged the king and the ministers to seek the status of inner subjects.

entries.zh: 即因使者上書，請比內諸侯，三歲一朝，除邊關。
entries.en: Through the envoys, a memorial was submitted requesting that Nanyue be treated as an inner feudal state, pay court once every three years, and have the border passes abolished.
entries.literal: Through the envoys, a memorial was submitted requesting the status of inner feudal lords, to pay court once every three years, and to abolish the border passes.

entries.zh: 於是天子許之，賜其丞相呂嘉銀印，及內史、中尉、太傅印，餘得自置。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven approved the request. He bestowed silver seals upon the chancellor, Lu Jia, as well as seals for the positions of Inner Historian, Colonel of the Guard, and Grand Tutor. The remaining officials could be appointed by Nanyue at its own discretion.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven approved the request and bestowed silver seals upon the Chancellor Lu Jia, as well as seals for the Inner Historian, the Colonel of the Guard, and the Grand Tutor. The remaining officials could be appointed by Nanyue itself.

entries.zh: 除其故黥劓刑，用漢法，比內諸侯。
entries.en: The old punishments of tattooing and nose-cutting were abolished, Han law was adopted, and Nanyue was treated on the same footing as the inner feudal lords.
entries.literal: The old punishments of branding and nose-cutting were abolished, Han law was adopted, and Nanyue was treated on par with the inner feudal lords.

entries.zh: 使者皆留填撫之。
entries.en: All the envoys remained in Nanyue to help maintain order and stability.
entries.literal: The envoys all remained to garrison and pacify the kingdom.

entries.zh: 王、王太后飭治行裝重齎，為入朝具。
entries.en: The king and the Queen Dowager began outfitting their traveling retinue and assembling lavish gifts in preparation for the journey to court.
entries.literal: The king and the Queen Dowager prepared their travel equipment and lavish gifts, making ready for the journey to court.

entries.zh: 元鼎五年秋，衛尉路博德為伏波將軍，出桂陽，下匯水；
entries.en: In the autumn of the fifth year of the Yuanding era, the Commandant of Guards Lu Bode was appointed General Who Calms the Waves. He marched out from Guiyang and descended the Hui River.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of the Yuanding era, the Commandant of Guards Lu Bode was appointed General Who Calms the Waves. He set out from Guiyang and descended the Hui River.

entries.zh: 主爵都尉楊仆為樓船將軍，出豫章，下橫浦；
entries.en: Yang Pu, the Commandant of Titles, was appointed General of the Tower Ships. He marched out from Yuzhang and descended through the Hengpu Pass.
entries.literal: The Commandant of Titles Yang Pu was appointed General of the Tower Ships. He set out from Yuzhang and descended through the Hengpu Pass.

entries.zh: 故歸義越侯二人為戈船、下厲將軍，出零陵，或下離水，或柢蒼梧；
entries.en: Two former Yue marquises who had submitted to the Han were appointed General of the War-Boats and General of the Lower Li. They set out from Lingling—one descending the Li River, the other advancing toward Cangwu.
entries.literal: Two former Yue marquises who had submitted to the Han were appointed the General of the War-Boat and the General of the Lower Li. They set out from Lingling, one descending the Li River and the other heading for Cangwu.

entries.zh: 使馳義侯因巴蜀罪人，發夜郎兵，下牂柯江：咸會番禺。
entries.en: The Marquis Who Gallops for Righteousness was ordered to recruit convicts from Ba and Shu, mobilize the soldiers of Yelang, and descend the Zangke River. All forces were to converge on Panyu.
entries.literal: The Marquis Who Gallops for Righteousness was ordered to use convicts from Ba and Shu, mobilize the troops of Yelang, and descend the Zangke River. All were to converge on Panyu.

entries.zh: 元鼎六年冬，樓船將軍將精卒先陷尋陜，破石門，得越船粟，因推而前，挫越鋒，以數萬人待伏波。
entries.en: In the winter of the sixth year of the Yuanding era, the General of the Tower Ships led his elite troops in capturing Xunxia first, then broke through the Stone Gate, seized Yue boats and grain stores, and pressed forward, blunting the Yue vanguard. He halted with tens of thousands of troops to await the General Who Calms the Waves.
entries.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of the Yuanding era, the General of the Tower Ships led his elite troops to first take Xunxia, broke through Shimen, captured Yue boats and grain, and pressed forward, blunting the Yue vanguard. He then waited with tens of thousands of men for the General Who Calms the Waves.

entries.zh: 伏波將軍將罪人，道遠，會期後，與樓船會乃有千餘人，遂俱進。
entries.en: The General Who Calms the Waves, leading his convict soldiers, had a long march and arrived after the appointed time. When he linked up with the Tower Ships general, he had only a little over a thousand men. Nevertheless, the two forces advanced together.
entries.literal: The General Who Calms the Waves led convict soldiers. The road was long, he missed the rendezvous deadline, and when he joined up with the Tower Ships general, he had only a little more than a thousand men. They then advanced together.

entries.zh: 樓船居前，至番禺。
entries.en: The Tower Ships general took the vanguard and arrived at Panyu.
entries.literal: The Tower Ships general took the lead and reached Panyu.

entries.zh: 建德、嘉皆城守。
entries.en: Jiande and Lu Jia had fortified the city and held their positions.
entries.literal: Jiande and Lu Jia both defended the city.

entries.zh: 樓船自擇便處，居東南面；
entries.en: The Tower Ships general chose a favorable position on the southeast side of the city.
entries.literal: The Tower Ships general chose a favorable position and took the southeast side of the city.

entries.zh: 伏波居西北面。
entries.en: The General Who Calms the Waves took up position on the northwest side.
entries.literal: The General Who Calms the Waves took the northwest side.

entries.zh: 會暮，樓船攻敗越人，縱火燒城。
entries.en: As dusk fell, the Tower Ships general launched his attack and defeated the Yue defenders, then set fire to the city.
entries.literal: At dusk, the Tower Ships general attacked and defeated the Yue defenders, and set fire to the city.

entries.zh: 越素聞伏波名，日暮，不知其兵多少。
entries.en: The Yue had long heard of the fearsome reputation of the General Who Calms the Waves. In the darkness, they had no way of knowing the size of his forces.
entries.literal: The Yue had long heard of the reputation of the General Who Calms the Waves. Now that darkness had fallen, they did not know the size of his forces.

entries.zh: 伏波乃為營，遣使者招降者，賜印，復縱令相招。
entries.en: The General Who Calms the Waves set up camp, sent out messengers to offer terms to those willing to surrender, bestowed seals upon them, and then released them to recruit more defectors.
entries.literal: The General Who Calms the Waves then made camp, sent out messengers to summon those who would surrender, bestowed seals upon them, and let them go to recruit others in turn.

entries.zh: 樓船力攻燒敵，反驅而入伏波營中。
entries.en: The Tower Ships general pressed his attack and set fires, but in the chaos, the fleeing Yue soldiers were driven straight into the camp of the General Who Calms the Waves.
entries.literal: The Tower Ships general attacked and burned the enemy with full force, but the fleeing enemy were driven into the camp of the General Who Calms the Waves instead.

entries.zh: 犁旦，城中皆降伏波。
entries.en: By dawn, the entire city had surrendered to the General Who Calms the Waves.
entries.literal: By dawn, everyone in the city had surrendered to the General Who Calms the Waves.

entries.zh: 呂嘉、建德已夜與其屬數百人亡入海，以船西去。
entries.en: Lu Jia and Jiande had slipped away under cover of night with several hundred followers, fleeing to the sea and sailing westward.
entries.literal: Lu Jia and Jiande had already fled during the night with several hundred of their followers, escaping to the sea and sailing westward by boat.

entries.zh: 伏波又因問所得降者貴人，以知呂嘉所之，遣人追之。
entries.en: The General Who Calms the Waves interrogated the surrendered nobles to learn where Lu Jia had fled, then sent men in pursuit.
entries.literal: The General Who Calms the Waves interrogated the captured nobles who had surrendered to learn Lu Jia's whereabouts, and sent men in pursuit.

entries.zh: 以其故校尉司馬蘇弘得建德，封為海常侯；
entries.en: His former Colonel Commandant, Su Hong, captured Jiande and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Haichang.
entries.literal: His former Colonel Commandant Su Hong captured Jiande and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Haichang.

entries.zh: 越郎都稽得嘉，封為臨蔡侯。
entries.en: A Yue Gentleman-Attendant named Du Ji captured Lu Jia and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Lincai.
entries.literal: The Yue Gentleman-Attendant Du Ji captured Lu Jia and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Lincai.

entries.zh: 天子聞嘉不聽王，王、王太后弱孤不能制，使者怯無決。
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven learned that Lu Jia defied the king, that the king and the Queen Dowager were too weak and isolated to control him, and that the envoys were timid and indecisive.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven heard that Lu Jia refused to obey the king, that the king and the Queen Dowager were weak and isolated and could not control him, and that the envoys were timid and irresolute.

entries.zh: 又以為王、王太后已附漢，獨呂嘉為亂，不足以興兵，欲使莊參以二千人往使。
entries.en: He also reckoned that since the king and the Queen Dowager had already aligned with the Han, it was Lu Jia alone who was causing trouble. This did not warrant a full military campaign. He planned to send Zhuang Can with two thousand men on a diplomatic mission.
entries.literal: He also believed that since the king and Queen Dowager had already submitted to Han, it was Lu Jia alone who was causing trouble. This was not sufficient grounds to raise a full army. He wished to send Zhuang Can with two thousand men as an envoy.

entries.zh: 參曰：「以好往，數人足矣；
entries.en: Zhuang Can replied: "If the purpose is diplomacy, a handful of men will do.
entries.literal: Zhuang Can said: "If the mission is a friendly one, a few men will suffice.

entries.zh: 以武往，二千人無足以為也。」
entries.en: If the purpose is war, two thousand men are nowhere near enough."
entries.literal: If the mission is a military one, two thousand men are far from sufficient."

entries.zh: 辭不可，天子罷參也。
entries.en: He firmly declined the assignment, and the Son of Heaven relieved him of it.
entries.literal: He firmly declined, and the Son of Heaven dismissed Zhuang Can from the assignment.

entries.zh: 郟壯士故濟北相韓千秋奮曰：「以區區之越，又有王、太后應，獨相呂嘉為害，願得勇士二百人，必斬嘉以報。」
entries.en: Han Qianqiu, a bold warrior from Jia and former Chancellor of Jibei, stepped forward and declared: "Yue is a trifling state, and the king and the Queen Dowager are on our side. Only Chancellor Lu Jia stands in the way. Give me two hundred brave men, and I will take Lu Jia's head."
entries.literal: The bold warrior Han Qianqiu from Jia, the former Chancellor of Jibei, stepped forward and declared: "Against such a small state as Yue, and with the king and Queen Dowager on our side, it is only Chancellor Lu Jia who is causing trouble. Give me two hundred brave men, and I will surely behead Lu Jia and bring back his head."

entries.zh: 於是天子遣千秋與王太后弟樛樂將二千人往，入越境。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven then dispatched Han Qianqiu along with the Queen Dowager's younger brother, Jiu Le, at the head of two thousand soldiers to enter Yue territory.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven then dispatched Han Qianqiu, together with the Queen Dowager's younger brother Jiu Le, to lead two thousand men into Yue territory.

entries.zh: 呂嘉等乃遂反，下令國中曰：「王年少。
entries.en: Lu Jia and his faction then launched their rebellion in earnest, issuing a proclamation throughout the kingdom: "The king is young.
entries.literal: Lu Jia and his faction then launched their rebellion and issued a proclamation throughout the kingdom: "The king is young.

entries.zh: 太後，中國人也，又與使者亂，專欲內屬，盡持先王寶器入獻天子以自媚，多從人，行至長安，虜賣以為僮仆。
entries.en: The Queen Dowager is a woman from the Central Plains who has carried on a sordid affair with the envoy. She is bent on submitting our kingdom to the Han, carrying off all the treasures of the former kings to present to the Son of Heaven and ingratiate herself. She plans to take many of our people along to Chang'an, where they will be seized and sold into servitude.
entries.literal: The Queen Dowager is a woman from the Central States who has had illicit relations with the envoy. She is intent on submitting to Han as an inner subject, taking all the treasures of the former kings to present to the Son of Heaven in order to curry favor. She plans to bring many of our people with her to Chang'an, where they will be captured and sold as slaves and servants.

entries.zh: 取自脫一時之利，無顧趙氏社稷，為萬世慮計之意。」
entries.en: She seeks only to save herself for a fleeting advantage, with no thought for the Zhao ancestral altars or for the kingdom's future across ten thousand generations."
entries.literal: She seeks only to save herself for a moment's advantage, with no thought for the Zhao ancestral altars or for plans that would last ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 乃與其弟將卒攻殺王、太后及漢使者。
entries.en: Lu Jia and his brother then led their soldiers in an assault on the palace, killing the king, the Queen Dowager, and the Han envoys.
entries.literal: Lu Jia and his brother then led their soldiers in an attack, killing the king, the Queen Dowager, and the Han envoys.

entries.zh: 遣人告蒼梧秦王及其諸郡縣，立明王長男越妻子術陽侯建德為王。
entries.en: He sent word to the King of Cangwu and to all the commanderies and counties, and installed as the new king Jiande, the Marquis of Shuyang, who was King Ming's eldest son by a Yue wife.
entries.literal: He sent men to inform the King of Cangwu and all the commanderies and counties, and installed King Ming's eldest son Jiande, the Marquis of Shuyang, who was born of a Yue wife, as the new king.

entries.zh: 而韓千秋兵入，破數小邑。
entries.en: Meanwhile, Han Qianqiu's forces crossed into Yue and overran several small towns.
entries.literal: Meanwhile, Han Qianqiu's forces entered Yue and captured several small towns.

entries.zh: 其後越直開道給食，未至番禺四十里，越以兵擊千秋等，遂滅之。
entries.en: The Yue then deliberately cleared the roads and provided provisions to lure them deeper. When the Han force was within forty li of Panyu, the Yue attacked and annihilated Han Qianqiu and all his men.
entries.literal: Afterwards, the Yue deliberately opened the roads and provided provisions. When they were within forty li of Panyu, the Yue attacked Han Qianqiu and his men with their forces, and annihilated them all.

entries.zh: 使人函封漢使者節置塞上，好為謾辭謝罪，發兵守要害處。
entries.en: They sealed the credentials of the Han envoys in a case and left them at the frontier pass. They composed a disingenuous letter of apology and deployed troops to guard the strategic passes.
entries.literal: They then had the credentials of the Han envoys sealed in a box and placed at the frontier pass. They composed deceitful words of apology and deployed troops to guard the strategic positions.

entries.zh: 於是天子曰：「韓千秋雖無成功，亦軍鋒之冠。」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven declared: "Although Han Qianqiu did not succeed, he was the vanguard of our military valor."
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven said: "Although Han Qianqiu did not succeed, he was still the foremost in martial courage."

entries.zh: 封其子延年為成安侯。
entries.en: He made Han Qianqiu's son Yannian Marquis of Cheng'an.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Han Qianqiu's son Yannian as the Marquis of Cheng'an.

entries.zh: 樛樂，其姊為王太后，首願屬漢，封其子廣德為龍亢侯。
entries.en: As for Jiu Le, whose elder sister had been the Queen Dowager—he had been the first to volunteer to submit to the Han. His son Guangde was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Longkang.
entries.literal: As for Jiu Le, whose elder sister was the Queen Dowager, he had been the first to express willingness to submit to Han. His son Guangde was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Longkang.

entries.zh: 乃下赦曰：「天子微，諸侯力政，譏臣不討賊。
entries.en: The emperor then issued an edict: "When the Son of Heaven's authority wanes, the feudal lords seize power by force, and ministers are condemned for failing to punish rebels.
entries.literal: The emperor then issued an edict saying: "When the Son of Heaven is weak, the feudal lords rule by force, and ministers are reproached for not punishing rebels.

entries.zh: 今呂嘉、建德等反，自立晏如，令罪人及江淮以南樓船十萬師往討之。」
entries.en: Now Lu Jia, Jiande, and the rest have risen in rebellion and sit at ease as though nothing were amiss. I hereby command that convicts and a hundred thousand tower-ship soldiers from south of the Yangzi and Huai be dispatched to crush them."
entries.literal: Now Lu Jia, Jiande, and the others have rebelled and established themselves as though nothing were amiss. I hereby order convicts and one hundred thousand tower-ship soldiers from south of the Yangzi and Huai rivers to go and punish them."

entries.zh: 閩越王無諸及越東海王搖者，其先皆越王句踐之後也，姓騶氏。
entries.en: Wuzhu, the King of Minyue, and Yao, the King of Eastern Sea Yue, were both descendants of King Goujian of Yue and bore the clan name Zou.
entries.literal: The King of Minyue, Wuzhu, and the King of the Eastern Sea Yue, Yao, were both descendants of King Goujian of Yue, and bore the surname Zou.

entries.zh: 秦已并天下，皆廢為君長，以其地為閩中郡。
entries.en: When the Qin dynasty united the realm, it stripped them of their royal titles, reducing them to local chieftains, and incorporated their territory into the Commandery of Minzhong.
entries.literal: After Qin had unified the realm, it deposed them all to the status of chieftains and made their territory the Commandery of Minzhong.

entries.zh: 及諸侯畔秦，無諸、搖率越歸鄱陽令吳芮，所謂鄱君者也，從諸侯滅秦。
entries.en: When the lords rose against Qin, Wuzhu and Yao led their Yue followers to join Wu Rui, the magistrate of Poyang—known as Lord Po—and fought alongside the other lords to bring down the Qin dynasty.
entries.literal: When the feudal lords rebelled against Qin, Wuzhu and Yao led the Yue people to submit to the magistrate of Poyang, Wu Rui—the one known as Lord Po—and joined the feudal lords in overthrowing Qin.

entries.zh: 當是之時，項籍主命，弗王，以故不附楚。
entries.en: At that time, Xiang Yu held the power to bestow titles but did not make them kings, and so they never aligned themselves with Chu.
entries.literal: At that time, Xiang Ji held the power to grant titles and did not make them kings, so they did not attach themselves to Chu.

entries.zh: 漢擊項籍，無諸、搖率越人佐漢。
entries.en: When the Han forces campaigned against Xiang Yu, Wuzhu and Yao led their Yue warriors to fight on the side of Han.
entries.literal: When Han attacked Xiang Ji, Wuzhu and Yao led the Yue people to assist Han.

entries.zh: 漢五年，復立無諸為閩越王，王閩中故地，都東冶。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Han dynasty, Wuzhu was restored as the King of Minyue, reigning over the old Minzhong territory from his capital at Dongye.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Han, Wuzhu was again established as the King of Minyue, ruling over the former territory of Minzhong, with his capital at Dongye.

entries.zh: 孝惠三年，舉高帝時越功，曰閩君搖功多，其民便附，乃立搖為東海王，都東甌，世俗號為東甌王。
entries.en: In the third year of Emperor Hui's reign, the court reviewed the wartime contributions of the Yue dating back to Emperor Gao's era. It was noted that Yao, the lord of Min, had distinguished himself through exceptional service and commanded the loyal devotion of his people. He was therefore made the King of the Eastern Sea, with his capital at Dong'ou—and so the people came to call him the King of Dong'ou.
entries.literal: In the third year of Emperor Xiaohui, reviewing the merits of the Yue from the time of Emperor Gao, it was said that Lord Yao of Min had rendered great service and his people readily submitted to him, so Yao was established as the King of the Eastern Sea, with his capital at Dong'ou; the common people called him the King of Dong'ou.

entries.zh: 後數世，至孝景三年，吳王濞反，欲從閩越，閩越未肯行，獨東甌從吳。
entries.en: Several generations later, in the third year of Emperor Jing's reign, King Bi of Wu launched his rebellion and tried to recruit the Minyue to his cause, but they refused. Only Dong'ou chose to side with Wu.
entries.literal: Several generations later, in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing, King Bi of Wu rebelled and sought to enlist Minyue, but Minyue refused to go along; only Dong'ou joined Wu.

entries.zh: 及吳破，東甌受漢購，殺吳王丹徒，以故皆得不誅，歸國。
entries.en: After Wu fell, Dong'ou accepted a bounty from the Han court and killed the King of Wu at Dantu. For this reason they were all spared punishment and allowed to return to their kingdoms.
entries.literal: When Wu was defeated, Dong'ou accepted Han's bounty and killed the King of Wu at Dantu, and for this reason all were spared execution and returned to their kingdoms.

entries.zh: 吳王子子駒亡走閩越，怨東甌殺其父，常勸閩越擊東甌。
entries.en: Ziju, the prince of Wu, fled to Minyue. Harboring a deep resentment against Dong'ou for slaying his father, he constantly urged the Minyue to attack them.
entries.literal: The son of the King of Wu, Ziju, fled to Minyue, bore a grudge against Dong'ou for killing his father, and constantly urged Minyue to attack Dong'ou.

entries.zh: 至建元三年，閩越發兵圍東甌。
entries.en: In the third year of the Jianyuan era, the Minyue sent their army to lay siege to Dong'ou.
entries.literal: In the third year of the Jianyuan era, Minyue dispatched troops to besiege Dong'ou.

entries.zh: 東甌食盡，困，且降，乃使人告急天子。
entries.en: Dong'ou's provisions ran out. Desperate and on the brink of surrender, they dispatched envoys to make an urgent appeal to the emperor.
entries.literal: Dong'ou's food supplies were exhausted, they were in dire straits, and on the verge of surrender, so they sent envoys to urgently appeal to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 天子問太尉田蚡，蚡對曰：「越人相攻擊，固其常，又數反覆，不足以煩中國往救也。
entries.en: The emperor consulted Grand Commandant Tian Fen, who replied: 'The Yue attacking one another is simply their custom. They have been fickle time and again, and it is hardly worth troubling the Middle Kingdom to send troops to rescue them.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven consulted Grand Commandant Tian Fen. Fen replied: 'The Yue people attacking each other is simply their custom; moreover, they have been fickle time and again, so it is not worth troubling the Middle Kingdom to go rescue them.

entries.zh: 自秦時棄弗屬。」
entries.en: They have been beyond our domain since the days of Qin.'
entries.literal: Since the time of Qin, they have been abandoned and not governed.'

entries.zh: 於是中大夫莊助詰蚡曰：「特患力弗能救，德弗能覆；
entries.en: At this, the Palace Grandee Zhuang Zhu confronted Fen, saying: 'The only question is whether we lack the strength to rescue them or the virtue to shelter them;
entries.literal: Thereupon the Palace Grandee Zhuang Zhu challenged Fen, saying: 'One would only worry that our strength might be insufficient to rescue them or our virtue insufficient to shelter them;

entries.zh: 誠能，何故棄之？
entries.en: If we truly have the power, why should we abandon them?
entries.literal: If we truly are able, why then abandon them?

entries.zh: 且秦舉咸陽而棄之，何乃越也！
entries.en: Moreover, Qin abandoned even Xianyang itself—how much less should we trouble ourselves over Yue!
entries.literal: Moreover, Qin abandoned even Xianyang itself—how much less should we fuss about Yue!

entries.zh: 今小國以窮困來告急天子，天子弗振，彼當安所告愬？
entries.en: Now a small kingdom, driven to desperation, has come to plead with the emperor. If the emperor refuses to act, where else are they to turn?
entries.literal: Now a small kingdom comes in desperation to urgently appeal to the Son of Heaven; if the Son of Heaven does not come to its aid, where else shall they turn to plead their case?

entries.zh: 又何以子萬國乎？」
entries.en: And how then can we claim to be a parent to the myriad kingdoms?'
entries.literal: And how then can we serve as parent to the ten thousand kingdoms?'

entries.zh: 上曰：「太尉未足與計。
entries.en: The emperor said: 'The Grand Commandant is not fit to be consulted on this matter.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'The Grand Commandant is not one to plan with.

entries.zh: 吾初即位，不欲出虎符發兵郡國。」
entries.en: I have only just come to the throne, and I am reluctant to issue the tiger tallies to mobilize the armies of the commanderies and kingdoms.'
entries.literal: I have only just ascended the throne and do not wish to issue tiger tallies to mobilize troops from the commanderies and kingdoms.'

entries.zh: 乃遣莊助以節發兵會稽。
entries.en: He therefore sent Zhuang Zhu with an imperial tally to raise troops from Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Then he dispatched Zhuang Zhu with the imperial credentials to mobilize troops from Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 會稽太守欲距不為發兵，助乃斬一司馬，諭意指，遂發兵浮海救東甌。
entries.en: The Grand Administrator of Kuaiji tried to obstruct the mobilization, but Zhu executed one of his colonels to demonstrate his authority, and the troops were duly dispatched across the sea to relieve Dong'ou.
entries.literal: The Grand Administrator of Kuaiji wanted to refuse and would not dispatch troops, but Zhu then executed one colonel, made his intentions clear, and thereupon mobilized the troops to sail across the sea and rescue Dong'ou.

entries.zh: 未至，閩越引兵而去。
entries.en: Before the relief force even arrived, the Minyue pulled back their troops and withdrew.
entries.literal: Before they arrived, Minyue withdrew its troops and departed.

entries.zh: 東甌請舉國徙中國，乃悉舉眾來，處江淮之閒。
entries.en: Dong'ou petitioned to relocate their entire kingdom to the interior. They moved all their people and resettled in the lands between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.
entries.literal: Dong'ou requested to relocate the entire kingdom to the interior, so they moved all their people and settled between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.

entries.zh: 至建元六年，閩越擊南越。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the Jianyuan era, the Minyue launched an attack on Nanyue.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of the Jianyuan era, Minyue attacked Nanyue.

entries.zh: 南越守天子約，不敢擅發兵擊而以聞。
entries.en: Nanyue honored its covenant with the emperor and refrained from retaliating on its own, choosing instead to report the aggression to the court.
entries.literal: Nanyue observed the Son of Heaven's covenant and did not dare to send troops on its own to counterattack, but instead reported the matter.

entries.zh: 上遣大行王恢出豫章，大農韓安國出會稽，皆為將軍。
entries.en: The emperor sent the Grand Herald Wang Hui forth from Yuzhang and the Grand Minister of Agriculture Han Anguo from Kuaiji, each to serve as a commanding general.
entries.literal: The emperor dispatched the Grand Herald Wang Hui from Yuzhang and the Grand Minister of Agriculture Han Anguo from Kuaiji, both serving as generals.

entries.zh: 兵未踰嶺，閩越王郢發兵距險。
entries.en: Before the Han armies had even crossed the mountain passes, King Ying of Minyue sent his own troops to fortify the defiles.
entries.literal: Before the troops had crossed the mountain ranges, the King of Minyue, Ying, dispatched troops to hold the defiles.

entries.zh: 其弟餘善乃與相、宗族謀曰：「王以擅發兵擊南越，不請，故天子兵來誅。
entries.en: His younger brother, Yu Shan, conspired with the chancellor and their kinsmen, saying: 'The king attacked Nanyue without imperial permission, and that is why the emperor's armies have come to punish him.
entries.literal: His younger brother Yu Shan then plotted with the chancellor and the clansmen, saying: 'The king launched an unauthorized attack on Nanyue without requesting permission, so the Son of Heaven's troops have come to punish him.

entries.zh: 今漢兵眾彊，今即幸勝之，后來益多，終滅國而止。
entries.en: The Han armies are vast and powerful. Even if we were lucky enough to repel them today, they would only send more, and in the end our kingdom would be destroyed.
entries.literal: Now the Han troops are numerous and strong; even if we are fortunate enough to defeat them now, more will come later, and it will only end with the destruction of our kingdom.

entries.zh: 今殺王以謝天子。
entries.en: Let us kill the king and apologize to the emperor.
entries.literal: Let us now kill the king to apologize to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 天子聽，罷兵，固一國完；
entries.en: If the emperor accepts, he will withdraw his forces, and the kingdom can be preserved;
entries.literal: If the Son of Heaven accepts, he will withdraw the troops, and surely the kingdom will be preserved intact;

entries.zh: 不聽，乃力戰；
entries.en: If he does not, then we fight with everything we have;
entries.literal: If he does not accept, then we fight with all our strength;

entries.zh: 不勝，即亡入海。」
entries.en: And if we cannot prevail, we flee to the sea.'
entries.literal: If we cannot win, then we flee into the sea.'

entries.zh: 皆曰「善」。
entries.en: They all said, "Good."
entries.literal: All said: 'Agreed.'

entries.zh: 即鏦殺王，使使奉其頭致大行。
entries.en: They struck the king down and sent an envoy to deliver his head to the Grand Herald.
entries.literal: They then assassinated the king with a lance and sent an envoy to present his head to the Grand Herald.

entries.zh: 大行曰：「所為來者誅王。
entries.en: The Grand Herald declared: 'Our purpose in coming was to punish the king.
entries.literal: The Grand Herald said: 'The reason we came was to execute the king.

entries.zh: 今王頭至，謝罪，不戰而耘，利莫大焉。」
entries.en: Now that the king's head has been delivered, and they have submitted, we reap the harvest without shedding a drop of blood—there is no greater advantage.'
entries.literal: Now the king's head has arrived, they have apologized for their crimes, and we achieve our aim without battle—there is no greater advantage than this.'

entries.zh: 乃以便宜案兵告大農軍，而使使奉王頭馳報天子。
entries.en: Acting on his own authority, he halted the advance and notified the army of the Grand Minister of Agriculture, while dispatching a rider to present the king's head to the emperor.
entries.literal: He then, acting on his own discretion, halted the troops and informed the Grand Minister of Agriculture's army, while sending an envoy to present the king's head and gallop to report to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 詔罷兩將兵，曰：「郢等首惡，獨無諸孫繇君丑不與謀焉。」
entries.en: An imperial edict ordered both armies to stand down, declaring: 'Ying and his accomplices were the chief culprits. Only Chou, Lord Yao, a grandson of Wuzhu, had no part in the conspiracy.'
entries.literal: An edict dismissed both generals' troops, stating: 'Ying and the others were the principal offenders; only Chou, Lord Yao, the grandson of Wuzhu, did not participate in the conspiracy.'

entries.zh: 乃使郎中將立丑為越繇王，奉閩越先祭祀。
entries.en: A Palace Gentleman-General was then dispatched to install Chou as the King of Yueyao, charged with maintaining the ancestral rites of the Minyue.
entries.literal: Then a Palace Gentleman was sent to establish Chou as King of Yueyao, to maintain the ancestral sacrifices of Minyue.

entries.zh: 餘善已殺郢，威行於國，國民多屬，竊自立為王。
entries.en: Having killed Ying, Yu Shan's authority spread across the land. The people rallied to him in great numbers, and he secretly proclaimed himself king.
entries.literal: After Yu Shan had killed Ying, his authority prevailed throughout the kingdom, many of the people attached themselves to him, and he secretly declared himself king.

entries.zh: 繇王不能矯其眾持正。
entries.en: The King of Yao could not correct his people and uphold proper order.
entries.literal: The King of Yao was unable to correct his people and maintain proper order.

entries.zh: 天子聞之，為餘善不足復興師，曰：「餘善數與郢謀亂，而後首誅郢，師得不勞。」
entries.en: When the emperor learned of this, he decided it was not worth mobilizing the army again on account of Yu Shan, remarking: 'Yu Shan plotted rebellion alongside Ying time and again, yet in the end he was the first to bring Ying to justice, sparing our forces the trouble.'
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of this, he deemed it not worth raising troops again over Yu Shan, saying: 'Yu Shan repeatedly plotted rebellion with Ying, but then was the first to execute Ying, so the troops were spared their labor.'

entries.zh: 因立餘善為東越王，與繇王并處。
entries.en: And so Yu Shan was made the King of Dongyue, to rule alongside the King of Yao.
entries.literal: Therefore, Yu Shan was established as the King of Dongyue, dwelling alongside the King of Yao.

entries.zh: 餘善刻「武帝」璽自立，詐其民，為妄言。
entries.en: Yu Shan had an imperial seal carved bearing the title 'Martial Emperor' and declared himself sovereign, deceiving his people with extravagant claims.
entries.literal: Yu Shan carved an imperial seal inscribed 'Martial Emperor' and proclaimed himself sovereign, deceiving his people with false pronouncements.

entries.zh: 天子遣橫海將軍韓說出句章，浮海從東方往；
entries.en: The emperor dispatched the General Who Crosses the Sea, Han Yue, from Gouzhang to sail across the sea and approach from the east;
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched the General Who Crosses the Sea, Han Yue, from Gouzhang to sail across the sea and approach from the east;

entries.zh: 樓船將軍楊仆出武林；
entries.en: The General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, marched from Wulin;
entries.literal: The General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, set out from Wulin;

entries.zh: 中尉王溫舒出梅嶺；
entries.en: The Commandant of the Capital, Wang Wenshu, advanced from Meiling;
entries.literal: The Commandant of the Capital, Wang Wenshu, set out from Meiling;

entries.zh: 越侯為戈船、下瀨將軍，出若邪、白沙。
entries.en: The Marquis of Yue, appointed as the General of Spear Boats and Rapids, set out from Ruoye and Baisha.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Yue served as the General of the Spear Boats and Rapids, setting out from Ruoye and Baisha.

entries.zh: 元封元年冬，咸入東越。
entries.en: In the winter of the first year of the Yuanfeng era, all the forces converged on Dongyue.
entries.literal: In the winter of the first year of the Yuanfeng era, they all entered Dongyue.

entries.zh: 東越素發兵距險，使徇北將軍守武林，敗樓船軍數校尉，殺長吏。
entries.en: Dongyue had already dispatched forces to hold the mountain passes, placing the General Who Patrols the North at Wulin. He routed several colonels of the Towered Ships army and killed their commanding officers.
entries.literal: Dongyue had already sent troops to block the defiles, assigning the General Who Patrols the North to defend Wulin; he defeated several colonels of the Towered Ships army and killed their senior officers.

entries.zh: 樓船將軍率錢唐轅終古斬徇北將軍，為御兒侯。
entries.en: The General of the Towered Ships directed Yuan Zhonggu, the garrison commander of Qiantang, to slay the General Who Patrols the North. For this feat, Yuan Zhonggu was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yu'er.
entries.literal: The General of the Towered Ships led the Qiantang garrison commander Yuan Zhonggu to behead the General Who Patrols the North, and Yuan Zhonggu was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yu'er.

entries.zh: 自兵未往。
entries.en: His main force, however, had yet to move forward.
entries.literal: His own troops had not yet advanced.

entries.zh: 於是天子曰東越狹多阻，閩越悍，數反覆，詔軍吏皆將其民徙處江淮閒。
entries.en: The emperor then declared that Dongyue was narrow and full of barriers, that Minyue was fierce, and that they were repeatedly fickle. He decreed that the military officers were all to relocate their people to settle between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven declared that Dongyue was narrow and full of obstacles, Minyue fierce and repeatedly fickle, and decreed that the military officials should all lead the people to relocate between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.

entries.zh: 東越地遂虛。
entries.en: And so the lands of Dongyue were left desolate.
entries.literal: The lands of Dongyue were thus emptied.

entries.zh: 至元鼎五年，南越反，東越王餘善上書，請以卒八千人從樓船將軍擊呂嘉等。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Yuanding era, when Nanyue rebelled, Yu Shan, the King of Dongyue, submitted a petition offering to lead eight thousand troops to join the General of the Towered Ships in the campaign against Lu Jia and his allies.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Yuanding era, Nanyue rebelled, and the King of Dongyue, Yu Shan, submitted a memorial requesting to lead eight thousand soldiers to follow the General of the Towered Ships in attacking Lu Jia and the others.

entries.zh: 兵至揭揚，以海風波為解，不行，持兩端，陰使南越。
entries.en: When his forces reached Jieyang, he used the stormy seas as a pretext to halt his advance. He played both sides, secretly sending envoys to Nanyue.
entries.literal: When his troops reached Jieyang, he used rough seas and storms as an excuse not to advance, played both sides, and secretly communicated with Nanyue.

entries.zh: 及漢破番禺，不至。
entries.en: By the time the Han forces took Panyu, he had still not appeared.
entries.literal: When Han defeated Panyu, he had still not arrived.

entries.zh: 是時樓船將軍楊仆使使上書，願便引兵擊東越。
entries.en: At that time, the General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, sent a memorial to the throne requesting permission to turn his forces against Dongyue.
entries.literal: At that time, the General of the Towered Ships, Yang Pu, sent an envoy to submit a memorial, requesting permission to conveniently lead his troops to attack Dongyue.

entries.zh: 上曰士卒勞倦，不許，罷兵，令諸校屯豫章梅領待命。
entries.en: The emperor, saying the troops were weary from their campaigns, denied the request. He ordered the army to stand down and the officers to encamp at Meiling in Yuzhang to await further orders.
entries.literal: The emperor said the soldiers were weary and exhausted, did not permit it, dismissed the troops, and ordered the various officers to encamp at Meiling in Yuzhang to await further orders.

entries.zh: 元鼎六年秋，餘善聞樓船請誅之，漢兵臨境，且往，乃遂反，發兵距漢道。
entries.en: In the autumn of the sixth year of the Yuanding era, Yu Shan learned that the General of the Towered Ships had petitioned for his execution and that Han forces were massing on the border. He rose in open rebellion, sending his troops to block the roads leading into his territory.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Yuanding, Yu Shan heard that the General of the Towered Ships had requested to execute him and that Han troops were approaching the border and about to advance, so he rebelled and sent troops to block the Han routes.

entries.zh: 號將軍騶力等為「吞漢將軍」，入白沙、武林、梅嶺，殺漢三校尉。
entries.en: He gave his general Zou Li and others the title of 'Han-Devouring Generals,' then launched attacks on Baisha, Wulin, and Meiling, killing three Han colonels.
entries.literal: He titled generals Zou Li and others as 'Han-Devouring Generals,' invaded Baisha, Wulin, and Meiling, and killed three Han colonels.

entries.zh: 是時漢使大農張成、故山州侯齒將屯，弗敢擊，卻就便處，皆坐畏懦誅。
entries.en: At that time, the Han court had placed the Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Cheng and the former Marquis of Shanzhou, Chi, in command of the garrisons, but neither dared engage the enemy. They withdrew to safer positions, and both were later executed for cowardice.
entries.literal: At that time, the Han had sent the Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Cheng and the former Marquis of Shanzhou, Chi, to command the encampments, but they did not dare to attack, retreated to convenient positions, and were all executed for cowardice.

entries.zh: 會孝惠、高后時天下初定，遼東太守即約滿為外臣，保塞外蠻夷，無使盜邊；
entries.en: It happened that during the reigns of Emperor Hui and Empress Dowager Gao, when the empire had only just been pacified, the Governor of Liaodong made an agreement with Wiman to serve as an outer vassal. He was charged with keeping the barbarians beyond the frontier in check and preventing them from raiding the border.
entries.literal: It happened that during the reigns of Emperor Hui and Empress Dowager Gao, when the empire had only just been pacified, the Governor of Liaodong made an agreement with Wiman for him to serve as an outer vassal, protecting the barbarians beyond the frontier and preventing them from raiding the border;

entries.zh: 諸蠻夷君長欲入見天子，勿得禁止。
entries.en: In return, any barbarian chieftains who wished to travel to the capital for an audience with the Son of Heaven were not to be obstructed.
entries.literal: Any barbarian chiefs who wished to enter and see the Son of Heaven should not be prohibited.

entries.zh: 以聞，上許之，以故滿得兵威財物侵降其旁小邑，真番、臨屯皆來服屬，方數千里。
entries.en: When this arrangement was reported to the throne, the emperor approved it. Armed with this mandate, Wiman used his military power and wealth to invade and subjugate the smaller settlements around him. Before long, Zhendan and Lintun had all submitted to his authority, and his domain stretched over several thousand li.
entries.literal: This was reported to the emperor, who approved it, so Wiman used military might and wealth to invade and subjugate neighboring small settlements, and Zhendan and Lintun all came to submit and belong to him, his domain covering several thousand li on a side.

entries.zh: 傳子至孫右渠，所誘漢亡人滋多，又未嘗入見；
entries.en: The throne passed to his son and then to his grandson, Ugeo. Under Ugeo's rule, ever more Han fugitives were lured into the kingdom, yet he never once traveled to court to pay his respects.
entries.literal: The throne passed to his son and then to his grandson Ugeo, who lured ever more Han fugitives into the kingdom, yet never once went to court to pay his respects;

entries.zh: 真番旁眾國欲上書見天子，又擁閼不通。
entries.en: When the neighboring states near Zhendan wished to send memorials requesting an audience with the Son of Heaven, Ugeo blocked their way and refused to let them through.
entries.literal: When the neighboring states near Zhendan wished to submit memorials requesting an audience with the Son of Heaven, Ugeo blocked and obstructed them.

entries.zh: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
entries.en: In the second year of the Yuanfeng era, the Han court dispatched the envoy She He to rebuke Ugeo, but the king stubbornly refused to obey the imperial edict.
entries.literal: In the second year of the Yuanfeng era, Han sent She He to reproach Ugeo, but he ultimately refused to obey the imperial edict.

entries.zh: 何去至界上，臨浿水，使御刺殺送何者朝鮮裨王長，即渡，馳入塞，遂歸報天子曰「殺朝鮮將」。
entries.en: As She He departed and reached the border at the Pae River, he ordered his chariot driver to stab and kill the Joseon deputy king, Chang, who had been escorting him. He then immediately crossed the river and galloped back through the frontier passes to report to the Son of Heaven: 'I have slain a Joseon general.'
entries.literal: She He left and reached the border at the Pae River, had his chariot driver stab and kill the Joseon deputy king Chang who was escorting him, then immediately crossed, galloped into the passes, and returned to report to the Son of Heaven, saying, "I have killed a Joseon general."

entries.zh: 上為其名美，即不詰，拜何為遼東東部都尉。
entries.en: The emperor, pleased by the impressive claim, did not investigate the matter further and appointed She He as the Commandant of the Eastern Division of Liaodong.
entries.literal: The emperor, for the beauty of his claim, did not investigate, and appointed He as the Commandant of the Eastern Division of Liaodong.

entries.zh: 朝鮮怨何，發兵襲攻殺何。
entries.en: The Joseon court, outraged by this treachery, dispatched troops to attack and kill She He.
entries.literal: Joseon resented He, sent troops to attack and kill him.

entries.zh: 天子募罪人擊朝鮮。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven recruited convicted criminals to form an army against Joseon.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven recruited criminals to attack Joseon.

entries.zh: 其秋，遣樓船將軍楊仆從齊浮渤海；
entries.en: That autumn, the emperor dispatched the General of the Tower Ships, Yang Pu, to sail from Qi across the Bohai Sea.
entries.literal: That autumn, he sent the Tower Ship General Yang Pu from Qi by sea across the Bohai;

entries.zh: 兵五萬人，左將軍荀彘出遼東：討右渠。
entries.en: With a combined force of fifty thousand men, and the Left General, Xun Zhi, marching overland from Liaodong, they set out to punish Ugeo.
entries.literal: With 50,000 troops, and the Left General Xun Zhi from Liaodong, to attack Ugeo.

entries.zh: 右渠發兵距險。
entries.en: Ugeo deployed his troops to hold the mountain passes.
entries.literal: Ugeo sent troops to defend the dangerous passes.

entries.zh: 左將軍卒正多率遼東兵先縱，敗散，多還走，坐法斬。
entries.en: The Left General's battalion commander, Duo, led the Liaodong troops in an early charge, but they were routed and scattered. Many of the men fled in retreat, and Duo was executed under military law.
entries.literal: The Left General's battalion commander, Duo, led the Liaodong troops in a rash advance, but they were defeated and scattered; many retreated and fled, and Duo was executed under military law.

entries.zh: 樓船將軍將齊兵七千人先至王險。
entries.en: The General of the Tower Ships led seven thousand Qi soldiers and reached Wanggeom first.
entries.literal: The Tower Ship General led 7,000 Qi troops and arrived first at Wanggeom Fortress.

entries.zh: 右渠城守，窺知樓船軍少，即出城擊樓船，樓船軍敗散走。
entries.en: Ugeo held fast within the city walls. When he saw that the Tower Ships force was small, he sallied forth to attack them. The Tower Ships army was defeated and scattered in flight.
entries.literal: Ugeo defended the city, saw that the tower ship army was small, immediately came out of the city to attack the tower ships; the tower ship army was defeated and scattered in flight.

entries.zh: 將軍楊仆失其眾，遁山中十餘日，稍求收散卒，復聚。
entries.en: General Yang Pu lost his men and fled into the mountains, where he hid for more than ten days. Gradually, he managed to round up his scattered soldiers and reassemble them.
entries.literal: General Yang Pu lost his troops, fled into the mountains for over ten days, gradually gathered the scattered soldiers, and reformed them.

entries.zh: 左將軍擊朝鮮浿水西軍，未能破自前。
entries.en: The Left General attacked the Joseon forces west of the Pae River but could not defeat them and advance.
entries.literal: The Left General attacked the Joseon army west of the Pae River but could not defeat it and advance.

entries.zh: 天子為兩將未有利，乃使衛山因兵威往諭右渠。
entries.en: Since neither general had gained the upper hand, the Son of Heaven sent Wei Shan to use the might of the army as leverage and persuade Ugeo to submit.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven, because neither general had achieved victory, sent Wei Shan to use the army's might to persuade Ugeo.

entries.zh: 右渠見使者頓首謝：「願降，恐兩將詐殺臣；
entries.en: Ugeo received the envoy and bowed his head in apology. 'I am willing to surrender,' he said, 'but I fear the two generals will use treachery to kill me.
entries.literal: Ugeo saw the envoy and bowed his head in apology: 'I wish to surrender, but fear the two generals will deceitfully kill me;

entries.zh: 今見信節，請服降。」
entries.en: Now that I have seen the imperial credential, I am ready to submit.'
entries.literal: Now seeing the trustworthy tally, I request to submit and surrender.'

entries.zh: 遣太子入謝，獻馬五千匹，及饋軍糧。
entries.en: He sent his crown prince to make a formal apology, presenting five thousand horses and supplies of grain for the army.
entries.literal: He sent his crown prince to apologize, offering five thousand horses, and supplying army provisions.

entries.zh: 人眾萬餘，持兵，方渡浿水，使者及左將軍疑其為變，謂太子已服降，宜命人毋持兵。
entries.en: The prince arrived with a retinue of more than ten thousand men, all bearing arms, and was about to cross the Pae River. The envoy and the Left General, suspecting a ruse, told the prince that since he had already agreed to surrender, his people should lay down their weapons.
entries.literal: With a crowd of over ten thousand people bearing arms, when they were about to cross the Pae River, the envoy and Left General suspected they would rebel, told the crown prince that since he had already submitted, the people should not bear arms.

entries.zh: 太子亦疑使者左將軍詐殺之，遂不渡浿水，復引歸。
entries.en: The crown prince, in turn, suspected that the envoy and the Left General were plotting to kill him, and so refused to cross the Pae River. He led his men back the way they had come.
entries.literal: The crown prince also suspected the envoy and Left General would deceitfully kill him, so did not cross the Pae River, and led them back again.

entries.zh: 山還報天子，天子誅山。
entries.en: Wei Shan returned and reported on the failed negotiations. The Son of Heaven had him executed.
entries.literal: Shan returned and reported to the Son of Heaven, who executed Shan.

entries.zh: 左將軍素侍中，幸，將燕代卒，悍，乘勝，軍多驕。
entries.en: The Left General had once served as an attendant at court and enjoyed the emperor's favor. He commanded soldiers from Yan and Dai—fierce men flushed with victory—and his army had grown arrogant.
entries.literal: The Left General had formerly been a palace attendant, was favored, commanded Yan and Dai troops, who were fierce, rode on victory, the army was mostly arrogant.

entries.zh: 樓船將齊卒，入海，固已多敗亡；
entries.en: The General of the Tower Ships, commanding troops from Qi who had crossed the sea, had already suffered heavy losses.
entries.literal: The tower ship general commanded Qi troops who entered by sea, had already suffered many defeats and losses;

entries.zh: 其先與右渠戰，因辱亡卒，卒皆恐，將心慚，其圍右渠，常持和節。
entries.en: In their earlier battle against Ugeo, they had shamed and abused their fleeing soldiers, leaving the troops fearful and the general ashamed. During the siege, he frequently displayed credentials of peace.
entries.literal: In their earlier battle against Ugeo, they distressed and humiliated the soldiers who had fled; the troops were all fearful and the general was ashamed; while besieging Ugeo, they often displayed credentials of peace.

entries.zh: 左將軍急擊之，朝鮮大臣乃陰閒使人私約降樓船，往來言，尚未肯決。
entries.en: While the Left General pressed the attack, the senior ministers of Joseon secretly dispatched envoys to negotiate a private surrender to the General of the Tower Ships. Messages passed back and forth, but no final agreement was reached.
entries.literal: The Left General urgently attacked, the Joseon ministers secretly sent people to privately agree to surrender to the tower ships, coming and going with messages, but not yet willing to decide.

entries.zh: 左將軍數與樓船期戰，樓船欲急就其約，不會；
entries.en: The Left General repeatedly scheduled joint attacks with the Tower Ships forces, but the Tower Ships general, eager to finalize his private agreement with Joseon, failed to appear.
entries.literal: The Left General repeatedly made battle appointments with the tower ships, the tower ships wished to quickly fulfill their agreement, did not meet;

entries.zh: 左將軍亦使人求閒卻降下朝鮮，朝鮮不肯，心附樓船：以故兩將不相能。
entries.en: The Left General also sent agents to secretly persuade the Joseon court to surrender to him, but they refused, their loyalty inclined toward the Tower Ships general. For this reason, the two commanders could no longer work together.
entries.literal: The Left General also sent people to seek to secretly persuade Joseon to surrender, Joseon refused, their hearts attached to the tower ships: therefore the two generals could not cooperate.

entries.zh: 左將軍心意樓船前有失軍罪，今與朝鮮私善而又不降，疑其有反計，未敢發。
entries.en: The Left General harbored suspicions: the Tower Ships general had previously committed the offense of losing his army and was now secretly colluding with Joseon while refusing to compel their surrender. He suspected the man of harboring treasonous designs but dared not act.
entries.literal: The Left General thought: the Tower Ships general had earlier committed the offense of losing his army; now he was on friendly terms with Joseon in secret and still would not bring about their surrender; he suspected him of harboring treasonous designs but did not dare to act.

entries.zh: 天子曰將率不能，前（及）［乃］使衛山諭降右渠，右渠遣太子，山使不能剸決，與左將軍計相誤，卒沮約。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven declared that the commanders could not advance, and then sent Wei Shan to negotiate Ugeo's surrender. Ugeo dispatched his crown prince in response, but Wei Shan failed to handle the matter decisively; his actions clashed with the Left General's plans, and in the end the agreement fell through.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven said the commanders could not advance, and then sent Wei Shan to persuade Ugeo to surrender; Ugeo sent his crown prince, but Shan could not decide the matter decisively, clashed with the Left General's plans, and ultimately ruined the agreement.

entries.zh: 今兩將圍城，又乖異，以故久不決。
entries.en: Now the two generals were besieging the city yet remained at odds, and for this reason the campaign dragged on without resolution.
entries.literal: Now the two generals surround the city, but are at odds, therefore long undecided.

entries.zh: 使濟南太守公孫遂往（征）［正］之，有便宜得以從事。
entries.en: He dispatched Gongsun Sui, the Governor of Jinan, to set matters right, granting him full authority to act as he saw fit.
entries.literal: Sent the Jinan governor Gongsun Sui to correct it, with discretion to handle affairs.

entries.zh: 遂至，左將軍曰：「朝鮮當下久矣，不下者有狀。」
entries.en: When Gongsun Sui arrived, the Left General told him, 'Joseon should have fallen long ago. There is a reason it has not.'
entries.literal: Sui arrived, the Left General said: 'Joseon should have surrendered long ago, not surrendering has a reason.'

entries.zh: 言樓船數期不會，具以素所意告遂，曰：「今如此不取，恐為大害，非獨樓船，又且與朝鮮共滅吾軍。」
entries.en: He described how the Tower Ships general had repeatedly failed to keep their battle appointments, laid out all his longstanding suspicions, and said, 'If we do not act now, I fear the consequences will be dire. The Tower Ships general may not only refuse to fight—he may join forces with Joseon to destroy our army.'
entries.literal: He told Sui about the tower ships repeatedly not meeting appointments, fully informed him of his longstanding suspicions, saying: 'Now like this not taking it, I fear it will become a great harm, not only the tower ships, but also together with Joseon will destroy our army.'

entries.zh: 遂亦以為然，而以節召樓船將軍入左將軍營計事，即命左將軍麾下執捕樓船將軍，并其軍，以報天子。
entries.en: Gongsun Sui agreed. Using the imperial tally, he summoned the General of the Tower Ships to the Left General's camp to discuss strategy. Once there, he ordered the Left General's officers to seize and arrest the Tower Ships general, absorbed his troops, and sent a report to the Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Sui also thought it so, and used the tally to summon the tower ship general into the Left General's camp to discuss matters, immediately ordered the Left General's subordinates to arrest the tower ship general and his army, reporting to the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 天子誅遂。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven had Gongsun Sui executed.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven executed Sui.

entries.zh: 左將軍已并兩軍，即急擊朝鮮。
entries.en: Having now combined both armies under his command, the Left General launched an all-out assault on Joseon.
entries.literal: The Left General already combined the two armies, immediately urgently attacked Joseon.

entries.zh: 朝鮮相路人、相韓陰、尼谿相參、將軍王唊相與謀曰：「始欲降樓船，樓船今執，獨左將軍并將，戰益急，恐不能與，（戰）王又不肯降。」
entries.en: The Joseon Chancellor Lu Ren, Chancellor Han Yin, the Chancellor of Nixi, Shen, and General Wang Xia plotted together. 'We had intended to surrender to the Tower Ships general,' they said, 'but now he has been arrested. The Left General alone commands both armies, the fighting grows fiercer by the day, and we fear we cannot hold out—yet the king still refuses to surrender.'
entries.literal: The Joseon chancellor Lu Ren, Chancellor Han Yin, the Chancellor of Nixi, Shen, and General Wang Xia plotted together, saying, "We had at first wished to surrender to the Tower Ships general, but he has now been arrested. The Left General alone commands both armies, the fighting grows fiercer by the day, and we fear we cannot hold out—yet the king still refuses to surrender."

entries.zh: 陰、唊、路人皆亡降漢。
entries.en: Han Yin, Wang Xia, and Lu Ren all deserted and surrendered to the Han.
entries.literal: Yin, Xia, and Lu Ren all fled and surrendered to Han.

entries.zh: 路人道死。
entries.en: Lu Ren died on the road.
entries.literal: Lu Ren died en route.

entries.zh: 元封三年夏，尼谿相參乃使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。
entries.en: In the summer of the third year of the Yuanfeng era, Shen, the Chancellor of Nixi, sent men to assassinate King Ugeo of Joseon and came to surrender.
entries.literal: In the summer of the third year of the Yuanfeng era, Shen, the Chancellor of Nixi, sent men to kill King Ugeo of Joseon and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 王險城未下，故右渠之大臣成巳又反，復攻吏。
entries.en: But the fortress of Wanggeom had not yet fallen. Cheng Ji, one of Ugeo's former ministers, raised another rebellion and turned his forces against the Han officials.
entries.literal: Wanggeom Fortress was not yet taken; therefore Ugeo's minister Cheng Ji again rebelled and attacked the officials again.

entries.zh: 左將軍使右渠子長降、相路人之子最告諭其民，誅成巳，以故遂定朝鮮，為四郡。
entries.en: The Left General had Ugeo's son, Changjiang, surrender and had Lu Ren's son, Zui, issue a proclamation to the people. He executed Cheng Ji, and with this, Joseon was at last pacified and divided into four commanderies.
entries.literal: The Left General had Ugeo's son Changjiang surrender and had Lu Ren's son Zui proclaim and instruct the people; he executed Cheng Ji, and thereby finally pacified Joseon and established four commanderies.

entries.zh: 封參為澅清侯，陰為荻苴侯，唊為平州侯，長［降］為幾侯。
entries.en: Shen was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Huaqing, Han Yin as the Marquis of Diqu, Wang Xia as the Marquis of Pingzhou, and Chang as the Marquis of Ji.
entries.literal: Shen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaqing, Han Yin as Marquis of Diqu, Wang Xia as Marquis of Pingzhou, and Chang as Marquis of Ji.

entries.zh: 最以父死頗有功，為溫陽侯。
entries.en: Zui, because his father had died in loyal service and earned considerable merit, was made the Marquis of Wenyang.
entries.literal: Zui, because his father died and had considerable merit, became Marquis of Wenyang.

entries.zh: 左將軍徵至，坐爭功相嫉，乖計，棄市。
entries.en: The Left General was recalled to the capital. He was charged with disputing credit, jealousy toward his colleague, and disobedience of orders, and was publicly executed.
entries.literal: The Left General was summoned, sat for disputing merit and being jealous, conflicting plans, and was executed in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 樓船將軍亦坐兵至洌口，當待左將軍，擅先縱，失亡多，當誅，贖為庶人。
entries.en: The General of the Tower Ships was also charged: when his troops reached Liekou, he should have waited for the Left General but instead launched an unauthorized attack and suffered heavy losses. He deserved execution but was permitted to pay a fine and was reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: The Tower Ships general was also charged: when his troops reached Liekou, he should have waited for the Left General but presumptuously charged first, suffered heavy losses, deserved execution, and was permitted to ransom his life and was reduced to commoner status.

entries.zh: 朝鮮王滿者，故燕人也。
entries.en: Wiman, the king of Joseon, was originally a man of the state of Yan.
entries.literal: King Wiman of Joseon was originally a man of Yan.

entries.zh: 自始全燕時嘗略屬真番、朝鮮，為置吏，筑鄣塞。
entries.en: In the early days, when Yan was still whole, it had conquered and laid claim to Zhendan and Joseon, appointing officials there and constructing border fortifications.
entries.literal: From the time when Yan was still whole, it had often subdued and brought Zhendan and Joseon under its control, appointing officials there and building barrier forts.

entries.zh: 秦滅燕，屬遼東外徼。
entries.en: After the Qin destroyed Yan, the region was placed under the outer frontier of Liaodong.
entries.literal: Qin destroyed Yan, and it became part of the outer defenses of Liaodong.

entries.zh: 漢興，為其遠難守，復修遼東故塞，至浿水為界，屬燕。
entries.en: When the Han dynasty arose, the court considered the territory too remote and difficult to defend. They restored the old Liaodong border fortifications, setting the Pae River as the boundary, and placed the region under the Kingdom of Yan.
entries.literal: When Han arose, because the region was distant and difficult to defend, they restored the old Liaodong border fortifications, set the Pae River as the boundary, and placed the region under Yan.

entries.zh: 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴，滿亡命，聚黨千餘人，魋結蠻夷服而東走出塞，渡浿水，居秦故空地上下鄣，稍役屬真番、朝鮮蠻夷及故燕、齊亡命者王之，都王險。
entries.en: When Lu Wan, the King of Yan, rose in rebellion and fled to the Xiongnu, Wiman went into exile. He gathered more than a thousand followers, tied up their hair in the fashion of the eastern barbarians, donned barbarian clothing, and fled east beyond the frontier passes. After crossing the Pae River, he settled in the abandoned Qin territories between the upper and lower fortifications, and gradually brought the barbarians of Zhendan and Joseon under his rule, along with refugees from the former states of Yan and Qi. He made himself their king and established his capital at Wanggeom.
entries.literal: When the King of Yan, Lu Wan, rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu, Wiman went into exile, gathered more than a thousand followers, tied up their hair in barbarian fashion and wore barbarian clothing, fled east out of the passes, crossed the Pae River, and settled in the old Qin empty lands between the upper and lower barriers, gradually bringing Zhendan, Joseon barbarians, and former Yan and Qi fugitives under his rule and making himself their king, with his capital at Wanggeom.

entries.zh: 建元六年，大行王恢擊東越，東越殺王郢以報。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the Jianyuan era, the Grand Herald Wang Hui attacked the Eastern Yue, and the Eastern Yue killed their king, Ying, in response.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jianyuan, the Grand Herald Wang Hui attacked Eastern Yue, and Eastern Yue killed King Ying in response.

entries.zh: 恢因兵威使番陽令唐蒙風指曉南越。
entries.en: Riding the momentum of this campaign, Hui dispatched Tang Meng, the Prefect of Fanyang, to deliver veiled warnings to the Southern Yue.
entries.literal: Hui, taking advantage of the military momentum, sent the Prefect of Fanyang, Tang Meng, to convey hints and make things known to the Southern Yue.

entries.zh: 南越食蒙蜀枸醬，蒙問所從來，曰「道西北牂柯，牂柯江廣數里，出番禺城下」。
entries.en: The Southern Yue served Tang Meng a citrus sauce from Shu. When he asked where it came from, they told him, 'It comes by way of Zangke to the northwest. The Zangke River is several li across and flows down to the walls of Panyu.'
entries.literal: The Southern Yue served Tang Meng a citrus sauce from Shu. When Meng asked where it came from, they said, 'It comes via the northwest through Zangke; the Zangke River is several li wide and flows out below the city of Panyu.'

entries.zh: 蒙歸至長安，問蜀賈人，賈人曰：「獨蜀出枸醬，多持竊出市夜郎。
entries.en: When Tang Meng returned to Chang'an, he questioned merchants from Shu. They told him, 'Only Shu produces this citrus sauce. Traders smuggle large quantities of it out to sell in Yelang.
entries.literal: When Meng returned to Chang'an, he asked Shu merchants, and the merchants said: 'Only Shu produces citrus sauce. Many carry it out secretly to trade in Yelang.

entries.zh: 夜郎者，臨牂柯江，江廣百餘步，足以行船。
entries.en: Yelang sits along the Zangke River, which is over a hundred paces wide — more than enough to sail boats upon.
entries.literal: Yelang borders the Zangke River, which is over a hundred paces wide, enough to navigate boats.

entries.zh: 南越以財物役屬夜郎，西至同師，然亦不能臣使也。」
entries.en: The Southern Yue used its wealth to command the allegiance of Yelang and the peoples westward to Tongshi, but even so it could not truly bring them to heel as subjects.'
entries.literal: The Southern Yue used wealth and goods to command the allegiance of Yelang, westward to Tongshi, but it still could not truly make them its subjects.'

entries.zh: 蒙乃上書說上曰：「南越王黃屋左纛，地東西萬餘里，名為外臣，實一州主也。
entries.en: Tang Meng then submitted a memorial to the Emperor, arguing, 'The King of Southern Yue rides beneath a yellow canopy with a great banner at his left, and his domains stretch more than ten thousand li from east to west. In name, he is an outer vassal, but in truth he is the lord of an entire province.
entries.literal: Meng then submitted a memorial persuading the Emperor, saying: 'The King of Southern Yue rides under a yellow canopy with a left-side banner, his territory stretches over ten thousand li from east to west; he is nominally an outer vassal, but in reality he is the master of an entire province.

entries.zh: 今以長沙、豫章往，水道多絕，難行。
entries.en: At present, approaching by way of Changsha and Yuzhang, the waterways are frequently impassable and the route extremely difficult.
entries.literal: Now, going by way of Changsha and Yuzhang, the waterways are mostly impassable and difficult to travel.

entries.zh: 竊聞夜郎所有精兵，可得十餘萬，浮船牂柯江，出其不意，此制越一奇也。
entries.en: I have learned that Yelang commands elite troops numbering over a hundred thousand. Were we to launch boats down the Zangke River and strike without warning, it would be a masterstroke for subduing the Yue.
entries.literal: I have heard that Yelang possesses elite troops that could number over a hundred thousand. If we float boats down the Zangke River and strike by surprise, this would be a masterstroke for subduing Yue.

entries.zh: 誠以漢之彊，巴蜀之饒，通夜郎道，為置吏，易甚。」
entries.en: With the might of Han and the riches of Ba and Shu behind us, opening a road through Yelang and installing officials there would be the simplest of undertakings.'
entries.literal: Truly, with the strength of Han and the wealth of Ba and Shu, opening a road through Yelang and installing officials there would be extremely easy.'

entries.zh: 上許之。
entries.en: The Emperor approved the plan.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved it.

entries.zh: 乃拜蒙為郎中將，將千人，食重萬餘人，從巴蜀筰關入，遂見夜郎侯多同。
entries.en: Tang Meng was appointed Palace Gentleman General and given command of a thousand soldiers with over ten thousand supply personnel. He entered through the Zuo Pass from Ba and Shu and secured an audience with Duotong, the Marquis of Yelang.
entries.literal: He then appointed Meng as a Palace Gentleman General, leading a thousand soldiers and over ten thousand supply personnel, entering through the Zuo Pass from Ba and Shu, and thereupon met with the Marquis of Yelang, Duotong.

entries.zh: 蒙厚賜，喻以威德，約為置吏，使其子為令。
entries.en: Tang Meng lavished gifts upon him, impressed upon him the might and benevolence of Han, and negotiated an agreement to install officials, with the marquis's own son appointed as a local magistrate.
entries.literal: Meng gave generous gifts, explained Han's might and virtue, agreed to install officials, and had the marquis's son appointed as a magistrate.

entries.zh: 夜郎旁小邑皆貪漢繒帛，以為漢道險，終不能有也，乃且聽蒙約。
entries.en: The smaller settlements surrounding Yelang all coveted Han silks, yet they believed that the treacherous roads would forever prevent Han from exerting real control over them. For the time being, they agreed to Tang Meng's terms.
entries.literal: The small settlements beside Yelang all coveted Han silks, but believed the roads from Han were too perilous for Han to ever control them, so they tentatively agreed to Meng's terms.

entries.zh: 還報，乃以為犍為郡。
entries.en: When Tang Meng returned and made his report, the court established the Commandery of Jianwei.
entries.literal: When he returned and reported, the area was made into the Commandery of Jianwei.

entries.zh: 發巴蜀卒治道，自僰道指牂柯江。
entries.en: Soldiers from Ba and Shu were conscripted to construct a road from Bodao toward the Zangke River.
entries.literal: Troops from Ba and Shu were mobilized to build a road from Bodao pointing toward the Zangke River.

entries.zh: 蜀人司馬相如亦言西夷邛、筰可置郡。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru, a man of Shu, likewise argued that commanderies could be established in the western Yi territories of Qiong and Zuo.
entries.literal: Sima Xiangru of Shu also said that commanderies could be established in the western Yi lands of Qiong and Zuo.

entries.zh: 使相如以郎中將往喻，皆如南夷，為置一都尉，十餘縣，屬蜀。
entries.en: Sima Xiangru was dispatched as a Palace Gentleman General to win them over. The arrangements followed the same pattern as with the southern Yi: a commandant was appointed, more than ten counties were established, and all were placed under the jurisdiction of Shu.
entries.literal: Xiangru was sent as a Palace Gentleman General to persuade them, and all was arranged as with the southern Yi: a commandant and over ten counties were established, subordinate to Shu.

entries.zh: 西南夷君長以什數，夜郎最大；
entries.en: Among the chieftains of the southwestern Yi, who numbered in the dozens, Yelang was the most powerful.
entries.literal: The chieftains of the southwestern Yi numbered in the tens; Yelang was the largest.

entries.zh: 其西靡莫之屬以什數，滇最大；
entries.en: To the west, the peoples affiliated with Mimo also numbered in the dozens, with Dian being the greatest among them.
entries.literal: To its west, those belonging to Mimo numbered in the tens; Dian was the largest.

entries.zh: 自滇以北君長以什數，邛都最大：此皆魋結，耕田，有邑聚。
entries.en: North of Dian, the chieftains again numbered in the dozens, with Qiongdu the most prominent. All these peoples wore their hair in topknots, cultivated the fields, and lived in towns and settlements.
entries.literal: North of Dian, chieftains numbered in the tens; Qiongdu was the largest. All of these wore mallet-shaped chignons, tilled the fields, and had towns and settlements.

entries.zh: 其外西自同師以東，北至楪榆，名為巂、昆明，皆編發，隨畜遷徙，毋常處，毋君長，地方可數千里。
entries.en: Beyond these settled peoples, stretching from Tongshi in the west eastward and north to Dieyu, were the tribes known as Sui and Kunming. They braided their hair, followed their herds from pasture to pasture, had no permanent settlements and no chieftains, and their lands stretched across several thousand li.
entries.literal: Beyond them, from Tongshi in the west to the east, and north to Dieyu, those called Sui and Kunming all braided their hair, migrated with their herds, had no fixed dwellings and no chieftains, and their territory extended for several thousand li.

entries.zh: 自冄以東北，君長以什數，徙、筰都最大；
entries.en: To the northeast of Ran, the chieftains numbered in the dozens, with Xi and Zuodu the most powerful among them.
entries.literal: Northeast of Ran, chieftains numbered in the tens; Xi and Zuodu were the largest.

entries.zh: 自筰以東北，君長以什數，冄駹最大。
entries.en: Farther to the northeast of Zuo, the chieftains again numbered in the dozens, with Ranmang the greatest.
entries.literal: Northeast of Zuo, chieftains numbered in the tens; Ranmang was the largest.

entries.zh: 其俗或士箸，或移徙，在蜀之西。
entries.en: Some of these peoples were settled while others were migratory, and they all lived to the west of Shu.
entries.literal: Their customs were partly sedentary and partly migratory; they lived to the west of Shu.

entries.zh: 自冄駹以東北，君長以什數，白馬最大，皆氐類也。
entries.en: Northeast of Ranmang, the chieftains numbered in the dozens, with Baima the most prominent. All of them belonged to the Di people.
entries.literal: Northeast of Ranmang, chieftains numbered in the tens; Baima was the largest, and all were of the Di people.

entries.zh: 此皆巴蜀西南外蠻夷也。
entries.en: All of these were the outlying barbarian peoples beyond the southwest of Ba and Shu.
entries.literal: These were all the barbarian peoples beyond the southwest of Ba and Shu.

entries.zh: 汲黯字長孺，濮陽人也。
entries.en: Ji An, whose courtesy name was Changru, was a native of Puyang.
entries.literal: Ji An, courtesy name Changru, was a man of Puyang.

entries.zh: 其先有寵於古之衛君。
entries.en: His forebears had enjoyed the favor of the ancient rulers of Wei.
entries.literal: His ancestors were favored by the ancient lords of Wei.

entries.zh: 至黯七世，世為卿大夫。
entries.en: For seven generations down to Ji An himself, every generation had produced ministers and grandees.
entries.literal: For seven generations down to An, each generation served as ministers and grandees.

entries.zh: 黯以父任，孝景時為太子洗馬，以莊見憚。
entries.en: Through the privilege of his father's rank, Ji An served as Attendant to the Crown Prince during the reign of Emperor Jing, and his solemn bearing inspired awe in all who knew him.
entries.literal: An, through his father's rank, served as Crown Prince's Attendant in the time of Emperor Jing, and was feared for his gravity.

entries.zh: 孝景帝崩，太子即位，黯為謁者。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing passed away and the Crown Prince ascended the throne, Ji An was appointed Master of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing died and the Crown Prince ascended the throne, An became a Master of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 東越相攻，上使黯往視之。
entries.en: When the tribes of Eastern Yue fell to fighting among themselves, the Emperor dispatched Ji An to investigate.
entries.literal: When the Eastern Yue peoples attacked each other, the Emperor sent An to go observe the situation.

entries.zh: 不至，至吳而還，報曰：「越人相攻，固其俗然，不足以辱天子之使。」
entries.en: He never reached his destination but turned back at Wu, reporting to the throne: 'The Yue people have always fought among themselves—it is simply their way. Such matters are beneath the dignity of an envoy of the Son of Heaven.'
entries.literal: He did not reach there, but turned back at Wu and reported: 'The Yue people attack each other; it has always been their custom. It is not worth troubling the Son of Heaven's envoy.'

entries.zh: 河內失火，延燒千餘家，上使黯往視之。
entries.en: When a fire broke out in Henei and spread to consume more than a thousand homes, the Emperor once again sent Ji An to investigate.
entries.literal: When a fire broke out in Henei and spread to burn over a thousand households, the Emperor sent An to go observe.

entries.zh: 還報曰：「家人失火，屋比延燒，不足憂也。
entries.en: Upon his return, he reported: 'A household fire spread to the neighboring buildings—this is no cause for concern.
entries.literal: He returned and reported: 'A household's fire spread between adjoining buildings—it is not worth worrying about.

entries.zh: 臣過河南，河南貧人傷水旱萬餘家，或父子相食，臣謹以便宜，持節發河南倉粟以振貧民。
entries.en: But as I passed through Henan, I found more than ten thousand households ravaged by flood and drought—so desperate that in some cases fathers and sons were reduced to eating one another. I took it upon myself, bearing my staff of authority, to open the Henan granaries and distribute grain to the starving people.
entries.literal: As your servant passed through Henan, over ten thousand households of poor people in Henan had been injured by flood and drought, and in some cases fathers and sons were eating one another. Your servant humbly took the liberty, bearing his staff of authority, to open the Henan granaries and distribute grain to relieve the poor.

entries.zh: 臣請歸節，伏矯制之罪。」
entries.en: I now return my staff of authority and humbly submit myself to punishment for acting without imperial sanction.'
entries.literal: Your servant requests to return his staff of authority and submit to the punishment for falsely acting under imperial decree.'

entries.zh: 上賢而釋之，遷為滎陽令。
entries.en: The Emperor, impressed by his integrity, pardoned him and appointed him Magistrate of Xingyang.
entries.literal: The Emperor considered him worthy and pardoned him, then transferred him to be the Magistrate of Xingyang.

entries.zh: 黯恥為令，病歸田里。
entries.en: Ji An considered a mere magistrate's post beneath his dignity and, claiming illness, retired to his country home.
entries.literal: An considered it shameful to serve as a county magistrate and, pleading illness, returned to his fields and home.

entries.zh: 上聞，乃召拜為中大夫。
entries.en: When the Emperor learned of this, he summoned Ji An back to court and appointed him Palace Grandee.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he summoned and appointed An as a Palace Grandee.

entries.zh: 以數切諫，不得久留內，遷為東海太守。
entries.en: But because he so often spoke his mind in blunt remonstrance, he was unable to remain at court for long and was transferred to serve as Governor of Donghai.
entries.literal: Because he repeatedly offered blunt remonstrances, he could not remain long at court, and was transferred to be Governor of Donghai.

entries.zh: 黯學黃老之言，治官理民，好清靜，擇丞史而任之。
entries.en: Ji An was a student of Huang-Lao philosophy. In governing, he preferred tranquility and non-interference, carefully selecting able deputies and entrusting them with the administration.
entries.literal: An studied the teachings of Huang-Lao, governed his officials and managed the people, favored quiet non-action, and selected capable deputy administrators to entrust with affairs.

entries.zh: 其治，責大指而已，不苛小。
entries.en: His style of rule focused on the broad strokes and did not trouble itself with petty details.
entries.literal: In his governance, he held to the broad principles only and did not fuss over small details.

entries.zh: 黯多病，臥閨閤內不出。
entries.en: Ji An was frequently ill and would remain bedridden in his private quarters, rarely venturing out.
entries.literal: An was often ill, and lay within his inner chambers without going out.

entries.zh: 歲餘，東海大治。
entries.en: Yet after little more than a year, the Donghai commandery was flourishing under exemplary governance.
entries.literal: After more than a year, Donghai was excellently governed.

entries.zh: 稱之。
entries.en: The people praised him widely.
entries.literal: People praised him.

entries.zh: 上聞，召以為主爵都尉，列於九卿。
entries.en: When the Emperor heard of his success, he summoned Ji An to court and appointed him Commandant of the Noble Ranks, elevating him to the ranks of the Nine Ministers.
entries.literal: The Emperor heard of this and summoned him to serve as Commandant of the Noble Ranks, ranked among the Nine Ministers.

entries.zh: 治務在無為而已，弘大體，不拘文法。
entries.en: His approach to governance remained one of non-interference—he upheld broad principles and refused to be constrained by the letter of the law.
entries.literal: His administration aimed only at non-action, upholding the broad principles and not being bound by regulations and statutes.

entries.zh: 鄭莊以任俠自喜，脫張羽於緦聲聞梁楚之閒。
entries.en: Zheng Zhuang prided himself on his chivalrous spirit. He rescued Zhang Yu from peril, and his reputation spread throughout the lands of Liang and Chu.
entries.literal: Zheng Zhuang took pride in acting as a knight-errant. He rescued Zhang Yu from peril, and his fame spread throughout the regions of Liang and Chu.

entries.zh: 孝景時，為太子舍人。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jing, Zheng Zhuang served in the Crown Prince's household.
entries.literal: During the reign of Emperor Jing, he served as a Gentleman of the Crown Prince's Household.

entries.zh: 每五日洗沐，常置驛馬安諸郊，存諸故人，請謝賓客，夜以繼日，至其明旦，常恐不遍。
entries.en: Whenever he was granted his five-day leave, he would station relay horses in the outskirts and ride out to call upon his old friends. He received and bid farewell to guests through the night until dawn, always fearing he would not have time to see them all.
entries.literal: On each five-day rest period, he would station relay horses in the outskirts, visit his old friends, receive and send off guests, continuing day and night until dawn, always fearing he could not visit everyone.

entries.zh: 莊好黃老之言，其慕長者如恐不見。
entries.en: Zheng Zhuang was devoted to the teachings of Huang-Lao, and he sought out men of virtue with an urgency that suggested he feared he might never get the chance to meet them.
entries.literal: Zhuang was fond of the teachings of Huang-Lao, and his eagerness to meet worthy elders was as if he feared he would never get to see them.

entries.zh: 年少官薄，然其游知交皆其大父行，天下有名之士也。
entries.en: Though young and of modest rank, the men he befriended were all of his grandfather's generation—men of renown throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Though young in years and low in rank, the friends and acquaintances with whom he associated were all of his grandfather's generation—renowned men of the realm.

entries.zh: 武帝立，莊稍遷為魯中尉、濟南太守、江都相，至九卿為右內史。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu took the throne, Zheng Zhuang rose steadily through the ranks—serving as Commandant of Lu, Governor of Jinan, and Chancellor of Jiangdu—until he reached the Nine Ministers as Right Prefect of the Capital.
